definitions: English: to be, as a verb substantive or a copula.
Latin: exsisto in vero
Latin: verbum copulativum, qui existere in aliquo modo vel aliquo relatione indicat
irregularForms: The present system is highly irregular (sum, es, est, sumus, estis, sunt).
entries.etymology: From PIE *h₁ésmi 'I am'; Greek εἰμί and English 'is' are cognates.

examples.original: Studia mihi nostra saluti fuerunt.
examples.translation: My studies were my salvation.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Id erat liber aliquis antiquus pulcher aut rarior.
examples.translation: This was some old book, either beautiful or rare.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Quamdiu tibi satis nihil fuerit, ipse aliis non eris.
examples.translation: And as long as nothing satisfies you, you yourself cannot satisfy others.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: who? which? what? what kind or sort of a? (adjectively; while quis, quid is used substantively; qui, of persons, asks for the character, quis usu. for the name).
Latin: quis
Latin: Quo modo? (adverbium interrogativum)
irregularForms: The relative pronoun has a full three-gender paradigm; the listing is representative.
entries.etymology: From PIE *kʷos, the base of many relative and interrogative pronouns.

examples.original: Quod paulo minus utrumque evenit;
examples.translation: And both predictions were all but fulfilled;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Qua ut poteretur, virum eius Atticum Vestinum consulem in honore ipso trucidavit.
examples.translation: To possess the latter he slew her husband Atticus Vestinus while he held the office of consul.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Drusum fratrem in Germania amisit, cuius corpus pedibus toto itinere praegrediens Romam usque pervexit.
examples.translation: He lost his brother Drusus in Germany and conveyed his body to Rome, going before it on foot all the way.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: and.
Latin: particula quae est coniunctio generalis
Latin: X et Y — X Y-que
entries.etymology: From PIE *eti 'further, still'; Greek ἔτι is a cognate.

examples.original: Tiberius I. Patricia gens Claudia—fuit enim et alia plebeia, nec potentia minor nec dignitate—orta est ex Regillis oppido Sabinorum.
examples.translation: Tiberius Tiberius I. The patrician branch of the Claudian family (for there was, besides, a plebeian branch of no less influence and prestige) originated at Regilli, a town of the Sabines.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Quare et pontifex in locum P. Scipionis substitutus et ad deducendas in Galliam colonias, in quis Narbo et Arelate erant, missus est.
examples.translation: For this he was made pontiff in place of Publius Scipio and sent to conduct colonies to Gaul, among them Narbo and Arelate.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: within, on, upon, among, at; into, to, towards.
Latin: indicat locationem, incusionem, positionem spatialem
Latin: indicat locum ubi
entries.etymology: From PIE *h₁en 'in'; Greek ἐν and English 'in' are cognates.

examples.original: Lite fugent nuptaeque viros nuptasque mariti, Inque vicem credant res sibi semper agi;
examples.translation: With quarrels let wives pursue husbands and husbands wives, and deem that they are ever at issue with each other;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quare et pontifex in locum P. Scipionis substitutus et ad deducendas in Galliam colonias, in quis Narbo et Arelate erant, missus est.
examples.translation: For this he was made pontiff in place of Publius Scipio and sent to conduct colonies to Gaul, among them Narbo and Arelate.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Hos scelerum ritus, haec dirae crimina gentis Effera damnarat nimiae pietatis Erictho Inque novos ritus pollutam duxerat artem.
examples.translation: These criminal rites and malpractices of an accursed race fierce Erictho had scouted as not wicked enough, and had turned her loathsome skill to rites before unknown.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: He, she, it; this or that man, woman, thing.
Latin: (pronomen tertiae personae)
irregularForms: The pronoun has distinct masculine, feminine, and neuter forms; the listing is representative.
entries.etymology: Etymology uncertain; the stem supplies the basis of several Latin anaphoric pronouns.

examples.original: Valitudo ei neque corporis neque animi constitit.
examples.translation: He was sound neither of body nor mind.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Id erat liber aliquis antiquus pulcher aut rarior.
examples.translation: This was some old book, either beautiful or rare.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Singillatim crudeliter facta eius exsequi longum est;
examples.translation: It is a long story to run through his acts of cruelty in detail;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: who? which? what? what man?
Latin: (pronomen interrogativum substantivum)

examples.original: Curam quoque solito exactiorem praestitit.
examples.translation: He also observed more scrupulous care than usual.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tam bibit hunc avide, quam bibit ante merum.
examples.translation: He drinks it as greedily as he drank undiluted wine before.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ac primo eatenus interveniebat, ne quid perperam fieret.
examples.translation: His intervention too was at first limited to the prevention of abuses.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: not
Latin: Adverbium negativum, potest negāre nomina, adverbia, verba et adiectiva
Latin: Adverbium negativum

examples.original: Nam Claudium patruum non nisi in ludibrium reservavit.
examples.translation: As for his uncle Claudius, he spared him merely as a laughingstock.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Ex plurimis maximisque honoribus praeter paucos et modicos non recepit.
examples.translation: Of many high honours he accepted only a few of the more modest.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Non ita multo post Iuniam Claudillam M. Silani nobilissimi viri filiam duxit uxorem.
examples.translation: Not so very long afterward Gaius took as wife Junia Claudilla, daughter of Marcus Silanus, a man of noble rank.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: this; the present, near, or mentioned person or thing
Latin: (in loco prope locutorem)
irregularForms: The paradigm shows the characteristic -ius genitive and -ī dative singular.
entries.etymology: A compound demonstrative; the final -c is an old deictic particle.

examples.original: Ordinem vitae hunc fere tenuit.
examples.translation: This was in general his manner of life.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Saevitiam ingenii per haec maxime ostendit.
examples.translation: The following are special instances of his innate brutality.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Atque hic tam docilis ad cetera natare nesciit.
examples.translation: And yet varied as were his accomplishments, the man could not swim.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: how
Latin: Quomodo
Latin: Eo modo quo

examples.original: Censuerunt etiam quidam ut Pannonicus, alii ut Invictus, nonnulli ut Pius cognominaretur.
examples.translation: Some also recommended that he be given the surname of Pannonicus, others of Invictus, others of Pius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Sed ut praecipua commemorem, Appius Caecus societatem cum rege Pyrrho ut parum salubrem iniri dissuasit.
examples.translation: But to mention only the principal instances, Appius the Blind advised against forming an alliance with king Pyrrhus as not at all expedient.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Satis constat, Cn. Lentulum Augurem, cui census maximus fuerit, metu et angore ad fastidium vitae ab eo actum et ut ne quo nisi ipso herede moreretur;
examples.translation: All the world knows that he drove Gnaeus Lentulus Augur, a man of great wealth, to take his own life through fear and mental anxiety, and to make the emperor his sole heir;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: with, together, together with, in connection or company with, along with; sometimes also to be translated and.
Latin: Quando
Latin: Quia (cum causale + coniunctivus)

examples.original: Sed ut praecipua commemorem, Appius Caecus societatem cum rege Pyrrho ut parum salubrem iniri dissuasit.
examples.translation: But to mention only the principal instances, Appius the Blind advised against forming an alliance with king Pyrrhus as not at all expedient.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: O praeclarum diem cum in illud divinum animorum concilium coetumque proficiscar cumque ex hac turba et colluvione discedam!
examples.translation: O glorious day, when I shall set out to join the assembled hosts of souls divine and leave this world of strife and sin!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed hunc quoque iam tum quom ab Alpe descenderat, apud Metaurum castra metantem Claudius Nero cum Livio Salinatore debellat.
examples.translation: However, when Hasdrubal had just descended from the Alps, as he was planning out a camp near the Metaurus, Claudius Nero, together with Livius Salinator, defeated him also.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: in to
Latin: Appropinquans, adveniens (rem), et esse in loco prope ea; oppositum ab
entries.etymology: From PIE *h₂éd 'to, near'; English 'at' is a cognate.

examples.original: Agrippinam, Marco Agrippa genitam, neptem Caecili Attici equitis R., ad quem sunt Ciceronis epistulae, duxit uxorem;
examples.translation: Tiberius He married Agrippina, daughter of Marcus Agrippa, and granddaughter of Caecilius Atticus, a Roman knight, to whom Cicero’s letters are addressed;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Quare et pontifex in locum P. Scipionis substitutus et ad deducendas in Galliam colonias, in quis Narbo et Arelate erant, missus est.
examples.translation: For this he was made pontiff in place of Publius Scipio and sent to conduct colonies to Gaul, among them Narbo and Arelate.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nihil ex eo tempore praetermissum est ad maiestatem eius augendam ac multo magis, postquam Agrippa abdicato atque seposito certum erat, uni spem successionis incumbere.
examples.translation: From this time on nothing was left undone which could add to his prestige, especially after the disowning and banishment of Agrippa made it clear that the hope of the succession lay in him alone.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: I
Latin: (Pronomen primae personae.)
irregularForms: The accusative and ablative singular share the form mē; nōs serves as nominative and accusative plural.
entries.etymology: From PIE *éǵh₂ 'I'; Greek ἐγώ and English 'I' are cognates.

examples.original: Mihi autem de vocabulo pugna non est;
examples.translation: Now I am not going to fight about a word;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Oratio me istius philosophi non offendit;
examples.translation: With your master’s style I have no fault to find.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Civiline parum est bello, si meque meorque Obruit?
examples.translation: Is civil war still unsatisfied, if it destroy me and mine?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: that; he, she, it
Latin: Demonstrans rem non prope dictorem (haec res) nec prope auditorem (ista res)

examples.original: Sed nec hae nec illae docent aluntve virtutem.
examples.translation: But neither the new system nor the old teaches or nourishes virtue.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec vero alia sunt quaerenda contra Carneadiam illam sententiam;
examples.translation: Nor need we look for other arguments to refute the opinion of Carneades;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quid enim me prohiberet Epicureum esse, si probarem quae ille diceret?
examples.translation: What should prevent me from being an Epicurean, if I accepted the doctrines of Epicurus?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: thou; you (singular)
Latin: Pronomen secundae personae
irregularForms: The accusative and ablative singular share the form tē; vōs serves as nominative and accusative plural.
entries.etymology: From PIE *túh₂ 'you'; Greek σύ and English 'thou' are cognates.

examples.original: In tuto pars tui melior est.
examples.translation: The better part of yourself is on safe ground.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Poteram tecum hac Maecenatis sententia parem facere rationem.
examples.translation: This saying of Maecenas’s might have squared my account with you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Piso igitur hoc modo, vir optimus tuique, ut scis, amantissimus;
examples.translation: So said Piso, an excellent man and, as you know, a devoted friend to yourself.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: if.
Latin: Conditionem vel suppositionem indicans
Latin: Condicionem vel suppositionem indicans

examples.original: Agere enim fortius iam et audentius volo, si illud ante praedixero, mutari cum temporibus formas quoque et genera dicendi.
examples.translation: I want to take a bolder line now, and to speak more resolutely, first premising however that the forms and types of oratory change with the times.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Licet haec ipsa et quae deinceps dicturus sum aures tuae, Materne, respuant, cui bono est si apud te Agamemnon aut Iason diserte loquitur?
examples.translation: Very likely you will not relish what I am saying, Maternus, or what I intend to state in the course of my argument;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nam si est artius, ut ita dicam, holocleros, quid est quod dubitemus, quin per eosdem articulos et gradus producendus sit, per quos frater eius productus sit?
examples.translation: For if he be sound and so to say complete, what reason have we for doubting that he ought to be advanced through the same grades and steps through which his brother has been advanced?
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: but
Latin: Coniunctio limitationis

examples.original: Sed ut praecipua commemorem, Appius Caecus societatem cum rege Pyrrho ut parum salubrem iniri dissuasit.
examples.translation: But to mention only the principal instances, Appius the Blind advised against forming an alliance with king Pyrrhus as not at all expedient.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Neque spectaculis semper ipse praesedit, sed interdum aut magistratibus aut amicis praesidendi munus iniunxit.
examples.translation: He did not always preside at the games in person, but sometimes assigned the honour to the magistrates or to friends.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Scribonius mathematicus praeclara spopondit, etiam regnaturum quandoque, sed sine regio insigni, ignota scilicet tunc adhuc Caesarum potestate.
examples.translation: Tiberiusinfancy the astrologer Scribonius promised him an illustrious career and even that he would one day be king, but without the crown of royalty;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: To proclaim, make known. So perh. only in the foll. passage: pugnam, Lucil. ap.
Latin: Loqui, verba facere
Latin: Pronuntiare
entries.etymology: From PIE *deyḱ- 'show, point out'; Greek δίκη 'justice' is related.

examples.original: Scis quem nunc virum bonum dicam?
examples.translation: I mean one of the second grade, like your friend.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Erat enim apud eos, ut est rerum ipsarum natura, sic dicendi exercitatio duplex.
examples.translation: In fact, their rhetorical exercises were twofold, like the nature of the subjects themselves.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tu autem, Laterensis, qui tum lacrimas meas gratas esse dicebas, nunc easdem vis invidiosas videri.
examples.translation: And you, Laterensis, who then expressed yourself as touched by my tears, now turn round and try to cast infamy upon them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: all, every
Latin: Cunctus; numerus totus

examples.original: Frumentum omne ad se referri iubet;
examples.translation: He ordered all the corn to be brought in to his headquarters;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Liberalis disciplinas omnis fere puer attigit.
examples.translation: When a boy he took up almost all the liberal arts;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Omnia ea auctor fuit Cornutus matri eius ut aboleret.
examples.translation: All these Cornutus advised the poet’s mother to destroy.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

definitions: English: of himself, of herself, of itself, of themselves; one another, each other, etc.
Latin: (Pronomen reflexivum.)

examples.original: Sese tamen et amore fraterno et existimatione vulgi commoveri.
examples.translation: For all that, I feel the force of brotherly love and public opinion.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Habet enim secum voluptatem, sine qua non est, etiam cum sola est.
examples.translation: For virtue keeps pleasure in its company, and does not exist without it, even when alone.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Post has Valeriam Messalinam, Barbati Messalae consobrini sui filiam, in matrimonium accepit.
examples.translation: Then he married Valeria Messalina, daughter of his cousin Messala Barbatus.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a thing, object, being; a matter, affair, event, fact, circumstance, occurrence, deed, condition, case, etc.; and sometimes merely = something (cf.: causa, ratio, negotium).
Latin: Quidquid exsistat, vel cogitetur ut exsistere, quam ens discretum, vel animatum vel inanimatum; aliqui discretus est ut cogitare
entries.etymology: Etymology uncertain; the word has a very broad range of meanings.

examples.original: Rem videlicet difficilem et obscuram!
examples.translation: As though it were a difficult or recondite notion!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Eius rei quae causa esset, miratus ex ipsis quaesiit.
examples.translation: He asked them, wondering, what might be the cause thereof.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Matri summam omnium rerum privatarum publicarumque permisit.
examples.translation: He left to his mother the management of all public and private business.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to be able, have power; I (thou, he, etc.)
Latin: Potis esse aliquid facere
irregularForms: Compounded from potis + sum; the prefix changes before vowels (possum, potes, potest).
entries.etymology: A compound of potis 'able' + sum 'be'.

examples.original: Ac fieri potest ut errem;
examples.translation: I may possibly be mistaken;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum Sabinus respondisset: ”Et quomodo possum?
examples.translation: Sabinus answered: ”How can I?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quis est enim in quo sit cupiditas, quin recte cupidus dici possit?
examples.translation: On your principle there is no form of desire whose possessor could not be morally approved.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make, do, act; to perform, accomplish, bring about
Latin: efficere
Latin: agere
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; fēci, factum, 3
irregularForms: The perfect stem fēc- and the passive factus are not built on the present stem faci-.
entries.etymology: From PIE *dʰeh₁- 'put, make'; Greek τίθημι is related.

examples.original: Nihil opus est exemplis hoc facere longius;
examples.translation: There is no need to enlarge upon or illustrate this point;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Singillatim crudeliter facta eius exsequi longum est;
examples.translation: It is a long story to run through his acts of cruelty in detail;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Cato grammaticus, Latina Siren, Qui solus legit ac facit poetas.
examples.translation: Cato, teacher of letters, Siren Latin-born, He, and none other, poets reads and makes.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: self, in person, he (emphatic), himself, herself, itself, used both substantively and adjectively, to denote that person (thing) of which something is eminently or exclusively
Latin: (pronomen emphaticum)

examples.original: Huius, Lyco, oratione locuples, rebus ipsis ieiunior.
examples.translation: His successor Lyco has a copious style, but his matter is somewhat barren.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Reliquit filium Orbilium, et ipsum grammaticum professorem.
examples.translation: He left a son Orbilius, who was also a teacher of grammar.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Qua ut poteretur, virum eius Atticum Vestinum consulem in honore ipso trucidavit.
examples.translation: To possess the latter he slew her husband Atticus Vestinus while he held the office of consul.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: short or long in every part of the word; as, ăb, păter, ită; ā, māter, frustrā. During a short period (between about 620 and 670 A. U. C. = from 134 to 84 B.C.) long a was written
Latin: Littera prima abecedarii Latini: A, seu a

examples.original: In primis tuendae pacis a grassaturis ac latrociniis seditionumque licentia curam habuit.
examples.translation: He gave special attention to securing safety from highway banditry and lawless outbreaks.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Munera, quibus a Pompeia Sex. Pompei sorore in Sicilia donatus est, chlamys et fibula, item bullae aureae, durant ostendunturque adhuc Baiis.
examples.translation: The gifts which were given him in Sicily by Pompeia, sister of Sextus Pompeius, a cloak and clasp, as well as studs of gold, are still kept and exhibited at Baiae.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: one, a single.
Latin: Numerus I
Latin: Qui singularis est

examples.original: Uni Crassicio se credere Zmyrna probavit;
examples.translation: Zmyrna will trust her fate but to Crassicius;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Putas tu posse unam omnium esse sententiam?
examples.translation: And can you suppose that all men are able to hold one opinion?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac primo eatenus interveniebat, ne quid perperam fieret.
examples.translation: His intervention too was at first limited to the prevention of abuses.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: out of, from
Latin: (motionem ab interiore indicans)

examples.original: Tiberius Nero advenientem ex Hispania cum ingentibus copiis Hasdrubalem, prius quam Hannibali fratri coniungeretur, oppressit.
examples.translation: Tiberius Nero crushed Hasdrubal, on his arrival from Spain with a vast army, before he could unite with his brother Hannibal.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tiberius I. Patricia gens Claudia—fuit enim et alia plebeia, nec potentia minor nec dignitate—orta est ex Regillis oppido Sabinorum.
examples.translation: Tiberius Tiberius I. The patrician branch of the Claudian family (for there was, besides, a plebeian branch of no less influence and prestige) originated at Regilli, a town of the Sabines.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: the going out, departure, removal, or separating of an object from any fixed point
Latin: (praepositio significans separatum esse)

examples.original: Tamen longe maiora et firmiora de eo iudicia in morte ac post mortem exstiterunt.
examples.translation: Yet far greater and stronger tokens of regard were shown at the time of his death and immediately afterwards.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Mentis valitudinem et ipse senserat ac subinde de secessu deque purgando cerebro cogitavit.
examples.translation: He himself realised his mental infirmity, and thought at times of going into retirement and clearing his brain.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: At illa commota veteres quosdam ad se Augusti codicillos de acerbitate et intolerantia morum eius e sacrario protulit atque recitavit.
examples.translation: Then Livia, in a rage, drew from a secret place and read some old letters written to her by Augustus with regard to the austerity and stubbornness of Tiberius’ disposition.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: addition is prominent in
Latin: sed etiam, sed et
Latin: “at differentiam rerum significat: ut cum dicimus, Scipio est bellator, at M. Cato orator”

examples.original: Egerat cum Vario, priusquam Italia decederet, ut siquid sibi accidisset, ”Aeneida” combureret; at is ita facturum se pernegarat;
examples.translation: He had arranged with Varius, before leaving Italy, that if anything befell him his friend should burn the ”Aeneid”;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: At illa commota veteres quosdam ad se Augusti codicillos de acerbitate et intolerantia morum eius e sacrario protulit atque recitavit.
examples.translation: Then Livia, in a rage, drew from a secret place and read some old letters written to her by Augustus with regard to the austerity and stubbornness of Tiberius’ disposition.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: In extructionibus praetoriorum atque villarum omni ratione posthabita nihil tam efficere concupiscebat quam quod posse effici negaretur.
examples.translation: He built villas and country houses with utter disregard of expense, caring for nothing so much as to do what men said was impossible.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: nor, and..not; not..either, not even

examples.original: Nec multo post diem obiit, utroque liberorum superstite, Tiberio Drusoque Neronibus.
examples.translation: Not long afterward he died, survived by both his sons, Tiberius Nero and Drusus Nero.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tiberius I. Patricia gens Claudia—fuit enim et alia plebeia, nec potentia minor nec dignitate—orta est ex Regillis oppido Sabinorum.
examples.translation: Tiberius Tiberius I. The patrician branch of the Claudian family (for there was, besides, a plebeian branch of no less influence and prestige) originated at Regilli, a town of the Sabines.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: or; and repeated: aut... aut, either... or; so in Sanscr. vā... vā.
Latin: aut X aut Y — vel X vel Y sed non ambo
Latin: coniunctio indicans rem alterum

examples.original: Neque spectaculis semper ipse praesedit, sed interdum aut magistratibus aut amicis praesidendi munus iniunxit.
examples.translation: He did not always preside at the games in person, but sometimes assigned the honour to the magistrates or to friends.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Licet haec ipsa et quae deinceps dicturus sum aures tuae, Materne, respuant, cui bono est si apud te Agamemnon aut Iason diserte loquitur?
examples.translation: Very likely you will not relish what I am saying, Maternus, or what I intend to state in the course of my argument;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nec excusatur offensa necessitudine officii aut fide advocationis aut fortuitae et subitae dictionis impetu: meditatus videris \[aut\] elegisse personam notabilem et cum auctoritate dicturam.
examples.translation: And the offence you give cannot be held excused by the obligation to render a friendly service, or by loyalty to a client, or by the excitement of an unpremeditated utterance, made off-hand;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: perceive, with the eyes (syn. cerno).
Latin: Cernere oculis lucis ope aliquid, aliquem; videre aliquem: occurrere. || iudicare, visare, examinare nunc ea videamus quae
Latin: modus passivus: putare aliquam rem bonam esse, placere
entries.etymology: From PIE *weyd- 'see, know'; Greek εἶδον and English 'wit' are related.

examples.original: Non solebat mihi tam velox tempus videri;
examples.translation: In other years time did not seem to me to go so swiftly;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Incredibilia nobis haec videntur et supra humanam naturam excurrentia.
examples.translation: These goods seem to us incredible and transcending man’s nature;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: An ille Ciceroni invideret, qui mihi videtur ne Caesari quidem invidisse?
examples.translation: Why, he does not seem to me to have felt any for Julius Caesar himself.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: great, large.
Latin: Grandis spatio; amplus magnitudine; immensus
Latin: Cognomen Romanum / Latinum
entries.etymology: From PIE *méǵh₂s 'great'; Greek μέγας is a cognate.

examples.original: Videsne quam sit magna dissensio?
examples.translation: Do you realize how vast a difference of opinion this is?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Saevitiam ingenii per haec maxime ostendit.
examples.translation: The following are special instances of his innate brutality.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Et accesserunt maioris sollicitudinis causae.
examples.translation: He had besides reasons for still greater anxiety;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to walk, ride, sail
Latin: Movere a loco ad alterum
Latin: In eo loco

examples.original: Non ire istuc, sed errare est.
examples.translation: What you suggest is not travelling; it is mere tramping.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Expeditionem unam omnino suscepit eamque modicam.
examples.translation: He made but one campaign and that of little importance.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Eaque cupiditas agendi aliquid adulescit una cum aetatibus.
examples.translation: And this passion for activity grows as they grow older.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to hold, keep
Latin: Possidere
entries.etymology: From PIE *gʰh₁bʰ- 'take, hold'; German geben 'give' is related.

examples.original: Memoriae Domiti patris honores maximos habuit.
examples.translation: He paid the highest honours to the memory of his father Domitius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Dictatore comitia habente consules creati sunt T. Veturius Sp. Postumius.
examples.translation: Under the presidency of the dictator, Titus Veturius and Spurius Postumius were chosen consuls.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Homines optimi non intellegunt totam rationem everti si ita res se habeat.
examples.translation: These worthy people do not realize that, if this is true, it upsets the theory altogether.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: and also, and furthermore, also, likewise, besides (syn. quoque).
Latin: Et quoque

examples.original: Censuerunt etiam quidam ut Pannonicus, alii ut Invictus, nonnulli ut Pius cognominaretur.
examples.translation: Some also recommended that he be given the surname of Pannonicus, others of Invictus, others of Pius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Quin etiam speciem libertatis quandam induxit conservatis senatui ac magistratibus et maiestate pristina et potestate.
examples.translation: He even introduced a semblance of free government by maintaining the ancient dignity and powers of the senate and the magistrates;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Scribonius mathematicus praeclara spopondit, etiam regnaturum quandoque, sed sine regio insigni, ignota scilicet tunc adhuc Caesarum potestate.
examples.translation: Tiberiusinfancy the astrologer Scribonius promised him an illustrious career and even that he would one day be king, but without the crown of royalty;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: Elian; subst., a native of Elis, a town in Achaia
Latin: Differens a quibus qui iam dicti sunt; non eadem; alter trium vel ampliorum
Latin: alius ... alius

examples.original: Alii gladium facilius recipiunt quam vident.
examples.translation: And others meet the sword-stroke more readily than they see it dealt.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Utinam quidem dicerent alium alio beatiorem!
examples.translation: I only wish that they did allow degrees of happiness!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Atqui hoc perspicuum est, vitia alia aliis esse maiora;
examples.translation: Now, that some vices are worse than others is certain;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: truly, certainly, to be sure, indeed, in fact: Ch. Te uxor aiebat tua Me vocare.
Latin: Certe, sine ullo dubio
Latin: Vērō

examples.original: Agere enim fortius iam et audentius volo, si illud ante praedixero, mutari cum temporibus formas quoque et genera dicendi.
examples.translation: I want to take a bolder line now, and to speak more resolutely, first premising however that the forms and types of oratory change with the times.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Tiberius I. Patricia gens Claudia—fuit enim et alia plebeia, nec potentia minor nec dignitate—orta est ex Regillis oppido Sabinorum.
examples.translation: Tiberius Tiberius I. The patrician branch of the Claudian family (for there was, besides, a plebeian branch of no less influence and prestige) originated at Regilli, a town of the Sabines.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: from, away from; out of; by
Latin: Praepositio digressum de quodam loco indicans
Latin: sine digressu, sed solum de distantia

examples.original: Satis constat, Cn. Lentulum Augurem, cui census maximus fuerit, metu et angore ad fastidium vitae ab eo actum et ut ne quo nisi ipso herede moreretur;
examples.translation: All the world knows that he drove Gnaeus Lentulus Augur, a man of great wealth, to take his own life through fear and mental anxiety, and to make the emperor his sole heir;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Gaio et Lucio intra triennium defunctis adoptatur ab Augusto simul cum fratre eorum M. Agrippa, coactus prius ipse Germanicum fratris sui filium adoptare.
examples.translation: When Gaius and Lucius died within three years, he was adopted by Augustus along with their brother Marcus Agrippa, being himself first compelled to adopt his nephew Germanicus.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: whereby, Inscr. Miseni Repert. ex a. p. Chr. n. 159
Latin: A fine ad finem; a latere ad latus; in rem et e latere opposito

examples.original: Numquam tibi, Magne, per umbras Perque meos manes genero non esse licebit;
examples.translation: In vain you sever with the sword the tie of kinship that binds you.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Kal. Dec. M. Aemilio Lepido iterum L. Munatio Planco conss. per bellum Philippense.
examples.translation: In fact it is so recorded both in the calendar and in the public gazette.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Praecipiti cursu vaesanum Caesaris agmen In densos agitur cuneos, perque arma, per hostem Quaerit iter.
examples.translation: With headlong speed and fury Caesar’s men charged the close-packed columns, forcing a way through shields and through soldiers.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: my, mine, belonging to me, my own
Latin: Mei, vel qui ad me pertinet

examples.original: Id non de meo fiet;
examples.translation: The payment shall not be made from my own property;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid ergo mei consili est?
examples.translation: What, then, is my counsel?
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Non est quod mireris animum meum;
examples.translation: You need not wonder at any genius of mine;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: ex conject.—Inf.: DASI = dari, acc. to Paul. ex
Latin: Movere aliquid ab ipso ad aliquem

examples.original: Hi nec dant malum nec habent;
examples.translation: They neither give nor have evil;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hernicis ipsum agerque dono datus.
examples.translation: The town itself and its territory were given to the Hernici.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Consulatum in senos plerumque menses dedit.
examples.translation: He commonly appointed consuls for a period of six months.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: and, and also, and besides

examples.original: Quin etiam speciem libertatis quandam induxit conservatis senatui ac magistratibus et maiestate pristina et potestate.
examples.translation: He even introduced a semblance of free government by maintaining the ancient dignity and powers of the senate and the magistrates;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nihil ex eo tempore praetermissum est ad maiestatem eius augendam ac multo magis, postquam Agrippa abdicato atque seposito certum erat, uni spem successionis incumbere.
examples.translation: From this time on nothing was left undone which could add to his prestige, especially after the disowning and banishment of Agrippa made it clear that the hope of the succession lay in him alone.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to spin.
Latin: Ducere et torquere in filos, vel cum manu vel cum machina
Latin: implectere

examples.original: In classem cadit omne nemus;
examples.translation: Cohorts are raised to their full strength with recruits;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Interdictum ne capite damnatos propinqui lugerent.
examples.translation: The relatives of the victims were forbidden to mourn for them.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Quamquam ista assentatio, quamvis perniciosa sit, nocere tamen nemini potest nisi ei, qui eam recipit atque ea delectatur.
examples.translation: And yet this flattery of which I spoke, however deadly it may be, can harm no one except him who receives and delights in it.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: much, great, many, of things corporeal and incorporeal.
Latin: Qui numerum magnum complectitur; numerosus; haud paucus
entries.etymology: Probably from PIE *mel- 'strong, great'; the exact formation is debated.

examples.original: Summa adiectio quare plurimum facit vel exigua?
examples.translation: And why does the last addition, although very slight, make a great deal of difference?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vota illorum multos conpilant, ut te locupletent.
examples.translation: Their prayers plunder many another person, simply that you may be enriched.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Multi enim sunt ex his togatis, quibus pax operosior bello est.
examples.translation: For there are many of our toga-clad citizens to whom peace brings more trouble than war.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: st pers. plur. volumus, but volĭmus
Latin: īre ālīs per āërem
Latin: aufugere, fēstīnāre

examples.original: Volo illam tibi domi nasci;
examples.translation: I would have it born in your house;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vivere noluit, qui mori non vult.
examples.translation: He who does not wish to die cannot have wished to live.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ipsis permittimus, unde velint sumere exemplaria.
examples.translation: We allow the purchasers themselves to get their samples from anywhere they please.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: I, whence
Latin: Genere simili vel aequali; res ipsa

examples.original: Bonum omne in easdem cadit leges;
examples.translation: The good, in every instance, is subject to these same laws.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: De vacuitate doloris eadem sententia erit.
examples.translation: As regards freedom from pain her decision will be the same.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ita tribuni plebis magna ex parte iidem refecti.
examples.translation: So, for the most part, the same tribunes were returned to office.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: true, real, actual, genuine, etc. (opp. falsus, fictus).
Latin: Qui cum realitate congruit, realitati aequalis est

examples.original: Veri boni aviditas tuta est.
examples.translation: The real good may be coveted with safety.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ad veras potius te converte divitias.
examples.translation: Turn thyself rather to the true riches.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In edito stat admirabilis, celsus, magnitudinis verae.
examples.translation: He stands in a high place, worthy of admiration, lofty, and really great.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Of time, denoting a point or moment of time as coinciding with that of the action, etc., described.
Latin: Cum ego dico; ad hoc tempus; nunc
Latin: Ante quiddam tempus

examples.original: Iamque haud procul seditione res erat;
examples.translation: By this time the feeling was grown well-nigh seditious;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Agere enim fortius iam et audentius volo, si illud ante praedixero, mutari cum temporibus formas quoque et genera dicendi.
examples.translation: I want to take a bolder line now, and to speak more resolutely, first premising however that the forms and types of oratory change with the times.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Iamque haud procul iusto proelio res erat, ni celeriter diremptum certamen per centuriones esset;
examples.translation: And now the mellay was likely to end in a regular battle, had not the centurions speedily parted the combatants.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: we
Latin: (Pronomen primae personae.)

examples.original: Hanc si nostri transirent, hostes exspectabant;
examples.translation: The enemy waited to see whether our men would cross it;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Mnesarchum, Panaetium, multos alios, in primisque familiarem nostrum Posidonium.
examples.translation: Mnesarchus, Panaetius, and many others, not least our friend Posidonius.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Oculorum, inquit Plato, est in nobis sensus acerrimus, quibus sapientiam non cernimus;
examples.translation: The sense of sight, says Plato, is the keenest sense we possess, yet our eyes cannot behold Wisdom;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a human being
Latin: Animal mammiferum specie Homo sapiens; vir vel mulier. Specialiter
Latin: Homo ut rationalis vel moralis
entries.etymology: From PIE *dʰǵʰm̥mō 'earthling'; Latin humus 'earth' and Greek χθών 'earth' are related.

examples.original: Rationale enim animal est homo.
examples.translation: For man is a reasoning animal.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quod naturae satis est, homini non est.
examples.translation: But that which is enough for nature, is not enough for man.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ecce altera quaestio, quomodo hominibus sit utendum.
examples.translation: Then comes the second problem,—how to deal with men.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a measure with which, or according to which, any thing is measured, its size, length, circumference, quantity (freq. and class.).
Latin: Mensura
Latin: Methodus

examples.original: Quis sit divitiarum modus, quaeris?
examples.translation: Do you ask what is the proper limit to wealth?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Monstras mihi, qui sint modi flebiles;
examples.translation: You are showing me what the doleful keysb are;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hoc etsi multis modis reprendi potest, tamen accipio quod dant;
examples.translation: It is possible to take exception to this on several grounds;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: good; comp.
Latin: Qui qualitates desiderabiles possidet; haud malus
entries.etymology: From Old Latin duonus; the further derivation is debated.

examples.original: Atqui melius fuisset non queri quam vindicari.
examples.translation: Yet surely it were better to have no grievances than to need to seek redress.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Bona autem corporis huic sunt quod posterius posui similiora.
examples.translation: For they contribute something worth an effort to obtain;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Homines optimi non intellegunt totam rationem everti si ita res se habeat.
examples.translation: These worthy people do not realize that, if this is true, it upsets the theory altogether.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: thine, your, yours.
Latin: Tui, vel qui ad te pertinet

examples.original: Quid est autem hoc ”de tuo”?
examples.translation: And what do I mean by ”from your own store”?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quod istic credulitatis tuae damnum est?
examples.translation: And what harm does it do to you to give such credence?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Studia te tua clarum et nobilem efficient.
examples.translation: It is your own studies that will make you shine and will render you eminent.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: notwithstanding, nevertheless, for all that, however
Latin: Non obstante

examples.original: Tuum tamen, Messalla, promissum immutasse non debet;
examples.translation: All the same, Messalla, he must not be allowed to make you break your promise.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Tamen longe maiora et firmiora de eo iudicia in morte ac post mortem exstiterunt.
examples.translation: Yet far greater and stronger tokens of regard were shown at the time of his death and immediately afterwards.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a god, a deity (for syn. cf.: divus, numen).
Latin: Ens cui vis supernaturalis conceptum est, et quod a sacrificiis, suppliciis, etc., propitiatum est; divinitas; divus
Latin: deus unicus Iudaeorum, Christianorum, et Musulmanorum
irregularForms: The vocative singular is deus (also dīve); the plural is often dī in classical usage.
entries.etymology: From PIE *deywós 'god'; Sanskrit devá- is a cognate.

examples.original: Non homines timere, non deos;
examples.translation: It means not fearing either men or gods;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tunc enimvero deorum ira admonuit.
examples.translation: Then at last the anger of the gods taught him wisdom.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non sunt di fastidiosi, non invidi;
examples.translation: The gods are not disdainful or envious;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: piece, portion, share, etc.
Latin: Una ex portionum, aequales inaequalesve, in quibus res dividitur, vel divisam esse imputatur; res minus quam totum; fragmentum; divisio; membrum

examples.original: Vitiosum est enim in dividendo partem in genere numerare.
examples.translation: It is a fault in division to reckon a species as a genus.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In his igitur partibus duabus nihil erat quod Zeno commutare gestiret;
examples.translation: In these two departments then, there was nothing that Zeno need have desired to alter;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quod insigne mansit et in posteris eius, ac magna pars rutila barba fuerunt.
examples.translation: This sign was perpetuated in his descendants, a great part of whom had red beards.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: on the other hand, but
Latin: atque, porro

examples.original: Incohavit autem aquae ductum regione Tiburti et amphitheatrum iuxta Saepta, quorum operum a successore eius Claudio alterum peractum, omissum alterum est.
examples.translation: He likewise began an aqueduct in the region near Tibur and an amphitheatre beside the Saepta, the former finished by his successor Claudius, while the latter was abandoned.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Observatum autem notatumque est in primis Caesares omnes, quibus Gai praenomen fuerit, ferro perisse, iam inde ab eo, qui Cinnanis temporibus sit occisus.
examples.translation: Men further observed and commented on the fact that all the Caesars whose forename was Gaius perished by the sword, beginning with the one who was slain in the times of Cinna.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Ego autem oratorem, sicut locupletem ac lautum patrem familiae, non eo tantum volo tecto tegi quod imbrem ac ventum arceat, sed etiam quod visum et oculos delectet;
examples.translation: My own view is that the orator, like a prosperous and well-found householder, ought to live in a house that is not only wind and weather proof, but pleasing also to the eye;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: descends to each of us
Latin: Hūc movere; appropinquare, accedere
irregularForms: Present venit 'he comes' and perfect vēnit 'he came' differ only by vowel length; macrons are essential.
entries.etymology: From PIE *gʷem- 'go, come'; Greek βαίνω and English 'come' are related.

examples.original: Venit ad extremum; haeret in salebra;
examples.translation: But when it comes to its conclusion, it finds itself in trouble;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Brundisium veni, vel potius ad moenia accessi.
examples.translation: I came to Brundisium, or rather approached the walls;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum autem venissemus in Academiae non sine causa nobilitata spatia, solitudo erat ea quam volueramus.
examples.translation: When we reached the walks of the Academy, which are so deservedly famous, we had them entirely to ourselves, as we had hoped.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the rational soul in man
Latin: Psyche; ratio; mens

examples.original: Valitudo ei neque corporis neque animi constitit.
examples.translation: He was sound neither of body nor mind.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Si posset per se nudos edere animos, fecisset; nunc, quod amplius est, facit;
examples.translation: Had it been possible for her to produce souls by themselves and naked, she would have done so;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quicquid facies, cito redi a corpore ad animum. Illum noctibus ac diebus exerce;
examples.translation: The mind must be exercised both day and night, for it is nourished by moderate labour;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

Latin: Adiectivum pronominale, ad quantus respondens

examples.translation: Ah, late so mighty, where art thou?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fiscus tanti est, quantum habet;
examples.translation: A strong-box is worth just what it holds;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Discedit a Melino Cluentia, ut in tantis iniuriis non invita, ut a viro non libenter.
examples.translation: Cluentia leaves Melinus, neither sorry to do so, considering what she had suffered, nor yet glad, considering that he was her husband.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Indeed
Latin: Vero

examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;

examples.translation: Cicero himself, as is well known, had his detractors: they thought him turgid and puffy, wanting in conciseness, inordinately exuberant and redundant—in short, not Attic enough.

examples.translation: Ready for the fray and breathing defiance, he could parry the blows of the philosopher Helvidius, who for all his clever speaking was, as regards that sort of contest, an inexperienced novice.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: not; and not, also not.
Latin: Et non
Latin: Ne, non

examples.original: Pudicitiae neque suae neque alienae pepercit.
examples.translation: He respected neither his own chastity nor that of anyone else.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Neque spectaculis semper ipse praesedit, sed interdum aut magistratibus aut amicis praesidendi munus iniunxit.
examples.translation: He did not always preside at the games in person, but sometimes assigned the honour to the magistrates or to friends.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Princeps neque opera ulla magnifica fecit—nam et quae sola susceperat, Augusti templum restitutionemque Pompeiani theatri, imperfecta post tot annos reliquit—neque spectacula omnino edidit;
examples.translation: While emperor he constructed no magnificent public works, for the only ones which he undertook, the temple of Augustus and the restoration of Pompey’s theatre, he left unfinished after so many years.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: tempp. perff.
Latin: Vehere vel portare quoquomodo a loco ad alium, vel habere ut onus cum inter locos iens; habere cum se ipso

examples.translation: For the first time a land-law was proposed.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Atque haec ratio late patet.
examples.translation: And this is a principle of wide application.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Deinde quod acerbum fuit ferre, tulisse iucundum est;
examples.translation: And that which was bitter to bear is pleasant to have borne;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to be born, to be begotten (of or by male or female).
Latin: Gigni

examples.original: Id adeo malum ex provocatione natum;
examples.translation: That was precisely the mischief which the appeal occasioned;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ateius Philologus libertinus Athenis est natus.
examples.translation: Lucius Ateius Philologus was a freedman, born at Athens.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Ex rebus enim timiditas, non ex vocabulis nascitur.
examples.translation: Timidity springs from facts, not from words.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: that by, on account of, or through which any thing takes place or is done; a cause, reason, motive, inducement; also, in gen., an occasion, opportunity
Latin: Id per quod vel propter quod res agitur

examples.original: Et accesserunt maioris sollicitudinis causae.
examples.translation: He had besides reasons for still greater anxiety;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nunc initia causasque motus Vitelliani expediam.
examples.translation: I will now relate the origin and causes of the revolt of Vitellius.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Caesar his de causis quas commemoravi Rhenum transire decreverat;
examples.translation: For the reasons above mentioned Caesar had decided to cross the Rhine;

definitions: English: for
Latin: Coniunctio confirmationem vel explanationem indicans

examples.translation: As for his uncle Claudius, he spared him merely as a laughingstock.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.translation: You on your part are never done assailing the poets with your invective, and I, whom you charge with neglect of professional duty, am daily retained to defend the art of poetry against you.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Princeps neque opera ulla magnifica fecit—nam et quae sola susceperat, Augusti templum restitutionemque Pompeiani theatri, imperfecta post tot annos reliquit—neque spectacula omnino edidit;
examples.translation: While emperor he constructed no magnificent public works, for the only ones which he undertook, the temple of Augustus and the restoration of Pompey’s theatre, he left unfinished after so many years.
examples.author: Suetonius

Latin: (Trans.) ante se pellere, ducere pecora seu armenta
Latin: Urgere

examples.original: Quid enim possumus hoc agere divinius?”
examples.translation: What sublimer occupation could we find?”
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Illi enim consentire debet, quicquid agimus;
examples.translation: For whatever we do ought to be in harmony with this;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eaque cupiditas agendi aliquid adulescit una cum aetatibus.
examples.translation: And this passion for activity grows as they grow older.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: stitch

examples.original: Hoc felicitatem suam fine designat.
examples.translation: Such are the bounds which he sets to his own happiness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Suo enim quisque studio maxime ducitur.”
examples.translation: For we are all specially influenced by our own favourite study.”
examples.author: Cicero

examples.translation: He himself completed the last book of Sulla’s ”Autobiography,” which the dictator left unwritten.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

Latin: In scientiis quidquid esse potest fons disputationis vel expositionis (plur. -ī)

examples.original: Quid cognitio urbium aut locorum?
examples.translation: Or in surveying cities and spots of interest?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid ergo hoc loco intellegit honestum?
examples.translation: What therefore does he understand by ’moral’ in this passage?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cogis adulterium dando tempusque locumque;
examples.translation: By giving time and place you are compelling adultery;

definitions: English: not any, none, no.
Latin: Ne ullus

examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nullius rei meditatio tam necessaria est.
examples.translation: And yet there is nothing so essential for us to consider.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.translation: Galba Book VIIGalba • Otho • Vitellus Galba I. The race of the Caesars ended with Nero. That this would be so was shown by many portents and especially by two very significant ones.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Hoc consilio per conscios parum celato solutilem navem, cuius vel naufragio vel camarae ruina periret, commentus est atque ita reconciliatione simulata iucundissimis litteris Baias evocavit ad sollemnia Quinquatruum simul celebranda;

Latin: Nulla res

examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Ibidem saepius et per complures cantavit dies;

examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tum de diebus religiosis agitari coeptum, diemque a. d.

examples.author: Suetonius

examples.author: Livy

examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Coepi gubernatorem rogare, ut me in aliquo litore exponeret.

Latin: Demonstrans rem non prope dictorem (haec res) nec procul a dictore et auditore (illa res)

examples.translation: I have no time for such nonsense;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.translation: But what is this method, pray?

examples.translation: With your master’s style I have no fault to find.
examples.author: Cicero

Latin: Aliquid in usu habere. Adhibere

examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.translation: For these things that I speak of, like opportuneness before mentioned, are not made greater by prolongation.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.translation: The cause of his hesitation was fear of the dangers which threatened him on every hand, and often led him to say that he was ”holding a wolf by the ears.

examples.translation: Cicero’s letters keep the name of Atticus from perishing.

examples.original: Quod bene vertat, castra Albanos Romanis castris iungere iubet;

examples.author: Livy

Latin: Non notabilis

examples.translation: And both predictions were all but fulfilled;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Is mortuus est; reliquit pupillum parvum filium.
examples.translation: He died, leaving a young son, not yet of age.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nec minore saevitia foris et in exteros grassatus est.

examples.translation: Accordingly they surrendered themselves and all they had to Caesar.

Latin: Vigor, robur

examples.translation: To possess the latter he slew her husband Atticus Vestinus while he held the office of consul.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: pretty, handsome, charming, fine, lovely, neat, pleasant, agreeable, etc.
Latin: pulcher
