examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to cause to hang down, to suspend; esp. of scales in weighing.
Latin: in libra suspensus esse
Latin: pondus habere

examples.original: Nunc flere potestas, Dum pendet fortuna ducum;
examples.translation: Do not delay your grief, nor keep it for the crowning sorrows.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed ita, si illa ex nobis pendent, non ex illis nos.
examples.translation: But only if they depend on us, and not we on them.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tunc neque marmoreo pendebant vela theatro, Nec fuerant liquido pulpita rubra croco;
examples.translation: No awnings then hung o’er a marble theatre, nor was the platform ruddy with crocus-spray;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a spring, fountain, well-source (syn.: scaturigo, puteus).
Latin: Ubi aqua oritur
Latin: ubi aqua oritur

examples.original: Ipse Pompeius in originem fontemque belli Ciliciam;
examples.translation: Pompeius himself proceeded against Cilicia, the origin and source of the war;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Etenim ad caput et ad fontem utriusque generis veniamus.
examples.translation: But let us pursue this question of birth to the fountain-head.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quae si cui levior videtur, illa quidem certe, quae summa sunt, ex quo fonte hauriam sentio.
examples.translation: Yet insignificant though these powers may seem to be, I fully realize from what source I draw all that is highest in them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to long for, greatly wish for, to desire something not possessed

examples.original: Eo die milites sunt paulo minus septingenti desiderati.
examples.translation: On that day little less than seven hundred soldiers were missing.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Non desidero maiorem melioremque te fieri quam moliebaris.
examples.translation: I would not have you greater or better than you planned;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Facile est pascere paucos ventres et bene institutos et nihil aliud desiderantes quam inpleri.
examples.translation: It is easy to fill a few stomachs, when they are well trained and crave nothing else but to be filled.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a yoke for oxen, a collar for horses.

examples.original: Aspicis, ut prensos urant iuga prima iuvencos, Et nova velocem cingula laedat equum?
examples.translation: Do you see how the first yoke chafes the captured bullocks, how the new saddle hurts the flying steed?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Eo et Romana erigitur acies, nec quicquam satis tuti loci victis est, et de iugis quae ceperant funduntur;
examples.translation: The conquered could find no refuge anywhere that afforded safety, but were driven pell-mell from the ridges where they had made a stand.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: T. Quinctium Poenum legatum occupare montes iubet occultumque id iugum capere quod ab tergo hostibus foret.
examples.translation: His lieutenant Titus Quinctius Poenus he commanded to secure the mountains and secretly to occupy the ridge which lay to the enemy’s rear.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: run to meet; to go or

examples.original: Occurrent acti in exilium et evoluti bonis.
examples.translation: You will readily recall those who have been driven into exile and dispossessed of their property.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ut Cremonam venere, novum immensumque opus occurrit.
examples.translation: When they reached Cremona they found a new task of enormous difficulty before them.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Erras, si istorum tibi qui occurrunt vultibus credis;
examples.translation: You are wrong to trust the countenances of those you meet.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a bird; or collect., the winged tribe
Latin: Animal vertebratum homoeothermum pinnatum alatumque
Latin: → omen (propter usum in auspicio)

examples.original: Non avis utiliter viscatis effugit alis;
examples.translation: The bird cannot make good its escape when once its wings are limed;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Confer avum tuum Drusum cum C. Graccho, eius fere aequali.
examples.translation: Compare your grandfather Drusus with Gaius Gracchus, who was nearly his contemporary.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Pari in meliora praesagio in Caesaris castris omnia aves victimaeque promiserant.
examples.translation: In Caesar’s camp birds and victims had with equal clearness given every promise of better fortune.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to put between.
Latin: Occidere, obtruncare
Latin: Exstinguere, perdere

examples.original: Eo die Quintus Laberius Durus, tribunus militum, interficitur.
examples.translation: On that day a tribune, Quintus Laberius Durus, was killed.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Multis interfectis, compluribus equis captis Germani sese recipiunt.
examples.translation: After much slaughter and the capture of many horses the Germans retired.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ne eo quidem tempore quisquam loco cessit, sed circumventi omnes interfectique sunt.
examples.translation: Not even then did any man yield his ground, but all were surrounded and slain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a town in Lydia; afterwards the region around it; hence
Latin: Oppidum in Lydia
Latin: → Asia Minor

examples.original: Mithridates in Asia, cum eam provinciam totam occupasset, Mucia non sustulit;
examples.translation: When Mithridates overran Asia from end to end, he did not suppress the Scaevola Festival;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Huius adventus et Mithridatem insolita inflammatum victoria continuit et Tigranem magnis copiis minitantem Asiae retardavit.
examples.translation: His arrival restrained Mithridates, who was elated by the unusual experience of victory, and checked Tigranes, who was threatening Asia with great forces.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Praefecerat hunc Perdiccas ei parti Asiae quae inter Taurum montem iacet atque Hellespontum, et illum unum opposuerat Europaeis adversariis;
examples.translation: Perdiccas had made him governor of the part of Asia lying between the Taurus mountains and the Hellespont and had left him to face his European opponents alone;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: a party to an action (res), either plaintiff or defendant; afterwards restricted to the party accused, defendant, prisoner, etc.

examples.original: Res agi coepta est: citatus est Scamander reus.
examples.translation: The trial began: Scamander was put in the dock.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Eius rei quae causa esset, miratus ex ipsis quaesiit.
examples.translation: He asked them, wondering, what might be the cause thereof.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Nec diutius, ut fit, quam dum recens erat quaestio per clara nomina reorum viguit;
examples.translation: But the inquisition, as often happens, had the vigour to deal with illustrious defendants no longer than while its novelty lasted;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to act sparingly, be sparing with respect to a thing, to spare; constr. usually with

examples.original: Iam illa externa parce tu quidem;
examples.translation: As for external goods, you were, it is true, cautious;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Pudicitiae neque suae neque alienae pepercit.
examples.translation: He respected neither his own chastity nor that of anyone else.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Venit enim mihi in mentem, in hoc sene et adulescentem esse, cui parcitur.
examples.translation: For it comes into my mind that in this old man there is a youth also, and youth needs tenderness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: on the outside, without (syn.: extrinsecus, foris; opp. intra, intus, in).
Latin: Extera parte
Latin: Extera parte aliquid

examples.original: Tamen etiam quod prope est, extra est.
examples.translation: Yet even that which is not far away is still outside.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nam si, quae extra virtutem posita sunt, aut minuere illam aut augere possunt, desinit unum bonum esse, quod honestum.
examples.translation: For if things which are extrinsic to virtue can either diminish or increase virtue, then that which is honourablea ceases to be the only good.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et quamvis conscientia tibi tua fiduciam faciat, tamen quia multa extra causam valent, et quod aequissimum est spera, et ad id te quod est iniquissimum conpara.
examples.translation: Although your conscience makes you confident, yet, since many things have weight which are outside your case,a both hope for that which is utterly just, and prepare yourself against that which is utterly unjust.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that has not long existed, fresh, young, recent

examples.original: Nec diutius, ut fit, quam dum recens erat quaestio per clara nomina reorum viguit;
examples.translation: But the inquisition, as often happens, had the vigour to deal with illustrious defendants no longer than while its novelty lasted;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In civitate plena religionum, tunc etiam ab recenti clade superstitiosis principibus, ut renovarentur auspicia res ad interregnum rediit.
examples.translation: The citizens were much given to religious fears, and at that time, owing to the recent calamity, even the leaders were a prey to superstition;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ex istis etiam tu rebus effugere te posse confidis, cum te nos non opinione dubia sed tuis vestigiis persequamur, quae tu in tabulis publicis expressa ac recentia reliquisti?
examples.translation: Do you think to escape our pursuit here, where we are tracking you with the help not of vague conjectures but of your own footprints, left clear and fresh on this official document?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to set over any thing (as officer, superintendent, leader, etc.), to place in authority over, place at the head, appoint to the command of.

examples.original: Q. Sulpicium legatum praeficit castris;
examples.translation: The lieutenant Quintus Sulpicius he put in charge of the camp;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Iulium Burdonem Germanicae classis praefectum astu subtraxit.
examples.translation: Julius Burdo, commander of the German fleet, he saved by a clever ruse.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sex Liburnicae inter primum tumultum evasere, in quis praefectus classis Apollinaris;
examples.translation: Six Liburnian galleys escaped at the first alarm with Apollinaris the prefect of the fleet on board;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a maker, producer (ante-class.)

examples.original: Quid petitur sacris, nisi tantum fama, poetis?
examples.translation: What is sought by the sacred bards save fame alone?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cato grammaticus, Latina Siren, Qui solus legit ac facit poetas.
examples.translation: Cato, teacher of letters, Siren Latin-born, He, and none other, poets reads and makes.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Aliud est enim poetarum more verba fundere, aliud ea quae dicas ratione et arte distinguere.
examples.translation: A poetic out-pouring of language is one thing, the systematic and scientific marshalling of one’s matter is another.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to go forth or before, to go forwards, advance, proceed (class.; cf.: progredior, prodeo).

examples.original: Consules in sedem processere suam, missique lictores ad sumendum supplicium.
examples.translation: The consuls advanced to their tribunal and dispatched the lictors to execute the sentence.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Constantia non habet, quo procedat, non magis quam fiducia aut veritas aut fides.
examples.translation: Constancy cannot advance further, any more than fidelity, or truthfulness, or loyalty.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: At ei qui ab Alesia processerant maesti prope victoria desperata se in oppidum receperunt.
examples.translation: But the Gauls who had come forth from Alesia, almost despairing of victory, sadly withdrew again into the town.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to lead to, to bring or convey to, draw to any place or to one's self (opp. abduco, q. v.; syn.: adfero, apporto, adveho, induco).
Latin: Ducere aliquem aliquo vel ad se ipsum

examples.original: Quibus adductis eos in fidem recepit.
examples.translation: He therefore ordered them to furnish a large number of hostages;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ceterum et Fabius supplementum ab Roma adduxit et novus exercitus domo accitus Etruscis venit.
examples.translation: Fabius brought up replacements from Rome, and a new army came from Etruria to reinforce the enemy.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: A. Atilius et eius filius L. Atilius et armatos ibi fuisse et se suos armatos adduxisse dixerunt.
examples.translation: Aulus Atilius and his son Lucius Atilius stated both that armed men were there and that they brought thither their own slaves;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: verily, truly, indeed, at all events, = certe, revera, etc. (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Omnino canorum illud in voce splendescit etiam nescio quo pacto in senectute, quod equidem adhuc non amisi, et videtis annos.
examples.translation: In old age, no doubt, the voice actually gains (I know not how) that magnificent resonance which even I have not lost, and you see my years;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Equidem e Cn. Aufidio, praetorio, erudito homine, oculis capto, saepe audiebam cum se lucis magis quam utilitatis desiderio moveri diceret.
examples.translation: I myself frequently heard the blind ex-praetor and scholar Gnaeus Aufidius declare that he felt the actual loss of light more than the inconvenience of blindness.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Maior sum et ad maiora genitus, quam ut mancipium sim mei corporis, quod equidem non aliter aspicio quam vinclum aliquod libertati meae circumdatum.
examples.translation: I was born to a greater destiny than to be a mere chattel of my body, and I regard this body as nothing but a chainb which manacles my freedom.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: having wide interstices between its parts, of a loose texture, not thick or

examples.original: Scriptitavit et raro et tarde.
examples.translation: He wrote rarely and slowly.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

examples.original: Sunt tamen et doctae, rarissima turba, puellae;
examples.translation: Yet there are learned women too, a scanty number;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Id erat liber aliquis antiquus pulcher aut rarior.
examples.translation: This was some old book, either beautiful or rare.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: born at the same time, twin-born, twin- (class.).

examples.original: Parnasus geminos fertur iunxisse volatus;
examples.translation: On Parnassus, as they tell, their twin flights met;
examples.author: Claudian
examples.work: Panegyric On The Consulship Of Fl. Manlius Theodorus (A.D. 399)

examples.original: Infelix gemino cecidit prope Pergamon igni, Et paene est alio Troia cremata rogo.
examples.translation: All but twice in the flames unhappy Pergamum perished Troy on a second pyre narrowly failed of her doom.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Hermionam Pylades quo Pallada Phoebus, amabat, Quodque tibi geminus, Tyndari, Castor, erat.
examples.translation: Pylades loved Hermione as Phoebus Pallas, and as twin Castor was to thee, O Tyndaris.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: the east, as a quarter of the heavens
Latin: Orbis luminosus, cuius lux diem constituit, cuiusque absentia noctem; corpus centrale circum quod terra et planetae revolvunt, a quo in orbitis habiti sunt, et a quo lucem caloremque recipiunt
Latin: Lux vel calor solis

examples.original: Crastino die oriente sole redite in aciem;
examples.translation: To-morrow at sunrise form your battle-line again;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sol me invitabat, fames ad monebat, nubes minabantur;
examples.translation: The sunlight called to me, hunger warned, and clouds were lowering;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Stagna avidi texere soli laxaeque paludes Depositum, Fortuna, tuum;
examples.translation: Engulfing quicksands and spongy marshes hid the secret that Fortune had placed there;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: perhaps, peradventure, probably, possibly

examples.original: Nam ille alter fortasse tamquam phoenix semel anno quingentesimo nascitur.
examples.translation: And it is not surprising, either, that greatness develops only at long intervals;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et si sciret, quid esset vir bonus, nondum esse se crederet, fortasse etiam fieri posse desperaret.
examples.translation: And if he knew what it meant to be ”a good man,” he would not yet believe himself such;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nam adhuc, meo fortasse vitio, quid ego quaeram non perspicis.” ”Istic sum,” inquit, ”exspectoque quid ad id quod quaerebam respondeas.”
examples.translation: For so far, though perhaps I am to blame, you do not grasp the point of my question.” ”I am all attention,” he replied,” and await your reply to my inquiry.”
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To cry in public, make known by crying in public, to publish, proclaim.
Latin: Rem futuram dicere
Latin: Annuntiare, palam profere

examples.original: Quid est, quod praedicere velim?
examples.translation: And what is that preliminary remark?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Atque hoc non auditum, sed cognitum praedicamus;
examples.translation: And this I state not from hearsay, but from actual knowledge;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Videtisne, ut apud Homerum saepissime Nestor de virtutibus suis praedicet?
examples.translation: Do you not observe in Homer how, time and again, Nestor proclaims his own merits?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: lo! see! behold!

examples.original: Ecce hic dies ultimus est.
examples.translation: For what end should I toil?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In diversum ecce sapientia et stultitia discedunt;
examples.translation: Lo, Wisdom and Folly are taking opposite sides.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ecce altera quaestio, quomodo hominibus sit utendum.
examples.translation: Then comes the second problem,—how to deal with men.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: shame, a sense of shame, shamefacedness, shyness; modesty, decency, good manners, propriety, etc. (the general idea, while pudicitia is the particular one).

examples.original: Si pudorem haberes, ultimam mihi pensionem remisisses.
examples.translation: If you had any shame, you would have let me off from paying the last instalment.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Bassus pudore seu metu, quisnam exitus foret, intra domum opperiebatur.
examples.translation: Bassus waited in his quarters, prompted by shame or by fear as to the outcome.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Scaptium ipsum id quidem, etsi praemortui iam sit pudoris, non facturum.
examples.translation: Even Scaptius, though he had already outlived all sense of shame, would not do that.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to fall with violence, rush down; to fall down, tumble down, go to ruin (cf.: labor, procumbo, cado).
Latin: ardenter ac festinanter ire, festināre
Latin: cum impetu deicere, prosternere

examples.original: Inde ruunt toto concita pericula mundo.
examples.translation: And now dangers, summoned from all the world, came rushing on.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Rex Pharnaces magis discordiae nostrae fiducia quam suae virtutis infesto in Cappadociam agmine ruebat.
examples.translation: King Pharnaces, relying rather upon our internal feuds than upon his own valour, invaded Cappadocia with a hostile force.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: At id ne ferae quidem faciunt, ut ita ruant itaque turbent ut earum motus et impetus quo pertineant non intellegamus;
examples.translation: Why, even wild animals do not act in that way; they do not run amok so blindly that we cannot discern any purpose in their movements and their onslaughts.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to bring or carry out, to bring forth (very freq. and class.).
Latin: Vehere vel portare rem ex aliquo loco, extra ferre
Latin: Vehere vel portare rem ex aliquo loco

examples.original: Et Volumnius signa canere ac vexilla efferri castris iussit;
examples.translation: Volumnius, too, bade sound the signal and advance the banners from the camp.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hic cum semianimis de templo elatus esset, confestim animam efnavit.
examples.translation: He was half dead when taken from the precinct and at once breathed his last.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

examples.original: Nilum non extulit aestas, Maeander derexit aquas, Rhodanumque morantem Praecipitavit Arar.
examples.translation: The Nile fails to rise in summer; the Maeander straightens its course;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to throw
Latin: Iacere sub aliquid

examples.original: Ipse manu subicit gladios ac tela ministrat Adversosque iubet ferro confundere voltus.
examples.translation: In person he advances the fighting line and urges on his rearguard;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Tum neque subiectus, solito nec blandior esto: Haec animi multum signa nocentis habent: Sed lateri ne parce tuo: pax omnis in uno est;
examples.translation: Be not submissive then, nor more flattering than of wont; such signs point overmuch to guilt;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Atque in sensibus est sua cuiusque virtus, ut ne quid impediat quo minus suo sensus quisque munere fungatur in iis rebus celeriter expediteque percipiendis quae subiectae sunt sensibus.
examples.translation: The senses also possess their several virtues or excellences, consisting in the unimpeded performance of their several functions of swiftly and readily perceiving sensible objects.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: it is evident, clear, plain, or manifest; of course, naturally, evidently, certainly, undoubtedly, etc. (freq. and class.; cf.: nimirum, nempe).

examples.original: Magna scilicet laus est, si homo mansuetus homini est.
examples.translation: It is indeed worthy of great praise, when man treats man with kindness!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque erit aliquid animantibus antiquius, corpus scilicet.
examples.translation: But there is still something superior to ”substance”;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Scribonius mathematicus praeclara spopondit, etiam regnaturum quandoque, sed sine regio insigni, ignota scilicet tunc adhuc Caesarum potestate.
examples.translation: Tiberiusinfancy the astrologer Scribonius promised him an illustrious career and even that he would one day be king, but without the crown of royalty;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: To call back, recall (class. and freq., esp. in the trop. sense).

examples.original: Omnes, si ad originem primam revocantur, a dis sunt.
examples.translation: All men, if traced back to their original source, spring from the gods.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non est quod nos paupertas a philosophia revocet, ne egestas quidem.
examples.translation: There is no reason why poverty should call us away from philosophy,—no, nor even actual want.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Septem milia passuum cum abessent a Cominio, revocati ab suis neutri proelio occurrerunt.
examples.translation: Recalled by their leaders when seven miles from Cominium, they had not been present at either engagement.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: no. III.

examples.original: Sed quid ages tandem si utilitas ab amicitia, ut fit saepe, defecerit?
examples.translation: But what, pray, will you do, if, as often happens, expediency parts company with friendship?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nec ulla apud Vitellianos flagitii poena, et praemiis defectorum versa fides ac reliquum perfidiae certamen.
examples.translation: With the Vitellians there was no punishment for cowardice; those who went over to the Flavians received the rewards of their treachery;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Vaesanus in ortus Cambyses longi populos pervenit ad aevi, Defectusque epulis et pastus caede suorum Ignoto te, Nile, redit.
examples.translation: The madman Cambyses penetrated the East as far as the land of the long-lived people; food ran short, and he had to feed on his own men;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to prepare, get ready, be about to do a thing (Plautin.)

examples.original: Quid C. Caesarem in sua fata pariter ac publica inmisit?
examples.translation: And what impelled Gaius Caesar to the combined ruin of himself and of the state?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Solacia fati Carthago Mariusque tulit, pariterque iacentes Ignovere deis.
examples.translation: Carthage and Marius both drew consolation for their destiny ;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nepesinis inde edictum ut arma ponant, parcique iussum inermi: Etrusci pariter armati atque inermes caesi.
examples.translation: The Etruscans were put to death, whether armed or not. Of the Nepesini, too, those who were responsible for the surrender were executed;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to stretch, stretch out, distend, extend, etc. (class.; cf.: extendo, explico).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; tĕtendi, tentum and tensum, 3

examples.original: Ad profectum omnia tendunt, ad bonam mentem, non quaeritur plausus.
examples.translation: All his work makes for progress and for sanity, without any search for applause.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Missus et Celsus Marius ad electos Illyrici exercitus, Vipsania in porticu tendentis;
examples.translation: Celsus Marius was sent to the picked troops from Illyria, who were encamped in the Vipsanian Colonnade;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Miltiades, morandi tempus non habens, cursum derexit quo tendebat, pervenitque Chersonesum.
examples.translation: Miltiades, having no time to lose, kept on to his destination and arrived at the Chersonesus.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

definitions: English: Christ

examples.original: Adiuro te per Christum, ut ad ista respondeas.
examples.translation: I adjure you by Christ to reply to what I have written.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Cohibe itaque iam iniquum et inpacatum animum, ut in vera ecclesia Christi invenias salutare convivium.
examples.translation: So curb your hostile and rebellious spirit, that you may find the feast of salvation within the true Church of Christ.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Gratia te summi Pastoris ad pastionem ovium suarum salutiferam perpetuo conservet incolumem, dilectissime in Christo antistes.
examples.translation: May the grace of the chief Shepherd keep you continually in safety, bishop dearly beloved in Christ, for the wholesome feeding of His sheep.
examples.author: Bede

definitions: English: the office of consul, the consulate or consulship (very frq. in all periods)

examples.original: Consulatus super pristinum quattuor gessit;
examples.translation: He held four consulships in addition to his original one.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Consulatum in senos plerumque menses dedit.
examples.translation: He commonly appointed consuls for a period of six months.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: A. Postumium, quia collega dubiae fidei fuerit, se consulatu abdicasse; dictatorem inde factum.
examples.translation: They say that Aulus Postumius, because his colleague was of doubtful loyalty, resigned the consulship, and was then made dictator.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: an even, level surface
Latin: Superficies plana
Latin: Praesertim, mare quietum

examples.original: A quotiens frustra pulsatos aequore montes Obruit illa dies!
examples.translation: That day buried mountains which the waves had often before battered in vain;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Gabiis receptis Tarquinius pacem cum Aequorum gente fecit, foedus cum Tuscis renovavit.
examples.translation: He next turned his attention to affairs in the city.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Consilia ad movenda bella in Volscorum Aequorumque conciliis et in Etruria ad fanum Voltumnae agitata.
examples.translation: Schemes for instigating war were discussed in the councils of the Volsci and Aequi, and in Etruria at the shrine of Voltumna.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of or belonging to marriage, matrimonial, conjugal, nuptial, marriage-.
Latin: Qui ad nuptias pertinet
Latin: Coniunx; vir

examples.original: Respice Phylaciden et quae comes isse marito Fertur et ante annos occubuisse suos.
examples.translation: Consider Phylacides and her who is said to have accompanied her spouse, and to have died before her time.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Et utique maritum habebat multarum mulierum virum et deorum alienorum falsorumque cultorem.
examples.translation: And yet her husband was a man with many wives and worshipped strange, false gods.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Non enim quia pariter temperabatis a commixtione carnali, ideo tuus maritus esse destiterat;
examples.translation: For he had not ceased to be your husband because you had both agreed to abstain from carnal intercourse;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: wonderful, marvellous, astonishing, extraordinary (class.)
Latin: Admiratione dignus

examples.original: Pronuntiabat autem cum suavitate et lenociniis miris.
examples.translation: His own delivery, however, was sweet and wonderfully effective.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Nec est mirum cum eo nasci illa, sine quo frustra nascerentur.
examples.translation: No wonder that living things are born with a gift whose absence would make birth useless.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Erat in proximo lucus; hunc asylum facit, et statim mira vis hominum;
examples.translation: There was in the neighbourhood a grove, and this he made a place of refuge;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: from all parts, sides, or places, from every quarter, on all sides, on every part, everywhere
Latin: Ex omnibus directionibus
Latin: Omnibus rebus, omnibus respectibus

examples.original: Magnus undique numerus celeriter convenit.
examples.translation: A great number assembled speedily from every side.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ex hac fuga protinus, quae undique convenerant, auxilia discesserunt, neque post id tempus umquam summis nobiscum copiis hostes contenderunt.
examples.translation: After this rout the succours which had assembled from all quarters took their departure; and never afterwards did the enemy engage us at their full strength.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Id hoc facilius eis persuasit, quod undique loci natura Helvetii continentur: una ex parte flumine Rheno latissimo atque altissimo, qui agrum Helvetium a Germanis dividit;
examples.translation: On one side there is the river Rhine, exceeding broad and deep, which separates the Helvetian territory from the Germans;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: an agreement, stipulation, condition, compact, proposition, terms, demand.

examples.original: Quae condicio rerum, eadem hominum est.
examples.translation: The same thing holds good regarding men as regarding things.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hanc rerum condicionem mutare non possumus;
examples.translation: And we cannot change this order of things;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed si sapis, omnia humana condicione metire;
examples.translation: If, however, you are wise, measure all things according to the state of man;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: not to know (a person or thing), to have no knowledge of, to be unacquainted with, to be ignorant of, to mistake, misunderstand (a person or thing—class.; cf. nescio).—Constr. with

examples.original: An hoc tu, Laterensis, ignoras?
examples.translation: Are you blind to this truth, Laterensis?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quid ergo est ? Ignorantia rerum innocentes erant.
examples.translation: What, then, is the conclusion of the matter?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cuius avari modum ignorant, etiam non avari usum. ”Tolle,” inquit, ”errores;
examples.translation: Then comes the reply: ”Do away with error, and your precepts become unnecessary.” That is wrong;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to pour out, pour forth, shed, spread abroad (class.; esp. freq. in the transf. and trop. signif.).

examples.original: Id quod referendum est, effundit atque abicit.
examples.translation: That for which he should make return he wastes and loses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Finisque ille tam effuse evagandi Etruscis fuit.
examples.translation: This was the last time the Etruscans roamed so far afield.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec illi tulere impetum, sed ab effusa fuga flumen obiectum ab tergo arcebat.
examples.translation: They, too, failed to withstand his attack, but their rout was stopped by the river in their rear.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of or belonging to a deity
Latin: Ad Deum vel deos pertinens
Latin: Ens cui vis supernaturalis conceptum est

examples.original: Statue sex et quinquaginta annos, quibus mox divus Augustus rem publicam rexit;
examples.translation: Count the fifty-six years in which the sainted Augustus thereafter held the helm of state;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Quod primo ut augurium caelo missum laetus accepit tribunus, precatus deinde, si divus si diva esset qui sibi praepetem misisset, volens propitius adesset.
examples.translation: This the tribune first received with joy, as a heavensent augury, and then prayed that whosoever, be it god or goddess, had sent the auspicious bird might attend him with favour and protection.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Huic et divus Augustus dedit secreta mandata, cum illum praeponeret Thraciae, quam perdomuit, et Tiberius proficiscens in Campaniam, cum multa in urbe et suspecta relinqueret et invisa.
examples.translation: Tiberius, too, trusted him when he took his holiday in Campania, leaving behind him in the city many a critical matter that aroused both suspicion and hatred.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Sicily
Latin: Insula magna quae est ad inferiorem partem Italiae pertinet; Hodie est pars rei publicae italicae

examples.original: Maxime Siciliae fuisse tyrannos crediderim;
examples.translation: I am most inclined to think that they were Sicilian tyrants;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Edidit et peregre spectacula, in Sicilia Syracusis asticos ludos et in Gallia Luguduni miscellos;
examples.translation: He also gave shows in foreign lands, a city festival at Syracuse in Sicily, and mixed games at Lugdunum in Gaul;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Diem obiit circiter annos quinquaginta quinque natus, quartum post annum quam ex Peloponneso in Siciliam redierat.
examples.translation: He died at the age of about fifty-five, three years after returning from the Peloponnesus to Sicily.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

definitions: English: a breaking, beating, dashing to pieces; hence

examples.original: Sulla quoque inmensis accessit cladibus ultor.
examples.translation: And then, to crown the infinite slaughter, came Sulla’s vengeance.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Minus cladis ceterum non plus animorum ad hostes erat.
examples.translation: The enemy had suffered less, but was not less faint-hearted.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Coit area belli: Hic alitur sanguis terras fluxurus in omnes, Hic et Thessalicae clades Libycaeque tenentur;
examples.translation: The field of war was now contracted; here is preserved the blood that will flow hereafter over every land;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: of or belonging to a king, kingly, royal, regal.
Latin: Qui ad regem (vel reginam) pertinet, regis reginaeve

examples.original: Nomine enim tantum minus invidiosum, re ipsa prope atrocius quam regium esse;
examples.translation: For it was only in name, he said, that it was less hateful than that of a king;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec non et ratibus temptatur regia, qua se Protulit in medios audaci margine fluctus Luxuriosa domus.
examples.translation: They assailed the palace also by means of ships, at the point where the splendid pile projected with bold frontage right over the water.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ex his omnibus longe sunt humanissimi qui Cantium incolunt, quae regio est maritima omnis, neque multum a Gallica differunt consuetudine.
examples.translation: Of all the Britons the inhabitants of Kent, an entirely maritime district, are by far the most civilised, differing but little from the Gallic manner of life.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: foreign, strange, barbarous, opp. to Greek or Roman.
Latin: Peregrinus, alienus || Qui originem suam in alia terra habet

examples.original: Sed quod ius apud barbaros?
examples.translation: But what sense of justice could be expected from barbarians?
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: At barbaris consilium non defuit.
examples.translation: But the natives were not lacking in resource.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quod ubi accidit, barbari vehementissimo cursu refugerunt.
examples.translation: When this occurred, the natives fled away at a most furious speed.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: At a certain time, at one time, once, heretofore, formerly

examples.original: Scaenicos ludos et assidue et varii generis ac multifariam fecit, quondam et nocturnos accensis tota urbe luminibus.
examples.translation: He exhibited stage-plays continually, of various kinds and in many different places, sometimes even by night, lighting up the whole city.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Memini fuisse quondam in sermone nobilem patinam, in quam quicquid apud lautos solet diem ducere, properans in damnum suum popina congesserat;
examples.translation: I remember once hearing gossip about a notorious dish into which everything over which epicures love to dally had been heaped together by a cookshop that was fast rushing into bankruptcy;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Omnia deinde arbitrio militum acta: praetorii praefectos sibi ipsi legere, Plotium Firmum e manipularibus quondam, tum vigilibus praepositum et incolumi adhuc Galba partis Othonis secutum;
examples.translation: The soldiers’ will was henceforth supreme. The praetorians chose their own prefects,—Plotius Firmus, formerly a common soldier, but later chief of the city police, and a partisan of Otho even while Galba lived;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to bear or rest upon something.
Latin: ope alicuius rei melius stare

examples.original: Non est quod ad ulteriora nitaris;
examples.translation: There is no reason why you should be struggling on to something further;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nititur, ut profugae desint alimenta senectae: Heu!
examples.translation: He strives that my exiled old age may lack sustenance: ah!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Impia si nostros legisset Scylla libellos, Haesisset capiti purpura, Nise, tuo.
examples.translation: Had impious Scylla read my verse, the purple had stayed on thy head, O Nisus.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: pleasure, desire, eagerness, longing, fancy, inclination (cf.: appetitio, optatio, cupiditas, cupido, studium).

examples.original: Omnia feminea sunt ista libidine mota;
examples.translation: All those crimes were prompted by women’s lust;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Libidinis in feminas profusissimae, marum omnino expers.
examples.translation: He was immoderate in his passion for women, but wholly disinterested in male partners.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Volo luxuriam obiurgari, libidinem traduci, inpotentiam frangi.
examples.translation: I wish to see luxury rebuked, lust condemned, waywardness crushed out.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a stone (cf.: saxum, silex, cautes, cos, calculus).
Latin: Saxum
Latin: Miliarium

examples.original: Monte sub hoc lapidum tegitur Ballista sepultus;
examples.translation: Under this mountain of stones Ballista is covered and buried;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Artibus innumeris mens oppugnatur amantum, Ut lapis aequoreis undique pulsus aquis.
examples.translation: By innumerable arts are lovers’ feelings assailed, as the rock is beaten by waves on every side.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sepultus est iuxta viam Appiam ad quintum lapidem in monumento Q. Caecilii, avunculi sui.
examples.translation: He was buried near the fifth milestone of the Appian Way in the tomb of Quintus Caecilius, his maternal uncle.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

definitions: English: to delight, charm (only in the foll. passages)

examples.original: Delectat te nidor horum arte quaesitus.
examples.translation: You like the subtly devised flavour of these dishes.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non tantum delectatus, sed gavisus sum.
examples.translation: I was not merely pleased; I rejoiced.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid sit ergo, quod me delectaverit quaeris?
examples.translation: Do you ask, then, what it is that has pleased me?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that takes place repeatedly, often, or frequently, often, frequent (class.; syn.: celeber, creber).

examples.original: Frequens autem Massinissa finis territabat;
examples.translation: Massinissa, it is true, caused frequent alarms on their frontier;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Cessat omne studium et liberalia professi sine ulla frequentia desertis angulis praesident.
examples.translation: You need not wonder that diseases are beyond counting: count the cooks! All intellectual interests are in abeyance;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Conveniunt frequentes prima luce: ipse Tarquinius diem quidem servavit, sed paulo ante quam sol occideret venit.
examples.translation: There had been much talk in the council all day about various subjects.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: name of a Roman gens

examples.original: Fabioque ea provincia, Plautio Hernici evenere.
examples.translation: This campaign fell to Fabius, that against the Hernici to Plautius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fabii postera die arma capiunt; quo iussi erant conveniunt.
examples.translation: On the following day the Fabii arm and assemble at the designated place.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fabius, ut imperatum erat, non ita multum moratus in itinere cum legione occurrit.
examples.translation: Fabius and his legion, as ordered, after a brief delay met him on the march.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to bind together, connect, join, unite (very freq. in all perr. and species of composition); constr. with

examples.original: Inter se ista coniuncta sunt;
examples.translation: These tendencies are closely connected;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Antonium quaestorem cum legione duodecima sibi coniungit.
examples.translation: Marcus Antonius, the quartermaster-general, with the Twelfth Legion he attached to his own force.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Mihi crede, Caecili, non potest in accusando socios vere defendere is qui cum reo criminum societate coniunctus est.
examples.translation: Believe me, Caecilius, no man can honestly defend our allies as a prosecutor if he has been the ally and accomplice of the person prosecuted.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: saved, preserved, unharmed, safe, unhurt, uninjured, well, sound, etc.

examples.original: Non poterant salva esse, nisi vellent.
examples.translation: They could not survive except by desiring to do so.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cum salvum esse flentes sui respondissent, rogavit essentne fusi hostes.
examples.translation: His weeping followers told him that it was. He asked, were the enemy routed?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ne hunc quidem contempseris hominem, qui alieno beneficio esse salvus potest;
examples.translation: Nor need you despise a man who can gain salvation only with the assistance of another;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: olive-oil.
Latin: Liquidum unguinosum, praesertim ab olivis extractum
English: chances or tickets in a lottery
Latin: Pars capitalis, capitale

examples.original: Utrumque bellum Plautio sorte evenit.
examples.translation: Both wars were by lot assigned to Plautius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Si sortis, nullum crimen est in casu;
examples.translation: If you impute it to chance, then you have nothing to charge him with;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed tua sors levior, quoniam mors ultima poena est Nec metuenda viris.
examples.translation: But your lot is easier, since death, the utmost penalty, is not terrible to the brave.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to pick out, choose, elect

examples.original: Illyrici exercitus electi Celsum infestis pilis proturbant.
examples.translation: The picked troops from Illyria drove Celsus away at the point of their spears.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Non potest medicus per epistulas cibi aut balinei tempus eligere;
examples.translation: The physician cannot prescribe by letter the proper time for eating or bathing;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Missus et Celsus Marius ad electos Illyrici exercitus, Vipsania in porticu tendentis;
examples.translation: Celsus Marius was sent to the picked troops from Illyria, who were encamped in the Vipsanian Colonnade;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to creep, crawl (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Serpens, sitis, ardor harenae Dulcia virtuti;
examples.translation: Serpents, thirst, burning sand—all are welcomed by the brave;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Serpit enim nescio quo modo per omnium vitas amicitia nec ullam aetatis degendae rationem patitur esse expertem sui.
examples.translation: For it creeps imperceptibly, I know not how, into every life, and suffers no mode of existence to be devoid of its presence.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Serpsit tamen latius in proximos bellum, omnisque late Cephallenia, Zacynthos et quidquid insularum in eo mari inter Ceraunios montes iugumque Maleum Aetoli belli accessio fuerunt.
examples.translation: Hostilities, however, spread more widely among the neighbouring peoples; and all Cephallenia and Zacynthus and all the islands in that sea between the Ceraunian mountains and Cape Malea were involved in the Aetolian war.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to go over, to rise above, overtop, surmount.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Ostendes morbum posse superari vel certe sustineri.
examples.translation: You will be showing that a disease can be overcome, or at any rate endured.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tu licet et Thamyram superes et Amoebea cantu, Non erit ignotae gratia magna lyrae.
examples.translation: Though in song you may surpass Thamyras and Amoebeus, in an unknown lyre there is no great delight.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Idem iterum Sulla superavit: tum sine dubio habuit regalem potestatem, quamquam rem publicam recuperarat.
examples.translation: Once again Sulla prevailed; and then beyond all doubt he wielded a king’s power, albeit he had restored the republic.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to turn something away from a place, to avert, turn off, remove, etc. (opp. adverto).

examples.original: Eo vim Camilli ab Antio fortuna avertit.
examples.translation: To this quarter Fortune diverted the energies of Camillus, away from Antium.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Avertere omnes ab tanta foeditate spectaculi oculos.
examples.translation: All eyes were turned away from so dreadful a sight.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tota cogitatio a privatis commodis quam longissime aversa sit.
examples.translation: You need not look about for the reward of a just deed;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to acknowledge, confess, own, avow

examples.original: Ego certe confitebor inbecillitatem meam;
examples.translation: I shall admit my own weakness, at any rate;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Videor mihi in re confessa perdere operam;
examples.translation: It looks as if I were wasting time over something that is an acknowledged fact;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hisce ego auxiliis studentibus atque incitatis uti me, Laterensis, potuisse confiteor;
examples.translation: Of these helpers, Laterensis, so zealous and so enthusiastic, I admit that I might have availed myself.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: name of two Roman gentes, one patrician and one plebeian
Latin: Quae ad Claudiam gentem Romanam pertinet
Latin: Nomen et praenomen masculum
entries.grammaticalClass: like claudo and clodo, codex and caudex, plostrum and plaustrum
principalParts: like claudo and clodo, codex and caudex, plostrum and plaustrum

examples.original: Nam Claudium patruum non nisi in ludibrium reservavit.
examples.translation: As for his uncle Claudius, he spared him merely as a laughingstock.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Vercingetorix iubet portas claudi, ne castra nudentur.
examples.translation: Vercingetorix ordered the gates to be shut, lest the camp should be deserted.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ob hoc Claudia tribus adiecta est numerusque tribuum ampliatus est, ut essent xxi.
examples.translation: On this account the Claudian tribe was added and the number of tribes was increased to twenty-one.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: victory.
Latin: Actio vincendi

examples.original: Nec victoriam sperant nec reditum.
examples.translation: They have no hope of victory, no hope of returning.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed omnem prolationem ut inimicam victoriae suspectabant;
examples.translation: But his men suspected every delay as inimical to their victory;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: At ei qui ab Alesia processerant maesti prope victoria desperata se in oppidum receperunt.
examples.translation: But the Gauls who had come forth from Alesia, almost despairing of victory, sadly withdrew again into the town.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to strew, throw here and there, cast, hurl, or throw about, scatter; to bestrew; to sprinkle, spatter

examples.original: Per limitem viae sparguntur festinatione consectandi victores.
examples.translation: The victorious troops in their hasty pursuit were strung out along the sides of the road.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sparsit et missilia variarum rerum et panaria cum obsonio viritim divisit;
examples.translation: He also threw about gifts of various kinds, and gave each man a basket of prepared food.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Pulveris exigui sparget non longa vetustas Congeriem, bustumque cadet, mortisque peribunt Argumenta tuae.
examples.translation: For a short space of time will scatter the little heap of dust; the grave will fall in;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to creep, crawl (cf. serpo).

examples.original: Magna repente in ipsis operibus flamma exstitit.
examples.translation: A mighty flame suddenly shot forth in the midst of the works;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eodem anno, cum satis per se ipsum Samnitium bellum et defectio repens Lucanorum auctoresque defectionis, Tarentini, sollicitos haberent patres, accessit ut et Vestinus populus Samnitibus sese coniungeret.
examples.translation: This action was widely discussed in private conversations, without being made the subject, in that year, of any public deliberations;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Is diu sordidus, repente dives mutationem fortunae male tegebat, accensis egestate longa cupidinibus im moderatus et inopi iuventa senex prodigus.
examples.translation: His desires had been increased by long poverty, so that he now put no restraint upon himself, and after a youth of poverty became a prodigal old man.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English:  redupl.: descendidit, Valer. Antias ap.

examples.original: Descendisti ad Olympia, sed nemo praeter te;
examples.translation: You have entered as a contestant at the Olympic games, but none other besides you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: De castello descendunt, in fundum proficiscuntur.
examples.translation: Leaving the castle they set out for the estate.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Postremo quis hoc sibi persuaderet, sine certa re Ambiorigem ad eiusmodi consilium descendisse?
examples.translation: In fine, who could persuade himself that Ambiorix had engaged in such a design without sure cause?
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: To carry or bring out, to bring forth (class.; cf.: prodo, produco, adduco)
Latin: Vehere vel portare res ante se

examples.original: Profert se, laudari et aspici credit.
examples.translation: This spirit thrusts itself forward, confident of commendation and esteem.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non dest prolato ieiunus venditor auro.
examples.translation: By now mounds and hills are hidden;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Plato ipse ad senectutem se diligentia protulit.
examples.translation: Plato himself, by taking pains, advanced to old age.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to bloom, blossom, flower (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense; cf.: floresco, vigeo).

examples.original: O flores non plane fructuum sed spinarum!
examples.translation: Flowers indeed, but promising thorns, certainly not fruit!
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Quorum domus, cum honore et virtute florerent, signis et tabulis pictis erant vacuae;
examples.translation: These were men of high rank and eminent character,b but their houses were empty of statues and pictures;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Est prope purpureos colles florentis Hymetti Fons sacer et viridi caespite mollis humus: Silva nemus non alta facit;
examples.translation: Near the purple hills of flowery Hymettus there is a sacred spring and ground soft with green turf: trees of no great height form a grove;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to free the feet, i. e. from a snare; hence, in gen., to extricate, disengage, let loose, set free, liberate any thing entangled, involved
Latin: Ex impedimenta extricare; processum progressumve accelerare; festinare
Latin: Mittere

examples.original: Utique cum aliud tibi expediat, aliud mihi.
examples.translation: And this is particularly true when one thing is advantageous to you and another to me.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nunc initia causasque motus Vitelliani expediam.
examples.translation: I will now relate the origin and causes of the revolt of Vitellius.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Et harum quidem rerum facilis est et expedita distinctio.
examples.translation: These cases are perfectly simple and easy to distinguish.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: carefully; attentively; diligently

examples.original: Quae omnia ab his diligenter ad diem facta sunt.
examples.translation: All these commands were punctiliously and punctually performed.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eodem anno M. Valerius consul de provocatione legem tulit diligentius sanctam.
examples.translation: In the same year Marcus Valerius the consul proposed a law of appeal with stricter sanctions.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et eundem Popilium postea Lentulus in ambitus iudicio pro testimonio diligentissime laudat.
examples.translation: Moreover, Lentulus afterwards singled out this same Popilius for praise when giving evidence at a trial for bribery.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: leisure, vacant time, freedom from business (class.; opp. negotium; cf.: immunitas, vacatio): otio qui nescit uti plus negoti habet, Quam, etc., Enn. ap.

examples.original: Sed et ipsum otium absconde.
examples.translation: But at the same time conceal your retirement also.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Gloriari otio iners ambitio est.
examples.translation: To boast of our retirement is but idle self-seeking.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ergo ubi visus eris nostra medicabilis arte, Fac monitis fugias otia prima meis.
examples.translation: When therefore I shall find you amenable to my skill, obey my counsels and first of all shun leisure.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: juice, moisture
Latin: Latex praesertim plantae, frugis, &c

examples.original: Cetera saepe tamen potuere admissa negari, Et crimen nox est infitiata suum: Nostra notat fusco digitos iniuria suco Cortice contactas inficiente manus.
examples.translation: Yet other crimes when committed can often be denied, and night disavows her guilty deed: injury done to me marks the fingers with dark juice, and my bark stains the hands that touch it.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quique bibunt tenera dulces ab harundine sucos, Et qui tinguentes croceo medicamine crinem Fluxa coloratis astringunt carbasa gemmis, Quique suas struxere pyras vivique calentes Conscendere rogos.
examples.translation: Up rose the men who drink sweet juices from soft reeds; and those who colour their hair with saffron dye and loop up their robes of cotton with brighthued gems;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Reliqui arborum fructus vix specie figurave, non modo saporibus sucisque totiens permixtis atque insitis, enumerari queunt.
examples.translation: The other fruits found on trees can hardly be enumerated, from their diversity in shape and figure, without reference to their different flavours and juices, which have again been modified by repeated combinations and graftings.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: tyrant; an absolute ruler

examples.original: Maxime Siciliae fuisse tyrannos crediderim;
examples.translation: I am most inclined to think that they were Sicilian tyrants;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Atque hoc secunda victoria accidit; nam iam inclinatae erant tyrannorum copiae.
examples.translation: This happened in the full tide of victory, for the tyrants’ forces had already given way.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pelopidas

examples.original: Utque Milo, sub quo cruciata est Pisa tyranno, Vivus in occultas praecipiteris aquas.
examples.translation: And like Milo, under whose tyranny Pisa groaned, mayst thou be hurled alive into hidden waters.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to give aid to, to help, assist, support: aliquem.
Latin: Dare adiumentum sive auxilium

examples.original: Qui non habet, nihil a te adiuvabitur;
examples.translation: The latter will receive no benefit from you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quaeris quare te fuga ista non adiuvet?
examples.translation: Do you ask why such flight does not help you?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec mihi dederunt voluntatem adiuvandi me et patiendi omne tormentum;
examples.translation: All these things gave me the inclination to succour myself and to endure any torture;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: continuing throughout, continuous, unbroken, uninterrupted; constant, universal, general, entire, whole, perpetual
Latin: Semper manens, non interruptus

examples.original: Perpetuoque mihi sociatam foedere lecti Non patitur vivi funera flere viri.
examples.translation: And while I embrace the shattered fragments of my bark, he fights to possess my shipwrecked planks;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nihil enim dignum inventu iudicasset, quod non erat dignum perpetuo usu iudicaturus. Ponenda non sumeret.
examples.translation: He would not take up things which would have to be laid aside.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Omnes autem et dicuntur et habentur tyranni, qui potestate sunt perpetua in ea civitate quae libertate usa est.
examples.translation: But all men are called tyrants, and regarded as such, who hold permanent rule in a city which has enjoyed a democratic form of government.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

definitions: English: To draw violently, to drag
Latin: Saepe lubensque trahere, vi trahere
Latin: Frequenter tangere, manu versare

examples.original: Tractentur volnera nulla Sacra manu.
examples.translation: No other hand should meddle with the wounds of gods.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Durius tractandum est, ne animo male pareat.
examples.translation: The body should be treated more rigorously, that it may not be disobedient to the mind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic prout a nobis tractatus est, ita nos ipse tractat.
examples.translation: As we treat this spirit, so are we treated by it.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the slaves in a household, a household establishment, family servants, domestics (not = family, i. e. wife and children, domus, or mei, tui, sui, etc., but v. II. A. 3 infra)
Latin: Famuli domus cuncti
Latin: Res domus cunctae

examples.original: Sed agamus bonum patrem familiae;
examples.translation: But we should play the part of a careful householder;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Natus erat Valens Anagniae equestri familia.
examples.translation: Valens was born at Anagnia of an equestrian family.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sed tamen haec tibi est prima cum Plancio generis vestri familiaeque contentio, qua abs te vincitur.
examples.translation: However, the first comparison you make between yourself and Plancius is in the matter of birth and family.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: son of Jupiter and Alcmena, husband of Dejanira, and, after his deification

examples.original: Herculis magnum simulacrum in Capitolio positum dedicatumque.
examples.translation: The great statue of Hercules was set up and dedicated on the Capitol.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ubi nomen patremque ac patriam accepit, ”Iove nate, Hercules, salve,” inquit;
examples.translation: Upon learning his name, his father, and his birth-place, he exclaimed, ”Hail, Hercules, son of Jupiter!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Si Herculem vestrum dixeritis, porro reddemus; adsunt metalla, saxa nec desunt;
examples.translation: If you mention your Hercules, we shall straightway restore it to you;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: that exists or takes place in a continuous multitude, following closely together or one after another

examples.original: Allobroges crebris ad Rhodanum dispositis praesidiis magna cum cura et diligentia suos fines tuentur.
examples.translation: The Allobroges posted numerous detachments at intervals along the Rhone and protected their borders with great care and efficiency.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Periculi, quod differendo bello adimus, num oblivisci nos haec tam crebra Etruriae concilia de mittendis Veios auxiliis patiuntur?
examples.translation: Do the frequent debates in Etruria about the dispatch of succours to Veii allow us to forget it?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In civitate discordi et ob crebras principum mutationes inter libertatem ac licentiam incerta parvae quoque res magnis motibus agebantur.
examples.translation: In a state distracted by civil strife and wavering between liberty and licence because of the frequent changes of emperors, even smaller matters caused excitement.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: let loose, let fall.

examples.original: Omitto deditionem, quoniam de sponsione agitur;
examples.translation: But enough of surrender; we are talking of a guarantee.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In praesentia omnia praeter bellum omitti placere;
examples.translation: For the present he thought they should pay no attention to anything but the war.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cognoscendi morem eum tenuit, ut continuis actionibus omissis singillatim quaeque per vices ageret.
examples.translation: The procedure was, instead of continuous pleadings, to have each point presented separately by the parties in turn.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: Philip, the name of several kings of Macedonia, the most celebrated of whom was the son of Amyntas, and father of Alexander the Great
Latin: ‘Equos amans,’ nomen origine Graeca

examples.original: Hunc locum tenuit amicitiae apud Philippum annos septem.
examples.translation: This position of friendship with Philip Eumenes held for seven years.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Primum fuit belli consilium, ut in Albano monte festo die Latinarum Iulius Caesar et Marcius Philippus consules inter sacra et aras immolarentur.
examples.translation: The first plan of campaign was to murder the consuls, Julius Caesar and Marcius Philippus on the Alban Mount amid the sacrifices and altars at the celebration of the Latin Festival.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Hic peradulescentulus ad amicitiam accessit Philippi, Amyntae filii, brevique tempore in intimam pervenit familiaritatem; fulgebat enim iam in adulescentulo indoles virtutis.
examples.translation: Eumenes, when very young, became the friend of Philip, son of Amyntas, and soon grew very intimate with the king, being conspicuous even in his youth for his high character.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: Eagerly, impetuously, ardently, violently, earnestly, vehemently, etc.

examples.original: In hos igitur, quia vehementius agere nuntiabatur, non est mandata expeditio, sed sumpta.
examples.translation: The news of their unusual activity induced Caesar himself to undertake an expedition instead of entrusting it to another.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Quamquam quid est quod magis perspicuum sit quam non modo carum sibi quemque, verum etiam vehementer carum esse?
examples.translation: Yet what fact is more self-evident than that every man not merely of loves himself, but loves himself very much indeed?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quae cum ita sint, C. Manili, primum istam tuam et legem et voluntatem et sententiam laudo vehementissimeque comprobo;
examples.translation: Since this is so, Gaius Manilius, in the first place I applaud and most heartily commend this your law, your purpose and your proposal;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: fellowship, association, union, community, society

examples.original: Cum visum erit, distraham cum illo societatem.
examples.translation: When it seems proper, I shall sever my connexion with it.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Mihi crede, Caecili, non potest in accusando socios vere defendere is qui cum reo criminum societate coniunctus est.
examples.translation: Believe me, Caecilius, no man can honestly defend our allies as a prosecutor if he has been the ally and accomplice of the person prosecuted.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Haec est, inquam, societas, in qua omnia insunt, quae putant homines expetenda—honestas gloria tranquillitas animi atque iucunditas;
examples.translation: In such a partnership, I say, abide all things that men deem worthy of pursuit—honour and fame and delightful tranquillity of mind;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to couple together in the same relation, to connect in pairs, to pair, match, unite, join; constr. aliquid cum aliquā re, alicui rei

examples.original: Omnis auctoritas philosophiae, ut ait Theophrastus, consistit in beata vita comparanda;
examples.translation: The whole importance of philosophy lies, as Theophrastus says, in the attainment of happiness;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Si vis scire, quam nihil in illa mali sit, compara inter se pauperum et divitum vultus;
examples.translation: If you would know how little evil there is in poverty, compare the faces of the poor with those of the rich;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Illi comparatis ingentibus copiis eandem illam, quae fatalis Gnaeo Pompeio fuit, harenam insederant.
examples.translation: Brutus and Cassius, having collected vast forces, had occupied the same ground as had been fatal to Gnaeus Pompeius.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to deceive, disappoint
Latin: Quippiam exspectantem decipere
Latin: consilia cuiusdam annihilare

examples.original: Nec est mirum cum eo nasci illa, sine quo frustra nascerentur.
examples.translation: No wonder that living things are born with a gift whose absence would make birth useless.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quem postquam propius famulae videre fideles, Non ultra gemitus tacitos incessere fatum Permisere sibi, frustraque attollere terra Semianimem conantur eram;
examples.translation: When her faithful handmaids saw him close at hand, they dared not rail at destiny except with stifled groans, and tried in vain to lift their fainting mistress from the ground;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Quod nisi dux operis vatem frustratur Apollo, Aemulus est nostri maxima causa mali: At tu rivalem noli tibi fingere quemquam, Inque suo solam crede iacere toro.
examples.translation: Yet, unless Apollo, prince of the craft, deceives the bard, a rival is the chief cause of our malady: but picture no rival to yourself, and think she lies on her couch alone.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to break, burst, tear, rend, rive, rupture; to break asunder, burst in pieces, force open, etc. (very freq. and class.; a favorite word of the Aug. poets; cf. frango).

examples.original: Eo nisi corporibus armisque rupere cuneo viam.
examples.translation: Thither, by dint of main strength and arms, they forced their way with a wedge.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non proelia fessos Ulla vocant, certos non rumpunt classica somnos.
examples.translation: No battles call them from where they rest; no trumpet-call breaks their sound slumbers.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ipsa regit trepidum Pallas dextraque trementem Perseos aversi Cyllenida derigit harpen, Lata colubriferi rumpens confinia colli.
examples.translation: Pallas herself directed Perseus in his haste; her right hand guided the shaking scimitar of the Cyllenian which he held with his face averted;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to bring before; to present, offer; to show, exhibit (class.; cf. obicio, ostendo).
Latin: ante aliquem ferre
Latin: se, vitam suam, aliam personam aut rem periculis, aut morti obicere

examples.original: Manlius quoque ad restituendam aciem se ipse coram offert.
examples.translation: Manlius also showed himself among them, helping to restore the line;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vix etiam fueras paucas vitalis in horas, Obtulit invitae cum tibi Caesar opem;
examples.translation: Scarce hadst thou been like to live for even a few hours, when Caesar brought thee succour against thy will;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Qui se ultro morti offerant facilius reperiuntur quam qui dolorem patienter ferant.
examples.translation: It is easier to find men to fling themselves recklessly on death than men to endure pain patiently.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to call out or forth, to bring or send out, to wake or rouse up (freq. and class.; cf.: provoco, evoco; irrito, lacesso, invito).

examples.original: Merces seditionis proposita confestim seditionem excitavit.
examples.translation: The reward held out to sedition soon brought sedition to a head.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nunc te illa caelestis excitet flamma, nunc expergiscere vere.
examples.translation: Now is the time for that heaven-sent flame to quicken you!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Crassus equitum praefectos cohortatus, ut magnis praemiis pollicitationibusque suos excitarent, quid fieri velit ostendit.
examples.translation: Crassus exhorted the cavalry commanders to incite their men by great rewards and promises, and showed what he would have done.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: rich (cf.: pecuniosus, beatus, locuples, opulens, opulentus).
Latin: Pecuniosus, multam pecuniam possidens
Latin: Opulentus, abundans re

examples.original: An dives, omnes quaerimus, nemo, an bonus.
examples.translation: All ask how great my riches are, but none Whether my soul is good.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: At Zeno eum non beatum modo sed etiam divitem dicere ausus est.
examples.translation: But Zeno dared to say that a wise beggar was not only happy but also wealthy.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Si vis scire, quam nihil in illa mali sit, compara inter se pauperum et divitum vultus;
examples.translation: If you would know how little evil there is in poverty, compare the faces of the poor with those of the rich;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: not to suffer a thing to take place, not to permit, to advise against, oppose, forbid, prohibit a thing; and, with a personal object, not to permit one

examples.original: Summitti te ac deprimi veto.
examples.translation: I forbid you to be cast down or depressed.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fata vetant, murique vicem Fortuna tuetur.
examples.translation: Fate is against them, and Fortune performs the office of a wall.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Drusus ulterius egit et vetuit transire Danuvium.
examples.translation: Drusus forced them still further and prevented them from recrossing the Danube.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a race, breed, generation
Latin: saecŭl|um, -ī neut. {| width="99%" valign="top" style="vertical-align:top" cellpadding="5px" cellspacing="5px" |width="33%" style="border-right:1px solid darkgray; vertical-align:top"|

examples.original: Habes aditum mansurae in saecula famae.
examples.translation: Here is your opportunity for undying fame.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Idem est autem omni saeculo, quod sat est.
examples.translation: But in every age, what is enough remains the same.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: O quantum erat saeculi decus, imperatorem triumphalem, censorium, quod super omnia haec est, Catonem uno caballo esse contentum et ne toto quidem!
examples.translation: For part of the animal was preempted by the baggage that hung down on either flank.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: white
Latin: Color ninguis. Haud ater; candidus sine nitore
Latin: Color ninguis. Haud ater; candidus sine nitore. Color autem albus praecipue decorus deo est - Cic. De Legibus 2.45 albus aqua fontesque Velini - Verg. Aeneid 7.511

examples.original: Ascani regnum Albae et deinceps Silviorum.
examples.translation: Reign of Ascanius, and after him of the Silvii, at Alba.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Libri X Periocha Coloniae deductae sunt Sora et Alba et Carsioli.
examples.translation: Summaries Summary of Book X Colonies were planted at Sora, at Alba, and at Carseoli.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Albam in Aequos sex milia colonorum scripta: Sora agri Volsci fuerat, sed possederant Samnites;
examples.translation: Sora had belonged to the territory of the Volsci, but the Samnites had got possession of it;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A portion, point, or space of time, a time, season, period

examples.original: Atquin inde Mariana, inde Sullana tempestas.
examples.translation: Why, it was from this the Marian and Sullan disturbances arose.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Gubernatorem in tempestate, in acie militem intellegas.
examples.translation: You learn to know a pilot in a storm, a soldier in the battle-line.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Huic tantae tempestati cum se consules obtulissent, facile experti sunt parum tutam maiestatem sine viribus esse.
examples.translation: The consuls, exposed to this furious tempest, were quickly convinced of the insecurity of majesty when unaccompanied with force.
examples.author: Livy
