examples.original: Caecina e complexu Vitellii multo cum honore digressus partem equitum ad occupandam Cremonam praemisit.
examples.translation: Caecina, departing from the embraces of Vitellius with great honours, sent a part of his horse ahead to occupy Cremona.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Qui sint hi quaeris? Qui omnes iam adfectus ac vitia posuerunt, quae erant complectenda, didicerunt, sed illis adhuc inexperta fiducia est.
examples.translation: These, if you ask me, are men who have already laid aside all passions and vices, who have learned what things are to be embraced;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: O acerbam mihi, iudices, memoriam temporis illius et loci, cum hic in me incidit, cum complexus est conspersitque lacrimis nec loqui prae maerore potuit!
examples.translation: How bitter to me, gentlemen, is the memory of that time and that place, when he fell upon my neck, embraced me, bedewed me with his tears, and was dumb for very grief!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to entangle, ensnare, to shackle, hamper, hinder, hold fast (cf.: praepedio, implico, illigo, irretio, illaqueo).

examples.original: Ibi impedire opus conatos hostes fundit fugatque;
examples.translation: There, when the enemy sought to hinder the work, he defeated and routed them;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ea ne impedirent tribuni dictatoris obstitit metus.
examples.translation: The awe in which the tribunes held the dictator prevented them from interfering with the trial.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed loca difficilia hosti quaesita ipsos tum sua fraude impediebant.
examples.translation: And so, very few were able to get off;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a goddess: Juno sancta dearum, Enn. ap.
Latin: Deus femina

examples.original: Solacia fati Carthago Mariusque tulit, pariterque iacentes Ignovere deis.
examples.translation: Carthage and Marius both drew consolation for their destiny ;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Iuppiter optimus maximus, Iuno regina et Minerva, alii di deaeque obsidentur;
examples.translation: Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Queen Juno, and Minerva, and the other gods and goddesses, are beleaguered;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cura dabit faciem; facies neglecta peribit, Idaliae similis sit licet illa deae.
examples.translation: Care will give good looks: looks neglected go to waste though they resemble the Idalian goddess.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to advise, recommend, exhort, urge, persuade (freq. and class.; cf.: hortor, moneo).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; si, sum, 2

examples.original: Seducere me debeo et quid suadeam circumspicere.
examples.translation: I ought to go into retirement, and consider what sort of advice I should give you.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His interrogationibus suasuri aut dissuasuri sumus?
examples.translation: Shall we be supporting it, or opposing it, if we use these syllogisms?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec diutius Galba cunctatus speciosiora suadentibus accessit.
examples.translation: Galba did not delay any longer, but favoured those who offered the more specious advice.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: witness, evidence, attestation, testimony (oral or written)

examples.original: Haec in eo iudicio facta sunt, in quo, si nihil aliud, Cato testimonium dixerat.
examples.translation: All this was done at the trial in which Cato gave evidence, although that was his sole part therein.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et eundem Popilium postea Lentulus in ambitus iudicio pro testimonio diligentissime laudat.
examples.translation: Moreover, Lentulus afterwards singled out this same Popilius for praise when giving evidence at a trial for bribery.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Huic ego testi gratias agam, quod et in re misericordem se praebuerit et in testimonio religiosum.
examples.translation: I will ask this witness to accept my thanks for having shown himself merciful in his conduct and scrupulous in his evidence.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to that thing, to that subject in discourse, etc.

examples.original: Non ire istuc, sed errare est.
examples.translation: What you suggest is not travelling; it is mere tramping.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed quare istuc malum adstringo?
examples.translation: But why do I confine the scope of this evil?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Audisse te scribis Serapionem philosophum, cum istuc adplicuisset: ”Solet magno cursu verba convellere, quae non effundit una, sed premit et urguet.
examples.translation: You write me that you heard a lecture by the philosopher Serapio,a when he landed at your present place of residence.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: this, the very (person or thing).

examples.original: Quod istic credulitatis tuae damnum est?
examples.translation: And what harm does it do to you to give such credence?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: T. Quincti, quocumque istic loco seu volens seu invitus constitisti, si dimicandum erit, tum tu in novissimos te recipito;
examples.translation: Titus Quinctius, whatever be your position over there—whether you have taken it voluntarily or against your will,—if we must do battle, do you retire to the rear;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nam adhuc, meo fortasse vitio, quid ego quaeram non perspicis.” ”Istic sum,” inquit, ”exspectoque quid ad id quod quaerebam respondeas.”
examples.translation: For so far, though perhaps I am to blame, you do not grasp the point of my question.” ”I am all attention,” he replied,” and await your reply to my inquiry.”
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: warm
Latin: Magnae temperaturae (thermodynamicae)

examples.original: Massa per se nec calida nec frigida est;
examples.translation: An object is not by its own essence either hot or cold;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec tibi sol calidus, nec sit tibi lucida Phoebe, Destituant oculos sidera clara tuos.
examples.translation: May the sun not be warm for thee, nor Phoebe bright, may the clear stars fail thy vision.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nam prior e campis ut conspicit amne soluto Rumpi Caesar iter, calida proclamat ab ira: ”Non satis est muris latebras quaesisse pavori?
examples.translation: Caesar got the start of him: from the plain he saw that they were letting loose the river to interrupt his march; and in hot anger he cried out: ”Cowards!
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: that contains nothing, empty, void. vacant.

examples.original: Inbecilli fluvidique inter vana constitimus ;
examples.translation: We are weak, watery beings standing in the midst of unrealities;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hinc aemulatio ducibus: Caecina ut foedum ac maculosum, ille ut tumidum ac vanum inridebant.
examples.translation: This caused rivalry between the generals. Caecina made sport of Valens as a shameful and disgraceful character;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Hos delectat assentatio, his fictus ad ipsorum voluntatem sermo cum adhibetur, orationem illam vanam testimonium esse laudum suarum putant.
examples.translation: Such men delight in flattery, and when a complimentary speech is fashioned to suit their fancy they think the empty phrase is proof of their own merits.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: pertaining to heaven or to the heavens, found in heaven, coming from heaven, etc., heavenly, celestial (class. and very freq.)
Latin: Qui ad caelum pertinet

examples.original: Sic huius, ut caelestium, stata magnitudo est.
examples.translation: Her stature, like that of the stars in the heavens, is fixed.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nunc te illa caelestis excitet flamma, nunc expergiscere vere.
examples.translation: Now is the time for that heaven-sent flame to quicken you!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nisi enim id faceret, cur Plato Aegyptum peragravit ut a sacerdotibus barbaris numeros et caelestia acciperet?
examples.translation: Were it not so, why did Plato travel through Egypt to learn arithmetic and astronomy from barbarian priests?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To salt down, to salt: pernas, Cato ap.

examples.original: In nemus et saltus thalamo regina relicto Fertur, ut Aonio concita Baccha deo.
examples.translation: Leaving her bower the queen hies her to the woods and glens, like a Bacchanal sped by the Aonian god.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Aut ut Trinacrius salias super ora gigantis, Plurima qua flammas Sicanis Aetna vomit.
examples.translation: Or like the Trinacrian mayst thou leap into the giant’s mouth, where in full might Sicanian Aetna vomits flames.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hic ne intrare posset, saltum in quo Ciliciae portae sunt sitae Datames praeoccupare studuit.
examples.translation: To prevent him from entering the country, Datames wished to occupy the wooded gorge in which the Cilician Gates are situated;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Datames

definitions: English: To go to a place or person in great numbers or often, to frequent, to fill

examples.original: Privatim quoque id sacrum celebratum est.
examples.translation: They also observed the rite in their homes.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vergini patris sponsique Icili populare nomen celebrabatur.
examples.translation: Their acquaintance were led to support the girl out of regard for them;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Longe illi triplex murus totidemque arces, portus ille marmoreus et fons celebratus Arethusae;
examples.translation: Of no avail were its triple walls, its three citadels, its harbour of marble and the celebrated Fountain of Arethusa;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: justice, equity, righteousness, uprightness

examples.original: Res illa plena iustitiae, sapientiae, dignitatis.
examples.translation: His act breathed a spirit of justice, sagacity, and high-mindedness;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Veneranda enim sunt iustitia, pietas, fides, fortitudo, prudentia;
examples.translation: For reverence is due to justice, duty, loyalty, bravery, and prudence;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque et supplicationes ob rem bene gestam consulis nomine decernunt et iustitium remittitur quod fuerat dies duodeviginti;
examples.translation: They accordingly voted a thanksgiving for the victory, in the consul’s name, and reopened the courts, which had been closed for eighteen days.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to frighten, affright, put in fear or dread, to alarm, terrify.

examples.original: Terruerant satis haec pavidam praesagia plebem;
examples.translation: These forebodings were enough to alarm and terrify the populace;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Itaque istius vaecordissimi mentem cura metuque terrebant.
examples.translation: They therefore wrought upon his insensate mind with panic and apprehension.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Et uno proelio peractum erat bellum; iam enim urbem ipsam terrebat obsidio;
examples.translation: The war was thus finished by a single battle, and a siege already threatened the city itself;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: newly, lately, recently, not long ago.
Latin: Non longo ante tempore
Latin: de longiori ante tempore, paucis ante saeculis

examples.original: Nuper in ludo bestiariorum unus e Germanis, cum ad matutina spectacula pararetur, secessit ad exonerandum corpus;
examples.translation: For example, there was lately in a training-school for wild-beast gladiators a German, who was making ready for the morning exhibition;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec eodem tempore Caesari mandata referebantur, et legati ab Aeduis et a Treveris veniebant: Aedui questum, quod Harudes, qui nuper in Galliam transportati essent, fines eorum popularentur;
examples.translation: At the same hour in which this message was brought back to Caesar, deputies arrived from the Aedui and the Treveri.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quid aliud infestis patribus nuper Eprius Marcellus quam eloquentiam suam opposuit, qui accinctus et minax disertam quidem sed inexercitatam et eius modi certaminum rudem Helvidii sapientiam elusit?
examples.translation: Ready for the fray and breathing defiance, he could parry the blows of the philosopher Helvidius, who for all his clever speaking was, as regards that sort of contest, an inexperienced novice.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: truth, truthfulness, verity; the true or real nature, reality (always abstract; cf.: verum, vera).
Latin: Quod verum est

examples.original: Id enim tam supra nos est quam ipsa veritas.
examples.translation: For to do that is as far beyond our ken as truth itself.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Neque enim habent congruum libertati, nisi quod habent congruum veritati.
examples.translation: For they contain nothing consonant with liberty, unless what they contain consonant with truth.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Si probationes necessariae sunt, et decreta, quae veritatem argumentis colligunt.
examples.translation: If proofs are necessary, so are doctrines; for doctrines deduce the truth by reasoning.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to send out, send forth
Latin: Extra mittere, edere

examples.original: Magno emisse illum non est quod mireris;
examples.translation: You need not wonder that he paid high prices for these slaves;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Subito Labienus duabus portis omnem equitatum emittit;
examples.translation: Suddenly from two gates Labienus launched forth all his cavalry;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Cor iacet, et saniem per hiantes viscera rimas Emittunt, produntque suas omenta latebras.
examples.translation: The heart is flattened, the entrails exude corrupted blood through gaping cracks, and the caul reveals its hiding-place.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to point out, as with the finger; to indicate, designate, show (freq. and class.).
Latin: Aperte monstrare, quod digito fit, ostendere

examples.original: Inprobum risus, insanum vultus habitusque demonstrat.
examples.translation: The scamp is shown up by his laugh;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Caesar Atrebas venit, quem supra demonstraveram a Caesare in Britanniam praemissum.
examples.translation: Commius the Atrebatian, who, as shown above, had been sent forward by Caesar into Britain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ac si tibi nemo responsurus esset, tamen ipsam causam, ut ego arbitror, demonstrare non posses.
examples.translation: Even if no one were going to reply to you, I cannot believe that you would be able to establish your own case.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: That announces, signifies, makes known; announcing, informing
Latin: Relatus rerum recentium
Latin: Qui nuntiat

examples.original: Diem ad proficiscendum nuntius habuit;
examples.translation: The messenger had a day for the journey.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Eo nuntio erecti patres, erecta plebes.
examples.translation: These tidings cheered the Fathers and encouraged the plebs.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nuntium de caede Galbae et imperio Othonis Fabius Valens in civitate Leucorum accepit.
examples.translation: Fabius Valens heard the news of Galba’s death and the accession of Otho in the state of the Leuci.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: To go below or under
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; cessi, cessum, 3

examples.original: Eo successu studia populi aucta;
examples.translation: This success increased the enthusiasm of the people.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Numquam enim non succedent occupationes novae;
examples.translation: For there is never a moment when fresh employments will not come along;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quantum ad successus accesserit, accedet ad metus.
examples.translation: But all that is added to your successes will be added to your fears.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: empty, void, free, clear, devoid of, without something (freq. and class.; cf. inanis.)

examples.original: Vacuo illi loco opus est.
examples.translation: It needs plenty of free room.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quorum domus, cum honore et virtute florerent, signis et tabulis pictis erant vacuae;
examples.translation: These were men of high rank and eminent character,b but their houses were empty of statues and pictures;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Vulgus tamen vacuum curis et sine falsi verique discrimine solitas adulationes edoctum clamore et vocibus adstrepebat;
examples.translation: Yet the populace, careless and unable to distinguish between truth and falsehood, shouted loud the usual flattery, as it had been taught to do;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: palpable, clear, plain, apparent, evident, manifest.

examples.original: Ratio autem non impletur manifestis;
examples.translation: But reason is not satisfied by obvious facts;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quod dico conabor facere manifestum.
examples.translation: I shall endeavour to make clear what I mean.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid? aviam tuam, Oppianice, Dinaeam, cui tu es heres, pater tuus non manifesto necavit?
examples.translation: Again, is it not patent, Oppianicus, that your father murdered your grandmother, Dinea, whose heir you are?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to have and hold, to be master of

examples.original: Inmodicas possedit opes, sed plura retentis Intulit.
examples.translation: He snatched the sword; but he knew how to lay it down.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Paupertas enim est non quae pauca possidet, sed quae multa non possidet;
examples.translation: For poverty does not mean the possession of little, but the non-possession of much;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Albam in Aequos sex milia colonorum scripta: Sora agri Volsci fuerat, sed possederant Samnites;
examples.translation: Sora had belonged to the territory of the Volsci, but the Samnites had got possession of it;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a fish.
Latin: Animal nans aquaticum, praesertim quod non mammiferum est

examples.original: Hi iaculo pisces, illi capiuntur ab hamis: Hos cava contento retia fune trahunt.
examples.translation: These fish are caught with spears, those with hooks; these ones are dragged with taut ropes in bulging nets.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: having or keeping a proper measure, moderate (cf. mediocris); esp. in behavior, modest, temperate; also, of size, moderate-sized; middling, ordinary, mean, bad

examples.original: Habet pecuniae cupiditatem, sed modicam.
examples.translation: He has a craving for money, although in a moderate degree.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Supellex modica, non multa, ut in neutram partem conspici posset.
examples.translation: His furniture was modest, not abundant, so that it attracted attention in neither direction.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Ex plurimis maximisque honoribus praeter paucos et modicos non recepit.
examples.translation: Of many high honours he accepted only a few of the more modest.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: one who is chosen at the same time with another

examples.original: Collega ei T. Quinctius datur.
examples.translation: For colleague they gave him Titus Quinctius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ii tres collegas sibi creaverunt.
examples.translation: These appointed three others to be their colleagues.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Collegae funus quanto tum potuit apparatu fecit;
examples.translation: His colleague’s funeral he celebrated with all the pomp then possible;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: longing, desiring, desirous, eager, in a good and bad sense, wishing, loving, fond, etc. (very freq. and class.); constr. with

examples.original: Uter igitur nostrum est cupidior dicti?
examples.translation: Which of us, pray, is the more alert for the pun?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Patrum interim animos certamen regni ac cupido versabat.
examples.translation: The senators meanwhile were engaged in a struggle for the coveted kingship.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quis est enim in quo sit cupiditas, quin recte cupidus dici possit?
examples.translation: On your principle there is no form of desire whose possessor could not be morally approved.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a shapeless, huge, heavy mass, huge bulk.

examples.original: Sed in tanta mole belli plerumque cunctatio;
examples.translation: But a war of such scope can never be undertaken without hesitation;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Hic Opiterginis moles onerata colonis Constitit;
examples.translation: Here the hulk halted, weighed down with men of Opitergium;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Neque enim de more carinas Extendunt puppesque levant, sed firma gerendis Molibus insolito contexunt robora ductu.
examples.translation: They built no long hulls, no high sterns, as the custom is, but joined stout planks together on unwonted lines to carry heavy structures.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a wandering.

examples.original: Victoriam illi proelio error dedit.
examples.translation: A mistake decided the victory in this battle.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed inpatientem me esse tanti erroris dissimulare non possum.
examples.translation: But I cannot disguise my impatience with such a misconception as yours.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Cuius avari modum ignorant, etiam non avari usum. ”Tolle,” inquit, ”errores;
examples.translation: Then comes the reply: ”Do away with error, and your precepts become unnecessary.” That is wrong;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: cold, cool, chill, chilling
Latin: Parvae temperaturae (thermodynamicae)

examples.original: Massa per se nec calida nec frigida est;
examples.translation: An object is not by its own essence either hot or cold;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nondum me committo frigidae verae, adhuc rigorem eius infringo.
examples.translation: I do not yet trust myself to a bath which is absolutely cold;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vix proelia Caesar Senserat, elatus specula quae prodidit ignis: Invenit inpulsos presso iam pulvere muros, Frigidaque, ut veteris, deprendit signa ruinae.
examples.translation: Caesar had hardly been aware of the fighting; the news of it was conveyed to him by a fire-signal from a lofty tower.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to commit to one for preservation, protection, etc., to intrust to one's charge, commit to one'

examples.original: Cur deinde Metrodori liberos commendas?
examples.translation: And secondly, why do you provide for the children of Metrodorus?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum L. Metellus in provinciam profectus est, tum isti bene commendati cum Metello una proficiscuntur.
examples.translation: When Lucius Metellus left for the province, they left with him, recommended strongly to his protection.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to bring up to one's mind, to put one in mind of (in a friendly manner), to remind, suggest, advise, warn, admonish
Latin: Facere aliquem memorem alicuius rei; ferre in memoriam alicuius, ferre in mentem alicuius

examples.original: Tunc enimvero deorum ira admonuit.
examples.translation: Then at last the anger of the gods taught him wisdom.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Adversae deinde res admonuerunt religionum.
examples.translation: Adversity then turned our thoughts upon religion.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nunc quoque te admonebo: morbi sunt inveterata vitia et dura, ut avaritia, ut ambitio;
examples.translation: And I shall remind you once more: the diseases are hardened and chronic vices, such as greed and ambition;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To lead or bring back, to conduct back (very freq. and class.; syn. redigo).

examples.original: Item Marcus Mettius repertus et ad eum reductus est.
examples.translation: Marcus Mettius also was discovered and brought back to Caesar.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quam ob causam Datames primum experiri voluit ut sine armis propinquum ad officium reduceret.
examples.translation: That being the case, Datames wished first to try to recall his kinsman to his duty without resort to arms.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Datames

examples.original: Solis occasu suas copias Ariovistus multis et illatis et acceptis vulneribus in castra reduxit.
examples.translation: At sunset, when many blows had been dealt and taken, Ariovistus led his forces back to camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: not according to the standard.

examples.original: Non erat obscurum quid homo improbus ac nefarius cogitaret;
examples.translation: The rascal’s immoral plan was not obscure;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Dum fuit Atrides una contentus, et illa Casta fuit: vitio est improba facta viri.
examples.translation: While Atrides was content with one, she was chaste also; she was made wicked by her husband’s sin.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Haec homines improbi ad quosdam viros fortes longe aliter atque a me dicta erant detulerunt.
examples.translation: These complaints were reported by scoundrels to certain worthy gentlemenb in terms very far removed from those which I had used.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: made unsafe, disturbed, molested, infested; unquiet, unsafe (class.; cf. infensus).

examples.original: Alter consul Fabius infestus privatim Papirio erat;
examples.translation: The other consul, Fabius, had a private grudge against Papirius;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Illyrici exercitus electi Celsum infestis pilis proturbant.
examples.translation: The picked troops from Illyria drove Celsus away at the point of their spears.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ab triumpho exercitum in agrum Vescinum, quia regio ea infesta ab Samnitibus erat, hibernatum duxit.
examples.translation: After triumphing, Papirius led his army into the country of the Vescini—a district infested by the Samnites—to pass the winter.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to see forwards or before one's self, to see in the distance, to discern, descry (very rare)
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; vīdi, vīsum, 2

examples.original: Nero a pessimo quoque semper desiderabitur: mihi ac tibi providendum est ne etiam a bonis desideretur.
examples.translation: Nero will always be missed by the worst citizens; you and I must take care that he be not missed also by the good.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Missi ad Parthum Armeniumque legati, provisumque ne versis ad civile bellum legionibus terga nudarentur.
examples.translation: He was firmly opposed to extravagant gifts to the soldiers and therefore had a better army.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Haec ubi sunt provisa duci, tunc agmina victor Non armata trahens sed pacis habentia voltum, Tecta petit patriae.
examples.translation: When he had taken these precautions, the victorious general led his troops, unarmed and wearing the aspect of peace, to the city of his birth.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a load, burden (cf. pondus).

examples.original: Magnam partem oneris sui posuit.
examples.translation: It has laid aside the greater part of its load.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec omnia in dites a pauperibus inclinata onera. Deinde est honos additus;
examples.translation: All these burdens were shifted from the shoulders of the poor to those of the rich.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nam mihi non facit fidem tam multorum onerum, quae aliquando numeraveram, tam repentina depositio, quamvis te accepisse litteras meas non dubitem, quarum rescripta non habeo.
examples.translation: I can hardly believe I have so speedily discharged tasks I had once reckoned so numerous. Yet I am sure you must have had letters from me, to which I have received no answers.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to raise or

examples.original: Ille dat consilia magnifica et erecta.
examples.translation: He it is that gives noble and upright counsel.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eo nuntio erecti patres, erecta plebes.
examples.translation: These tidings cheered the Fathers and encouraged the plebs.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Animus esse debet alacer et fidens et super omnia erectus.
examples.translation: The very soul must be happy and confident, lifted above every circumstance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: capability, possibility, power, means, opportunity; skill, ability to do any thing easily (class.; syn.: dotes, virtutes, ingenium, indoles).
Latin: aliquid facere posse

examples.original: Omnibus hic labor meus propositus est, quicumque hac facultate defensionis contenti esse possunt.
examples.translation: These my endeavours are placed at the disposal of all who can find satisfaction in my powers of advocacy.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Erat autem in Caesare cum facultas atque elegantia summa scribendi, tum verissima scientia suorum consiliorum explicandorum.
examples.translation: Caesar possessed not only the greatest facility and refinement of style, but also the surest skill in explaining his own plans.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Amicorum in se tuendo caruit facultatibus, fide ad alios sublevandos saepe sic usus est, ut iudicari possit omnia ei cum amicis fuisse communia.
examples.translation: In aiding others, on the contrary, he made such use of their trust in him that one might suppose that he and his friends shared all their possessions in common.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Epaminondas

definitions: English: a smell, scent

examples.original: Inde in omnem vitam unguento abstinemus, quoniam optimus odor in corpore est nullus.
examples.translation: That is why I have also throughout my life avoided perfumes;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nam et ante iam fama et nunc fratres, qui venerunt a vobis, Eustasius et Andreas bonum Christi odorem de vestra sancta conversatione ad nos adtulerunt.
examples.translation: For a good savour of Christ from your holy conduct had already reached me, first through rumour and now through the brethren, Eustasius and Andrew, who have come from you.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Ea conluvio mixtorum omnis generis animantium et odore insolito urbanos et agrestem confertum in arta tecta aestu ac vigiliis angebat, ministeriaque in vicem ac contagio ipsa volgabant morbos.
examples.translation: This conflux of all kinds of living things distressed the citizens with its strange smells, while the country-people, being packed into narrow quarters, suffered greatly from the heat and want of sleep;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a bail, security, surety

examples.original: Reliquae Pergamenae naves cum adversarios premerent acrius, repente in eas vasa fictilia de quibus supra mentionem fecimus conici coepta sunt.
examples.translation: When the other Pergamene ships began to press their opponents too hard, on a sudden the earthenware jars of which I have spoken began to be hurled at them.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

examples.original: Ibi vadis repertis partem suarum copiarum traducere conati sunt, eo consilio ut, si possent, castellum, cui praeerat Quintus Titurius legatus, expugnarent pontemque interscinderent;
examples.translation: There they found fords, and endeavoured to throw part of their forces across, intending if they could to storm the fort commanded by the lieutenant-general, Quintus Titurius, and break down the bridge;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: go forth or away, to depart, retire, withdraw (freq. and class.; cf.: discedo, deficio, destituo, desero, linquo, relinquo).

examples.original: Ac nescio an nimis undique eam minimisque rebus muniendo modum excesserint.
examples.translation: Perhaps the pains they took to safeguard it, even in trivial details, may have been excessive.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His condicionibus composita pace exercitum ab Ianiculo deduxit Porsinna et agro Romano excessit.
examples.translation: On these terms peace was made, and Porsinna led his army down from Janiculum and evacuated the Roman territory.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mihi quidem numquam persuaderi potuit animos dum in corporibus essent mortalibus vivere, cum excessissent ex eis emori;
examples.translation: I, for my part, could never be persuaded that souls, which lived while they were in human bodies, perished when they left those bodies;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: rain, heavy or violent rain, a rain-storm, shower of rain, pelting or pouring rain (cf.: pluvia, nimbus).
Latin: Pluvia; nimbus

examples.original: Non caeli nox illa fuit: latet obsitus aer Infernae pallore domus nimbisque gravatus Deprimitur, fluctusque in nubibus accipit imbrem.
examples.translation: The darkness was not the common darkness of night: the heavens were hidden and veiled with the dimness of the infernal regions, and weighed down by clouds;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ego autem oratorem, sicut locupletem ac lautum patrem familiae, non eo tantum volo tecto tegi quod imbrem ac ventum arceat, sed etiam quod visum et oculos delectet;
examples.translation: My own view is that the orator, like a prosperous and well-found householder, ought to live in a house that is not only wind and weather proof, but pleasing also to the eye;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: that which heals again; a cure, remedy (class. and freq.).
Latin: Medicamentum, res qua morbus sanatur
Latin: Adiumentum, res quae quandam difficultatem expedit

examples.original: Ad haec ergo remedia te confer.
examples.translation: These, then, are the remedies to which you should have recourse.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Turpissimum autem est in homine prudente remedium maeroris lassitudo maerendi.
examples.translation: I should prefer you to abandon grief, rather than have grief abandon you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Servilius, lenibus remediis aptior, concitatos animos flecti quam frangi putabat cum tutius tum facilius esse.
examples.translation: Servilius, more inclined to gentle measures, believed that it was safer, as well as easier, to assuage their fury than to quell it.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a thinking, considering, deliberating; thought, reflection, meditation (in good prose, and very freq.).

examples.original: Quod nullius mortalium cogitatio recipit.
examples.translation: But no human being, on serious consideration, admits this idea.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non mortem timemus, sed cogitationem mortis.
examples.translation: We do not fear death; we fear the thought of death.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque ad patriam liberandam omni ferebatur cogitatione.
examples.translation: In consequence, all his thoughts were set upon freeing his country.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Alcibiades

definitions: English: to lay away, to put or place aside; to lay, put, or set down; to lay, place, set, deposit (freq. in all periods and sorts of writing).—Constr. with
Latin: Deorsum ponere
Latin: pro plantare terrae committere

examples.original: Stagna avidi texere soli laxaeque paludes Depositum, Fortuna, tuum;
examples.translation: Engulfing quicksands and spongy marshes hid the secret that Fortune had placed there;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nulla recantatas deponent pectora curas, Nec fugiet vivo sulpure victus amor.
examples.translation: No hearts will lay aside their passion by enchantment, nor love flee vanquished by strong sulphur.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Illic depositis habitat Concordia telis: Illo, crede mihi, Gratia nata loco est.
examples.translation: Therein dwells Concord when the fight is o’er; there, believe me, was Reconciliation born.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to recall an object to memory in all its particulars.

examples.original: Non opus est multa commemorare.
examples.translation: There is no need to give many illustrations.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: De quo quid ego plura commemorem?
examples.translation: About this I need surely say very little.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed quid ego longinqua commemoro?
examples.translation: But why do I remind you of events in distant places?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to lift up, raise, elevate (syn.: extollo, erigo).

examples.original: Ille caput labens et iam languentia colla Viso patre levat;
examples.translation: At sight of his father the son raised his sinking head and failing neck;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Asperitas autem vocis fit ab asperitate principiorum, et item levor levore creatur.
examples.translation: The roughness of voice, moreover, comes from roughness of the elements, as also smoothness from smoothness.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Ante diem morior, sed nulla paelice laesa: Hoc faciet positae te mihi, terra, levem.
examples.translation: Now goes my spirit out upon the air whose name I once suspected: I faint, I die;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a turning against. *

examples.original: Exultat et mihi facit controversiam de senectute.
examples.translation: It is alert; it takes issue with me on the subject of old age;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quum de iure et legitimis hominum controversiis loquimur, et in his rebus vim nominamus, pertenuis vis intelligi debet.
examples.translation: When we are speaking of rights and disputes at law and in that connexion use the word ”force,” a very slight degree of force should be understood.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In pace nullus est communis magistratus, sed principes regionum atque pagorum inter suos ius dicunt controversiasque minuunt.
examples.translation: Acts of brigandage committed outside the borders of each several state involve no disgrace;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a liquid, fluid of any kind, moisture (class.)

examples.original: Nunc redit ad Syrtes et fluctus accipit ore, Aequoreusque placet, sed non et sufficit, umor.
examples.translation: Aulus searches for water deep down in the barren sand, and then returns to the Syrtes, and swallows the brine;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Iam rarior aer Et par Phoebus aquis densas in vellera nubes Sparserat, et noctes ventura luce rubebant, Servatoque loco rerum discessit ab astris Umor, et ima petit, quidquid pendebat aquarum.
examples.translation: By this time the sky had cleared; the sun, a match for the waters, had broken up the thick clouds into fleeces;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a beginning, commencement, origin (class.; syn.: primordia, initium).
Latin: sententia prima
Latin: exordium

examples.original: Quid sibi istud principium velit quaeris?
examples.translation: Do you ask me what this preamble means?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Asperitas autem vocis fit ab asperitate principiorum, et item levor levore creatur.
examples.translation: The roughness of voice, moreover, comes from roughness of the elements, as also smoothness from smoothness.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Omnium enim rerum principia parva sunt, sed suis progressionibus usa augentur; nec sine causa;
examples.translation: All things are small in their first beginnings, but they grow larger as they pass through their regular stages of progress.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: for, truly, and indeed, because that, since (not freq. till class. times, esp. in Cic.)

examples.original: Etenim quod sacrificium tam vetustum est quam hoc, quod a regibus aequale huius urbis accepimus?
examples.translation: And indeed what sacrifice is so ancient as that which we received from our kings, and which is coeval with our city?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Etenim si eam tum defendebam, cum mihi aliquid illa debebat, quid nunc me facere oportet, cum ego illi plurimum debeo?
examples.translation: And indeed, if I defended her then, when she was somewhat in debt to me, what does my duty bid me do now, when I am deeply in debt to her?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Etenim omnium rerum quas et creat natura et tuetur, quae aut sine animo sunt aut non multo secus, earum summum bonum in corpore est;
examples.translation: For the inanimate or nearly inanimate creatures that are under nature’s charge, all of them have their supreme good in the body;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to kill, slay, put to death, destroy (usually without a weapon, by poison, hunger, etc.; cf.: occido, interficio, interimo, perimo).
Latin: Mori facere
Latin: Vitam alicujus finire

examples.original: Iunxit parricidio matris amitae necem.
examples.translation: To matricide he added the murder of his aunt.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Eodemque veneno C. Oppianicum fratrem necavit.
examples.translation: And he used poison, too, to murder his brother,G. Oppianicus.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Verba mihi captiosa conponis et interrogatiunculas nectis?
examples.translation: Do you propose to construct catchwords for me, or to string together petty syllogisms?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of free will, of one's own accord, of one's self, freely, willingly, voluntarily, spontaneously (syn. ultro)

examples.original: Se tamen, utcumque sit, etiam nunc paenitere sua sponte Aequos quam pati hostilia malle.
examples.translation: If they did so, they could count on a safe refuge in the clemency they had already proved;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In illis excusatius est voluntate peccare quam casu, in hac maxima culpa est sponte delinquere.
examples.translation: In the case of the latter, it is more pardonable to err voluntarily rather than by accident;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ita iam sua sponte aegris animis legati ab regibus superveniunt sine mentione reditus bona tantum repetentes.
examples.translation: The senate, having given them a hearing, debated the question for several days;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to fight against, to attack, assail, assault, storm, besiege

examples.original: Ita ancipiti proelio castra Romana oppugnabantur;
examples.translation: Thus a two-fold attack was directed against the camp.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quos primo Camillus vallo circumdare et aggere atque operibus oppugnare est adortus.
examples.translation: Camillus at first set about confining them with a palisade and mound, intending to lay siege to them;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum demum Ariovistus partem suarum copiarum, quae castra minora oppugnaret, misit. Acriter utrimque usque ad vesperum pugnatum est.
examples.translation: Then at last Ariovistus sent a part of his own forces to attack the lesser camp, and both sides fought in spirited fashion till eventide.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to shut up, shut in, confine, enclose, imprison, keep in (class.).—Constr. with in and

examples.original: Sed iam debeo epistulam includere.
examples.translation: But now I ought to close my letter.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iam non excludere tantum, Inclusisse volunt.
examples.translation: They say that they seek to drive away the horrid taint of war.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sic per omnis aequoris portus, sinus, latebras, recessus, promontoria, freta, paeninsulas quidquid piratarum fuit quadam indagine inclusum est.
examples.translation: Thus, in every harbour, bay, shelter, creek, promontory, strait and peninsula in the sea, every single pirate was enclosed as it were in a net.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: on
Latin: continuare
Latin: (Intrans.) continuare
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; perrexi, perrectum, 3

examples.original: In hortos, in quibus devertebatur Saturninus, pergunt.
examples.translation: They hurried to the gardens where Saturninus had his quarters;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nec deerant qui monerent ut cum fidissimis per occultos tramites vitata Ravenna Hostiliam Cremonamve pergeret;
examples.translation: Some advised him to take his most trusty men and, avoiding Ravenna, to push on by secret roads to Hostilia or Cremona;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Hic ego in tantis angustiis quasi aura spirante recreatus nihil ei respondi, sed ad fratrem Alypium gradu concitatiore perrexi eique quid dixerit, dixi.
examples.translation: At such an impasse, this refreshed me like a breath of air, but I said nothing to him and went with hurried step to brother Alypius and told him what he had said.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: farthest, most remote, last

examples.original: Ecce hic dies ultimus est.
examples.translation: For what end should I toil?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Si pudorem haberes, ultimam mihi pensionem remisisses.
examples.translation: If you had any shame, you would have let me off from paying the last instalment.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quaedam post multa incrementa ultima demum vertit adiectio et novam illis aliamque quam in qua fuerunt, condicionem inprimit.
examples.translation: There are others, however, which, after many increments, are altered by the last addition; there is stamped upon them a new character, different from that of yore.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Of living beings.

examples.original: Captivi sine pretio remissi sunt.
examples.translation: The prisoners were released without a price.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quibus in locis sit Caesar ex captivis quaerunt;
examples.translation: From prisoners they inquire in what district Caesar is;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Captivam pecuniam in aedificationem eius templi seposuit.
examples.translation: The money from the captured city he put aside to build this temple.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a sinew, tendon, nerve.

examples.original: Nec nocuisse ulli et fortunam habuisse nocendi, Nec quemquam nervos extimuisse tuos?
examples.translation: To have harmed none, yet to have had the power to harm, and that none feared thy might?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ut corpora nostra sine mente, sic civitas sine lege suis partibus, ut nervis et sanguine et membris, uti non potest.
examples.translation: The state without law would be like the human body without mind—unable to employ the parts which are to it as sinews, blood, and limbs.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Qui diutissime impuberes permanserunt, maximam inter suos ferunt laudem: hoc ali staturam, ali vires nervosque confirmari putant.
examples.translation: Those who remain longest in chastity win greatest praise among their kindred; some think that stature, some that strength and sinew are fortified thereby.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: uninterrupted, never-ending time, eternity; per aevom
Latin: Aetas, seu tempus in toto

examples.original: Sic longius aevum Destruit ingentes animos et vita superstes Imperio.
examples.translation: Thus length of days and life surviving power humble the proudest heart.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nec minore livore ac malignitate quam superbia saevitiaque paene adversus omnis aevi hominum genus grassatus est.
examples.translation: He assailed mankind of almost every epoch with no less envy and malice than insolence and cruelty.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Quid tibi nunc mores prosunt actumque pudice Omne aevum et tanto tam placuisse viro?
examples.translation: What now avails thy character, thy whole life chastely lived, thy having so pleased so mighty a lord?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: headforemost, headlong (class.)

examples.original: Statim a sapientia praeceps est?” Non, ut existimo.
examples.translation: Is there a sheer descent immediately below wisdom?” I think not.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Praecipiti cursu vaesanum Caesaris agmen In densos agitur cuneos, perque arma, per hostem Quaerit iter.
examples.translation: With headlong speed and fury Caesar’s men charged the close-packed columns, forcing a way through shields and through soldiers.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Eodem die ad Caecinam operi pontis intentum duo praetoriarum cohortium tribuni, conloquium eius postulantes, venerunt: audire condiciones ac reddere parabat, cum praecipites exploratores adesse hostem nuntiavere.
examples.translation: On the same day, while Caecina was busy with the construction of his bridge, two tribunes of the praetorian cohorts came to him and asked for an interview.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: question, inquire, interrogate (syn.: percontor, sciscitor; class.).

examples.original: Ad haec quae interrogatus es responde;
examples.translation: Answer these questions I have put to you;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quid sit istud, interrogas, aut unde subeat?
examples.translation: Do you ask me what this real good is, and whence it derives?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cuius? quis me umquam ulla lege interrogavit?
examples.translation: Then perhaps it was the result of an action at law.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to send to; hence with the access. idea of leave, permission (cf.: aditus, accessus), to suffer to come or

examples.original: Aliud litterarum genus adiutorium admittit.
examples.translation: The other kind of literary activitya admits of outside assistance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec lucem in thalamos totis admitte fenestris;
examples.translation: And let not light into your room by all the windows;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ac nostri, quo non metuant admittere manes Tartarei reges.
examples.translation: Tartarus would not fear to let the dead travel thus far.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: an entrance; hence

examples.original: Illius exemplo violes simulacra Minervae, Aulidis a portu qui leve vertit iter.
examples.translation: Mayst thou violate Minerva’s image after example of him who pursued a nimble path from Aulis’ haven.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Longe illi triplex murus totidemque arces, portus ille marmoreus et fons celebratus Arethusae;
examples.translation: Of no avail were its triple walls, its three citadels, its harbour of marble and the celebrated Fountain of Arethusa;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Publium Sulpicium Rufum legatum cum eo praesidio, quod satis esse arbitrabatur, portum tenere iussit.
examples.translation: He commanded Publius Sulpicius Rufus, lieutenant-general, with a garrison he considered sufficient, to hold the port.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to throw or cast down; to hurl down, precipitate (very freq., and class.).

examples.original: Verum ita est, uti dicis. Te deiectum debeo intelligere, etiamsi tactus non fueris.
examples.translation: But you are right—I am bound to consider you ejected even though you were not touched, am I not?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Deiectus verbo qui potest esse quisquam, nisi in inferiorem locum de superiore motus?
examples.translation: And how can anyone be literally ”ejecteda” unless he has been removed from higher to lower ground?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Leontinis, misera in civitate atque inani, tamen istius in gymnasio statua deiecta est.
examples.translation: At Leontini, wretched and poverty-stricken place though it is, his statue in the gymnasium was thrown down nevertheless.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To seek, to seek to obtain any thing (ante-class.)

examples.original: Ad eos igitur converte te, quaeso.
examples.translation: Do you then join them, I beg of you.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quid enim execrabilius, quaeso te, ut alia taceam, quam id quod nunc accidit?
examples.translation: I pass over other matters and ask you what could be more abominable than what has now happened?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Tum Verginius ubi nihil usquam auxilii vidit, ”Quaeso” inquit, ”Appi, primum ignosce patrio dolori, si quo inclementius in te sum invectus;
examples.translation: Then Verginius, seeing no help anywhere, said, ”I ask you, Appius, first to pardon a father’s grief if I have somewhat harshly inveighed against you;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a spear (syn.: hastile, dolo, gaesum, sarisa, sparus, lancea, pilum, spiculum, telum, etc.).
Latin: Genus armorum acutum ac longum

examples.original: Ad hastam publicam numquam accessit.
examples.translation: He was never present at an auction sale of confiscated property.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Praedae pars sua cognoscentibus Latinis atque Hernicis reddita, partem sub hasta dictator vendidit;
examples.translation: A portion of the booty was restored to the Latins and the Hernici, on their identifying it as their own;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: not?

examples.original: Nonne vobis Numa Pompilius videtur loqui?
examples.translation: The pronouncement of a veritable Numa Pompilius, is it not?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nonne vides etiam, nocturna ad lumina linum nuper ubi extinctum admoveas, accendier ante quam tetigit flammam, taedamque pari ratione?
examples.translation: Do you not see also that, if you move a wick newly extinguished near a night-light, it kindles before touching the flame, and the same with a torch?
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Mitto haruspices, mitto illam veterem ab ipsis dis immortalibus, ut hominum fama est, Etruriae traditam disciplinam: nos nonne haruspices esse possumus?
examples.translation: I will dispense with the lore which, as popular rumour has it, was committed to Etruria by the immortal gods;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: very clear, very bright.

examples.original: Praeclara voluntas atque omni laude digna.
examples.translation: His wish was a lofty one, and worthy of all praise;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Vives, inquit Aristo, magnifice atque praeclare;
examples.translation: O, says Aristo, you will get on splendidly, capitally;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: O praeclarum munus aetatis, si quidem id aufert a nobis, quod est in adulescentia vitiosissimum!
examples.translation: O glorious boon of age, if it does indeed free us from youth’s most vicious fault!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To determine or estimate the extrinsic (money) value of a thing, to value, rate, appraise; constr. with
Latin: Censere pretium alicuius; aut extrinsecus aut intrinsecus

examples.original: Pluris aestimo beneficium quam iniuriam.
examples.translation: I reckon a benefit at a higher rate than an injury.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hoc iudicio damnatur Timotheus lisque eius aestimatur centum talentis.
examples.translation: Timotheus was found guilty and his fine was fixed at one hundred talents.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timotheus

examples.original: Nam famae quidem ac fidei damna maiora esse quam quae aestimari possent.
examples.translation: For reputation at least and trustworthiness were things the loss of which was beyond all reckoning.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: unfruitful, not fertile

examples.original: Infelix est Fabricius, quod rus suum, quantum a re publica vacavit, fodit?
examples.translation: Is Fabricius unfortunate because, whenever he has leisure from affairs of state, he tills his fields?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His orationibus incitata plebs denis milibus aeris gravis reos condemnat, nequiquam Sergio Martem communem belli fortunamque accusante, Verginio deprecante ne infelicior domi quam militiae esset.
examples.translation: It was in vain that Sergius blamed Fortune and the common chance of war, while Verginius begged that he might not be more unlucky at home than he had been in the campaign.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Infelix gemino cecidit prope Pergamon igni, Et paene est alio Troia cremata rogo.
examples.translation: All but twice in the flames unhappy Pergamum perished Troy on a second pyre narrowly failed of her doom.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

definitions: English: to loosen from, to make loose, set free, detach, untie
Latin: Solvere ab aliquo, ut, pedicis (a vinculis solvere, vinculis exsolvere)
Latin: solvere a causa

examples.original: Qui damnabatur uni adulterio, absolutus est multis.
examples.translation: He to whom one adultery brought condemnation was acquitted because of many.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Dicam: quia quod aliud est, suum oportet esse et proprium et totum et intra se absolutum.
examples.translation: I will tell you: it is because that which is different, must be personal and peculiar to itself, a whole, and complete within itself.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque eleganter illis Catulus absoluto reo, ”quid vos,” inquit, ”praesidium a nobis petebatis?
examples.translation: Hence the witty remark of Catulus after the defendant had been acquitted: ”Why did you ask us for the guard?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the publication of a last will or testament; a will, testament (cf. codicilli).

examples.original: Ut in pauca conferam, testamento facto mulier moritur.
examples.translation: Shortly afterwards she married Aulus Caecina.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Eius testamentum erat nullum; lege hereditas ad gentem Minuciam veniebat.
examples.translation: Before he became praetor, a man named Minucius died.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Iam hoc ridiculum est: si de hereditate ambigetur, et tabulae testamenti obsignatae non minus multis signis quam e lege oportet ad me proferentur, secundum tabulas testamenti potissimum possessionem dabo.
examples.translation: That point you nowhere deal with; nor does your edict provide for anything else at all besides the case for which you got paid.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make sharp or pointed, to sharpen, whet.

examples.original: Acuebat hac moderatione tam iusta studia;
examples.translation: Such moderation but intensified the well-merited enthusiasm of his friends;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non ego per praeceps et acuta cacumina vadam, Nec iuvenum quisquam me duce captus erit.
examples.translation: I am not the man to go by precipitous paths and rocky heights; no youth under my leadership will be captured.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Tela iugo vincta est, stamen secernit harundo, Inseritur medium radiis subtemen acutis, Quod lato paviunt insecti pectine dentes.
examples.translation: The web is bound to frame; asunder now The reed doth part the warp.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To strike through and through, to thrust or pierce through (syn.: percello, transfigo).

examples.original: T. Manlius consul filium, quod contra edictum eius adversus Latinos pugnaverat, quamvis prospere pugnasset, securi percussit.
examples.translation: Titus Manlius the consul had his son beheaded, because he had fought—albeit successfully—against the Latins in defiance of his edict.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ceterum nihilo minus foeda dedita urbe quam si capta foret Aurunci passi: principes securi percussi, sub corona venierunt coloni alii;
examples.translation: Their chief men were beheaded, and the rest of the colonists were sold as slaves. The town was razed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum porro quid id est, animum quod percutit ipsum, quod movet et varios sensus expromere cogit. ex insensilibus ne credas sensile gigni?
examples.translation: Then further, what is that which strikes on your very mind, which moves it and compels it to express diverse feelings, forbidding you to believe that the sensible is born from the insensible?
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: to lay waste, ravage, devastate, desolate; to spoil, plunder, pillage (class.; syn.: vasto, vexo, diripio).

examples.original: Malis artibus popularis favor quaeritur.
examples.translation: It takes trickery to win popular approval;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed nec populo aut moenibus patriae pepercit.
examples.translation: But he showed no greater mercy to the people or the walls of his capital.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Vergini patris sponsique Icili populare nomen celebrabatur.
examples.translation: Their acquaintance were led to support the girl out of regard for them;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: twenty
Latin: Novemdecim et alius. Numerus XX

examples.original: Vixit annis viginti novem, imperavit triennio et decem mensibus diebusque octo.
examples.translation: He lived twenty-nine years and ruled three years, ten months and eight days.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: His rebus gestis, ex litteris Caesaris dierum viginti supplicatio a senatu decreta est.
examples.translation: And for these achievements, upon receipt of Caesar’s despatches, the Senate decreed a public thanksgiving of twenty days.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Duas validissimas gentes superque viginti oppida et insulam Vectem Britanniae proximam in dicionem redegit partim Auli Plauti legati consularis partim Claudi ipsius ductu.
examples.translation: He reduced to subjection two powerful nations, more than twenty towns, and the island of Vectis, near Britain, partly under the leadership of Aulus Plautius, the consular governor, and partly under that of Claudius himself.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to lead or bring through; hence

examples.original: Ap. Claudius censor aquam perduxit;
examples.translation: Appius Claudius the censor completed an aqueduct;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Res disputatione ad mediam noctem perducitur.
examples.translation: The matter continued in dispute till midnight.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Sed ad desperationem nos vitia nostra perducunt;
examples.translation: But it is our vices that bring us to despair;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the letter F
Latin: Littera sexta alphabeti Romani, ef dicitur

examples.original: Tumultus causa fuit, quem ab Aequis et Volscis Latini atque Hernici nuntiarant. T. Quinctius L. f.
examples.translation: Titus Quinctius Cincinnatus, son of Lucius—the same who is given the added surname Poenus,—and Gnaeus Julius Mento were made consuls.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: an heir, heiress.
Latin: heres Cui alius homo vetustatis causa suam proprietatem donat

examples.original: Fecit heredem M. Octavium Ligurem;
examples.translation: He left his property to Marcus Octavius Ligus;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Numerius autem Aurius frater eius mortuus est heredemque Cn. Magium fratrem reliquit.
examples.translation: N. Aurius, his brother, died, leaving his property to his brother Gn. Magius.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quid? aviam tuam, Oppianice, Dinaeam, cui tu es heres, pater tuus non manifesto necavit?
examples.translation: Again, is it not patent, Oppianicus, that your father murdered your grandmother, Dinea, whose heir you are?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a Roman family name in the plebeian gens Claudia

examples.original: Quid ego de M. Marcello loquar, qui Syracusas urbem ornatissimam cepit?
examples.translation: Need I quote the example of Marcus Marcellus, who captured Syracuse, that treasury of art?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Hi rem ad virum primarium, summo officio ac virtute praeditum, M. Marcellum, qui erat pupilli tutor, deferunt.
examples.translation: These three carried the matter to that eminent and most trustworthy and excellent man Marcus Marcellus, himself one of the guardians.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Perfacile vero apud istius modi praetorem, a quo M. Marcelli tutoris in causa pupilli Iunii et oratio et voluntas et auctoritas repudiata est.
examples.translation: An easy thing indeed, with a praetor such as this, with whom Marcus Marcellus pleaded for his ward Iunius, to find that his eloquence, his earnest wishes, his personal influence, all went for nothing!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to count, reckon, number (syn. recenseo).
Latin: Numerum rerum invenire unicuidam rei numerum addicendo
Latin: Pecuniam solvo

examples.original: Numerare eos noli, qui tibi metum faciunt.
examples.translation: Do not count the number of those who inspire fear in you.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ne diutius teneam, pecunia attributa, numerata est;
examples.translation: To cut the story short: funds were allotted and paid over to the quaestor;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Numera quam multa in ista defensione falsa sint, Piso.
examples.translation: Count the flaws in that argument, Piso!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: eight: milia militum octo, Enn. ap.
Latin: Septem et alius

examples.original: Caesar Ab his castris oppidum Remorum nomine Bibrax aberat milia passuum octo.
examples.translation: From this camp a town of the Remi called Bibrax was eight miles distant.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Vixit annis viginti novem, imperavit triennio et decem mensibus diebusque octo.
examples.translation: He lived twenty-nine years and ruled three years, ten months and eight days.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Per octo annos varie et inaequabiliter provinciam rexit, primo acer et vehemens et in coercendis quidem delictis vel immodicus.
examples.translation: For eight years he governed the province in a variable and inconsistent manner. At first he was vigorous and energetic and even over severe in punishing offences;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: Left, on the left, on the left hand or side

examples.original: Dextro cornu Galli, sinistro Samnites constiterunt.
examples.translation: On the right wing stood the Gauls, on the left the Samnites.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In acie Quinctius dextrum cornu, Agrippa sinistrum tenuit;
examples.translation: In the battle-line Quinctius held the right wing, Agrippa the left;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cornus tibi cura sinistri, Lentule, cum prima, quae tum fuit optima bello, Et quarta legione datur.
examples.translation: Lentulus had charge of the left wing with two legions—the first, which was then the most fit for war, and the fourth;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: To keep safe, to preserve
Latin: Aliquem salvum facere; acquīrere salutem alicuius; cōnservāre
Latin: Salutem dicere vel facere alicui

examples.original: Fratrem Severum et qui cum eo sunt salutamus.
examples.translation: Give my greetings to brother Severusb and his company.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Seneca Lvcilio svo salvtem Agnosco Lucilium meum;
examples.translation: On Siren Songs Now I recognize my Lucilius!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Terra salutares herbas, eademque nocentes Nutrit, et urticae proxima saepe rosa est;
examples.translation: The same earth fosters healing herbs and noxious, and oft is the nettle nearest to the rose;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: clean

examples.original: Nam cur tam variae res possent esse requiro, ex uno si sunt igni puroque creatae.
examples.translation: For I want to know why things could be so various, if they are made of fire pure and simple;
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: to move violently, to put in violent or quick motion, to stir up, rouse up, excite, incite, shake.

examples.original: Habet ambitionem, sed non concitatam.
examples.translation: He has ambition, but it is not yet fully aroused.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Si ille acer est et ferox, concitari gradum?
examples.translation: That a keen and confident soul quickens the step?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Facile est auditorem concitare ad cupidinem recti;
examples.translation: It is easy to rouse a listener so that he will crave righteousness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: near to, nigh.

examples.original: Syriam et quattuor legiones obtinebat Licinius Mucianus, vir secundis adversisque iuxta famosus.
examples.translation: Syria and its four legions were held by Licinius Mucianus, a man notorious in prosperity and adversity alike.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Huc cum ab Ostia navigaret, vehementi circio bis paene demersus est, prope Liguriam iuxtaque Stoechadas insulas.
examples.translation: On the voyage thither from Ostia he was nearly cast away twice in furious north-westers, off Liguria and near the Stoechades islands.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Incohavit autem aquae ductum regione Tiburti et amphitheatrum iuxta Saepta, quorum operum a successore eius Claudio alterum peractum, omissum alterum est.
examples.translation: He likewise began an aqueduct in the region near Tibur and an amphitheatre beside the Saepta, the former finished by his successor Claudius, while the latter was abandoned.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: join, annex, or bind to any thing.
Latin: Iungere (aliquid ad aliquam rei)
Latin: Iungere (aliquid ad aliquam rei). equos adiungere

examples.original: Ego illam, si pateris, adiungam.
examples.translation: But, with your permission, I shall add it.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Inde Patavium et Ateste partibus adiunxere.
examples.translation: Next they drew Padua and Ateste to their side.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Callipho ad virtutem nihil adiunxit nisi voluptatem;
examples.translation: Callipho coupled with virtue pleasure alone;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a sore, ulcer.
Latin: Nome; laesio cutis epitheliive
English: a chariot, car, wain.
Latin: Species vehiculi

examples.original: Ipse caput medio Titan cum ferret Olympo, Condidit ardentes atra caligine currus Involvitque orbem tenebris gentesque coegit Desperare diem;
examples.translation: The sun himself, while rearing his head in the zenith, hid his burning chariot in black darkness and veiled his sphere in gloom, forcing mankind to despair of daylight;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Quacumque vagatur, Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellona flagellum, Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, Nox ingens scelerum est;
examples.translation: He visits the corpses that sprawl on the wide plain; with his own hand he staunches the wound that would otherwise pour out all the blood of many a man.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Itaque hoste victo ruptorem foederis Mettum Fufetium religatum inter duos currus pernicibus equis distrahit, Albamque ipsam quamvis parentem, aemulam tamen diruit, cum prius omnes opes urbis ipsumque populum Romam transtulisset;
examples.translation: So after the defeat of the enemy Tullus bound Mettus Fufetius, the violator of the treaty, between two chariots, and tore him asunder with swift horses.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: quickly/rapidly/speedily; hastily; soon/at once/early moment
Latin: modō celerī, aliquid vēlōcitāte agere

examples.original: At Germani celeriter ex consuetudine sua phalange facta impetus gladiorum exceperunt.
examples.translation: But the Germans, according to their custom, speedily formed mass, and received the sword-attack.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: His rebus celeriter administratis ipse, cum primum per anni tempus potuit, ad exercitum contendit.
examples.translation: These requirements were rapidly executed, and so soon as the season allowed he himself hastened to join the army.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Atque in sensibus est sua cuiusque virtus, ut ne quid impediat quo minus suo sensus quisque munere fungatur in iis rebus celeriter expediteque percipiendis quae subiectae sunt sensibus.
examples.translation: The senses also possess their several virtues or excellences, consisting in the unimpeded performance of their several functions of swiftly and readily perceiving sensible objects.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to move a person or thing; to bring, conduct, lead, carry, etc., to or toward a place (syn.: adduco, adicio, adhibeo, appello).
Latin: Movēre (aliquem vel aliquid) ad (locum)

examples.original: Nunquam deos ipsos admovere nocentibus manus;
examples.translation: The gods themselves never laid hands upon the guilty;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Conversus ad ianuam ”Quis est iste?” inquam, ”iste decrepitus et merito ad ostium admotus?
examples.translation: You have done well to place him at the entrance;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Numquid tu invisos esse Lacedaemoniis liberos suos credis, quorum experiuntur indolem publice verberibus admotis?
examples.translation: Do you imagine that the Lacedaemonians hate their children when they test their mettle by lashing them in public?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: willingly; gladly, with pleasure

examples.original: Quem libenter cenasse nemo negat.
examples.translation: No one will deny that he dined pleasantly.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed quia bonus es amator iustitiae, inde te admoneo, ut de illa quam diligis, hoc a me libentius audias.
examples.translation: But since you are a good lover of justice, I warn you to hear with the greater favour what I say about this object of your affection.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Exilium Metellus fortiter tulit, Rutilius etiam libenter;
examples.translation: Exile was endured by Metellus with courage, by Rutilius even with gladness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the earth, the ground, the soil.
Latin: Solum, terrae solum
Latin: ager, arvum

examples.original: Aut ut Amastriacis quondam Lenaeus ab oris, Nudus Achillea destituaris humo.
examples.translation: Or like Lenaeus faring once from Amastris’ shores mayst thou be left destitute on Achillean soil.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Non mihi falx nimias Saturnia deputat umbras, Duratam renovat non mihi fossor humum;
examples.translation: Saturn’s sickle prunes not my superfluous shade, no digger renews my hardened soil;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Est prope purpureos colles florentis Hymetti Fons sacer et viridi caespite mollis humus: Silva nemus non alta facit;
examples.translation: Near the purple hills of flowery Hymettus there is a sacred spring and ground soft with green turf: trees of no great height form a grove;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to set fire to, to kindle, burn (freq. and class.; syn. inflammare).

examples.original: Deliberatur de Avarico in communi concilio, incendi placeret an defendi.
examples.translation: They deliberated in a general convention whether Avaricum should be burnt or defended.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quid signorum, quid vestium quidve tabularum raptum incensumque atque proiectum est!
examples.translation: What a vast quantity of statues, garments and pictures was carried off, burnt, and thrown away!
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Tu, qui flagrante minacem Scorpion incendis cauda chelasque peruris, Quid tantum, Gradive, paras?
examples.translation: But Mars—what dreadful purpose has he, when he kindles the Scorpion menacing with fiery tail and scorches its claws?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a basin, tank, tub; esp.
Latin: Sēria magna in qua liquidum continetur
Latin: Corpus magnum aquae, praesertim aquae dulcis

examples.original: Hoc modo ad lacum Regillum pugnatum est.
examples.translation: Such was the battle at Lake Regillus.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Thrasymennus lacus, tertium fulmen Annibalis, imperatore Flaminio.
examples.translation: Hannibal’s third thunderbolt was launched at Lake Trasimene, where Flaminius commanded the Romans.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Vinius pro M. Othone, Laco atque Icelus consensu non tam unum aliquem fovebant quam alium, Neque erat Galbae ignota Othonis ac Titi Vinii amicitia;
examples.translation: Vinius favoured Marcus Otho; Laco and Icelus agreed not so much in favouring any particular person as in supporting someone other than Otho.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to bear before, to carry in front, to hold forth.
Latin: aliquid plus amare quam aliud

examples.original: Sed latent, nihil habent quod intentent, quod praeferant;
examples.translation: They are, however, secret; they have no bluster and no heralding;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec facile est aut rem rei aut auctorem auctori praeferre.
examples.translation: It is not easy to choose between the accounts or the authorities.
examples.author: Livy
