Latin: Actus standi seu consistendi
Latin: locus, ubi quis moratur

examples.original: Stationem in castris agebat Iulius Martialis tribunus.
examples.translation: Julius Martialis the tribune was the officer of the day in the camp.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ubi praesenti ope res egebant, consul nec animo defecit nec consilio: pars militum portarum stationes firmant, pars corona vallum cingunt.
examples.translation: When circumstances required instant action, the consul proved to be wanting neither in resolution nor in judgment. With a part of his soldiers he reinforced the guards at the gates;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Qui postquam intentos homines in eventum periculi alieni pro se incautos neglectis vigiliis stationibusque est adortus, prius paene cepit castra quam oppugnari hostes satis scirent.
examples.translation: This officer found his foes absorbed in the issue of the dangerous work undertaken by their fellows, and with no thought for themselves, neglecting their sentinels and outguards;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to beseech, entreat, implore, supplicate, conjure: obsecrare est opem a sacris petere, Paul. ex

examples.original: Ita fac, oro atque obsecro.
examples.translation: And I beg and pray you to proceed in this course;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid est, obsecro te, Lucili, cur timeat laborem vir, mortem homo?
examples.translation: Why, pray, my dear Lucilius, should a man fear toil, or a mortal death?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Proinde obsecro, ut epistulam quam eis communi nomine scripsi, subscriptam non differas mittere.
examples.translation: I beseech you, therefore, not to postpone signing and sending the letter I have written them in our common name.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to be needy (for syn. cf.: indigeo, careo, vaco).

examples.original: Non enim ullo honestamento eget;
examples.translation: For virtue needs nothing to set it off;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quaeris, quare virtus nullo egeat?
examples.translation: Do you ask why virtue needs nothing?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Magnum opus est egetque exercitatione non parva.
examples.translation: This is a difficult thing to do and requires no little practice.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to watch, note, heed, observe a thing; to take notice of, pay attention to

examples.original: Quo praecepto ab eis diligentissime observato, cum quaepiam cohors ex orbe excesserat atque impetum fecerat, hostes velocissime refugiebant.
examples.translation: This instruction they most carefully observed. When any cohort left the square and made a charge the enemy would run back with great rapidity.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Observa te itaque, numquid vestis tua domusque dissentiant, numquid in te liberalis sis, in tuos sordidus, numquid cenes frugaliter, aedifices luxuriose.
examples.translation: Observe yourself, then, and see whether your dress and your house are inconsistent, whether you treat yourself lavishly and your family meanly, whether you eat frugal dinners and yet build luxurious houses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Observatum autem notatumque est in primis Caesares omnes, quibus Gai praenomen fuerit, ferro perisse, iam inde ab eo, qui Cinnanis temporibus sit occisus.
examples.translation: Men further observed and commented on the fact that all the Caesars whose forename was Gaius perished by the sword, beginning with the one who was slain in the times of Cinna.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: Far and wide, everywhere, nearly = ubique (not ante-Aug.)

examples.original: Dilectum haberi non ex toto passim populo placuit; decem tribus sorte ductae sunt.
examples.translation: It was determined not to make a general levy on the entire people, but ten tribes were chosen by lot.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hic igitur ventis atque ignibus omnia plena sunt; ideo passim fremitus et fulgura fiunt.
examples.translation: In such a case, then, all is full of winds and fires, therefore rumblings and lightnings are made every-where.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: A Priverno Plautius alter consul pervastatis passim agris praedaque abacta in agrum Fundanum exercitum inducit. Ingredienti fines senatus Fundanorum occurrit;
examples.translation: From Privernum the other consul Plautius, after everywhere pillaging the fields and driving off the cattle, led his army into the domain of Fundi.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: lowly, small, slight (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.).

examples.original: Cui plebeio et humili praesidium in legibus fore, si Ap. Claudio non sit?
examples.translation: What humble plebeian would find protection in the laws, if they afforded none to Appius Claudius?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Haec cogitatio nihil sordidum animo subsidere sinit, nihil humile, nihil crudele.
examples.translation: Such thoughts permit nothing mean to settle in the soul, nothing low, nothing cruel.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Potest ex casa vir magnus exire, potest et ex deformi humilique corpusculo formosus animus ac magnus.
examples.translation: A great man can spring from a hovel; so can a beautiful and great soul from an ugly and insignificant body.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Blood (which flows from a wound), a stream of blood (more restricted in meaning than sanguis, which designates both that circulating in bodies and that shed by wounding)

examples.original: Accipe regna Phari nullo quaesita cruore;
examples.translation: We give you the kingdom, to be yours without bloodshed;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Cruor altus in unda Spumat, et obducti concreto sanguine fluctus.
examples.translation: Their blood foamed deep upon the wave, and a crust of gore covered the sea.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ille cruor meus est, illo maculata cruore Non profectura dextra lavatur aqua.
examples.translation: That is my blood: the hand that blood has tainted is washed in unavailing water.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: of or belonging to the house.

examples.original: Hos igitur omnis domesticos motus separatos ab externis iustisque bellis ex ordine persequemur.
examples.translation: We will, therefore, now describe in their order all these domestic disturbances as distinct from foreign wars properly so called.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Quod facere illi necessarium est, cum ad haec civilia et domestica venitur et, ut ita dicam, mortalia.
examples.translation: Now he is compelled to do this when he approaches state and home duties—everything, so to speak, that is mortal.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Etsi ille domestico summo genere erat, tamen Macedones eum sibi aliquando anteponi indigne ferebant, neque tamen non patiebantur;
examples.translation: Although he was of the highest rank in his own country, yet the Macedonians were indignant that he was sometimes preferred to them;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: go forth (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Nihil est miserius dubitatione venientium quorsus evadant;
examples.translation: There is nothing more wretched than worry over the outcome of future events;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Pauci hostium evasere ex insidiis; praeda omnis recepta est.
examples.translation: But few of them escaped the ambush, and the spoils were all recovered.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Samnites desperato improviso tumultu, quando in apertum semel discrimen evasura esset res, et ipsi acie iusta maluerunt concurrere.
examples.translation: Balked of their surprise attack, the Samnites—since it must ultimately come to an open trial of strength—likewise preferred to fight a regular engagement.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A celebrated Grecian philosopher, the disciple of Socrates, the instructor of Aristotle, and founder of the Academic philosophy

examples.original: Quid de Pythagora, quid de Platone aut de Democrito loquar?
examples.translation: Why should I speak of Pythagoras, or of Plato, or Democritus?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Oculorum, inquit Plato, est in nobis sensus acerrimus, quibus sapientiam non cernimus;
examples.translation: The sense of sight, says Plato, is the keenest sense we possess, yet our eyes cannot behold Wisdom;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque illa non dico me expetere sed legere, nec optare sed sumere, contraria autem non fugere sed quasi secernere’ Quid ait Aristoteles reliquique Platonis alumni?
examples.translation: Do you see therefore that between your master Zeno and Aristo there is a verbal harmony but a real difference;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: diligent, assiduous, industrious (class.)

examples.original: Cui non industrio otium poena est?
examples.translation: To what energetic man is not idleness a punishment?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nam illa tumultu gaudens non est industria, sed exagitatae mentis concursatio.
examples.translation: For love of bustle is not industry,—it is only the restlessness of a hunted mind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quippe Thracas in res suas traxerant, atque ita industriam Macedonum viribus Thracum, ferociam Thracum disciplina Macedonica temperavere.
examples.translation: They had induced the Thracians to support their efforts and had thus tempered the Macedonian persistence with Thracian energy, and Thracian savagery with Macedonian discipline.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: of or belonging to the night, nocturnal (class.)

examples.original: In his rebus circiter dies x consumit ne nocturnis quidem temporibus ad laborem militum intermissis.
examples.translation: Upon this business he spent about ten days, allowing no interruption even at night-time in the work of the troops.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Scaenicos ludos et assidue et varii generis ac multifariam fecit, quondam et nocturnos accensis tota urbe luminibus.
examples.translation: He exhibited stage-plays continually, of various kinds and in many different places, sometimes even by night, lighting up the whole city.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Proxima inde nocte Volsci, discordia Romana freti, si qua nocturna transitio proditiove fieri posset, temptant castra.
examples.translation: But the sentries perceived them, the army was roused, and, the signal being given, rushed to arms.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the upper part of the throat, from the root of the tongue to the entrance of the gullet, the pharynx, throat, gullet (syn.: gula, guttur, jugulum).

examples.original: Cerberus et Furiae iam vero et lucis egestas, Tartarus horriferos eructans faucibus aestus— qui neque sunt usquam nec possunt esse profecto.
examples.translation: Cerberusb also and the Furies and the with-holding of light, and Tartarus belching horrible fires from his throat—these neither exist anywhere nor in truth can exist.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Nero in ultimum Italiae angulum summoverat Annibalem, Livius in diversissimam partem, id est in ipsas nascentis Italiae fauces signa converterat.
examples.translation: Nero had driven Hannibal into the uttermost corner of Italy, while Livius had advanced to the very opposite end of the country, the very entrance of the Italian frontier.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: In pedes suos ipse plurima dicebat et in fauces concisas; sic inimicorum, quos plures habebat quam morbos, et in primis Ciceronis urbanitatem effugerat.
examples.translation: He uttered many a jest at the expense of his own feet and his scarred jowls.b So he escaped the wit of his enemies—they outnumbered his afflictions—and, above all, Cicero’s.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to read out, recite a document, statement, report, etc., in public proceedings

examples.original: Iubet iste sibi legem recitari.
examples.translation: He told them to read him the text of the law;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Consistam in uno nomine: multa enim sunt ex eodem genere. Recita.
examples.translation: I will pause to consider a single item;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quod si nihil aliud esset actum nisi ut hanc causam obtineremus, lege recitata perorassem.
examples.translation: But had our only concern been to get a verdict, I should have read the statute aloud and then sat down.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a coming near, a being present, presence; hence meton. for persons present (only in post-Aug. poets): locus ab omni liber arbitrio.

examples.original: Quamdiu quidem illi licet suo arbitrio res suas ordinare, se contentus est et ducit uxorem;
examples.translation: As long as he is allowed to order his affairs according to his judgment, he is self-sufficient—and marries a wife;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid? Epicurei num desistunt de iisdem, de quibus et ab Epicuro scriptum est et ab antiquis, ad arbitrium suum scribere?
examples.translation: Nor do the Epicureans cease from writing as the spirit moves them on the same questions on which Epicurus and the ancients wrote.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Illud vero cuius dementiae est, credere, quarum rerum extra nostrum arbitrium posita principia sunt, earum nostri esse arbitrii terminos?
examples.translation: But what folly it is, when the beginnings of certain things are situated outside our control, to believe that their endings are within our control!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: black; and specif., coalblack, lustreless-black, sable, dark
Latin: Niger sine luce; cuius color ut carbonis, ligni usti, vel caeli nocturni

examples.original: Medio cum Phoebus in axe est Aut caelum nox atra tenet, pavet ipse sacerdos Accessus dominumque timet deprendere luci.
examples.translation: For, when the sun is in mid-heaven or dark night fills the sky, the priest himself dreads their approach and fears to surprise the lord of the grove.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ipse caput medio Titan cum ferret Olympo, Condidit ardentes atra caligine currus Involvitque orbem tenebris gentesque coegit Desperare diem;
examples.translation: The sun himself, while rearing his head in the zenith, hid his burning chariot in black darkness and veiled his sphere in gloom, forcing mankind to despair of daylight;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: gentle, quiet, still, calm, mild, peaceful, placid (class.; syn.: quietus, mollis, lenis).

examples.original: Sapiens ille plenus est gaudio, hilaris et placidus, inconcussus;
examples.translation: The wise man is joyful, happy and calm, unshaken;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: I, qua ire coepisti et in isto te vitae habitu conpone placide, non molliter.
examples.translation: Proceed as you have begun, and settle yourself in this way of living, not luxuriously, but calmly.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ita dico: ex quo natus es, duceris. Haec et eiusmodi versanda in animo sunt, si volumus ultimam illam horam placidi expectare, cuius metus omnes alias inquietas facit.
examples.translation: We must ponder this thought, and thoughts of the like nature, if we desire to be calm as we await that last hour, the fear of which makes all previous hours uneasy.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: first pers. pres. indic. and
English: to build a wall around, to defend with a wall, to fortify, defend, protect, secure, put in a state of defence (class.).
Latin: vallis vel muro circumdare, aedificare, facer, firmare, fulcire, defendere, tueri
Latin: moeniis, seu muris quodammodo cingere

examples.original: Eum locum vallo fossaque munivit.
examples.translation: He fortified the place with rampart and trench.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Primam et secundam aciem in armis esse, tertiam castra munire iussit.
examples.translation: The first and second line he ordered to keep under arms, the third to entrench a camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ac nescio an nimis undique eam minimisque rebus muniendo modum excesserint.
examples.translation: Perhaps the pains they took to safeguard it, even in trivial details, may have been excessive.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: that does no harm.

examples.original: Quid ergo est ? Ignorantia rerum innocentes erant.
examples.translation: What, then, is the conclusion of the matter?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Verum, si innocens Falcula, quaero qui sit nocens?
examples.translation: But if Falcula is innocent, what juror, I ask, can be guilty?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ac primum quanta innocentia debent esse imperatores!
examples.translation: First, how great is the integrity needed by a general;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: ancestors (pl.)

examples.original: Et accesserunt maioris sollicitudinis causae.
examples.translation: He had besides reasons for still greater anxiety;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Penes quos igitur sunt auspicia more maiorum?
examples.translation: Who then control the auspices, by the tradition of our fathers?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Maior ista hereditas a me ad posteros transeat.
examples.translation: This inheritance shall pass from me to my descendants larger than before.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a living together; hence, a meal in company, a social feast, entertainment, banquet (freq. and class.)

examples.original: Cohibe itaque iam iniquum et inpacatum animum, ut in vera ecclesia Christi invenias salutare convivium.
examples.translation: So curb your hostile and rebellious spirit, that you may find the feast of salvation within the true Church of Christ.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Homo, qui semper hospitalissimus amicissimusque nostrorum hominum existimatus esset, noluit videri ipsum illum Rubrium invitus domum suam recepisse: magnifice et ornate, ut erat in primis inter suos copiosus, convivium comparat;
examples.translation: He had always been considered most hospitable and cordial towards our people, and he did not wish to give the impression that he was receiving even a man like Rubrius into his house unwillingly.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: soft
Latin: Tactu cedens, mollis, tractabilis, flexibilis
Latin: Iuvenis, recens

examples.original: An populum teneri, te unum exlegem esse?
examples.translation: Or that the people is bound, but that you alone are exempt?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: At vestrae matres teneras peperere puellas.
examples.translation: But your mothers have borne delicate girls.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quique bibunt tenera dulces ab harundine sucos, Et qui tinguentes croceo medicamine crinem Fluxa coloratis astringunt carbasa gemmis, Quique suas struxere pyras vivique calentes Conscendere rogos.
examples.translation: Up rose the men who drink sweet juices from soft reeds; and those who colour their hair with saffron dye and loop up their robes of cotton with brighthued gems;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: meet, proper, becoming, suitable

examples.original: His rebus cognitis exploratores centurionesque praemittit, qui locum idoneum castris deligant.
examples.translation: Upon this information Caesar sent forward scouts and centurions to choose a fit place for the camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Caesar His constitutis rebus nactus idoneam ad navigandum tempestatem tertia fere vigilia solvit equitesque in ulteriorem portum progredi et naves conscendere et se sequi iussit.
examples.translation: These arrangements made, he caught a spell of fair weather for sailing, and weighed anchor about the third watch: he ordered the cavalry to proceed to the further harbour, embark, and follow him.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Putarem me idoneum qui exemplum sequerer humanitatis atque officii, proponeremque spem meis hospitibus ac necessariis quo tutiorem sese vitam meo praesidio victuros esse arbitrarentur.
examples.translation: I should offer those who have given me hospitality and friendship some reason to think that they will live lives of greater security because I am here to protect them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a hair (syn.: villus, seta).

examples.original: Illyrici exercitus electi Celsum infestis pilis proturbant.
examples.translation: The picked troops from Illyria drove Celsus away at the point of their spears.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sed me nec sanguis nec tantum volnera nostri Adfecere senis, quantum gestata per urbem Ora ducis, quae transfixo sublimia pilo Vidimus;
examples.translation: But the blood and wounds of our aged sire moved me less than the carrying of his head through the city: I saw it borne aloft on a pike driven through it;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Milites e loco superiore pilis missis facile hostium phalangem perfregerunt.
examples.translation: Then after a speech to encourage his troops he joined battle.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the name of many persons of antiquity; among whom
Latin: Nomen ortu Europaeo, 'viros tuens' indicans

examples.original: Post Dareum et Indos pauper est Alexander.
examples.translation: Alexander was poor even after his conquest of Darius and the Indies.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hunc Epaminondas recuperavit, bello persequens Alexandrum.
examples.translation: He was rescued by Epaminondas, who made war upon Alexander.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pelopidas

examples.original: Horum in quolibet cum indoles eadem quae in Alexandro erat animi ingeniique;
examples.translation: Any one of these was as highly endowed with courage and talents as was Alexander;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: ignorant of a thing, not knowing, unacquainted with, inexperienced, unaware (syn.: inscius, nescius, insciens).

examples.original: Auxerat id maxime animos quod ignari loco iniquo, non hosti cessum, velut fugientes ac territos terribiles ipsi secuti fuerant.
examples.translation: Their encouragement was due chiefly to ignorance that their enemies had retreated from an awkward position, and not from them;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Multa erumpentis seditionis indicia per conscios oppressa: quaedam apud Galbae auris praefectus Laco elusit, ignarus militarium animorum consiliique quamvis egregii, quod non ipse adferret, inimicus et adversus peritos pervicax.
examples.translation: There were many signs of the outbreak of the revolt, but these were repressed by the plotters. Some things reached Galba’s ears, but the prefect Laco made light of them;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Inritaverant turbidum ingenium Helvetii, Gallica gens olim armis virisque, mox memoria nominis clara, de caede Galbae ignari et Vitellii imperium abnuentes.
examples.translation: His restless spirit had been provoked by the Helvetii, a Gallic people once famous for their deeds in arms and for their heroes, later only for the memory of their name.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: foul, filthy, loathsome, ugly, unseemly, detestable, abominable, horrible (class.; cf.: deformis, turpis).
Latin: coniunctio hominum finem communem spectantium

examples.original: Pater patratus ad ius iurandum patrandum, id est sanciendum fit foedus;
examples.translation: The pater patratus is appointed to pronounce the oath, that is, to solemnize the pact;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hinc aemulatio ducibus: Caecina ut foedum ac maculosum, ille ut tumidum ac vanum inridebant.
examples.translation: This caused rivalry between the generals. Caecina made sport of Valens as a shameful and disgraceful character;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Calatia et Sora praesidiaque quae in his Romana erant expugnata et in captivorum corpora militum foede saevitum.
examples.translation: Calatia and Sora with their Roman garrisons were taken by assault, and the captured soldiers were treated with shameful rigour.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: at length, at last, not till then; just, precisely; only, etc.
Latin: Post tempus longum, in fine; tandem
Latin: Sōlus in catēgoriā; sōlum, tantum, modo

examples.original: Molaribus demum fracta saxis est.
examples.translation: It was finally destroyed by rocks equal in size to millstones.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Oportet me sedere: tunc demum sedeo.
examples.translation: Or suppose that I ought to seat myself;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tum demum Ariovistus partem suarum copiarum, quae castra minora oppugnaret, misit. Acriter utrimque usque ad vesperum pugnatum est.
examples.translation: Then at last Ariovistus sent a part of his own forces to attack the lesser camp, and both sides fought in spirited fashion till eventide.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: name of a Roman gens: e. g. M. and D. Junius Brutus.—Hence
Latin: Gens Romana
Latin: Qui ad gentem Iuniam pertinet

examples.original: Dixit iuratus P. Titius, tutor pupilli Iunii;
examples.translation: It has been told on oath by Publius Titius, guardian of young Iunius.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Papirius C. Iunium Bubulcum magistrum equitum dixit;
examples.translation: Papirius named Gaius Junius Bubulcus master of the horse.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Arpineius et Iunius, quae audierunt, ad legatos deferunt.
examples.translation: Arpineius and Junius reported what they heard to the lieutenant-generals.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: Neutr., to be black
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Non opus est exhortatione, ne consilio quidem, ut colorum proprietates oculus intellegat, a nigro album etiam nullo monente distinguet.
examples.translation: There is no need of encouragement, or even of counsel, for the eye to be able to distinguish different colours;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the commander of a century, a captain, centurion, occupying a station below the tribunus

examples.original: Interim ut piaculum obicitur centurio Crispinus.
examples.translation: In the meantime the centurion Crispinus was offered as a scapegoat.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Discribitur in tribus populus, in centurias exercitus.
examples.translation: The people are divided into tribes, the army into centuries.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His rebus cognitis exploratores centurionesque praemittit, qui locum idoneum castris deligant.
examples.translation: Upon this information Caesar sent forward scouts and centurions to choose a fit place for the camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a Roman prænomen (abbrev. Ti.); as, Ti. Sempronius Gracchus, Ti. Claudius Asellus, Ti. Claudius Nero.—

examples.original: Nec multo post diem obiit, utroque liberorum superstite, Tiberio Drusoque Neronibus.
examples.translation: Not long afterward he died, survived by both his sons, Tiberius Nero and Drusus Nero.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tiberius Nero advenientem ex Hispania cum ingentibus copiis Hasdrubalem, prius quam Hannibali fratri coniungeretur, oppressit.
examples.translation: Tiberius Nero crushed Hasdrubal, on his arrival from Spain with a vast army, before he could unite with his brother Hannibal.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: In castris tiro etiam tum propter nimiam vini aviditatem pro Tiberio ”Biberius,” pro Claudio ”Caldius,” pro Nerone ”Mero” vocabatur.
examples.translation: Even at the outset of his military career his excessive love of wine gave him the name of Biberius, instead of Tiberius, Caldius for Claudius, and Mero for Nero.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: weight, heaviness.

examples.original: Non est praetereunda gravitas Lacedaemoniorum hoc loco;
examples.translation: We must not fail to observe the deliberateness of the Lacedaemonians on this occasion.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

examples.original: Erat enim in illo viro comitate condita gravitas, nec senectus mores mutaverat.
examples.translation: For there was in him a dignity tempered with courtesy, and age had not altered his disposition;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Concinnus deinde et elegans huius, Aristo, sed ea quae desideratur a magno philosopho gravitas in eo non fuit;
examples.translation: Lyco’s pupil Aristo is polished and graceful, but has not the authority that we expect to find in a great thinker;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: that cannot speak, without speech, mute, speechless (class.)

examples.original: Infans sine dentibus est: huic constitutioni suae conciliatur.
examples.translation: The child is toothless, and he is fitted to this condition.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sic infantibus quoque animalibusque principalis partis suae sensus est non satis dilucidus nec expressus.
examples.translation: Thus even children and animals have a consciousness of their primary element, but it is not very clearly outlined or portrayed.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hoc tam perplexum et subtile et vobis quoque vix enarrabile quomodo infans intellegit?
examples.translation: But how can a child comprehend this intricate and subtle principle, which I can scarcely explain even to you?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a. [1. cedo]; lit., to stand back very much; hence, to be remiss in any thing, to delay, loiter, or, in gen., to cease from, stop, give over
Latin: Cedere ab opere illudque intermittere
Latin: Desistere ab agendo, nihil agere

examples.original: Cum per totum diem stetissent intenti ad certamen, nocti cessere.
examples.translation: And they, on their side, were full of hope, as they ate their evening meal;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et quando ego vobis pro tantis vestris in me meritis gratiam referam, si nunc cessavero?
examples.translation: And when shall I show gratitude for your great kindnesses to me, if I am backward now?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cessat omne studium et liberalia professi sine ulla frequentia desertis angulis praesident.
examples.translation: You need not wonder that diseases are beyond counting: count the cooks! All intellectual interests are in abeyance;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to retain, keep something in existence, to hold up, maintain, to preserve, leave unhurt or safe (class.; esp. freq. in prose).
Latin: Habere aliquem ut servatum

examples.original: Conseruere manus et multo bracchia nexu;
examples.translation: They locked hands and arms in manifold embrace;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Iuravit autem uterque se sine dolo indutias conservaturum.
examples.translation: The two parties took oath that they would loyally observe the armistice.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

examples.original: Sic conservatis suis rebus, Poenus illusis Cretensibus omnibus, ad Prusiam in Pontum pervenit.
examples.translation: Thus he saved his goods, and having tricked all the Cretans, the Carthaginian joined Prusias in Pontus.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

definitions: English: to explain, expound, interpret, give expression to, translate; to understand, conclude

examples.original: Nam si ea vocabula interpretemur, Namphamo quid aliud significat quam boni pedis hominem?
examples.translation: If we interpret those words, what does Namphamo mean but ”the man with the lucky foot”?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Quod responsum cum ipsi aliter interpretarentur, Iunius Brutus, qui cum his profectus erat, prolapsum se simulavit et terram osculatus est;
examples.translation: This response the princes themselves explained otherwise, but Junius Brutus, who had accompanied them, pretended to fall upon his face, and kissed the earth.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nimio otio ingenia natura infirma et muliebria et inopia verae iniuriae lascivientia his commoventur, quorum pars maior constat vitio interpretantis.
examples.translation: And it is generally the pampered and prosperous who indulge in them; for if a man is pressed by worse ills, he has not time to notice such things.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to be favorable, to be well disposed or inclined towards

examples.original: Nunc mihi, siquando, puer et Cytherea, favete, Nunc Erato, nam tu nomen amoris habes.
examples.translation: Now, if ever, favour me, Cytherea and thy Boy! and thou, Erato, for thy name is a name of Love.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Non arma nec muros nec bello utilia molitur, paci favet et genus humanum ad concordiam vocat.
examples.translation: It is not wisdom that contrives arms, or walls, or instruments useful in war;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nam ut non dicam nulla, certe non magna culpa meus error veritati favet, si recte in te potest veritas favere mendacio.
examples.translation: For a mistake on my part that favours truth is, I will not say no fault at all, but certainly no serious fault, if in you the truth can rightly favour lying.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: strolling about, rambling, roving, roaming, wandering, unfixed, unsettled, vagrant (freq. and class.; syn. errabundus).

examples.original: Habet inconstantiam, sed minus vagam ac mobilem.
examples.translation: He has inconstancy, but not the kind that is very capricious or easily set in motion.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hinc montes natura vagis circumdedit undis, Qui Libyae te, Nile, negent;
examples.translation: From this point Nature has surrounded the wandering stream with mountains, which rob Libya of the Nile;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Illud autem vide, ne ista lectio auctorum multorum et omnis generis voluminum habeat aliquid vagum et instabile.
examples.translation: Be careful, however, lest this reading of many authors and books of every sort may tend to make you discursive and unsteady.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to swim, float.
Latin: In aqua fluitāre, per aquam excurrere
Latin: nāvigāre

examples.original: In classem cadit omne nemus;
examples.translation: Cohorts are raised to their full strength with recruits;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Quid fodis inmeritis, Phineu, sua lumina natis?
examples.translation: Why piercest thou, O Phineus, the eyes of thine innocent sons?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hic aures, alius spiramina naris aduncae Amputat;
examples.translation: The arms, wrenched from the shoulders, fell to the ground;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: an eager stretching, a straining, exertion of the powers of body or mind, tension, effort, a vigorous struggling or striving for something, a struggle after

examples.original: Fit magna contentione diversum proelium.
examples.translation: In different parts of the field a fierce struggle began;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Omnis est enim de virtutis dignitate contentio.
examples.translation: For the whole dispute turns on the true worth of virtue.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quare noli me ad contentionem vestrum vocare, Laterensis.
examples.translation: Do not, therefore, Laterensis, challenge me to institute a comparison between you.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Quintius, a Roman gens

examples.original: Collega ei T. Quinctius datur.
examples.translation: For colleague they gave him Titus Quinctius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Itaque se dictatorem L. Quinctium dicturum;
examples.translation: He would therefore name Lucius Quinctius dictator;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Census deinde actus et conditum ab Quinctio lustrum.
examples.translation: The census was then taken and Quinctius solemnized the concluding purification.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: spotted, covered, or stained with blood, bloody.

examples.original: Tum quoque cruentus in suos.
examples.translation: At the same time he was bloodthirsty towards his own family;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Litore constiterant: illic quoque pulchra Calypso Exigit Odrysii fata cruenta duci.
examples.translation: They stood upon the shore; there also fair Calypso inquired the cruel fate of the Odrysian chief.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Otho cruento adhuc foro per stragem iacentium in Capitolium atque inde in Palatium vectus concedi corpora sepulturae cremarique permisit.
examples.translation: He was then carried through the heaps of dead bodies, while the forum still reeked with blood, first to the Capitol and then to the Palatine;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to cast away, to throw away, throw down.
Latin: Iacere a se

examples.original: Id quod referendum est, effundit atque abicit.
examples.translation: That for which he should make return he wastes and loses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque abicio legem: morem Cluentio gero: tibi tamen, Acci, pauca, quae ab huius causa seiuncta sunt, respondebo.
examples.translation: For there is an aspect of this case which Cluentius thinks to be his concern;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque cum Oppianicum iam perditum et duobus iugulatum praeiudiciis videret, promissis suis eum excitavit abiectum et simul saluti desperare vetuit.
examples.translation: And so, seeing Oppianicus already lost and with two previous verdicts like millstones round his neck,c he raised his drooping spirits, bidding him not despair of success.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: high ground, a hill (opp. mons and campus)
Latin: Parvus mons

examples.original: Duxit via in editum leniter collem.
examples.translation: Their road led up a gentle acclivity.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Colle tumet modico lenique excrevit in altum Pingue solum tumulo;
examples.translation: The fertile land rises in a hill of moderate height and ascends with easy slope;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nunc desuper Alpis Nubiferae colles atque aeriam Pyrenen Abripimur.
examples.translation: Next I am spirited away over the cloud-capped Alps and soaring Pyrenees.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to make an objection against, in statement or reply; to decline, reject, refuse, be reluctant or unwilling to do a thing, etc. (freq. and class.; cf.: abnuo, renuo, denego)

examples.original: Nihil recusatur; tempus et locus convenit.
examples.translation: No objection was raised, and time and place were agreed on.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Senatoriam dignitatem recusantibus equestrem quoque ademit.
examples.translation: If any refused senatorial rank, he took from them that of knight also.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nullum laborem recusant manus, quae ad arma ab aratro transferuntur;
examples.translation: The hand which turns from the plough to the sword never objects to toil;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: divination by observing the flight of birds, augury from birds, auspices (cf. augurium).

examples.original: Penes quos igitur sunt auspicia more maiorum?
examples.translation: Who then control the auspices, by the tradition of our fathers?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Omnia quae quisquam in illo contubernio locutus est, unius ductu et auspiciis dicta sunt.
examples.translation: In that brotherhood, everything that any man utters is spoken under the leadership and commanding authorityd of one alone.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Terrebatur ad hoc evidentibus portentis somniorum et auspiciorum et ominum, cum veteribus tum novis.
examples.translation: In addition he was frightened by manifest portents from dreams, auspices and omens, both old and new.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a show, sight, spectacle (class.).
Latin: Quidquid spectandum obiicitur, et saepe dicitur de re, quae non modo attentionem sed admirationem excitat
Latin: fabula, lūdus, vel alter genus oblectāmentī; extrāōrdināria excitāns exhibitiō

examples.original: Avertere omnes ab tanta foeditate spectaculi oculos.
examples.translation: All eyes were turned away from so dreadful a sight.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nihil vero tam damnosum bonis moribus quam in aliquo spectaculo desidere.
examples.translation: But nothing is so damaging to good character as the habit of lounging at the games;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non immerito inter spectacula ab eo edita et Tiridatis in urbem introitum rettulerim.
examples.translation: I may fairly include among his shows the entrance of Tiridates into the city.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to shake, quake, quiver, tremble, etc. (freq. and class.; cf. trepido): sapiens si algebis, tremes, Novat. ap.

examples.original: At miseranda parens suprema neque oscula legit, Frigida nec fovit membra tremente sinu;
examples.translation: But thy unhappy mother neither imprinted her last kisses nor cherished the cold limbs in her trembling bosom;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ipsa regit trepidum Pallas dextraque trementem Perseos aversi Cyllenida derigit harpen, Lata colubriferi rumpens confinia colli.
examples.translation: Pallas herself directed Perseus in his haste; her right hand guided the shaking scimitar of the Cyllenian which he held with his face averted;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ostendat ex constitutione vulgi beatos in illo invidioso fastigio suo trementes et adtonitos longeque aliam de se opinionem habentes quam ab aliis habetur.
examples.translation: He should point out persons, happy in the popular estimation, who totter on their envied heights of power, who are dismayed and hold a far different opinion of themselves from what others hold of them.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: some, several
Latin: Aliquo numero; pauci, nonnulli

examples.original: Hic non tam discipulos quam sectatores aliquot habuit.
examples.translation: He had a few followers, rather than pupils;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Munera gladiatoria partim in amphitheatro Tauri partim in Saeptis aliquot edidit, quibus inseruit catervas Afrorum Campanorumque pugilum ex utraque regione electissimorum.
examples.translation: He gave several gladiatorial shows, some in the amphitheatre of Taurus and some in the Saepta, in which he introduced pairs of African and Campanian boxers, the pick of both regions.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Erant in Romana iuventute adulescentes aliquot, nec ii tenui loco orti, quorum in regno libido solutior fuerat, aequales sodalesque adulescentium Tarquiniorum, adsueti more regio vivere.
examples.translation: This licence they missed, now that all enjoyed equal rights, and they had got into the way of complaining to each other that the liberty of the rest had resulted in their own enslavement.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to go among several things, so as no longer to be perceived (class.).
Latin: pereo

examples.original: Utque ferunt caesos sex cum Damasicthone fratres, Intereat tecum sic genus omne tuum.
examples.translation: And as they say his six brethren perished with Damasichthon, so may all thy race perish with thee.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sed propera, ne vela cadant auraeque residant: Ut fragilis glacies, interit ira mora.
examples.translation: But be speedy, lest the sails sink and the breezes fail: like brittle ice, so perishes anger by delaying.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quod si indiligentiores fuerint, milia hominum delecta octoginta una secum interitura demonstrat.
examples.translation: He showed them that if they proved indifferent eighty thousand chosen men were doomed to perish with him.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: uplifted, high, lofty, exalted, elevated

examples.original: Sed me nec sanguis nec tantum volnera nostri Adfecere senis, quantum gestata per urbem Ora ducis, quae transfixo sublimia pilo Vidimus;
examples.translation: But the blood and wounds of our aged sire moved me less than the carrying of his head through the city: I saw it borne aloft on a pike driven through it;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sapiens adsectatorque sapientiae adhaeret quidem in corpore suo, sed optima sui parte abest et cogitationes suas ad sublimia intendit. Velut sacramento rogatus hoc, quod vivit, stipendium putat.
examples.translation: The wise man, the seeker after wisdom, is bound closely, indeed, to his body, but he is an absentee so far as his better self is concerned, and he concentrates his thoughts upon lofty things.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to make hard, to harden (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; not in Cic.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Vero tenor permanet, falsa non durant.
examples.translation: It is indeed consistency that abides;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quare quaedam dura patiuntur? Ut alios pati doceant;
examples.translation: It is that they may teach others to endure them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Illic et iuvenes votis oblivia poscunt, Et siqua est duro capta puella viro.
examples.translation: There youths seek oblivion for their vows, and maidens under the spell of a heartless lover.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a torch, firebrand, flambeau, link, orig. of pine or other resinous wood.
Latin: Frustum ligni, ut pinus, taedae, laricis etc., cera aut oleo inunctum, aut etiam per se solum; vel alterius materiae igni concipiendo aptae, ad lumen faciendum ignemque circumferendum

examples.original: His de rebus si quid geri volueris, certum hominem ad eum mittas face, cum quo conloquatur.”
examples.translation: If you desire to consider this proposal, see that you send him a trustworthy man with whom he may confer.”
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

examples.original: Lentulus, destinatum familiae suae Sibyllinis versibus regnum sibi vaticinans, ad praestitutum a Catilina diem urbe tota viros, faces, tela disponit.
examples.translation: Lentulus, prophesying for himself the kingship which the Sibylline verses foretold should belong to his family, disposed throughout the city men, torches and arms ready for the day prearranged by Catiline.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Bellvm Civile Svb Lepido III, 23Marco Lepido Quinto Catulo consulibus civile bellum paene citius oppressum est quam inciperet: sed quantulacumque fax illius motus ab ipso Sullae rogo exarsit.
examples.translation: The Civil War under Lepidus 23. In the consulship of Marcus Lepidus and Quintus Catulus, a civil war which arose was suppressed almost as soon as it began.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to take wholly, to seize entirely (cf. occupo).

examples.original: Idem immortali memoria percepta retinebat beneficia;
examples.translation: He had besides an unfailing memory for kindnesses received;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Non minor, inquit, voluptas percipitur ex vilissimis rebus quam ex pretiosissimis.
examples.translation: As much pleasure, he says, is derived from the cheapest things as from the most costly.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed vobis voluptatum perceptarum recordatio vitam beatam facit, et quidem corpore perceptarum;
examples.translation: But with you it is the recollection of pleasures enjoyed that gives happiness;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: therefore, for that cause, on that account

examples.original: Nam diligi et carum esse iucundum est propterea quia tutiorem vitam et voluptatum pleniorem efficit.
examples.translation: For esteem and affection are gratifying, because they render life safer and fuller of pleasure.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: An forte propterea non habes unde reddas quod dare iussi sunt rebaptizatores, dum multum erogas, ut emas quos rebaptizes?
examples.translation: Or perhaps you have no money with which to pay the fine imposed on those who re-baptize, after your great expenses in bribing people to accept re-baptism?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Quippe etenim primum terrai corpora quaeque, propterea quod erant gravia et perplexa, coibant in medio atque imas capiebant omnia sedes;
examples.translation: For in plain fact firstly all the bodies of earth, being heavy and entangled, came together in the midst and all took the lowest place;
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: to take, give, or bring out or forth, to produce (freq. and class.; syn.: profero, effero)

examples.original: Nunc iubent Etruscos probra iacere, nunc armati sibi quisque lingua promptum hostem offerri.
examples.translation: Now—they all cried—now, when they were armed, let the lip-bold enemy face them!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quis autem, vir modo et erectus ad honesta, non est laboris adpetens iusti et ad officia cum periculo promptus?
examples.translation: Who, moreover, if he is a man and intent upon the right, is not eager for reasonable toil and ready for duties accompanied by danger?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Erat tum in castris inter primores iuvenum Cn. Marcius,4 adulescens et consilio et manu promptus, cui cognomen postea Coriolano fuit.
examples.translation: There was in camp at that time amongst the young nobles Gnaeus Marcius, a youth of active mind and ready hand, who afterwards gained the surname of Coriolanus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a. [pro-facio], to go forward, advance, gain ground, make progress.

examples.original: Si imperio proficitur, et admonitione;
examples.translation: If commands are helpful, so is advice.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Caesarem arbitrari profectum in Italiam;
examples.translation: He believed that Caesar had started for Italy;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Horum illa nihil fecit nam et in Macedoniam profecta est et ibi crudelissime se gessit.
examples.translation: She adopted neither of these recommendations; for she proceeded to Macedonia and conducted herself there most cruelly.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: a drug, remedy, physic, medicine, medicament.
Latin: Res ad morbos vulnerave medicandum adhibita; res medicina

examples.original: Quod si tum indicatum non esset, non huic aerumnosissimo venenum illud fuisset, sed multorum medicamentum maerorum: postremo etiam fortassis mater exsequias illius funeris prosecuta mortem se filii lugere simulasset.
examples.translation: For if it had not then come to light it would have been to my suffering client no poison but the healing balm of many woes.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: by chance, by accident, at random, without design, intent, or purpose, casually, fortuitously, rashly, heedlessly, thoughtlessly, inconsiderately, indiscreetly, etc.

examples.original: Victores quoque, quod non temere alias in civilibus bellis, pace contenti fuerunt.
examples.translation: The victors were content with restoring peace, a thing which has rarely happened in civil wars.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Is Valentem comiter exceptum, ne Galliam Narbonensem temere ingrederetur, monendo terruit;
examples.translation: He received Valens kindly, and persuaded him by his advice not to risk entering Narbonese Gaul.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Multitudo hostium, nulli rei praeterquam numero freta et oculis utramque metiens aciem, temere proelium iniit, temere omisit;
examples.translation: The hostile multitude, relying on numbers only and measuring both armies with their eyes, recklessly began the fight and as recklessly gave it up;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a flock, herd, drove, swarm (cf.: armentum, jumentum, pecus).
Latin: numerus rerum vel hominum, qui inter se cōnsortiōnem habent; turma
Latin: numerus parvarum animalium; praesertim ovium, caprorum, vel avium
English: the palm of the hand.
Latin: Planum illus, et ex parte concavum in manu
Latin: Arbor, cuius fructus dactylus dicitur
English: a fever.
Latin: Status aegrotus, in quo corpori calor enormis est
Latin: Dea Romana febris

examples.original: Illae pestes non minus graves sunt, famem dico et sitim et praecordiorum subpurationes et febrem viscera ipsa torrentem.
examples.translation: Those other troubles are of course not less serious; I mean hunger, thirst, ulcers of the stomach, and fever that parches our very bowels.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Sicilian
Latin: Siciliae

examples.original: Triumviri ad coloniam Ardeam deducendam creati Agrippa Menenius T. Cloelius Siculus, M. Aebutius Helva;
examples.translation: As triumvirs for establishing the colony at Ardea they appointed Agrippa Menenius, Titus Cloelius Siculus, Marcus Aebutius Helva.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ora ferox Siculae laxavit Mulciber Aetnae Nec tulit in caelum flammas, sed vertice prono Ignis in Hesperium cecidit latus.
examples.translation: In Sicily fierce Mulciber opened wide the mouths of Etna; nor did he lift its flames skyward, but the lire bowed its crest and fell on the Italian shore.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: At enim solum id est, ut me Siculi maxime velint: alterum illud, credo, obscurum est, a quo Verres minime se accusari velit.
examples.translation: The other point is, By whom does Verres particularly wish not to be prosecuted? That no doubt is a very hard point to settle!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a tower
Latin: Alta domus, palatium, arx

examples.original: Portis fores altioresque turres imposuit.
examples.translation: At the gateways he set doors and higher turrets.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quibus fortiter resistentibus vineas turresque egit.
examples.translation: When they offered a brave resistance he brought up mantlets and towers.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Non vivunt contra naturam qui pomaria in summis turribus serunt? Quorum silvae in tectis domuum ac fastigiis nutant, inde ortis radicibus quo inprobe cacumina egissent?
examples.translation: Or raise waving forests upon the roofs and battlements of their houses—the roots starting at a point to which it would be outlandish for the tree-tops to reach?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a raised heap of earth, a mound, hill, hillock (freq. and class.; cf.: agger, moles).

examples.original: Calones in proximum tumulum procurrunt.
examples.translation: The camp-followers dashed forward to the nearest rise.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Planities erat magna et in ea tumulus terrenus satis grandis.
examples.translation: There was a large plain, and in it a mound of earth of considerable size.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Colle tumet modico lenique excrevit in altum Pingue solum tumulo;
examples.translation: The fertile land rises in a hill of moderate height and ascends with easy slope;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: nearly, almost, about; (with negatives) hardly ever

examples.original: Caesa ibi milia hominum duo ferme atque octingenti, capta quattuor milia ducenti septuaginta.
examples.translation: There about two thousand eight hundred men were slain and four thousand two hundred and seventy made prisoners.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Haec monendo obtestandoque prope restitantes consules in contionem pertraxerunt. Ibi orationes longiores habitae in eandem ferme sententiam in quam inter paucos certatum verbis fuerat.
examples.translation: Thus admonishing and entreating them they dragged the all but resisting consuls to the place of assembly.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Conspecta et ex muris Aquiloniae ea multitudo erat iamque etiam legionariae cohortes sequebantur; ceterum nec pedes fugientes persequi potuit et ab equite novissimi agminis ducenti ferme et octoginta interfecti;
examples.translation: But the infantry could not overtake the fugitives, though the cavalry killed some two hundred and eighty of the rear-guard, who in their fright abandoned a quantity of arms and eighteen military standards.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: habit, state, or condition of body, state of health, health, whether good or bad.

examples.original: Color egregius, integra valetudo, summa gratia;
examples.translation: He had excellent health and a sound constitution.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Corpore et statura fuit grandi, aquilo colore, facie rusticana, valetudine varia;
examples.translation: He was tall and of full habit, with a dark complexion and a rustic appearance.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Munus vigiliarum senatores, qui per aetatem ac valetudinem poterant, per se ipsi obibant;
examples.translation: The watchmen’s duty was performed by those of the senators themselves whose years and strength admitted of it;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a Roman prænomen, abbreviated T.
Latin: Praenomen virile Romanum
Latin: Septimus decimus Novi Testamenti Christiani liber: Ad Titum epistula Pauli apostoli (solum tribus capitulis composita est)

examples.original: Aquilium et in Ti. Guttam video esse subscriptum.
examples.translation: Aquilius and Ti. Gutta.a What does that tell us?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ex hac liberos tulit Titum et Domitianum et Domitillam.
examples.translation: By her he had three children, Titus, Domitian, and Domitilla.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Titus Vinius quinquaginta septem annos variis moribus egit.
examples.translation: Titus Vinius lived fifty-seven years; his character varied at different times.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: inward, inner

examples.original: Ecce Ocriculum, ecce Grumentum, ecce Faesulae, ecce Carseoli, Aesernia, Nuceria, Picentia penitus ferro et igne vastantur.
examples.translation: Lo! Ocriculum, Grumentum, Faesulae, Carseoli, Aesernia, Nuceria and Picentia were utterly laid waste by fire and sword.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Inest hoc tempore haud obscurum odium atque id insitum penitus et inustum animis hominum amplissimorum: dissident principes: captatur occasio.
examples.translation: At the present time hatred does more than merely rankle; it is engrained and inured in the souls of our proudest;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to drive together to a place, to collect, assemble

examples.original: Hoc crimine in contione ab inimicis compellabatur. Sed instabat tempus ad bellum proficiscendi.
examples.translation: It was this charge that was brought against him by his enemies in the public assembly.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Alcibiades

examples.original: Nulla adeo suspicio, nullus auctor tam levis exstitit, a quo non mediocri scrupulo iniecto ad cavendum ulciscendumque compelleretur.
examples.translation: No suspicion was too trivial, nor the inspirer of it too insignificant, to drive him on to precaution and vengeance, once a slight uneasiness entered his mind.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nec mirum, quod inconstans variusque ex discordi cibo morbus est et illa ex contrariis naturae partibus in eundem compulsa redundant.
examples.translation: And no wonder, that diseases which result from ill-assorted food are variable and manifold; there must be an overflow when so many unnatural combinations are jumbled together.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a going out, egress (ante-class.): exitium antiqui ponebant pro exitu; nunc exitium pessimum exitum dicimus, Paul. ex

examples.original: Ira militum in Tampium Flavianum incubuit, nullo criminis argumento, sed iam pridem invisus turbine quodam ad exitium poscebatur: propinquum Vitellii, proditorem Othonis, interceptorem donativi clamitabant.
examples.translation: The soldiers’ wrath fell on Tampius Flavianus, of whose guilt there was not the slightest proof; but the troops already hated him and now in a whirlwind of rage demanded his death.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a Roman magistrate, of whom there were two, chosen orig. every five, and afterwards every one and a half years, who at first only had the charge of the Roman people and their

examples.original: Censores ab re appellati sunt.
examples.translation: They were called censors from their function.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Lustrum a censoribus conditum est.
examples.translation: The lustrum, was closed by the censors.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ap. Claudius censor aquam perduxit;
examples.translation: Appius Claudius the censor completed an aqueduct;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to dip, dip in, immerse; absol. also to plunge into water, to sink.
Latin: (Transitīvē) in liquorem immittere
Latin: submergere in liquidum

examples.original: Quis omnia in uno mersa et materia inerti convoluta discreverit?
examples.translation: Do you compel me to withdraw from the whole and restrict me to a part?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Urebant montana nives camposque iacentes Non duraturae conspecto sole pruinae, Atque omnis propior mergenti sidera caelo Aruerat tellus hiberno dura sereno.
examples.translation: The mountains were nipped by snow, and the low-lying plains by hoar frost that would vanish at first sight of the sun;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Si Venerem Cous nusquam posuisset Apelles, Mersa sub aequoreis illa lateret aquis.
examples.translation: If Coan Apelles had never painted Venus, she would still be lying hid in the sea’s depths.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a piece of money, a coin, money.
Latin: elementum pecūniae; metallo disculus factus; monēta

examples.original: Sedecim dico iudices, ut Oppianicus absolveretur, corrumpendos fuisse: ad Staienum sescenta quadraginta milia nummum esse delata.
examples.translation: I depose that, to secure the acquittal of Oppianicus sixteen jurors would have had to be bribed: 640,000 sesterces were paid to Staienus.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Vectigal quoque eis Campanus populus iussus pendere in singulos quotannis—fuere autem mille et sexcenti—denarios a.u.c. 415nummos quadringenos quinquagenos.
examples.translation: Moreover, the 340Campanian people were commanded to pay them each a yearly stipend—there were sixteen hundred of them—amounting to four hundred and fifty denarii.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cum esset in aedibus armarium, in quo sciret esse nummorum aliquantum et auri, noctu duos conservos dormientes occidit in piscinamque deiecit: ipse armarii fundum exsecuit, et HS . .
examples.translation: There was a safe in the house which he knew to contain a quantity of cash and of gold;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: The hinder part of a ship, the stern or poop (where also the helm was placed)
Latin: pars navis posterior est

examples.original: Cilicum per litora tutus Parva puppe fugit.
examples.translation: Now he flees unharmed along the coast of the pirates in his little vessel.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Neque enim de more carinas Extendunt puppesque levant, sed firma gerendis Molibus insolito contexunt robora ductu.
examples.translation: They built no long hulls, no high sterns, as the custom is, but joined stout planks together on unwonted lines to carry heavy structures.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Fabricavit et deceris Liburnicas gemmatis puppibus, versicoloribus velis, magna thermarum et porticuum et tricliniorum laxitate magnaque etiam vitium et pomiferarum arborum varietate;
examples.translation: He also built Liburnian galleys with ten banks of oars, with sterns set with gems, particoloured awnings, huge spacious baths, colonnades, and banquet-halls, and even a great variety of vines and fruit trees;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: to warm, keep warm (class.; esp. freq. in the transf. and trop. signif.; syn.: calefacio: faveo, studeo, adjuvo, etc.).

examples.original: Legatus legionis et fovit Verginium et infamavit;
examples.translation: As a legate of a legion he courted Verginius and then defamed him.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ne mutas quidem bestias minus alere ac fovere si quid ex progenie sua parum prosperum sit;
examples.translation: Why even the dumb brutes, if one of their young is unfortunate, do none the less cherish it and foster it.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vinius pro M. Othone, Laco atque Icelus consensu non tam unum aliquem fovebant quam alium, Neque erat Galbae ignota Othonis ac Titi Vinii amicitia;
examples.translation: Vinius favoured Marcus Otho; Laco and Icelus agreed not so much in favouring any particular person as in supporting someone other than Otho.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to keep off or away, to hold back, to hold at a distance. In the comic writers and Cic. this verb is in most cases purely active, hence constr. with aliquem
Latin: Teneo ab aliquem
Latin: (intransitive) Se abstinere

examples.original: Et iam ne tergo quidem abstinebatur;
examples.translation: And now they ceased even to respect a man’s person;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ac ne principum quidem virorum insectatione abstinuit;
examples.translation: He did not even refrain from gibes at men of distinction;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Ii, quorum pedes dolor repetit, aut vino aut balineo abstinent.
examples.translation: Those whose feet are visited by pain abstain either from wine or from the bath.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: alive, living, that has life.
Latin: In statu vivendi

examples.original: Quam bene vivas refert, non quam diu;
examples.translation: The point is, not how long you live, but how nobly you live.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et hi mortem timent, in quam se vivi condiderunt?
examples.translation: Do these men fear death, if they have buried themselves alive?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Opillia virgo Vestalis ob incestum viva defossa est.
examples.translation: Opillia, a Vestal Virgin, was buried alive for unchastity.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: An engine for hurling missiles.

examples.original: Tormenta abesse a me velim;
examples.translation: I should prefer to be free from torture;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quanto plus tormenti tanto plus erit gloriae.
examples.translation: But the greater his torture is, the greater shall be his glory.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Deinde etiam tormentorum fortis patientia optabilis est.
examples.translation: And, lastly, because a brave endurance even under torture is desirable.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a blossom, flower.
Latin: pars florens herbae
Latin: Pars pulchrissima, recentissima, altissima, vel electissima cuiusquam

examples.original: Quid florum in consulem profuderunt!
examples.translation: What flowers they showered upon the consul!
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: O flores non plane fructuum sed spinarum!
examples.translation: Flowers indeed, but promising thorns, certainly not fruit!
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Id ex similitudine floris lilium appellabant.
examples.translation: Eight rows of this kind were dug, three feet apart.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: name of a Roman family in the gens Caecilia

examples.original: Exilium Metellus fortiter tulit, Rutilius etiam libenter;
examples.translation: Exile was endured by Metellus with courage, by Rutilius even with gladness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quanta fuit in L. Caecilio Metello, quanta in A. Atilio Calatino!
examples.translation: How great was the influence of Lucius Caecilius Metellus!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Omnia erant Metelli eius modi ut non tam suam praeturam gerere quam istius praeturam retexere videretur.
examples.translation: All his actions were such that he seemed less to be doing his own work as praetor than undoing the work of his predecessor.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: rich, oily wine (= plenum)

examples.original: Colle tumet modico lenique excrevit in altum Pingue solum tumulo;
examples.translation: The fertile land rises in a hill of moderate height and ascends with easy slope;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a mortar

examples.original: Piso igitur hoc modo, vir optimus tuique, ut scis, amantissimus;
examples.translation: So said Piso, an excellent man and, as you know, a devoted friend to yourself.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Liviam Orestillam C. Pisoni nubentem, cum ad officium et ipse venisset, ad se deduci imperavit intraque paucos dies repudiatam biennio post relegavit, quod repetisse usum prioris mariti tempore medio videbatur.
examples.translation: At the marriage of Livia Orestilla to Gaius Piso, he attended the ceremony himself, gave orders that the bride be taken to his own house, and within a few days divorced her;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Facete M. Piso familiaris noster et alia multa et hoc loco Stoicos irridebat.
examples.translation: Our friend Marcus Piso was often witty, but never more so than when he ridiculed the Stoics on this score.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: warmth, heat, glow.

examples.original: Est etiam calor ille animo, quem sumit, in ira cum fervescit et ex oculis micat acrius ardor;
examples.translation: The mind has also that heat, which it takes on when it boils in wrath and fire flashes more fiercely from the eyes;
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: a Roman cognomen in the gens Caecilia, Domitia, Egnatia, etc.
Latin: Qui tempus parvum longe movetur, rapidus

examples.original: Sed celeriora prope omnia imperio erant;
examples.translation: But everything was almost sooner done than ordered;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tam celer adsiduos explevit cursus honores;
examples.translation: So swiftly did thy career fill office after office;
examples.author: Claudian
examples.work: Panegyric On The Consulship Of Fl. Manlius Theodorus (A.D. 399)

examples.original: Quo simul ventum est, praeco ad tribunum celerum, in quo tum magistratu forte Brutus erat, populum advocavit.
examples.translation: No sooner were they there than a crier summoned the people before the Tribune of the Celeres, which office Brutus then happened to be holding.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To stop behind, keep back, stand still

examples.original: Papirio ad Saepinum maior vis hostium restitit.
examples.translation: Papirius, before Saepinum, had a larger body of the enemy still to reckon with.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed tolli me de medio puta et post mortem nihil ex homine restare;
examples.translation: But suppose that I am utterly annihilated, and that after death nothing mortal remains;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Restat ergo ut iste pecuniae turpissimus appetitus ex obliquo in clericos et maxime in episcopum dirigatur.
examples.translation: It remains, then, that your charge of a most sordid lust for money is indirectly levelled at the clergy, and especially at the bishop.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: That cannot be believed, incredible, extraordinary, unparalleled (class.)
Latin: Qui non credi potest (dicitur modo de rebus)

examples.original: Quid incredibile, quid novum evenit?
examples.translation: What can happen that is beyond belief?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Est haec divina atque incredibilis virtus imperatoris. Quid?
examples.translation: Such is his superhuman and unbelievable genius as a commander.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: O di immortales, incredibilem avaritiam singularemque audaciam!
examples.translation: God help us, what incredible greed, what matchless impudence!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to overwhelm, overthrow, strike down; to cover, cover over with any thing; also to hide in the ground, bury by heaping over (class.; cf.: opprimo, subruo).

examples.original: Rapum autem arboris, antequam obruat, radit.
examples.translation: These are of necessity still soft;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Civiline parum est bello, si meque meorque Obruit?
examples.translation: Is civil war still unsatisfied, if it destroy me and mine?
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nec vero quemquam senem audivi oblitum, quo loco thesaurum obruisset.
examples.translation: I certainly never heard of any old man forgetting where he had hidden his money!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make a thing like another; to imitate, copy, represent a thing

examples.original: Simulat his se rebus confidere;
examples.translation: He does indeed pretend that it is here his confidence lies;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: At quae cum posset cogi, non tacta recessit, Ut simulet vultu gaudia, tristis erit.
examples.translation: But she who, when she might have been compelled, departs untouched, though her looks feign joy, will yet be sad.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fugae quoque, quae simulanda erat, eadem equestris pugna causam minus mirabilem dedit.
examples.translation: For the flight, too, which had next to be feigned, the cavalry engagement afforded a favourable pretext.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of a smooth tongue, flattering, fawning, caressing (class and very freq.).

examples.original: Scis, quam multa mala blanda sint.
examples.translation: You know how seductive many evils are.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Venit ad me pro amico blandus inimicus.
examples.translation: An enemy comes to me full of compliments, in the guise of a friend.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quis sapiens blandis non misceat oscula verbis?
examples.translation: Who that is wise would not mingle kisses with coaxing words?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: good taste, i. e. good sense, discernment, discretion, prudence, intelligence (class.; syn. prudentia): pellitur e medio sapientia, vi geritur res, Enn. ap.

examples.original: Quid est usus sapientiae? Sapere;
examples.translation: And wherein consists the use of wisdom?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quomodo hoc fiat, sapientia sola monstrabit.
examples.translation: And wisdom alone can show you how this may be done.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Oculorum, inquit Plato, est in nobis sensus acerrimus, quibus sapientiam non cernimus;
examples.translation: The sense of sight, says Plato, is the keenest sense we possess, yet our eyes cannot behold Wisdom;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a defending, defence.

examples.original: Numera quam multa in ista defensione falsa sint, Piso.
examples.translation: Count the flaws in that argument, Piso!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: O causam singularem! o defensionem miseram ac perditam!
examples.translation: What an amazing position, what a miserable and hopeless line of defence!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In quo quae vestra defensio futura sit coniectura assequi non queo.
examples.translation: And here I cannot guess what your line of defence is to be.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to trust confidently in something, confide in, rely firmly upon, to believe, be assured of

examples.original: Simulat his se rebus confidere;
examples.translation: He does indeed pretend that it is here his confidence lies;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ego vero non gravarer, si mihi ipse confiderem, nam et praeclara res est et sumus, ut dixit Fannius, otiosi.
examples.translation: I certainly should raise no objection if I felt confidence in myself, for the subject is a noble one, and we are, as Fannius said, free from public business.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Spes maior esset salutis, si praeter te nemo esset impurus: plures sunt: hoc et tu tibi confidis magis et nos prope iure diffidimus.
examples.translation: We should have better assurance of well-being if none save you were tainted: but there are others; and this fact, which increases your confidence, makes us, almost justly, less confident.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the hair.

examples.original: Nam timor unus erat, facies non una timoris: Pars laniat crines, pars sine mente sedet;
examples.translation: For their fear was one, but not one was the appearance of their fear: some tear their hair, some sit crazed;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nec tibi turpe puta crinem, ut Phylleïa mater, Solvere, et effusis colla reflecte comis.
examples.translation: Nor think it unbecoming to loose your hair, like the Phylleian mother, and bend back your neck amid flowing tresses.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Exspectate, dum vobis singulis, ut olim Coriolano, matres coniugesque crinibus passis obviae ab urbe veniant!
examples.translation: Wait until to each of you—as once to Coriolanus —your mothers and wives come forth from the City with dishevelled hair.
examples.author: Livy
