definitions: English: to stretch or spread out before one's self, to put forth, reach out, extend (class.; syn. extendo).

examples.original: Nunc ad cotidianam stipem manum porrigis.
examples.translation: Now you are stretching forth your hand for the daily gift.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to place one's self anywhere, to stand still, stand, halt, stop, make a stop (very freq. and class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Inbecilli fluvidique inter vana constitimus ;
examples.translation: We are weak, watery beings standing in the midst of unrealities;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Valitudo ei neque corporis neque animi constitit.
examples.translation: He was sound neither of body nor mind.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Non est magnus pumilio, licet in monte constiterit;
examples.translation: A dwarf is not tall, though he stand upon a mountain-top;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a marriage, wedding, nuptials.

examples.original: Atque harum nuptiarum conciliator fuit—non est enim celandum—M. Antonius, triumvir rei publicae constituendae.
examples.translation: And the one who arranged the marriage (we must admit it) was Marcus Antonius, one of the triumvirs for reorganizing the government;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Nobilis superior iudicio matris esse, quae quam splendidissimis nuptiis iungi puellam volebat: tutores in ea quoque re partium memores ad suum tendere.
examples.translation: The guardians, mindful even in a matter like this of political interests, held out for their fellow plebeian.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ac vix uno interposito die confecit nuptias, non repertis qui sequerentur exemplum, excepto libertino quodam et altero primipilari, cuius nuptiarum officium et ipse cum Agrippina celebravit.
examples.translation: And he married her with hardly a single day’s delay; but none were found to follow his example save a freedman and a chief centurion, whose marriage ceremony he himself attended with Agrippina.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: the name of a Roman gens. Esp.

examples.original: Tarquinius Superbus occiso Tullio regnum invasit.
examples.translation: Tarquinius Superbus slew Tullius and seized the kingship.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Servius Tullius Veientes devicit et populum in classes divisit, aedem Dianae dedicavit.
examples.translation: Servius Tullius conquered the Veientes and divided the people into classes; dedicated a temple to Diana.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His duobus, ut ante dictum est, duae Tulliae regis filiae nupserant, et ipsae longe dispares moribus.
examples.translation: These two, as has been said before, had married the two Tullias, daughters of the king, themselves of widely different characters.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: wild, bold, courageous, warlike, spirited, brave, gallant, savage, headstrong, untamable, fierce, insolent
Latin: Indomitus, non domesticus; violentus perquam; ferus
Latin: Nimius superbia habens; arrogāns, superbus, īnsolēns

examples.original: Ite feroces Caesaris in iugulum;
examples.translation: Go forth, all of you, bravely against Caesar’s life;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Si ille acer est et ferox, concitari gradum?
examples.translation: That a keen and confident soul quickens the step?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Foedus Lucanis provolvitur ursus ab antris, Quid nisi pondus iners stolidaeque ferocia mentis?
examples.translation: From his Lucanian den waddles forth the ugly Bear,—what save sluggish weight and stolid fierceness?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: of or belonging to former times, of many years ago
Latin: vetus, antiquus

examples.original: Hic L. Tarquinius—Prisci Tarquini regis filius neposne fuerit parum liquet;
examples.translation: This Lucius Tarquinius—whether he was the son or the grandson of King Tarquinius Priscus is uncertain;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Dictatorem dici Q. Servilium placet, cui Prisco alii, alii Structo fuisse cognomen tradunt.
examples.translation: It was resolved that Quintus Servilius, whose surname some give as Priscus, others as Structus, should be appointed dictator.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Lex vetusta est, priscis litteris verbisque scripta, ut qui praetor maximus sit idibus Septembribus clavum pangat;
examples.translation: There is an ancient law, recorded in archaic words and letters, that the chief magistrate shall on the thirteenth of September drive a nail;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to mistrust, suspect (class.).

examples.original: Nam quid quisquam suspicari aliud potest?
examples.translation: For what else but theft could anyone suspect?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Mater misera nihil mali suspicans mittit.
examples.translation: His poor mother sent him without a suspicion of harm;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tale itaque aliquid et in hoc esse suspicor, quod prima specie pulchrum atque magnificum est, nec iniuriam nec contumeliam accepturum esse sapientem.
examples.translation: And so I suspect that something of this sort lurks behind this maxim also, ’A wise man will receive neither injury nor insult’—a maxim which, at first sight, appears noble and splendid.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to make a low roaring, to roar, resound, to growl
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; ŭi, ĭtum, 3

examples.original: Et primo fremitus fuit aspernantium imperium;
examples.translation: They had indeed murmured at first, and had flouted the order;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quorum timor cum fremitu et concursu significaretur, milites nostri pristini diei perfidia incitati in castra irruperunt.
examples.translation: When their alarm was betrayed by the uproar and bustle, our troops, stung by the treachery of the day before, burst into the camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ceterum postquam ibi neque stationes pro portis nec quemquam in vallo nec fremitum consuetum castrorum animadverterunt, insolito silentio moti metu insidiarum subsistunt.
examples.translation: But not perceiving any outposts before the gates or anybody on the rampart, and missing the usual noises of a camp, they were troubled by the unaccustomed silence, and apprehending an ambush, halted.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to make one thing equal to another; constr. with
Latin: Efficere aliquid aequalem alii esse
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Et hoc, quod dico ”possit,” tale est: amissum aequo animo fert.
examples.translation: When I say ”can,” I mean this: he endures the loss of a friend with equanimity.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ut fuerit torva violentior illa Medusa, Fiet amatori lenis et aequa suo.
examples.translation: Though she be more violent than grim Medusa, she will be mild and gentle to her lover.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Si cui virtus animusque in corpore praesens, hic deos aequat, illo tendit originis suae memor.
examples.translation: He in whose body virtue dwells, and spirit E’er present,a is equal to the gods;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that knows something in company with others or by himself, knowing with others or self-knowing (freq. in all periods and species of composition).

examples.original: Huius rei conscius mihi sum;
examples.translation: I fully understand what this task is.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: At is et ex serrula insimulatus et a puero conscio est indicatus.
examples.translation: But he was incriminated by the saw and denounced by the boy, his accomplice.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Et soror et mater valeant et conscia nutrix, Et quisquis dominae pars erit ulla tuae.
examples.translation: Bid farewell to mother and sister, and to the nurse her confidant, and to whoever will be any part of your mistress.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: nowhere, in no place.
Latin: Nullo loco

examples.original: Cum esset annorum XVI, amicitia coepit uti Annaei Cornuti ita ut nusquam ab eo discederet;
examples.translation: When he was sixteen years old he became so intimate a friend of Annaeus Cornutus that he never left his side;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

examples.original: Id modo non conveniebat, quod senatus consulesque nusquam alibi spem quam in armis ponebant, plebes omnia quam bellum malebat.
examples.translation: In this one point they were unable to agree, that the senate and the consuls saw no hope anywhere but in arms, while the plebs preferred anything to war.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Apud Xenophontem autem moriens Cyrus maior haec dicit: ”nolite arbitrari, o mihi carissimi filii, me, cum a vobis discessero, nusquam aut nullum fore.
examples.translation: Again, in Xenophon, Cyrus the Elder utters the following words as he is dying: ”Think not, my dearest sons, that, when I have left you, I shall cease to be.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the last but one of the twelve celestial signs, Firm. Math. 2, 19: melior, Jul. Val. Res gest. A. M. 1, 27.—
Latin: Vis divina; genius sive bonus, sive malus
Latin: daemonium, genius malus; anima minor vel semidivina, praesertim, in religione Christiana, anima mala

examples.original: Execranda autem superstitio ligaturarum, in quibus etiam inaures virorum in summis ex una parte auriculis suspensae deputantur: non ad placendum hominibus sed ad serviendum daemonibus adhibentur.
examples.translation: It is an accursed superstition to wear amulets,a among which must be reckoned also the earringsb that men wear on the top part of the ear on one side;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to make clear, to show, prove, make known, declare, assert

examples.original: Quis tum posset arguere ab Oppianico temptatum esse iudicium pecunia?
examples.translation: Who could then have shown that it was Oppianicus who corrupted the court?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: A. Terentius, alter testis, non modo Aebutium sed etiam se pessimi facinoris arguit.
examples.translation: The second witness, Aulus Terentius, charges not only Aebutius but himself with a heinous crime.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Multa sunt eius modi: verum cum habeam rem non dubiam, sed apertam atque manifestam, enumeratio singulorum argu mentorum non est necessaria.
examples.translation: There are many such arguments; but when my case is not a doubtful one but clear and obvious, I do not need to rehearse my proofs one by one.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: divide

examples.original: Si mala bonaque non populo auctore distinxeris.
examples.translation: Simply by distinguishing between good and bad things without patterning your opinion from the populace.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Aliud est enim poetarum more verba fundere, aliud ea quae dicas ratione et arte distinguere.
examples.translation: A poetic out-pouring of language is one thing, the systematic and scientific marshalling of one’s matter is another.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quidam ita distinxerunt, ut dicerent: ”Temperans ac prudens positione quidem mentis et habitu tranquillus est, eventu non est.
examples.translation: For it is easier to keep a thing out than to keep it under after you have let it in.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To cause to stand, place, = colloco, pono; II. To stand, be placed, = sto.
Latin: ponere
Latin: stare facere, quod erat in cursu aut motu

examples.original: Sic huius, ut caelestium, stata magnitudo est.
examples.translation: Her stature, like that of the stars in the heavens, is fixed.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Per ista ad perfectum animi statum pervenitur.
examples.translation: It is by such methods that we arrive at a perfect condition of mind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Corpore et statura fuit grandi, aquilo colore, facie rusticana, valetudine varia;
examples.translation: He was tall and of full habit, with a dark complexion and a rustic appearance.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

definitions: English: to the measure or limit (scarcely found in the poets, except the comic poets)

examples.original: Ipsum erat oppidum Alesia in colle summo admodum edito loco, ut nisi obsidione expugnari non posse videretur;
examples.translation: The actual stronghold of Alesia was set atop of a hill, in a very lofty situation, apparently impregnable save by blockade.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Deinde non quaerimus quid obscuretur aut intereat quia sit admodum parvum, sed quid tale sit ut expleat summam.
examples.translation: In the life of pleasure of which we spoke, one pleasure is lost to sight among the many;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Qua in re admodum fuit militum virtus laudanda, qui vectoriis gravibusque navigiis non intermisso remigandi labore longarum navium cursum adaequarunt.
examples.translation: And herein was the spirit of the troops much to be commended, who, in the heavily built transports, by uninterrupted effort of rowing kept level with the men-of-war.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to disturb, stir, agitate, move; to distress, harass, make uneasy

examples.original: Nemo autem sollicito bono fruitur;
examples.translation: No man, however, enjoys a blessing that brings anxiety;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Oratio sollicita philosophum non decet;
examples.translation: A meticulous manner of writing does not suit the philosopher;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Inde ob residuas bellorum iras maxime sollicitatis ad defectionem animis voluntarios traxere, et apud vagos quosdam ex inopi plebe etiam merces valuit.
examples.translation: There the resentment left over from the wars was the strongest incentive to revolt, and procured them some volunteers; while with certain vagrant and poverty-stricken plebeians even the prospect of pay was effectual.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: one by one, one at a time
Latin: Ad singulum pertinens

examples.original: O illam mirabilem laudem et singularem!
examples.translation: What wonderful and rare distinction!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In omnibus rebus singulari fuit industria;
examples.translation: In all lines he was a man of extraordinary activity;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Cato

examples.original: O di immortales, incredibilem avaritiam singularemque audaciam!
examples.translation: God help us, what incredible greed, what matchless impudence!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: over against, opposite to (cf.: adversus, versus, contra, e regione, e contrario).

examples.original: Sermo erga patrem imperatoremque reverens, de se moderatus;
examples.translation: He answered with the reverence due to a father and an emperor;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Fuit morum lenissimorum, verecundiae virginalis, formae pulchrae, pietatis erga matrem et sororem et amitam exemplo sufficientis.
examples.translation: He was very gentle in manner, of virginal modesty and very handsome; and he showed an exemplary devotion to his mother, sister, and aunt.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

examples.original: Ut terrorem Italiae possessa Mevania ac velut renatum ex integro bellum intulerat, ita haud dubium erga Flavianas partis studium tam pavidus Vitellii discessus addidit.
examples.translation: While the occupation of Mevania had terrified Italy and had seemed to start a new war, it was also true that the timid retreat of Vitellius had increased the favourable feeling toward the Flavian party.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: by little and little, by degrees, gradually (syn. sensim).

examples.original: Caesar Locus erat castrorum editus et paulatim ab imo acclivis circiter passus mille.
examples.translation: The position of the camp was on high ground, with a gradual slope from the bottom of about a mile.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Interim, dum de condicionibus inter se agunt longiorque consulto ab Ambiorige instituitur sermo, paulatim circumventus interficitur.
examples.translation: While they two were discussing terms together, and Ambiorix was purposely making a longer speech than necessary, Titurius was gradually surrounded and slain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Horum vocibus ac timore paulatim etiam ei, qui magnum in castris usum habebant, milites centurionesque quique equitatui praeerant, perturbabantur.
examples.translation: By the cowardly utterances of such as these even men who had long experience in the field, soldiers, centurions, and cavalry commanders, were gradually affected.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: defender

examples.original: Hunc Venus e templis, quae sunt confinia, ridet: Qui modo patronus, nunc cupit esse cliens.
examples.translation: Venus laughs at him from her neighbouring shrine: he who was of late an advocate would fain be a client now.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hoc consilio a L. Metello legationes universae petiverunt ut quam primum isti succederet; hoc animo totiens apud patronos de suis miseriis deplorarunt;
examples.translation: This was the purpose of the entreaty made by all their deputations to Lucius Metellus, that he would take over the government from Verres at the earliest possible moment;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Verum id mihi non sumo, iudices, et hoc non modo in oratione mea non pono, sed ne in opinione quidem cuiusquam relinquo, me omnibus patronis esse praepositum.
examples.translation: I will not say so in this speech, and I will not even allow anyone to think so, for it is not true.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Straightforwards, right onwards, straight, direct (post-Aug.)
Latin: directe
Latin: simpliciter

examples.original: Quod enim vis, ut ad te prolixam epistulam scribam, et hoc quidem debeo, fateor; debeo prorsus hoc tam dulci, tam sincerae, tam merae voluntati tuae.
examples.translation: Yet, when you want me to write you a lengthy letter, I do indeed owe you that, I must confess: I surely do owe that to your sweet, sincere, and single-minded desire.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: dust, powder: jamque fere pulvis ad caelum vasta videtur, Enn. ap.
Latin: Multitudo mimimorum corpusculorum

examples.original: Omnia ista in longa vita sunt, quomodo in longa via et pulvis et lutum et pluvia.
examples.translation: I will touch the truth more closely, and say that you feared for your life.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Pulveris exigui sparget non longa vetustas Congeriem, bustumque cadet, mortisque peribunt Argumenta tuae.
examples.translation: For a short space of time will scatter the little heap of dust; the grave will fall in;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Vix proelia Caesar Senserat, elatus specula quae prodidit ignis: Invenit inpulsos presso iam pulvere muros, Frigidaque, ut veteris, deprendit signa ruinae.
examples.translation: Caesar had hardly been aware of the fighting; the news of it was conveyed to him by a fire-signal from a lofty tower.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to pour out or forth, to shed copiously, to cause to flow (class.).

examples.original: Quid florum in consulem profuderunt!
examples.translation: What flowers they showered upon the consul!
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Saeva quies pelagi, maestoque ignava profundo Stagna iacentis aquae;
examples.translation: A grim stillness broods over the dismal deep;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed profusa cupidine et insigni temeritate legati legionum Alienus Caecina et Fabius Valens;
examples.translation: But the commanders of the legions, Alienus Caecina and Fabius Valens, were men of boundless greed and extraordinary recklessness.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: Of or belonging to an enemy, hostile.
Latin: Qui ad hostem pertinet
Latin: Se ut hostis gerens, inimicus

examples.original: Cernit tabe iecur madidum, venasque minaces Hostili de parte videt.
examples.translation: He saw the liver flabby with corruption and with boding streaks in its hostile half.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Se tamen, utcumque sit, etiam nunc paenitere sua sponte Aequos quam pati hostilia malle.
examples.translation: If they did so, they could count on a safe refuge in the clemency they had already proved;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Gratias agimus et ducibus vestris et exercitibus, quod oculis magis quam auribus crediderunt, et ubi nihil hostile erat ne ipsi quidem fecerunt.
examples.translation: We give thanks to your commanders and your armies, since they have believed their eyes more than their ears, and where they encountered no hostility, themselves have showed none.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: not to be able, to be unable, I cannot (class.).

examples.original: Corpora si nequeunt, quae possunt, nomina tangunt, Famaque non tacto corpore crimen habet.
examples.translation: If bodies escape them, they take hold of names, and though the body escape, the name retains the charge.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Illud in his rebus minime mirabile habendumst, cur, ea quae feriant oculos simulacra videri singula cum nequeant, res ipsae perspiciantur.
examples.translation: But in this regard it should not be thought at all wonderful why the objects themselvesa are per ceived, and yet the images that strike our eyes cannot be seen singly.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Quod superest, non est mirandum qua ratione, per loca quae nequeunt oculi res cernere apertas, haec loca per voces veniant aurisque lacessant.
examples.translation: To proceed: there is no need to wonder how pass voices pass and assail the ears through places through which the eves cannot see plain objects.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: unrestrained joyfulness, gladness, pleasure, delight (cf.: gaudium, hilaritas).

examples.original: Immo contra nolo tibi umquam deesse laetitiam.
examples.translation: I do not wish you ever to be deprived of gladness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tum victi victoresque in lacrimas effusi, sortem civilium armorum misera laetitia detestantes;
examples.translation: Then vanquished and victors alike burst into tears, cursing, amid their melancholy joy, the fate of civil war.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sed cum ea quae praeterierunt acri animo et attento intuemur, tum fit ut aegritudo sequatur si illa mala sint, si bona, laetitia.
examples.translation: But when we fix our mental vision closely on the events of the past, then sorrow or gladness ensues according as these were evil or good.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a being born, birth; hence, transf.
Latin: actus pariendi, partus
Latin: Constitutio innata et naturalis, genus, praesertim

examples.original: Mithridates autem et suam manum iam confirmarat, et magnis adventiciis auxiliis multorum regum et nationum iuvabatur.
examples.translation: Mithridates meanwhile had rallied his own following and was aided by large bodies of foreign auxiliaries from many kings and peoples.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ac ne inermes provinciae barbaris nationibus exponerentur, principes Sarmatarum Iazugum, penes quos civitatis regimen, in commilitium adsciti.
examples.translation: To avoid exposing the provinces in their unprotected condition to barbarous nations, the ruling chiefs of the Sarmatian Iazuges were called into service with the army.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Caesar Quoniam ad hunc locum perventum est, non alienum esse videtur de Galliae Germaniaeque moribus et quo differant hae nationes inter sese proponere.
examples.translation: Since I have arrived at this point, it would seem to be not inappropriate to set forth the customs of Gaul and of Germany, and the difference between these nations.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a prayer, request, entreaty (class.).

examples.original: Hectora donavit Priamo prece motus Achilles;
examples.translation: Entreaty moved Achilles to give Hector back to Priam;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sed alii aversabantur preces aut verecundia aut metu;
examples.translation: But some turned away from the petitioner, through either embarrassment or fear;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Haec tibi, quem meritis precibus mea devovet ira, Evenient, aut his non leviora malis.
examples.translation: Such ills shall befall thee whom my anger execrates with merited curses, or ills no less than these!
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to make firm or fast, to strengthen, fortify, support (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Sed hoc, quod liquet, firmandum et altius cotidiana meditatione figendum est;
examples.translation: This idea, however, clear though it is, must be strengthened and implanted more deeply by daily reflection;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In utrumque enim monendi ac firmandi sumus, et ne nimis amemus vitam et ne nimis oderimus.
examples.translation: For we need to be warned and strengthened in both directions,—not to love or to hate life overmuch;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quinque cohortes, quas minime firmas ad dimicandum esse existimabat, castris praesidio relinquit;
examples.translation: He left as garrison for the camp the five cohorts which he regarded as least steady for action;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: one who approaches another (from unlawful or criminal love), an adulterer or adulteress

examples.original: Quaeritur, Aegisthus quare sit factus adulter?
examples.translation: Is it asked why Aegisthus became an adulterer?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Aut pia te caeso dicatur adultera, sicut Qua cecidit Leucon vindice, dicta pia est.
examples.translation: Or may an adulteress be called righteous for slaying thee, as she was called righteous by whose vengeance Leucon fell.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Concussa statim flagitio domus: pro marito studia civitatis, pro adultero libido reginae et saevitia.
examples.translation: Her house was at once shaken by this scandalous act. Her husband was favoured by the sentiments of all the citizens;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to disclose wholly, lay open (a fact), without the access. idea of communicating the thing disclosed (which aperio expresses; v. aperio)

examples.original: Huic ille quid ex litteris comperisset aperit.
examples.translation: The youth told him what he had learned from the letter.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

examples.original: Eum autem, cum modo regressus sum, periculosissime scandalizatum comperi de absentia mea;
examples.translation: When I returned recently, I found them offended to a very dangerous degree at my absence.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Aut illud adferant, aliquid sese, quod de his duobus habuerint compertum, de ceteris non comperisse.
examples.translation: Or else let them allege that they had discovered against those two something which they had not discovered against the others.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: The gullet, the alimentary canal, œsophagus

examples.original: Decessit autem vitio stomachi anno aetatis XXX.
examples.translation: He died of a stomach trouble in the thirtieth year of his age.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

examples.original: Illa tuas redolent, Phineu, medicamina mensas: Non semel hinc stomacho nausea facta meo est.
examples.translation: Such drugs smell of your table, Phineus; not once only has my stomach grown queasy at them.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quis autem negaverit haec acria quoque et habentia austeritatis aliquid stomachum excitare?” Ego non idem sentio, mihi amicorum defunctorum cogitatio dulcis ac blanda est.
examples.translation: To me, the thought of my dead friends is sweet and appealing. For I have had them as if I should one day lose them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to look forward or into the distance, to look out, to look
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; exi, ectum, 3

examples.original: Quidquid consilio prospici potest, prospice.
examples.translation: Be sure to foresee whatever can be foreseen by planning.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In hoc enim fallimur, quod mortem prospicimus;
examples.translation: For we are mistaken when we look forward to death;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Prospectu tenebris adempto multa utrimque vulnera accipiuntur.
examples.translation: As the darkness made it impossible to see far, many wounds were received on both sides.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the upper

examples.original: Laetus fragor aethera pulsat Victorum;
examples.translation: A shout from his conquerors made the welkin ring;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Tum, ne qua futuri Spes saltem trepidas mentes levet, addita fati Peioris manifesta fides, superique minaces Prodigiis terras inplerunt, aethera, pontum.
examples.translation: Then, that no hope even for the future might relieve anxiety, clear proof was given of worse to come, and the menacing gods filled earth, sky, and sea with portents.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: high, elevated, lofty, steep (syn.: altus, celsus, sublimis).
Latin: Qui paene directe sublimen eminet

examples.original: Locus erat arduus atque in parte una praeceps, ubi nunc Narnia sita est, nec vi nec munimento capi poterat.
examples.translation: It was a steep place and on one side precipitous—the site is now occupied by Narnia—and could be captured neither by assault nor by siege operations.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quod in magnis evenit montibus, quorum proceritas minus apparet longe intuentibus; cum accesseris, tunc manifestum fit, quo in arduo summa sint;
examples.translation: This phenomenon is seen in the case of high mountains, which appear less lofty when beheld from afar, but which prove clearly how high the peaks are when you come near them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Pompeio vincite, Parthi, Vinci Roma volet.’” Regem parere iubenti Ardua non piguit, positisque insignibus aulae Egreditur famulo raptos indutus amictus.
examples.translation: If the Parthians conquer for Pompey’s sake, Rome will welcome her conqueror.’” Hard was the task enjoined, but the king did not refuse;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to call
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Ad haec visa auditaque clamor ingens oritur.
examples.translation: The sight of these things and the man’s recital produced a mighty uproar.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Clamabat, flebatque simul, sed utrumque decebat;
examples.translation: She clamoured and wept together, but both became her;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Clamare omnes ex conventu neminem umquam in Sicilia fuisse Verrucium.
examples.translation: The whole audience shouted that there had never been in Sicily anyone called Verrucius.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to lead one away, to take or bring with one, to carry off, take or bring away, remove, etc.
Latin: Alio ducere

examples.original: Ita exercitus inde domos abducti.
examples.translation: The armies then marched home.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Dux deerat abducto Verginio per simulationem amicitiae;
examples.translation: But they had no leader, for Verginius had been taken away under the cloak of friendship.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Interdicis mihi inspectione rerum naturae, a toto abductum redigis in partem?
examples.translation: He is so trained that he neither loves nor hates life;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to take out, take away, remove (class.; syn.: demo, adimo, eripio, furor, etc.).

examples.original: Quod enim morti tempus exemptum est?
examples.translation: For what season of our life is exempt from death?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Catulus se ignis haustu ludibrio hostium exemit.
examples.translation: Catulus saved himself from the insults of his enemies by swallowing fire.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: At cum istud exemeris malum, omnis mutatio loci iucunda fiet;
examples.translation: That trouble once removed, all change of scene will become pleasant;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to bind, to bind or wind about; to fetter
Latin: Ligare, constringere

examples.original: Non dico, in his omnibus vincitur.
examples.translation: I do not say that man is surpassed in all these qualities.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Secuti alium ducem sequimini nunc Camillum et quod ductu meo soletis vincite.
examples.translation: You have followed another leader: follow now Camillus, and, as your habit is when I am leading, conquer.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tela iugo vincta est, stamen secernit harundo, Inseritur medium radiis subtemen acutis, Quod lato paviunt insecti pectine dentes.
examples.translation: The web is bound to frame; asunder now The reed doth part the warp.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: theft, robbery (class. and freq.; syn.: latrocinium, raptum).

examples.original: Hoc ipso fere tempore Strato ille medicus domi furtum fecit et caedem eius modi.
examples.translation: About that very time, this Strato, the doctor, committed theft and murder at her house in the following circumstances.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nos etiam veros parce profitemur amores, Tectaque sunt solida mystica furta fide.
examples.translation: As for me I recount even true amours but sparely, and a solid secrecy hides my dark intrigues.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sed melius nescisse fuit: sine furta tegantur, Ne fugiat ficto fassus ab ore pudor.
examples.translation: But ignorance were better: allow deceptions to be hid, lest the shame of confession fly from her dissembling countenance.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: daily, every day
Latin: Omni die

examples.original: Quisquis dixit ”vixi,” cotidie ad lucrum surgit.
examples.translation: When a man has said: ”have lived!”, every morning he arises he receives a bonus.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Qui hoc modo se aptavit, cui vita sua cotidie fuit tota, securus est;
examples.translation: He who has thus prepared himself, he whose daily life has been a rounded whole, is easy in his mind;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ariovistus his omnibus diebus exercitum castris continuit, equestri proelio cotidie contendit.
examples.translation: On all these days Ariovistus kept his army in camp, but engaged daily in a cavalry encounter.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the sending of an ambassador; hence, the office of an ambassador, an embassy, legation.
Latin: Actus legandi, legatorum missio
Latin: Munus et officium legati

examples.original: Qua legatione perlata praetor eorum Annius de Capitolio ita lapsus est ut exanimaretur.
examples.translation: After delivering these terms, their praetor Annius fell from the Capitol, and so lost consciousness.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum cives Romani, qui Lampsaci negotiabantur, concurrunt; orant Lampsacenos ut gravius apud eos nomen legationis quam iniuria legati putaretur;
examples.translation: They set to work battering the front door with stones and iron implements, and made a pile of logs and brushwood round it which they set on fire.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ei legationi Ariovistus respondit: Si quid ipsi a Caesare opus esset, sese ad eum venturum fuisse; si quid ille se velit, illum ad se venire oportere.
examples.translation: To the deputation Ariovistus made reply that if he had had need of aught from Caesar, he would have come to him, and if Caesar desired aught of him, he ought to come to him.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to cause to repent, to displease (anteclass. and late Lat.)

examples.original: Se tamen, utcumque sit, etiam nunc paenitere sua sponte Aequos quam pati hostilia malle.
examples.translation: If they did so, they could count on a safe refuge in the clemency they had already proved;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec vos fidei nostrae nec nos imperii vestri paenitebit.” Camillo et ab hostibus et a civibus gratiae actae.
examples.translation: Neither shall you be disappointed in our fidelity nor we in your rule.” Camillus was thanked both by his enemies and by his fellow citizens.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Si quis collegam appellasset, ab eo ad quem venerat ita discedebat ut paeniteret non prioris decreto stetisse.
examples.translation: If anybody sought redress from another decemvir, he came away regretting that he had not accepted the decision of the first.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A projecting object, a column, pillar
English: twofold, double.
Latin: Qui duas partes in unione habet

examples.original: Huius munitionis duplex erat consilium.
examples.translation: The object of this fortification was twofold.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Sed neque iam ’duplicis’ nec iam ’sors altera partus,’ Gloria confectae nunc quoque matris, ubi es?
examples.translation: No more a ’twofold birth,’ no more ’one-half its fortune,’ yet still the glory of thy aged mother, where art thou?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ita duplici proditione et praesidium Samnitium insessis circa viam silvestribus locis necopinato oppressum est, et ab urbe plena hostium clamor sublatus;
examples.translation: Thus, in one crowded hour, the Samnites were slain and the Satricans captured, and all things brought under the power of the consul;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: Celebrity, fame, renown (very rare)

examples.original: Omnis noster equitatus, omnis nobilitas interiit;
examples.translation: All our horsemen, all our chivalry is perished;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Qui posteaquam id audivit, habuit et dignitatis et aetatis et nobilitatis suae rationem;
examples.translation: The other, on hearing this, behaved as became his rank, age, and birth.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quamquam nullam nobilitatem, nullos honores, nulla merita cuiquam ad dominationem pandere viam;
examples.translation: To be sure, no nobility, no honours, no merits, opened wide the road to tyranny for any man;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: teaching, instruction (class.; cf.: litterae, artes, disciplina, praecepta, scientia, humanitas).

examples.original: Philologi appellationem assumpsisse videtur, quia sic ut Eratosthenes, qui primus hoc cognomen sibi vindicavit, multiplici variaque doctrina censebatur.
examples.translation: And that he was such is evident from his commentaries, though very few of them survive;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Atque idem ego hoc contendo, cum ad naturam eximiam et illustrem accesserit ratio quaedam conformatioque doctrinae, tum illud nescio quid praeclarum ac singulare solere exsistere.
examples.translation: Yet I do at the same time assert that when to a lofty and brilliant character is applied the moulding influence of abstract studies, the result is often inscrutably and unapproachably noble.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: have you any thing further to say? do you want me longer? Eun. Quid? Me num quid vis?

examples.original: Numquid ultra quicquam ulli timendum est quam ut uratur, quam ut pereat?
examples.translation: Is there a worse fate that any man may fear than being burned or being killed?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Numquid accidere tibi, si damnaris, potest durius quam ut mittaris in exilium, ut ducaris in carcerem?
examples.translation: If you lose this case, can anything more severe happen to you than being sent into exile or led to prison?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Observa te itaque, numquid vestis tua domusque dissentiant, numquid in te liberalis sis, in tuos sordidus, numquid cenes frugaliter, aedifices luxuriose.
examples.translation: Observe yourself, then, and see whether your dress and your house are inconsistent, whether you treat yourself lavishly and your family meanly, whether you eat frugal dinners and yet build luxurious houses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: not enclosed within boundaries, boundless, unlimited.

examples.original: Paucis ante diebus ex his castris Atrebatem Commium discessisse ad auxilia Germanorum adducenda; quorum et vicinitas propinqua et multitudo esset infinita.
examples.translation: He further learnt that a few days before Commius the Atrebatian had left their camp to bring up succours from the Germans, whose proximity was as imminent as their numbers were infinite.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Haec non erant eius qui innumerabiles mundos infinitasque regiones, quarum nulla esset ora, nulla extremitas, ’mente peragravisset.’ Num quid tale Democritus?
examples.translation: Such a provision ill became one whose ’intellect had roamed’b over unnumbered worlds and realms of infinite space, without shores or circumference. Did Democritus do anything of the kind?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to scatter seed

examples.original: Disserebat populo Fabianus, sed audiebatur modeste.
examples.translation: Fabianus used to give popular talks, but his audience listened with self-control.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quae enim de voluptate dicuntur, ea nec acutissime nec abscondite disseruntur;
examples.translation: For pleasure is a topic that does not lend itself to very subtle or profound discussion;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Audite vero, optimi viri, ea quae saepissime inter me et Scipionem de amicitia disserebantur.
examples.translation: Then listen, most worthy gentlemen, to the points very frequently mentioned between Scipio and me in our discussions of friendship.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: unimpaired, uninjured, in good condition, still alive, safe, sound, entire, whole

examples.original: Fraus deinde rem inclinavit, quod vocem audiri praeconis passi sunt, incolumem abiturum qui arma posuisset.
examples.translation: The hope of this relaxed the tension of their courage and on every side they began throwing their arms away.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Huic rursus circumvento fert subsidium Pullo, atque ambo incolumes compluribus interfectis summa cum laude sese intra munitiones recipiunt.
examples.translation: He was surrounded in his turn, but Pullo brought assistance; and both, unhurt, though they had slain several men, retired with the utmost glory within the entrenchments.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Duo summi imperatores, Potitus a Faleriis, Camillus a Capena praedas ingentes egere nulla incolumi relicta re cui ferro aut igni noceri posset.
examples.translation: The two chief commanders, Potitus and Camillus,—one at Falerii, the other at Capena,—carried off huge spoils and left nothing untouched that iron or fire could destroy.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to declare publicly, to own freely, to acknowledge, avow, confess openly, profess (class.).

examples.original: Nos etiam veros parce profitemur amores, Tectaque sunt solida mystica furta fide.
examples.translation: As for me I recount even true amours but sparely, and a solid secrecy hides my dark intrigues.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: At haec, quae artem vitae professa est, nulla re, quo minus se exerceat, vetari potest;
examples.translation: But that artb which professes to teach the art of life cannot be forbidden by any circumstance from exercising its functions;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cessat omne studium et liberalia professi sine ulla frequentia desertis angulis praesident.
examples.translation: You need not wonder that diseases are beyond counting: count the cooks! All intellectual interests are in abeyance;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or pertaining to Athens, Athenian

examples.original: Hoc in tempore nulla civitas Atheniensibus auxilio fuit praeter Plataeenses; ea mille misit militum.
examples.translation: In that crisis no city gave help to the Athenians except the Plataeans.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

examples.original: Cum iam haud ita longe abesset a Peloponneso, obsistere ei conati sunt Athenienses et Boeotii ceterique eorum socii apud Coroneam;
examples.translation: He was already nearing the Peloponnesus, when the Athenians, the Boeotians and their allies attempted to stop him at Coronea;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

examples.original: Neque vero id satis habuit, sed etiam ut inviolatus in navem escenderet per Chabriam Atheniensem, de quo supra mentionem fecimus, effecit.
examples.translation: And he was not even satisfied with that, but through Chabrias, the Athenian, of whom I have already spoken, he saved Diomedon from being molested before he embarked.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Epaminondas

definitions: English: to bite, to bite into (class.).

examples.original: Morsu virus habent, et fatum dente minantur, Pocula morte carent.” Dixit dubiumque venenum Hausit;
examples.translation: There is no death in the cup.” He spoke and drank down the dreaded poison;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Insertum manibus chalybem nigramque per artus Stillantis tabi saniem virusque coactum Sustulit, et nervo morsus retinente pependit.
examples.translation: She purloins the nails that pierced the hands, the clotted filth, and the black humour of corruption that oozes over all the limbs;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed quem ad modum maxime mortiferi morsus solent esse morientium bestiarum, sic plus negotii fuit cum semiruta Carthagine quam cum integra.
examples.translation: But, just as the bite of a dying animal is always most deadly, even so Carthage, half destroyed, caused more trouble than when it was whole.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to stroke; to touch or move lightly

examples.original: Quem taurum metuis, vitulum mulcere solebas: Sub qua nunc recubas arbore, virga fuit: Nascitur exiguus, sed opes adquirit eundo, Quaque venit, multas accipit amnis aquas.
examples.translation: The bull you fear, you were wont to stroke as a calf; the tree under which you lie was once a sapling: a river at birth is small, but acquires force by flowing;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to break (class.; for syn. cf.: vinco, supero, devinco, fundo, fugo, profligo, subigo, subicio).
Latin: (Proprie beluas, feras, elephantos, leones) mansuefacere adeoque subigere
Latin: rem aliquam, aut homines feritate, duritia, vel contumacia resistentes vincere

examples.original: Memoriae Domiti patris honores maximos habuit.
examples.translation: He paid the highest honours to the memory of his father Domitius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Illud fortunae indulgentiam rexit, hoc violentiam domuit.
examples.translation: The one controls the favours of fortune; the other overcomes her onslaughts.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In hos domandos Vinnium misit. Caesi sunt in utrisque fluminibus.
examples.translation: Caesar sent Vinnius to subdue them, and they were defeated on both rivers.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a member of the Roman Senate, a body consisting originally of one hundred eminent citizens, selected by Romulus for their age, wisdom, and experience, out of the noblest families

examples.original: Adoptat annos viginti natus, etiam minor senatorem.
examples.translation: A man twenty years of age or even less adopts a senator.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Munus vigiliarum senatores, qui per aetatem ac valetudinem poterant, per se ipsi obibant;
examples.translation: The watchmen’s duty was performed by those of the senators themselves whose years and strength admitted of it;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In agrum senatorum coloni missi, quibus adscriptis speciem antiquae frequentiae Velitrae receperunt.
examples.translation: Colonists were settled on the senators’ lands, and on their enrolment Velitrae regained its former appearance of populousness.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: that may be trusted or relied upon, trusty, faithful

examples.original: At illud ex se ortum fidele firmumque est et crescit et ad extremum usque prosequitur;
examples.translation: But that joy which springs wholly from oneself is leal and sound; it increases and attends us to the last;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Huius opera Commi, ut antea demonstravimus, fideli atque utili superioribus annis erat usus in Britannia Caesar;
examples.translation: This Commius, as we have before mentioned, had rendered faithful and efficient service to Caesar in previous years in the expedition to Britain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quem postquam propius famulae videre fideles, Non ultra gemitus tacitos incessere fatum Permisere sibi, frustraque attollere terra Semianimem conantur eram;
examples.translation: When her faithful handmaids saw him close at hand, they dared not rail at destiny except with stifled groans, and tried in vain to lift their fainting mistress from the ground;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: death
Latin: solutio a corpore, finis vitae
Latin: excidium ac ruina rerum inanimatarum

examples.original: Nec derat robur in enses Ire duci iuguloque pati vel pectore letum;
examples.translation: He lacked not the courage to confront the swords and offer throat or breast to the fatal blow;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Fuga nulla patet, stant undique nostris Intenti cives iugulis: decernite letum, Et metus omnis abest.
examples.translation: No escape is open to us; our countrymen surround us, eager for our lives;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: bread, a loaf.
Latin: Cibus solidus, e farina et aqua subacta pistus, igni coctus

examples.original: Non habet panem meus pistor;
examples.translation: My baker is out of bread;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ad hoc panis usu carnisque coctae et dulcedine vini mitigatos Marius in tempore adgressus est.
examples.translation: When they had been further demoralized by the use of bread and cooked meat and the delights of wine, Marius opportunely approached them.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Hunc non ruricolae Panes nemorumque potentes Silvani Nymphaeque tenent, sed barbara ritu Sacra deum;
examples.translation: No rural Pan dwelt there, no Silvanus, ruler of the woods, no Nymphs;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: one who calls another to account; hence, transferred to public life, an accuser, a plaintiff, esp. in a state-offence

examples.original: Deinde accusatorem firmum verumque esse oportet.
examples.translation: In the next place, a prosecutor must show firmness and honesty.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sunt et haec et alia in te falsi accusatoris signa permulta, quibus ego nunc non utor;
examples.translation: You display all these marks of the counterfeit prosecutor, and many others besides. But I will make no use of them at present.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Plerumque improborum facta primo suspicio insequitur, dein sermo atque fama, tum accusator, tum iudex;
examples.translation: The usual consequences of crime are, first suspicion, next gossip and rumour, then comes the accuser, then the judge;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a Samnite, an inhabitant of Samnium

examples.original: Samnites nobiscum foedere iuncti sunt;
examples.translation: The Samnites and we are united by a covenant;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Id spatium Samnitibus datum est Romam legatos mittendi;
examples.translation: The Samnites thus had time to send ambassadors to Rome.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Samnitium exercitus, velut haud ulla mora pugnae futura esset, aciem instruit;
examples.translation: The Samnites, assuming that the battle would not be delayed, formed up in line;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a country in Asia, on the Mediterranean Sea
Latin: Natio in Asia occidentalis, est vicina Turciae Iracoque

examples.original: Quot oppida in Syria, quot in Macedonia devorata sunt?
examples.translation: How many towns in Syria, how many in Macedonia, have been swallowed up!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Syriam et quattuor legiones obtinebat Licinius Mucianus, vir secundis adversisque iuxta famosus.
examples.translation: Syria and its four legions were held by Licinius Mucianus, a man notorious in prosperity and adversity alike.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nec non in meridiem verso agmine Libanum Syriae Damascumque transgressus per nemora illa odorata, per turis et balsami silvas Romana signa circumtulit.
examples.translation: Furthermore, turning his army southwards, he passed through the Lebanon in Syria and through Damascus, and bore the Roman standards through the famous scented groves and woods of frankincense and balm.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a longing, ardent desire or wish, properly for something once possessed; grief, regret for the absence or loss of any thing

examples.original: Ut fortiter amissorum desideria pateremur praecepimus nobis;
examples.translation: We have taught ourselves to endure bravely the loss of those we love;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: De adventu autem ad vos nostro utrorumque desiderium deus impleat.
examples.translation: May God give fulfilment to the desire we both share, that I should visit you!
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Quod ex multorum episcoporum desiderio peto, quos mecum de hac re fama incerta perturbat;
examples.translation: This I beg at the desire of many bishops who have, like me, been troubled by the indefinite rumour about this;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a greedy desire for possessions, greediness, avarice, covetousness

examples.original: Effugit avaritiam, sed iram adhuc sentit;
examples.translation: They have escaped avarice, for example, but still feel anger;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Avaritia paupertatem intulit et multa concupiscendo omnia amisit.
examples.translation: It was avarice that introduced poverty and, by craving much, lost all.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Minus avaritiae in Caecina, plus ambitionis: Valens ob lucra et quaestus infamis eoque alienae etiam culpae dissimulator.
examples.translation: Caecina was less avaricious, but more eager for popularity; Valens, notorious for his greed and sordid gains, was more inclined to overlook the crimes of others.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to sever

examples.original: Hic exitus viri haud sane spernendi.
examples.translation: Thus died a man who was far from being despicable.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Omni acto triumpho depositus triumphus clarior fuit; adeo spreta in tempore gloria interdum cumulatior rediit.
examples.translation: The consul then solemnized, one after the other, the funerals of his colleague and his brother, and pronounced the eulogy of each;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Inde opes et rerum secundarum luxus: spreto Venutio (is fuit maritus) armigerum eius Vellocatum in matrimonium regnumque accepit.
examples.translation: She grew to despise her husband Venutius, and took as her consort his squire Vellocatus, whom she admitted to share the throne with her.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to stand apart
Latin: abesse

examples.original: Illic exiguo paulum distantia vallo Castra locant.
examples.translation: There the two camps with low ramparts were pitched not far apart.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Prima acies hastati erant, manipuli quindecim, distantes inter se modicum spatium;
examples.translation: The first line, or hastati, comprised fifteen maniples, stationed a short distance apart;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To lament, bewail, deplore: miseratur is, qui conqueritur aliena incommoda: miseretur is, qui miserum sublevat, Paul. ex

examples.original: O excubias tuas, Cn. Planci, miseras!
examples.translation: O the misery of your lonely watches, Plancius!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Mater misera nihil mali suspicans mittit.
examples.translation: His poor mother sent him without a suspicion of harm;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: At miseranda parens suprema neque oscula legit, Frigida nec fovit membra tremente sinu;
examples.translation: But thy unhappy mother neither imprinted her last kisses nor cherished the cold limbs in her trembling bosom;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a poetical appellation of Apollo as the god of light

examples.original: Vel tu venandi studium cole: saepe recessit Turpiter a Phoebi victa sorore Venus.
examples.translation: Or cultivate the pleasures of the chase: ofttimes has Venus, vanquished by Phoebus’ sister, beaten a base retreat.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hermionam Pylades quo Pallada Phoebus, amabat, Quodque tibi geminus, Tyndari, Castor, erat.
examples.translation: Pylades loved Hermione as Phoebus Pallas, and as twin Castor was to thee, O Tyndaris.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sed neque declament medio sermone diserti, Nec sua non sanus scripta poeta legat!” Sic monuit Phoebus: Phoebo parete monenti;
examples.translation: But neither let the eloquent declaim in the midst of talk, nor the frenzied poet recite his verses.” So Phoebus counselled: obey ye Phoebus’ counsels;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: long existence.
Latin: Longum decursi temporis spatium
Latin: Longinquitas temporis sive praeteriti sive futuri, duratio

examples.original: Id bonum cura, quod vetustate fit melius.
examples.translation: Cultivate that good which improves with the years.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Pulveris exigui sparget non longa vetustas Congeriem, bustumque cadet, mortisque peribunt Argumenta tuae.
examples.translation: For a short space of time will scatter the little heap of dust; the grave will fall in;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed pleni sunt omnes libri, plenae sapientium voces, plena exemplorum vetustas: quae iacerent in tenebris omnia, nisi litterarum lumen accederet.
examples.translation: All literature, all philosophy, all history, abounds with incentives to noble action, incentives which would be buried in black darkness were the light of the written word not flashed upon them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: that which preserves the remembrance of any thing, a memorial, a monument; esp. of buildings, statues, galleries, tombs erected to perpetuate the remembrance of a person or thing

examples.original: Sepultus est iuxta viam Appiam ad quintum lapidem in monumento Q. Caecilii, avunculi sui.
examples.translation: He was buried near the fifth milestone of the Appian Way in the tomb of Quintus Caecilius, his maternal uncle.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Credo, qui te in tua civitate incolumem esse nollent, hi monumenta tuae formae ac nominis in suis civitatibus esse cupiebant.
examples.translation: A likely tale, that while they would not have you go unpunished in your own country, they desired to have memorials of your appearance and illustrious name in theirs!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Monumentum illa amplitudine, illo opere, quamvis sartum tectum integrumque esset, tamen aliquid se inventurum in quo moliri praedarique posset arbitrabatur.
examples.translation: In so large and elaborate a building, even were it in sound and good repair, he calculated on finding some means of working a profitable job for himself.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an eager or furious demand, importunity, urgency

examples.original: Tu mihi, cum circumsessus a tam illustri civitate sis propter tuum scelus atque flagitium;
examples.translation: Seeing that you were beset by the people of that reputable town through your own criminal and wicked act;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Concussa statim flagitio domus: pro marito studia civitatis, pro adultero libido reginae et saevitia.
examples.translation: Her house was at once shaken by this scandalous act. Her husband was favoured by the sentiments of all the citizens;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nec ulla apud Vitellianos flagitii poena, et praemiis defectorum versa fides ac reliquum perfidiae certamen.
examples.translation: With the Vitellians there was no punishment for cowardice; those who went over to the Flavians received the rewards of their treachery;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to place by or upon each other; to pile up, arrange, etc.
Latin: Rem aliam super aliam componere

examples.original: Dictatorem dici Q. Servilium placet, cui Prisco alii, alii Structo fuisse cognomen tradunt.
examples.translation: It was resolved that Quintus Servilius, whose surname some give as Priscus, others as Structus, should be appointed dictator.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quaedam vero procul arceantur ut iam oblitterata et olentia: nullum sit verbum velut rubigine infectum, nulli sensus tarda et inerti structura in morem annalium componantur;
examples.translation: There should be never a word of the rusty, mouldy tinge, never a sentence put together in the lame and listless style of the chroniclers.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Quique bibunt tenera dulces ab harundine sucos, Et qui tinguentes croceo medicamine crinem Fluxa coloratis astringunt carbasa gemmis, Quique suas struxere pyras vivique calentes Conscendere rogos.
examples.translation: Up rose the men who drink sweet juices from soft reeds; and those who colour their hair with saffron dye and loop up their robes of cotton with brighthued gems;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Just so, in the same manner, in like manner, equally, just, even; usually with a foll.

examples.original: Proinde obsecro, ut epistulam quam eis communi nomine scripsi, subscriptam non differas mittere.
examples.translation: I beseech you, therefore, not to postpone signing and sending the letter I have written them in our common name.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Proinde ut aut de vestris futuris sociis atque amicis aut nusquam ullis futuris nobis consulite.”
examples.translation: Do you therefore deliberate regarding us, as regarding those who shall either be your allies and friends, or else have no being anywhere.”
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quaestorem se in senatu exspectare dixit: proinde quasi non, ut quaestor sine praetore possit rationem referre (ut tu, Hortensi, ut omnes), eodem modo sine quaestore praetor.
examples.translation: He told the Senate that he was waiting for his quaestor: ridiculous! a quaestor can submit accounts in his praetor’s absence—as you did yourself, Hortensius, and everyone else;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: One that is master in the liberal arts (while opifex is a master in the artes sordidae; cf. ars, I. B. 1.), an artist, artificer
Latin: Qui artem aliquam exercet
Latin: qui ad rem aliquam agendam ceteris praestat dexteritate

examples.original: Est enim artifex etiam sine istis;
examples.translation: For he is an artist even without them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Atqui ista magis inquinant animos quam corpora, et in possessore eorum quam in artifice plus sordium est.
examples.translation: And yet the stuff they handle soils the soul more than the body, and there is more foulness in the owner than in the workman.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nullos autem peius mereri de omnibus mortalibus iudico quam qui philosophiam velut aliquod artificium venale didicerunt, qui aliter vivunt quam vivendum esse praecipiunt.
examples.translation: And I hold that no man has treated mankind worse than he who has studied philosophy as if it were some marketable trade, who lives in a different manner from that which he advises.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a castle, fort, citadel, fortress, stronghold, Sisenn. ap.
Latin: Castrum, arx

examples.original: De castello descendunt, in fundum proficiscuntur.
examples.translation: Leaving the castle they set out for the estate.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Inde quinque castella locis sita munitis expugnavit.
examples.translation: He then stormed five fortresses situated in positions of great strength.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Caecina cum amicis ad diem venit in castellum Axiam; ex quo loco fundus is de quo agitur non longe abest.
examples.translation: Caecina came with his friends on the appointed day to the castle of Axia, from which the disputed estate was not far distant.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a movement, motion (as an indwelling force; cf.: motio, motus; class.).

examples.original: Iniquum loci ad declivitatem fastigium magnum habet momentum.
examples.translation: The unfavourable downward slope of the ground had great effect.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: A quo enim non prope est, parata omnibus locis omnibusque momentis?
examples.translation: It is ready for us in all places and at all times.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec neque cum ego dicerem neque cum tu negares magni momenti nostra esset oratio.
examples.translation: I might state these facts, and you might deny them; but our speeches would matter very little.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: The inner bark of a tree, used for writing-tablets: levis in aridulo malvae descripta libello (carmina), Cinna ap.

examples.original: Impia si nostros legisset Scylla libellos, Haesisset capiti purpura, Nise, tuo.
examples.translation: Had impious Scylla read my verse, the purple had stayed on thy head, O Nisus.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Et cum haec paucorum mensium ratio in his libellis sit, facite ut vobis triennii totius veniat in mentem.
examples.translation: Moreover, the return contained in these papers is for a few months only; so you must allow, gentlemen, for the full three years.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: thirty
Latin: Viginti novem et alius, ter dena. Numerus XXX

examples.original: Tullus magna gloria belli regnavit annos duos et triginta.
examples.translation: Tullus was greatly renowned in war and reigned thirty-two years.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Romulus septem et triginta regnavit annos, Numa tres et quadraginta.
examples.translation: Romulus ruled thirty-seven years, Numa forty-three.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Transeunt Rhenum navibus ratibusque triginta milibus passuum infra eum locum, ubi pons erat perfectus praesidiumque ab Caesare relictum: primos Eburonum fines adeunt;
examples.translation: On boats and rafts they crossed the Rhine thirty miles below the spot where the bridge had been built and a garrison left by Caesar;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: treasurers of State, treasurers. They distributed their duties among themselves by lot

examples.original: Quaestorum numerus ampliatus est, ut essent octo.
examples.translation: The number of quaestors was enlarged, so that there were eight.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Antonium quaestorem cum legione duodecima sibi coniungit.
examples.translation: Marcus Antonius, the quartermaster-general, with the Twelfth Legion he attached to his own force.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: In Macedonia tribunus militum fuit: in eadem provincia postea quaestor.
examples.translation: In Macedonia he was military tribune, and afterwards quaestor in the same province.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: A Persian; v. Persae.—

examples.original: Hos versus Lacedaemonii exsculpserunt neque aliud scripserunt quam nomina earum civitatum quarum auxilio Persae erant victi.
examples.translation: Those verses the Lacedaemonians erased and put in their place only the names of the cities with whose help the Persians had been defeated.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

definitions: English: to strike asunder, dash to pieces, shatter, etc.

examples.original: Sed cetera lege, cetera discute.
examples.translation: But read all the rest and examine it well.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: In hac ergo morum perversitate desideratur solito vehementius aliquid, quod mala inveterata discutiat;
examples.translation: Amid this upset condition of morals, something stronger than usual is needed,—something which will shake off these chronic ills;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Unum hercule virum—id enim plus esse quam consulem—qualis Ap. Claudius fuerit, momento temporis discussurum illos coetus fuisse.
examples.translation: One single man—a more significant word than consul—of the type of Appius Claudius, would have dispersed those assemblages in a moment.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: place around, i. e. both to wrap around (e. g. a mantle). and also to enclose

examples.original: At te Corfini validis circumdata muris Tecta tenent, pugnax Domiti;
examples.translation: But Domitius, eager for battle, lay behind strong walls in the city of Corfinium;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Hinc montes natura vagis circumdedit undis, Qui Libyae te, Nile, negent;
examples.translation: From this point Nature has surrounded the wandering stream with mountains, which rob Libya of the Nile;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Quos primo Camillus vallo circumdare et aggere atque operibus oppugnare est adortus.
examples.translation: Camillus at first set about confining them with a palisade and mound, intending to lay siege to them;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: accoutrement, equipment, furniture, trappings, etc. (class.)

examples.original: Tiberius patruus petenti honores consularia ornamenta detulit;
examples.translation: His paternal uncle Tiberius gave him the consular regalia, when he asked for office;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nam maximum ornamentum amicitiae tollit, qui ex ea tollit vere- cundiam.
examples.translation: For he who takes reverence from friendship, takes away its brightest jewel.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ornamenta consularia etiam procuratoribus ducenariis indulsit.
examples.translation: He gave the consular regalia even to the second grade of stewards.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: just so many, just as many.

examples.original: Omnibus nobis totidem ante nos sunt;
examples.translation: We have all had the same number of forefathers;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed quoniam totidem mores totidemque figurae, Non sunt iudiciis omnia danda meis.
examples.translation: What cannot offend your feelings, perhaps will be a reproach to another’s judgment.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Si bene promittent, totidem promittite verbis: Si dederint, et vos gaudia pacta date.
examples.translation: If they make fair promises, promise in as many words; if they give, give also your bargained joys.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a Roman high-priest, a pontiff

examples.original: Quod est, pontifices, ius adoptionis?
examples.translation: What, gentlemen, is the law relating to adoption?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Pontificibus bona causa visa est: approbaverunt.
examples.translation: The Pontifical College thought your reason a just one, and gave their sanction.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ita octo pontificum, novem augurum numerus factus.
examples.translation: Thus the number of pontiffs became eight and of augurs nine.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: plqpf. subj. sync. delesset
Latin: ad nihilum redigere, exstinguere
Latin: dēstruere, ēvertere

examples.original: Sic miserabili strage deletus exercitus.
examples.translation: Thus the army was destroyed in lamentable slaughter.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Deletusque exercitus foret, ni fugientis silvae texissent.
examples.translation: If the forests had not covered the flight, their army would have been utterly destroyed.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum ab incolis deserta civitas direpta primum, deinde tuba praecinente deleta est.
examples.translation: The city, deserted by its inhabitants, was first plundered and then destroyed at a signal given by trumpets.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: there, thither, to that place/point

examples.original: Huc atque illuc signa moveri ac modo in unum conferri modo educi videtis; opus quidem incipit nemo, cum iam circumdati vallo potuerimus esse.
examples.translation: You see their standards moving now this way, now that, first closing in together, then deploying, while no man falls to work, though we might ere this have been fenced in with a palisade.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Etiam illuc misi, quo dicebatur abductus, ubi memoratus officialis inventus concedere presbytero quem miseram, noluit, ut eum saltem videret.
examples.translation: When the afore-mentioned officer was found, he refused to grant to the priest I had sent permission even to see him.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Atque etiam, cum hominis natura morte dissolvitur, ceterarum rerum perspicuum est quo quaeque discedat, abeunt enim illuc omnia, unde orta sunt;
examples.translation: And even when man is dissolved by death it is evident to the sight whither each bodily element departs;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to arrive at, to reach.

examples.original: Quo in genere est in primis senectus, quam ut adipiscantur omnes optant, eandem accusant adeptam ;
examples.translation: To this class old age especially belongs, which all men wish to attain and yet reproach when attained;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Maiore adeo et favore et auctoritate adeptus est quam gessit imperium, quanquam multa documenta egregii principis daret;
examples.translation: Thus his popularity and prestige were greater when he won, than while he ruled the empire, though he gave many proofs of being an excellent prince;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Verum Claudio imperium adepto non solum paternas opes reciperavit, sed et Crispi Passieni vitrici sui hereditate ditatus est.
examples.translation: But when Claudius became emperor, Nero not only recovered his father’s property, but was also enriched by an inheritance from his stepfather, Passienus Crispus.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to throw forth or before; to fling away, throw down; to throw, thrust, drive, or

examples.original: Quid signorum, quid vestium quidve tabularum raptum incensumque atque proiectum est!
examples.translation: What a vast quantity of statues, garments and pictures was carried off, burnt, and thrown away!
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Est idem Verres qui fuit semper, ut ad audendum proiectus, sic paratus ad audiendum. Praesto est, respondet, defenditur;
examples.translation: But he is still Verres, true to his name as ever, daring the worst without hesitation, and hearing the worst without reluctance.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Patriam tutore carentem Excepit, populi trepidantia membra refovit, Ignavis manibus proiectos reddidit enses, Nec regnum cupiens gessit civilia bella Nec servire timens.
examples.translation: When his country had no guardian, he took her in charge; he revived the trembling limbs of the nation, and replaced the swords that coward hands had thrown down;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: inconvenient, unsuitable, unfit, unseasonable, troublesome, disagreeable.

examples.original: Omnia corporis aut incommoda aut pericula per me transierunt;
examples.translation: I have passed through all the ills and dangers of the flesh;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Alia condicio est in iis, quae ablata in locum suum aliquid incommodi substituunt;
examples.translation: The situation is entirely different in the case of goods whose loss entails some hardship substituted in their place;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vercingetorix tot continuis incommodis Vellaunoduni, Cenabi, Novioduni acceptis suos ad concilium convocat.
examples.translation: Having experienced three continuous reverses—at Vellaunodunum, Cenabum, and Noviodunum—Vercingetorix summoned his followers to a convention.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a strife, dispute, quarrel.
Latin: pugna, proelium, conflictus

examples.original: Hoc iudicio damnatur Timotheus lisque eius aestimatur centum talentis.
examples.translation: Timotheus was found guilty and his fine was fixed at one hundred talents.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timotheus

examples.original: Lite fugent nuptaeque viros nuptasque mariti, Inque vicem credant res sibi semper agi;
examples.translation: With quarrels let wives pursue husbands and husbands wives, and deem that they are ever at issue with each other;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: In his sic illi opus est alieno consilio quomodo medico, quomodo gubernatori, quomodo advocato et litis ordinatori.
examples.translation: He needs outside advice on such matters, as does the physician, the pilot, the attorney, or the pleader of cases.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger
