definitions: English: salt.
English: the skin.
English: to deny, disown, refuse, reject.—With
Latin: abnegare, recusare, reiicere
Latin: negare alicui ius repetendi aliquid tamquam suum

examples.original: Quinctius sexto decimo die dictatura in sex menses accepta se abdicavit.
examples.translation: On the sixteenth day Quinctius surrendered the dictatorship which he had received for six months.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His senatus consultis perfectis dimisso senatu decemviri prodeunt in contionem abdicantque se magistratu ingenti hominum laetitia.
examples.translation: Having so decreed the senate adjourned and the decemvirs went before the people and laid down their office, to the great delight of all.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nihil ex eo tempore praetermissum est ad maiestatem eius augendam ac multo magis, postquam Agrippa abdicato atque seposito certum erat, uni spem successionis incumbere.
examples.translation: From this time on nothing was left undone which could add to his prestige, especially after the disowning and banishment of Agrippa made it clear that the hope of the succession lay in him alone.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: an appellation, designation, name of any thing (cf.: nomen, vox).

examples.original: Mihi autem de vocabulo pugna non est;
examples.translation: Now I am not going to fight about a word;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ex rebus enim timiditas, non ex vocabulis nascitur.
examples.translation: Timidity springs from facts, not from words.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam si ea vocabula interpretemur, Namphamo quid aliud significat quam boni pedis hominem?
examples.translation: If we interpret those words, what does Namphamo mean but ”the man with the lucky foot”?
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to call or summon one to a place, esp. for counsel, aid, etc.; constr.

examples.original: P. Vetilius, propinquus Aebutii, se Aebutio cum armatis servis venisse advocatum.
examples.translation: Publius Vetilius, his neighbour, says that he came on the summons of Aebutius with some armed slaves.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quo simul ventum est, praeco ad tribunum celerum, in quo tum magistratu forte Brutus erat, populum advocavit.
examples.translation: No sooner were they there than a crier summoned the people before the Tribune of the Celeres, which office Brutus then happened to be holding.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In his sic illi opus est alieno consilio quomodo medico, quomodo gubernatori, quomodo advocato et litis ordinatori.
examples.translation: He needs outside advice on such matters, as does the physician, the pilot, the attorney, or the pleader of cases.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: A messenger
Latin: Nuntius
Latin: Ens caelestis et spiritalis, hominum superior potestate intellegentiaque, ut qui in sanctis scripturis dicuntur nuntios Dei esse

examples.original: Si autem pax humana tam dulcis est pro temporali salute mortalium, quanto est dulcior pax divina pro aeterna salute angelorum!
examples.translation: So let it be your necessity and not your choice that slays the enemy who is fighting against you.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: simple, plain, uncompounded, unmixed, =
Latin: Non multifarius vel multiiugus; una parte vel sine partibus

examples.original: Una enim est ratio recta simplexque.
examples.translation: For right reason is single and of but one kind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Simplicis illius verbi usus amissus est.
examples.translation: The plain word has become obsolete.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vides, quam simplex et imperiosa virtus sit;
examples.translation: You see, then, how straightforward and peremptory virtue is;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: fearful, afraid, faint-hearted, cowardly, timid (opp. audax; cf.: pavidus, trepidus, iners, ignavus): timido metu refugere, Enn. ap.

examples.original: Hinc celeriter deiecti se in signa manipulosque coniciunt: eo magis timidos perterrent milites.
examples.translation: They were speedily hurled down from thence, and ran headlong into the company formations, scaring the soldiers into greater alarm.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ut fugiunt aquilas, timidissima turba, columbae, Ut fugit invisos agna novella lupos: Sic illae timuere viros sine more ruentes;
examples.translation: As doves, most timorous of birds, flee from the eagles, as the weanling lamb from the hated wolf, so feared they the men rushing wildly on them;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Omnia pone feros (pones invitus) in ignes, Et dic ”ardoris sit rogus iste mei.” Thestias absentem succendit stipite natum: Tu timide flammae perfida verba dabis?
examples.translation: Consign them all, though unwillingly, to the fierce flames, and say, ”Let that be my passion’s funeral pyre.” Thestias burnt in the brand her absent son: will you be cowardly in burning treacherous words?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: firm
Latin: Cuius partes tam compactae sunt, vel quae tam firme inter se adhaerent, impressionem penetrationemve ab aliis corporibus resistit; cui forma fixa est; densus; firmus; compactus
Latin: Integer, totus

examples.original: Nam etiam maximum solida non receperunt;
examples.translation: For solid timbers have repelled a very great fire;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tum porro si nil esset quod inane vacaret, omne foret solidum;
examples.translation: Then further, if there were nothing void and empty, the universe would be solid;
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Bona eius solidis et inexsuperabilibus munimentis praecincta sunt.
examples.translation: His goods are girt about by strong and insurmountable defences.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: wood
Latin: Pars solida arborum, sub cortecem
English: ah! alas!

examples.original: Nititur, ut profugae desint alimenta senectae: Heu!
examples.translation: He strives that my exiled old age may lack sustenance: ah!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Dolet heu semperque dolebit, Quod scelerum, Caesar, prodest tibi summa tuorum, Cum genero pugnasse pio.
examples.translation: Grievous alas! is it, and ever will be, that Caesar profited by his worst crime—his fighting against a kinsman who had scruples.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Heu nimium felix aeterno nomine Lesbos, Sive doces populos regesque admittere Magnum, Seu praestas mihi sola fidem.
examples.translation: Ah, too happy Lesbos, and famous for ever, whether she teaches other nations and kings to harbour me or alone proves faithful to me.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: before, in front.
Latin: A fronte; ante locum
Latin: A fronte; ante; praesens

examples.original: Princeps Horatius ibat trigemina spolia prae se gerens;
examples.translation: In the van of the Romans came Horatius, displaying his triple spoils.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Prae ardore impetuque tantae rei sensus non pervenit ad militem;
examples.translation: In the ardour and enthusiasm of the soldiers so important an event passed unnoticed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Latentem discurrens forte gregarius miles, animadversis pedibus, studio sciscitandi quisnam esset, adgnovit extractumque et prae metu ad genua sibi accidentem imperatorem salutavit.
examples.translation: As he cowered there, a common soldier, who was prowling about at random, saw his feet, and intending to ask who he was, pulled him out and recognized him;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: before
Latin: (indicans statum prae alia re, quae post quam indicatur.), antequam
Latin: antequam

examples.original: Vercingetorix, priusquam munitiones ab Romanis perficiantur, consilium capit omnem ab se equitatum noctu dimittere.
examples.translation: Vercingetorix now made up his mind to send away all his horsemen by night, before the Romans could complete their entrenchments.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Egerat cum Vario, priusquam Italia decederet, ut siquid sibi accidisset, ”Aeneida” combureret; at is ita facturum se pernegarat;
examples.translation: He had arranged with Varius, before leaving Italy, that if anything befell him his friend should burn the ”Aeneid”;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Alii proelio victum Latinum pacem cum Aenea, deinde affinitatem iunxisse tradunt: alii, cum instructae acies constitissent, priusquam signa canerent processisse Latinum inter primores ducemque advenarum evocasse ad conloquium;
examples.translation: Some say that Latinus, having been defeated in the battle, made a peace with Aeneas, and later an alliance of marriage.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: rankness.

examples.original: Licet enim sine luxuria agere festum diem.
examples.translation: For one may keep holiday without extravagance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Volo luxuriam obiurgari, libidinem traduci, inpotentiam frangi.
examples.translation: I wish to see luxury rebuked, lust condemned, waywardness crushed out.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec ergo et eiusmodi vitia, quae alicui inpressit imitatio, non sunt indicia luxuriae nec animi corrupti;
examples.translation: These and similar faults, which imitation stamps upon one’s style, are not necessarily indications of loose standards or of debased mind;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to bring under, get under; bring or

examples.original: Nulli subigebant arva coloni, Ne signare quidem aut partiri limite campum Fas erat;
examples.translation: No ploughman tilled the soil, nor was it right To portion off or bound one’s property.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quae cum gremio mollito ac subacto sparsum semen excepit, primum id occaecatum cohibet, ex quo occatio quae hoc efficit nominata est;
examples.translation: And yet what I enjoy is not the fruit alone, but I also enjoy the soil itself, its nature and its power.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Eaque clade haud minus quam adversa pugna subacti Veientes pacem petitum oratores Romam mittunt. Agri parte multatis in centum annos indutiae datae.
examples.translation: They were deprived of a part of their land, and a truce was granted them for a hundred years.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: set before, to place first (syn.: praefero, praeficio).

examples.original: Adfer, quem Fabiano possis praeponere.
examples.translation: Mention someone whom you may rank ahead of Fabianus.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Stoici autem tantummodo praeponendam in seligendo, non quo beatior ea vita sit, sed quod ad naturam accommodatior;
examples.translation: Those men of old then, with their duller wits, think that the former life is more desirable, more excellent, more happy;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quoniam autem omne quod est bonum primum locum tenere dicimus, necesse est nec bonum esse nec malum hoc quod praepositum vel praecipuum nominamus;
examples.translation: But since we declare that everything that is good occupies the first rank, it follows that this which we entitle preferred or superior is neither good nor evil;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make publicly known, to publish, proclaim, announce (cf.: edico, promulgo).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Victorem autem se ipse pronuntiabat;
examples.translation: When the victory was won, he made the announcement himself;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Consulti augures vitiosum videri dictatorem pronuntiaverunt.
examples.translation: This sentence the tribunes by their accusations made suspect and infamous;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cogebantur itaque victi, quia cedentibus spei nihil erat, pugnam inire, cum pronuntiatum repente, ne quis praeter armatos violaretur, reliquam omnem multitudinem voluntariam exuit armis;
examples.translation: And so the vanquished, since they could hope for no mercy if they yielded, were compelled to fight; when suddenly the command was given that none should be hurt but those who carried weapons.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: broad, wide.
Latin: Pars corporis quae nec a fronte nec a tergo sit; margo
Latin: Cui spatium magnum est inter latera

examples.original: Lex agraria primum lata est.
examples.translation: For the first time a land-law was proposed.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Atque haec ratio late patet.
examples.translation: And this is a principle of wide application.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Aequaliter splendebit omne caeli latus;
examples.translation: The whole expanse of heaven will shine evenly;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: abuse, insult, affront, reproach, invective, contumely

examples.original: Si merito, non est contumelia, iudicium est;
examples.translation: If I do deserve them, there is no insult—it is justice;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ferro igitur eam arcere contumeliam statuunt.
examples.translation: They therefore determined to repel that insult with the sword.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cavendum vero ne etiam in gravis inimicitias convertant se amicitiae ex quibus iurgia maledicta contumeliae gignuntur.
examples.translation: And you must indeed be on your guard lest friendships be changed into serious enmities, which are the source of disputes, abuse, and invective.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To take or snatch away, esp. any thing which is in motion; to seize upon, catch

examples.original: Non enim ex praeparato locutus est, sed subito deprehensus.
examples.translation: For he spoke not from forethought, but was suddenly caught off his guard.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Medium erat tempus forte sementis, cum patricium virum innixum aratro suo lictor in ipso opere deprehendit.
examples.translation: It happened to be the middle of the season of sowing, when the lictor found the patrician actually at work bending over his plough.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nam Cluentius, iudices, primum nomen eius detulit, cuius in manibus venenum deprehenderat. Is erat libertus Fabriciorum Scamander.
examples.translation: There was no bias on the part of the jury, no suspicion that the court had been bribed.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to cause to lean, bend, incline, turn a thing in any direction; to bend down
Latin: Facere aliquid clinatum
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Huc inclinavit Antonius cingique vallum corona iussit.
examples.translation: Antonius inclined to meet his troops’ desires and ordered the investment of the enemy’s camp.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Consilium erat, qua fortuna rem daret ea inclinare vires.
examples.translation: His purpose was to swing his forces to the side which fortune favoured.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Haec omnia in dites a pauperibus inclinata onera. Deinde est honos additus;
examples.translation: All these burdens were shifted from the shoulders of the poor to those of the rich.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a flame, fire, heat, burning heat, lit. and trop.

examples.original: Serpens, sitis, ardor harenae Dulcia virtuti;
examples.translation: Serpents, thirst, burning sand—all are welcomed by the brave;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Prae ardore impetuque tantae rei sensus non pervenit ad militem;
examples.translation: In the ardour and enthusiasm of the soldiers so important an event passed unnoticed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mox et ardores per Armeniam et nives per Cappadociam et utriusque caeli subita mutatio pro pestilentia fuit.
examples.translation: Afterwards the heat in Armenia and the snows of Cappadocia and the sudden change from one climate to another were as destructive as a plague.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a narrative of past events, history (syn.: annales, fasti).
Latin: narratio eventorum praeteritorum; narratio et expositio rerum gestarum
Latin: quaevis narratio vera. quaevis descriptio, interpretatio seu expositio

examples.original: Eiusmodi vocibus referta sunt carmina, refertae historiae.
examples.translation: A single tree is not remarkable if the whole forest rises to the same height.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ab hoc sunt imperatoris Galbae avus ac pater: avus clarior studiis quam dignitate—non enim egressus praeturae gradum—multiplicem nec incuriosam historiam edidit;
examples.translation: The former, who was more eminent for his learning than for his rank—for he did not advance beyond the grade of praetor—published a voluminous and painstaking history.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ut enim nos ex annalium monumentis testes excitamus eos quorum omnis vita consumpta est in laboribus gloriosis, qui voluptatis nomen audire non possent, sic in vestris disputationibus historia muta est.
examples.translation: On our side we cite in evidence from our records and our annals men who spent their whole lives in glorious toils, men who would not have borne to hear pleasure so much as named;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to search out, seek to discover, to examine, investigate, explore
Latin: Diligenter inquirere
Latin: in alia re quaerere

examples.original: Primo non accredidit itaque Pharnabazum misit exploratum.
examples.translation: At first, Artaxerxes was incredulous and so sent Pharnabazus to investigate.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Datames

examples.original: Huic mandat ut exploratis omnibus rebus ad se quam primum revertatur.
examples.translation: His orders were to spy out everything and to return to him at once.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ea quamquam similia veris erant, certius tamen exploranda ratus dimittit equites, qui vagos praedatores in agris palantes intercipiant;
examples.translation: These reports were plausible enough; nevertheless he thought it right to obtain more authentic information.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to overturn, turn upside down (syn. demolior, destruo, extinguo, diruo, deleo, etc.).

examples.original: Homines optimi non intellegunt totam rationem everti si ita res se habeat.
examples.translation: These worthy people do not realize that, if this is true, it upsets the theory altogether.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Etenim quam tu domum, quam urbem adiisti, quod fanum denique, quod non eversum atque extersum reliqueris?
examples.translation: What house or town or sanctuary did you ever visit without verily straining and draining it dry?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ratio ista quam defendis, praecepta quae didicisti, quae probas, funditus evertunt amicitiam, quamvis eam Epicurus, ut facit, in caelum efferat laudibus.
examples.translation: The system you uphold, the principles you have studied and accept, undermine the very foundations of friendship, however much Epicurus may, as he does, praise friendship up to the skies.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an agreeing together, union, harmony, concord

examples.original: Illic depositis habitat Concordia telis: Illo, crede mihi, Gratia nata loco est.
examples.translation: Therein dwells Concord when the fight is o’er; there, believe me, was Reconciliation born.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Non arma nec muros nec bello utilia molitur, paci favet et genus humanum ad concordiam vocat.
examples.translation: It is not wisdom that contrives arms, or walls, or instruments useful in war;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Huic tantae concordiae ducis exercitusque non ausi offerre se Aequi, vagari populabundum hostem per agros passi;
examples.translation: Against this complete harmony between commander and army the Aequi ventured no opposition, but suffered their enemies to devastate their fields at will;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a foreboding, prognostic, sign, token

examples.original: Nubit genero socrus, nullis auspicibus, nullis auctoribus, funestis ominibus omnium. VI.
examples.translation: She is reluctant that her fair fame should any longer be damaged by dim and doubtful suspicion;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Accipere se omen consules aiunt et eam precari mentem hostibus ut ne vallum quidem defendant;
examples.translation: The consuls declared that they embraced the omen, praying that the enemy might be so minded as not even to defend his rampart.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Terrebatur ad hoc evidentibus portentis somniorum et auspiciorum et ominum, cum veteribus tum novis.
examples.translation: In addition he was frightened by manifest portents from dreams, auspices and omens, both old and new.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: the talk of the many, whether relating facts or expressing opinions.

examples.original: Is qui scit plurumum, rumor.
examples.translation: It was that most knowing of persons,—gossip.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: difference, diversity, variety

examples.original: In quo fortunae varietas est animadversa.
examples.translation: In this event we see the inconsistency of Fortune;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timotheus

examples.original: Pro vitae varietate et pro actionibus explicantur;
examples.translation: They unfold themselves according as life varies and as actions differ;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In cognoscendo autem ac decernendo mira varietate animi fuit, modo circumspectus et sagax, interdum inconsultus ac praeceps, nonnumquam frivolus amentique similis.
examples.translation: But in hearing and deciding cases he showed strange inconsistency of temper, for he was now careful and shrewd, sometimes hasty and inconsiderate, occasionally silly and like a crazy man.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: the condition of a servus; slavery, serfdom, service, servitude (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Nam vita, si moriendi virtus abest, servitus est.
examples.translation: For life, if courage to die be lacking, is slavery.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In eam demissus es vitam, quae numquam tibi terminum miseriarum ac servitutis ipsa factura sit.
examples.translation: You have been thrust into an existence which will never of itself put an end to your wretchedness and your slavery.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eam tum aequato iure omnium licentiam quaerentes, libertatem aliorum in suam vertisse servitutem inter se conquerebantur: regem hominem esse, a quo impetres, ubi ius, ubi iniuria opus sit;
examples.translation: A king was a man, from whom one could obtain a boon, whether it were just or unjust; there was room for countenance and favour;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to sail, set sail.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Huc cum ab Ostia navigaret, vehementi circio bis paene demersus est, prope Liguriam iuxtaque Stoechadas insulas.
examples.translation: On the voyage thither from Ostia he was nearly cast away twice in furious north-westers, off Liguria and near the Stoechades islands.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Marco Fabio Buteone consule hostium classem iam in Africo mari apud Aegimurum in Italiam ultro navigantem cecidit.
examples.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Fabius Buteo they defeated the enemy’s fleet near Aegimurus in the African sea, while it was actually sailing against Italy.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Caesar His constitutis rebus nactus idoneam ad navigandum tempestatem tertia fere vigilia solvit equitesque in ulteriorem portum progredi et naves conscendere et se sequi iussit.
examples.translation: These arrangements made, he caught a spell of fair weather for sailing, and weighed anchor about the third watch: he ordered the cavalry to proceed to the further harbour, embark, and follow him.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a surname of a distinguished family in the gens Cornelia.

examples.original: Misso igitur Lentulo ultra ulteriorem perpulit ripam;
examples.translation: He, therefore, sent Lentulus and pushed them beyond the further bank of the river;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Et eundem Popilium postea Lentulus in ambitus iudicio pro testimonio diligentissime laudat.
examples.translation: Moreover, Lentulus afterwards singled out this same Popilius for praise when giving evidence at a trial for bribery.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cornus tibi cura sinistri, Lentule, cum prima, quae tum fuit optima bello, Et quarta legione datur.
examples.translation: Lentulus had charge of the left wing with two legions—the first, which was then the most fit for war, and the fourth;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: green.
Latin: Herbecei coloris, color ex.gr. herbarum
Latin: color ex.gr. herbarum

examples.original: Iamque recessurae viridi de stipite factas Admorunt oculos usque sub ora faces.
examples.translation: And now, about to withdraw, they placed before his eyes, close by his face, a green-wood torch.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Est prope purpureos colles florentis Hymetti Fons sacer et viridi caespite mollis humus: Silva nemus non alta facit;
examples.translation: Near the purple hills of flowery Hymettus there is a sacred spring and ground soft with green turf: trees of no great height form a grove;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: the bill or beak of a bird; the snout, muzzle, mouth of animals (cf. proboscis).
Latin: Os, nasus, maxillaque animalis avisve. Rostrum
Latin: Os, nasus, maxillaque animalis avisve

examples.original: Rostro enim noceri non posse cognoverant;
examples.translation: For our commanders knew the enemy could not be damaged by the ram;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Is, quasi non esset ullo modo ferendum se ex iudicio discessisse victum, rem a subselliis ad Rostra detulit.
examples.translation: He then, as if it were not to be borne that he should leave the court defeated, carried the case from the bench to the platform.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Postquam rogationis dies aderat, ingenti stipatus agmine rostra conscendit, nec deerat obvia manu tota inde nobilitas;
examples.translation: When the day for bringing forward the bill was at hand, he ascended the rostra surrounded by a large following;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a surname in the gens Terentia, e. g.
Latin: Auctor Romanus, circa 116 a. Chr. n. - 27 a. Chr. n
English: the chief city of Campania, celebrated for its riches and luxury, now
Latin: Urbs quae est caput Italiae regio Campania

examples.original: Ab Suessula nuntii trepidi Capuam, inde equites citati ad Valerium consulem opem oratum veniunt.
examples.translation: From Suessula the alarming news was carried to Capua, whence gallopers were dispatched to Valerius the consul, to implore assistance.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Urbes ad mare Formiae, Cumae, Puteoli, Neapolis, Herculaneum, Pompei, et ipsa caput urbium Capua, quondam inter tres maximas numerata.
examples.translation: Towards the sea-coast lie the cities of Formiae. Cumae, Puteoli, Naples, Herculaneum and Pompeii, and Capua, queen among cities, formerly accounted among the three greatest in the world.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Cum aliquot ibi dies castra habuisset et Capuam reverteretur, Q. Fabius Maximus, dictator Romanus, in agro Falerno ei se obiecit.
examples.translation: After he had remained in camp there for several days and was returning to Capua, the Roman dictator Quintus Fabius Maximus opposed himself to him in the Falernian region.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

definitions: English: snow.
Latin: Particulae aquae congelatae in crystallum candidum pellucidumve in aëre
Latin: color nivis

examples.original: Nihil praeter nives pruinasque et silvas habent.
examples.translation: Their territory consists entirely of snow, ice and forest.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Mox et ardores per Armeniam et nives per Cappadociam et utriusque caeli subita mutatio pro pestilentia fuit.
examples.translation: Afterwards the heat in Armenia and the snows of Cappadocia and the sudden change from one climate to another were as destructive as a plague.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Urebant montana nives camposque iacentes Non duraturae conspecto sole pruinae, Atque omnis propior mergenti sidera caelo Aruerat tellus hiberno dura sereno.
examples.translation: The mountains were nipped by snow, and the low-lying plains by hoar frost that would vanish at first sight of the sun;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: wretchedness, unhappy condition, misfortune, misery; affliction, distress, etc.

examples.original: Verum quod institui dicere, miserias cognoscite sociorum.
examples.translation: But let us return to what I began to tell you of our allies’ unhappy position.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tu ullos esse condicionis peioris existimas quam qui habent et miseriam et invidiam?
examples.translation: Do you think that there is any more pitiable lot in life than to possess misery and hatred also?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In eam demissus es vitam, quae numquam tibi terminum miseriarum ac servitutis ipsa factura sit.
examples.translation: You have been thrust into an existence which will never of itself put an end to your wretchedness and your slavery.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: withered, arid, parched.
Latin: Humore carens

examples.original: O, ego, cum longae venerunt taedia vitae, Optavi quotiens arida facta mori!
examples.translation: Ah! how oft, grown weary of my long life, have I wished to wither up and die!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nostri, simul in arido constiterunt, suis omnibus consecutis in hostes impetum fecerunt atque eos in fugam dederunt;
examples.translation: The moment our men stood firm on dry land, they charged with all their comrades close behind, and put the enemy to rout;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Non corniger Hammon Mittere Marmaricas cessavit in arma catervas, Quidquid ab occiduis Libye patet arida Mauris Usque Paraetonias eoa ad litora Syrtes.
examples.translation: Nor was horned Ammon slow to send to battle African squadrons from the whole extent of parched Libya—from the Moors in the West to Egyptian Syrtes on the eastern coast.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: To build, erect (post-Aug.): neque quis quid molit, S. C. ap.

examples.original: Non desidero maiorem melioremque te fieri quam moliebaris.
examples.translation: I would not have you greater or better than you planned;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iam molire animum, qui duret, et adstrue formae: Solus ad extremos permanet ille rogo.
examples.translation: Now make thee a soul that will abide, and add it to thy beauty; only that endures to the ultimate pyre.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Non arma nec muros nec bello utilia molitur, paci favet et genus humanum ad concordiam vocat.
examples.translation: It is not wisdom that contrives arms, or walls, or instruments useful in war;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to look at closely, attentively, carefully, to inspect, examine (class. in prose and poetry, esp. in the trop. signif.).

examples.original: Alio loco hoc cuius modi sit considerabimus;
examples.translation: We will consider the significance of this elsewhere;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Causa quae sit, videtis: nunc, quid agendum sit, considerate.
examples.translation: You see what the situation is: now consider what is to be done.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cui ratiocinationi utrum nihil valide inimicum sit, peto mecum consideres.
examples.translation: For the present I find it stimulating;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: the open sea, the main.

examples.original: Saeva quies pelagi, maestoque ignava profundo Stagna iacentis aquae;
examples.translation: A grim stillness broods over the dismal deep;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: by Pollux!
English: so often, so many times, as often, as many times.

examples.original: Et forsitan, quem ille obrutum ignem reliquerit, ita ut totiens novum ex improviso incendium daret, eum se exstincturum.
examples.translation: And perhaps that fire which Fabius had left covered up, but so that it was continually breaking out into new flames, might be by him extinguished.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hoc consilio a L. Metello legationes universae petiverunt ut quam primum isti succederet; hoc animo totiens apud patronos de suis miseriis deplorarunt;
examples.translation: This was the purpose of the entreaty made by all their deputations to Lucius Metellus, that he would take over the government from Verres at the earliest possible moment;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tot praetores in Sicilia fuerunt, totiens apud maiores nostros Siculi senatum adierunt, totiens hac memoria: tamen huiusce novi postulati genus atque principium tua praetura attulit.
examples.translation: How many praetors have governed Sicily! How often the Sicilians have approached the Senate, in our fathers’ times and within our own memory!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the forearm, from the hand to the elbow (while lacertus is the upper arm, from the elbow to the shoulder)
Latin: Membrum hominis a cubito ad manum
Latin: Membrum hominis a umero ad manum

examples.original: Conseruere manus et multo bracchia nexu;
examples.translation: They locked hands and arms in manifold embrace;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Hunc quidem in secundam aciem Latini recepere: Aebutius cum saucio bracchio tenere telum non posset, pugna excessit.
examples.translation: Mamilius was received by the Latins within their second line: Aebutius, being unable to manage a weapon with his wounded arm, retired from the battle.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to cast, thrust, or drive out; to eject, expel (class.).
Latin: Expellere; dimittere; iacere ex aliquo
Latin: De navibus vel hominibus, iacere ad litus; praesertim cum destructione vel debilitatione navis

examples.original: Illi cum ludos facerent, servos de cavea exire iubebant: tu in alteram servos immisisti, ex altera liberos eiecisti.
examples.translation: When they held the games, they bade slaves depart from the auditorium; you let slaves loose upon one auditorium, and ejected freemen from the other.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: His igitur depulsa locis eiectaque classis Syrtibus haud ultra Garamantidas attigit undas, Sed duce Pompeio Libyae melioris in oris Mansit.
examples.translation: Thus the ships, driven from their course and cast forth from the Syrtes, remained in this region, on the shore of the better part of Libya, with Pompeius as commander;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Denique ex omni numero, qui fuit circiter milium xl, vix dccc, qui primo clamore audito se ex oppido eiecerunt, incolumes ad Vercingetorigem pervenerunt.
examples.translation: Eventually of all the number, which was about forty thousand, scarcely eight hundred, who had flung themselves out of the town when they heard the first shout, reached Vercingetorix in safety.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: ye late-learned
Latin: Qui diu differtur
Latin: Serotinus

examples.original: Non vixit iste, sed in vita moratus est, nec sero mortuus est, sed diu.
examples.translation: A person like him has not lived; he has merely tarried awhile in life.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: I nunc, claude fores, custos odiose puellae, Et centum duris postibus obde seras!
examples.translation: Go now, hateful guardian, bar the lady’s door, and add a hundred bolts to the sturdy posts.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cogeris voti nescius esse tui: Seu te forte iuvat sera et sapientior aetas, Hoc quoque, crede mihi, plenius agmen erit.
examples.translation: Or do you perchance prefer a later and staider age? still more numerous, believe me, will be their array.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to fall together, to fall down, to tumble to the ground (class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Dividi enim illam, non concidi, utile est.
examples.translation: For it is useful that philosophy should be divided, but not chopped into bits.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In pedes suos ipse plurima dicebat et in fauces concisas; sic inimicorum, quos plures habebat quam morbos, et in primis Ciceronis urbanitatem effugerat.
examples.translation: He uttered many a jest at the expense of his own feet and his scarred jowls.b So he escaped the wit of his enemies—they outnumbered his afflictions—and, above all, Cicero’s.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et paucorum dierum iter progressus prosperas apud Bedriacum res ac morte Othonis concidisse bellum accepit: vocata contione virtutem militum laudibus cumulat.
examples.translation: After he had advanced a few days, he heard of the success at Bedriacum and learned that at Otho’s death the war had collapsed;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: the side, flank of men or animals.
Latin: Pars corporis quae nec a fronte nec a tergo sit; margo
Latin: Cui spatium magnum est inter latera

examples.original: Aequaliter splendebit omne caeli latus;
examples.translation: The whole expanse of heaven will shine evenly;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid tibi mentis erat, cum sic male sana lateres, Procri?
examples.translation: What were thy feelings, Procris, when thus frantic thou lurkedst there?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Valerius Catullus, consulari familia iuvenis, stupratum a se ac latera sibi contubernio eius defessa etiam vociferatus est.
examples.translation: Valerius Catullus, a young man of a consular family, bragged that he had penetrated the emperor and worn himself out in intercourse with him.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: the pupil of the eye

examples.original: Manlius quoque ad restituendam aciem se ipse coram offert.
examples.translation: Manlius also showed himself among them, helping to restore the line;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cora —quis credat?—et Alsium terrori fuerunt, Satricum atque Corniculum provinciae.
examples.translation: Cora (though it seems incredible) and Alsium were formidable: Satricum and Corniculum were provinces.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Libenter haec coram cum Q. Catulo et Q. Hortensio, summis et clarissimis viris, disputarem;
examples.translation: I would gladly discuss the matter personally with eminent and distinguished men like Quintus Catulus and Quintus Hortensius;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the name of a Roman gens.

examples.original: Navis, quae in flumine magna est, in mari parvula est.
examples.translation: A ship which looms large in the river seems tiny when on the ocean.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Mancino deinde consule terra marique fervebat obsidio.
examples.translation: The harbours were blocked up;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Solacia fati Carthago Mariusque tulit, pariterque iacentes Ignovere deis.
examples.translation: Carthage and Marius both drew consolation for their destiny ;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to separate, set apart.

examples.original: Quis omnia in uno mersa et materia inerti convoluta discreverit?
examples.translation: Do you compel me to withdraw from the whole and restrict me to a part?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Petimus non singula busta Discretosque rogos: unum da gentibus ignem, Non interpositis urantur corpora flammis;
examples.translation: We ask not a pyre for each or a separate burning: provide a single fire for all;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a playhouse, theatre (cf.: scena, spectaculum, ludus).

examples.original: Sed tu praecipue curvis venare theatris: Haec loca sunt voto fertiliora tuo.
examples.translation: But specially do your hunting in the round theatres: more bountifully do these repay your vows.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Visite turicremas vaccae Memphitidos aras, Visite conspicuis terna theatra locis;
examples.translation: Visit the incense-burning altars of the Memphian heifer; visit three theatres in conspicuous seats.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Tunc neque marmoreo pendebant vela theatro, Nec fuerant liquido pulpita rubra croco;
examples.translation: No awnings then hung o’er a marble theatre, nor was the platform ruddy with crocus-spray;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: half (for the diff. between it and dimidiatus, v. dimidio).

examples.original: Dimidium fere spatium confecerat, cum ex fumo castrorum eius suspicio adlata est ad Eumenem hostem appropinquare.
examples.translation: He had covered nearly half the distance, when the smoke from his camp led Eumenes to suspect that the enemy were approaching.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Nam quod dixisti: ”Cavendum est, ne cum rem dubiam emendari volumus, maiora vulnera faciamus,” tantundem valebit, si eis dimidium concedatur.
examples.translation: For your remark that we must beware, while endeavouring to settle a doubtful matter, of causing more serious wounds, will have as much force if they be granted a half.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: an enclosed place; hence

examples.original: Ex quibus Appius, qui praecipuam poenam meruerat, in carcerem coniectus est;
examples.translation: Of these, Appius, who had been most guilty, was flung into prison;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed nec illo voluntario ad hostis suos reditu nec ultimo sive carceris seu crucis supplicio deformata maiestas;
examples.translation: His voluntary return to his enemies and his final sufferings, whether in prison or on the cross, in no way sullied his dignity;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Et si quis deus mihi largiatur ut ex hac aetate repuerascam et in cunis vagiam, valde recusem, nec vero velim quasi decurso spatio ad carceres a calce revocari.
examples.translation: And when I shall have set out to join them, assuredly no one will easily draw me back, or boil me up again, as if I were a Pelias.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: A name added to the nomen (or name of the gens), usu. the third word in order in the full name of each citizen; sometimes followed by a fourth, the agnomen, but in the class. per

examples.original: Alexandrini Cybiosacten eum vocare perseveraverunt, cognomine unius e regibus suis turpissimarum sordium.
examples.translation: The Alexandrians persisted in calling him Cybiosactes, the surname of one of their kings who was scandalously stingy.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Philologi appellationem assumpsisse videtur, quia sic ut Eratosthenes, qui primus hoc cognomen sibi vindicavit, multiplici variaque doctrina censebatur.
examples.translation: And that he was such is evident from his commentaries, though very few of them survive;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Kal. Ian. in villa colli superposita prope Tarracinam sinistrorsus Fundos petentibus, adoptatusque a noverca sua Livia nomen et Ocellare cognomen assumpsit mutato praenomine;
examples.translation: Adopted by his stepmother Livia, he took her name and the surname Ocella, and also changed his forename;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to watch, i. e. to be or keep awake at night, not to sleep, be wakeful (class.; syn. excubo).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Tarentum vero qua vigilantia, quo consilio recepit!
examples.translation: Indeed, with what vigilance, with what skill he recaptured Tarentum!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In principatu maturius semper ac de nocte vigilabat;
examples.translation: While emperor, he always rose very early, in fact before daylight;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Et illa quidem nocte nihil praeterquam vigilatum est in urbe.
examples.translation: That night nothing more was done than to keep a watch in the City.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to bury

examples.original: Monte sub hoc lapidum tegitur Ballista sepultus;
examples.translation: Under this mountain of stones Ballista is covered and buried;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Antigonus autem Eumenem mortuum propinquis eius sepeliendum tradidit.
examples.translation: Antiochus, however, sent the body of Eumenes to his relatives for burial.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Parthe, dabis poenas: Crassi gaudete sepulti, Signaque barbaricas non bene passa manu.
examples.translation: Parthian, thou shalt pay penalty; rejoice, ye buried Crassi, and ye standards that shamefully endured barbarian violence.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: morally pure, unpolluted, spotless, guiltless, = purus, integer

examples.original: Dum fuit Atrides una contentus, et illa Casta fuit: vitio est improba facta viri.
examples.translation: While Atrides was content with one, she was chaste also; she was made wicked by her husband’s sin.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Spectatum veniunt, veniunt spectentur ut ipsae: Ille locus casti damna pudoris habet.
examples.translation: They come to see, they come that they may be seen: to chastity that place is fatal.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quod cum Deiotarus religione sua castissime tueretur, quem unum habemus in orbe terrarum fidelissimum huic imperio atque amantissimum nostri nominis, Brogitaro, ut ante dixi, addictum pecunia tradidisti.
examples.translation: The former, however, owes his kingly title, through us, to the senatorial pronouncement, while Brogitarus owes his, through you, to the price which he paid you.a . .
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a Roman surname

examples.original: Cura ripae Hordeonio Flacco permissa;
examples.translation: The duty of guarding the Rhine he assigned to Hordeonius Flaccus.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Verrius Flaccus libertinus docendi genere maxime claruit.
examples.translation: Marcus Verrius Flaccus, a freedman, gained special fame by his method of teaching.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Flaccum iam adultum, cuius exitum sub nomine Daphnidis deflet.
examples.translation: Virgil grow up, and whose death he laments under the name of Daphnis.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

definitions: English: to parch, roast, bake, scorch, burn, etc. (syn. frigo)

examples.original: Illae pestes non minus graves sunt, famem dico et sitim et praecordiorum subpurationes et febrem viscera ipsa torrentem.
examples.translation: Those other troubles are of course not less serious; I mean hunger, thirst, ulcers of the stomach, and fever that parches our very bowels.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Documenta cladis cruentus aliquandiu Aufidus, pons de cadaveribus iussu ducis factus in torrente Vergello, modii duo anulorum Carthaginem missi dignitasque equestris taxata mensura.
examples.translation: As proofs of the vastness of the slaughter the Aufidus for a long time ran with blood; a bridge of corpses was constructed by order of the general over the torrent of Vergellus;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Coronopus oblonga herba est cum fissuris. seritur interim, quoniam radix coeliacis praeclare facit in cinere tosta.
examples.translation: The coronopus is an elongated plant, with fissures in the leaves. It is sometimes cultivated, as the root, roasted in hot ashes, is found to be an excellent remedy for cœliac complaints.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: belonging to a horseman, equestrian.
Latin: Equitis vel qui ad equitem pertinet

examples.original: Is finis pugnae equestris fuit.
examples.translation: This ended the cavalry-battle.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Magister equitum et ipse novat pugnam equestrem.
examples.translation: The master of the horse on his part invented a new kind of cavalry-fighting.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Adflictas opes equestri proelio Bellovacorum esse;
examples.translation: The power of the Bellovaci was crushed, they said, by the cavalry combat;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: backwards, back; on the back side, behind.
Latin: loc. versus regionem posteriorem
Latin: temp. versus tempus posterius

examples.original: Vide rursus retro. Dato hoc, dandum est illud.
examples.translation: Or again conversely: given the latter, you must grant the former.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Iam ibi sunt, unde non est retro lapsus, sed hoc illis de se nondum liquet;
examples.translation: They have already arrived at a point from which there is no slipping back, but they are not yet aware of the fact;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Invenietur autem, si coeperimus singula retro legere; sic enim perducemur ad primum.
examples.translation: And the idea of genus will be reached if we begin to reckon back from particulars;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: raised high, extending upward, high, lofty (syn.: altus, erectus, sublimis, elatus, procerus).
Latin: Cognomen Romanum

examples.original: In edito stat admirabilis, celsus, magnitudinis verae.
examples.translation: He stands in a high place, worthy of admiration, lofty, and really great.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Illyrici exercitus electi Celsum infestis pilis proturbant.
examples.translation: The picked troops from Illyria drove Celsus away at the point of their spears.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Missus et Celsus Marius ad electos Illyrici exercitus, Vipsania in porticu tendentis;
examples.translation: Celsus Marius was sent to the picked troops from Illyria, who were encamped in the Vipsanian Colonnade;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to shake (class.; syn.: concutio, convello).

examples.original: Quatiebatur his segne ingenium ut concupisceret magis quam ut speraret.
examples.translation: These arguments stirred his sluggish nature to covetousness rather than to hope.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Seneca Lvcilio svo salvtem Bassum Aufidium, virum optimum, vidi quassum, aetati obluctantem.
examples.translation: On Conquering the Conqueror I have beheld Aufidius Bassus, that noble man, shattered in health and wrestling with his years.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tristes praesagia curas Exagitant, trepida quatitur formidine somnus, Thessaliam nox omnis habet;
examples.translation: For her sorrow is intensified by forebodings, and her sleep broken by anxious fears.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a spear

examples.original: Nos consules an vos, Quirites?
examples.translation: For us, the consuls, or for you, Quirites?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Iam primum omnium” inquit, ”Quirites, in Volscos et Aequos mihi atque collegae legiones ducere in animo est.
examples.translation: First of all then, Quirites,” he concluded, ”I and my colleague are resolved to lead the legions against the Volsci and the Aequi.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ibi in hanc sententiam locutum accipio: ”Etsi mihi nullius noxae conscius, Quirites, sum, tamen cum pudore summo in contionem in conspectum vestrum processi.
examples.translation: There he spoke, as I understand, to the following effect: ”Although I am conscious, Quirites, of no wrong-doing, nevertheless it is with great shame that I have come to this assembly to confront you.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a cutting or lopping off (post-class. and rare)
Latin: Actus secandi atque ad terram prosternendi percutiendo
Latin: Saepius accipitur pro percussione, qua homo aut aliud animal vulneratur atque occiditur

examples.original: Homicidia compescimus et singulas caedes;
examples.translation: We check manslaughter and isolated murders;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Caedem eius laetam fuisse Muciano accepimus.
examples.translation: According to report his death gave Mucianus pleasure.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nec magis post proelium quam in proelio caedibus temperatum est;
examples.translation: After the battle, as well as during its progress, no quarter was given.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to be courteous or complaisant; to be kind, tender, indulgent to; to be pleased with or inclined to, to give one's self up to, yield to, indulge in a thing (as joy or grief)
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; si, tum, 2

examples.original: Indulgendum est enim honestis adfectibus;
examples.translation: For one must indulge genuine emotions;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ornamenta consularia etiam procuratoribus ducenariis indulsit.
examples.translation: He gave the consular regalia even to the second grade of stewards.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: At tanti tibi sit non indulgere theatris, Dum bene de vacuo pectore cedat amor.
examples.translation: But let it be worth while to abstain from theatres, until love ebb quite away from your empty heart.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: not strong, weak, feeble.

examples.original: Scis illum semper infirmi corporis et exsucti fuisse.
examples.translation: You know that his body was always delicate and sapless.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Id autem maxime tracta, quod in te esse infirmissimum senties.
examples.translation: Above all, however, ponder that which you come to feel is your greatest weakness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Pax erit haec nobis, donec mihi vita manebit, Cum pecore infirmo quae solet esse lupis.
examples.translation: That peace shall we enjoy, while life remains to me, which wolves are wont to keep with the defenceless flock.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: that can be put on an equality with; conseq., equal, like; constr. with

examples.original: Confer avum tuum Drusum cum C. Graccho, eius fere aequali.
examples.translation: Compare your grandfather Drusus with Gaius Gracchus, who was nearly his contemporary.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Etenim quod sacrificium tam vetustum est quam hoc, quod a regibus aequale huius urbis accepimus?
examples.translation: And indeed what sacrifice is so ancient as that which we received from our kings, and which is coeval with our city?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Erant in Romana iuventute adulescentes aliquot, nec ii tenui loco orti, quorum in regno libido solutior fuerat, aequales sodalesque adulescentium Tarquiniorum, adsueti more regio vivere.
examples.translation: This licence they missed, now that all enjoyed equal rights, and they had got into the way of complaining to each other that the liberty of the rest had resulted in their own enslavement.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: unwrought, untilled, unformed, unused, rough

examples.original: Imperitis ac rudibus nullus praecipitationis finis est;
examples.translation: For those who lack experience and training, there is no limit to the downhill course;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tanta rudi populo cura pudoris erat. At nunc nocturnis titulos inponimus actis, Atque emitur magno nil, nisi posse loqui!
examples.translation: But now we make our nightly exploits a title to renown, and purchase at a high price naught but the power to brag!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nolebat in agendo discere tametsi non provinciae rudis erat et tiro, sed Siciliae paratus ad praedam meditatusque venire cupiebat.
examples.translation: He was not content to discover these methods on the spot, though he was no raw new-comer to the work of government;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of bronze [aes].
Latin: Qui ex aere factum vel compositus est
Latin: Colore aeris

examples.original: Nondum maturus imperio Ascanius Aeneae filius erat;
examples.translation: Ascanius, Aeneas’ son, was not yet ripe for authority;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Aeneam ab simili clade domo profugum, sed ad maiora rerum initia ducentibus fatis, primo in Macedoniam venisse, inde in Siciliam quaerentem sedes delatum, ab Sicilia classe ad Laurentem agrum tenuisse.
examples.translation: Aeneas, driven from home by a similar misfortune, but guided by fate to undertakings of greater consequence, came first to Macedonia; thence was carried, in his quest of a place of settlement, to Sicily;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Alii proelio victum Latinum pacem cum Aenea, deinde affinitatem iunxisse tradunt: alii, cum instructae acies constitissent, priusquam signa canerent processisse Latinum inter primores ducemque advenarum evocasse ad conloquium;
examples.translation: Some say that Latinus, having been defeated in the battle, made a peace with Aeneas, and later an alliance of marriage.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to hasten, make haste, hurry, be quick (class.; not in Caes.; syn.: propero, celero, maturo): aliud est properare, aliud festinare. Qui unum quid mature transigit, is properat
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Festinanti ergo ut occurrerem, malui festinanter aliquid scribere quam religiosum tuum desiderium retardare, domine eximie et merito insignis atque honorabilis fili.
examples.translation: To meet his haste, then, I have chosen rather to write something in haste than to keep your holy desire in suspense, my noble and justly distinguished lord and honourable son.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: loss, injury, damage, mischief, harm: sed ecca ipsa egreditur, nostri fundi calamitas

examples.original: Sed ille quidem par tantae calamitati fuit;
examples.translation: But he proved himself able to face such a calamity;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Interim accidit illa calamitas apud Leuctra Lacedaemoniis.
examples.translation: In the meantime that famous disaster at Leuctra befell the Lacedaemonians.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

examples.original: Itaque haec vobis provincia, Quirites, si et belli utilitatem et pacis dignitatem retinere vultis, non modo a calamitate, sed etiam a metu calamitatis est defendenda.
examples.translation: This province, gentlemen, if you wish to retain what makes either war possible or peace honourable, it is your duty to defend not only from disaster but from fear of disaster.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Love as a person
English: To pour, mingle, or mix together (class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Conlaudatis ab senatu tribunis et ipse Camillus confusus animo gratias egit.
examples.translation: The senate commended the tribunes, and Camillus himself, deeply moved, expressed his thanks.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Iamque ubi pulvereae fuerint confusa farinae, Protinus in cumeris omnia cerne cavis.
examples.translation: And now when it is mixed with the dusty grain, sift it all straightway in hollow sieves.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ipse manu subicit gladios ac tela ministrat Adversosque iubet ferro confundere voltus.
examples.translation: In person he advances the fighting line and urges on his rearguard;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to fight, struggle, contend (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Quam atrociter dimicatum sit, exitus docuit.
examples.translation: The result of the battle showed how desperate was the fighting;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Spartacus ipse in primo agmine fortissime dimicans quasi imperator occisus est.
examples.translation: Spartacus himself fell, as became a general, fighting most bravely in the front rank.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Quinque cohortes, quas minime firmas ad dimicandum esse existimabat, castris praesidio relinquit;
examples.translation: He left as garrison for the camp the five cohorts which he regarded as least steady for action;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: flowing, fluid, liquid.

examples.original: Aspicies oculos tremulo fulgore micantes, Ut sol a liquida saepe refulget aqua.
examples.translation: You will see her eyes shooting tremulous gleams, as the sun often glitters in clear water.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Tunc neque marmoreo pendebant vela theatro, Nec fuerant liquido pulpita rubra croco;
examples.translation: No awnings then hung o’er a marble theatre, nor was the platform ruddy with crocus-spray;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: At liquidas avium voces imitarier ore ante fuit multo quam levia carmina cantu concelebrare homines possent aurisque iuvare.
examples.translation: To imitate with the mouth the liquid notes of the birds came long before men could delight their ears by warbling smooth carols in song.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: by, from; used with the ablative to indicate source, cause, or agent

examples.original: Quaero abs te, simne deiectus: non de Fulciniano fundo;
examples.translation: I ask you, was I driven out?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed tamen haec tibi est prima cum Plancio generis vestri familiaeque contentio, qua abs te vincitur.
examples.translation: However, the first comparison you make between yourself and Plancius is in the matter of birth and family.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Respondebo tibi nunc, Laterensis, minus fortasse vehementer, quam abs te sum provocatus: sed profecto nec considerate minus, nec minus amice.
examples.translation: I now proceed to reply to you, Laterensis, using less vehemence, perhaps, than you prompt me to use, but in a spirit, I dare avow, of no less consideration and friendship.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to flow over and down, to overflow
Latin: Expleor plus quam plenus

examples.original: Insulam veteribus divitiis abundantem et ob hoc Veneri sacram Ptolemaeus regebat.
examples.translation: This island, rich in ancient wealth and therefore dedicated to Venus, was under the rule of Ptolemy.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Semper enim boni assiduique domini referta cella vinaria, olearia, etiam penaria est, villaque tota locuples est, abundat porco haedo agno gallina, lacte caseo melle.
examples.translation: For the provident and industrious proprietor always has his store-room and cellars well filled with oil and wine and provisions;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Is quod eius ex populis abundabat, Bituriges Arvernos Senones Haeduos Ambarros Carnutes Aulercos excivit. Profectus ingentibus peditum equitumque copiis in Tricastinos venit.
examples.translation: Taking out with him the surplus population of his tribes, the Bituriges, Arverni, Senones, Haedui, Ambarri, Carnutes, and Aulerci, he marched with vast numbers of infantry and cavalry into the country of the Tricastini.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: exercise

examples.original: Tum imperatori exercituique honos suus redditus;
examples.translation: The general and his army then received their meed of honour;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ariovistus his omnibus diebus exercitum castris continuit, equestri proelio cotidie contendit.
examples.translation: On all these days Ariovistus kept his army in camp, but engaged daily in a cavalry encounter.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Cum Fidenae aperte descissent, Tullus Mettio exercituque eius ab Alba accito contra hostes ducit.
examples.translation: Fidenae having openly revolted, Tullus summoned Mettius and his army from Alba, and led his forces against the enemy.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: home, or hearth and home, and pro aris et focis pugnare, to fight for altars and fires, for one's dearest possessions
Latin: ār|a, -ae fem

examples.original: Iam stat, ut ipse vides, funeris ara tui.
examples.translation: The procession is ready for thee;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Eo ille index confugit in araque consedit.
examples.translation: To this that informer fled and seated himself upon the altar.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

examples.original: Visite turicremas vaccae Memphitidos aras, Visite conspicuis terna theatra locis;
examples.translation: Visit the incense-burning altars of the Memphian heifer; visit three theatres in conspicuous seats.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: The fruit of the vine, a grape
Latin: Fructus vitis

examples.original: Est tibi rure bono generosae fertilis uvae Vinea?
examples.translation: You have a fruitful estate and a vineyard abundant in fine grapes?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Temporibus certis maturam rusticus uvam Deligit, et nudo sub pede musta fluunt;
examples.translation: At fixed seasons the countryman picks the ripened grapes, and the vintage flows beneath his naked foot;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Rure suburbano poteris tibi dicere missa, Illa vel in Sacra sint licet empta via. Adferat aut uvas, aut quas Amaryllis amabat— At nunc castaneas non amat illa nuces.
examples.translation: You can say they were sent to you from your suburban property, though you bought them in the Sacred Way. Let him bring either grapes or the chestnuts ”that Amaryllis loved” but loves no more.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to feign that a thing is not that which it is; to dissemble, disguise; to hide, conceal, keep secret (cf.: fingo, simulo, confingo, comminiscor—very freq. and class.).

examples.original: Cupiebam dissimulare me id moleste ferre;
examples.translation: I did my best to pretend that I felt no uneasiness myself;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Utque viro furtiva venus, sic grata puellae: Vir male dissimulat: tectius illa cupit.
examples.translation: And as stolen love is pleasant to a man, so is it also to a woman;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ita nec dissimulantem quid mallet nec petentem tamen, aedilem curulem cum L. Papirio Cursore factum.
examples.translation: And so, neither dissembling what he had in mind nor yet seeking it, he was elected curule aedile, with Lucius Papirius Cursor.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to set in rapid motion, to hasten, urge forwards; and with se

examples.original: Incitat et ficti tristis custodia servi, Et nimium duri cura molesta viri.
examples.translation: The surly guardianship of a pretended slave excites him, and the irksome vigilance of a husband too severe.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hisce ego auxiliis studentibus atque incitatis uti me, Laterensis, potuisse confiteor;
examples.translation: Of these helpers, Laterensis, so zealous and so enthusiastic, I admit that I might have availed myself.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quorum timor cum fremitu et concursu significaretur, milites nostri pristini diei perfidia incitati in castra irruperunt.
examples.translation: When their alarm was betrayed by the uproar and bustle, our troops, stung by the treachery of the day before, burst into the camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to cause to flee, to put to flight, drive or chase away, to rout, discomfit (rare but class.)

examples.original: Faeneratorem non fugat a foro decoctor.
examples.translation: The banker is not frightened away from the forum by the swindler.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ibi impedire opus conatos hostes fundit fugatque;
examples.translation: There, when the enemy sought to hinder the work, he defeated and routed them;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vir fortis ac sapiens non fugere debet e vita, sed exire.
examples.translation: The brave and wise man should not beat a hasty retreat from life;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Penates; (usu. pl.); gods of home/larder/family

examples.original: Caesar et Fimbria in penatibus domuum suarum trucidantur, Crassi pater et filius in mutuo alter alterius aspectu.
examples.translation: Caesar and Fimbria were butchered at the household shrines of their own homes. The elder and younger Crassus were slain in the sight of one another.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Ista tua pulcra Libertas deos penates et familiares meos lares expulit, ut se ipsa tamquam in captivis sedibus collocaret?
examples.translation: Did your darling Liberty drive out my household gods and the spirits of my family, that she might establish herself in what was virtually a captive’s dwelling?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of Romulus; Roman
Latin: Qui ad Romulum pertinet; Romanus
Latin: Conditor mythicus urbis Romae, et geminus Remi

examples.original: Agrippa inde Tiberini filius, post Agrippam Romulus Silvius a patre accepto imperio regnat.
examples.translation: Then Agrippa, son of Tiberinus, reigned, and after Agrippa Romulus Silvius was king, having received the power from his father.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Publico auxilio nullo adiuti sunt, valuitque apud Veientes—nam de ceteris minus mirum est—pacta cum Romulo indutiarum fides.
examples.translation: Official aid there was none, and the Veientes (for there is less to surprise us in the others) held firmly to the truce they had agreed upon with Romulus.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec nominis homines tum pertaesum esse, quippe quo Iovem appellari fas sit, quo Romulum, conditorem urbis, deincepsque reges, quod sacris etiam ut sollemne retentum sit: superbiam violentiamque tum perosos regis.
examples.translation: Nor was it the name, said he, which had then disgusted men, since by this name Jupiter was duly called; and Romulus, the founder of the City: and the successive kings;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: Alps (usually pl.), mountains to the north of Italy

examples.original: Nunc desuper Alpis Nubiferae colles atque aeriam Pyrenen Abripimur.
examples.translation: Next I am spirited away over the cloud-capped Alps and soaring Pyrenees.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Aberat tunc Caesar Ravennae dilectum agens, et hieme creverant Alpes: sic interclusum putabant iter.
examples.translation: Caesar was absent at the time holding a levy at Ravenna, and the Alps had been swollen by winter snows;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed hunc quoque iam tum quom ab Alpe descenderat, apud Metaurum castra metantem Claudius Nero cum Livio Salinatore debellat.
examples.translation: However, when Hasdrubal had just descended from the Alps, as he was planning out a camp near the Metaurus, Claudius Nero, together with Livius Salinator, defeated him also.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: To drive, lead, or bring back (syn. reduco).

examples.original: Fidenae in potestatem redactae eoque coloni missi sunt;
examples.translation: Fidenae was subjugated and colonists were sent thither;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Interdicis mihi inspectione rerum naturae, a toto abductum redigis in partem?
examples.translation: He is so trained that he neither loves nor hates life;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quidquid captum ex hostibus est, vendidit Fabius consul ac redegit in publicum.
examples.translation: Whatever was taken from the enemy Fabius sold and placed the proceeds in the public treasury.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to fill up, fill full, fill out (class. in prose and poetry).
Latin: Refercīre (fossas complere, paginam complere)
Latin: Perficere (actionem, causam, laborem complere)

examples.original: Illi subito ex omnibus partibus evolaverunt murumque celeriter compleverunt.
examples.translation: They dashed out suddenly from all sides and speedily lined the wall.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Itaque horum adventu decem milia armatorum completa sunt, quae manus mirabili flagrabat pugnandi cupiditate.
examples.translation: They sent a thousand soldiers, whose arrival raised the number of combatants to ten thousand.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

examples.original: Illa enim quae sunt a nobis bona corporis numerata complent ea quidem beatissimam vitam, sed ita ut sine illis possit beata vita exsistere.
examples.translation: The things we reckon as bodily goods do, it is true, form a factor in supreme happiness, but yet happiness is possible without them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To hold to, to bring or hold near
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; Dietsch; tĭnui, tentum, 2

examples.original: Sed quid attinet de rebus tam apertis plura requirere?
examples.translation: But what is the point of inquiring further into matters so obvious?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Et ille quidem in recusando perstabat: quid ergo attineret leges ferri, quibus per eosdem qui tulissent fraus fieret.
examples.translation: Fabius, for his part, stoutly persisted in his refusal. What, in that case, he demanded, was the good of making laws, when their very makers broke them?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed cum ea quae praeterierunt acri animo et attento intuemur, tum fit ut aegritudo sequatur si illa mala sint, si bona, laetitia.
examples.translation: But when we fix our mental vision closely on the events of the past, then sorrow or gladness ensues according as these were evil or good.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: human nature, humanity, in a good sense; the qualities, feelings, and inclinations of mankind.

examples.original: Sive enim non respuit, humanitate eius inritamur, sive contempsit, superbia accendimur.
examples.translation: If our love be not spurned, we are excited by its kindness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic Philodamus, posteaquam ius suum obtinere non potuit, ut humanitatem consuetudinemque suam retineret laborabat.
examples.translation: Unable to maintain his rights, Philodamus now did his best to maintain his accustomed courtesy.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Putarem me idoneum qui exemplum sequerer humanitatis atque officii, proponeremque spem meis hospitibus ac necessariis quo tutiorem sese vitam meo praesidio victuros esse arbitrarentur.
examples.translation: I should offer those who have given me hospitality and friendship some reason to think that they will live lives of greater security because I am here to protect them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to seize or snatch up, to collect, to seize upon, take hold of (very freq., and class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Primus statim impetus belli Bithyniam rapuit, Asia inde pari terrore correpta est, nec cunctanter ad regem ab urbibus nostris populisque descitum est.
examples.translation: The first assault immediately won Bithynia; whereupon Asia was seized by a general panic, and without delay our cities and peoples revolted to the king.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Si autem ille qui corripit, reddere vult malum pro malo ei qui corripienti indignatur, non fuit dignus qui corriperet, sed dignus plane, qui etiam ipse corripi deberet.
examples.translation: If the reprover, however, choose to render evil for evil to the man who takes offence at being reproved, he was not fit to reprove another, but clearly fit to be reproved himself.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Vocibus his correpta viri vix aegra levavit Membra solo tales gemitu rumpente querellas: ”O utinam in thalamos invisi Caesaris issem Infelix coniunx et nulli laeta marito!
examples.translation: Thus rebuked by her husband, slowly she raised her ailing limbs from the ground, and her wailing broke out into complaints like these: ”Would that I had been wedded to hated Caesar;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to regulate

examples.original: Sermo erga patrem imperatoremque reverens, de se moderatus;
examples.translation: He answered with the reverence due to a father and an emperor;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Scire debet quid petat ille, qui sagittam vult mittere, et tunc derigere ac moderari manu telum.
examples.translation: The archer must know what he is seeking to hit; then he must aim and control the weapon by his skill.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ser. Tullius regnavit annos quattuor et quadraginta ita ut bono etiam moderatoque succedenti regi difficilis aemulatio esset.
examples.translation: Servius Tullius had ruled forty-four years, so well that even a good and moderate successor would have found it hard to emulate him.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: something bent; hence
Latin: Quaedam porta supra curvata
Latin: Arcus scilicet caelestis

examples.original: Sp. Tarpeius Romanae praeerat arci.
examples.translation: Spurius Tarpeius commanded the Roman citadel.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non ego Dulichio furari more sagittas, Nec raptas ausim tinguere in amne faces: Nec nos purpureas pueri resecabimus alas, Nec sacer arte mea laxior arcus erit.
examples.translation: I would not dare to pilfer arrows in Dulichian wise, nor to drench in water the stolen torch; I shall not clip the Boy’s bright wings, nor by my art unstring the sacred bow.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: twelve
Latin: Undecim et alius. Numerus XII
Latin: undecim et alius

examples.original: Antonium quaestorem cum legione duodecima sibi coniungit.
examples.translation: Marcus Antonius, the quartermaster-general, with the Twelfth Legion he attached to his own force.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: In duodecimo autem libro eorum quos de genesi scripsi, versatur haec quaestio vehementer et multis exemplis rerum expertarum atque credibiliter auditarum disputatio illa silvescit.
