examples.translation: However, in the twelfth book of my treatise on Genesis,a this problem is examined with thoroughness, and the discussion there is luxuriant with numerous examples drawn from personal experience and trustworthy report.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Et ipse magnus abbas Benedictus, sicut de illo beatus papa Gregorius scribit, duodecim abbates suis discipulis, prout utile iudicavit, sine charitatis detrimento, immo pro augmento charitatis praefecit.
examples.translation: And the great abbot Benedict himself, as blessed Gregory telleth us of him, set 12 abbots over his disciples, as he judged expedient, neither did he thereby lessen brotherly love but rather enlarged it.
examples.author: Bede

definitions: English: An arrow, shaft, bolt
Latin: Telum quod arcus mittit

examples.original: Denique Sarmaticas inter Geticasque sagittas His precor ut vivas et moriare locis.
examples.translation: Finally, I pray that in these regions, among Sarmatian and Getic arrows, thou mayst live and die.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Utque coturnatum periisse Lycophrona narrant, Haereat in fibris fixa sagitta tuis.
examples.translation: And as they say buskined Lycophron perished, so in thy flesh may the barb stick fast.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Scire debet quid petat ille, qui sagittam vult mittere, et tunc derigere ac moderari manu telum.
examples.translation: The archer must know what he is seeking to hit; then he must aim and control the weapon by his skill.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a trembling, quaking, throbbing, panting with fear, desire, joy, etc., anxiety, fear, dread, alarm, etc. (perh. not used by Cic.; syn.: metus, timor, tremor)

examples.original: Ita magna pars absenti hosti cessit: quos intra vallum egerat pavor—fuere autem ad triginta milia —omnes caesi, castra direpta.
examples.translation: Those whom panic had driven within the enclosure—to the number of some thirty thousand—were all put to the sword, and the camp was spoiled.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: A quibus perlatus ad primos tumultus eo pavore signaque et ordines turbavit ut neque imperia exaudiri neque instrui acies posset.
examples.translation: At the very instant when the column was getting clear of the camp, the Volsci, as though set in motion by the same signal, fell upon their rear.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nam prior e campis ut conspicit amne soluto Rumpi Caesar iter, calida proclamat ab ira: ”Non satis est muris latebras quaesisse pavori?
examples.translation: Caesar got the start of him: from the plain he saw that they were letting loose the river to interrupt his march; and in hot anger he cried out: ”Cowards!
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: humbly begging or entreating; humble, submissive, beseeching, suppliant, supplicant (class.; syn.: humilis, submissus).

examples.original: Sic Numitori ad supplicium Remus deditur.
examples.translation: So Remus was given up to Numitor to be punished.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quam quidem nunc multitudinem videtis, iudices, in squalore et luctu supplicem vobis.
examples.translation: You see them thronging this court to-day, gentlemen of the jury;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Atqui maximum scelerum supplicium in ipsis est.
examples.translation: And yet the worst punishment for crime lies in the crime itself.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: efficacious, effectual, powerful, efficient (mostly postAug.; not in Cic. and Caes; but cf. efficacitas): nosti Marcellum, quam tardus et parum efficax sit, Cael. ap.
Latin: Efficiens

examples.original: Negat quicquam esse hac, ut ait, pisatione efficacius;
examples.translation: There is nothing, he says, more effective than this packing processb;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Primum adeo anceps fuit, ut—par utrimque discrimen—capta sint hinc Caesaris castra, inde Cassi. Sed quanto efficacior est fortuna, quam virtus!
examples.translation: At first the issue was so doubtful that, danger threatening both sides alike, the camp of Caesar was captured on the one hand and that of Cassius on the other.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a wall (cf.: murus, maceria): aut permaceat paries percussus trifaci, Enn. ap. Fest. s. v. trifax, p. 367 Müll. (Ann. v. 524 Vahl.): tosti alti stant parietes, id. ap.
Latin: Murus domum, aliudve privatum aedificium ambiens et sustinens

examples.original: Tectis ac parietibus iura dicturi estis?
examples.translation: Is it to roofs and walls you will render judgment?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Statuam habet Praeneste, in inferiore fori parte contra hemicyclium, in quo fastos a se ordinatos et marmoreo parieti incisos publicarat.
examples.translation: His statue stands at Praeneste in the upper part of the forum near the hemicycle, on which he exhibited the calendar which he had arranged and inscribed upon its marble walls.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: to shake, jolt, toss in carrying; hence, in gen., to move violently, to shake, agitate.

examples.original: Quam copiose ac varie vexavit antiquos!
examples.translation: With what readiness and versatility did he make war upon the ancients!
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Caesar rursus ad vexandos hostes profectus magno coacto numero ex finitimis civitatibus in omnes partes dimittit.
examples.translation: Caesar marched forth again to harass the enemy, and, collecting a great host from the neighbouring states, he sent them off in every direction.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Multas enim civitates incendium vexavit, nullam abstulit.
examples.translation: For fire has damaged many a city, but has annihilated none.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: but anyhow

examples.original: Atqui melius fuisset non queri quam vindicari.
examples.translation: Yet surely it were better to have no grievances than to need to seek redress.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Atqui haec patefactio quasi rerum opertarum, cum quid quidque sit aperitur, definitio est;
examples.translation: Now this process of disclosing latent meanings, of revealing what a particular thing is, is the process of definition;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Atqui pugnantibus et contrariis studiis consiliisque semper utens nihil quieti videre, nihil tranquilli potest.
examples.translation: But one who is perpetually swayed by conflicting and incompatible counsels and desires can know no peace or calm.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make fast, make firm, bind (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense—for syn. cf.: decerno, scisco, statuo, jubeo, constituo, sancio, definio).

examples.original: Non certum ad hos ictus destinavi locum;
examples.translation: For these mortal strokes I have set no definite spot;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec inter seniores morti destinatos iactata solacia.
examples.translation: Such were the consolations which the old men appointed to die exchanged among themselves;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed nec tum inminentia cladis destinatae signa latuerunt.
examples.translation: On this occasion too threatening signs of impending disaster were not lacking.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: as, like as, just as
Latin: Eo modo quo
Latin: (relativ.) Eo modo quo

examples.original: Omnibus illa Civibus effudit totas per moenia vires Obvia ceu laeto: promittunt munera flentes, Pandunt templa, domos, socios se cladibus optant.
examples.translation: She poured out all her population through her gates, and met him like a conqueror with all her inhabitants;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Et quidem unum esse deum summum sine initio, sine prole naturae ceu patrem magnum atque magnificum quis tam demens, tam mente captus neget esse certissimum?
examples.translation: And indeed, who is so foolish, so mentally astray, as to deny the very certain truth that there is one supreme god, without beginning, without natural offspring, like a great and splendid father?
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a noise, sound (syn. fragor): et pereunte viro raucum sonus aere cucurrit, Enn. ap. Lact. ap.
Latin: Res percepta aures afficiens per impulsum vel vibrationem substantiae materialis

examples.original: Nec facile est animo dulcem sonum excutere;
examples.translation: It is not easy to rid the memory of a catching tune;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tu quoque, cui veneris sensum natura negavit, Dulcia mendaci gaudia finge sono.
examples.translation: You to whom nature has denied the sensation of love, counterfeit the sweet bliss with lying sounds.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Et hunc tu, non dico inter viros numeras, sed inter homines, cuius summum bonum saporibus et coloribus sonisque constat?
examples.translation: And do you rate, I will not say among heroes, but among men, the person whose Supreme Good is a matter of flavours and colours and sounds?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: harshness, severity, cruelty, barbarity (in good prose and very freq.)

examples.original: Non avaritia, non crudelitas modum novit.
examples.translation: There are no limits to our greed, none to our cruelty.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac variis dictis sententiis, quarum pars deditionem, pars, dum vires suppeterent, eruptionem censebat, non praetereunda oratio Critognati videtur propter eius singularem et nefariam crudelitatem.
examples.translation: Various opinions were expressed, one party voting for surrender, another for a sortie while their strength sufficed: but the speech of Critognatus should not, I think, be omitted, because of its remarkable and abominable cruelty.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Crescit insolenti superbia, crudelitas saevo, malignitas livido.
examples.translation: The haughty man increases his arrogance, the ruthless man his cruelty, the slanderer his spitefulness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: dirty, unclean, foul, filthy, squalid, sordid (class.).

examples.original: Haerebit tibi avaritia, quamdiu avaro sordidoque convixeris;
examples.translation: As long as this companion is avaricious and mean, greed will stick to you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec cogitatio nihil sordidum animo subsidere sinit, nihil humile, nihil crudele.
examples.translation: Such thoughts permit nothing mean to settle in the soul, nothing low, nothing cruel.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Is diu sordidus, repente dives mutationem fortunae male tegebat, accensis egestate longa cupidinibus im moderatus et inopi iuventa senex prodigus.
examples.translation: His desires had been increased by long poverty, so that he now put no restraint upon himself, and after a youth of poverty became a prodigal old man.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to make joyful, to delight, cheer, gladden.

examples.original: Laeta enim principia magistratus eius nimis luxuriavere;
examples.translation: For the luxuriant beginnings of this magistracy took on too rank a growth;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Omnibus illa Civibus effudit totas per moenia vires Obvia ceu laeto: promittunt munera flentes, Pandunt templa, domos, socios se cladibus optant.
examples.translation: She poured out all her population through her gates, and met him like a conqueror with all her inhabitants;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Inclita Caesareis Genabos dissolvitur alis.\] Tu quoque laetatus converti proelia, Trevir, Et nunc tonse Ligur, quondam per colla decore Crinibus effusis toti praelate Comatae;
examples.translation: The Treviri too rejoiced that the troops were moved; so did the Ligurians with hair now cropped, though once they excelled all the longhaired land in the locks that fell in beauty over their necks;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a rock

examples.original: Quis rupium praerupta inimicus opposuit?
examples.translation: Who has out of enmity set up steep rocks against you?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Non speciem agminis Gallorum per Tarpeiam rupem scandentis?
examples.translation: Could they not see the line of Gauls scaling the Tarpeian Rock?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Thessaliam, qua parte diem brumalibus horis Attollit Titan, rupes Ossaea coercet;
examples.translation: Thessaly is bounded by the peak of Ossa in the quarter where the sun rises in winter;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: lo! behold! see! see there!

examples.original: En cor Zenodoti, en iecur Cratetis.
examples.translation: Lo! Crates’ heart, mind of Zenodotus.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Arma cuncti spectant et bellum: en unquam futurum ut congredi armatis cum Samnite liceat?
examples.translation: Would ever the hour come, they asked, when they might encounter the Samnites, sword in hand?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: En vobis” inquit ”iuvenem” filium tenens, ”effigiem atque imaginem eius quem vos antea tribunum militum ex plebe primum fecistis.
examples.translation: Here,” he cried, laying hold of his son, ”here is a young man, the effigy and likeness of him you formerly chose for military tribune first of all plebeians.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to wash, lave.—

examples.original: Et utinam sic denique lues ista vindicetur!
examples.translation: And would that this pest might so at last be overcome!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Magno malo ulla voce interpellatum silentium luitur.
examples.translation: There is a grievous penalty for the slightest breach of silence.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Omnia ista in longa vita sunt, quomodo in longa via et pulvis et lutum et pluvia.
examples.translation: I will touch the truth more closely, and say that you feared for your life.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: some, several
Latin: Aliquis, quidam

examples.original: Censuerunt etiam quidam ut Pannonicus, alii ut Invictus, nonnulli ut Pius cognominaretur.
examples.translation: Some also recommended that he be given the surname of Pannonicus, others of Invictus, others of Pius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Unde existimo nonnullos tradere ausos, suspectum eum Augusto revocatumque ex provincia et quia cunctaretur, interceptum veneno.
examples.translation: This I have mentioned, rather not to pass it by, than that I think it true or even probable;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nam in provincias quoque grammatica penetraverat, ac nonnulli de notissimis doctoribus peregre docuerunt, maxime in Gallia Togata; inter quos Octavius Teucer et Sescenius Iaccus et Oppius Chares;
examples.translation: In fact, Grammar even made its way into the provinces, and some of the most famous teachers gave instruction abroad, especially in Gallia Togata, including Octavius Teucer, Sescenius Iaccus and Oppius Chares;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: to stand out, project; to be extant

examples.original: Quid tuti superest, cum nominis extat adulter, Et credi quod non contigit esse, cupit?
examples.translation: What remains secure, when the dishonourer of her name abides, and would have what ne’er befell believed?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Bellvm Civile Caesaris et Pompei IIII, 2Iam toto orbe paene pacato maius erat imperium Romanum, quam ut ullis exteris viribus opprimi posset.
examples.translation: The Civil War between Caesar and Pompeius 2. Almost the whole world having been now subjugated, the Roman Empire was too strong to be overcome by any foreign power.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Extiterat quidam Scribonianum se Camerinum ferens, Neronianorum temporum metu in Histria occultatum, quod illic clientelae et agri veterum Crassorum ac nominis favor manebat.
examples.translation: A man appeared who gave himself out as Scribonianus Camerinus, alleging that he had remained concealed in Istria during Nero’s reign, for there the ancient Crassi still possessed clients, lands, and popularity.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: To visit or resort to frequently, to frequent; to do or make use of frequently, to repeat (class.)

examples.original: Quorundam illustrium exsequias usque ad rogum frequentavit.
examples.translation: He attended the obsequies of certain distinguished men, even going to the funeral-pyre.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Cogita, quod soleo frequenter tibi dicere, in istis nos nihil aliud quam acumen exercere.
examples.translation: For I return again and again to the thought: ”What good does this do me?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Conveniunt frequentes prima luce: ipse Tarquinius diem quidem servavit, sed paulo ante quam sol occideret venit.
examples.translation: There had been much talk in the council all day about various subjects.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: that comes from foreign parts, strange, foreign, exotic (cf.: exter, externus).

examples.original: Haec tum sacra Romulus una ex omnibus peregrina suscepit, iam tum inmortalitatis virtute partae, ad quam eum sua fata ducebant, fautor.
examples.translation: This was the only sacred observance, of all those of foreign origin, which Romulus then adopted, honouring even then the immortality won by worth to which his own destiny was leading him.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vos omnibus, civibus, peregrinis, tot finitimis populis, spectaculo abeuntes fuisse, vestras coniuges, vestros liberos traductos per ora hominum?
examples.translation: That you furnished a spectacle to everybody when you departed—to the citizens, to the strangers, to all the neighbouring nations?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mox, ne honore nullo regium genus peregrinam stirpem antecelleret, ipsa quam intulerant scientia hospites cessere: tantum Cinyrades sacerdos consulitur.
examples.translation: Only a descendant of Cinyras is now consulted as priest. Such victims are accepted as the individual vows, but male ones are preferred.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to stay or remain behind (freq. and class.: cf. commoror).

examples.original: Adhuc enim non pueritia sed, quod est gravius, puerilitas remanet.
examples.translation: For it is not boyhood that still stays with us, but something worse,—boyishness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Maturo ceterisque remanere et in verba Vespasiani adigi volentibus fuit.
examples.translation: Maturus and the rest chose to remain and take the oath of fidelity to Vespasian.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Legati quoque (nam senatus electionem Galbae permiserat) foeda inconstantia nominati, excusati, substituti, ambitu remanendi aut eundi, ut quemque metus vel spes impulerat.
examples.translation: With disgraceful lack of firmness he named men, excused them, made substitutions, as they pleaded with him to stay or go, according to their fears or hopes.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: of or belonging to the country, rural, rustic
Latin: Qui ad rus pertinet, rure

examples.original: Vehiculum, in quod inpositus sum, rusticum est;
examples.translation: The vehicle in which I have taken my seat is a farmer’s cart.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Temporibus certis maturam rusticus uvam Deligit, et nudo sub pede musta fluunt;
examples.translation: At fixed seasons the countryman picks the ripened grapes, and the vintage flows beneath his naked foot;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nec Venus oranti (neque enim dea mollior ulla est) Rustica Gradivo difficilisque fuit.
examples.translation: Nor was Venus bashful (for no goddess has a tenderer heart), nor unresponsive to Gradivus’ prayers.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a Parthian; v. Parthi.

examples.original: Sed cecidit Babylone sua Parthoque verendus.
examples.translation: He died, however, in Babylon he had conquered;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Tu quoque, cui rugis uterum Lucina notavit, Ut celer aversis utere Parthus equis.
examples.translation: And you whose belly Lucina has marked with wrinkles, like the swift Parthian, use a backward-turned steed.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Parthe, dabis poenas: Crassi gaudete sepulti, Signaque barbaricas non bene passa manu.
examples.translation: Parthian, thou shalt pay penalty; rejoice, ye buried Crassi, and ye standards that shamefully endured barbarian violence.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: of or belonging to the Stoic philosophy or to the Stoics, Stoic

examples.original: Quid enim est a Chrysippo praetermissum in Stoicis?
examples.translation: Take Stoicism: what aspect of it has Chrysippus left untouched?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Facete M. Piso familiaris noster et alia multa et hoc loco Stoicos irridebat.
examples.translation: Our friend Marcus Piso was often witty, but never more so than when he ridiculed the Stoics on this score.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: At vero illa quae Peripatetici, quae Stoici dicunt, semper tibi in ore sunt in iudiciis, in senatu.
examples.translation: Ah, but it is the vocabulary of the Peripatetics and the Stoics that is always on your lips, in the law-courts and the senate.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: dark, gloomy, frowning, horrible, hideous, frightful, dreadful; and trop., savage, cruel, fierce, atrocious, harsh

examples.original: Atrox ingenium accenderat eo facto magis quam conterruerat;
examples.translation: The man’s fierce nature was rather aroused by this than terrified;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Initium atrocis in Caecinam sententiae a L. Vitellio factum;
examples.translation: Lucius Vitellius took the lead in proposing severe measures directed against Caecina;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Eo anno non segnior discordia domi et bellum foris atrocius fuit.
examples.translation: The Aequi took up arms, and the Veientes even made a foray into Roman territory.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: place

examples.original: Non dicimus ”reposuit beneficium” aut ”solvit”;
examples.translation: We do not say, ”He has ’restored’ the benefit,” or ’settled’ it;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: At vero praeclarum diem illis reposuisti Verria ut agerent, et ut ad eum diem quae sacris epulisque opus essent in complures annos locarentur.
examples.translation: What a day for which to make contracts, years in advance, for supplying the materials of its ceremonies and banquets!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Haec singuli, haec universi, ut quemque dolor impulerat, vociferantes, initio a quinta legione orto, repositis Vitellii imaginibus vincla Caecinae iniciunt;
examples.translation: With such cries, now separately, now in a body, as indignation moved each, the Fifth legion taking the lead, they replaced the statues of Vitellius and threw Caecina into chains.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: A moving, agitating, setting in motion

examples.original: Magnum opus est egetque exercitatione non parva.
examples.translation: This is a difficult thing to do and requires no little practice.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Hic autem est exercitationis etiam fortissimis finis.
examples.translation: And weariness is the aim and end of exercise, no matter how strong one is.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hae sunt exercitationes ingeni, haec curricula mentis;
examples.translation: These employments are my intellectual gymnastics; these the race-courses of my mind;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: useless, unserviceable, unprofitable; constr.

examples.original: Sed ne inutilis quidem haec fabella fuerit.
examples.translation: The anecdote may also be of some use;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quaedam inutilia et inefficacia ipsa subtilitas reddit.
examples.translation: And certain arguments are rendered useless and unavailing by their very subtlety.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Magnopere se suadere populo, ne inutili pudore suam ipse causam damnaret.
examples.translation: He earnestly counselled the people not to condemn their own cause from an unreasonable motive of propriety.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: in before
Latin: Secunda littera alphabeti Romani, be dicitur

examples.original: B. Latinis victis montem Aventinum adsignavit, fines protulit, Hostiam coloniam deduxit, caerimonias a Numa institutas renovavit.
examples.translation: Summary of Book I B. Having beaten the Latins, he assigned them the Aventine Hill; planted a colony at Ostia;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to place together, to arrange, to station

examples.original: At illum in aliis mundi finibus sua virtus collocavit nihil vobiscum commune habentem.
examples.translation: But his virtue has placed him in another region of the universe; he has nothing in common with you.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Huic permisit, si opus esse arbitraretur, uti in his locis legionem hiemandi causa collocaret.
examples.translation: A certain number of successful engagements were fought; several of the enemy’s forts were taken by storm;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quintum Tullium Ciceronem et Publium Sulpicium Cabilloni et Matiscone in Aeduis ad Ararim rei frumentariae causa collocat.
examples.translation: Quintus Tullius Cicero and Publius Sulpicius he stationed at Cabillonum and Matisco, Aeduan towns near the Arar, to secure the corn-supply.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: incense, frankincense.

examples.original: Dique latent templis neque iniqua ad funera vultus Praebent nec poscunt tura ferenda rogo: Obscuros delubra tenent;
examples.translation: The gods are hidden in their temples, nor show their faces at this unrighteous death, nor demand the incense needed by the pyre;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nec non in meridiem verso agmine Libanum Syriae Damascumque transgressus per nemora illa odorata, per turis et balsami silvas Romana signa circumtulit.
examples.translation: Furthermore, turning his army southwards, he passed through the Lebanon in Syria and through Damascus, and bore the Roman standards through the famous scented groves and woods of frankincense and balm.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nunc quoque, tela licet paveant victoris iniqui, Nuntiet ipse licet Caesar tua funera, flebunt, Sed dum tura ferunt, dum laurea serta Tonanti.
examples.translation: Even as it is, though men dread the arms of the tyrannous conqueror, though Caesar himself announce the death, weep they will, even while offering incense and laurel wreaths to the Thunderer. Unhappy Romans!
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: step, pace
Latin: Gradus, gressus
Latin: Mensura Romana, quinque pedes longitudine

examples.original: Hic locus ab hoste circiter passus sescentos, uti dictum est, aberat.
examples.translation: The spot, as has been said, was about six hundred paces away from the enemy.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quae putas me passum, dum per aspera erepo, dum viam quaero, dum facio?
examples.translation: What do you think my feelings were, scrambling over the rocks, searching out the path, or making one for myself?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eam rem aegre passi Romani M. Furium Camillum sextum tribunum militum creavere.
examples.translation: This incensed the Romans, and they elected Marcus Furius Camillus tribune of the soldiers, for the sixth time.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to shut out, exclude; to cut off, remove

examples.original: Iam non excludere tantum, Inclusisse volunt.
examples.translation: They say that they seek to drive away the horrid taint of war.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Omnes exclusi sunt non minus aperte quam pupillus. Diem praestituit operi faciundo Kalendas Decembres, locat circiter Idus Septembres;
examples.translation: The day Verres fixed for the undertaking to be completed was the 1st of December, and he let the contract about the 13th of September;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum vagus et exsul erraret atque undique exclusus Oppianicus in Falernum se ad L. Quinctium contulisset, ibi primum in morbum incidit ac satis vehementer diuque aegrotavit.
examples.translation: Wandering about, a vagabond and an exile, and finding all doors shut against him, Oppianicus betook himself to L. Quinctius in the Falernian district. It was there that he first fell sick;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the name of a Roman gens. So esp., A. Vitellius, a Roman emperor.—Hence

examples.original: Pro consule Vitellium Siliani in Africa habuerant;
examples.translation: This detachment had served under Vitellius when he was proconsul in Africa;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Vitelliis Aquiliisque fratribus primo commissa res est.
examples.translation: The brothers Vitellii and Aquilii were the first to be entrusted with the project.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Trachalum adversus criminantis Galeria uxor Vitellii protexit.
examples.translation: Trachalus was protected against his accusers by Galeria, the wife of Vitellius.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to push, strike, beat (cf.: tundo, ferio, pello).

examples.original: Laetus fragor aethera pulsat Victorum;
examples.translation: A shout from his conquerors made the welkin ring;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: A quotiens frustra pulsatos aequore montes Obruit illa dies!
examples.translation: That day buried mountains which the waves had often before battered in vain;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Plus tamen vis potuit quam voluntas patris aut verecundia aetatis: pulso fratre Amulius regnat.
examples.translation: Amulius drove out his brother and ruled in his stead. Adding crime to crime, he destroyed Numitor’s male issue;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a wolf.
Latin: Animal mammiferum speciei Canis lupus. Lupus
Latin: Piscis familiae Anarhichadidae, praesertim Anarhichas lupus. Lupus

examples.original: Pax erit haec nobis, donec mihi vita manebit, Cum pecore infirmo quae solet esse lupis.
examples.translation: That peace shall we enjoy, while life remains to me, which wolves are wont to keep with the defenceless flock.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ut fugiunt aquilas, timidissima turba, columbae, Ut fugit invisos agna novella lupos: Sic illae timuere viros sine more ruentes;
examples.translation: As doves, most timorous of birds, flee from the eagles, as the weanling lamb from the hated wolf, so feared they the men rushing wildly on them;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: ripe, mature (class.).

examples.original: Nondum maturus imperio Ascanius Aeneae filius erat;
examples.translation: Ascanius, Aeneas’ son, was not yet ripe for authority;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In principatu maturius semper ac de nocte vigilabat;
examples.translation: While emperor, he always rose very early, in fact before daylight;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: At mihi maturos numquam licet edere fetus, Ante diemque meae decutiuntur opes.
examples.translation: But I may never bring forth ripe progeny, and my wealth is struck off before its prime.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to be fierce or furious, to rage, to vent one's rage (very freq. since the Aug. per.; once in Cæs.; not in Cic.; but saevus and saevitia several times in Cic.).

examples.original: Calatia et Sora praesidiaque quae in his Romana erant expugnata et in captivorum corpora militum foede saevitum.
examples.translation: Calatia and Sora with their Roman garrisons were taken by assault, and the captured soldiers were treated with shameful rigour.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: length.

examples.original: Hoc milia passuum octingenta in longitudinem esse existimatur.
examples.translation: The side is supposed to be eight hundred miles long.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to flame, blaze, burn (class.; trop. signif. most freq.; not in Caes.; syn.: ardeo, deflagro, caleo, ferveo, etc.).

examples.original: Tu, qui flagrante minacem Scorpion incendis cauda chelasque peruris, Quid tantum, Gradive, paras?
examples.translation: But Mars—what dreadful purpose has he, when he kindles the Scorpion menacing with fiery tail and scorches its claws?
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Itaque horum adventu decem milia armatorum completa sunt, quae manus mirabili flagrabat pugnandi cupiditate.
examples.translation: They sent a thousand soldiers, whose arrival raised the number of combatants to ten thousand.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

examples.original: Haec ergo atque eiusmodi solacia admoveo Liberali nostro incredibili quodam patriae suae amore flagranti, quae fortasse consumpta est, ut in melius excitaretur.
examples.translation: Hence it is thoughts like these, and of this kind, which I am offering as consolation to our friend Liberalis, who burns with a love for his country that is beyond belief.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to draw out or forth, to drag out (class.).

examples.original: Tollenda est atque extrahenda radicitus.
examples.translation: It ought to be destroyed, uprooted altogether.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ita extracta utraque res in consulum adventum est.
examples.translation: So both affairs dragged on till the arrival of the consuls.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Extrahitur domo latitans Oppianicus a Manlio: index Avillius ex altera parte coram tenetur.
examples.translation: Manlius dragged the skulking Oppianicus from his house, and the informer Avillius was made to confront him.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: monstrous in size, enormous, immense, huge, vast (class.).
English: slow, tardy, slack, dilatory, lingering, sluggish, inactive, unenergetic, lazy

examples.original: An similem vestri segnemque ad fata putatis?
examples.translation: Think you that I am like yourselves and unwilling to die?
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Non segnior oppugnatio est quam pugna fuerat.
examples.translation: The assault was no less vigorous than the battle had been.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quatiebatur his segne ingenium ut concupisceret magis quam ut speraret.
examples.translation: These arguments stirred his sluggish nature to covetousness rather than to hope.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: icy cold, very cold

examples.original: Vesperascente die sitim haustu gelidae aquae sedavit.
examples.translation: As evening approached he slaked his thirst with a draught of cold water.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Tum Sadalam fortemque Cotyn fidumque per arma Deiotarum et gelidae dominum Rhascypolin orae Conlaudant, Libyamque iubent auctore senatu Sceptrifero parere Iubae.
examples.translation: Praise was given also to Sadalas and brave Cotys, to the faithful ally, Deiotarus, and to Rhascypolis, lord of a frozen land;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a gift, present.
Latin: Aliquid, quod alicui datur gratis et quod reddere huic necesse non est
Latin: Aliquid, quod alicui datur et quod reddere huic necesse non est
entries.etymology: From the PIE root *deh₃- 'give'; Greek δῶρον is a cognate.

examples.original: Hernicis ipsum agerque dono datus.
examples.translation: The town itself and its territory were given to the Hernici.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Coronam auream Iovi donum in Capitolium mittunt.
examples.translation: They sent a golden crown as a gift to the Capitoline Jupiter.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec minus quam est pollicitus Vercingetorix animo laborabat ut reliquas civitates adiungeret, atque eas donis pollicitationibusque alliciebat.
examples.translation: As good as his promise, Vercingetorix worked with a will to bring in the remaining states, and tried to attract them by presents and promises.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the name of a Roman gens; so

examples.original: Idea erat Vergilii facies, futuri operis exemplar.
examples.translation: The ”idea” was Vergil’s outward appearance, and this was the pattern of the intended work.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed Vergilius a Cremona Mediolanum et inde paulo post transiit in urbem.
examples.translation: Virgil, however, moved from Cremona to Mediolanum, and shortly afterwards from there to Rome.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Quem quo minus Ovidius tractaret, nihil obstitit, quod iam Vergilius impleverat.
examples.translation: Ovidc could not be prevented from using this theme simply because Vergild had already fully covered it;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to supply with a mouth or outlet, to extend a channel, e. g. the veins

examples.original: Quis sapiens blandis non misceat oscula verbis?
examples.translation: Who that is wise would not mingle kisses with coaxing words?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quod responsum cum ipsi aliter interpretarentur, Iunius Brutus, qui cum his profectus erat, prolapsum se simulavit et terram osculatus est;
examples.translation: This response the princes themselves explained otherwise, but Junius Brutus, who had accompanied them, pretended to fall upon his face, and kissed the earth.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Brutus alio ratus spectare Pythicam vocem velut si prolapsus cecidisset terram osculo contigit, scilicet quod ea communis mater omnium mortalium esset.
examples.translation: Brutus thought the Pythian utterance had another meaning; pretending to stumble, he fell and touched his lips to Earth, evidently regarding her as the common mother of all mortals.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To shut up, to enclose.

examples.original: Ferro igitur eam arcere contumeliam statuunt.
examples.translation: They therefore determined to repel that insult with the sword.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quid mundi gladios a sanguine Caesaris arces?
examples.translation: Why do you keep away the swords of all mankind from Caesar’s throat?
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nec illi tulere impetum, sed ab effusa fuga flumen obiectum ab tergo arcebat.
examples.translation: They, too, failed to withstand his attack, but their rout was stopped by the river in their rear.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the lower part of the trunk of plants, including the roots; a stock, stem, stalk; a root

examples.original: De hominum genere aut omnino de animalium loquor, cum arborum et stirpium eadem paene natura sit?
examples.translation: But do I speak of the human race or of animals generally, when the nature of trees and plants is almost the same?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Mox, ne honore nullo regium genus peregrinam stirpem antecelleret, ipsa quam intulerant scientia hospites cessere: tantum Cinyrades sacerdos consulitur.
examples.translation: Only a descendant of Cinyras is now consulted as priest. Such victims are accepted as the individual vows, but male ones are preferred.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: with sails and oars, i. e. with all one's might, with all possible speed
Latin: Instrumentum, quo naves aguntur

examples.original: Sic Numitori ad supplicium Remus deditur.
examples.translation: So Remus was given up to Numitor to be punished.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Caesar Ab his castris oppidum Remorum nomine Bibrax aberat milia passuum octo.
examples.translation: From this camp a town of the Remi called Bibrax was eight miles distant.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Cum mora non tuta est, totis incumbere remis Utile, et admisso subdere calcar equo.
examples.translation: When delay is dangerous, it is best to press on with all oars, and to spur the galloping horse.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to blow
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; flāvi, flātum, 1

examples.original: Satius est amicum reparare quam flere.
examples.translation: It is better to replace your friend than to weep for him.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid M. Plaetori et C. Flamini inter sicarios?
examples.translation: What of the Assassination Court of M. Plaetorius and G. Flaminius?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In incessu, in statu, in habitu, in omnibus motibus vestris nihil flat, quod inliciat cuiusquam libidinem, sed quod vestram deceat sanctitatem.
examples.translation: In walking, in standing, in deportment, in all your movements, let nothing be done that might attract the desire of anyone, but let everything be in keeping with your holy character.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: one after the other, by turns, interchangeable, alternate

examples.original: Hos tam graves dominos, interdum alternis imperantes, interdum pariter, dimittit a te sapientia, quae sola libertas est.
examples.translation: These passions, which are heavy taskmasters, sometimes ruling by turns, and sometimes together, can be banished from you by wisdom, which is the only real freedom.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: pertaining to the house

examples.original: Tum pulsus Etruria Libo, Vmbria Thermus, Domitius Corfinio.
examples.translation: Libo was driven out of Etruria, Thermus from Umbria, Domitius from Corfinium.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nero I. Ex gente Domitia duae familiae claruerunt, Calvinorum et Ahenobarborum.
examples.translation: Nero Nero I. Of the Domitian family two branches have acquired distinction, the Calvini and the Ahenobarbi.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Non te pudet, Verres, eius mulieris arbitratu gessisse praeturam quam L. Domitius ab se nominari vix sibi honestum esse arbitrabatur?
examples.translation: Do you feel no shame, Verres, that your conduct as praetor has been wholly governed by a woman whose very name Domitius feels it hardly decent for him to mention?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: plant in; to ingraft (class.).
Latin: struere aliquid in aliqua re

examples.original: Nam et horum inprecatio falsos nobis metus inserit et illorum amor male docet bene optando.
examples.translation: The angry prayers of our enemies instil false fears in us; and the affection of our friends spoils us through their kindly wishes.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tela iugo vincta est, stamen secernit harundo, Inseritur medium radiis subtemen acutis, Quod lato paviunt insecti pectine dentes.
examples.translation: The web is bound to frame; asunder now The reed doth part the warp.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Insertum manibus chalybem nigramque per artus Stillantis tabi saniem virusque coactum Sustulit, et nervo morsus retinente pependit.
examples.translation: She purloins the nails that pierced the hands, the clotted filth, and the black humour of corruption that oozes over all the limbs;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: very eager, violent, furious, impetuous, ardent, vehement, etc. (syn. violentus).

examples.original: Quod ubi accidit, barbari vehementissimo cursu refugerunt.
examples.translation: When this occurred, the natives fled away at a most furious speed.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: In hos igitur, quia vehementius agere nuntiabatur, non est mandata expeditio, sed sumpta.
examples.translation: The news of their unusual activity induced Caesar himself to undertake an expedition instead of entrusting it to another.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Etenim paucis postea mensibus alia vehemens erat in iudiciis ex notatione tabellarum invidia versata.
examples.translation: No one had a chance to denounce that view; no one in fact exerted himself to urge the opposite side.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: difficulty, trouble, distress, poverty, want.

examples.original: Ex ea difficultate illae ’fallaciloquae,’ ut ait Attius, ’malitiae,’ natae sunt.
examples.translation: This is the difficulty that gave birth to those ’base conceits deceitful-tongued,’ as Attius has it.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: and not, nor, and that not, and lest: utinam ne in nemore, etc.... neve inde, etc., Enn. ap.

examples.original: Nec quae ferre solet spatiantem porticus illam, Te ferat, officium neve colatur idem.
examples.translation: And frequent not the colonnade that she frequents when walking, nor cultivate the same society.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Est enim boni viri, quem eundem sapientem licet dicere, haec duo tenere in amicitia : primum, ne quid fictum sit neve simulatum;
examples.translation: For it is characteristic of the good man, whom I may also call the wise man, to maintain these two rules in friendship : first, let there be no feigning or hypocrisy;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Omnino omnium horum vitiorum atque incommodorum una cautio est atque una provisio, ut ne nimis cito diligere incipiant neve non dignos.
examples.translation: In short : there is but one security and one provision against these ills and annoyances, and that is, neither to enlist your love too quickly nor to fix it on unworthy men.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: similarly
Latin: simili modo

examples.original: Ut quid dicit similiter: Spiritus adiuvat infirmitatem nostram, si natura nostra sic creata est, ut spiritu ad opera iustitiae non indigeat adiuvari?
examples.translation: And why does he likewise say, ”The Spirit helpeth our infirmities,”f if our nature is created such that it does not need any help from the Spirit to do the works of righteousness?
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: the troops stationed in reserve in the third line of battle (behind the principes), the line of reserve, reserve-ranks

examples.original: Impulsa frons prima et trepidatio subsidiis inlata;
examples.translation: Their front was first driven in and communicated its disorder to the supports;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Prima luce ad moenia omnibus copiis admotis corona cinxit urbem subsidiaque firma, ne qua eruptio fieret, portis opposuit.
examples.translation: With the dawn he led up all his forces under the walls and invested the city, posting strong supports to prevent any sally from the gates.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Aedui de consilio legatorum, quos Caesar ad exercitum reliquerat, copias equitatus peditatusque subsidio Biturigibus mittunt.
examples.translation: When they were come to the river Loire, which parts the Bituriges from the Aedui, they halted there for a few days;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to place a ladder on one's shoulders by putting one's head between the rounds

examples.original: Discolor et vario furialis cultus amictu Induitur, voltusque aperitur crine remoto, Et coma vipereis substringitur horrida sertis.
examples.translation: She put on motley raiment, whose parti-coloured woof was fit for a fiend to wear; she threw back her hair and revealed her face;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Pompeio vincite, Parthi, Vinci Roma volet.’” Regem parere iubenti Ardua non piguit, positisque insignibus aulae Egreditur famulo raptos indutus amictus.
examples.translation: If the Parthians conquer for Pompey’s sake, Rome will welcome her conqueror.’” Hard was the task enjoined, but the king did not refuse;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to pick, pluck, pluck off, cull, crop, gather (class.; in prose and poetry, esp. in the latter very freq.; syn. decerpere).

examples.original: Ipsae te fugient, quae carpunt omnia, flammae;
examples.translation: The very flames, which consume all things, shall shun thee;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fixus et in duris carparis viscera saxis, Ut cui Pyrrha sui filia fratris erat.
examples.translation: And chained on the hard rocks mayst thou have thine entrails torn, as he whose brother’s daughter Pyrrha was.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Credula si fueris, aliae tua gaudia carpent, Et lepus hic aliis exagitatus erit.
examples.translation: If you are too trusting, other women will reap your joys, and that hare will be hunted by others.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to fight against, oppose; to make resistance, resist, defend one's self (class.; syn.: adversor, resisto, renitor).

examples.original: Tertio Aracelium oppidum magna vi repugnat;
examples.translation: Next the town of Aracelium offered a stout resistance, but was eventually taken.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed id ne cogitari quidem potest quale sit ut non repugnet ipsum sibi.
examples.translation: But it is impossible even to imagine a self-consistent picture of what such a creature would be like.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Missus extemplo Varus cum expedita manu paucos repugnantium interfecit;
examples.translation: Varus was despatched at once with a force in light marching order.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to lash, scourge, whip, flog, beat, drub (class.; syn.: ferio, pulso).

examples.original: Quid tamen hoc prodest, media si luce palamque Verberor et tutae non licet esse nuci?
examples.translation: Yet what does this avail, if openly in broad day I am beaten, and if a nut tree may not be safe?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sic invenies servum qui flagellis quam colaphis caedi malit et qui mortem ac verbera tolerabiliora credat quam contumeliosa verba.
examples.translation: And so you will find the slave who would rather be struck with the lash than the fist, who considers stripes and death more endurable than insulting words.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: (In laevum cecidere latus veloxque Metaurus Crustumiumque rapax et iuncto Sapis Isauro Senaque et Hadriacas qui verberat Aufidus undas;
examples.translation: (Eastward flow the swift Metaurus and rushing Crustumium, the Sapis together with the Isaurus, the Sena, the Aufidus which buffets the waves of the Adriatic;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to set a mark upon, to mark, mark out

examples.original: Nulli subigebant arva coloni, Ne signare quidem aut partiri limite campum Fas erat;
examples.translation: No ploughman tilled the soil, nor was it right To portion off or bound one’s property.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Parthe, dabis poenas: Crassi gaudete sepulti, Signaque barbaricas non bene passa manu.
examples.translation: Parthian, thou shalt pay penalty; rejoice, ye buried Crassi, and ye standards that shamefully endured barbarian violence.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hinc celeriter deiecti se in signa manipulosque coniciunt: eo magis timidos perterrent milites.
examples.translation: They were speedily hurled down from thence, and ran headlong into the company formations, scaring the soldiers into greater alarm.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: serious, grave, strict
Latin: Cognomen Romanum

examples.original: Fratrem Severum et qui cum eo sunt salutamus.
examples.translation: Give my greetings to brother Severusb and his company.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Is A. Postumium Tubertum, socerum suum, severissimi imperii virum, dictatorem dixit;
examples.translation: He appointed Aulus Postumius Tubertus, his father-in-law, a man of the sternest authority;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fortissimae rei inertissima adstruitur, severissimae parum seria, sanctissimae intemperans usque ad incesta.
examples.translation: What elements so inharmonious as these can be found united?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: an auqur, diviner, soothsayer; at Rome, a member of a particular college of priests, much reverenced in earlier ages, who made known the future by observing the lightning, the

examples.original: Ita octo pontificum, novem augurum numerus factus.
examples.translation: Thus the number of pontiffs became eight and of augurs nine.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quanta notitia antiquitatis, scientia iuris auguri!
examples.translation: What a knowledge of ancient history! What skill in augural law!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Consulti augures vitiosum videri dictatorem pronuntiaverunt.
examples.translation: This sentence the tribunes by their accusations made suspect and infamous;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of a good kind or nature, beneficent, kind.

examples.original: Ibi benigne excepti divisique in hospitia.
examples.translation: There they were kindly received and were quartered about among the citizens.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Atque utinam, cum magna et dura quatiuntur, parva et flexibilia corrigantur. De domo illa quid dicam, nisi benignissimae tuae curae gratias agam?
examples.translation: And would that, when the tall and sturdy things are shaken, the lowly and yielding may receive correction!
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Venientem Volsci benigne excepere benigniusque in dies colebant, quo maior ira in suos eminebat crebraeque nunc querellae, nunc minae percipiebantur.
examples.translation: Condemned in his absence, he went into exile with the Volsci, uttering threats against his country, and even then breathing hostility.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: disunion, disagreement, dissension, variance, discord (class.)

examples.original: Veientes contra taedio annuae ambitionis, quae interdum discordiarum causa erat, regem creavere.
examples.translation: But the Veientes, weary of annual canvassing, which was sometimes the cause of brawls, chose a king.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Rex Pharnaces magis discordiae nostrae fiducia quam suae virtutis infesto in Cappadociam agmine ruebat.
examples.translation: King Pharnaces, relying rather upon our internal feuds than upon his own valour, invaded Cappadocia with a hostile force.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Proxima inde nocte Volsci, discordia Romana freti, si qua nocturna transitio proditiove fieri posset, temptant castra.
examples.translation: But the sentries perceived them, the army was roused, and, the signal being given, rushed to arms.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to stand out, project (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Secundum ex his, quae sunt, ponit Plato quod eminet et exsuperat omnia. Hoc ait per excellentiam esse.
examples.translation: The second class of ”things which exist,” according to Plato, is that which is prominent and stands out above everything else;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Mors tamen eminuit clarorum in strage virorum Pugnacis Domiti, quem clades fata per omnes Ducebant: nusquam Magni fortuna sine illo Succubuit.
examples.translation: Yet one death was most noticeable in that carnage of famous men—the death of that stubborn warrior, Domitius. Fate led him from defeat to defeat;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Venientem Volsci benigne excepere benigniusque in dies colebant, quo maior ira in suos eminebat crebraeque nunc querellae, nunc minae percipiebantur.
examples.translation: Condemned in his absence, he went into exile with the Volsci, uttering threats against his country, and even then breathing hostility.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to lie down.
English: three hundred each, three hundred distributively

examples.original: Scribebantur autem quattuor fere legiones quinis milibus peditum, equitibus in singulas legiones trecenis.
examples.translation: There were customarily four legions raised of five thousand foot each, with three hundred horse to every legion.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Volscos consilii poenam non metuentes necopinata res perculit; armorum immemores obsides dant trecentos principum a Cora atque Pometia liberos.
examples.translation: They had no thought of resisting, and surrendered as hostages three hundred children of the nobility of Cora and Pometia, and so the legions were withdrawn without a conflict.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Idem ille populus, postea quam maius imperium est nactus et largitione magistratuum corruptus est, trecentas statuas Demetrio Phalereo decrevit.
examples.translation: But that same people, after it had gained greater power and was corrupted by the largess of the magistrates, voted three hundred statues to Demetrius of Phalerum.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

definitions: English: mistress, she who rules or commands, esp. in a household, = hera, materfamilias
Latin: Dominus femineus, era

examples.original: Quam stultum est aetatem disponere ne crastini quidem dominum!
examples.translation: O what madness it is to plot out far-reaching hopes!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed neque tu dominam velis maioribus usus Desere, nec cursus anteat illa tuos;
examples.translation: But neither do you, spreading too full sail, leave your mistress behind, nor let her outstrip your speed;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Paruit imperio dominae Tirynthius heros: I nunc et dubita ferre, quod ille tulit.
examples.translation: The Tirynthian hero obeyed a mistress’ command: go, shrink from enduring what he endured!
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: unskilled in any art or trade, without skill, unskilful (class.): ut perhibetur iners, ars in quo non erit ulla, Lucil. ap.

examples.original: Gloriari otio iners ambitio est.
examples.translation: To boast of our retirement is but idle self-seeking.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid ergo est, quod nos facit pigros inertesque?
examples.translation: What, then, is it which makes us lazy and sluggish?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quis omnia in uno mersa et materia inerti convoluta discreverit?
examples.translation: Do you compel me to withdraw from the whole and restrict me to a part?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to step out or forth, to come forth, emerge, appear (very freq. and class.).
Latin: pro ire
Latin: esse (Latinitas nova)

examples.original: Reliqua vendita, quibus domini non exstitere.
examples.translation: That the consul had earned a triumph all agreed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Magna repente in ipsis operibus flamma exstitit.
examples.translation: A mighty flame suddenly shot forth in the midst of the works;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Tamen longe maiora et firmiora de eo iudicia in morte ac post mortem exstiterunt.
examples.translation: Yet far greater and stronger tokens of regard were shown at the time of his death and immediately afterwards.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: immediately after, just after, presently, forthwith, thereupon (not ante-Aug.)

examples.original: Subinde itaque, Lucili, quam multa sis consecutus recordare.
examples.translation: Therefore continually remind yourself, Lucilius, how many ambitions you have attained.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Mentis valitudinem et ipse senserat ac subinde de secessu deque purgando cerebro cogitavit.
examples.translation: He himself realised his mental infirmity, and thought at times of going into retirement and clearing his brain.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Et subinde matre etiam relegata paene inops atque egens apud amitam Lepidam nutritus est sub duobus paedagogis saltatore atque tonsore.
examples.translation: Then his mother was banished too, and he was brought up at the house of his aunt Lepida almost in actual want, under two tutors, a dancer and a barber.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to wonder at, to be astonished at, to regard with admiration, to admire, to be in a state of mind in which something pleases us by its extraordinary greatness, its sublimity, or
Latin: Mirari ad aliquem

examples.original: Quem Dion adeo admiratus est atque adamavit, ut se ei totum traderet.
examples.translation: Him Dion so admired and loved that he devoted himself to him heart and soul.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

examples.original: Et quod magis admireris: unum bonum est, quod honestum est, cetera falsa et adulterina bona sunt.
examples.translation: Besides (and you may be still more surprised at this), that which is honourable is the only good;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Deinde idem admiratur, quod dicimus fidem nisi in sapiente non esse, tamquam non ipse idem dicat.
examples.translation: Or do you think that there is any loyalty in him who does not know how to return a favour?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: great in deeds or in sentiment, noble, distinguished, eminent, august, great in soul, high-minded (cf. splendidus).

examples.original: Ille dat consilia magnifica et erecta.
examples.translation: He it is that gives noble and upright counsel.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vives, inquit Aristo, magnifice atque praeclare;
examples.translation: O, says Aristo, you will get on splendidly, capitally;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Elegans, non magnificus, splendidus, non sumptuosus;
examples.translation: He was tasteful rather than magnificent, distinguished rather than extravagant;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

definitions: English: a wonderful, strange, or marvellous thing, a wonder, marvel, miracle; wonderfulness, marvellousness (class.; syn.: prodigium, portentum)

examples.original: Ab eo ad stabula Larentiae uxori educandos datos. Sunt qui Larentiam vulgato corpore lupam inter pastores vocatam putent: inde locum fabulae ac miraculo datum.
examples.translation: Some think that Larentia, having been free with her favours, had got the name of ”she-wolf” among the shepherds, and that this gave rise to this marvellous story.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Experiundam rem denique in uno aut altero esse sitne aliqui plebeius ferendo magno honori, an portento simile miraculoque sit fortem ac strenuum virum aliquem exsistere ortum ex plebe.
examples.translation: By exerting their utmost force they had carried the point that military tribunes with consular powers might be chosen even from the plebs.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the bark, rind, shell, hull.

examples.original: At cum maturas fisso nova cortice rimas Nux agit, ad partes pertica saeva venit;
examples.translation: But when the new nut in due season shows chinks in its splitting rind thither comes the cruel rod;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cetera saepe tamen potuere admissa negari, Et crimen nox est infitiata suum: Nostra notat fusco digitos iniuria suco Cortice contactas inficiente manus.
examples.translation: Yet other crimes when committed can often be denied, and night disavows her guilty deed: injury done to me marks the fingers with dark juice, and my bark stains the hands that touch it.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: breadth, width of any thing (class.).

examples.original: Erat quidem corpus validum ac forte sortitus et illi nomen latitudo pectoris fecerat, sed navigationes ac pericula multum detraxerant viribus;
examples.translation: To be sure, he was the fortunate possessor of a strong and sound body (his very name was given him because of his broad chesta);
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quod cum ex omnibus in circuitu partibus altissimas rupes despectusque haberet, una ex parte leniter acclivis aditus in latitudinem non amplius ducentorum pedum relinquebatur;
examples.translation: On every side of its circumference it looked down over the steepest rocks, and on one side only was left a gently sloping approach, not more than two hundred feet in breadth.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: impost, tribute, contribution (payable in money; whereas vectigal in kind; the former being regarded as the more humiliating; v. stipendiarius, I.): Poeni stipendia pendunt, Enn

examples.original: Additae huic classi duae fabrum centuriae, quae sine armis stipendia facerent;
examples.translation: There were added to this class two centuries of mechanics, who were to serve without arms;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hunc eximium florem iuventutis eo etiam quod ut duplex acciperent stipendium decreverant, spei animorumque implevere;
examples.translation: This choice flower of their manhood they inspired with additional hope and courage by a decree which allowed them double pay.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Samnitem illis exercitum paratum, instructum armis, stipendio venisse, et confestim secuturos, vel si ad ipsam Romanam urbem oppugnandam ducant.
examples.translation: Here was a Samnite army, provided with arms and pay, and ready to follow on the instant, though they should lead it to the assault of Rome itself.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: rich in something, full, fruitful, fertile, abundant, plentiful, copious, productive (class.; syn.: ferax, fertilis, fecundus).
Latin: Qui multos fructus dare potest, fertilis (dicitur de agris, regionibus et similibus)

examples.original: Fertilior seges est alienis semper in agris, Vicinumque pecus grandius uber habet.
examples.translation: In fields not ours the crops are ever more bounteous, and the neighbouring herd has richer udders.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: pass to and fro: remeare redire, ut commeare ultro citroque ire, unde commeatus

examples.original: Ab urbe commeatus intentiore quam antea subvehi cura, ne quid tam bene merito exercitui ad usum deesset.
examples.translation: The city dispatched provisions with more than its former zeal, that nothing might be lacking to an army that had deserved so well.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ad cuius spectaculum commeare in urbem non solum praesidibus provinciarum permisit, verum etiam exsulibus quibusdam;
examples.translation: To witness the sight he allowed not only the governors of the provinces to come to Rome, but even some of the exiles;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ibi Vespasiani virtutem virisque partium extollit: transfugisse classem, in arto commeatum, adversas Gallias Hispaniasque, nihil in urbe fidum;
examples.translation: There he spoke in high terms of Vespasian’s courage and the strength of his party.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to stay to the end; to hold out, last

examples.original: Vero tenor permanet, falsa non durant.
examples.translation: It is indeed consistency that abides;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Inde mihi quaedam permansere, Lucili. Magno enim in omnia inceptu veneram.
examples.translation: And that is why some of these habits have stayed with me, Lucilius.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cingetorigi, quem ab initio permansisse in officio demonstravimus, principatus atque imperium est traditum.
examples.translation: The prerogative of chieftaincy was delivered to Cingetorix, who, as we have shown, had remained loyal from the beginning.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: borrowed, lent (class.).

examples.original: Haec nobis amorem indidit mutuum et sociabiles fecit.
examples.translation: She engendered in us mutual affection, and made us prone to friendships.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed et conloquium fuit inter ipsos de legibus pacis, et steterunt diu mutua admiratione defixi.
examples.translation: But first a conference was held between them about terms of peace, and they stood for a while motionless in mutual admiration.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Caesar et Fimbria in penatibus domuum suarum trucidantur, Crassi pater et filius in mutuo alter alterius aspectu.
examples.translation: Caesar and Fimbria were butchered at the household shrines of their own homes. The elder and younger Crassus were slain in the sight of one another.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: name of a Roman gens

examples.original: Furius inde et C. Manlius consules.
examples.translation: To Manlius fell the command against the Veientes.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec variatum comitiis est, quin cum Manlio Naevio censor Marcius crearetur.
examples.translation: There was no dissenting opinion shown at the assembly, and Marcius was elected, along with Manlius Naevius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Manlius quoque ad restituendam aciem se ipse coram offert.
examples.translation: Manlius also showed himself among them, helping to restore the line;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of or belonging to the sea, sea-, marine (class.)
English: urine.
English: a male swine, boar-pig

examples.original: Sunt multa quae Verres in me esse arbitratur, quae scit in te, Q. Caecili, non esse;
examples.translation: Verres believes me, Caecilius, to possess many qualities that he knows well you do not possess.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Huic eidem Sopatro idem inimici ad C. Verrem, cum is Sacerdoti successisset, eiusdem rei nomen detulerunt.
examples.translation: When Verres succeeded Sacerdos, this same Sopater was prosecuted before him by these same enemies again on the same charge.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Est idem Verres qui fuit semper, ut ad audendum proiectus, sic paratus ad audiendum. Praesto est, respondet, defenditur;
examples.translation: But he is still Verres, true to his name as ever, daring the worst without hesitation, and hearing the worst without reluctance.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the leg, shank, shin.

examples.original: Spongia pectori tegumentum et sinistrum crus ocrea tectum;
examples.translation: Their helmets were crested, to make their stature appear greater.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In capitis mei levitatem iocatus est et in oculorum valitudinem et in crurum gracilitatem et in staturam.
examples.translation: Some jest at the baldness of my head, the weakness of my eyes, the thinness of my legs, my build.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non est formonsa, cuius crus laudatur aut brachium, sed illa, cuius universa facies admirationem partibus singulis abstulit.
examples.translation: She is not a beautiful woman whose ankle or arm is praised, but she whose general appearance makes you forget to admire her single attributes.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a superscription, inscription, label, litle; a ticket, bill, placard, notice that a thing is to be sold or let (syn. index).

examples.original: Omnes illos megistanas et satrapas et regem ipsum, ex quo Idomenei titulus petebatur, oblivio alta suppressit.
examples.translation: All the grandees and satraps, even the king himself, who was petitioned for the title which Idomeneus sought, are sunk in deep oblivion.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Tanta rudi populo cura pudoris erat. At nunc nocturnis titulos inponimus actis, Atque emitur magno nil, nisi posse loqui!
examples.translation: But now we make our nightly exploits a title to renown, and purchase at a high price naught but the power to brag!
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: sweat, perspiration: manat ex omni corpore sudor, Enn. ap.
Latin: Humor qui exit a corpore cum calet. Compositus est sale et aqua

examples.original: Quibusdam etiam constantissimis in conspectu populi sudor erumpit, non aliter quam fatigatis et aestuantibus solet, quibusdam tremunt genua dicturis, quorundam dentes colliduntur, lingua titubat, labra concurrunt.
examples.translation: The steadiest speaker, when before the public, often breaks into a perspiration, as if he had wearied or over-heated himself; some tremble in the knees when they rise to speak;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fessa iacet cervix, fumant sudoribus artus, Oraque proiecta squalent arentia lingua, Pectora rauca gemunt, quae creber anhelitus urguet, Et defecta gravis longe trahit ilia pulsus, Siccaque sanguineis durescit spuma lupatis.
examples.translation: The weary neck sinks down, the limbs reek with sweat, the tongue protrudes and the mouth is rough and dry; the lungs, driven by quick pants, give a hoarse murmur;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: the name of a Roman gens, greatly distinguished for the illustrious men whom it furnished. The most celebrated of them was L
Latin: Gens Romana

examples.original: Aemilius inde et C. Servilius consules facti.
examples.translation: Lucius Aemilius and Gaius Servilius were then chosen consuls.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Kal. Dec. M. Aemilio Lepido iterum L. Munatio Planco conss. per bellum Philippense.
examples.translation: In fact it is so recorded both in the calendar and in the public gazette.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tribunos etiam militares patricios omnes coacta principum opibus fecit: L. Aemilium P. Valerium quartum C. Veturium Ser. Sulpicium L. et C. Quinctios Cincinnatos.
examples.translation: Servius Sulpicius, Lucius and Gaius Quinctius Cincinnatus. The same influence enabled them to carry through their plans against the Latins and the Volsci, who had united their forces and were encamped near Satricum.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A father-in-law

examples.original: Quod socero bellum praeter civile reliqui?”
examples.translation: I have left my kinsman no war to wage, except civil war.”
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Is A. Postumium Tubertum, socerum suum, severissimi imperii virum, dictatorem dixit;
examples.translation: He appointed Aulus Postumius Tubertus, his father-in-law, a man of the sternest authority;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Inde L. Tarquinius regnare occepit, cui Superbo cognomen facta indiderunt, quia socerum gener sepultura prohibuit, Romulum quoque insepultum perisse dictitans, primoresque patrum, quos Servi rebus favisse credebat, interfecit;
examples.translation: For he denied the rites of sepulture to his own father-in-law, asserting that Romulus had also perished without burial.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: an inner room, chamber, apartment

examples.original: Forte erat in thalamo virgo regalis eodem;
examples.translation: It chanced that in the same chamber was the royal maid;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nec lucem in thalamos totis admitte fenestris;
examples.translation: And let not light into your room by all the windows;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Aspicit Hesiones scopulos silvaque latentes Anchisae thalamos;
examples.translation: He sees Hesione’s rock and the secret marriage-chamber of Anchises in the wood;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to bear, support, sustain (syn.: fero, patior, sustineo, sino).

examples.original: Toleranda est enim ad hoc properantibus vel fames.
examples.translation: For when hastening after wisdom, we must endure even hunger.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Damna, quae inlata sunt, vel tolerantur a Christianis vel resarciuntur per Christianos.
examples.translation: The losses that were inflicted are either being borne by Christians or are being made good by Christians.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Aeque reliqua quoque inter se paria sunt, tranquillitas, simplicitas, liberalitas, constantia, aequanimitas, tolerantia.
examples.translation: In like manner, the other virtues are also equal as compared with one another: tranquillity, simplicity, generosity, constancy, equanimity, endurance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To buy back, repurchase (freq. and class.; syn.: recupero, reparo).

examples.original: Quod repetam, si te dimisero, et redimam.
examples.translation: But, if I can once dispose of you, I shall reseek and rescue it.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed semel est custos longum redimendus in aevum: Saepe dabit, dederit quas semel ille manus.
examples.translation: But the guardian must be bought outright for a long time; the service he has given once he will often give.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fabricius missus ad eum a senatu, ut de redimendis captivis ageret, frustra ut patriam desereret a rege temptatus est.
examples.translation: Gaius Fabricius, being sent to him by the senate to treat for the ransom of the prisoners, was in vain solicited by the King to forsake his country.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a knowing of a thing together with another person, joint knowledge, consciousness (in good prose, and very freq.).

examples.original: Gaudium hoc non nascitur nisi ex virtutum conscientia.
examples.translation: This joy springs only from the knowledge that you possess the virtues.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Prius igitur quam ultra progrederetur, praeventus est ab Agrippina, quam praeter haec conscientia quoque nec minus delatores multorum criminum arguebant.
examples.translation: But before he could go any farther, he was cut short by Agrippina, who was being accused besides of many other crimes both by her own conscience and by informers.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Et quamvis conscientia tibi tua fiduciam faciat, tamen quia multa extra causam valent, et quod aequissimum est spera, et ad id te quod est iniquissimum conpara.
examples.translation: Although your conscience makes you confident, yet, since many things have weight which are outside your case,a both hope for that which is utterly just, and prepare yourself against that which is utterly unjust.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Neutr., to pimp, pander
English: hollow, excavated, concave (opp. plenus, full, round; class.).
Latin: Spatium concludens
Latin: nil concludens
