examples.translation: By that they burst forth, and escaping in a disordered column, fell in the way of the other, the victorious consul, where they were again cut to pieces, and dispersed in all directions.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to measure; v. metor

examples.original: Sed hunc quoque iam tum quom ab Alpe descenderat, apud Metaurum castra metantem Claudius Nero cum Livio Salinatore debellat.
examples.translation: However, when Hasdrubal had just descended from the Alps, as he was planning out a camp near the Metaurus, Claudius Nero, together with Livius Salinator, defeated him also.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: the month of May
Latin: Qui ad mensem quintum calendarii Gregoriani pertinet
Latin: Mensis Maius

examples.original: Aedes Mercuri dedicata est idibus Maiis.
examples.translation: The temple of Mercury was consecrated on the fifteenth of May.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Penes quos igitur sunt auspicia more maiorum?
examples.translation: Who then control the auspices, by the tradition of our fathers?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Maius est istud malum, quam ut gestatione curetur.
examples.translation: The complaint is too deep-seated to be cured by a journey.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to run under.

examples.original: Succurrit inimicus illi Vorenus et laboranti subvenit.
examples.translation: His enemy, Vorenus, ran up to him and helped him in his distress.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Illud non succurrit, vivere nos quod maturarimus proficisci?
examples.translation: What of those who have met this ignominious procession?
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English:  redupl. scicidi, Enn., Naev., Att, and Afran. ap.

examples.original: Nam saevus in ipso Septimius sceleris maius scelus invenit actu, Ac retegit sacros scisso velamine voltus Semianimis Magni spirantiaque occupat ora Collaque in obliquo ponit languentia transtro.
examples.translation: The head was severed; for savage Septimius, in the very doing of his crime, devised a crime still worse.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: To fasten, attach, join, bind

examples.original: Ad utrosque casus aptus est: bonorum rector est, malorum victor.
examples.translation: He is ready for either outcome: if it brings goods, he controls them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Temporis ars medicina fere est: data tempore prosunt, Et data non apto tempore vina nocent.
examples.translation: The art of being timely is almost a medicine: wine timely given helps, untimely, harms.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Illa leget tempus (medici quoque tempora servant) Quo facilis dominae mens sit et apta capi.
examples.translation: She will choose a time (physicians also observe times) when her mistress is in an easy mood and apt for winning.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: the celebrated Grecian hero in the Trojan
Latin: Heros Graecus belli Troiani

examples.original: Arma dedi vobis: dederat Vulcanus Achilli;
examples.translation: Vulcan gave armour to Achilles;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hectora donavit Priamo prece motus Achilles;
examples.translation: Entreaty moved Achilles to give Hector back to Priam;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Huic memoria tam mala erat, ut illi nomen modo Vlixis excideret, modo Achillis, modo Priami, quos tam bene quam paedagogos nostros novimus.
examples.translation: His memory was so faulty that he would sometimes forget the name of Ulysses, or Achilles, or Priam,—names which we know as well as we know those of our own attendants.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a sheep (class.).
Latin: Animal mammiferum specie Ovis aries vel generaliter genere Ovis

examples.original: Gratia te summi Pastoris ad pastionem ovium suarum salutiferam perpetuo conservet incolumem, dilectissime in Christo antistes.
examples.translation: May the grace of the chief Shepherd keep you continually in safety, bishop dearly beloved in Christ, for the wholesome feeding of His sheep.
examples.author: Bede

definitions: English: Five hundred each (class.)

examples.original: Hoc pertinet circiter milia passuum quingenta.
examples.translation: This side stretches about five hundred miles.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Nam ille alter fortasse tamquam phoenix semel anno quingentesimo nascitur.
examples.translation: And it is not surprising, either, that greatness develops only at long intervals;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Exsules servique, ad duo milia hominum et quingenti, duce Ap. Herdonio Sabino nocte Capitolium atque arcem occupavere.
examples.translation: Exiles and slaves to the number of twenty-five hundred, led by Appius Herdonius, the Sabine, came by night and seized the Capitol and the Citadel.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a slender green branch, a twig, sprout, switch

examples.original: Quem taurum metuis, vitulum mulcere solebas: Sub qua nunc recubas arbore, virga fuit: Nascitur exiguus, sed opes adquirit eundo, Quaque venit, multas accipit amnis aquas.
examples.translation: The bull you fear, you were wont to stroke as a calf; the tree under which you lie was once a sapling: a river at birth is small, but acquires force by flowing;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: dark-colored, dark blue, dark green, cerulean, azure
Latin: color caeli ex.gr
entries.grammaticalClass: adj.; and in poetry equally common; a, um

examples.original: His igitur rebus retractis terra repente, maxuma qua nunc se ponti plaga caerula tendit, succidit et salso suffudit gurgite fossas.
examples.translation: Therefore when these bodies were withdrawn, suddenly the earth sank down where now the blue expanse of the sea extends so wide, and drowned its hollows with the salt flood.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: to abide by or adhere to strictly; to continue steadfastly, to persist
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Cotta se ad armatum hostem iturum negat atque in eo perseverat.
examples.translation: Cotta refused to go to an armed enemy, and persisted in the refusal.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quoniam hac similitudine usus sum, perseverabo: animus noster modo rex est, modo tyrannus.
examples.translation: To persist in my use of this simile—our soul is at one time a king, at another a tyrant.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Perseverandum est et adsiduo studio robur addendum, donec bona mens sit quod bona voluntas est.
examples.translation: You must persevere, must develop new strength by continuous study, until that which is only a good inclination becomes a good settled purpose.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to call or summon, to fetch (rare but class.).

examples.original: Verum alia causa tum Staieni fuit, alia nunc Acci, tua est.
examples.translation: But your present case, Accius, has no connexion with Staienus’s case in the past;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Septimam decimam cohortem e colonia Ostiensi in urbem acciri Otho iusserat;
examples.translation: Otho had given orders that the Seventeenth cohort be brought from the colony of Ostia to Rome.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ceterum et Fabius supplementum ab Roma adduxit et novus exercitus domo accitus Etruscis venit.
examples.translation: Fabius brought up replacements from Rome, and a new army came from Etruria to reinforce the enemy.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a place dedicated to some deity by forms of consecration, a sanctuary, temple

examples.original: Cum haec agerentur, iam consul via Labicana ad fanum Quietis erat.
examples.translation: Meanwhile the consul had already reached the shrine of Quies on the Labican road.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non dicam illinc hoc signum ablatum esse et illud: hoc dico, nullum te Aspendi signum, Verres, reliquisse, omnia ex fanis, ex locis publicis, palam, spectantibus omnibus, plaustris evecta exportataque esse.
examples.translation: I shall not allege that from this town this or that particular statue was removed. My charge is that Verres did not leave one single statue behind;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Consilia ad movenda bella in Volscorum Aequorumque conciliis et in Etruria ad fanum Voltumnae agitata.
examples.translation: Schemes for instigating war were discussed in the councils of the Volsci and Aequi, and in Etruria at the shrine of Voltumna.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to take a meal
Latin: cēnam edere
Latin: cōnsūmere, vorāre

examples.original: Tanti enim illam putas, ut tardius cenes?
examples.translation: Do you think enough of your country to be late to dinner?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In cena fit, quod fieri debebat in ventre.
examples.translation: The dinner table does work which the stomach ought to do.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ex quo illud efficitur, qui bene cenent omnes libenter cenare, qui libenter, non continuo bene.
examples.translation: The conclusion is that though all who dine well dine pleasantly, yet he who dines pleasantly does not necessarily dine well.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Adultery

examples.original: Cogis adulterium dando tempusque locumque;
examples.translation: By giving time and place you are compelling adultery;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Qui damnabatur uni adulterio, absolutus est multis.
examples.translation: He to whom one adultery brought condemnation was acquitted because of many.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iacis adulteria, quae nemo non modo nomine, sed ne suspicione quidem possit agnoscere.
examples.translation: You hint darkly at acts of immorality, charges which cannot even be suspected, far less substantiated, against him.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a banished person, wanderer, exile.

examples.original: Capitolium ab exulibus et servis occupatum caesis his receptum est.
examples.translation: The Capitol was seized by exiles and slaves; who were slain and the Capitol recovered.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: necessity, inevitableness, want, need, distress.

examples.original: Atque ipse Vitellius respectu suarum necessitudinum nihil in Domitianum atrox parabat.
examples.translation: And yet Vitellius himself out of regard for his own relatives, cherished no cruel purpose against Domitian.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Namque etsi Dionysii crudelitas ei displicebat, tamen salvum propter necessitudinem, magis etiam suorum causa studebat.
examples.translation: He was intimate with the elder Dionysius as much because of his character as their relationship;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

examples.original: Nec excusatur offensa necessitudine officii aut fide advocationis aut fortuitae et subitae dictionis impetu: meditatus videris \[aut\] elegisse personam notabilem et cum auctoritate dicturam.
examples.translation: And the offence you give cannot be held excused by the obligation to render a friendly service, or by loyalty to a client, or by the excitement of an unpremeditated utterance, made off-hand;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to flee to for refuge or succor, take refuge in or with (class. in prose and poetry).
Latin: Fugere ad aliquem auxilii, aut salutis causa

examples.original: Ad philosophiam ergo confugiendum est;
examples.translation: One must therefore take refuge in philosophy;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eo ille index confugit in araque consedit.
examples.translation: To this that informer fled and seated himself upon the altar.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

examples.original: Huc ex ephoris quidam descenderunt. Pausanias ut audivit Argilium confugisse in aram, perturbatus venit eo.
examples.translation: When Pausanias heard that the Argilian had taken refuge at the altar, he went there in a state of great anxiety;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

definitions: English: sprung from the same stock, related by blood, kindred; and

examples.original: Fecit amicus recens et cognatus voluntarius;
examples.translation: It was done in fact by your new friend, your volunteer cousin;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Idem decem fere annis summe dilectus a Paeto Thrasea est ita ut peregrinaretur quoque cum eo aliquando, cognatam eius Arriam uxorem habente.
examples.translation: He was also for nearly ten years so great a favourite of Paetus Thrasea that he sometimes even travelled abroad with him; and Paetus’s wife, Arria, was a relative of his.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

examples.original: Illud nullo modo probo, quod ait Metrodorus: esse aliquam cognatam tristitiae voluptatem, hanc esse captandam in eiusmodi tempore. Ipsa Metrodori verba subscripsi.
examples.translation: And in no wise do I approve of the remark of Metrodorus—that there is a certain pleasure akin to sadness, and that one should give chase thereto at such times as these.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: mindful of a thing, remembering; constr. with

examples.original: O quam te memorem, virgo?
examples.translation: O maiden, words are weak!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Calvisius Sabinus memoria nostra fuit dives.
examples.translation: Within our own time there was a certain rich man named Calvisius Sabinus;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quod si vos aliquis casus conducet in unum, Mente memor tota quae damus arma, tene.
examples.translation: But if some chance brings you together, use all your memory and wit to wield the arms I give you.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: To look up or upwards, to look up at a thing.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; spexi, spectum, 3

examples.original: Suspiciendi tamen sunt et ritu deorum colendi.
examples.translation: They deserve respect, however, and should be worshipped with a divine ritual.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Difficiles adfectus, dubia omnia invenies, levia, suspecta.
examples.translation: You will find perplexing emotions—everything doubtful, inconstant, untrustworthy.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Plerumque improborum facta primo suspicio insequitur, dein sermo atque fama, tum accusator, tum iudex;
examples.translation: The usual consequences of crime are, first suspicion, next gossip and rumour, then comes the accuser, then the judge;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to present to view, to show, exhibit (class.).

examples.original: Et foris, cum tot terrores a finitimis ostentati essent, et domi otium fuit.
examples.translation: Things were quiet both abroad and at home, despite the numerous alarms which neighbouring states had caused.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: fifty
Latin: Quinquies dena. Numerus L
Latin: Quinquies dena

examples.original: Titus Vinius quinquaginta septem annos variis moribus egit.
examples.translation: Titus Vinius lived fifty-seven years; his character varied at different times.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Statue sex et quinquaginta annos, quibus mox divus Augustus rem publicam rexit;
examples.translation: Count the fifty-six years in which the sainted Augustus thereafter held the helm of state;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ab eis qui emerant capitum numerus ad eum relatus est milium quinquaginta trium.
examples.translation: The purchasers furnished a return to him of three-and-fifty thousand persons.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the south wind (opp. aquilo, the north wind).
Latin: Ventus, qui ex meridie flat
Latin: meridies
English: to thunder.

examples.original: Nec caelum servare licet: tonat augure surdo, Et laetae iurantur aves bubone sinistro.
examples.translation: It is not permitted to watch the sky: it thunders, but the augur is deaf;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nunc quoque, tela licet paveant victoris iniqui, Nuntiet ipse licet Caesar tua funera, flebunt, Sed dum tura ferunt, dum laurea serta Tonanti.
examples.translation: Even as it is, though men dread the arms of the tyrannous conqueror, though Caesar himself announce the death, weep they will, even while offering incense and laurel wreaths to the Thunderer. Unhappy Romans!
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to point out, indicate (future events, misfortunes, etc.), to foretell, predict, presage, portend

examples.original: Magnis telis magna portenta feriuntur.
examples.translation: It takes great weapons to strike down great monsters.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Mater Antonia portentum eum hominis dictitabat, nec absolutum a natura, sed tantum incohatum;
examples.translation: His mother Antonia often called him ”a monster of a man, not finished but merely begun by Dame Nature”;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Terrebatur ad hoc evidentibus portentis somniorum et auspiciorum et ominum, cum veteribus tum novis.
examples.translation: In addition he was frightened by manifest portents from dreams, auspices and omens, both old and new.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: mingle together; to commingle, intermingle.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; scŭi, stum, and xtum, 2

examples.original: Non tamen in caeca bellorum nube cadendum est, Aut cum permixtas acies sua tela tenebris Involvent.
examples.translation: Yet we are not compelled to fall on the blind haze of battle, or when their own missiles cover the confused armies with darkness.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Isti vero praepostero officia permiscent, qui contra praecepta Theophrasti, cum amaverunt, iudicant, et non amant, cum iudicaverunt.
examples.translation: When friendship is settled, you must trust; before friendship is formed, you must pass judgment.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Pauci gladiatorum resistentes neque inulti cecidere: ceteri ad navis ruebant, ubi cuncta pari formidine implicabantur, permixtis paganis, quos nullo discrimine Vitelliani trucidabant.
examples.translation: The rest rushed to the ships; but there an equal panic caused utter confusion, for the Vitellians slew without distinction the townspeople who joined the soldiers in their flight.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: the flowing hair on the neck of an animal, the mane.

examples.original: Tum Sadalam fortemque Cotyn fidumque per arma Deiotarum et gelidae dominum Rhascypolin orae Conlaudant, Libyamque iubent auctore senatu Sceptrifero parere Iubae.
examples.translation: Praise was given also to Sadalas and brave Cotys, to the faithful ally, Deiotarus, and to Rhascypolis, lord of a frozen land;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to wage or carry on war

examples.original: Eodem anno et a consulibus vario eventu bellatum;
examples.translation: In the same year the consuls, too, waged war with varying success.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hic omnem militarem disciplinam artemque bellandi condidit.
examples.translation: It was he who founded all military discipline and the art of warfare.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed ad bella externa prope supererant vires, abutebanturque iis inter semet ipsos certando.
examples.translation: But for foreign wars there was almost a superabundance of resources, and men misused them in quarrelling amongst themselves.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: dry land, a dry place; dry places

examples.original: Odi quae praebet, quia sit praebere necesse, Siccaque de lana cogitat ipsa sua.
examples.translation: I hate her who gives because she must, and who, herself unmoved, is thinking of her wool.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Si ille sanus est, si compositus, gravis, temperans, ingenium quoque siccum ac sobrium est;
examples.translation: If his soul be wholesome, well-ordered, serious, and restrained, his ability also is sound and sober.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fessa iacet cervix, fumant sudoribus artus, Oraque proiecta squalent arentia lingua, Pectora rauca gemunt, quae creber anhelitus urguet, Et defecta gravis longe trahit ilia pulsus, Siccaque sanguineis durescit spuma lupatis.
examples.translation: The weary neck sinks down, the limbs reek with sweat, the tongue protrudes and the mouth is rough and dry; the lungs, driven by quick pants, give a hoarse murmur;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: of Mars; of March
Latin: Qui ad Martem (vel deum, bellum ipsum, vel planetam) pertinet
Latin: Qui ad mensem Martium pertinet

examples.original: Isdem diebus a Martio Macro haud procul Cremona prospere pugnatum;
examples.translation: During these same days, Martius Macer had had a successful engagement not far from Cremona;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ager Tarquiniorum, qui inter urbem ac Tiberim fuit, consecratus Marti Martius deinde campus fuit.
examples.translation: The land of the Tarquinii, lying between the City and the Tiber, was consecrated to Mars and became the Campus Martius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et vidi non tantum mense Februario positas, sed etiam Martio exacto;
examples.translation: I have seen such plantings made not only in February, but at the very end of March;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: sex

examples.original: Id vero haud secus quam praesentem mercedem regni aspernata plebes;
examples.translation: But this the people spurned, as a downright attempt to purchase regal power;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Evidentissimum id fuit, quod, quacumque equo invectus est, ibi haud secus quam pestifero sidere icti pavebant;
examples.translation: This was most clearly seen in that, wherever he rode, men cowered as though blasted by some baleful star;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Etenim omnium rerum quas et creat natura et tuetur, quae aut sine animo sunt aut non multo secus, earum summum bonum in corpore est;
examples.translation: For the inanimate or nearly inanimate creatures that are under nature’s charge, all of them have their supreme good in the body;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a prostitute, harlot, courtesan
Latin: Femina, quae corpore quaestum facit
English: To load, lade, burden, freight with any thing (class.).

examples.original: Hic Opiterginis moles onerata colonis Constitit;
examples.translation: Here the hulk halted, weighed down with men of Opitergium;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Haec omnia in dites a pauperibus inclinata onera. Deinde est honos additus;
examples.translation: All these burdens were shifted from the shoulders of the poor to those of the rich.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et ipsos nominatim iuvenes, pari comitate utrumque, nunc laudibus nunc promissis onerat.
examples.translation: Addressing each of the young men by name, he loaded them now with praise and now with promises.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: illness, sickness (both of body and mind; while aegrotatio denotes only physical disease).

examples.original: Sed cum ea quae praeterierunt acri animo et attento intuemur, tum fit ut aegritudo sequatur si illa mala sint, si bona, laetitia.
examples.translation: But when we fix our mental vision closely on the events of the past, then sorrow or gladness ensues according as these were evil or good.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cui tempus locumque aptum ut daret Romulus, aegritudinem animi dissimulans ludos ex industria parat Neptuno equestri sollemnis; Consualia vocat.
examples.translation: Expressly to afford a fitting time and place for this, Romulus, concealing his resentment, made ready solemn games in honour of the equestrian Neptune, which he called Consualia.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to carry, bear, or bring to or into a place, in one's hands, on a horse, by water, etc.

examples.original: Ibi integrae vires sistunt invehentem se iam Samnitem;
examples.translation: Their fresh strength halted the Samnites, who were now pressing forward;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ab equitibus repente invectis turbati ordines sunt Sabinorum;
examples.translation: The cavalry made a sudden charge;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Evidentissimum id fuit, quod, quacumque equo invectus est, ibi haud secus quam pestifero sidere icti pavebant;
examples.translation: This was most clearly seen in that, wherever he rode, men cowered as though blasted by some baleful star;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: author of an encyclopedical work in 37 books, who lost his life in an eruption of Vesuvius, A. D. 79.—
English: to breathe, blow, etc. (cf. flo).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Hic ego in tantis angustiis quasi aura spirante recreatus nihil ei respondi, sed ad fratrem Alypium gradu concitatiore perrexi eique quid dixerit, dixi.
examples.translation: At such an impasse, this refreshed me like a breath of air, but I said nothing to him and went with hurried step to brother Alypius and told him what he had said.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Nam saevus in ipso Septimius sceleris maius scelus invenit actu, Ac retegit sacros scisso velamine voltus Semianimis Magni spirantiaque occupat ora Collaque in obliquo ponit languentia transtro.
examples.translation: The head was severed; for savage Septimius, in the very doing of his crime, devised a crime still worse.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a herdsman, esp. a shepherd (syn. opilio)
Latin: Curator animalium
Latin: Curator ovis

examples.original: Gratia te summi Pastoris ad pastionem ovium suarum salutiferam perpetuo conservet incolumem, dilectissime in Christo antistes.
examples.translation: May the grace of the chief Shepherd keep you continually in safety, bishop dearly beloved in Christ, for the wholesome feeding of His sheep.
examples.author: Bede

examples.original: Pastor fatigatus aestu cum sub arbore condormisset et serpens ad eum proreperet, e palude culex provolavit atque inter duo tempora aculeum fixit pastori.
examples.translation: When a shepherd, exhausted by the heat, had fallen asleep under a tree, and a snake was creeping upon him, a gnat flew from a marsh and stung the shepherd between his two temples;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Ab eo ad stabula Larentiae uxori educandos datos. Sunt qui Larentiam vulgato corpore lupam inter pastores vocatam putent: inde locum fabulae ac miraculo datum.
examples.translation: Some think that Larentia, having been free with her favours, had got the name of ”she-wolf” among the shepherds, and that this gave rise to this marvellous story.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To stand off from a thing, to stand apart

examples.original: Sed quia finem aliquam pariendi debet habere, destitit, ut mulier spatio defessa vetusto.
examples.translation: But because she must have some limit to her bearing, she ceased, like a woman worn out by old age.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Non enim quia pariter temperabatis a commixtione carnali, ideo tuus maritus esse destiterat;
examples.translation: For he had not ceased to be your husband because you had both agreed to abstain from carnal intercourse;
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Quid? Epicurei num desistunt de iisdem, de quibus et ab Epicuro scriptum est et ab antiquis, ad arbitrium suum scribere?
examples.translation: Nor do the Epicureans cease from writing as the spirit moves them on the same questions on which Epicurus and the ancients wrote.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: across, over, beyond, on the farther side of.
Latin: Ad ulterius latus

examples.original: Item Allobroges, qui trans Rhodanum vicos possessionesque habebant, fuga se ad Caesarem recipiunt et demonstrant sibi praeter agri solum nihil esse reliqui.
examples.translation: The Allobroges also, who had villages and settlements across the Rhone, fled to Caesar, affirming that they had nothing left to them save the bare ground.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Germani desperata expugnatione castrorum, quod nostros iam constitisse in munitionibus videbant, cum ea praeda quam in silvis deposuerant trans Rhenum sese receperunt.
examples.translation: The Germans despaired of storming the camp, for they could see that our men had now taken post in the entrenchments;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Hoc proelio trans Rhenum nuntiato Suebi, qui ad ripas Rheni venerant, domum reverti coeperunt; quos ubi qui proximi Rhenum incolunt perterritos senserunt, insecuti magnum ex eis numerum occiderunt.
examples.translation: When the news of this battle was carried across the Rhine, the Suebi who had come to the banks of the river began to return homewards;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to cause any one to come, to call, send for

examples.original: Mittuntur etiam ad eas civitates legati quae sunt citerioris Hispaniae finitimae Aquitaniae: inde auxilia ducesque arcessuntur.
examples.translation: They even sent deputies to those states of Nearer Spain which border on Aquitania, inviting succours and leaders from thence.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Cum adversus Aequos male gesta res esset, L. Quintius Cincinnatus dictator factus, cum rure intentus operi rustico esset, ad id bellum gerendum arcessitus est Is victos hostes sub iugum misit.
examples.translation: After a defeat had been sustained at the hands of the Aequi, Lucius Quintius Cincinnatus, being appointed dictator, was summoned to the control of the war while engaged in working on his farm.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: The priest of a curia

examples.original: Curio Dacia tenus venit, sed tenebras saltuum expavit.
examples.translation: Curio reached Dacia, but shrank from its gloomy forests.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a grandfather, grandsire.
Latin: Pater patris vel matris
Latin: Atavus, progenitor

examples.original: Non avis utiliter viscatis effugit alis;
examples.translation: The bird cannot make good its escape when once its wings are limed;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Confer avum tuum Drusum cum C. Graccho, eius fere aequali.
examples.translation: Compare your grandfather Drusus with Gaius Gracchus, who was nearly his contemporary.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Inducite in animum quod non induxerunt patres avique vestri, non illi qui in Sacrum montem secesserunt, non hi qui postea Aventinum insederunt.
examples.translation: Steel your hearts to do that which neither your fathers nor yet your grandfathers could resolve upon—neither those who seceded to the Sacred Mount, nor those who later encamped upon the Aventine.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the time between the age of the puer and juvenis, i. e. from the 15th to the 30th year, the time of youth, youth, =
Latin: Status adulescentis; pars vitae inter pueritiam et iuventatem, ab 15. anno usque ad 30. anno

examples.original: Est alter, qui annos adulescentiae cludit.
examples.translation: The next circle limits the period of our young manhood.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Infantiam amisimus, deinde pueritiam, deinde adulescentiam.
examples.translation: We lose our childhood, then our boyhood, and then our youth.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et multa fortasse quae volt, atque in ea, quae non volt, saepe etiam adulescentia incurrit.
examples.translation: Possibly, also, many things he likes; and as for things one does not wish to see, even youth often encounters them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: trouble, troublesomeness, irksomeness, uneasiness, annoyance, molestation, vexation, disgust, dislike, etc. (class.).

examples.original: Et haec non est quies, quae motum omnem molestiam iudicat, sed dissolutio et languor.
examples.translation: And true repose does not consist in condemning all motion as merely vexation; that kind of repose is slackness and inertia.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Temporibus autem quibusdam et aut officiis debitis aut rerum necessitatibus saepe eveniet ut et voluptates repudiandae sint et molestiae non recusandae.
examples.translation: But in certain emergencies and owing to the claims of duty or the obligations of business it will frequently occur that pleasures have to be repudiated and annoyances accepted.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quis autem vel eum iure reprehenderit qui in ea voluptate velit esse quam nihil molestiae consequatur, vel illum qui dolorem eum fugiat quo voluptas nulla pariatur?
examples.translation: But who has any right to find fault with a man who chooses to enjoy a pleasure that has no annoying consequences, or one who avoids a pain that produces no resultant pleasure?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: nothing

examples.original: Nilum non extulit aestas, Maeander derexit aquas, Rhodanumque morantem Praecipitavit Arar.
examples.translation: The Nile fails to rise in summer; the Maeander straightens its course;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Haec dum apud Hellespontum geruntur, Perdiccas apud Nilum flumen interficitur ab Seleuco et Antigene, rerumque summa ad Antipatrum defertur.
examples.translation: While these events were taking place at the Hellespont, Perdiccas was slain near the river Nile by Seleucus and Antigenes, and the supreme power passed to Antipater.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: a gaining, acquiring; gain, acquisition, profit, advantage (quite class.; syn.: lucrum, emolimentum).

examples.original: Minus avaritiae in Caecina, plus ambitionis: Valens ob lucra et quaestus infamis eoque alienae etiam culpae dissimulator.
examples.translation: Caecina was less avaricious, but more eager for popularity; Valens, notorious for his greed and sordid gains, was more inclined to overlook the crimes of others.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: no. 169

examples.original: Hoc enim tale est, quale si peritus gubernator etiam formosus est.
examples.translation: For the case is no different from that of a skilled pilot who is also handsome.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et tibi iam venient cani, formose, capilli, Iam venient rugae, quae tibi corpus arent.
examples.translation: And to thee, O handsome youth, will soon come hoary hairs, soon will come wrinkles to make furrows in your body.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Potest ex casa vir magnus exire, potest et ex deformi humilique corpusculo formosus animus ac magnus.
examples.translation: A great man can spring from a hovel; so can a beautiful and great soul from an ugly and insignificant body.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: A celebrated athlete of Crotona
Latin: Cognomen Romanum

examples.original: Quae enim vox potest esse contemptior quam Milonis Crotoniatae?
examples.translation: For what utterance can be more pitiable than that of Milo of Crotona?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Utque Milo, sub quo cruciata est Pisa tyranno, Vivus in occultas praecipiteris aquas.
examples.translation: And like Milo, under whose tyranny Pisa groaned, mayst thou be hurled alive into hidden waters.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a going round.

examples.original: Est aliqua et doloris ambitio.
examples.translation: There is an element of self-seeking even in our sorrow.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nihil sit illi cum ambitione famaque;
examples.translation: It should have nothing to do with ambition and reputation;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Habet ambitionem, sed non concitatam.
examples.translation: He has ambition, but it is not yet fully aroused.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to send forward or before, to despatch in advance.

examples.original: Caesar Atrebas venit, quem supra demonstraveram a Caesare in Britanniam praemissum.
examples.translation: Commius the Atrebatian, who, as shown above, had been sent forward by Caesar into Britain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: His rebus cognitis exploratores centurionesque praemittit, qui locum idoneum castris deligant.
examples.translation: Upon this information Caesar sent forward scouts and centurions to choose a fit place for the camp.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Caecina e complexu Vitellii multo cum honore digressus partem equitum ad occupandam Cremonam praemisit.
examples.translation: Caecina, departing from the embraces of Vitellius with great honours, sent a part of his horse ahead to occupy Cremona.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: The celebrated Greek philosopher

examples.original: Sed et illum quem nominavi et ceteros sophistas, ut e Platone intellegi potest, lusos videmus a Socrate.
examples.translation: But we read how Socrates made fun of the aforesaid Gorgias, and the rest of the Sophists also, as we can learn from Plato.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ineunte adulescentia amatus est a multis amore Graecorum, in iis Socrate, de quo mentionem facit Plato in Symposio.
examples.translation: In early youth he was beloved by many, after the Greek fashion, including Socrates, as Plato mentions in his Banquet.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Alcibiades

definitions: English: a helmet (usually of leather), head-piece

examples.original: Non galea, non scuto repellitur ferrum.
examples.translation: What is the need of defensive armour, or of skill?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ea legio linteata ab integumento consaepti, in quo sacrata nobilitas erat, appellata est; his arma insignia data et cristatae galeae, ut inter ceteros eminerent.
examples.translation: These were 293named the ”Linen Legion,” from the roof of the enclosure wherein the nobles had been sworn, and were given splendid arms and crested helmets, to distinguish them from the rest.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: food, nourishment.

examples.original: Non pabula tellus Pascendis summittit equis, non proserit ullam Flava Ceres segetem;
examples.translation: The earth sends up no fodder to feed his horses; golden Ceres puts forth no corn there;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nam et signis insedit examen et adsuetae cadaverum pabulo volucres castra quasi iam sua circumvolabant, et in aciem prodeuntibus obvius Aethiops nimis aperte ferale signum fuit.
examples.translation: A swarm of bees settled on the standards; the birds which usually feed upon corpses flew round the camp, as though it were already their prey;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: meet with one, esp. with the access. idea of intention, in a friendly or hostile sense (class. in prose and poetry); constr. with

examples.original: Subinde congressus Caesaris naves et incendit et demersit;
examples.translation: Then, meeting with Caesar’s fleet, he burnt and sank it;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Ne a fortuna quidem, quae quotiens cum virtute congressa est, numquam par recessit.
examples.translation: No, not even from Fortune, who, whenever she has encountered virtue, has always left the field outmatched.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Arma cuncti spectant et bellum: en unquam futurum ut congredi armatis cum Samnite liceat?
examples.translation: Would ever the hour come, they asked, when they might encounter the Samnites, sword in hand?
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to open, stand or be open, to gape.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Cor iacet, et saniem per hiantes viscera rimas Emittunt, produntque suas omenta latebras.
examples.translation: The heart is flattened, the entrails exude corrupted blood through gaping cracks, and the caul reveals its hiding-place.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nascuntur et alio modo terrae ac repente in aliquo mari emergunt, velut paria secum faciente natura quaeque hauserit hiatus alio loco reddente.
examples.translation: Land is sometimes formed in a different manner, rising suddenly out of the sea, as if nature was compensating the earth for its losses, restoring in one place what she had swallowed up in another.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: to break off something violently, to rend, tear, sever

examples.original: Sed ne tarn abrupta quidem sunt quam quidam putant.
examples.translation: But the way is not so sheer as some suppose.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et fuere qui se statim dederent: plures abrupto ponte instanti hosti viam abstulerunt.
examples.translation: The larger part, however, broke down the bridge and so, by cutting off the road, blocked their foes’ advance.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Dividit Euphrates ingentem gurgite mundum, Caspiaque inmensos seducunt claustra recessus, Et polus Assyrias alter noctesque diesque Vertit, et abruptum est nostro mare discolor unda Oceanusque suus.
examples.translation: The waters of the Euphrates shut off from us a mighty world, and the Caspian Gates hide boundless solitudes; in Assyria a different hemisphere makes the changes of night and day;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to take steps, to step, walk
Latin: magnis passibus ire
English: Italian divinity, later identified with Artemis

examples.original: Servius Tullius Veientes devicit et populum in classes divisit, aedem Dianae dedicavit.
examples.translation: Servius Tullius conquered the Veientes and divided the people into classes; dedicated a temple to Diana.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: yearly, annual; hence, in gen.

examples.original: Non enim luxuria, sed inpensa sollemnis est.
examples.translation: For it is not luxury but an expenditure sanctioned by custom.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et a Volscis et Aequis statum iam ac prope sollemne in singulos annos bellum timebatur, propiusque aliud novum malum necopinato exortum.
examples.translation: Also men feared the Volsci and Aequi, whose attack was by this time almost a regular and stated custom of annual recurrence; and a new and unexpected danger sprang up nearer home.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Idus tum Maiae sollemnes ineundis magistratibus erant. Inito igitur magistratu primum honoris diem denuntiatione ingentis terroris insignem fecere.
examples.translation: So then, when they had taken up their duties, they signalized the first day of their administration by a terrible threat.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To avert, ward off (from one's self or others) by earnest prayer; to deprecate

examples.original: His orationibus incitata plebs denis milibus aeris gravis reos condemnat, nequiquam Sergio Martem communem belli fortunamque accusante, Verginio deprecante ne infelicior domi quam militiae esset.
examples.translation: It was in vain that Sergius blamed Fortune and the common chance of war, while Verginius begged that he might not be more unlucky at home than he had been in the campaign.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: clear, fair, bright

examples.original: Dividamus, si tibi videtur, Serene, iniuriam a contumelia.
examples.translation: The former is by its nature more serious;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Urebant montana nives camposque iacentes Non duraturae conspecto sole pruinae, Atque omnis propior mergenti sidera caelo Aruerat tellus hiberno dura sereno.
examples.translation: The mountains were nipped by snow, and the low-lying plains by hoar frost that would vanish at first sight of the sun;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: an opening or aperture produced by boring, a hole (rare but class.): neque porta neque ullum foramen erat, qua posset eruptio fieri, outlet, Sisenn. ap.
English: name of a Roman gens

examples.original: Ergo Fulvio Nobiliori mandata ultio est.
examples.translation: And so the task of vengeance was committed to Fulvius Nobilior.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Fulvius consul de Samnitibus triumphavit.
examples.translation: The consul Fulvius triumphed over the Samnites.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Itaque eam infectam rem M. Fulvius Paetus T. Manlius Torquatus novi consules acceperunt.
examples.translation: The enterprise was therefore still unfinished when Marcus Fulvius Paetus and Titus Manlius Torquatus, the new consuls, took it over.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: place, or
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Tumultus e castris et in urbem penetrat;
examples.translation: What followed within the stockade was a massacre rather than a battle.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mox cetera cantu Explicat Haemonio penetratque in Tartara lingua;
examples.translation: The dog’s bark and the wolfs howl were in that voice;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Adiuvabant eum optumatium studia, per quae in domum quoque puellae certamen partium penetravit.
examples.translation: The noble was preferred by the mother, who wished her daughter to make as grand a match as possible.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to whom; for whom
English: To sentence, condemn, convict (in good prose; rare in the poets).

examples.original: Quid, quod Staienus est condemnatus?
examples.translation: What of the fact that Staienus was condemned?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Audebis ita accusare alterum ut quo minus tute condemnere recusare non possis?
examples.translation: If on the other hand you pass this charge over, what can be your value as a prosecutor?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Fannium Caepionem, qui cum Varrone Murena in Augustum conspiraverat, reum maiestatis apud iudices fecit et condemnavit.
examples.translation: Fannius Caepio, who had conspired with Varro Murena against Augustus, he arraigned for high treason and secured his condemnation.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: heteroclit. abl. plur.: fetis, Att. ap.

examples.original: At mihi maturos numquam licet edere fetus, Ante diemque meae decutiuntur opes.
examples.translation: But I may never bring forth ripe progeny, and my wealth is struck off before its prime.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: cloudy, overcast, lowering

examples.original: Nubila tanguntur velis et terra carina.
examples.translation: The sails reach the clouds, the keel rests on the bottom.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Fulgit item, cum rarescunt quoque nubila caeli;
examples.translation: It lightens also when the clouds grow thin in the sky as well.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: distressed, solicitous, uneasy, troubled, anxious (as a permanent state of mind).
Latin: Sollicitus, pavidus, pavorem patiens
Latin: Pavorem faciens

examples.original: At sunt morosi et anxii et iracundi et difficiles senes.
examples.translation: But, the critics say, old men are morose, troubled, fretful, and hard to please;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Seneca Lvcilio svo salvtem Nimis anxium esse te circa verba et compositionem, mi Lucili, nolo;
examples.translation: On the Superficial Blessings I wish, my dear Lucilius, that you would not be too particular with regard to words and their arrangement;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Feliciorem ergo tu Maecenatem putas, cui amoribus anxio et morosae uxoris cotidiana repudia deflenti somnus per symphoniarum cantum ex longinquo lene resonantium quaeritur?
examples.translation: Do you, then, think Maecenas a happier man, who, distressed by love and grieving over the daily repulses of his wayward wife, courted slumber by means of harmonious music, echoing faintly from a distance?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: dog; hound; subordinate

examples.original: Videtur autem species eius, equus et canis.
examples.translation: A particular animal, however, is seen, for example, a horse, a dog.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et tibi iam venient cani, formose, capilli, Iam venient rugae, quae tibi corpus arent.
examples.translation: And to thee, O handsome youth, will soon come hoary hairs, soon will come wrinkles to make furrows in your body.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: In omni enim animante est summum aliquid atque optimum, ut in equis, in canibus, quibus tamen et dolore vacare opus est et valere;
examples.translation: Every animal, for instance the horse, or the dog, has some supreme good quality, yet at the same time they require to have health and freedom from pain;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: name of a Roman gens

examples.original: Licinio libros haud dubie sequi linteos placet: Tubero incertus veri est.
examples.translation: Licinius sees fit to follow without hesitation the Linen Rolls: Tubero is uncertain where the truth lies.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Suetonius Paulinus et Licinius Proculus diversis itineribus castra vitavere.
examples.translation: Suetonius Paulinus and Licinius Proculus took different roads and avoided the camp.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Syriam et quattuor legiones obtinebat Licinius Mucianus, vir secundis adversisque iuxta famosus.
examples.translation: Syria and its four legions were held by Licinius Mucianus, a man notorious in prosperity and adversity alike.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: of or belonging to a woman, womanly, female, feminine.
Latin: Qui ad mulieres pertinet
Latin: Qui ad mulieres pertinet. vestis muliebris; muliebria pati

examples.original: Nimio otio ingenia natura infirma et muliebria et inopia verae iniuriae lascivientia his commoventur, quorum pars maior constat vitio interpretantis.
examples.translation: And it is generally the pampered and prosperous who indulge in them; for if a man is pressed by worse ills, he has not time to notice such things.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to draw from under or from below.

examples.original: Quae tam emunita et in altum subducta vitae quies, quam non dolor territet?
examples.translation: What peaceful haunts are there, so fortified and so far withdrawn that pain does not fill them with fear?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Postquam id animum advertit, copias suas Caesar in proximum collem subducit equitatumque qui sustineret hostium impetum misit.
examples.translation: As soon as he remarked this, Caesar withdrew his troops to the nearest hill, and sent the horse to check the enemy’s charge.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: sweet, pleasant, agreeable, grateful, delightful (freq. and class.; cf.: dulcis, jucundus).
English: or not, and not; (for negative of IMP)

examples.original: Itaque ne ab se imperatoria consilia neu consulares artes exquirerent, quae pensitanda magnis quoque animis atque ingeniis essent;
examples.translation: It was not, therefore, to him that they must address inquiries concerning the strategy of commanders and the qualifications of consuls;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quod ne intermitteretur opus neu sub terra continuus labor eosdem conficeret, in partes sex munitorum numerum divisit; senae horae in orbem operi attributae sunt;
examples.translation: That this work might not be interrupted nor the same men become exhausted by perpetually toiling under ground, he divided the workers into six parties and assigned them six-hour shifts in rotation;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a burial-place, grave, tomb, sepulchre

examples.original: Notum est totum carmen incisum in sepulcro.
examples.translation: But the entire epitaph is known because it is inscribed upon his tomb.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a bridle, curb

examples.original: Non faciunt meliorem equum aurei freni.
examples.translation: A golden bit does not make a better horse.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Te quoque falle tamen, nec sit tibi finis amandi Propositus: frenis saepe repugnat equus.
examples.translation: Yet deceive yourself also, nor think to make an end of loving: the steed often resists the reins.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: An tu existimas quemquam soluto vultu et, ut isti delicati locuntur, hilariculo mortem contemnere, paupertati domum aperire, voluptates tenere sub freno, meditari dolorum patientiam?
examples.translation: Can one, do you think, despise death with a care-free countenance, or with a ”blithe and gay” expression, as our young dandies are accustomed to say?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: trusty, truslworthy, faithful, sure (class.).

examples.original: An, quod ad diem non venerunt, de eorum fide constantiaque dubitatis?
examples.translation: Or do you doubt their faithfulness, their resolution, because they are not arrived to the day?
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Mota et Dacorum gens numquam fida, tunc sine metu, abducto e Moesia exercitu.
examples.translation: The Dacians also, never trustworthy, became uneasy and now had no fear, for our army had been withdrawn from Moesia.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Haec pro virtute tua fideque, qua una hoc bello res publica stetit, dicenda tibi sunt hodie;
examples.translation: In the name of your courage and your loyalty, which alone have preserved the republic in this war, you must now answer these questions;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a wood with open glades and meadows for cattle, a wood with much pasture-land, a grove
Latin: Silva parva

examples.original: In classem cadit omne nemus;
examples.translation: Cohorts are raised to their full strength with recruits;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Hunc non ruricolae Panes nemorumque potentes Silvani Nymphaeque tenent, sed barbara ritu Sacra deum;
examples.translation: No rural Pan dwelt there, no Silvanus, ruler of the woods, no Nymphs;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nec non in meridiem verso agmine Libanum Syriae Damascumque transgressus per nemora illa odorata, per turis et balsami silvas Romana signa circumtulit.
examples.translation: Furthermore, turning his army southwards, he passed through the Lebanon in Syria and through Damascus, and bore the Roman standards through the famous scented groves and woods of frankincense and balm.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: reflect upon, to muse over, consider, meditate upon; neutr., to think, reflect, muse, consider, meditate; to design, purpose, intend, etc.; constr. with

examples.original: Venit in curiam tamen expeditionem Parthicam meditans.
examples.translation: Yet he came into the senate-house thinking of his campaign against Parthia.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Si me quidem velis audire, hoc meditare et exerce, ut mortem et excipias et, si ita res suadebit, accersas.
examples.translation: If you will give ear to my advice, ponder and practise this,—how to welcome death, or even, if circumstances commend that course, to invite it.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Detegit inbelles animas nil fortiter ausa Seditio tantumque fugam meditata iuventus Ac ducis invicti rebus lassata secundis.
examples.translation: That you have no stomach for fighting is revealed; for your mutiny ends in words;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: the natural feeling of shame, by whatever cause produced, shamefacedness, bashfulness, shyness, coyness, modesty, etc.

examples.original: Sed alii aversabantur preces aut verecundia aut metu;
examples.translation: But some turned away from the petitioner, through either embarrassment or fear;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fuit morum lenissimorum, verecundiae virginalis, formae pulchrae, pietatis erga matrem et sororem et amitam exemplo sufficientis.
examples.translation: He was very gentle in manner, of virginal modesty and very handsome; and he showed an exemplary devotion to his mother, sister, and aunt.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

examples.original: Plus tamen vis potuit quam voluntas patris aut verecundia aetatis: pulso fratre Amulius regnat.
examples.translation: Amulius drove out his brother and ruled in his stead. Adding crime to crime, he destroyed Numitor’s male issue;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: empty, unoccupied, i.e. waste, desert.

examples.original: Vastae tum in his locis solitudines erant.
examples.translation: In those days this was a wild and uninhabited region.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non opus est vasto vulnere dividere praecordia;
examples.translation: If you would pierce your heart, a gaping wound is not necessary;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hoc itaque solacium vasti doloris est, quod necesse est desinas illum sentire, si nimis senseris.
examples.translation: This is, accordingly, a consolation for excessive pain,—that you cannot help ceasing to feel it if you feel it to excess.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: mild, to soften, mollify, alleviate, mitigate, assuage, soothe, calm (syn.: mitigo, placo, sedo, mulceo).

examples.original: Colle tumet modico lenique excrevit in altum Pingue solum tumulo;
examples.translation: The fertile land rises in a hill of moderate height and ascends with easy slope;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ut fuerit torva violentior illa Medusa, Fiet amatori lenis et aequa suo.
examples.translation: Though she be more violent than grim Medusa, she will be mild and gentle to her lover.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ipse autem Antigonus adeo erat incensus, ut nisi magna spe maximarum rerum leniri non posset.
examples.translation: And besides, Antigonus himself was so incensed that he could not be appeased except by great hope of the greatest advantages.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: to make a noise, sound, resound, to rush, rustle, patter, rattle, whiz (class.).

examples.original: Equitem clara increpans voce, ut hostes exaudirent, redire in proelium iubet: nihil trepidatione opus esse;
examples.translation: The horseman he reprimanded in a loud voice, that the enemy might overhear him, and ordered him to go back and fight;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Postulamus ut ii, qui maxime ignaviam increpant, adsint nobis habentibus dilectum. Acerrimi cuiusque arbitrio, quando ita placet, rem agemus.” Redeunt in tribunal;
examples.translation: The most severe amongst you, since such is your pleasure, shall guide our procedure.” They returned to the tribunal, and purposely commanded to cite by name one of those who were present.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Alium crederes senatum, alium populum: ruere cuncti in castra, anteire proximos, certare cum praecurrentibus, increpare Galbam, laudare militum iudicium, exosculari Othonis manum;
examples.translation: The senate and the people seemed wholly changed: all rushed to the camp, striving to pass those next them and to overtake those before;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to erect a building, to build; and in gen., to build, raise, erect, or establish any thing.
Latin: Aedem seu habitationem facere, aut aliam quamvis e muro extructionem

examples.original: Observa te itaque, numquid vestis tua domusque dissentiant, numquid in te liberalis sis, in tuos sordidus, numquid cenes frugaliter, aedifices luxuriose.
examples.translation: Observe yourself, then, and see whether your dress and your house are inconsistent, whether you treat yourself lavishly and your family meanly, whether you eat frugal dinners and yet build luxurious houses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that takes place by chance or accident, casual, accidental, fortuitous (rare but class.)
Latin: ob fortunam; quod nullae cuidam ratione fit

examples.original: Ad omne fortuitum bonum suspiciosi pavidique subsistite;
examples.translation: Halt before every good which Chance brings to you, in a spirit of doubt and fear;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Incredibilis philosophiae vis est ad omnem fortuitam vim retundendam.
examples.translation: The power of philosophy to blunt the blows of chance is beyond belief.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec excusatur offensa necessitudine officii aut fide advocationis aut fortuitae et subitae dictionis impetu: meditatus videris \[aut\] elegisse personam notabilem et cum auctoritate dicturam.
examples.translation: And the offence you give cannot be held excused by the obligation to render a friendly service, or by loyalty to a client, or by the excitement of an unpremeditated utterance, made off-hand;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a wild boar.

examples.original: Nam lucrosae huius et sanguinantis eloquentiae usus recens et ex malis moribus natus, atque, ut tu dicebas, Aper, in locum teli repertus.
examples.translation: The age of bliss, on the other hand, the golden age, as we poets call it, knew nothing of either accusers or accusations;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Feta tibi occurrat patrio popularis in arvo, Sitque Phalaeceae causa leaena necis. Quique Lycurgiden letavit, et arbore natum, Idmonaque audacem, te quoque rumpat aper.
examples.translation: And may the boar that slew Lycurgus’ son, and him that was born of a tree, and courageous Idmon, tear thee too asunder.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: Egyptian (the class. word for the later Aegyptiacus in Gell., Plin., and Treb.)

examples.original: Parabatur et in noctem spectaculum, quo argumenta inferorum per Aegyptios et Aethiopas explicarentur. LVIII.
examples.translation: A nocturnal performance besides was rehearsing, in which scenes from the lower world were represented by Egyptians and Aethiopians.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Itaque magnifice Datamen donatum ad exercitum misit, qui tum contrahebatur duce Pharnabazo et Tithrauste ad bellum Aegyptium, parique eum atque illos imperio esse iussit.
examples.translation: Accordingly, he rewarded Datames munificently and sent him to the army which was then being mustered under Pharnabazus and Tithraustes for the war in Egypt, 378 b.c.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Datames

definitions: English: forty
Latin: Quater dena. Triginta novem et alius. Numerus XL
Latin: Quater dena

examples.original: Romulus septem et triginta regnavit annos, Numa tres et quadraginta.
examples.translation: Romulus ruled thirty-seven years, Numa forty-three.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ab illo enim profecto viribus datis tantum valuit ut in quadraginta deinde annos tutam pacem haberet.
examples.translation: For it was to him, assuredly, that Rome owed the vigour which enabled her to enjoy an untroubled peace for the next forty years.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ser. Tullius regnavit annos quattuor et quadraginta ita ut bono etiam moderatoque succedenti regi difficilis aemulatio esset.
examples.translation: Servius Tullius had ruled forty-four years, so well that even a good and moderate successor would have found it hard to emulate him.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a bundle of wood, twigs, straw, reeds, etc.

examples.original: Haec dicta vulgo creditaque cum indignitate angerent consulis animum, vocato ad concilium populo submissis fascibus in contionem escendit.
examples.translation: He summoned the people to a council, and with lowered fasces mounted the speaker’s platform.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Panegyricus Ipsa quidem Virtus pretium sibi, solaque late Fortunae secura nitet nec fascibus ullis erigitur plausuve petit clarescere vulgi.
examples.translation: The Consulship of Manlius Panegyric (XVII) Virtue is its own reward; alone with its far-flung splendour it mocks at Fortune;
examples.author: Claudian
examples.work: Panegyric On The Consulship Of Fl. Manlius Theodorus (A.D. 399)

definitions: English: to fall upon, assault, assail, attack (perh. not ante-Aug.).

examples.original: Est et in incessu pars non temnenda decoris: Allicit ignotos ille fugatque viros.
examples.translation: In walk too there is no mean part of charm; it attracts or repels unknown admirers.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Rapax et prima Italica incessere cum vexillariis trium Britannicarum legionum et electis auxiliis.
examples.translation: First Italic with detachments from the three legions in Britain and with picked auxiliary troops.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Timor deinde patres incessit, ne civitatem sine imperio, exercitum sine duce multarum circa civitatium inritatis animis vis aliqua externa adoriretur.
examples.translation: Then the senators became alarmed, lest the state wanting a ruler and the army a leader, and many neighbouring states being disaffected, some violence might be offered from without.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: meet together with something.

examples.original: Cum ad iudicium ire non auderet, omnes eae res in unum congruentes haud magis dubiam damnationem Volsci quam Caesonis Volscio teste fuerat faciebant.
examples.translation: Since he did not dare proceed to arbitration, all these things, pointing in one direction, made the condemnation of Volscius as certain as that of Caeso had been made by Volscius’s evidence.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to flow, run, trickle, drop, distil, etc.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Ac nostri, quo non metuant admittere manes Tartarei reges.
examples.translation: Tartarus would not fear to let the dead travel thus far.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ad Romuleam urbem hinc eamus, ubi vos labor haud maior, praeda maior manet.”
examples.translation: Let us go from here to the city Romulea, where no greater toil awaits you, but greater booty.”
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In quo enim plura sunt quae secundum naturam sunt, huius officium est in vita manere;
examples.translation: When a man’s circumstances contain a preponderance of things in accordance with nature, it is appropriate for him to remain alive;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to bind to something
Latin: Ligare ad aliquid

examples.original: Nos multa alligant, multa debilitant.
examples.translation: We human beings are fettered and weakened by many vices;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iamque omissa cunctando victoria erat, cum consul volnere alligato revectus ad prima signa ”Quid stas, miles?” inquit;
examples.translation: And now the delay had almost lost them the victory, when the consul, whose wound had been dressed, rode up again to the front.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: complaint, accusation, indictment.

examples.original: Ex quo igitur crimen atque accusatio nascitur?
examples.translation: What does give ground, then, for a prosecutor’s attacks?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Neque tantum me exspectatio accusationis meae concursusque tantae multitudinis, quibus ego rebus vehementissime perturbor, commovet quantum istius insidiae nefariae, quas uno tempore mihi, vobis, M’.
examples.translation: Yet never have I felt myself facing such grave danger, nor been so thoroughly alarmed, as now when the trial has begun.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Simul et illud quis est qui dubitet quin hac re comperta manifesteque deprehensa aut obeunda mors Cluentio aut suscipienda accusatio fuerit?
examples.translation: And further, who could possibly doubt, with these facts before him, this actual discovery of the crime, that Cluentius was bound either to face death or to prosecute?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the state of being swollen or tumid; a swelling

examples.original: Quantosne tumores Mente gerit famulus!
examples.translation: What pride the menial cherishes in his heart!
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Extollunt quidem et dilatant, sed sine tumore.
examples.translation: They do, indeed, uplift and broaden the spirit, but without puffing it up.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hinc, Abaton quam nostra vocat veneranda vetustas, †Terra potens† primos sentit percussa tumultus, Et scopuli, placuit fluvii quos dicere venas, Quod manifesta novi primum dant signa tumoris.
examples.translation: Here too are the rocks which are commonly called the springs of the river, because they give the first clear indication when the water begins to rise.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to reverence with religious awe, to worship, adore, revere, venerate.
Latin: orare ad aliquod, aliquod mirari

examples.original: Veneranda enim sunt iustitia, pietas, fides, fortitudo, prudentia;
examples.translation: For reverence is due to justice, duty, loyalty, bravery, and prudence;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Si Venerem Cous nusquam posuisset Apelles, Mersa sub aequoreis illa lateret aquis.
examples.translation: If Coan Apelles had never painted Venus, she would still be lying hid in the sea’s depths.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Si quis collegam appellasset, ab eo ad quem venerat ita discedebat ut paeniteret non prioris decreto stetisse.
examples.translation: If anybody sought redress from another decemvir, he came away regretting that he had not accepted the decision of the first.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: feeling, sense, understanding
Latin: Cōnscientia
Latin: Ēventus sentiendi

examples.original: Nec puto, nec sensi tunicam laniasse;
examples.translation: I do not think nor did I notice that I tore her vest;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Itaque sensibus rationem adiunxit et ratione effecta sensus non reliquit.
examples.translation: Thus she added to sensation reason, and after creating reason did not discard sensation.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: At hic, qui se ad id, quod exigit natura, composuit, non tantum extra sensum est paupertatis, sed extra metum.
examples.translation: He, however, who has arranged his affairs according to nature’s demands, is free from the fear, as well as from the sensation, of poverty.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a ring, esp. for the finger, a finger-ring; and for sealing, a seal-ring, signet-ring.
Latin: genus circulāris ōrnāmentī, saepissime geritur in digitis

examples.original: Documenta cladis cruentus aliquandiu Aufidus, pons de cadaveribus iussu ducis factus in torrente Vergello, modii duo anulorum Carthaginem missi dignitasque equestris taxata mensura.
examples.translation: As proofs of the vastness of the slaughter the Aufidus for a long time ran with blood; a bridge of corpses was constructed by order of the general over the torrent of Vergellus;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: the space of three days, three days

examples.original: Inter pulcherrimos hunc quoque populus Romanus de Macedonia duxit ac vidit triumphum, quippe cuius spectaculo triduum impleverit.
examples.translation: The triumph in honour of the conquest of Macedonia was among the most splendid which the Roman people ever held and witnessed.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a watching, keeping, charge

examples.original: Haec est istius praeclara tutela.
examples.translation: This is the edifying story of his guardianship.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Omnium tamen maximum eius operum fuit tutela per omne regni tempus haud minor pacis quam regni.
examples.translation: But of all his services the greatest was this, that throughout his reign he guarded peace no less jealously than his kingdom.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to rise up for the purpose of going to some one or something, or of undertaking something great, difficult, or hazardous
Latin: Ad aliquem oriri, praesertim aggressu

examples.original: Cum maxime agmen e castris explicaretur, Volsci, ut eodem signo excitati, novissimos adoriuntur.
examples.translation: At daybreak he caused the signal for departure to be sounded on the trumpet.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Eodem anno Valerius consul cum exercitu in Aequos profectus cum hostem ad proelium elicere non posset, castra oppugnare est adortus.
examples.translation: The same year. Valerius the consul, having marched with an army against the Aequi, was unable to entice the enemy into a battle, and directed an assault upon their camp.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et consul alter Fabius proeliis primum parvis, postremo una insigni pugna, cum hostes totis adorti copiis essent, Hernicos devincit.
examples.translation: And the other consul Fabius defeated the Hernici—at first in little skirmishes, but ultimately in one remarkable battle, in which the enemy attacked with all their forces.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to long much for a thing, to be very desirous of, to covet, to aspire to, strive after (class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Concupisces et ipse ex illis unus esse.
examples.translation: You will desire eagerly to be one of them yourself.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et mundus transit et concupiscentia eius;
examples.translation: And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof;
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Inventus est qui concupisceret aliquid post omnia;
examples.translation: There have been found persons who crave something more after obtaining everything;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: rage, madness

examples.original: Sed non auctore furoris Sublato cecidit rabies; nam rursus in arma Auspiciis Ganymedis eunt ac multa secundo Proelia Marte gerunt.
examples.translation: But the madness did not cease with the death of its originator: again, led by Ganymede, the people rush to arms and are often victorious in battle.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Incensos ea rabie impetus Tusculum tulit ob iram, quod deserto communi concilio Latinorum non in societatem modo Romanam sed etiam in civitatem se dedissent.
examples.translation: They were angry that the Tusculans had deserted the common council of the Latins and had yielded themselves to be not only allies but citizens of Rome.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Inminet armorum rabies, ferrique potestas Confundet ius omne manu, scelerique nefando Nomen erit virtus, multosque exibit in annos Hic furor.
examples.translation: The madness of war is upon us, when the power of the sword shall violently upset all legality, and atrocious crime shall be called heroism.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to press or squeeze together, compress (very freq and class.).

examples.original: Numitoris filia a Marte compressa nati Romulus et Remus.
examples.translation: Romulus and Remus born to Mars by the daughter of Numitor.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Adventus eius compressit Etruscos adeo ut nemo extra munimenta egredi auderet timorque ipsorum obsidioni similis esset.
examples.translation: His arrival so damped the ardour of the Etruscans that none ventured outside their fortifications, and their own fear was like a besieging host.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a married woman, wife, matron (whether she was in manu or not; consequently more general in its application than mater familias, which always denoted one who was in manu).

examples.original: Comprehensae extemplo earum comites magnum numerum matronarum indicaverunt; ex quibus ad centum septuaginta damnatae.
examples.translation: Their attendants being instantly arrested informed against a large number of matrons, of whom one hundred and seventy were found guilty;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Iuno regina transvecta a Veiis nuper in Aventino quam insigni ob excellens matronarum studium celebrique dedicata est die!
examples.translation: Queen Juno was lately conveyed from Veii and enshrined on the Aventine, and how notable was that day, for the zeal of the matrons and the throng!
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a hare
Latin: Animal notum, timidissimum, velocissimum, fecundissimum

examples.original: Leporem et gallinam et anserem gustare fas non putant;
examples.translation: They account it wrong to eat of hare, fowl, and goose;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Credula si fueris, aliae tua gaudia carpent, Et lepus hic aliis exagitatus erit.
examples.translation: If you are too trusting, other women will reap your joys, and that hare will be hunted by others.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a. [no], to swim, to float.
Latin: in aqua volvi et excurrere
Latin: natando decurrere, tranatare

examples.original: Possum, quamvis in aqua sim, non natare;
examples.translation: It is possible for me, though being in the water, not to swim;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nomina ex ambitione aut ex iniuria nata.
examples.translation: They are mere titles, born of ambition or of wrong.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iamque volaturus parvo dedit oscula nato, Nec patriae lacrimas continuere genae.
examples.translation: There was a hill smaller than a mountain, but rising above the level plains;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: the top of a gable, a gable end, pediment (syn.: cacumen, culmen, vertex, apex).

examples.original: Hos ludos spectavit e proscaeni fastigio.
examples.translation: These plays he viewed from the top of the proscenium.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Confragosa in fastigium dignitatis via est;
examples.translation: It is a rough road that leads to the heights of greatness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non vivunt contra naturam qui pomaria in summis turribus serunt? Quorum silvae in tectis domuum ac fastigiis nutant, inde ortis radicibus quo inprobe cacumina egissent?
examples.translation: Or raise waving forests upon the roofs and battlements of their houses—the roots starting at a point to which it would be outlandish for the tree-tops to reach?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the office or functions of a minister, attendance, service, ministry, in a good or bad sense; an office, occupation, work, labor, employment, administration, etc.

examples.original: Aliquid nobis praestat geometriae ministerium;
