examples.translation: For the mass of man-kind consider that a person is at leisure who has with-drawn from society, is free from care, self-sufficient, and lives for himself;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Huius igitur rei tractatus, si tamen ad liquidum a talibus, quales nos sumus, examinari potest, curam atque operam negotiosissimam postulat ac per hoc mentem ab his occupationibus otiosissimam.
examples.translation: The treatment of this problem, if indeed it can be clearly investigated by one such as myself, demands attention and the most laborious application, and therefore a mind quite free from such occupations as mine.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to search out diligently, to seek for; to make inquiry, to inquire
Latin: Diligenter inquirere

examples.original: Exquisitis palam pretiis et licitationibus factis, discribebat censores binos in singulas civitates Timarchides.
examples.translation: Prices were openly ascertained and offers openly made, after which the two censors for each state were assigned by Timarchides.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque ne ab se imperatoria consilia neu consulares artes exquirerent, quae pensitanda magnis quoque animis atque ingeniis essent;
examples.translation: It was not, therefore, to him that they must address inquiries concerning the strategy of commanders and the qualifications of consuls;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of that kind, of such a kind, such

examples.original: Postremo quis hoc sibi persuaderet, sine certa re Ambiorigem ad eiusmodi consilium descendisse?
examples.translation: In fine, who could persuade himself that Ambiorix had engaged in such a design without sure cause?
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quod quamquam Aristippi est a Cyrenaicisque melius liberiusque defenditur, tamen eiusmodi esse iudico ut nihil homine videatur indignius.
examples.translation: This is the doctrine of Aristippus, and it is upheld more cogently and more frankly by the Cyrenaics;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ita dico: ex quo natus es, duceris. Haec et eiusmodi versanda in animo sunt, si volumus ultimam illam horam placidi expectare, cuius metus omnes alias inquietas facit.
examples.translation: We must ponder this thought, and thoughts of the like nature, if we desire to be calm as we await that last hour, the fear of which makes all previous hours uneasy.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: out through the doors, out of doors, forth
Latin: Adverbium motus ad locum, quod significat extra
English: the purple-fish
Latin: color purpureus
Latin: piscis purpureus, genus conchae

examples.original: Impia si nostros legisset Scylla libellos, Haesisset capiti purpura, Nise, tuo.
examples.translation: Had impious Scylla read my verse, the purple had stayed on thy head, O Nisus.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: ground corn, meal, flour.

examples.original: Iamque ubi pulvereae fuerint confusa farinae, Protinus in cumeris omnia cerne cavis.
examples.translation: And now when it is mixed with the dusty grain, sift it all straightway in hollow sieves.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: made of iron, iron.

examples.original: Aquibus tantum dissentio ut, cum Sophocles vel optime scripserit Electram, tamen male conversam Atili mihi legendam putem, de quo Licinius ’ferreum scriptorem,’ verum opinor scriptorem tamen, ut legendus sit.
examples.translation: With this sort of person I disagree so strongly, that, admitting the Electra of Sophocles to be a masterpiece, I yet think Atilius’s poor translation of it worth my while to read.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a walk covered by a roof supported on columns, a colonnade, piazza, arcade, gallery, porch, portico, =

examples.original: Nec quae ferre solet spatiantem porticus illam, Te ferat, officium neve colatur idem.
examples.translation: And frequent not the colonnade that she frequents when walking, nor cultivate the same society.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Missus et Celsus Marius ad electos Illyrici exercitus, Vipsania in porticu tendentis;
examples.translation: Celsus Marius was sent to the picked troops from Illyria, who were encamped in the Vipsanian Colonnade;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Fabricavit et deceris Liburnicas gemmatis puppibus, versicoloribus velis, magna thermarum et porticuum et tricliniorum laxitate magnaque etiam vitium et pomiferarum arborum varietate;
examples.translation: He also built Liburnian galleys with ten banks of oars, with sterns set with gems, particoloured awnings, huge spacious baths, colonnades, and banquet-halls, and even a great variety of vines and fruit trees;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: shut up, closed; hence, trop.
English: to wound, to hurt, or injure by a wound (syn.: saucio, ferio).

examples.original: Prospectu tenebris adempto multa utrimque vulnera accipiuntur.
examples.translation: As the darkness made it impossible to see far, many wounds were received on both sides.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ab hoc aliquot plagis Eumenes vulneratur neque eo magis ex proelio excessit, sed acrius hostis institit.
examples.translation: From his opponent Eumenes suffered several wounds, but he did not on that account leave the field, but attacked the enemy with renewed vigour.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Est tibi agendus amans, imitandaque vulnera verbis; Haec tibi quaeratur qualibet arte fides.
examples.translation: You must play the lover, and counterfeit heartache with words: her belief in that you must win by any device.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to spread abroad, scatter

examples.original: Primo impetu ac clamore dissipati ordines sunt;
examples.translation: Their ranks were broken at the first shout and charge;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Equitum acies, qualis quae esse instructissima potest, invecta in dissipatos impeditosque hostes caede omnia replet.
examples.translation: The cavalry, drawn up in the most perfect order, charged their scattered and embarrassed enemies and cut them down on every hand.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Itaque non fusi modo hostes sunt, sed ne castris quidem suis fugam impedire ausi Apuliam dissipati petiere;
examples.translation: And so not only were the Samnites routed, but not daring to interrupt their flight even at their camp, they dispersed and struck out for Apulia;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A changing, altering, a change, alteration, mutation
Latin: Actus mutandi

examples.original: Nulla sine motu ars, nulla mutatio est.
examples.translation: There is no art without motion, no change of any kind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid enim mutationis periculo exceptum?
examples.translation: For what is free from the risk of change?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ipse tantum itinerum faciebat, quantum satis esse ad mutationem locorum propter salubritatem existimabat.
examples.translation: He himself marched as far as he deemed sufficient for change of stations, to keep the troops in health.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: of or belonging to one's birth, birth-, natal
Latin: Qui ad alicuius partum pertinet
Latin: subst.m. Dies natalis; dies anniversarius alicuius partus

examples.original: Quin et natalem Vitellii diem Caecina ac Valens editis tota urbe vicatim gladiatoribus celebravere, ingenti paratu et ante illum diem insolito.
examples.translation: Moreover, Caecina and Valens celebrated his birthday by giving gladiatorial shows in every precinct of the city on an enormous scale unheard of up to that time.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ob eam causam spatia omnis temporis non numero dierum sed noctium finiunt; dies natales et mensum et annorum initia sic observant ut noctem dies subsequatur.
examples.translation: For that reason they determine all periods of time by the number, not of days, but of nights, and in their observance of birthdays and the beginnings of months and years day follows night.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Blaeso super claritatem natalium et elegantiam morum fidei obstinatio fuit. Integris quoque rebus a Caecina et primoribus partium iam Vitellium aspernantibus ambitus abnuere perseveravit.
examples.translation: Even while the position of Vitellius was still unshaken, he had been solicited by Caecina and the party leaders who already despised the emperor, but he persisted in rejecting their advances.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to cheer, comfort, console.

examples.original: His adductis, in eis filio propinquisque eius omnibus, quos nominatim evocaverat, consolatus Indutiomarum hortatusque est uti in officio maneret;
examples.translation: When these were brought in, among them his son and all his relatives, whom Caesar had summoned by name, he comforted Indutiomarus and exhorted him to abide in loyalty.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quo in negotio tamen illa me res, iudices, consolatur, quod haec quae videtur esse accusatio mea non potius accusatio, quam defensio est existimanda.
examples.translation: At the same time, this business brings me one consolation. In form, it is an act of prosecution: but it may fairly be regarded as equally an act of defence.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to strive to seize, lay hold of a thing with zeal, longing, etc., to catch at, snatch, chase, etc.

examples.original: Eodem impetu castra capta debellatumque est.
examples.translation: By a single rush the camp was captured and the war ended.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quid enim turpius philosophia captante clamores?
examples.translation: For what is baser than philosophy courting applause?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Coloniae deductae sunt in agro de Gallis capto Placentia et Cremona.
examples.translation: Colonies were established in the territory taken from the Gauls, at Placentia and Cremona.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: decemvir, one of ten men; (commission of ten, board with consular powers)

examples.original: Primores patrum odisse decemviros, odisse plebem;
examples.translation: They could not approve of the things that were being done;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His senatus consultis perfectis dimisso senatu decemviri prodeunt in contionem abdicantque se magistratu ingenti hominum laetitia.
examples.translation: Having so decreed the senate adjourned and the decemvirs went before the people and laid down their office, to the great delight of all.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum Valerius Horatiusque missi ad plebem condicionibus quibus videretur revocandam componendasque res, decemviris quoque ab ira et impetu multitudinis praecavere iubentur.
examples.translation: Valerius and Horatius were then sent to bring back the plebs and adjust all differences, on such terms as might seem good to them;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a relating, narrating, a narration, narrative.
English: crooked, not straight, distorted, misshapen, deformed (opp. rectus; class.).

examples.original: Nec ut iniustus in pace rex, ita dux belli pravus fuit;
examples.translation: But if the king was unjust in peace, yet he was not a bad general in war.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Huic bellum adversus Aequos permissum est, pravae mentis homini, quam tamen victoria magis quam bellum ostendit.
examples.translation: He was a wrong-headed man, yet he showed it more in the hour of victory than during the campaign.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Atque ut a corpore ordiar, videsne ut si quae in membris prava aut debilitata aut imminuta sint occultent homines?
examples.translation: To start with the body, do you notice how men try to hide a deformed or infirm or maimed limb?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a small board, a little table or tablet

examples.original: Sed tabellas, si quae ibi nostrae sunt, propter huius modi necessitates mittas peto.
examples.translation: If you have any tablets of mine beside you, please send them back for such emergencies as this.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Etenim paucis postea mensibus alia vehemens erat in iudiciis ex notatione tabellarum invidia versata.
examples.translation: No one had a chance to denounce that view; no one in fact exerted himself to urge the opposite side.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Esto: in tabellis nihil est auctoritatis: quid, ipsa quaestio iudicibus, quid, amicis hospitibusque Oppianici, quos adhibuerat antea, quid, huic tandem ipsi tempori cur non servata est?
examples.translation: Why not for the friends and associates of Oppianicus whom she had summoned in the first instance? Why not indeed for the present occasion?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: good-looking, showy, handsome, beautiful, splendid, brilliant (not freq. till after the Aug. period; syn.: venustus, pulcher, formosus, spectabilis).

examples.original: Perinde speciosa mors earum fuit quam pugna.
examples.translation: Their death was as honourable as their resistance;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nec diutius Galba cunctatus speciosiora suadentibus accessit.
examples.translation: Galba did not delay any longer, but favoured those who offered the more specious advice.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Libri XVIIII Periocha Caecilius Metellus rebus adversus Poenos prospere gestis speciosum egit triumphum, xiii ducibus hostium et cxx elephantis in eo ductis.
examples.translation: Summary of Book XIX Caecilius Metellus, after a prosperous campaign against the Carthaginians, triumphed brilliantly, having thirteen of the enemy’s generals and a hundred and twenty elephants in his procession.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To deprive of air or wind.

examples.original: Qua legatione perlata praetor eorum Annius de Capitolio ita lapsus est ut exanimaretur.
examples.translation: After delivering these terms, their praetor Annius fell from the Capitol, and so lost consciousness.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Exanimati omnes tam atroci imperio nec aliter quam in se quisque destrictam cernentes securem, metu magis quam modestia quievere.
examples.translation: All were astounded at so shocking a command; every man looked upon the axe as lifted against himself, and they were hushed with fear more than with reverence.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hic alter inperitus est, rebus suis timet ad omnem crepitum expavescens, quem una quaelibet vox pro fremitu accepta deicit, quem motus levissimi exanimant;
examples.translation: This man in his second state lacks knowledge fearing for his own concerns, he pales at every sound; any cry is taken for the battle-shout and overthrows him;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to foam, froth
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Cruor altus in unda Spumat, et obducti concreto sanguine fluctus.
examples.translation: Their blood foamed deep upon the wave, and a crust of gore covered the sea.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nec cerussa tibi nec nitri spuma rubentis Desit et Illyrica quae venit iris humo.
examples.translation: Nor let white lead nor foam of red nitre be lacking, nor the iris that comes from Illyrian soil.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fessa iacet cervix, fumant sudoribus artus, Oraque proiecta squalent arentia lingua, Pectora rauca gemunt, quae creber anhelitus urguet, Et defecta gravis longe trahit ilia pulsus, Siccaque sanguineis durescit spuma lupatis.
examples.translation: The weary neck sinks down, the limbs reek with sweat, the tongue protrudes and the mouth is rough and dry; the lungs, driven by quick pants, give a hoarse murmur;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: out of one's senses, beside one's self, senseless

examples.original: Quae, malum, ista fuit amentia!
examples.translation: O you knave, O you fool!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quae cum ita sint, iste homo amens ac perditus alia mecum ratione pugnat.
examples.translation: The knowledge of all these things has led this abandoned madman to adopt a new method of fighting me.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In cognoscendo autem ac decernendo mira varietate animi fuit, modo circumspectus et sagax, interdum inconsultus ac praeceps, nonnumquam frivolus amentique similis.
examples.translation: But in hearing and deciding cases he showed strange inconsistency of temper, for he was now careful and shrewd, sometimes hasty and inconsiderate, occasionally silly and like a crazy man.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to surround with a hedge, to hedge in, fence in, enclose (class.; cf. vallo).

examples.original: Incohavit autem aquae ductum regione Tiburti et amphitheatrum iuxta Saepta, quorum operum a successore eius Claudio alterum peractum, omissum alterum est.
examples.translation: He likewise began an aqueduct in the region near Tibur and an amphitheatre beside the Saepta, the former finished by his successor Claudius, while the latter was abandoned.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Munera gladiatoria partim in amphitheatro Tauri partim in Saeptis aliquot edidit, quibus inseruit catervas Afrorum Campanorumque pugilum ex utraque regione electissimorum.
examples.translation: He gave several gladiatorial shows, some in the amphitheatre of Taurus and some in the Saepta, in which he introduced pairs of African and Campanian boxers, the pick of both regions.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Hanc virginem adultam forma excellentem Appius amore amens pretio ac spe perlicere adortus, postquam omnia pudore saepta animadvertit, ad crudelem superbamque vim animum convertit.
examples.translation: But finding that her modesty was proof against everything, he resolved on a course of cruel and tyrannical violence.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: former, early, original, primitive, pristine (class.)

examples.original: Consulatus super pristinum quattuor gessit;
examples.translation: He held four consulships in addition to his original one.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Hoc unum ad pristinam fortunam Caesari defuit.
examples.translation: This one thing was lacking to complete the wonted success of Caesar.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quin etiam speciem libertatis quandam induxit conservatis senatui ac magistratibus et maiestate pristina et potestate.
examples.translation: He even introduced a semblance of free government by maintaining the ancient dignity and powers of the senate and the magistrates;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: A funeral pile (syn. bustum): ROGVM ASCIA NE POLITO, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap.

examples.original: Sine funeris ullo Ardet honore rogus;
examples.translation: The pyre burns on with no funeral honours;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ut potiare, roga: tantum cupit illa rogari;
examples.translation: That you may gain her, ask: she only wishes to be asked;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quorundam illustrium exsequias usque ad rogum frequentavit.
examples.translation: He attended the obsequies of certain distinguished men, even going to the funeral-pyre.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: robber, thief; pirate (if at sea)

examples.original: Pauci hostium evasere ex insidiis; praeda omnis recepta est.
examples.translation: But few of them escaped the ambush, and the spoils were all recovered.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quam provinciam tenuistis a praedonibus liberam per hosce annos?
examples.translation: What province did you keep free from the pirates during those years?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque non ego vobis ut indicem praedas vestras, sed vos id cogendi estis ut in medium proferatis.”
examples.translation: And so it is not I that must be forced to tell of your plunder, but you that must be compelled to give it up.”
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: willing

examples.original: Haec vox significat voluntariam relationem;
examples.translation: The phrase implies a voluntary return;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fecit amicus recens et cognatus voluntarius;
examples.translation: It was done in fact by your new friend, your volunteer cousin;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed nec illo voluntario ad hostis suos reditu nec ultimo sive carceris seu crucis supplicio deformata maiestas;
examples.translation: His voluntary return to his enemies and his final sufferings, whether in prison or on the cross, in no way sullied his dignity;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: inexperienced in any thing, not knowing, unacquainted with, unskilled, ignorant, without experience (class.; syn.: ignarus, rudis; opp. prudens, callidus); constr. usually with the

examples.original: Neque vero id imperite fecit;
examples.translation: And, indeed, he acted wisely in so doing;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timoleon

examples.original: Imperitis ac rudibus nullus praecipitationis finis est;
examples.translation: For those who lack experience and training, there is no limit to the downhill course;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His imperitorum feriuntur oculi omnia subita, quia causas non novere, mirantium.
examples.translation: The eye of the inexperienced is struck with amazement by these things;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to order, set in order, arrange, adjust, dispose, regulate.

examples.original: Ordinem vitae hunc fere tenuit.
examples.translation: This was in general his manner of life.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Simili superbia violentiaque ceteros tractavit ordines.
examples.translation: He treated the other orders with like insolence and cruelty.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: De ordinando autem, qui in parte Donati baptizatus est, auctor tibi esse non possum;
examples.translation: I cannot accept responsibility for the ordaining of one who was baptized in the Donatist party;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: A furrow

examples.original: Tum in Etruscos versum bellum;
examples.translation: The campaign was then directed against the Etruscans;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quantum disertissimorum versuum inter mimos iacet!
examples.translation: What a quantity of sagacious verses lie buried in the mime!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ita metu ancipiti versi a fuga Romani in hostem et restituta acies.
examples.translation: The cohort of the dictator then entered the engagement for the first time.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the condition of a slave or servant, slavery, servitude (not so in Cic., who has servitus).

examples.original: Et primo in agrestes ingruerant servitiaque;
examples.translation: At first they attacked country people and slaves;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vidi ego pallentes isto terrore puellas Servitium miseras tempus in omne pati.
examples.translation: I have seen women pale with terror on that account, suffering in their misery unending servitude.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to find out by thinking, to contrive, devise, invent

examples.original: Nihil excogitem quam ob rem Oppianicum damnari necesse sit?
examples.translation: Can’t I devise some way of making Oppianicus’s conviction inevitable?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In illo quoque dissentio a Posidonio, quod ferramenta fabrilia excogitata a sapientibus viris iudicat.
examples.translation: On another point also I differ from Posidonius, when he holds that mechanical tools were the invention of wise men.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nihil relinquebatur quod ad ornatum portarum, itinerum, locorum omnium qua Caesar iturus erat excogitari poterat.
examples.translation: Nothing was omitted that wit could devise for the decoration of gates, roads, and every place where Caesar was to pass.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: of the rank or dignity of the patres; belonging to the patricians, patrician, noble (cf. nobilis)

examples.original: Patricii vi contra vim resistunt.
examples.translation: The patricians resisted force with force.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nos citius caruerimus patriciis magistratibus quam illi plebeiis.
examples.translation: We will sooner dispense with patrician magistrates than they with plebeian.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nemo plebeius patriciae virgini vim adferret; patriciorum ista libido est;
examples.translation: No plebeian would offer violence to a patrician maiden: that is a patrician vice.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to pollute, defile, contaminate, desecrate

examples.original: Sed non diu latent scelera.
examples.translation: But crimes do not long remain undetected.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Eodem modo ex sacrilegio lucrum fit, non quia turpe et sceleratum est sacrilegium, sed quia et lucrum habet.
examples.translation: As the serpent in the jar is an evil, and not the gold which lies there beside the serpent;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Omnia scelera etiam ante effectum operis, quantum culpae satis est, perfecta sunt.
examples.translation: All crimes, so far as guilt is concerned, are completed even before the accomplishment of the deed.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that has many folds (class.).

examples.original: Marco Antonio Publio Dolabella consulibus imperium Romanum iam ad Caesarem transferente fortuna varius et multiplex motus civitatis fuit.
examples.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Antonius and Publius Dolabella, while fortune was already transferring the Roman Empire to Caesar, diverse and manifold confusion afflicted the State.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Philologi appellationem assumpsisse videtur, quia sic ut Eratosthenes, qui primus hoc cognomen sibi vindicavit, multiplici variaque doctrina censebatur.
examples.translation: And that he was such is evident from his commentaries, though very few of them survive;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Ab hoc sunt imperatoris Galbae avus ac pater: avus clarior studiis quam dignitate—non enim egressus praeturae gradum—multiplicem nec incuriosam historiam edidit;
examples.translation: The former, who was more eminent for his learning than for his rank—for he did not advance beyond the grade of praetor—published a voluminous and painstaking history.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: To set down; to set, place anywhere (ante-class. and freq. in Liv.; elsewh. rare): destituit omnes servos ad mensam ante se, Caecil. ap.
Latin: Deorsum statuere
Latin: Se removere, derelinquere, deserere, decipere

examples.original: Et Nero quoque vos destituit, non vos Neronem.
examples.translation: It was Nero, too, who deserted you, not you Nero.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Denique quem umquam ista destituere temptantem?
examples.translation: To whom that ever tried have these tasks proved false?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Aut ut Amastriacis quondam Lenaeus ab oris, Nudus Achillea destituaris humo.
examples.translation: Or like Lenaeus faring once from Amastris’ shores mayst thou be left destitute on Achillean soil.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: made of or belonging to wine.

examples.original: Est tibi rure bono generosae fertilis uvae Vinea?
examples.translation: You have a fruitful estate and a vineyard abundant in fine grapes?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quibus fortiter resistentibus vineas turresque egit.
examples.translation: When they offered a brave resistance he brought up mantlets and towers.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Vineis incensis, multis hostium volneratis et occisis, consulum quoque alterum—sed utrum auctores non adiciuat—gravi volnere ex equo deiectum prope interfecerunt.
examples.translation: The mantlets were burned, many of their enemies were wounded or slain, and one of the consuls—which one the historians do not add—was seriously wounded, thrown from his horse, and almost killed.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: inward, internal, intestine (class.).

examples.original: Magna pars vociferantur Servilio Ahala opus esse, qui non in vincla duci iubendo inritet publicum hostem sed unius iactura civis finiat intestinum bellum.
examples.translation: The majority exclaimed that a Servilius Ahala was needed, one who would not exasperate a public enemy by ordering his imprisonment, but would sacrifice a single citizen to end a domestic war.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To balance, make even, level, to determine a level: aquam, to level water, i. e. to ascertain the fall of water by means of a level

examples.original: Erat etiam Stesichori poetae statua, senilis, incurva, cum libro, summo, ut putant, artificio facta;
examples.translation: There was also a statue of the poet Stesichorus, represented as an old man leaning forward and holding a book;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tempus erat, quo Libra pares examinat horas, Non uno plus aequa die, noctique rependit Lux minor hibernae verni solacia damni.
examples.translation: It was the season when Libra balances the hours of day and night in equal scales, and stays level for one day only;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Scripsit enim et multis saepe verbis et breviter aperteque in eo libro quem modo nominavi, ’mortem nihil ad nos pertinere;
examples.translation: For he repeatedly argued at length, and also stated briefly and plainly in the book I have just mentioned, that ’death does not affect us at all;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a place of rest, a couch, bed.

examples.original: His sunt arbores pro cubilibus: ad eas se applicant atque ita paulum modo reclinatae quietem capiunt.
examples.translation: Trees serve them as couches; they bear against them, and thus, leaning but a little, take their rest.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: To frighten from any thing; to deter, discourage from, prevent, hinder (class.).—Constr.

examples.original: Eo autem magis te deterreo ab isto morbo, quod non potest tibi ista res contingere aliter quam si te pudere desierit;
examples.translation: However, I have this further reason for frightening you away from the latter malady, namely, that you could only be successful in practising this style by losing your sense of modesty;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quare non est quod fastidiosi isti te deterreant, quo minus servis tuis hilarem te praestes et non superbe superiorem;
examples.translation: You should therefore not be deterred by these finicky persons from showing yourself to your slaves as an affable person and not proudly superior to them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ille hac religione non modo non est deterritus, sed ad maturandum concitatus est, verens ne prius consilium aperiretur suum, quam cogitata perfecisset.
examples.translation: But the conspirator, far from being turned from his purpose by such an oath, was urged to greater haste, for fear that his design should be disclosed before he had accomplished his purpose.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

definitions: English: not at all, by no means; in class. prose most freq. with adverbs; rarely with adjectives, pronouns, or verbs
English: If only, if indeed (class.)

examples.original: Siquidem inter cetera monasterii necessaria quae longo regendi tempore disponenda comperit, etiam plura fecit oratoria;
examples.translation: For beside all other things needful for the monastery, which his long rule thereof taught him should be provided, he built many chapels;
examples.author: Bede

definitions: English: only, merely

examples.original: Stoici autem tantummodo praeponendam in seligendo, non quo beatior ea vita sit, sed quod ad naturam accommodatior;
examples.translation: Those men of old then, with their duller wits, think that the former life is more desirable, more excellent, more happy;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to beat, strike, thump, buffet with repeated strokes.
English: a beast distinguished for size or ferocity, a monster
Latin: bestia, animalia magna

examples.original: Beluarum hoc quidem extremum, illa autem superiora caduca et incerta, posita non tam in consiliis nostris quam in fortunae temeritate.
examples.translation: This last is the highest aim of brutes; the others are fleeting and unstable things and dependent less upon human foresight than upon the fickleness of fortune.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to excuse a person or thing.

examples.original: Irae atque iracundiae conscius sibi, utramque excusavit edicto distinxitque, pollicitus alteram quidem brevem et innoxiam, alteram non iniustam fore.
examples.translation: He was conscious of his tendency to wrath and resentment and excused both in an edict;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Legati quoque (nam senatus electionem Galbae permiserat) foeda inconstantia nominati, excusati, substituti, ambitu remanendi aut eundi, ut quemque metus vel spes impulerat.
examples.translation: With disgraceful lack of firmness he named men, excused them, made substitutions, as they pleaded with him to stay or go, according to their fears or hopes.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nec excusatur offensa necessitudine officii aut fide advocationis aut fortuitae et subitae dictionis impetu: meditatus videris \[aut\] elegisse personam notabilem et cum auctoritate dicturam.
examples.translation: And the offence you give cannot be held excused by the obligation to render a friendly service, or by loyalty to a client, or by the excitement of an unpremeditated utterance, made off-hand;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: rich/wealthy; richly adorned; fertile/productive (land)
Latin: Status dei; divinitas; deus, praesertim
Latin: Iuppiter

examples.original: Haec omnia in dites a pauperibus inclinata onera. Deinde est honos additus;
examples.translation: All these burdens were shifted from the shoulders of the poor to those of the rich.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to be light or clear, to shine, beam, glitter (syn.: splendeo, fulgeo).
Latin: lucem emittere
Latin: aliquid ad lucem emittendum redigere

examples.original: Luce prima inermos plerosque oppressere.
examples.translation: At daybreak they cut down many of them quite unarmed.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Prima luce hostium equitatus ad castra accedit proeliumque cum nostris equitibus committit.
examples.translation: At break of day the enemy’s horsemen came up to the camp and engaged our own cavalry.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Prima luce magnum numerum impedimentorum ex castris mulorumque produci deque his stramenta detrahi mulionesque cum cassidibus equitum specie ac simulatione collibus circumvehi iubet.
examples.translation: With them he put a few cavalry, to range more widely by way of demonstration, and ordered them all to make for the same general destination by a long circuit.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the quality of being audax, boldness, in a good, but oftener in a bad sense (syn.: fortitudo, audentia, animus, virtus).

examples.original: Quae bona sunt fiduciam faciunt, divitiae audaciam.
examples.translation: Those things which are goods produce confidence, but riches produce shamelessness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Verum hoc adhuc percommode cadit, quod cum incredibili eius audacia singularis stultitia coniuncta est.
examples.translation: But it has very fortunately come about, hitherto, that his incredible audacity has been accompanied by unparalleled folly.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: O di immortales, incredibilem avaritiam singularemque audaciam!
examples.translation: God help us, what incredible greed, what matchless impudence!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to give an official intimation, to make an official announcement or declaration of one's intentions (by means of a messenger, herald, etc.)

examples.original: Postea cur tu, Aebuti, de isto potius fundo quam de alio, si quem habes, Caecinae denuntiabas, si Caecina non possidebat?
examples.translation: Why, subsequently, did you, Aebutius, serve Caecinawith notice toquitthis particular farm rather than any other you may have, if Caecina had no possession?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: unconquered, unsubdued, not vanquished; hence unconquerable, invincible; constr. with

examples.original: Recto tibi invictoque moriendum est.
examples.translation: You must die erect and unyielding.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Censuerunt etiam quidam ut Pannonicus, alii ut Invictus, nonnulli ut Pius cognominaretur.
examples.translation: Some also recommended that he be given the surname of Pannonicus, others of Invictus, others of Pius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Invictus ergo Alexander cum invictis ducibus bella gessisset et eadem fortunae pignora in discrimen detulisset;
examples.translation: So then, an undefeated Alexander would have warred against undefeated generals, and would have brought the same pledges of Fortune to the crisis.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A country of Asia, divided into Armenia Major (eastern, now Turcomania and Kurdistan) and Minor (western, now Anatolia)
Latin: Provincia Romana, in Armenia Minore et Armenia Maiore divisa
Latin: Natio hodiernae Asiae, inter Atropatiam, Turciam, et Persiam

examples.original: Bellvm Armenicvm Ad orientem plus negotii cum Armeniis.
examples.translation: The Armenian War In the east the Armenians caused more trouble.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Missi ad Parthum Armeniumque legati, provisumque ne versis ad civile bellum legionibus terga nudarentur.
examples.translation: He was firmly opposed to extravagant gifts to the soldiers and therefore had a better army.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Mox et ardores per Armeniam et nives per Cappadociam et utriusque caeli subita mutatio pro pestilentia fuit.
examples.translation: Afterwards the heat in Armenia and the snows of Cappadocia and the sudden change from one climate to another were as destructive as a plague.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: that may be assumed, believed, or proved; likely, credible, probable (class.)
English: to be warm or

examples.original: Ista decent pueros aetate et amore calentes;
examples.translation: Such doings suit lads aflame with youth and love;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ausonibus victis et oppido ex is capto Cales item Fregellae coloniae deductae sunt.
examples.translation: The Ausonians were defeated; and their town being taken from them, the colonies of Cales and Fregellae were established.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quique bibunt tenera dulces ab harundine sucos, Et qui tinguentes croceo medicamine crinem Fluxa coloratis astringunt carbasa gemmis, Quique suas struxere pyras vivique calentes Conscendere rogos.
examples.translation: Up rose the men who drink sweet juices from soft reeds; and those who colour their hair with saffron dye and loop up their robes of cotton with brighthued gems;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: violent passion, rage, madness, fury.

examples.original: Eam rem aegre passi Romani M. Furium Camillum sextum tribunum militum creavere.
examples.translation: This incensed the Romans, and they elected Marcus Furius Camillus tribune of the soldiers, for the sixth time.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His vivus furiis agitabere, mortuus isdem, Et brevior poena vita futura tua est.
examples.translation: Cruel thongs shall crack and twined serpents hiss, and torches smoke before thy guilty face.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cerberus et Furiae iam vero et lucis egestas, Tartarus horriferos eructans faucibus aestus— qui neque sunt usquam nec possunt esse profecto.
examples.translation: Cerberusb also and the Furies and the with-holding of light, and Tartarus belching horrible fires from his throat—these neither exist anywhere nor in truth can exist.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: that which fertilizes or manures, dung, ordure, excrement
English: tree-trunk, beam, timber; ship
English: to send or let into a place, to introduce, admit, to send or despatch against, to let loose at, discharge at, to cast or throw into

examples.original: Iuventute armata immissa vastatur agri quod inter urbem ac Fidenas est.
examples.translation: Arming the young men, they sent them to ravage the land between the City and Fidenae.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Illi cum ludos facerent, servos de cavea exire iubebant: tu in alteram servos immisisti, ex altera liberos eiecisti.
examples.translation: When they held the games, they bade slaves depart from the auditorium; you let slaves loose upon one auditorium, and ejected freemen from the other.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of or belonging to a mother, maternal (class.): sanguis, Enn. ap.

examples.original: Facile persuadet ut cupido honorum et cui Tarquinii materna tantum patria esset. Sublatis itaque rebus amigrant Romam.
examples.translation: She had no trouble in persuading a man who was eager for distinction, to whom Tarquinii was only his mother’s birthplace.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Licet haec ipsa et quae deinceps dicturus sum aures tuae, Materne, respuant, cui bono est si apud te Agamemnon aut Iason diserte loquitur?
examples.translation: Very likely you will not relish what I am saying, Maternus, or what I intend to state in the course of my argument;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ex hac stirpe Tiberius Caesar genus trahit, et quidem utrumque: paternum a Tiberio Nerone, maternum ab Appio Pulchro, qui ambo Appi Caeci filii fuerunt.
examples.translation: Such was the stock from which Tiberius Caesar derived his origin, and that too on both sides: on his father’s from Tiberius Nero;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: without doubt, doubtless, indisputably, certainly, surely, truly

examples.original: Octo nimirum legiones unius classis accessionem fore.
examples.translation: No doubt eight legions are to go over to one poor fleet!
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nemo, ut opinor, in culpa est: et nimirum tibi istud lex ipsa renuntiavit.
examples.translation: My belief is that no one is to blame: no doubt the statute itself was your informant;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the murder of one's father or parents, parricide.

examples.original: Iunxit parricidio matris amitae necem.
examples.translation: To matricide he added the murder of his aunt.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Bellvm Cassi et Brvti IIII, 7Brutus et Cassius sic Caesarem quasi Tarquinium regem depulisse regno videbantur, sed libertatem, quam maxime restitutam voluerunt, illo ipso parricidio perdiderunt.
examples.translation: The War against Cassius and Brutus 7. Brutus and Cassius seemed to have cast forth Caesar from the throne like another King Tarquin;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: wool shorn off, a fleece

examples.original: Confer Amyclaeis medicatum vellus aënis Murice cum Tyrio;
examples.translation: Compare a fleece that Amyclae’s vats have dyed, with Tyrian purple;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Iam rarior aer Et par Phoebus aquis densas in vellera nubes Sparserat, et noctes ventura luce rubebant, Servatoque loco rerum discessit ab astris Umor, et ima petit, quidquid pendebat aquarum.
examples.translation: By this time the sky had cleared; the sun, a match for the waters, had broken up the thick clouds into fleeces;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Neutr., to be sad or mournful, to mourn, grieve, lament

examples.original: Turpissimum autem est in homine prudente remedium maeroris lassitudo maerendi.
examples.translation: I should prefer you to abandon grief, rather than have grief abandon you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Departing, either physically or (more freq.) morally, from the right shape, quality, etc.; misshapen, deformed, unsightly, ugly, odious, disgusting; disgraceful, base

examples.original: Potest ex casa vir magnus exire, potest et ex deformi humilique corpusculo formosus animus ac magnus.
examples.translation: A great man can spring from a hovel; so can a beautiful and great soul from an ugly and insignificant body.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Deformis suapte natura res cum speciem iniuriae magis quam doli prae se ferret, concitati homines cogunt clamore suo magistratus senatum vocare;
examples.translation: This spectacle, so hideous in itself, pointed clearly to injury and not to guile. In an uproar of excitement, the people obliged their magistrates to convoke the senate.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of flax or lint, flaxen, linen-
English: excellent, outstanding (in quality/worth/degree/importance), surpassing all

examples.original: Sed quis eam iustius explicabit quam tu, ad cuius summam eruditionem et praestantissimum ingenium cura quoque et meditatio accessit?”
examples.translation: But is there anyone who could more properly unfold it than yourself, seeing that to profound scholarship and eminent ability you have added much careful study?”
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Tum incubuit hostium acies, integris ordinibus, robore et numero praestantior: Othoniani, quamquam dispersi, pauciores, fessi, proelium tamen acriter sumpsere.
examples.translation: The fact that in places the ground was encumbered by trees and vineyards gave the battle many aspects: the troops fought now hand to hand, again at a distance;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: no indeed (contradiction); on the contrary, more correctly; indeed, nay more
Latin: Ex contrario

examples.original: Caesar Locus erat castrorum editus et paulatim ab imo acclivis circiter passus mille.
examples.translation: The position of the camp was on high ground, with a gradual slope from the bottom of about a mile.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Certe, cum commotus ira se a vestibulo templi citato gradu proriperet, lapsus per gradus capite graviter offenso impactus imo ita est saxo ut sopiretur.
examples.translation: At all events, as he hurried, beside himself with rage, from the entrance of the temple, he slipped on the stairs, and struck his head so hard on the lowest stone that he lost consciousness.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: confusion, disorder, disturbance.

examples.original: Compluribus navibus fractis reliquae cum essent funibus, ancoris reliquisque armamentis amissis ad navigandum inutiles, magna, id quod necesse erat accidere, totius exercitus perturbatio facta est.
examples.translation: This, as was inevitable, caused great dismay throughout the army. For there were no other ships to carry them back;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: ugliness, unsightliness, foulness, deformity (syn. deformitas).

examples.original: Quid sibi vult ista carminis effeminati turpitudo?
examples.translation: What does he mean by making terms with panic fear?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et si turpitudinem fugimus in statu et motu corporis, quid est cur pulchritudinem non sequamur?
examples.translation: And if we avoid ugliness in bodily movement and posture, why should we not pursue beauty?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam illud me non praeterit, cuiuscumque modi sit mater, tamen in iudicio filii de turpitudine parentis dici vix oportere.
examples.translation: For I am not unaware that, whatever character his mother bears, it is hardly becoming at the trial of a son to mention the depravity of his parent.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: upon a thing (class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; ŭi, ĭtum, āre; 1

examples.original: Tum incubuit hostium acies, integris ordinibus, robore et numero praestantior: Othoniani, quamquam dispersi, pauciores, fessi, proelium tamen acriter sumpsere.
examples.translation: The fact that in places the ground was encumbered by trees and vineyards gave the battle many aspects: the troops fought now hand to hand, again at a distance;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ira militum in Tampium Flavianum incubuit, nullo criminis argumento, sed iam pridem invisus turbine quodam ad exitium poscebatur: propinquum Vitellii, proditorem Othonis, interceptorem donativi clamitabant.
examples.translation: The soldiers’ wrath fell on Tampius Flavianus, of whose guilt there was not the slightest proof; but the troops already hated him and now in a whirlwind of rage demanded his death.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: before, precede (in space), to take the lead, get the start; with

examples.original: Quae ista dementia est malum suum antecedere?
examples.translation: What madness it is to anticipate one’s troubles!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cum aspexeris, quot te antecedant, cogita, quot sequantur.
examples.translation: When you see many ahead of you, think how many are behind!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Postquam in agrum Romanum ventum est, obviam hosti consules eunt: Valerius quadrato agmine peditem ducit; Brutus ad explorandum cum equitatu antecessit.
examples.translation: When they had come into Roman territory the consuls went out to meet the enemy: Valerius led the foot in defensive formation;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to need, want, to stand in need or want of any thing (class.).

examples.original: Ut quid dicit similiter: Spiritus adiuvat infirmitatem nostram, si natura nostra sic creata est, ut spiritu ad opera iustitiae non indigeat adiuvari?
examples.translation: And why does he likewise say, ”The Spirit helpeth our infirmities,”f if our nature is created such that it does not need any help from the Spirit to do the works of righteousness?
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a small ladle for transferring the wine from the mixing-bowl (crater) to the drinking-cup (cf. Becker, Gall. 3, p. 221).
English: the reed, cane

examples.original: Tela iugo vincta est, stamen secernit harundo, Inseritur medium radiis subtemen acutis, Quod lato paviunt insecti pectine dentes.
examples.translation: The web is bound to frame; asunder now The reed doth part the warp.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quique bibunt tenera dulces ab harundine sucos, Et qui tinguentes croceo medicamine crinem Fluxa coloratis astringunt carbasa gemmis, Quique suas struxere pyras vivique calentes Conscendere rogos.
examples.translation: Up rose the men who drink sweet juices from soft reeds; and those who colour their hair with saffron dye and loop up their robes of cotton with brighthued gems;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: To leave off, intermit, omit, neglect; constr. with
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; mīsi, missum, 3

examples.original: In his rebus circiter dies x consumit ne nocturnis quidem temporibus ad laborem militum intermissis.
examples.translation: Upon this business he spent about ten days, allowing no interruption even at night-time in the work of the troops.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eo infestior facta plebes seditione domestica bellum externum excivit. Bello deinde civiles discordiae intermissae.
examples.translation: This increased the rancour of the plebeians, and by their seditions at home they brought about a foreign war.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Septimo die, cum iter non intermitteret, ab exploratoribus certior factus est Ariovisti copias a nostris milibus passuum quattuor et xx abesse.
examples.translation: On the seventh day of continuous marching the scouts reported that the forces of Ariovistus were four-and-twenty miles away from our own.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a violent wind (by which things are prostrated), a storm, hurricane, tempest (class.).
English: to attend, wait upon, serve, esp. at table, to serve up, pour out, hand food or drink (syn.: servio, appareo, praebeo, suggero; class.).

examples.original: Ipse manu subicit gladios ac tela ministrat Adversosque iubet ferro confundere voltus.
examples.translation: In person he advances the fighting line and urges on his rearguard;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed hoc ipsum quo modo ministrem ad salutem aliorum non quaerens, quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis, ut salvi fiant?
examples.translation: But how am I to minister even that for the salvation of others, not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saveda?
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to infold, involve, entangle, entwine, inwrap, envelop, encircle, embrace, clasp, grasp (freq. and class.; cf.: irretio, impedio).

examples.original: Sed forte iterum quaeris a me, quo modo ista facias tantis mundi huius necessitatibus implicatus.
examples.translation: But perhaps you ask me again how you are to accomplish this, involved as you are in the great distresses of this world.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Nec enim in Torquati sermone quidquam implicatum aut tortuosum fuit, nostraque, ut mihi videtur, dilucida oratio.
examples.translation: There was nothing abstruse or intricate in the discourse of Torquatus, and my own exposition was, I believe, as clear as daylight.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quies necessaria morbo implicitum exercitum tenuit. Extractum in tertium annum bellum est Q. Fabio et T. Quinctio consulibus.
examples.translation: The war dragged on into its third year, the consulship of Quintus Fabius and Titus Quinctius.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to make soft, pliant, flexible, or supple, to soften (class.).

examples.original: Molli consurgit Amyclas, Quem dabat alga, toro.
examples.translation: Amyclas rose up from the soft bed that seaweed gave him.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed prius ancillam captandae nosse puellae Cura sit: accessus molliet illa tuos.
examples.translation: But take care first to know the handmaid of the woman you would win;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cappadoces mea signa timent et dedita sacris Incerti Iudaea dei mollisque Sophene.
examples.translation: My standards overawe Cappadocia, and Judaea given over to the worship of an unknown god, and effeminate Sophene;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: that which spins or twirls round (cf. vertex).
Latin: turbas excitare, discordiam moliri
Latin: res confundere

examples.original: Is erat ex hac turba lucifugarum.
examples.translation: Papinius belonged to the tribe of those who shun the light.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac primi quidem impetus turbo inter Padum atque Ticinum valido statim fragore detonuit.
examples.translation: The tempest of the first assault crashed with a mighty roar between the Padus and the Ticinus.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Ira militum in Tampium Flavianum incubuit, nullo criminis argumento, sed iam pridem invisus turbine quodam ad exitium poscebatur: propinquum Vitellii, proditorem Othonis, interceptorem donativi clamitabant.
examples.translation: The soldiers’ wrath fell on Tampius Flavianus, of whose guilt there was not the slightest proof; but the troops already hated him and now in a whirlwind of rage demanded his death.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a bridge across a river, ditch, or marsh, between towers, etc.
Latin: aedificium quod trans flumen, fossam vel vallem munitur

examples.original: In eo flumine pons erat.
examples.translation: There was a bridge over the river;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Consules profecti ad Pontium in conloquium, cum de foedere victor agitaret,.
examples.translation: The consuls then went to confer with Pontius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et fuere qui se statim dederent: plures abrupto ponte instanti hosti viam abstulerunt.
examples.translation: The larger part, however, broke down the bridge and so, by cutting off the road, blocked their foes’ advance.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a tree, frame, or other wooden instruments of execution, on which criminals were impaled or hanged
Latin: Instrumentum e duplici ligno, recto et transverso, in quo damnati clavis, aut funibus affigebantur

examples.original: Hannibal, dux Poenorum, victa classe cui praefuerat, a militibus suis in crucem sublatus est.
examples.translation: Hannibal, a Carthaginian general, on the defeat of the fleet which he commanded, was crucified by his own soldiers.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed nec illo voluntario ad hostis suos reditu nec ultimo sive carceris seu crucis supplicio deformata maiestas;
examples.translation: His voluntary return to his enemies and his final sufferings, whether in prison or on the cross, in no way sullied his dignity;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nam Stratonem quidem, iudices, in crucem esse actum exsecta scitote lingua: quod nemo Larinatium est qui nesciat.
examples.translation: As for Strato, gentlemen, I have to inform you that he was crucified, after first having had his tongue cut out, as everyone at Larinum knows.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to divide, distribute (class.; cf.: divido, impertio, dispenso, participo, communico).

examples.original: Tum copiis in tres partes distributis impedimenta omnium legionum Aduatucam contulit.
examples.translation: Then, dividing his forces into three parts, he concentrated the baggage of all the legions at Aduatuca.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Huc accedebant xviii onerariae naves, quae ex eo loco ab milibus passuum octo vento tenebantur quo minus in eundem portum venire possent: has equitibus distribuit.
examples.translation: To the total stated eighteen transports should be added, which were detained eight miles off by the wind, and prevented from entering the port of concentration; these he allotted to the cavalry.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: To bring or carry back word, to report, give notice, declare, announce.

examples.original: Itaque renuntiat Habonius illam decisionem tutoribus.
examples.translation: Habonius accordingly cancelled the agreement with the other guardians.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nemo, ut opinor, in culpa est: et nimirum tibi istud lex ipsa renuntiavit.
examples.translation: My belief is that no one is to blame: no doubt the statute itself was your informant;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Homo, id quod erat facillimum, primo vetat sortiri, iubet extra sortem Theomnastum renuntiari.
examples.translation: The man first tried the simple plan of forbidding the lot, ordering Theomnastus to be returned as appointed without it.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a raging, rage, fierceness, ferocity.

examples.original: Saevitiam ingenii per haec maxime ostendit.
examples.translation: The following are special instances of his innate brutality.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Nec minore saevitia foris et in exteros grassatus est.
examples.translation: Those outside his family he assailed with no less cruelty.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Nec minore livore ac malignitate quam superbia saevitiaque paene adversus omnis aevi hominum genus grassatus est.
examples.translation: He assailed mankind of almost every epoch with no less envy and malice than insolence and cruelty.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: to cast off, put away, divorce, repudiate (cf. reicio)

examples.original: Eorum ego voluntatem omnium repudiavi; non modo proditori sed ne perfugae quidem locus in meis castris cuiquam fuit.
examples.translation: I rejected the advances of all such persons: no room has been found in my camp for traitors, nor even for simple deserters.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Perfacile vero apud istius modi praetorem, a quo M. Marcelli tutoris in causa pupilli Iunii et oratio et voluntas et auctoritas repudiata est.
examples.translation: An easy thing indeed, with a praetor such as this, with whom Marcus Marcellus pleaded for his ward Iunius, to find that his eloquence, his earnest wishes, his personal influence, all went for nothing!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Temporibus autem quibusdam et aut officiis debitis aut rerum necessitatibus saepe eveniet ut et voluptates repudiandae sint et molestiae non recusandae.
examples.translation: But in certain emergencies and owing to the claims of duty or the obligations of business it will frequently occur that pleasures have to be repudiated and annoyances accepted.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to weigh well in one's mind, to consider maturely, deliberate respecting a thing; to take counsel, consult, advise upon

examples.original: Tu vero omnia cum amico delibera, sed de ipso prius.
examples.translation: Indeed, I would have you discuss everything with a friend;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Deliberatur de Avarico in communi concilio, incendi placeret an defendi.
examples.translation: They deliberated in a general convention whether Avaricum should be burnt or defended.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Caesar Legati haec se ad suos relaturos dixerunt et re deliberata post diem tertium ad Caesarem reversuros: interea ne propius se castra moveret, petierunt.
examples.translation: The envoys said that they would report this to their people and, after deliberation upon the matter, return to Caesar in three days: they asked him not to move his camp nearer in the meanwhile.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to strew in front of, to strew before one; also, to throw to the ground, throw down, overthrow, prostrate (syn.: fundo, profligo, provolvo).
English: shamefacedness, modesty, chastity, virtue (freq. and class.)

examples.original: Pudicitiae neque suae neque alienae pepercit.
examples.translation: He respected neither his own chastity nor that of anyone else.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: the tail of animals

examples.original: Tu, qui flagrante minacem Scorpion incendis cauda chelasque peruris, Quid tantum, Gradive, paras?
examples.translation: But Mars—what dreadful purpose has he, when he kindles the Scorpion menacing with fiery tail and scorches its claws?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to be struck senseless, to be stunned, benumbed; to be struck aghast, to be astonished, astounded, amazed, confounded, stupefied, etc.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; ui, ēre

examples.original: Ille in se stupet, ille caligat, invidet caecis.
examples.translation: Such a man is internally dazed; his vision is darkened;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Stupebam, ubi aliquid ex illis alio atque alio loco fulserat.
examples.translation: I used to be dazed when I caught some gleam of them here and there.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Multi, Pharsalica castra Cum peterent nondum fama prodente ruina, Occursu stupuere ducis vertigine rerum Attoniti, cladisque suae vix ipse fidelis Auctor erat.
examples.translation: Many who were on their way to the camp at Pharsalia, before rumour had published his defeat abroad, were startled to meet their leader and astounded by the sudden change of fortune;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Native, indigenous, not foreign.
Latin: natus liber

examples.original: Super ingenuorum paedagogia et nuptarum concubinatus Vestali virgini Rubriae vim intulit.
examples.translation: Besides abusing freeborn boys and seducing married women, he debauched the vestal virgin Rubria.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Bellvm Servile III, 19Etsi cum sociis—nefas—cum liberis tamen et ingenuis dimicatum est: quis aequo animo ferat in principe populo bella servorum?
examples.translation: The Servile War 19. Although we fought with allies—in itself an impious act—yet we fought with men who enjoyed liberty and were of free birth;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Melissus, Spoleti natus ingenuus, sed ob discordiam parentum expositus, cura et industria educatoris sui altiora studia percepit, ac Maecenati pro grammatico muneri datus est.
examples.translation: Nevertheless through the care and devotion of the man who reared him, he received a superior education, and was presented to Maecenas as a grammarian.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: of or belonging to a garden

examples.original: Nunc vero quid faciat Hortensius?
examples.translation: But in this case, what is Hortensius to do?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Libenter haec coram cum Q. Catulo et Q. Hortensio, summis et clarissimis viris, disputarem;
examples.translation: I would gladly discuss the matter personally with eminent and distinguished men like Quintus Catulus and Quintus Hortensius;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Plebs propter aes alienum post graves et longas seditiones ad ultimum secessit in Ianiculum, unde a Q. Hortensio dictatore deducta est; isque in ipso magistratu decessit.
examples.translation: Because of their debts, the plebs, after serious and protracted quarrels, seceded to Janiculum, whence they were brought back by Quintus Hortensius the dictator, who died before the expiration of his term.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to cut off in front; hence, in gen.

examples.original: Da mihi hoc, iam tibi maximam partem defensionis praecideris; non enim poteris aratores tibi iratos esse atque inimicos dicere.
examples.translation: Allow me this and instantly you have cut away the main prop of your defence, being then unable to allege that the farmers are angry and hostile.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the stem, stock, bole, or trunk of a tree (without regard to its branches).

examples.original: Quam nodosi sunt et retorridi rami, quam tristes et squalidi trunci!
examples.translation: Their branches are so gnarled and shrivelled; the boles are so rough and unkempt!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sero tandem dispensator Argivus et hoc et ceterum truncum in privatis eius hortis Aurelia via sepulturae dedit.
examples.translation: At last, however, his steward Argivus consigned it to the tomb with the rest of the body in Galba’s private gardens on the Aurelian Road.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ecce procul saevus sterilis se robore trunci Torsit et inmisit—iaculum vocat Africa—serpens Perque caput Pauli transactaque tempora fugit.
examples.translation: Behold! a fierce serpent, called by Africa iaculus, aimed and hurled itself at Paulus from a barren tree far off;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: plant with something (class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; sēvi, sĭtum or sătum, 3

examples.original: Conseruere manus et multo bracchia nexu;
examples.translation: They locked hands and arms in manifold embrace;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Cum his manum conseruit utrosque profligavit.
examples.translation: With those two he joined battle and routed them both.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

definitions: English: To think over, bethink one's self of, be mindful of a thing (as the result of the reminisci, the recalling of it to memory), to call to mind, remember, recollect

examples.original: Quid enim non ”modo” est, si recorderis?
examples.translation: For what is not ”but a moment ago” when one begins to use the memory?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Subinde itaque, Lucili, quam multa sis consecutus recordare.
examples.translation: Therefore continually remind yourself, Lucilius, how many ambitions you have attained.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Populum brevi, postquam periculum ab eo nullum erat, per se ipsas recordantem virtutes desiderium eius tenuit.
examples.translation: In a short time the people, remembering—now that he was no longer a source of danger—only his good qualities, regretted him.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: advance to one's assistance (the figure taken from the advance of a military reserve; v. subsidium)

examples.original: Succurrit inimicus illi Vorenus et laboranti subvenit.
examples.translation: His enemy, Vorenus, ran up to him and helped him in his distress.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Nec multo post Vestricius Spurinna iussu Othonis, relicto Placentiae modico praesidio, cum cohortibus subvenit.
examples.translation: Shortly after, at Otho’s orders, Vestricius Spurinna left a small garrison at Placentia and came with his cohorts of auxiliaries.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: steam, exhalation
English: a thick atmosphere, a mist

examples.original: Ipse caput medio Titan cum ferret Olympo, Condidit ardentes atra caligine currus Involvitque orbem tenebris gentesque coegit Desperare diem;
examples.translation: The sun himself, while rearing his head in the zenith, hid his burning chariot in black darkness and veiled his sphere in gloom, forcing mankind to despair of daylight;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a trumpet, esp. a war-trumpet

examples.original: Tum ab incolis deserta civitas direpta primum, deinde tuba praecinente deleta est.
examples.translation: The city, deserted by its inhabitants, was first plundered and then destroyed at a signal given by trumpets.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Non decoros corporis motus nec varios per tubam ac tibiam cantus, quibus exceptus spiritus aut in exitu aut in transitu formatur in vocem.
examples.translation: It is not the graceful poses of the body, or the varied notes produced by horn and flute, whereby the breath is received and, as it passes out or through, is transformed into voice.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac reliquarum legionum milites non exaudito sono tubae, quod satis magna valles intercedebat, tamen ab tribunis militum legatisque, ut erat a Caesare praeceptum, retinebantur.
examples.translation: But the rank and file of the other legions did not hear the trumpet-call, as a considerable valley lay in between;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: strength.
Latin: Robur corporis
Latin: virtus rerum fortiter agendarum sine metus impeditione

examples.original: Etiamnunc interrogo: nempe fortitudo optabilis est?
examples.translation: At this point I ask you: Is not bravery desirable?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Usus est Thrasybulus non minus prudentia quam fortitudine;
examples.translation: Thrasybulus showed no less judgment than courage;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Thrasybulus

examples.original: An ab hac eius infamia ac nequitia vestros animos in aliam partem fortitudinis commemoratione traducat?
examples.translation: Is he to divert your attention from his scandalous immorality by dwelling upon his bravery?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: come between, to intervene, to be between (syn. intervenio).

examples.original: Neque ullum fere totius hiemis tempus sine sollicitudine Caesaris intercessit, quin aliquem de consiliis ac motu Gallorum nuntium acciperet.
examples.translation: And scarcely a moment the whole winter through passed without anxiety for Caesar, without the receipt of some message concerning the projected rising of the Gauls.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Una nox intercesserat cum iste Dorotheum sic diligebat ut diceres omnia inter eos esse communia, Agathinum ita observabat ut aliquem affinem atque propinquum;
examples.translation: After one night there he was so fond of Dorotheus that one would have supposed they had all things in common, and was paying Agathinus the attentions due to a near connexion;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ac reliquarum legionum milites non exaudito sono tubae, quod satis magna valles intercedebat, tamen ab tribunis militum legatisque, ut erat a Caesare praeceptum, retinebantur.
examples.translation: But the rank and file of the other legions did not hear the trumpet-call, as a considerable valley lay in between;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: unfruitful, barren, sterile, of plants and animals

examples.original: Non equidem invideo: numquid tamen ulla feritur Quae sterilis sola conspicienda coma est?
examples.translation: I do not envy them: yet is any tree struck that is sterile, and admired for its leaves alone?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ecce procul saevus sterilis se robore trunci Torsit et inmisit—iaculum vocat Africa—serpens Perque caput Pauli transactaque tempora fugit.
examples.translation: Behold! a fierce serpent, called by Africa iaculus, aimed and hurled itself at Paulus from a barren tree far off;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: the evening, even

examples.original: Inumbrante vespera universum Flaviani exercitus robur advenit.
examples.translation: As evening fell, the great mass of the Flavian troops arrived in a body.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Tum demum Ariovistus partem suarum copiarum, quae castra minora oppugnaret, misit. Acriter utrimque usque ad vesperum pugnatum est.
examples.translation: Then at last Ariovistus sent a part of his own forces to attack the lesser camp, and both sides fought in spirited fashion till eventide.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Iamque dies medius tenues contraxerat umbras, Inque pari spatio vesper et ortus erant: Ecce, redit Cephalus silvis, Cyllenia proles, Oraque fontana fervida pulsat aqua.
examples.translation: And now midday had drawn short the unsubstantial shadows, and evening and morning were equally removed: lo! Cephalus, son of Cyllene, returns from the woods, and scatters spring water on his glowing cheeks.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to search carefully, examine thoroughly, explore a thing; to search, examine a person (syn.: indago, rimo).

examples.original: Scrutatus sum quae potui et quaesivi omnia;
examples.translation: I examined everything I could, and asked questions about everything.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Scrutabitur scholas nostras et obiciet philosophis congiaria, amicas, gulam.
examples.translation: He will forestall every word which I am about to utter.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac ne tribuniciam quidem potestatem statim nec patris patriae appellationem nisi sero recepit. Nam consuetudinem scrutandi salutantes manente adhuc bello civili omiserat.
examples.translation: As for the custom of searching those who came to pay their morning calls, he gave that up before the civil war was over.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a divine omen indicating misfortune, an evil omen, portent
Latin: Monstratu dignum

examples.original: Nam rictus oraque monstri Quis timuit?
examples.translation: For who ever felt fear of the monster’s face and open mouth?
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed illud horrentius, quod molientibus aedem in fundamentis humanum repertum est caput, nec dubitavere cuncti monstrum pulcherrimum imperii sedem caputque terrarum promittere.
examples.translation: A more alarming incident was the discovery of a human head in the foundations when they were building the temple;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nil, Africa, de te Nec de te, natura, queror: tot monstra ferentem Gentibus ablatum dederas serpentibus orbem, Inpatiensque solum Cereris cultore negato Damnasti atque homines voluisti desse venenis.
examples.translation: I do not blame Africa, nor Nature: Nature had taken from men and assigned to serpents a region so fertile of monsters: the soil would bear no corn, and she condemned it to lie untilled;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to displease (opp. placeo and complaceo, v. 3. dis, II. —rare but class.): quodne vobis placeat, displiceat mihi?

examples.original: Condicio itaque quam insinuare dignatus es, non mihi displicet, si nuptura est;
examples.translation: The condition, therefore, that you are good enough to suggest seems to me satisfactory, if she gets married;
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Namque etsi Dionysii crudelitas ei displicebat, tamen salvum propter necessitudinem, magis etiam suorum causa studebat.
examples.translation: He was intimate with the elder Dionysius as much because of his character as their relationship;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

definitions: English: to grow red, to redden.

examples.original: Fabianum, cum in senatum testis esset inductus, erubuisse memini, et hic illum mire pudor decuit.
examples.translation: Fabianus also, I remember, reddened when he appeared as a witness before the senate; and his embarrassment became him to a remarkable degree.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Neque hoc tibi tantum sed etiam mihi prodest. Si enim non sunt in me, salubriter erubesco, atque ut sint, inardesco.
examples.translation: This benefits not only you, but me too, for if they are lacking in me, it is wholesome for me to be shamed and inflamed with desire to acquire them.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Noli erubescere, Appi, collegam in sacerdotio habere quem in censura quem in consulatu collegam habere potuisti, cuius tam dictatoris magister equitum quam magistri equitum dictator esse potes.
examples.translation: It is quite as possible that he should be dictator and you his master of the horse as that it should be the other way about.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a door, house-door.
Latin: porta domus
Latin: aditus
