examples.translation: This conflux of all kinds of living things distressed the citizens with its strange smells, while the country-people, being packed into narrow quarters, suffered greatly from the heat and want of sleep;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A nail, usually of metal.

examples.original: Lex vetusta est, priscis litteris verbisque scripta, ut qui praetor maximus sit idibus Septembribus clavum pangat;
examples.translation: There is an ancient law, recorded in archaic words and letters, that the chief magistrate shall on the thirteenth of September drive a nail;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: lightness, as to weight.

examples.original: In capitis mei levitatem iocatus est et in oculorum valitudinem et in crurum gracilitatem et in staturam.
examples.translation: Some jest at the baldness of my head, the weakness of my eyes, the thinness of my legs, my build.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Neque enim oratorius iste, immo hercle ne virilis quidem cultus est, quo plerique temporum nostrorum actores ita utuntur ut lascivia verborum et levitate sententiarum et licentia compositionis histrionales modos exprimant.
examples.translation: There is a fashion much in vogue with quite a number of counsel nowadays that ill befits an orator, and is indeed scarce worthy even of a man.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: the womb

examples.original: Dissiluit stringens uterum membrana, fluuntque Viscera;
examples.translation: The membrane that confines the belly snapped asunder, and the bowels gushed out.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Quare si ad melius cogitandum quies aliqua data est, utere divino beneficio.
examples.translation: So, if you do obtain some quietness for deeper reflection, avail yourself of what is a heavenly boon.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Tu quoque, cui rugis uterum Lucina notavit, Ut celer aversis utere Parthus equis.
examples.translation: And you whose belly Lucina has marked with wrinkles, like the swift Parthian, use a backward-turned steed.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: an attendant granted to a magistrate, as a sign of official dignity. The Romans adopted this custom from the Etrurians

examples.original: Ille cum a lictoribus iam traheretur, provocavit;
examples.translation: The lictors were already dragging the man away, when he appealed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Consules in sedem processere suam, missique lictores ad sumendum supplicium.
examples.translation: The consuls advanced to their tribunal and dispatched the lictors to execute the sentence.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Medium erat tempus forte sementis, cum patricium virum innixum aratro suo lictor in ipso opere deprehendit.
examples.translation: It happened to be the middle of the season of sowing, when the lictor found the patrician actually at work bending over his plough.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: want of strength; weakness, feebleness.

examples.original: Ut quid dicit similiter: Spiritus adiuvat infirmitatem nostram, si natura nostra sic creata est, ut spiritu ad opera iustitiae non indigeat adiuvari?
examples.translation: And why does he likewise say, ”The Spirit helpeth our infirmities,”f if our nature is created such that it does not need any help from the Spirit to do the works of righteousness?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Nam corporis quidem nostri infirmitas multos subit casus per se: denique ipsum corpus tenuissima de causa saepe conficitur: deorum tela in impiorum mentibus figuntur.
examples.translation: The very frailty of our physical structure exposes it to many disasters; and, indeed, often the structure is even destroyed by the slightest of influences;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Lavacrum etiam corporum ususque balnearum non sit assiduus, sed eo, quo solet, intervallo temporis tribuatur, hoc est semel in mense. Cuius autem infirmitatis necessitas cogit lavandum corpus, non longius differatur;
examples.translation: If, however, the need arising from any illness demands the washing of the body, let it not be too long postponed, and let it be done without murmuring for medical reasons;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to carry, pour, throw, or put into, in, or upon a place.

examples.original: Hos mihi circulatores, qui philosophiam honestius neglexissent quam vendunt, in faciem ingeret.
examples.translation: But I have decided to put up with taunts;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sancto fratri nostro filio tuo Piniano nullus ab Hipponiensibus metus mortis ingestus est, etiamsi forte ipse tale aliquid timuit;
examples.translation: The people of Hippo did nothing to make our holy brother, your son Pinianus, apprehensive of death, even though he himself perhaps entertained some fear of it.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Est ille plus quam capit, et ingenti aviditate onerat distentum ventrem ac desuetum iam ventris officio, ut maiore opera omnia egerat quam ingessit;
examples.translation: The master eats more than he can hold, and with monstrous greed loads his belly until it is stretched and at length ceases to do the work of a belly;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: A moderating, moderation in any thing; moderateness, temperateness of the weather (Ciceron.)

examples.original: Acuebat hac moderatione tam iusta studia;
examples.translation: Such moderation but intensified the well-merited enthusiasm of his friends;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Moderationis eorum argumentum exemplo unius rei notasse satis erit.
examples.translation: As proof of their moderation, it will suffice to note a single example.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Atque his tribus generibus honestorum notatis, quartum sequitur et in eadem pulchritudine et aptum ex illis tribus, in quo inest ordo et moderatio.
examples.translation: These three kinds of moral goodness being noted, there follows a fourth kind, possessed of equal beauty, and indeed arising out of the other three. This is the principle of order and of restraint.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a vessel, a ship, bark, boat.

examples.original: Navigio ista obsunt, non rectori eius, qua rector est.
examples.translation: These mishaps obstruct the voyage but not the steersman qua steersman.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Qua in re admodum fuit militum virtus laudanda, qui vectoriis gravibusque navigiis non intermisso remigandi labore longarum navium cursum adaequarunt.
examples.translation: And herein was the spirit of the troops much to be commended, who, in the heavily built transports, by uninterrupted effort of rowing kept level with the men-of-war.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: remains, relics, remnants; what is left
English: a crab, a river-crab, sea-crab.
Latin: Saeptum ex rectis et obliquis lignis, aut ferramentis, modicoque intervallo distinctis contextum
Latin: Piscis crusta munitus, pedibus octonis in obliquum flexis, et praeterea binis brachiis in denticulatas forcipes desinentibus
English: a commendation, recommending (in good prose, and very freq.).
English: rich, wealthy, opulent

examples.original: Melius in Volscis imperatum est; fusi primo proelio hostes fugaque in urbem Antium, ut tum res erant, opulentissimam, acti.
examples.translation: The Volscian expedition was better directed: the enemy were routed in the first engagement and driven in flight to Antium, a very opulent city for those days.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Contra ipsis omnia opulenta et fida, Pannoniam Moesiam Dalmatiam Orientem cum integris exercitibus, Italiam et caput rerum urbem senatumque et populum, nunquam obscura nomina, etiam si aliquando obumbrentur;
examples.translation: On the other hand, our own resources are rich and certain: Pannonia, Moesia, Dalmatia and the East are with us; their armies are undiminished;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Postero die singulis captivis ab equite ac centurionibus sorte ductis, et quorum eximia virtus fuerat, binis, aliis sub corona venundatis exercitum victorem opulentumque praeda triumphans dictator Romam reduxit;
examples.translation: After commanding his master of the horse to lay down his office, he himself abdicated, giving up in peace on the sixteenth day the supreme authority he had received in time of war and danger.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: faint, languid, weary, tired, exhausted

examples.original: Fecit et in capta Lyrneside magnus Achilles, Cum premeret mollem lassus ab hoste torum.
examples.translation: Thus did the great Achilles with the Lyrnesian captive, when weary from the foe he burdened the soft couch.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a foreteller, soothsayer, prophet

examples.original: In hac omnes sancti patres nostri et patriarchae et prophetae et apostoli placuerunt deo;
examples.translation: In this love all our holy fathers and patriarchs and prophets and apostles pleased God;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: weariness, irksomeness, tediousness; loathing, disgust (not freq. till after the Aug. period; perh. not at all in Cic. or Cæs.).

examples.original: O, ego, cum longae venerunt taedia vitae, Optavi quotiens arida facta mori!
examples.translation: Ah! how oft, grown weary of my long life, have I wished to wither up and die!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Veientes contra taedio annuae ambitionis, quae interdum discordiarum causa erat, regem creavere.
examples.translation: But the Veientes, weary of annual canvassing, which was sometimes the cause of brawls, chose a king.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nam illa quoque inopia et exilitas minus intentum auditorem habet taedio interruptae tarditatis, facilius tamen insidit, quod exspectatur, quam quod praetervolat.
examples.translation: For that poverty-stricken and thin-spun style also makes the audience less attentive because they are weary of its stammering slowness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that part of the abdomen which extends from the lowest ribs to the pubes, the groin, flank.

examples.original: Interest nihil, ilia ad nos veniat an ad illam nos.
examples.translation: There is no difference whether death comes to us, or whether we go to death.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fessa iacet cervix, fumant sudoribus artus, Oraque proiecta squalent arentia lingua, Pectora rauca gemunt, quae creber anhelitus urguet, Et defecta gravis longe trahit ilia pulsus, Siccaque sanguineis durescit spuma lupatis.
examples.translation: The weary neck sinks down, the limbs reek with sweat, the tongue protrudes and the mouth is rough and dry; the lungs, driven by quick pants, give a hoarse murmur;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a Roman surname.

examples.original: Sed insidiatores ab Othone in Germaniam, a Vitellio in urbem missi.
examples.translation: Otho sent secret agents to Germany, and Vitellius sent his agents to Rome.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Septimam decimam cohortem e colonia Ostiensi in urbem acciri Otho iusserat;
examples.translation: Otho had given orders that the Seventeenth cohort be brought from the colony of Ostia to Rome.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Vinius pro M. Othone, Laco atque Icelus consensu non tam unum aliquem fovebant quam alium, Neque erat Galbae ignota Othonis ac Titi Vinii amicitia;
examples.translation: Vinius favoured Marcus Otho; Laco and Icelus agreed not so much in favouring any particular person as in supporting someone other than Otho.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: Endowed, gifted, or provided with, possessed of something (above others) (freq. and class.; syn.: instructus, ornatus); constr. with

examples.original: Virtute enim ipsa non tam multi praediti esse quam videri volunt.
examples.translation: For many wish not so much to be, as to seem to be, endowed with real virtue.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quam doleo abesse ab huius iudicio L. Volusienum, summo splendore hominem ac virtute praeditum.
examples.translation: How much I regret, gentlemen, the absence from my client’s trial of the eminent and virtuous L. Volusienus!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nemo mirabatur in Africano illo, quod in me nunc, homine parvis opibus ac facultatibus praedito, simulant sese mirari, cum moleste ferunt: ”Quid sibi iste vult?
examples.translation: No one thought it strange then that Africanus should do what people to-day pretend to think strange when done by a man of such moderate wealth and modest capacity as myself.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to cut to pieces, to slay or kill cruelly, to slaughter, butcher, massacre (class.; syn.: obtrunco, jugulo, perimo).

examples.original: Qua ut poteretur, virum eius Atticum Vestinum consulem in honore ipso trucidavit.
examples.translation: To possess the latter he slew her husband Atticus Vestinus while he held the office of consul.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Caesar et Fimbria in penatibus domuum suarum trucidantur, Crassi pater et filius in mutuo alter alterius aspectu.
examples.translation: Caesar and Fimbria were butchered at the household shrines of their own homes. The elder and younger Crassus were slain in the sight of one another.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Res svb Caesare Avgvsto IIII, 3Populus Romanus Caesare et Pompeio trucidatis redisse in statum pristinum libertatis videbatur.
examples.translation: The State under Caesar Augustus 3. The Roman people, after the murders of Caesar and Pompeius, seemed to have returned to their former state of liberty;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: flashing, gleaming/glittering, resplendent; brilliant (white); bright, splendid
English: mid-day, noon.
Latin: medius dies, regio ubi sol stat medio die
Latin: pars caeli, qua meridies notatur; regio in meridiem spectans

examples.original: Nec non in meridiem verso agmine Libanum Syriae Damascumque transgressus per nemora illa odorata, per turis et balsami silvas Romana signa circumtulit.
examples.translation: Furthermore, turning his army southwards, he passed through the Lebanon in Syria and through Damascus, and bore the Roman standards through the famous scented groves and woods of frankincense and balm.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: with impunity; without punishment/retribution/restraint/consequences/harm

examples.original: Ludite, si sapitis, solas impune puellas: Hac minus est una fraude tuenda fides.
examples.translation: If you are wise, cheat women only, and avoid trouble; keep faith save for this one deceitfulness.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quod sua victoria tam insolenter gloriarentur quodque tam diu se impune iniurias tulisse admirarentur, eodem pertinere.
examples.translation: Their insolent boast of their own victory, their surprise that their outrages had gone on so long with impunity, pointed the same way;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: one who seizes by force, a robber, plunderer, abductor, ravisher

examples.original: Romanos terror per tota castra trepidos agit, et ad extrema ventum foret, ni legati rapto consulis corpore patefecissent una porta hostibus viam.
examples.translation: By that they burst forth, and escaping in a disordered column, fell in the way of the other, the victorious consul, where they were again cut to pieces, and dispersed in all directions.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Aquileiam progressae, proturbatis qui de Othone nuntiabant laceratisque vexillis nomen Vitellii praeferentibus, rapta postremo pecunia et inter se divisa, hostiliter egerant.
examples.translation: Their conduct filled them with fear, and then fear brought the reflection that acts might win them credit with Vespasian for which they would have to apologize to Vitellius.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a standing on end, standing erect, bristling.

examples.original: Niger inficit horror Terga maris, longo per multa volumina tractu Aestuat unda minax, flatusque incerta futuri Turbida testantur conceptos aequora ventos.
examples.translation: A shudder of darkness blackened the ridges of the sea; the angry deep boiled with a long swell, wave following wave;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: wide extent, breadth, width, amplitude, size, bulk (class., but only in prose).

examples.original: Monumentum illa amplitudine, illo opere, quamvis sartum tectum integrumque esset, tamen aliquid se inventurum in quo moliri praedarique posset arbitrabatur.
examples.translation: In so large and elaborate a building, even were it in sound and good repair, he calculated on finding some means of working a profitable job for himself.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: by turns, in turn, one after another, alternately

examples.original: Si autem invicem se laeserint, invicem sibi debita relaxare debebunt propter orationes vestras, quas utique quanto crebriores tanto sanctiores habere debetis.
examples.translation: But if they have caused mutual injury, they will require to grant mutual pardon because of your prayers, which from their frequency ought to be the holier.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a sailor, seaman, mariner
Latin: Qui in navibus navigandis adiuvat

examples.original: Intellexi non inmerito nautis terram timeri.
examples.translation: I understood that sailors have good reason to fear the land.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec piger ignis erat per stuppea vincula perque Manantes cera tabulas, et tempore eodem Transtraque nautarum summique arsere ceruchi.
examples.translation: He ordered brands steeped in resin to be hurled at the sails of the crowded ships;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: in close contest, hand to hand (with the sword, etc.), Gr.
English: abundant, copious, plentiful, large, much.

examples.original: Nec cruor emicuit solitus, sed volnere largo Diffusum rutilo dirum pro sanguine virus.
examples.translation: No red blood spouted forth from the gaping wound, but a slimy liquid, strange and dreadful, came out instead.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to make liquid, to melt, dissolve, liquefy.

examples.original: Iam ibi sunt, unde non est retro lapsus, sed hoc illis de se nondum liquet;
examples.translation: They have already arrived at a point from which there is no slipping back, but they are not yet aware of the fact;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Urbem populis victisque frequentem Gentibus et generis, coeat si turba, capacem Humani facilem venturo Caesare praedam Ignavae liquere manus.
examples.translation: Rome that was crowded with citizens and conquered peoples, Rome that could contain the human race assembled, was left by coward hands an easy prey to invading Caesar.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed hoc, quod liquet, firmandum et altius cotidiana meditatione figendum est;
examples.translation: This idea, however, clear though it is, must be strengthened and implanted more deeply by daily reflection;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a large hammer
Latin: secundum liber Novum Testamentum, compositum sedecim capitula

examples.original: Sevius Nicanor Marci libertus negabit;
examples.translation: Sevius Nicanor, the freedman of Marcus, may deny this;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Item Marcus Mettius repertus et ad eum reductus est.
examples.translation: Marcus Mettius also was discovered and brought back to Caesar.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Marco Fabio Buteone consule hostium classem iam in Africo mari apud Aegimurum in Italiam ultro navigantem cecidit.
examples.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Fabius Buteo they defeated the enemy’s fleet near Aegimurus in the African sea, while it was actually sailing against Italy.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: known, familiar
Latin: Cognitus, manifestus
Latin: Ventus austrinus, procellosus atque imbrifer

examples.original: Nos ex illa prima nota non sumus;
examples.translation: We ourselves are not of that first class, either;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Notum est totum carmen incisum in sepulcro.
examples.translation: But the entire epitaph is known because it is inscribed upon his tomb.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Pelopidas Thebanus, magis historicis quam vulgo notus.
examples.translation: Pelopidas, the Theban, is better known to historians than to the general public.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pelopidas

definitions: English: learned, taught
Latin: doctus < doceō
Latin: Doctrina imbutus

examples.original: Postquam docti prodierunt, boni desunt.
examples.translation: When savants have appeared, sages have become rare.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sunt tamen et doctae, rarissima turba, puellae;
examples.translation: Yet there are learned women too, a scanty number;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Docta, quid ad magicas, Erato, deverteris artes?
examples.translation: Why turnest thou, learned Erato, to magical arts?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: place before.
Latin: Ponere aliquid ante aliam rem

examples.original: Quam ob rem cave Catoni anteponas ne istum quidem ipsum, quem Apollo, ut ais, sapientissimum iudicavit;
examples.translation: Therefore, take care not to give the precedence over Cato even to that man, whom, as you say, Apollo adjudged the wisest of men;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Et hi quidem ita non sola virtute finem bonorum contineri putant, ut rebus tamen omnibus virtutem anteponant;
examples.translation: And these, though holding that the End of Goods is not limited to virtue alone, yet rate virtue higher than all other things;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Etsi ille domestico summo genere erat, tamen Macedones eum sibi aliquando anteponi indigne ferebant, neque tamen non patiebantur;
examples.translation: Although he was of the highest rank in his own country, yet the Macedonians were indignant that he was sometimes preferred to them;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: a watching, observing, observance (class.).
Latin: Informationis acquisitio ab fontibus primariis

examples.original: Nimis pauca et exigua de quibusdam minutis quaestiunculis edidit. Reliquit autem non mediocrem ”Silvam Observationum Sermonis Antiqui.”
examples.translation: He published a few slight works on divers minute points, and also left a good sized ”Grove of Observations on our Early Language.”
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Quomodo ista perplexa sunt, sic ex istis non singulares morbi nascuntur, sed inexplicabiles, diversi, multiformes, adversus quos et medicina armare se coepit multis generibus, multis observationibus.
examples.translation: And as the food itself is complicated, so the resulting diseases are complex, unaccountable, manifold, variegated; medicine has begun to campaign against them in many ways and by many rules of treatment.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to become very much frightened, to be greatly afraid of any thing, to fear greatly

examples.original: Semel ait se in vita pertimuisse, tum cum primum reus a me factus sit;
examples.translation: He says he was really frightened once in his life—on the day when I first issued the summons against him;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cuius ego ingenium ita laudo ut non pertimescam, ita probo ut me ab eo delectari facilius quam decipi putem posse.
examples.translation: I can admire him, and yet believe it possible that he will enchant me more easily than entrap me.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam miles, qui locum non tenuit, qui hostium impetum vimque pertimuit, potest idem postea et miles esse melior et vir bonus et civis utilis.
examples.translation: For a soldier who has deserted his post, or shown cowardice before the furious onset of the enemy, may still turn out a better soldier, an honest man, and a good citizen.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: as, just as; like; in same way

examples.original: Reddite igitur animas, quas truculenta vestra manus contorsit, et, sicuti a nobis vester Hercules redhibetur, sic etiam a vobis tantorum animae reddantur.
examples.translation: Restore then the souls that your ferocious hand has destroyed, and as we give back your Hercules, so do you restore these many souls.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: continuing two days, of two days; as

examples.original: Eo anno prodigia multa fuerunt, quorum averruncandorum causa supplicationes in biduum senatus decrevit;
examples.translation: In that year were many portents, to avert which the senate decreed supplications for two days.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: At Caesar biduum in his locis moratus, quod haec de Vercingetorige usu ventura opinione praeceperat, per causam supplementi equitatusque cogendi ab exercitu discedit;
examples.translation: Caesar, however, having anticipated that this would be the natural course of things for Vercingetorix, halted for two days in this locality;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Cum paucissimis servis, quos unum capere vehiculum potuit, sine ullis rebus, nisi quae corpore nostro continebantur, ego et Maximus meus biduum iam beatissimum agimus.
examples.translation: My friend Maximus and I have been spending a most happy period of two days, taking with us very few slaves—one carriage-load—and no paraphernalia except what we wore on our persons.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To send, carry, or convey across, over, or through; to send off, despatch, transmit from one place or person to another (syn.: transfero, traicio, traduco).
Latin: De loco ad locum mittere

examples.original: Sociis ego nostris mare per hos annos clausum fuisse dicam, cum exercitus vestri numquam a Brundisio nisi hieme summa transmiserint?
examples.translation: Need I mention that the sea during those wars was closed to our allies, when your own armies never made the crossing from Brundisium save in the depth of winter?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Is quibusdam piacularibus sacrificiis factis, quae deinde genti Horatiae tradita sunt, transmisso per viam tigillo capite adoperto velut sub iugum misit iuvenem.
examples.translation: And so, that the flagrant murder might yet be cleansed away, by some kind of expiatory rite, the father was commanded to make atonement for his son at the public cost.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to prop up, to keep upright by props, to stay, support (class.; syn.: sustento, sustineo, munio).

examples.original: Stupebam, ubi aliquid ex illis alio atque alio loco fulserat.
examples.translation: I used to be dazed when I caught some gleam of them here and there.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haud magis expertus discrimine Caesar in ullo est, Quam non e stabili tremulo sed culmine cuncta Despiceret staretque super titubantia fultus.
examples.translation: Or was it greed for greater rewards that made the soldiers repudiate their cause and their leader, and again put up for sale the swords already stained with guilt?
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Membraque vinxerunt tinctis ferrugine pannis, A male deserto quos rapuere rogo: Et, ne non fultum nuda tellure iaceret, Molle super silices inposuere caput.
examples.translation: They swathed his limbs in bands of dusky hue, snatched from a pyre abandoned as accursed; and lest it lie unpropped on the naked earth they set a flint-stone beneath his baby head.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: grave, earnest, serious, opp. to sportive, jocular

examples.original: Fortissimae rei inertissima adstruitur, severissimae parum seria, sanctissimae intemperans usque ad incesta.
examples.translation: What elements so inharmonious as these can be found united?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Virtutis enim beataeque vitae, quae duo maxime expetenda sunt, serius lumen apparet, multo etiam serius, ut plane qualia sint intellegantur.
examples.translation: The radiance of virtue and of happiness, the two things most to be desired, dawns upon us later, and far later still comes a full understanding of their nature.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a collection of people, an association, gathering, union, meeting, assembly, = coetus (class.).

examples.original: Hac oratione habita concilium dimisit.
examples.translation: With this speech he dissolved the convention.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Accedebat huc quod in concilio Aeduorum Dumnorix dixerat sibi a Caesare regnum civitatis deferri;
examples.translation: Moreover, in the council of the Aedui Dumnorix had said that Caesar meant to offer him the kingship of the state;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Consilia ad movenda bella in Volscorum Aequorumque conciliis et in Etruria ad fanum Voltumnae agitata.
examples.translation: Schemes for instigating war were discussed in the councils of the Volsci and Aequi, and in Etruria at the shrine of Voltumna.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: containing ten.
Latin: Qui decem partes comprehendit
Latin: Nummus argenteus Romanus qui ab origine decem asses valuit; deinde, 16 asses

examples.original: Ne in cellam quod imperatur aestiment: hoc quoque propter tuos ternos denarios nunc primum postulatur, sed genus ipsum postulandi non est novum.
examples.translation: They ask that governors shall not require fixed money payments instead of supplies demanded for their households. Here too is a request made now for the first time, due to your 3-denarius exactiona;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Vectigal quoque eis Campanus populus iussus pendere in singulos quotannis—fuere autem mille et sexcenti—denarios a.u.c. 415nummos quadringenos quinquagenos.
examples.translation: Moreover, the 340Campanian people were commanded to pay them each a yearly stipend—there were sixteen hundred of them—amounting to four hundred and fifty denarii.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: an implement of any kind, a utensil, tool, instrument (class.).
Latin: res quae auxilio est alias res faciendo
Latin: documentum, scriptum officiale (saeculo XVII)

examples.original: Quod sit hoc instrumentum, scire desideras?
examples.translation: Do you wish to know what this weapon of defence is?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec erit ultimum vitae instrumentum et, ut ita dicam, additamentum?
examples.translation: Is philosophy to be the last requisite in life,—a sort of supplement?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Testudinum putamina secare in laminas lectosque et repositoria iis vestire Carvilius Pollio instituit, prodigi et sagacis ad luxuriae instrumenta ingenii.
examples.translation: Carvilius Pollio, a man of prodigal habits and ingenious in inventing the refinements of luxury, was the first to cut the shell of the tortoise into laminæ, and to veneer beds and cabinets with it.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: freedom from care, unconcern, composure.
Latin: Status seu qualitas rei quae securus est

examples.original: Quae est enim ista securitas?
examples.translation: For of what value is their vaunted ”freedom from care”?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Securitatis magna portio est nihil inique facere.
examples.translation: The most important contribution to peace of mind is never to do wrong.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid est turpius quam in ipso limine securitatis esse sollicitum?
examples.translation: But what is baser than to fret at the very threshold of peace?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or belonging to a tribune, tribunitial

examples.original: Tribunicia primum comitia sunt habita.
examples.translation: The last-named held the election for quaestors.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Neque enim ullam aliam ob causam populus Romanus tribuniciam potestatem tanto studio requisivit;
examples.translation: We have been groaning, and that for many years, under a heavy load of infamy.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quod si consulatus tanta dulcedo sit, iam nunc ita in animum inducant consulatum captum et oppressum ab tribunicia potestate esse;
examples.translation: But if the consulship was so alluring to them, let them recognize at once that it had been fettered and enslaved by the might of the tribunes;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To alter wholly, change entirely (class.; most freq. in Cic.).
Latin: In aliam formam vel faciem vertere
Latin: Aliud pro alio substituere

examples.original: In his igitur partibus duabus nihil erat quod Zeno commutare gestiret;
examples.translation: In these two departments then, there was nothing that Zeno need have desired to alter;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a falling (acc. to cado, I. A. and C.).
Latin: dēscēnsus
Latin: forma inflecta vocabuli

examples.original: Totum autem id externum est, et quod externum, id in casu est.
examples.translation: But all the apparatus of pleasure is external, and what is external must depend on chance.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ad utrosque casus aptus est: bonorum rector est, malorum victor.
examples.translation: He is ready for either outcome: if it brings goods, he controls them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fabium illis Valentem, captivum et casibus dubiis reservatum, praegravem fuisse, nedum Primus ac Fuscus et specimen partium Mucianus ullam in Vitellium nisi occidendi licentiam habeant.
examples.translation: Will Primus and Fuscus or that leading representative of their party, Mucianus, have any liberty in dealing with you except the liberty of killing? Caesar did not leave Pompey unharmed or Augustus Antony.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to lift out or

examples.original: Extollunt quidem et dilatant, sed sine tumore.
examples.translation: They do, indeed, uplift and broaden the spirit, but without puffing it up.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Animum virilem et Christianum nec debent, si accedunt, extollere nec debent frangere, si recedunt.
examples.translation: The manly Christian spirit ought neither to be elated by their accession nor depressed by their departure.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Ibi Vespasiani virtutem virisque partium extollit: transfugisse classem, in arto commeatum, adversas Gallias Hispaniasque, nihil in urbe fidum;
examples.translation: There he spoke in high terms of Vespasian’s courage and the strength of his party.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to write in full or at length, to write out, to write without abbreviations (cf.: conscribo, compono): verbo non perscripto, not being written in full, Tiro Tullius ap.
English: wheel-shaped, i. e. round, circular, spherical, rotund (very freq. and class.; cf. teres).

examples.original: Quid lapideas moles in rotundum ac leve formatas, quibus porticus et capacia populorum tecta suscipimus?
examples.translation: Or the rounded and polished masses of stone by means of which we erect colonnades and buildings roomy enough for nations?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Si rotundam illis qualem deo dederint, quaeram, an et avaritia et luxuria et dementia aeque rotundae sint.
examples.translation: If they are given a round shape, like that of a god, I shall ask whether greed and luxury and madness are equally round.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to press back, keep back; to check, curb, restrain (class., partic. in the trop. sense; cf.: repello, refuto).

examples.original: Caesar His rebus comparatis, represso iam Lucterio et remoto, quod intrare intra praesidia periculosum putabat, in Helvios proficiscitur.
examples.translation: By these measures of security Lucterius was checked and set back, for he deemed it dangerous to penetrate the line of garrisons;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Non voluptates illa temperavit, non cupiditates refrenavit, non iras repressit, non indomitos amoris impetus fregit, nulla denique animo mala eduxit.
examples.translation: No restraint upon pleasure, no bridling of desire, no checking of bad temper, no crushing of the wild assaults of passion, no opportunity to rid the soul of evil.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Turbati ibi Vitellianorum auxilia, et ceteris Cremonam fugientibus caesi qui restiterant: sed repressus vincentium impetus ne novis subsidiis firmati hostes fortunam proelii mutarent.
examples.translation: This had thrown the auxiliaries of Vitellius into confusion and, while most fled to Cremona, those who resisted were cut down.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: sweetness, pleasantness, agreeableness (class. and freq.).

examples.original: Pronuntiabat autem cum suavitate et lenociniis miris.
examples.translation: His own delivery, however, was sweet and wonderfully effective.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

definitions: English: moisten, bathe with or in any liquid (class.; cf.: aspergo, irroro, imbuo).

examples.original: Membraque vinxerunt tinctis ferrugine pannis, A male deserto quos rapuere rogo: Et, ne non fultum nuda tellure iaceret, Molle super silices inposuere caput.
examples.translation: They swathed his limbs in bands of dusky hue, snatched from a pyre abandoned as accursed; and lest it lie unpropped on the naked earth they set a flint-stone beneath his baby head.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Di tibi non mortem, quae cunctis poena paratur, Sed sensum post fata tuae dent, Crastine, morti, Cuius torta manu commisit lancea bellum Primaque Thessaliam Romano sanguine tinxit.
examples.translation: Heaven punish Crastinus! and not with death alone, for that is a punishment in store for all mankind alike;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: an evil deed, misdeed, wickedness, offence, crime.
English: that excites laughter.
Latin: Risum movens, iocosus, qui ridere facit
Latin: Qui in rebus turpibus ridetur

examples.original: Turpis et ridicula res est elementarius senex; iuveni parandum, seni utendum est.
examples.translation: An old man learning his A B C is a disgraceful and absurd object;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iam hoc ridiculum est: si de hereditate ambigetur, et tabulae testamenti obsignatae non minus multis signis quam e lege oportet ad me proferentur, secundum tabulas testamenti potissimum possessionem dabo.
examples.translation: That point you nowhere deal with; nor does your edict provide for anything else at all besides the case for which you got paid.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: moist, to drip or flow with any thing (class.).
English: a loud noise, a cry, clamor, outcry (class.).

examples.original: Ubi crudescere seditio et a conviciis ac probris ad tela et manus transibant, inici catenas Flaviano iubet.
examples.translation: But the troops saw through the ruse, thrust aside those who guarded the tribunal, and prepared to use extreme violence.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Quanta autem dementia est isdem modo delectari, modo offendi, et rem ab amico dictam maledictum vocare, a servulo ioculare convicium!
examples.translation: But what madness it is at one time to be amused, at another to be affronted, by the same things, and to call something, if spoken by a friend, a slander;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to add to by mingling

examples.original: Admiscenda tamen venus est secura timori, Ne tanti noctes non putet esse tuas.
examples.translation: Yet with fear must be mingled secure enjoyment, lest he think your nights are not worth while.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a noble youth employed in the sacrifices of the Flamen Dialis, and then, gen., in religious offices, Paul. ex

examples.original: Eo vim Camilli ab Antio fortuna avertit.
examples.translation: To this quarter Fortune diverted the energies of Camillus, away from Antium.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cum Graecis a Camillo nulla memorabilis gesta res;
examples.translation: With the Greeks, Camillus fought no memorable action;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Secuti alium ducem sequimini nunc Camillum et quod ductu meo soletis vincite.
examples.translation: You have followed another leader: follow now Camillus, and, as your habit is when I am leading, conquer.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To charge with a load, to load, burden, weigh down, oppress
Latin: pondere premere
Latin: onerare

examples.original: Illud, quod paupertatem nobis gravem fecerat, et divitias graves fecit.
examples.translation: That which had made poverty a burden to us, has made riches also a burden.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ego vero non gravarer, si mihi ipse confiderem, nam et praeclara res est et sumus, ut dixit Fannius, otiosi.
examples.translation: I certainly should raise no objection if I felt confidence in myself, for the subject is a noble one, and we are, as Fannius said, free from public business.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Non caeli nox illa fuit: latet obsitus aer Infernae pallore domus nimbisque gravatus Deprimitur, fluctusque in nubibus accipit imbrem.
examples.translation: The darkness was not the common darkness of night: the heavens were hidden and veiled with the dimness of the infernal regions, and weighed down by clouds;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to daub, besmear, anoint, to spread or rub over.

examples.original: Lite fugent nuptaeque viros nuptasque mariti, Inque vicem credant res sibi semper agi;
examples.translation: With quarrels let wives pursue husbands and husbands wives, and deem that they are ever at issue with each other;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Evolvam busto iam numen gentibus Isim Et tectum lino spargam per volgus Osirim, Suppositisque deis uram caput.
examples.translation: And the land I shall punish too; I shall leave their fields with none to till them;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: In his sic illi opus est alieno consilio quomodo medico, quomodo gubernatori, quomodo advocato et litis ordinatori.
examples.translation: He needs outside advice on such matters, as does the physician, the pilot, the attorney, or the pleader of cases.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: resin, rosin, Auct. B. Hisp. 33
English: veteran (in technical lang.)

examples.original: Bellvm Pervsinvm IIII, 5Alterum bellum concitavit agrorum divisio, quod Caesar veteranis patris pretium militiae persolvebat.
examples.translation: The War round Perusia 5. The distribution of lands to the soldiers was the cause of another war;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed primus dies impetu magis quam veterani exercitus artibus transactus: aperti incautique muros subiere, cibo vinoque praegraves.
examples.translation: The first day was spent in a furious onslaught rather than in skilful attacks appropriate to a veteran army.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a newly-levied soldier, a young soldier, recruit.
Latin: inceptor

examples.original: Nolebat in agendo discere tametsi non provinciae rudis erat et tiro, sed Siciliae paratus ad praedam meditatusque venire cupiebat.
examples.translation: He was not content to discover these methods on the spot, though he was no raw new-comer to the work of government;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In castris tiro etiam tum propter nimiam vini aviditatem pro Tiberio ”Biberius,” pro Claudio ”Caldius,” pro Nerone ”Mero” vocabatur.
examples.translation: Even at the outset of his military career his excessive love of wine gave him the name of Biberius, instead of Tiberius, Caldius for Claudius, and Mero for Nero.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a taking vengeance, avenging, revenge

examples.original: Ergo Fulvio Nobiliori mandata ultio est.
examples.translation: And so the task of vengeance was committed to Fulvius Nobilior.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Fruetur Vitellius fratre, coniuge, liberis: mihi non ultione neque solaciis opus est.
examples.translation: Vitellius shall enjoy his brother, his wife, and his children; I require neither vengeance nor solace.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to cut the throat, to kill, slay, murder (class.).

examples.original: Nec derat robur in enses Ire duci iuguloque pati vel pectore letum;
examples.translation: He lacked not the courage to confront the swords and offer throat or breast to the fatal blow;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Iulianus ad L. Vitellium perductus et verberibus foedatus in ore eius iugulatur.
examples.translation: Julianus was taken before Lucius Vitellius, flogged, and slain before his eyes.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Itaque cum Oppianicum iam perditum et duobus iugulatum praeiudiciis videret, promissis suis eum excitavit abiectum et simul saluti desperare vetuit.
examples.translation: And so, seeing Oppianicus already lost and with two previous verdicts like millstones round his neck,c he raised his drooping spirits, bidding him not despair of success.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a cultivator of land, in the widest sense, a husbandman, agriculturist (including even the vine-dresser, gardener; also one who takes pleasure in agriculture, etc.)
Latin: Qui agros colit, cultor agri
Latin: Qui agros colit

examples.original: Sed venio ad agricolas, ne a me ipso recedam.
examples.translation: But, lest I wander from my subject, I return to the farmers.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nec minimam partem ex agris is maeror in urbem confluxit, languens quem contulit agricolarum copia conveniens ex omni morbida parte.
examples.translation: And in no small degree this affliction flowed from the country into the city, for the fainting crowd people of countrymen brought it, gathering from all quarters with disease.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: use, practice, experience
Latin: Actio utendi
Latin: Consuetudo, mos

examples.original: Haec si est qua nos usi sumus, te iudice vincamus necesse est.
examples.translation: But if it be this same procedure which we have employed, your own judgement gives us the verdict.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cuius avari modum ignorant, etiam non avari usum. ”Tolle,” inquit, ”errores;
examples.translation: Then comes the reply: ”Do away with error, and your precepts become unnecessary.” That is wrong;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quis sapientissimos ac fortissimos viros non miretur ad ultimum non suis manibus usos?
examples.translation: Who can but wonder that these wise and brave men did not die by their own hands?
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a judging, judgment, opinion, supposition

examples.original: Sese tamen et amore fraterno et existimatione vulgi commoveri.
examples.translation: For all that, I feel the force of brotherly love and public opinion.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Itaque semper ii diligentissime laboriosissimeque accusarunt qui se ipsos in discrimen existimationis venire arbitrati sunt.
examples.translation: That is why the most energetic and painstaking prosecutors have always been men who feel that their own reputations are at stake.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque nunc quem ad modum audiar sentio, non modo ab eis, quorum iudicium ac potestas est, sed etiam ab illis, quorum tantum est existimatio.
examples.translation: And so I am conscious how close is the attention now not only of those to whom belongs the prerogative of judgement, but of those, too, who can only form an opinion on the case.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to call upon, invoke (cf. imploro), esp. as a witness or for aid.

examples.original: Is in maestitiam compositus et fidem suorum quondam militum invocans, ut eum in Syria aut Aegypto sisterent orabat.
examples.translation: The pretender, assuming a look of sorrow and calling on the soldiers, once his own, for protection, begged them to land him in Syria or Egypt.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: destructive, ruinous, baleful, pernicious

examples.original: Eam rem consules rati, ut erat, perniciosam ad patres deferunt, sed delatam consulere ordine non licuit;
examples.translation: This seemed to the consuls, as indeed it was, a mischievous practice.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quamquam ista assentatio, quamvis perniciosa sit, nocere tamen nemini potest nisi ei, qui eam recipit atque ea delectatur.
examples.translation: And yet this flattery of which I spoke, however deadly it may be, can harm no one except him who receives and delights in it.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nobis itaque cordi est neque Christianam amittere mansuetudinem neque perniciosum ceteris imitationis exemplum in illa civitate relinquere.
examples.translation: Therefore is it our dear desire neither to put away Christian meekness nor to leave your country as a baleful example for others to follow.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: Of or belonging to the common people or commonalty, plebeian (opp. to patricius)

examples.original: Et adhuc plebeias fistulas loquor;
examples.translation: I have so far been speaking of the ordinary bathing-establishments;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ap. Claudium virginis plebeiae stuprandae libido cepit.
examples.translation: Appius Claudius was seized with the desire to debauch a certain maiden belonging to the plebs.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nos citius caruerimus patriciis magistratibus quam illi plebeiis.
examples.translation: We will sooner dispense with patrician magistrates than they with plebeian.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: ruddy
Latin: Color sanguinis

examples.original: Tunc neque marmoreo pendebant vela theatro, Nec fuerant liquido pulpita rubra croco;
examples.translation: No awnings then hung o’er a marble theatre, nor was the platform ruddy with crocus-spray;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: Leisure given to learning, a learned conversation or debate, a disputation, lecture, dissertation, etc.

examples.original: Scrutabitur scholas nostras et obiciet philosophis congiaria, amicas, gulam.
examples.translation: He will forestall every word which I am about to utter.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Scholam eius claros quoque viros frequentasse aiunt, in iis M. Ciceronem, etiam cum praetura fungeretur.
examples.translation: They say also that distinguished men attended his school, including Cicero even while he was praetor.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Quare ab Augusto quoque nepotibus eius praeceptor electus, transiit in Palatium cum tota schola, verum ut ne quem amplius posthac discipulum reciperet;
examples.translation: He was therefore chosen by Augustus as the tutor of his grandsons and he moved to the Palace with his whole school, but with the understanding that he should admit no more pupils.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: to wash to pieces, wash away; to dissolve, dilute, cause to melt away; to wash, drench (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Hoc ego si sic agerem, tamquam mihi crimen esset diluendum, haec pluribus verbis dicerem, per quae nunc paucis percurrit oratio mea.
examples.translation: If I were dealing with the charge as if I really had to disprove it, I should do so at length; whereas I am now dismissing it with a brief notice.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of an evil nature or disposition, ill-disposed, wicked, mischievous, malicious, spiteful, envious, malignant, malign

examples.original: Sed nihil facere hoc loco diligentia potest nisi te malignum.
examples.translation: In this case, however, caution can effect nothing but to make you ungenerous.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: gently/mildly/lightly/slightly; w/gentle movement/incline; smoothly

examples.original: Duxit via in editum leniter collem.
examples.translation: Their road led up a gentle acclivity.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Noli ergo atrocius vindicare quod lenius invenisti. Inquirendi quam puniendi neces-sitas maior est;
examples.translation: Do not then punish with harsher sentence what you found out by gentler methods.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Qui tamen lenius sunt profecto tractandi; quid enim eos terreri opus est, quos satis territos ipsa taciturnitas monstrat?
examples.translation: These, however, surely call for milder treatment: what need is there to terrify them, when their very silence shows that they are terrified enough?
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to dedicate, devote something as sacred to a deity (class., esp. in prose).

examples.original: Lex Papiria vetat aedes iniussu plebis consecrari.
examples.translation: The law of Papirius forbids the consecration of a building without a mandate from the people.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ager Tarquiniorum, qui inter urbem ac Tiberim fuit, consecratus Marti Martius deinde campus fuit.
examples.translation: The land of the Tarquinii, lying between the City and the Tiber, was consecrated to Mars and became the Campus Martius.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a being known, celebrity, note, fame.

examples.original: Ii propter notitiam sunt intromissi.
examples.translation: The youths, since they were acquaintances, were admitted;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

examples.original: Quanta notitia antiquitatis, scientia iuris auguri!
examples.translation: What a knowledge of ancient history! What skill in augural law!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Fidenatium plurimi locorum notitia effugere in montes.
examples.translation: Large numbers of the Fidenates escaped, thanks to their knowledge of the ground, into the mountains.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the name of a Roman gens

examples.original: Fecit heredem M. Octavium Ligurem;
examples.translation: He left his property to Marcus Octavius Ligus;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum Octavio collega Cinna dissedit: utrique horum secunda fortuna regnum est largita, adversa mortem.
examples.translation: Cinna fell out with his colleague Octavius; upon each of these prosperity bestowed a tyrant’s power, adversity death.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam in provincias quoque grammatica penetraverat, ac nonnulli de notissimis doctoribus peregre docuerunt, maxime in Gallia Togata; inter quos Octavius Teucer et Sescenius Iaccus et Oppius Chares;
examples.translation: In fact, Grammar even made its way into the provinces, and some of the most famous teachers gave instruction abroad, especially in Gallia Togata, including Octavius Teucer, Sescenius Iaccus and Oppius Chares;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: very small, little, petty, slight, (class.)

examples.original: Navis, quae in flumine magna est, in mari parvula est.
examples.translation: A ship which looms large in the river seems tiny when on the ocean.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vita omnis in venationibus atque in studiis rei militaris consistit: ab parvulis labori ac duritiae student.
examples.translation: Their whole life is composed of hunting expeditions and military pursuits; from early boyhood they are zealous for toil and hardship.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Longius prosequi veritus, quod silvae paludesque intercedebant neque etiam parvulo detrimento illorum locum relinqui videbat, omnibus suis incolumibus copiis eodem die ad Ciceronem pervenit.
examples.translation: He feared to pursue very far, because there were woods and marshes in the way, and, as he saw, there was no chance now of doing even slight damage to the enemy;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to call forth, call out.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Atqui pericula contemnit et provocat.
examples.translation: And yet bravery despises and challenges danger.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ille cum a lictoribus iam traheretur, provocavit;
examples.translation: The lictors were already dragging the man away, when he appealed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Respondebo tibi nunc, Laterensis, minus fortasse vehementer, quam abs te sum provocatus: sed profecto nec considerate minus, nec minus amice.
examples.translation: I now proceed to reply to you, Laterensis, using less vehemence, perhaps, than you prompt me to use, but in a spirit, I dare avow, of no less consideration and friendship.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Singly, to effect

examples.original: Promovent et Samnites signa; insequitur acies ornata armata-que, ut hostium quoque magnificum spectaculum esset.
examples.translation: The Samnites, too, advanced their standards, which were followed by the battle-line in gorgeous armour—a splendid spectacle, though composed of enemies.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ut et levi momento nec ambigue est victus, ita brevitate ipsa loci facili-que receptu in tam propinqua castra haud aegre militem a multa caede est tutatus;
examples.translation: He was easily and decisively defeated; yet, because his camp was so near and so readily accessible, he was able without great difficulty to save his men from heavy losses;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: the Latin name for Odysseus, Engl.

examples.original: Penelopen absens sollers torquebat Ulixes;
examples.translation: In the absence of crafty Ulysses was Penelope racked;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Huic memoria tam mala erat, ut illi nomen modo Vlixis excideret, modo Achillis, modo Priami, quos tam bene quam paedagogos nostros novimus.
examples.translation: His memory was so faulty that he would sometimes forget the name of Ulysses, or Achilles, or Priam,—names which we know as well as we know those of our own attendants.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vlixes ad Ithacae suae saxa sic properat, quemadmodum Agamemnon ad Mycenarum nobiles muros.
examples.translation: Ulysses hastens back to the rocks of his Ithaca as eagerly as Agamemnon speeds to the kingly walls of Mycenae.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: emptiness, nothingness, nullity, want of reality: nulla in caelo nec fortuna, nec temeritas, nec erratio, nec vanitas inest
Latin: Status vanus; absentia substantiae; vacuum; praesertim veritatis
Latin: Vanitas rationis vel causae; futtilitas, frivolitas

examples.original: Flavium Sabinum inermem neque fugam coeptantem circumsistunt, et Quintium Atticum consulem, umbra honoris et suamet vanitate monstratum, quod edicta in populum pro Vespasiano magnifica, probrosa adversus Vitellium iecerat.
examples.translation: Flavius Sabinus, who was unarmed and did not attempt to flee, the Vitellians surrounded; they likewise took Quintus Atticus, the consul.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a storeroom, chamber.

examples.original: Ne in cellam quod imperatur aestiment: hoc quoque propter tuos ternos denarios nunc primum postulatur, sed genus ipsum postulandi non est novum.
examples.translation: They ask that governors shall not require fixed money payments instead of supplies demanded for their households. Here too is a request made now for the first time, due to your 3-denarius exactiona;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Semper enim boni assiduique domini referta cella vinaria, olearia, etiam penaria est, villaque tota locuples est, abundat porco haedo agno gallina, lacte caseo melle.
examples.translation: For the provident and industrious proprietor always has his store-room and cellars well filled with oil and wine and provisions;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to strike, beat, esp. with a noise.
English: to speak between, i. e. to interpose by speaking.

examples.original: Interdictum ne capite damnatos propinqui lugerent.
examples.translation: The relatives of the victims were forbidden to mourn for them.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ad duas dissimiles res duo diiuncta interdicta sunt.
examples.translation: To meet the two different cases, two separate injunctions have been framed.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Interdicis mihi inspectione rerum naturae, a toto abductum redigis in partem?
examples.translation: He is so trained that he neither loves nor hates life;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a tiger, tigress.
Latin: Panthera tigris, maxima exstans species felidae, animal formose virgatum
English: rest, quiet.

examples.original: Ne tribunal quidem satis quietum erat;
examples.translation: Not even the tribunal itself was quiet;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cum haec agerentur, iam consul via Labicana ad fanum Quietis erat.
examples.translation: Meanwhile the consul had already reached the shrine of Quies on the Labican road.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Multi in utroque exercitu sicut modesti quietique ita mali et strenui.
examples.translation: There were many in both armies obedient and law-abiding, as well as many unprincipled and energetic.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to share, part; to divide, distribute
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; ĭi or īvi, ītum, 4; partītus

examples.original: Superfluente multitudine curam dilectus in consules partitur;
examples.translation: On the senators he imposed a contribution of slaves and cash.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nulli subigebant arva coloni, Ne signare quidem aut partiri limite campum Fas erat;
examples.translation: No ploughman tilled the soil, nor was it right To portion off or bound one’s property.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sic infantibus quoque animalibusque principalis partis suae sensus est non satis dilucidus nec expressus.
examples.translation: Thus even children and animals have a consciousness of their primary element, but it is not very clearly outlined or portrayed.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the gall-bladder, gall, bile (cf. bilis)
English: deep yellow, reddish yellow, gold-colored, tawny
Latin: colorem habens, qui in leonino pilo esse solet ex viridi et rufo mixtum
Latin: (Poet.) colorem habens, qui in leonino pilo esse solet ex viridi et rufo mixtum. Color inter gilvum et rubrum
English: a being new, newness, novelty.

examples.original: Utrisque frustra fuit, Vitellianis inpune, per tantam hominum multitudinem mutua ignorantia fallentibus: Othoniani novitate vultus, omnibus in vicem gnaris, prodebantur.
examples.translation: Neither accomplished anything, but the agents of Vitellius got off safely, since amid the great multitude they neither knew people nor were themselves known;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: in the same manner, just as, quite as, equally; in like manner, just so (class.; cf. proinde, with which it is frequently confounded in MSS. and edd.).

examples.original: Perinde speciosa mors earum fuit quam pugna.
examples.translation: Their death was as honourable as their resistance;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Ea legatione Papirius audita perinde ac motus dictis eorum cum collega se communicaturum respondit;
examples.translation: After listening to these envoys, Papirius as though moved by what they said, replied that he would consult his colleague.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Perinde legati provinciaeque cunctabantur, Hordeonius Flaccus suspectis iam Batavis anxius proprio bello, Vettius Bolanus numquam satis quieta Britannia, et uterque ambigui.
examples.translation: The governors and the provinces moved as slowly as he. Hordeonius Rufus already suspected the Batavians and was disturbed by the possibility of having a war of his own ;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: of great value, valuable, precious.

examples.original: Quo tibi, Pasiphaë, pretiosas sumere vestes?
examples.translation: Pasiphaë, to wear thy purple gowns?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Non minor, inquit, voluptas percipitur ex vilissimis rebus quam ex pretiosissimis.
examples.translation: As much pleasure, he says, is derived from the cheapest things as from the most costly.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make or offer a sacrifice, to sacrifice (freq. and class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

definitions: English: to run forth, rush forwards.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n.; cŭcurri and curri, cursum, 3

examples.original: Calones in proximum tumulum procurrunt.
examples.translation: The camp-followers dashed forward to the nearest rise.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Hoc ut scias ita esse, ad omne pulchrum vir bonus sine ulla cunctatione procurret;
examples.translation: This can be proved to you by the fact that the good man will hasten unhesitatingly to any noble deed;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ne procurri quidem ab acie velim, sed obnixos vos stabili gradu impetum hostium excipere.
examples.translation: I would have none run out from the line, but all stand firmly planted and receive the onset of our enemies.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: in that very place, on the spot, there.
English: A trying, proving; a trial, inspection, examination (class.)

examples.original: Si probationes necessariae sunt, et decreta, quae veritatem argumentis colligunt.
examples.translation: If proofs are necessary, so are doctrines; for doctrines deduce the truth by reasoning.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: containing five (mostly post-Aug.)
English: to go apart, go away

examples.original: Secessi non tantum ab hominibus, sed a rebus, et inprimis a meis rebus;
examples.translation: I have withdrawn not only from men, but from affairs, especially from my own affairs;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sunt qui tradant, ob infamiam quandam eum in Sardiniam secessisse ibique diem obisse.
examples.translation: Some write that because of some disgrace he retired to Sardinia and there died.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Mentis valitudinem et ipse senserat ac subinde de secessu deque purgando cerebro cogitavit.
examples.translation: He himself realised his mental infirmity, and thought at times of going into retirement and clearing his brain.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: carefulness, attentiveness, earnestness, diligence (freq. and class.; cf.: labor, aerumna, opera, industria, assiduitas, sedulitas, studium, cura).

examples.original: Plato ipse ad senectutem se diligentia protulit.
examples.translation: Plato himself, by taking pains, advanced to old age.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cui ille: ”Tu quidem macte virtute diligentiaque esto!
examples.translation: The consul replied: ”For yourself, I commend your conduct and your diligence;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Id ne accidat, positum in eius diligentia atque auctoritate.
examples.translation: The prevention of that depended upon Caesar’s energy and authority.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a kindling, setting on fire, conflagration.
English: that is at hand, that serves, ministers
English: by weight, in weight.
English: frightful, dreadful, terrible (class.; syn.: dirus, horribilis, torvus).

examples.original: Mars pater, insano Veneris turbatus amore, De duce terribili factus amator erat.
examples.translation: Father Mars, plagued by frenzied love of Venus, from a terrible captain became a lover.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Auxerat id maxime animos quod ignari loco iniquo, non hosti cessum, velut fugientes ac territos terribiles ipsi secuti fuerant.
examples.translation: Their encouragement was due chiefly to ignorance that their enemies had retreated from an awkward position, and not from them;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec villarum atque vicorum vastatione contenti Nolam atque Nuceriam, Thurios atque Metapontum terribili strage populantur.
examples.translation: Not content with the plundering of country houses and villages, they laid waste Nola, Nuceria, Thurii and Metapontum with terrible destruction.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to trust, confide, put confidence in, rely upon a person or thing

examples.original: Ab hoc discede iudicio; non pietas constabit, non fides.
examples.translation: Dissent from this judgment, and duty and loyalty will not abide.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Animus esse debet alacer et fidens et super omnia erectus.
examples.translation: The very soul must be happy and confident, lifted above every circumstance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: An, quod ad diem non venerunt, de eorum fide constantiaque dubitatis?
examples.translation: Or do you doubt their faithfulness, their resolution, because they are not arrived to the day?
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a breaking, breaking to pieces.

examples.original: Laetus fragor aethera pulsat Victorum;
examples.translation: A shout from his conquerors made the welkin ring;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Quantum aquarum per gradus cum fragore labentium!
examples.translation: And what masses of water that fall crashing from level to level!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac primi quidem impetus turbo inter Padum atque Ticinum valido statim fragore detonuit.
examples.translation: The tempest of the first assault crashed with a mighty roar between the Padus and the Ticinus.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: impious, heinous, execrable, abominable

examples.original: Inminet armorum rabies, ferrique potestas Confundet ius omne manu, scelerique nefando Nomen erit virtus, multosque exibit in annos Hic furor.
examples.translation: The madness of war is upon us, when the power of the sword shall violently upset all legality, and atrocious crime shall be called heroism.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: A bath, a place for bathing

examples.original: Non multum mihi ad balneum superest.
examples.translation: I have very little energy left for bathing.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to steer or pilot a ship (class.).

examples.original: Hoc enim tale est, quale si peritus gubernator etiam formosus est.
examples.translation: For the case is no different from that of a skilled pilot who is also handsome.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Duas personas habet gubernator: alteram communem cum omnibus, qui eandem conscenderunt navem: ipse quoque vector est;
examples.translation: A pilot has a double rôle: one he shares with all his fellow-passengers, for he also is a passenger;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a chief, noble; plur., the leading men, chiefs, nobles, princes (class.; syn.: primores, optimates, primi): scindunt proceres Pergamum, the Grecian chiefs, princes, *

examples.original: Recipit extemplo animum pedestris acies, postquam iuventutis proceres aequato genere pugnae secum partem periculi sustinentes vidit.
examples.translation: It restored at once the courage of the foot to see the young nobles on even terms with themselves and sharing in the danger.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A discovering, betraying; a discovery, betrayal, treason, treachery (class.)

examples.original: Et sit in infida proditione fides.
examples.translation: What is easily given ill fosters an enduring love;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sed ubi totis castris in fama proditio, recurrens in principia miles praescriptum Vespasiani nomen, proiectas Vitellii effigies aspexit, vastum primo silentium, mox cuncta simul erumpunt.
examples.translation: But when the news of the treason spread through the whole camp, the soldiers ran to headquarters, where they saw Vespasian’s name put up on the standards and the statues of Vitellius overthrown;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ita duplici proditione et praesidium Samnitium insessis circa viam silvestribus locis necopinato oppressum est, et ab urbe plena hostium clamor sublatus;
examples.translation: Thus, in one crowded hour, the Samnites were slain and the Satricans captured, and all things brought under the power of the consul;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the dignity or office of a prœtor, the prœtorship (class.)

examples.original: Libri VII Periocha Libri VII Periocha Duo novi magistratus adiecti sunt, praetura et curulis aedilitas.
examples.translation: Summary of Book VII Summary of Book VII Two new magistracies were added, the praetorship and the curule aedileship.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Omnia erant Metelli eius modi ut non tam suam praeturam gerere quam istius praeturam retexere videretur.
examples.translation: All his actions were such that he seemed less to be doing his own work as praetor than undoing the work of his predecessor.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ab hoc sunt imperatoris Galbae avus ac pater: avus clarior studiis quam dignitate—non enim egressus praeturae gradum—multiplicem nec incuriosam historiam edidit;
examples.translation: The former, who was more eminent for his learning than for his rank—for he did not advance beyond the grade of praetor—published a voluminous and painstaking history.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: juger of land, measuring 28,800 square feet, or 240 feet in length by 120 in breadth (whereas the English acre measures 43,560 square feet)

examples.original: Taurus paucissimorum iugerum pascuo impletur;
examples.translation: The bull is filled when he feeds over a few acres;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a wet-nurse, nurse.
Latin: Quae lac praebet, nutrit, educat
Latin: nūtrī|x, -cis fem

examples.original: Et soror et mater valeant et conscia nutrix, Et quisquis dominae pars erit ulla tuae.
examples.translation: Bid farewell to mother and sister, and to the nurse her confidant, and to whoever will be any part of your mistress.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a machine, i. e. any artificial contrivance for performing work, an engine, fabric, frame, scaffolding, staging, easel, warlike engine, military machine, etc.
English: good-will, benevolence, kindness

examples.original: Neque id magis benevolentia factum est quam prudentia.
examples.translation: And that was due less to good-will than to discretion.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timoleon

examples.original: Nihil est enim remuneratione benevolentiae, nihil vicissitudine studiorum officiorumque iucundius. Quid?
examples.translation: For nothing gives more pleasure than the return of goodwill and the interchange of zealous service.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Et tamen tantis vectigalibus ad liberalitatem utens, etiam sine hac Pyladea amicitia multorum te benevolentia praeclare tuebere et munies.
examples.translation: And in any case, with so large an income to give away, you can dispense with the romantic sort of friendship that we have in mind;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a priest of one particular deity

examples.original: Quid M. Plaetori et C. Flamini inter sicarios?
examples.translation: What of the Assassination Court of M. Plaetorius and G. Flaminius?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Flaminius censor viam Flaminiam muniit et circum Flaminium exstruxit.
examples.translation: The censor Gaius Flaminius built the Flaminian Way and the Flaminian Circus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a nodding, a nod.

examples.original: Quorum non in sententia solum, sed etiam in nutu residebat auctoritas.
examples.translation: These men had power, not only in their speech, but in their very nod.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: notwithstanding that, although, though (class. and freq.).
Latin: Etiamsi, etsi, cum

examples.original: Nolebat in agendo discere tametsi non provinciae rudis erat et tiro, sed Siciliae paratus ad praedam meditatusque venire cupiebat.
examples.translation: He was not content to discover these methods on the spot, though he was no raw new-comer to the work of government;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Noster autem exercitus tametsi urbem ex Tigranis regno ceperat et proeliis usus erat secundis, tamen nimia longinquitate locorum ac desiderio suorum commovebatur.
examples.translation: Our own army, moreover, despite their capture of a city from the kingdom of Tigranes and their successes in battle, began to feel the extreme remoteness of their position and to long for home.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to prick with a goad, to prick or goad on, to urge on (syn. pungo).

examples.original: Quacumque vagatur, Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellona flagellum, Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, Nox ingens scelerum est;
examples.translation: He visits the corpses that sprawl on the wide plain; with his own hand he staunches the wound that would otherwise pour out all the blood of many a man.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: striving after another earnestly, emulating, rivalling, emulous (cf. aemulatio and aemulor), in a good and bad sense; constr. with

examples.original: Quod nisi dux operis vatem frustratur Apollo, Aemulus est nostri maxima causa mali: At tu rivalem noli tibi fingere quemquam, Inque suo solam crede iacere toro.
