examples.translation: Yet, unless Apollo, prince of the craft, deceives the bard, a rival is the chief cause of our malady: but picture no rival to yourself, and think she lies on her couch alone.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Itaque hoste victo ruptorem foederis Mettum Fufetium religatum inter duos currus pernicibus equis distrahit, Albamque ipsam quamvis parentem, aemulam tamen diruit, cum prius omnes opes urbis ipsumque populum Romam transtulisset;
examples.translation: So after the defeat of the enemy Tullus bound Mettus Fufetius, the violator of the treaty, between two chariots, and tore him asunder with swift horses.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: praecidere, the latter to avellere

examples.original: Abscidis frustra ferro tua pignora: bellum Te faciet civile meum.” Sic fata refugit Umbra per amplexus trepidi dilapsa mariti.
examples.translation: The civil war shall make you mine.” Thus speaking, the ghost fled away, dissolving in the arms of her eager husband.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Lateque cladem intulisset ni duo milites praeclarum facinus ausi, arreptis e strage scutis ignorati, vincla ac libramenta tormentorum abscidissent.
examples.translation: They were at once run through and thus their names were lost; but there is no doubt about their deed.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: A foreseeing (very rare): id enim est sapientis providere: ex quo sapientia est appellata prudentia

examples.original: Veneranda enim sunt iustitia, pietas, fides, fortitudo, prudentia;
examples.translation: For reverence is due to justice, duty, loyalty, bravery, and prudence;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Celsus et Paulinus, cum prudentia eorum nemo uteretur, inani nomine ducum alienae culpae praetendebantur;
examples.translation: As for Celsus and Paulinus, no one made any use of their practical knowledge;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Habitus statim cum M. Baebio senatore, familiarissimo suo, communicavit: qui qua fide, qua prudentia, qua diligentia fuerit meminisse vos arbitror.
examples.translation: Habitus immediately confided in his friend, M Baebius, the senator, and I think that you remember the honour, foresight, and care which characterized him.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: difference of opinion, disagreement, dissension, discord (good prose)

examples.original: Quid de quo nulla dissensio est?
examples.translation: Then what of a point on which no disagreement exists?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Haec causa fecit, ut non venirem ad vos, cum meam praesentiam quaereretis, non ad pacis vestrae gaudium, sed ad dissensionis vestrae augmentum.
examples.translation: That was the motive which withheld me from coming to you, when you besought my presence, not to rejoice in your peacefulness, but to increase your strife.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Videsne quam sit magna dissensio?
examples.translation: Do you realize how vast a difference of opinion this is?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: shining, glittering, bright, polished, clear (class.; syn.: splendidus, lautus).

examples.original: Quo factum est, quod omnibus mirabile est visum, ut aeque nitida iumenta ex castello educeret, cum complures menses in obsidione fuisset, ac si in campestribus ea locis habuisset.
examples.translation: The result was that, to the surprise of all, the animals were led out of the fortress after a siege of several months in as good condition as if he had kept them in pasture.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: of or belonging to the earth or to the land
Latin: Terrae sive qui ad terram pertinet

examples.original: Omne animal terrestre alget, esurit, sitit;
examples.translation: Now every earthly living thing gets cold or hungry or thirsty;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Erras enim, si tibi illam putas tantum terrestres operas promittere;
examples.translation: You are indeed mistaken if you think that philosophy offers you nothing but worldly assistance;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: face, expression; looks
entries.grammaticalClass: old forms for vult, vultis, from volo
principalParts: old forms for vult, vultis, from volo

examples.original: Et multa fortasse quae volt, atque in ea, quae non volt, saepe etiam adulescentia incurrit.
examples.translation: Possibly, also, many things he likes; and as for things one does not wish to see, even youth often encounters them.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: At est eo meliore condicione quam adulescens, quoniam id quod ille sperat hic consecutus est: ille volt diu vivere, hic diu vixit.
examples.translation: Yet he is in better case than the young man, since what the latter merely hopes for, the former has already attained; the one wishes to live long, the other has lived long.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Frequentia quoque prosequentium rogantiumque num quid vellet credo fortunatum matrimonium ei sororis visum suique ipsam, malo arbitrio quo a proximis quisque minime anteiri volt, paenituisse.
examples.translation: She was still suffering from the smart of wounded pride, when her father, happening to see her, asked if anything was wrong.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the shortest day in the year, the winter solstice, *

examples.original: Consurgere in ipsis Ius tibi solstitiis, aliena crescere bruma Atque hiemes adferre tuas, solique vagari Concessum per utrosque polos.
examples.translation: He is privileged to rise at midsummer, to be flooded by a winter out of season, and to bring with him a rainy season of his own;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to strike one thing against or on another, to strike, bring, or join together, to unite.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; xi, ctum, 3

examples.original: Prius ad Privernum profectus extemplo acie conflixit.
examples.translation: He marched first on Privernum and at once gave battle.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Q. Fabius pro consule ad urbem Allifas cum Samnitium exercitu signis conlatis confligit.
examples.translation: The proconsul Quintus Fabius fought near the city Allifae a pitched battle with the army of the Samnites.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Pugna indicio fuit quos gesserint animos; namque ita conflixerunt ut aliquamdiu in neutram partem inclinarent acies.
examples.translation: The engagement testified how resolute they were, for they so fought that for some time neither battle-line gave ground.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To force or work one's way out; or (more freq.) to force one's way up, to mount up, climb, ascend.

examples.original: In quo ego quid eniti aut quid efficere possim malo in aliorum spe relinquere quam in oratione mea ponere.
examples.translation: How far I can succeed, how far I can achieve this end, I will rather leave to the hopes of others than declare with my own lips.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to crowd or press together, to compress

examples.original: Nunc ad cotidianam stipem manum porrigis.
examples.translation: Now you are stretching forth your hand for the daily gift.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non arma movendi Iam locus est pressis, stipataque membra teruntur;
examples.translation: The crowded soldiers have no longer space to ply their weapons;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Postquam rogationis dies aderat, ingenti stipatus agmine rostra conscendit, nec deerat obvia manu tota inde nobilitas;
examples.translation: When the day for bringing forward the bill was at hand, he ascended the rostra surrounded by a large following;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: honorableness.

examples.original: Diodorus, eius auditor, adiungit ad honestatem vacuitatem doloris.
examples.translation: Diodorus, his pupil, couples with Moral Worth freedom from pain.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Haec est, inquam, societas, in qua omnia insunt, quae putant homines expetenda—honestas gloria tranquillitas animi atque iucunditas;
examples.translation: In such a partnership, I say, abide all things that men deem worthy of pursuit—honour and fame and delightful tranquillity of mind;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ad honestatem enim illum omnem conatum suum referebat, non ad voluptatem.
examples.translation: For honour and not pleasure was the aim of that great enterprise.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to frighten or terrify thoroughly

examples.original: Multis hominum milibus captis perterriti Bituriges;
examples.translation: The capture of many thousand persons struck terror into the Bituriges;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Hinc celeriter deiecti se in signa manipulosque coniciunt: eo magis timidos perterrent milites.
examples.translation: They were speedily hurled down from thence, and ran headlong into the company formations, scaring the soldiers into greater alarm.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eo circiter hominum numero sedecim milia expedita cum omni equitatu Ariovistus misit, quae copiae nostros perterrerent et munitione prohiberent.
examples.translation: Towards it Ariovistus sent some sixteen thousand light-armed troops with all the horse, as a force to frighten our men and to prevent their entrenching work.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: Any crude metal dug out of the earth, except gold and silver; esp.
Latin: Metallum rude
Latin: Cuprum; hoc est, aes Cyprium

examples.original: Aes prima statuae causa est.
examples.translation: The ”second cause” is the artist;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic est locus solvendi aeris alieni.
examples.translation: Now is the time for me to pay my debt.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Aera non potuit Minos, alia omnia clausit;
examples.translation: The air Minos could not close, though he had closed all else;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: A wavering in opinion or judgment; a being uncertain, a doubting; uncertainty, doubt.

examples.original: Nihil est miserius dubitatione venientium quorsus evadant;
examples.translation: There is nothing more wretched than worry over the outcome of future events;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic tum iniectus est hominibus scrupulus et quaedam dubitatio quidnam esset actum.
examples.translation: This made people feel uneasy and somewhat doubtful as to what had happened.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quae tanta religio est, qua non in nostris dubitationibus atque in maximis superstitionibus unius P. Servilii aut M. Luculli responso ac verbo liberemur?
examples.translation: What sanctity can be so potent, that amid all our doubts and gravest scruples the plain pronouncement of Publius Servilius alone or of Marcus Lucullus cannot absolve us therefrom?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the Greek poet Homer
English: s self upon, to lean or recline upon a thing (cf. ingruo; class., partic. in the trop. sense).

examples.original: Cum mora non tuta est, totis incumbere remis Utile, et admisso subdere calcar equo.
examples.translation: When delay is dangerous, it is best to press on with all oars, and to spur the galloping horse.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nihil ex eo tempore praetermissum est ad maiestatem eius augendam ac multo magis, postquam Agrippa abdicato atque seposito certum erat, uni spem successionis incumbere.
examples.translation: From this time on nothing was left undone which could add to his prestige, especially after the disowning and banishment of Agrippa made it clear that the hope of the succession lay in him alone.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a sharp point or edge; esp., the point of a sword, the sword's point (class.; cf.: acies, cuspis).

examples.original: Iamque hebes et crasso non asper sanguine mucro Perdidit ensis opus, frangit sine volnere membra.
examples.translation: All the host and all the weapons make him their sole object; no hand missed its aim, no lance failed of its mark;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: To drive through, i. e. to thrust or stick a weapon through (syn. traicio)

examples.original: Cum Habonio tutore, quod erat vix HS quadraginta milium, transigunt HS ducentis milibus.
examples.translation: They agreed with the guardian Habonius to pay £2000 for an operation whose real cost was barely £400.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Eo die transigi nihil potuit, quod et id temporis erat et ille pater istius invenerat homines qui dicendo tempus consumerent.
examples.translation: No final decision could be reached that day, both because it was so late, and because Verres’ father secured certain members to spin out the proceedings with long speeches.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed primus dies impetu magis quam veterani exercitus artibus transactus: aperti incautique muros subiere, cibo vinoque praegraves.
examples.translation: The first day was spent in a furious onslaught rather than in skilful attacks appropriate to a veteran army.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: A going round, a circling, revolving, a revolution

examples.original: Ita omnis insula est in circuitu viciens centum milium passuum.
examples.translation: Thus the whole island is two thousand miles in circumference.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quod cum ex omnibus in circuitu partibus altissimas rupes despectusque haberet, una ex parte leniter acclivis aditus in latitudinem non amplius ducentorum pedum relinquebatur;
examples.translation: On every side of its circumference it looked down over the steepest rocks, and on one side only was left a gently sloping approach, not more than two hundred feet in breadth.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: unwilling, reluctant, averse (rare)

examples.original: Quid ergo est, quod nos facit pigros inertesque?
examples.translation: What, then, is it which makes us lazy and sluggish?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec piger ignis erat per stuppea vincula perque Manantes cera tabulas, et tempore eodem Transtraque nautarum summique arsere ceruchi.
examples.translation: He ordered brands steeped in resin to be hurled at the sails of the crowded ships;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: sharing, partaking, participant (class.; syn.: consors, socius); constr. usually with

examples.original: Huic infensi milites erant, quod semper adversatus novis consiliis fuisset et, ne particeps eorum esset, ab Lautulis fugisset.
examples.translation: The men were incensed at Salonius because he had always opposed their mutinous schemes, and had fled from Lautulae that he might not share in them.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fama fuit quosdam ex Fidenatium iuventute participes eius populationis fuisse, cognitioque eius rei L. Sergio et Q. Servilio et Mam. Aemilio permissa.
examples.translation: It was rumoured that certain young men of Fidenae had shared in the pillaging. The investigation of this report was intrusted to Lucius Sergius, Quintus Servilius, and Mamercus Aemilius;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Admovebatur altaribus magis ut victima quam ut sacri particeps adigebaturque iure iurando quae visa auditaque in eo loco essent, non enuntiaturum.
examples.translation: The man was brought up to the altar, more like a victim than a partaker in the rite, and was sworn not to divulge what he should there see or hear.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: height/peak/top/summit/zenith; roof, gable, ridge-pole; head, chief

examples.original: Itaque Pometinae manubiae, quae perducendo ad culmen operi destinatae erant, vix in fundamenta suppeditavere.
examples.translation: Hence the Pometian spoils, which had been destined to carry the building up to the roof, barely sufficed for the foundations.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Haud magis expertus discrimine Caesar in ullo est, Quam non e stabili tremulo sed culmine cuncta Despiceret staretque super titubantia fultus.
examples.translation: Or was it greed for greater rewards that made the soldiers repudiate their cause and their leader, and again put up for sale the swords already stained with guilt?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: untouched, uninjured, intact.

examples.original: Nullum erat genus hominum in castris intactum cupiditate pugnae, summi infimique aeque intenti erant;
examples.translation: There was no class of men in camp who were not affected by the lust of battle;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Alterum intactum ferro corpus et geminata victoria ferocem in certamen tertium dabat: alter fessum vulnere fessum cursu trahens corpus, victusque fratrum ante se strage victori obicitur hosti.
examples.translation: The other dragged himself along, faint from his wound and exhausted with running; he thought how his brothers had been slaughtered before him, and was a beaten man when he faced his triumphant foe.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a frequent surname in the gens Aemilia and Aurelia. So, M. Aemilius Scaurus, whom Cicero defended in an oration, part of which is still extant.—Hence

examples.original: Itaque M. Scaurus, qui Cn. Dolabellam accusavit, istum in sua potestate ac dicione tenuit.
examples.translation: And that, gentlemen, is why Marcus Scaurus, the prosecutor of Dolabella, kept Verres in his power and under his control.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque neque L. Philoni in C. Servilium nominis deferendi potestas est data, neque M. Aurelio Scauro in L. Flaccum, neque Cn. Pompeio in T. Albucium;
examples.translation: For this reason Lucius Philo was not allowed to prosecute Gaius Servilius; Marcus Aurelius Scaurus was not allowed to prosecute Lucius Flaccus;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to surround with a rampart and palisades, to palisade, intrench, circumvallate (syn. saepio).

examples.original: Eum locum vallo fossaque munivit.
examples.translation: He fortified the place with rampart and trench.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Sic enim sentio, ius legatorum, quum hominum praesidio munitum sit, tum etiam divino iure esse vallatum.
examples.translation: For I hold that ambassadorial rights, fortified as they are by human protection, are also reinforced by divine ordinance.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ac reliquarum legionum milites non exaudito sono tubae, quod satis magna valles intercedebat, tamen ab tribunis militum legatisque, ut erat a Caesare praeceptum, retinebantur.
examples.translation: But the rank and file of the other legions did not hear the trumpet-call, as a considerable valley lay in between;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: that has existed a long time, aged
Latin: Qui iam diu constat, permanet

examples.original: Sed quia finem aliquam pariendi debet habere, destitit, ut mulier spatio defessa vetusto.
examples.translation: But because she must have some limit to her bearing, she ceased, like a woman worn out by old age.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Etenim quod sacrificium tam vetustum est quam hoc, quod a regibus aequale huius urbis accepimus?
examples.translation: And indeed what sacrifice is so ancient as that which we received from our kings, and which is coeval with our city?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Pulveris exigui sparget non longa vetustas Congeriem, bustumque cadet, mortisque peribunt Argumenta tuae.
examples.translation: For a short space of time will scatter the little heap of dust; the grave will fall in;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a confession, acknowledgment.

examples.original: Carthaginis.” Haec fuit illius viri non sine praesagio quodam fati inminentis prima confessio.
examples.translation: Carthage.” This was his first confession, fraught with foreknowledge of approaching failure.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sume itaque, mi fili, sume, vir bone et non in superficie sed Christiana caritate Christiane, sume, inquam, etiam libros quos desiderasti, confessionum. mearum;
examples.translation: Take then, my son, take, excellent Sir, Christian that you are not on the surface only, but with Christian love—take, I repeat, those books of my Confessions that you asked for;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a soothsayer, diviner among the Etruscans, who foretold future events from the inspection of the entrails of victims; from this people they were introduced among the Romans
Latin: Vates qui omina ab extis victimarum specit
Latin: Qui res futura praedicit

examples.original: Haruspices secreto ac sine testibus consuli vetuit.
examples.translation: He forbade anyone to consult soothsayers secretly and without witnesses.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Mitto haruspices, mitto illam veterem ab ipsis dis immortalibus, ut hominum fama est, Etruriae traditam disciplinam: nos nonne haruspices esse possumus?
examples.translation: I will dispense with the lore which, as popular rumour has it, was committed to Etruria by the immortal gods;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: worthy of pity, pitiable, miserable, deplorable, lamentable, wretched, sad (class.)
Latin: Miserandus, cuius miseret

examples.original: Sic miserabili strage deletus exercitus.
examples.translation: Thus the army was destroyed in lamentable slaughter.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: easy to be moved, movable; loose, not firm (class.).
Latin: Quod facile movi potest

examples.original: Habet inconstantiam, sed minus vagam ac mobilem.
examples.translation: He has inconstancy, but not the kind that is very capricious or easily set in motion.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec suus Andromedae color est obiectus ab illo, Mobilis in gemino cui pede pinna fuit.
examples.translation: Her complexion was not made a reproach against Andromeda by him on whose either foot was a swift moving pinion.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: A dance in a ring, a choral dance, a dance, = chorea

examples.original: Non vides, quam multorum vocibus chorus constet?
examples.translation: Do you not see how many voices there are in a chorus?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a taking by hand; hence, law t. t., the formal acceptance, the taking possession of a purchase and sale

examples.original: Maior sum et ad maiora genitus, quam ut mancipium sim mei corporis, quod equidem non aliter aspicio quam vinclum aliquod libertati meae circumdatum.
examples.translation: I was born to a greater destiny than to be a mere chattel of my body, and I regard this body as nothing but a chainb which manacles my freedom.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eadem causa est, cur nos mancipiorum nostrorum urbanitas in dominos contumeliosa delectet, quorum audacia ita demum sibi in convivas ius facit, si coepit a domino;
examples.translation: For the same reason the waggery of slaves, insulting to their masters, amuses us, and their boldness at the expense of guests has licence only because they begin with their master himself;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to look about one's self, to cast a look around; or, with an

examples.original: Seducere me debeo et quid suadeam circumspicere.
examples.translation: I ought to go into retirement, and consider what sort of advice I should give you.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Dum tibi tutum non est ad te recedere, circumspice singulos;
examples.translation: You ought to make yourself of a different stamp from the multitude.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In cognoscendo autem ac decernendo mira varietate animi fuit, modo circumspectus et sagax, interdum inconsultus ac praeceps, nonnumquam frivolus amentique similis.
examples.translation: But in hearing and deciding cases he showed strange inconsistency of temper, for he was now careful and shrewd, sometimes hasty and inconsiderate, occasionally silly and like a crazy man.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to seize, snatch, lay hold of, draw a person or thing to one's self (esp. with haste).

examples.original: Verginius arripi iubet hominem et in vincula duci.
examples.translation: Verginius gave orders to seize the fellow and throw him into prison.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Abeuntes magistratu Cn. Genucius tribunus plebis arripuit.
examples.translation: As their term expired, Gnaeus Genucius, a plebeian tribune, haled them to trial.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Lateque cladem intulisset ni duo milites praeclarum facinus ausi, arreptis e strage scutis ignorati, vincla ac libramenta tormentorum abscidissent.
examples.translation: They were at once run through and thus their names were lost; but there is no doubt about their deed.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a coal, charcoal (dead or burning); of dead coals

examples.original: Tum Marius iuvenis et Carbo consules quasi desperata victoria, ne inulti perirent, in antecessum sanguine senatus sibi parentabant, obsessaque curia sic de senatu quasi de carcere qui iugularentur educti.
examples.translation: Then the consuls, the younger Marius and Carbo, as though despairing of victory and desirous of not perishing unavenged, offered sacrifice beforehand to their own shades with the blood of the senate;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: rule, dominion.

examples.original: Postremo Superbi illius inportuna dominatio non nihil, immo vel plurimum profuit.
examples.translation: Finally, the outrageous tyranny of Tarquinius Superbus was of some, nay, of great service;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Quamquam nullam nobilitatem, nullos honores, nulla merita cuiquam ad dominationem pandere viam;
examples.translation: To be sure, no nobility, no honours, no merits, opened wide the road to tyranny for any man;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed Vitellius adventu fratris et inrepentibus dominationis magistris superbior et atrocior occidi Dolabellam iussit, quem in coloniam Aquinatem sepositum ab Othone rettulimus.
examples.translation: But Vitellius was moved to greater arrogance and cruelty by the arrival of his brother and by the cunning approaches of his teachers in the imperial art;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to soil, defile, pollute.

examples.original: Hos scelerum ritus, haec dirae crimina gentis Effera damnarat nimiae pietatis Erictho Inque novos ritus pollutam duxerat artem.
examples.translation: These criminal rites and malpractices of an accursed race fierce Erictho had scouted as not wicked enough, and had turned her loathsome skill to rites before unknown.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: any body, any thing

examples.original: Quis nos magno opere attendit umquam, in hoc quidem genere causarum, ubi aliquid ereptum aut ablatum a quopiam dicitur?
examples.translation: In cases of this type, where anyone is alleged to have stolen or appropriated anything, who cares much what we pleaders say?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Utrum gravius aliquid in quempiam dici potest quam ad hominem condemnandum, quem numquam vidisset neque audisset, adductum pretio esse?
examples.translation: Or, again, can any allegation be made with more certainty than one which the object of it cannot attempt to dispute even by shaking his head?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: sadness, mournfulness, sorrow, grief, melancholy, gloominess, dejection (class.; syn. maestitia).

examples.original: Stultius vero nihil est quam famam captare tristitiae et lacrimas adprobare, quas iudico sapienti viro alias permissas cadere, alias vi sua latas.
examples.translation: But nothing is more foolish than to court a reputation for sadness and to sanction tears; for I hold that with a wise man some tears fall by consent, others by their own force.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Illud nullo modo probo, quod ait Metrodorus: esse aliquam cognatam tristitiae voluptatem, hanc esse captandam in eiusmodi tempore. Ipsa Metrodori verba subscripsi.
examples.translation: And in no wise do I approve of the remark of Metrodorus—that there is a certain pleasure akin to sadness, and that one should give chase thereto at such times as these.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to put away, conceal carefully, hide
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; condi and condĭdi, condĭtum and consum, 3
principalParts: condi and condĭdi, condĭtum and consum, 3

examples.original: Sed et ipsum otium absconde.
examples.translation: But at the same time conceal your retirement also.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quae enim de voluptate dicuntur, ea nec acutissime nec abscondite disseruntur;
examples.translation: For pleasure is a topic that does not lend itself to very subtle or profound discussion;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Dixi a principio nihil me de scientia vestra, nihil de sacris, nihil de abscondito iure pontificum dicturum.
examples.translation: I said at the outset that I should base no assertion upon my own knowledge, upon religious observance, or upon the secret regulations of the pontiffs.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a farm, estate, a manor (either in town or country)

examples.original: Ne parum locuples esset? at erat, et esset amplius si velles, populo cautum praedibus et praediis.
examples.translation: Even if the actual facts, the shamefulness of the wrong you were doing, left you unmoved;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a Roman prœnomen; e. g. Spurius Cassius, Spurius Maelius

examples.original: Sp. Tarpeius Romanae praeerat arci.
examples.translation: Spurius Tarpeius commanded the Roman citadel.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Duos tamen cum eo pudor tenuit, Sp. Larcium ac T. Herminium, ambos claros genere factisque.
examples.translation: Yet were there two who were prevented by shame from leaving him.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sp. Lucretius cum P. Valerio Volesi filio, Collatinus cum L. Iunio Bruto venit, cum quo forte Romam rediens ab nuntio uxoris erat conventus.
examples.translation: Collatinus brought Lucius Junius Brutus, with whom he chanced to be returning to Rome when he was met by the messenger from his wife.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: level ground, vacant place; building site
Latin: Planities, in qua frumenta secta teruntur et arescunt
Latin: Locus in urbe purus, hoc est vacuus, in quo aedificari potest

examples.original: Coit area belli: Hic alitur sanguis terras fluxurus in omnes, Hic et Thessalicae clades Libycaeque tenentur;
examples.translation: The field of war was now contracted; here is preserved the blood that will flow hereafter over every land;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: dark, swarthy, dusky, tawny
Latin: color similis coloribus qui sunt ater; niger, vel fulvus

examples.original: Cetera saepe tamen potuere admissa negari, Et crimen nox est infitiata suum: Nostra notat fusco digitos iniuria suco Cortice contactas inficiente manus.
examples.translation: Yet other crimes when committed can often be denied, and night disavows her guilty deed: injury done to me marks the fingers with dark juice, and my bark stains the hands that touch it.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fabium illis Valentem, captivum et casibus dubiis reservatum, praegravem fuisse, nedum Primus ac Fuscus et specimen partium Mucianus ullam in Vitellium nisi occidendi licentiam habeant.
examples.translation: Will Primus and Fuscus or that leading representative of their party, Mucianus, have any liberty in dealing with you except the liberty of killing? Caesar did not leave Pompey unharmed or Augustus Antony.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: death (syn.: mors, letum).
Latin: Mors, praesertim caedes violenta

examples.original: Iunxit parricidio matris amitae necem.
examples.translation: To matricide he added the murder of his aunt.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Illis te manibus tangi, Briseï, sinebas, Imbutae Phrygia quae nece semper erant.
examples.translation: By those hands didst thou suffer thyself to be touched, Briseis, that were ever imbued in Phrygian blood;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Noli ergo atrocius vindicare quod lenius invenisti. Inquirendi quam puniendi neces-sitas maior est;
examples.translation: Do not then punish with harsher sentence what you found out by gentler methods.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to say often; to pronounce, declare, or assert repeatedly.
Latin: pluries vel saepius
Latin: dict|ō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum

examples.original: Mamilius Tusculi tum dictator erat.
examples.translation: Lucius Mamilius was then dictator at Tusculum.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quinctius sexto decimo die dictatura in sex menses accepta se abdicavit.
examples.translation: On the sixteenth day Quinctius surrendered the dictatorship which he had received for six months.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Deinceps procedente tempore duodetriginta consulatus, dictaturas quinque, censuras septem, triumphos sex, duas ovationes adepta est.
examples.translation: Then as time went on it was honoured with twenty-eight consulships, five dictatorships, seven censorships, six triumphs, and two ovations.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a breaking out, bursting forth.

examples.original: Atqui si nox opportuna est eruptioni, sicut est, haec profecto noctis aptissima hora est.
examples.translation: And yet, if night is favourable for our sally, as it is, this is surely the fittest hour of the night.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et Fabius cum equitatu impetum dederat et consul eruptionem e castris in trepidos iam hostes fecerat;
examples.translation: Fabius had delivered a charge with his cavalry; the consul had made a sally from the camp against the enemy, who were already wavering;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Prima luce ad moenia omnibus copiis admotis corona cinxit urbem subsidiaque firma, ne qua eruptio fieret, portis opposuit.
examples.translation: With the dawn he led up all his forces under the walls and invested the city, posting strong supports to prevent any sally from the gates.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To hear or perceive clearly (class.)
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; īvi or ii, ītum, 4

examples.original: Equitem clara increpans voce, ut hostes exaudirent, redire in proelium iubet: nihil trepidatione opus esse;
examples.translation: The horseman he reprimanded in a loud voice, that the enemy might overhear him, and ordered him to go back and fight;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: A quibus perlatus ad primos tumultus eo pavore signaque et ordines turbavit ut neque imperia exaudiri neque instrui acies posset.
examples.translation: At the very instant when the column was getting clear of the camp, the Volsci, as though set in motion by the same signal, fell upon their rear.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ac reliquarum legionum milites non exaudito sono tubae, quod satis magna valles intercedebat, tamen ab tribunis militum legatisque, ut erat a Caesare praeceptum, retinebantur.
examples.translation: But the rank and file of the other legions did not hear the trumpet-call, as a considerable valley lay in between;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: bosom (freq. and class.; cf. sinus).

examples.original: Quae cum gremio mollito ac subacto sparsum semen excepit, primum id occaecatum cohibet, ex quo occatio quae hoc efficit nominata est;
examples.translation: And yet what I enjoy is not the fruit alone, but I also enjoy the soil itself, its nature and its power.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a share

examples.original: Securitatis magna portio est nihil inique facere.
examples.translation: The most important contribution to peace of mind is never to do wrong.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Censorem, aedilem curulem, tres tribunos plebis mortuos ferunt, pro portione et ex multitudine alia multa funera fuisse;
examples.translation: It is stated that a censor, a curule aedile, and three plebeian tribunes died, with a correspondingly large number from the rest of the population.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a public prayer or supplication, a religious solemnity in consequence of certain (fortunate or unfortunate) public events

examples.original: His rebus gestis, ex litteris Caesaris dierum viginti supplicatio a senatu decreta est.
examples.translation: And for these achievements, upon receipt of Caesar’s despatches, the Senate decreed a public thanksgiving of twenty days.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eo anno prodigia multa fuerunt, quorum averruncandorum causa supplicationes in biduum senatus decrevit;
examples.translation: In that year were many portents, to avert which the senate decreed supplications for two days.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ob easque res ex litteris Caesaris dies quindecim supplicatio decreta est, quod ante id tempus accidit nulli.
examples.translation: And for those achievements, upon receipt of Caesar’s despatches, a fifteen days’ thanksgiving was decreed, an honour that had previously fallen to no man.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: bent, stretched, or grown inwards, or awry.

examples.original: Omnis Romanis quae cesserat Africa signis, Tum Vari sub iure fuit;
examples.translation: All of Africa that had yielded to the Roman arms was then commanded by Varus;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Missus extemplo Varus cum expedita manu paucos repugnantium interfecit;
examples.translation: Varus was despatched at once with a force in light marching order.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Vitellius ut e somno excitus Iulium Priscum et Alfenum Varum cum quattuordecim praetoriis cohortibus et omnibus equitum alis obsidere Appenninum iubet;
examples.translation: Vitellius was like a man wakened from a deep sleep. He ordered Julius Priscus and Alfenus Varus to block the passes of the Apennines with fourteen praetorian cohorts and all the cavalry.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to stretch something (e. g. the bow) toward something; so only in Appul.: arcum, Met. 2, p. 122, 5.—Hence

examples.original: Quae vobis alio loco planius explicabuntur: nunc hoc attendite.
examples.translation: The story of all this shall be told in clearer detail later on;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quis nos magno opere attendit umquam, in hoc quidem genere causarum, ubi aliquid ereptum aut ablatum a quopiam dicitur?
examples.translation: In cases of this type, where anyone is alleged to have stolen or appropriated anything, who cares much what we pleaders say?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sed cum ea quae praeterierunt acri animo et attento intuemur, tum fit ut aegritudo sequatur si illa mala sint, si bona, laetitia.
examples.translation: But when we fix our mental vision closely on the events of the past, then sorrow or gladness ensues according as these were evil or good.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: The moongoddess, sister of Phœbus, i. e.

examples.original: Quod Phoebum decuit, quem non decet?
examples.translation: Whom does that not become which became Phoebus?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Nec tibi sol calidus, nec sit tibi lucida Phoebe, Destituant oculos sidera clara tuos.
examples.translation: May the sun not be warm for thee, nor Phoebe bright, may the clear stars fail thy vision.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a Roman emperor, reigned between 69 and 79 A. D.

examples.original: Obstitit Antonius datisque defensoribus ad Vespasianum dimisit.
examples.translation: Antonius interposed, gave him a guard, and sent him to Vespasian.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Propinqua adfinitas Ceriali cum Vespasiano, nec ipse inglorius militiae, eoque inter duces adsumptus est.
examples.translation: Cerialis was closely connected with Vespasian, and being himself not without reputation in war, was made one of the commanders.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ego te, Vespasiane, ad imperium voco, quam salutare rei publicae, quam tibi magnificum, iuxta deos in tua manu positum est.
examples.translation: I call you, Vespasian, to the throne. How advantageous to the state, how glorious for you this may prove, are questions which depend, after the gods, on your own acts.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to feel disgust, loathing, or
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; īvi, or ĭi, ītum, 4

examples.original: Sed rursus etiam illae quae aliquid esse videbantur in saeculo, non habeant fastidio sorores suas quae ad illam sanctam societatem ex paupertate venerunt;
examples.translation: But again, let not those who in the world considered themselves something, hold in scorn their sisters who have come to that holy fellowship from povertyb;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: Robbery, plundering, pillage, rapine

examples.original: Quaecumque est veneris subita violata rapina, Gaudet, et inprobitas muneris instar habet.
examples.translation: She whom a sudden assault has taken by storm is pleased, and counts the audacity as a compliment.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Caesar suos a proelio continebat, ac satis habebat in praesentia hostem rapinis pabulationibus populationibusque prohibere.
examples.translation: Caesar kept his troops from fighting, accounting it sufficient for the present to prevent the enemy from plundering, foraging, and devastation.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ibi per occasionem ac licentiam omni rapinarum genere grassati, cum timerent ne sibi reversis reddenda ratio ac subeunda poena esset, consilium inierunt eligendi creandique imperatoris;
examples.translation: There, taking advantage of the lawless state of the times, they indulged in every kind of pillage;
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: assistant, deputy; accomplice; supporter
Latin: Qui adiuvit
Latin: Aliqui cui officium adiuvandi est

examples.original: Aliud litterarum genus adiutorium admittit.
examples.translation: The other kind of literary activitya admits of outside assistance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His adiutor contra patriam inventus est nemo;
examples.translation: Not one single supporter could be found to aid these men against their country;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: one who bestows care or labor upon a thing, an elaborator, cultivator, etc.

examples.original: Et utique maritum habebat multarum mulierum virum et deorum alienorum falsorumque cultorem.
examples.translation: And yet her husband was a man with many wives and worshipped strange, false gods.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Famem quoque ex pestilentia morbo implicitis cultoribus agrorum timentes in Etruriam Pomptinumque agrum et Cumas, postremo in Siciliam quoque frumenti causa misere.
examples.translation: They therefore sent to Etruria and the Pomptine district, and to Cumae, and finally to Sicily itself, for corn.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nil, Africa, de te Nec de te, natura, queror: tot monstra ferentem Gentibus ablatum dederas serpentibus orbem, Inpatiensque solum Cereris cultore negato Damnasti atque homines voluisti desse venenis.
examples.translation: I do not blame Africa, nor Nature: Nature had taken from men and assigned to serpents a region so fertile of monsters: the soil would bear no corn, and she condemned it to lie untilled;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: now... now, at one time... at another

examples.original: Terra salutares herbas, eademque nocentes Nutrit, et urticae proxima saepe rosa est;
examples.translation: The same earth fosters healing herbs and noxious, and oft is the nettle nearest to the rose;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to be against, be prejudicial to; to hinder, hurt, injure; opp. to prodesse (cf.: officio, noceo, injuriam facio; class.)
Latin: esse contra

examples.original: Hoc vos Cluentio iudicium putatis obesse oportere?
examples.translation: Ought this trial, think you, to reflect on Cluentius?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Navigio ista obsunt, non rectori eius, qua rector est.
examples.translation: These mishaps obstruct the voyage but not the steersman qua steersman.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quae gratia ne quid tibi prodesse posset ego mea diligentia perfeci, ut etiam obesse deberet tu tua sapientia curasti.
examples.translation: My watchfulness has made it impossible for this popularity at all to help your case; and your intelligence has taken effective steps to make it actually tell against you.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Consisting of a great number, numerous, manifold (post-Aug.)
English: a small stone, a pebble

examples.original: An si ad calculos eum res publica vocet, non merito dicat: ’annua aera habes, annuam operam ede;
examples.translation: Why, if the commonwealth should call him to a reckoning, would it not justly say, ’You have a year’s stipend, render a year’s service;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sic ista sine noxa decipiunt, quomodo praestigiatorum acetabula et calculi, in quibus me fallacia ipsa delectat.
examples.translation: Such quibbles are just as harmlessly deceptive as the juggler’s cup and dice, in which it is the very trickery that pleases me.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hoc quidem est nimis exigue et exiliter ad calculos vocare amicitiam, ut par sit ratio acceptorum et datorum.
examples.translation: It surely is calling friendship to a very close and petty accounting to require it to keep an exact balance of credits and debits.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a stag, a deer
Latin: Animal mammiferum ruminans, genere Cervus
English: to pour out around, i.e. as in circumdo, either with the

examples.original: Id vero circumfuso undique equitatu—ut vallum peteretur opusque inciperet—fieri non poterat.
examples.translation: But enveloped, as they were, by the enemy’s horse, it was impossible to gather stakes and begin the work.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to stand opposite to one, to be against, i. e. to resist or oppose

examples.original: Quid est in tormentis, quid est in aliis, quae adversa appellamus, mali?
examples.translation: What element of evil is there in torture and in the other things which we call hardships?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sic enim populo erat persuasum, et adversas superiores et praesentes secundas res accidisse eius opera.
examples.translation: In fact, the people were convinced that it was to him that their former disasters and their present successes were due.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Alcibiades

examples.original: Eadem autem celeritate adverso colle ad nostra castra atque eos qui in opere occupati erant contenderunt.
examples.translation: Then with the same speed they hastened up-hill against our camp and the troops engaged in entrenching it.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to deem worthy: quis caelestes dignet decorare hostiis, Pac. ap.
Latin: dignitate afficere

examples.original: Dignus illa es, illa digna te est;
examples.translation: You are worthy of her; she is worthy of you;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Condicio itaque quam insinuare dignatus es, non mihi displicet, si nuptura est;
examples.translation: The condition, therefore, that you are good enough to suggest seems to me satisfactory, if she gets married;
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Quod ut nobiscum ab eo petere atque impetrare digneris, tantis precibus posco, quantis verba nulla sufficiunt.
examples.translation: With entreaties that surpass all expression I urge you to be good enough to join me in asking and obtaining a visit from him.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: of or belonging to fate, ordained by fate or destiny, decreed, destined, fated, fatal (class.).

examples.original: Illi comparatis ingentibus copiis eandem illam, quae fatalis Gnaeo Pompeio fuit, harenam insederant.
examples.translation: Brutus and Cassius, having collected vast forces, had occupied the same ground as had been fatal to Gnaeus Pompeius.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a crowd, troop, a band

examples.original: Non corniger Hammon Mittere Marmaricas cessavit in arma catervas, Quidquid ab occiduis Libye patet arida Mauris Usque Paraetonias eoa ad litora Syrtes.
examples.translation: Nor was horned Ammon slow to send to battle African squadrons from the whole extent of parched Libya—from the Moors in the West to Egyptian Syrtes on the eastern coast.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Munera gladiatoria partim in amphitheatro Tauri partim in Saeptis aliquot edidit, quibus inseruit catervas Afrorum Campanorumque pugilum ex utraque regione electissimorum.
examples.translation: He gave several gladiatorial shows, some in the amphitheatre of Taurus and some in the Saepta, in which he introduced pairs of African and Campanian boxers, the pick of both regions.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: to be under, among, or behind; to be near, close, or at hand (class.)

examples.original: Omnibus enim istis una virtus subest, quae animum rectum et indeclinabilem praestat.
examples.translation: For underlying them all is a single virtue—that which renders the soul straight and unswerving.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Suberat etiam alia causa maior, quae Oppianici hominis avarissimi mentem maxime com movebat.
examples.translation: But behind this there was another and a more cogent reason, appealing strongly to Oppianicus’s great love of money;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tandem vulneribus defessi et pedem referre et, quod mons suberat circiter mille passuum, eo se recipere coeperunt.
examples.translation: At length, worn out with wounds, they began to retreat, retiring towards a height about a mile away. They gained the height;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to throw asunder; to drive asunder; to scatter, disperse (freq. in poets and historians, esp. since the Aug. per.; not in Cic., Plaut., or Ter.).
English: adorned with a neck-chain or collar. In gen.

examples.original: Quare aliud aliquod, Torquate, hominis summum bonum reperiendum est;
examples.translation: Therefore we are bound, Torquatus, to find some other Chief Good for man.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque eam infectam rem M. Fulvius Paetus T. Manlius Torquatus novi consules acceperunt.
examples.translation: The enterprise was therefore still unfinished when Marcus Fulvius Paetus and Titus Manlius Torquatus, the new consuls, took it over.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec enim in Torquati sermone quidquam implicatum aut tortuosum fuit, nostraque, ut mihi videtur, dilucida oratio.
examples.translation: There was nothing abstruse or intricate in the discourse of Torquatus, and my own exposition was, I believe, as clear as daylight.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: scornful contempt or disdain of others, haughtiness, arrogance, pride

examples.original: Statuam habet Praeneste, in inferiore fori parte contra hemicyclium, in quo fastos a se ordinatos et marmoreo parieti incisos publicarat.
examples.translation: His statue stands at Praeneste in the upper part of the forum near the hemicycle, on which he exhibited the calendar which he had arranged and inscribed upon its marble walls.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: complaisance, indulgence, kindness, obliging disposition or conduct, mercy, grace

examples.original: Dixerit, ut venias: pacta tibi nocte venito;
examples.translation: She has bidden you come: come on the night arranged for you;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Periere latebrae Tot scelerum, populo venia est erepta nocenti: Agnovere suos.
examples.translation: For at this moment our age can exercise a mighty influence upon the future.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: At tibi ius veniae superest, Germania, nullum: Postmodo tu poenas, barbare, morte dabis.
examples.translation: But for thee, Germania, no right of pardon remains; thou shalt atone hereafter, barbarian, by thy death.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to roll to or upon any thing.

examples.original: Non tamen in caeca bellorum nube cadendum est, Aut cum permixtas acies sua tela tenebris Involvent.
examples.translation: Yet we are not compelled to fall on the blind haze of battle, or when their own missiles cover the confused armies with darkness.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Saetigerisque pares subus silvestria membra nuda dabant terrae nocturno tempore capti, circum se foliis ac frondibus involventes.
examples.translation: And when night overtook them, like bristly hogs they just cast their savage bodies naked upon the ground, rolling themselves in leaves and boughs.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Ipse caput medio Titan cum ferret Olympo, Condidit ardentes atra caligine currus Involvitque orbem tenebris gentesque coegit Desperare diem;
examples.translation: The sun himself, while rearing his head in the zenith, hid his burning chariot in black darkness and veiled his sphere in gloom, forcing mankind to despair of daylight;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Subject, liable to punishment, obnoxious to punishment, punishable: obnoxius poenae obligatus ob delictum, Paul. ex

examples.original: In hoc obnoxio domicilio animus liber habitat.
examples.translation: In this dwelling, which is exposed to peril, my soul lives free.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: De homine dixi, fluvida materia et caduca et omnibus obnoxia causis;
examples.translation: So much for man,—a substance that flows away and falls, exposed to every influence;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Exempla enim se ipsos inutilis disciplinae circumferunt nulli non vitio, quod insequuntur, obnoxii.
examples.translation: For those who are liable to every fault which they castigate advertise themselves as patterns of useless training.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or in a town other than Rome (since urbanus signifies, of Rome, from the capital); sometimes in a depreciating sense, opp

examples.original: Cuius flamma ut ab oppidanis et oppugnatoribus est visa, utrisque venit in opinionem signum a classiariis regis datum.
examples.translation: When the flames were seen by the besiegers and the townspeople, both parties thought it a signal given by the king’s marines.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Militiades

examples.original: Caesar Ibi crebris litteris Canini fit certior quae de Drappete et Lucterio gesta essent, quoque in consilio permanerent oppidani.
examples.translation: At this point Caesar learned by frequent despatches from Caninius what had been done with Drappes and Lucterius and what was the steadfast purpose of the townsfolk.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eo de media nocte Caesar, isdem ducibus usus qui nuntii ab Iccio venerant, Numidas et Cretas sagittarios et funditores Baleares subsidio oppidanis mittit;
examples.translation: Using again as guides the men who had come from Iccius to report, Caesar sent off to Bibrax in the middle of the night Numidian and Cretan archers and Balearic slingers, to reinforce the townsfolk.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: liveliness, activity, force
English: the beginning, the warp of a web (rare)
English: a violent or pouring rain, a rain-storm.
Latin: repentina et praeceps pluvia, imber

examples.original: Non caeli nox illa fuit: latet obsitus aer Infernae pallore domus nimbisque gravatus Deprimitur, fluctusque in nubibus accipit imbrem.
examples.translation: The darkness was not the common darkness of night: the heavens were hidden and veiled with the dimness of the infernal regions, and weighed down by clouds;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: moderately warm, lukewarm, tepid (cf.: calidus, fervidus).

examples.original: Quid iuvat admonitu tepidam recalescere mentem?
examples.translation: What boots it by remembrance to heat once more a cooling passion?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: wheat
English: of or pertaining to war
Latin: De bello
Latin: Bellicosus

examples.original: In hoc non minus eius pietas suspicienda est quam virtus bellica;
examples.translation: At this juncture his patriotism is no less to be admired than his valour in war;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

examples.original: Hic finis Augusto bellicorum certaminum fuit, idem rebellandi finis Hispaniae.
examples.translation: This was the end of Augustus’ campaigns as well as of the rebellion in Spain.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: the good quality of a thing, goodness, excellence

examples.original: Nec enim bonitas est pessimis esse meliorem.
examples.translation: For goodness does not mean merely being better than the lowest.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque pars magna bonitatis est velle fieri bonum.
examples.translation: You know what I mean by a good man?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed eadem bonitas etiam ad multitudinem pertinet.
examples.translation: But this same goodness belongs also to the generality of men.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: stammering, stuttering (opp. planus, speaking fluently, without impediment): balba, loqui non quit?

examples.original: Atque hoc priusquam ei accideret, postquam in dies dolores accrescere febresque accessisse sensit, Agrippam generum ad se accersi iussit et cum eo L. Cornelium Balbum Sextumque Peducaeum.
examples.translation: Even before this occurred, feeling a daily increase of pain attended with fever, he gave orders that his son-in-law Agrippa should be summoned, and with him Lucius Cornelius Balbus and Sextus Peducaeus.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

definitions: English: lighted up, clear, bright, light, lustrous (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.).
Latin: Qui illustratus est

examples.original: Quorundam illustrium exsequias usque ad rogum frequentavit.
examples.translation: He attended the obsequies of certain distinguished men, even going to the funeral-pyre.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Atque his de rebus et splendida est eorum et illustris oratio.
examples.translation: And these topics they handle in a style as brilliant as it is illuminating.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Tu mihi, cum circumsessus a tam illustri civitate sis propter tuum scelus atque flagitium;
examples.translation: Seeing that you were beset by the people of that reputable town through your own criminal and wicked act;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: pregnant, with child, with young (class.; syn. praegnans, fetus).

examples.original: Lucumo superfuit patri bonorum omnium heres: Arruns prior quam pater moritur uxore gravida relicta.
examples.translation: Lucumo survived his father and inherited all his property; Arruns died before his father, leaving his wife with child.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nocte sub extrema pulso torpore quietis, Dum fovet amplexu gravidum Cornelia curis Pectus et aversi petit oscula grata mariti, Umentes mirata genas percussaque caeco Volnere non audet flentem deprendere Magnum.
examples.translation: Night was ending and the drowsiness of sleep was banished, when Cornelia clasped in her arms the care-laden breast of her husband and sought the dear lips of him who turned from her;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nam cum esset gravida Auria, fratris uxor, et iam appropinquare partus putaretur, mulierem veneno interfecit, ut una illud, quod erat ex fratre conceptum, necaretur.
examples.translation: His brother’s wife Auria was pregnant, and was thought to be approaching her delivery; therefore he poisoned her in order that his brother’s seed might perish with her.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to refuse by a nod
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; ŭi, ŭĭtum; ūtum, 3

examples.original: Id primo quidam abnuentes iuraturos se obtruncati circa altaria sunt;
examples.translation: Some there were at first who refused to take this oath;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Iam primum, ut ordiar ab ducibus comparandis, haud equidem abnuo egregium ducem fuisse Alexandrum;
examples.translation: First of all—to begin by comparing commanders—I do not deny that Alexander was a remarkable general;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Neque enim tantum arte et scientia, sed longe magis facultate et <usu> eloquentiam contineri, nec tu, puto, abnues et hi significare vultu videntur.”
examples.translation: To this view I am sure you will not demur, and our friends here, to judge by their looks, seem to indicate concurrence.”
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: cheerful, of good cheer, lively
Latin: Laetus, laetitia plenus

examples.original: Sapiens ille plenus est gaudio, hilaris et placidus, inconcussus;
examples.translation: The wise man is joyful, happy and calm, unshaken;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quare non est quod fastidiosi isti te deterreant, quo minus servis tuis hilarem te praestes et non superbe superiorem;
examples.translation: You should therefore not be deterred by these finicky persons from showing yourself to your slaves as an affable person and not proudly superior to them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to kiss, Cn. Matius ap.

examples.original: Gratulatus sum protinus mihi et dixi: ”Non a summis labris ista venerunt, habent hae voces fundamentum.
examples.translation: I immediately congratulated myself and said: ”These words did not come from the edge of the lips; these utterances have a solid foundation.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quibusdam etiam constantissimis in conspectu populi sudor erumpit, non aliter quam fatigatis et aestuantibus solet, quibusdam tremunt genua dicturis, quorundam dentes colliduntur, lingua titubat, labra concurrunt.
examples.translation: The steadiest speaker, when before the public, often breaks into a perspiration, as if he had wearied or over-heated himself; some tremble in the knees when they rise to speak;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to throw round, to wrap about
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; ĭcui, or ixi, ictum, 4

examples.original: Et saepe incidunt magnae res, ut discedendum sit ab amicis;
examples.translation: Often, too, important duties arise which require the temporary separation of friends;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Me igitur ipsum ames oportet, non mea, si veri amici futuri sumus.
examples.translation: So you must love me myself, not my possessions, if we are to be genuine friends.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Discolor et vario furialis cultus amictu Induitur, voltusque aperitur crine remoto, Et coma vipereis substringitur horrida sertis.
examples.translation: She put on motley raiment, whose parti-coloured woof was fit for a fiend to wear; she threw back her hair and revealed her face;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a nostril, usually in

examples.original: Hic aures, alius spiramina naris aduncae Amputat;
examples.translation: The arms, wrenched from the shoulders, fell to the ground;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: golden yellow, reddish yellow, flaxen-colored
Latin: Cui color mellis vel auri est

examples.original: Non pabula tellus Pascendis summittit equis, non proserit ullam Flava Ceres segetem;
examples.translation: The earth sends up no fodder to feed his horses; golden Ceres puts forth no corn there;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Haec Libycos, pars tam flavos gerit altera crines, Ut nullis Caesar Rheni se dicat in arvis Tam rutilas vidisse comas;
examples.translation: Some had the hair of Africa, and others were so fair-headed that Caesar said he had never seen hair so red in the Rhine country;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Contionante Vitellio postulantur ad supplicium Asiaticus et Flavus et Rufinus duces Galliarum, quod pro Vindice bellassent.
examples.translation: When Vitellius was addressing his troops, the soldiers demanded the punishment of Asiaticus, Flavius, and Rufinus, Gallic chiefs who had fought for Vindex.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to feel annoyance or reluctance at; to repent of a thing.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; gŭi, and pĭgĭtum est, 2

definitions: English: a shameful or disgraceful act (class.; syn.: dedecus, flagitium).

examples.original: Nunc iubent Etruscos probra iacere, nunc armati sibi quisque lingua promptum hostem offerri.
examples.translation: Now—they all cried—now, when they were armed, let the lip-bold enemy face them!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ubi crudescere seditio et a conviciis ac probris ad tela et manus transibant, inici catenas Flaviano iubet.
examples.translation: But the troops saw through the ruse, thrust aside those who guarded the tribunal, and prepared to use extreme violence.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Cum utraque divortium fecit, sed cum Paetina ex levibus offensis, cum Urgulanilla ob libidinum probra et homicidii suspicionem.
examples.translation: He divorced both these, Paetina for trivial offences, but Urgulanilla because of scandalous lewdness and the suspicion of murder.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to write before or in front of, to write over or upon, to inscribe.

examples.original: A. Trebonium fratrem habuerat proscriptum.
examples.translation: His brother Aulus Trebonius was among the outlawed;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cn. Decidio Samniti, ei, qui proscriptus est, iniuriam in calamitate eius ab huius familia factam esse dixistis.
examples.translation: You have stated that Gn. Decidius the Samnite— the same who was proscribed—was insulted in his misfortune by my client’s slaves.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a mate, fellow, intimate, comrade, crony, boon-companion, etc.

examples.original: Ego Plancium, Laterensis, et ipsum gratiosum esse dico et habuisse in petitione multos cupidos sui gratiosos, quos tu si sodales vocas, officiosam amicitiam nomine inquinas criminoso.
examples.translation: I tell you, Laterensis, that not only is Plancius himself popular, but that the host of ardent supporters who backed his candidature were also popular.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Erant in Romana iuventute adulescentes aliquot, nec ii tenui loco orti, quorum in regno libido solutior fuerat, aequales sodalesque adulescentium Tarquiniorum, adsueti more regio vivere.
examples.translation: This licence they missed, now that all enjoyed equal rights, and they had got into the way of complaining to each other that the liberty of the rest had resulted in their own enslavement.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the bladder in the body of animals, the urinary bladder.

examples.original: Nihil interest, centum per vesicam tuam an mille amphorae transeant;
examples.translation: You know the taste of wine and cordials.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ait enim se vesicae et exulcerati ventris tormenta tolerare ulteriorem doloris accessionem non recipientia, esse nihilominus sibi illum beatum diem.
examples.translation: For he tells usb that he had to endure excruciating agony from a diseased bladder and from an ulcerated stomach,—so acute that it permitted no increase of pain;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: shortness.

examples.original: Virtus enim tantum bonum est, ut istas accessiones minutas non sentiat, brevitatem aevi et dolorem et corporum varias offensiones.
examples.translation: For virtue is so great a good that it is not affected by such insignificant assaults upon it as shortness of life, pain, and the various bodily vexations.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fuit etiam disertus ut nemo ei Thebanus par esset eloquentia, neque minus concinnus in brevitate respondendi quam in perpetua oratione ornatus.
examples.translation: Epaminondas was also so good a speaker that no Theban equalled him in eloquence, and he was not less clever in brief answers than brilliant in a set speech.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Epaminondas

examples.original: Ut et levi momento nec ambigue est victus, ita brevitate ipsa loci facili-que receptu in tam propinqua castra haud aegre militem a multa caede est tutatus;
examples.translation: He was easily and decisively defeated; yet, because his camp was so near and so readily accessible, he was able without great difficulty to save his men from heavy losses;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to beat, bruise, grind, crush, pound, break to pieces

examples.original: Is labor urbano militi insolitus contundit animos.
examples.translation: The work involved was strange to the town troops and broke their spirit.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to prick, puncture (class.).
English: to stick in, to stick, hang, or cleave to, to adhere to, inhere in.

examples.original: Quaeque de virtutibus dicta sunt, quemadmodum eae semper voluptatibus inhaererent, eadem de amicitia dicenda sunt.
examples.translation: All that has been said about the essential connexion of the virtues with pleasure must be repeated about friendship.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to call by name, to call, name
English: faithlessness, dishonesty, treachery, falsehood, perfidy (class.)

examples.original: Sine cupiditatibus vos genui, sine timoribus, sine superstitione, sine perfidia ceterisque pestibus;
examples.translation: I brought you into the world without desires or fears, free from superstition, treachery and the other curses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nec ulla apud Vitellianos flagitii poena, et praemiis defectorum versa fides ac reliquum perfidiae certamen.
examples.translation: With the Vitellians there was no punishment for cowardice; those who went over to the Flavians received the rewards of their treachery;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Accedebat huc Caecinae ambitio vetus, torpor recens, nimia fortunae indulgentia soluti in luxum, seu perfidiam meditanti infringere exercitus virtutem inter artes erat.
examples.translation: Another factor in the situation was furnished by Caecina’s old ambition and his newly acquired sloth, for an excess of Fortune’s favours had made him give way to luxury;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: beauty.

examples.original: Et si turpitudinem fugimus in statu et motu corporis, quid est cur pulchritudinem non sequamur?
examples.translation: And if we avoid ugliness in bodily movement and posture, why should we not pursue beauty?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Atque his tribus generibus honestorum notatis, quartum sequitur et in eadem pulchritudine et aptum ex illis tribus, in quo inest ordo et moderatio.
examples.translation: These three kinds of moral goodness being noted, there follows a fourth kind, possessed of equal beauty, and indeed arising out of the other three. This is the principle of order and of restraint.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Erat tum inter equites tribunus militum A. Cornelius Cossus, eximia pulchritudine corporis, animo ac viribus par memorque generis, quod amplissimum acceptum maius auctiusque reliquit posteris.
examples.translation: There was at that time among the cavalrymen a tribune of the soldiers named Aulus Cornelius Cossus, a man of strikingly handsome person and no less distinguished for courage and strength.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: soundness of body, health
English: banishment, exile.

examples.original: Volscius damnatus Lanuvium in exsilium abiit.
examples.translation: Volscius was condemned and went into exile at Lanuvium.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cadaver eius clam in hortos Lamianos asportatum et tumultuario rogo semiambustum levi caespite obrutum est, postea per sorores ab exsilio reversas erutum et crematum sepultumque.
examples.translation: His body was conveyed secretly to the gardens of the Lamian family, where it was partly consumed on a hastily erected pyre and buried beneath a light covering of turf;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Quid est aliud quam exsilium intra eadem moenia, quam relegationem pati?
examples.translation: What else is this but to suffer exile within the same walls and banishment?
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a priest in Spain in the time of Constantine the Great, who made a metrical version of the four Gospels

examples.original: Aspicis, ut prensos urant iuga prima iuvencos, Et nova velocem cingula laedat equum?
examples.translation: Do you see how the first yoke chafes the captured bullocks, how the new saddle hurts the flying steed?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to support with pales, stakes, or props; to prop up

examples.original: Ea quamquam similia veris erant, certius tamen exploranda ratus dimittit equites, qui vagos praedatores in agris palantes intercipiant;
examples.translation: These reports were plausible enough; nevertheless he thought it right to obtain more authentic information.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: open, opened
Latin: apertus < aperiō

examples.original: Servatur poenas in aperta luce daturus;
examples.translation: So he was spared, to suffer in the light of day;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Omnia enim vitia in aperto leniora sunt;
examples.translation: For all unconcealed vices are less serious;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed quid attinet de rebus tam apertis plura requirere?
examples.translation: But what is the point of inquiring further into matters so obvious?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the spoil of an animal, i. e. the skin or hide of an animal stripped off

examples.original: Spolia opima Feretrio Iovi lata.
examples.translation: Spolia opima dedicated to Jupiter Feretrius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Bellum cum Vulscis gessit et ex spoliis eorum templum in Capitolio Iovi fecit.
examples.translation: He waged war with the Volsci, and out of their spoils built a temple to Jupiter on the Capitol.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nuda quidem tunc sum, nudam tamen expedit esse, Non spolium de me quod petat hostis habet.
examples.translation: Then indeed am I naked, yet to be naked is an advantage; I have no spoil to tempt an enemy.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a wing, as of a bird: galli plausu premunt alas, Enn. ap.
Latin: Pars avis, qui volatur
Latin: Latus exercitus

examples.original: Non avis utiliter viscatis effugit alis;
examples.translation: The bird cannot make good its escape when once its wings are limed;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Capitur praefectus alae Iulius Flavianus;
examples.translation: Julius Flavianus, prefect of a squadron, was captured;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Et movet ipse suas, et nati respicit alas Daedalus, et cursus sustinet usque suos.
examples.translation: Daedalus, while he plies his own, looks back at his son’s wings, and ever keeps on his own course.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: the first, first

examples.original: Primores castrorum nomen atque imagines Vitellii amoliuntur;
examples.translation: The chief officers removed the name and statues of Vitellius from headquarters;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Blaeso super claritatem natalium et elegantiam morum fidei obstinatio fuit. Integris quoque rebus a Caecina et primoribus partium iam Vitellium aspernantibus ambitus abnuere perseveravit.
examples.translation: Even while the position of Vitellius was still unshaken, he had been solicited by Caecina and the party leaders who already despised the emperor, but he persisted in rejecting their advances.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Inde L. Tarquinius regnare occepit, cui Superbo cognomen facta indiderunt, quia socerum gener sepultura prohibuit, Romulum quoque insepultum perisse dictitans, primoresque patrum, quos Servi rebus favisse credebat, interfecit;
examples.translation: For he denied the rites of sepulture to his own father-in-law, asserting that Romulus had also perished without burial.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a round body, a ball, sphere, globe.
Latin: Corpus rotundum; sphaera, pila

examples.original: Messium impetus per stratos caede hostes cum globo fortissimorum iuvenum extulit ad castra Volscorum, quae nondum capta erant.
examples.translation: Messius pressed on with a band of courageous youths over the slain bodies of his enemies, and reached the Volscian camp, which had not yet been taken;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: ho! hello! hark!
English: fine, not thick or coarse, thin, slender

examples.original: Hoc tam perplexum et subtile et vobis quoque vix enarrabile quomodo infans intellegit?
examples.translation: But how can a child comprehend this intricate and subtle principle, which I can scarcely explain even to you?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a crier, herald, in a court of justice, in popular assemblies, at auctions, at public spectacles, games, or processions, etc.: exsurge, praeco, fac populo audientiam, Enn. ap.

examples.original: Fraus deinde rem inclinavit, quod vocem audiri praeconis passi sunt, incolumem abiturum qui arma posuisset.
examples.translation: The hope of this relaxed the tension of their courage and on every side they began throwing their arms away.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quo simul ventum est, praeco ad tribunum celerum, in quo tum magistratu forte Brutus erat, populum advocavit.
