examples.translation: No sooner were they there than a crier summoned the people before the Tribune of the Celeres, which office Brutus then happened to be holding.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ab isto et praeco qui voluit istum ordinem pretio mercatus est, et pueri annorum senum septenumque denum senatorium nomen nundinati sunt;
examples.translation: Verres was bribed to sell the title to an auctioneer who wanted it; from Verres boys of sixteen and seventeen purchased the rank of senator.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the signs of manhood, i. e. the hair which appears on the body at the age of puberty, Gr.
English: to feed with any thing

examples.original: Illi statim ante aciem inmolato equo concepere votum, ut caesorum extis ducum et litarent et vescerentur.
examples.translation: I can well believe that the gods heard their boast, for they would not even endure the sound of our trumpets.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: wise, judicious; a wise person, sage

examples.original: Quorum nihil sapienti viro potest evenire;
examples.translation: But none of these things can happen to the sage;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quomodo hoc fiat, sapientia sola monstrabit.
examples.translation: And wisdom alone can show you how this may be done.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Omnes qui non sint sapientes aeque miseros esse;
examples.translation: That those who are not wise are all equally wretched;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to call out or forth, to bring out: exciet, excutiet, Paul. ex

examples.original: Ea res ab stativis excivit Mettium.
examples.translation: This move drew Mettius out from his fortifications.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vitellius ut e somno excitus Iulium Priscum et Alfenum Varum cum quattuordecim praetoriis cohortibus et omnibus equitum alis obsidere Appenninum iubet;
examples.translation: Vitellius was like a man wakened from a deep sleep. He ordered Julius Priscus and Alfenus Varus to block the passes of the Apennines with fourteen praetorian cohorts and all the cavalry.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ibi Verginius maiorem quam reliquerat in urbe motum excivit.
examples.translation: There Verginius aroused a greater commotion than he had left in Rome.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to bring forth, bring to light, raise up (very rare; mostly with se, or pass. in mid. sense), to come forth
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; si, sum, 3

examples.original: Nemo per se satis valet ut emergat;
examples.translation: No man by himself has sufficient strength to rise above it;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Aut quia crassior est certis in partibus aer, sub terris ideo tremulum iubar haesitat ignis nec penetrare potest facile atque emergere ad ortus;
examples.translation: Or else because the air is thicker in certain parts, therefore under the earth the trembling gleam of his fire hesitates, and cannot easily penetrate and come forth to its rising;
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Nascuntur et alio modo terrae ac repente in aliquo mari emergunt, velut paria secum faciente natura quaeque hauserit hiatus alio loco reddente.
examples.translation: Land is sometimes formed in a different manner, rising suddenly out of the sea, as if nature was compensating the earth for its losses, restoring in one place what she had swallowed up in another.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: a stretching out, straining, tension.

examples.original: Nec tu intentionem vocis contempseris, quam veto te per gradus et certos modos extollere, deinde deprimere.
examples.translation: You need not scorn voice-culture; but I forbid you to practise raising and lowering your voice by scales and specific intonations.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nam si modo tanta cura, tanta intentione, tanto labore agitis ne in aliquos cruciatus transitorios incidatis, quantum vos oportet esse sollicitos, ut sempiternas miserias fugiatis!
examples.translation: And if the death which ends the toil of this life inspires such fear, how greatly that death is to be feared which casts men into everlasting pain!
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a. [kindred with experior, from perior, whence peritus].

examples.original: Bassus pudore seu metu, quisnam exitus foret, intra domum opperiebatur.
examples.translation: Bassus waited in his quarters, prompted by shame or by fear as to the outcome.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to mount, to ascend (in prose rare before the Aug. per.)
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; ndi, nsum, 3

examples.original: Duas personas habet gubernator: alteram communem cum omnibus, qui eandem conscenderunt navem: ipse quoque vector est;
examples.translation: A pilot has a double rôle: one he shares with all his fellow-passengers, for he also is a passenger;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Postquam rogationis dies aderat, ingenti stipatus agmine rostra conscendit, nec deerat obvia manu tota inde nobilitas;
examples.translation: When the day for bringing forward the bill was at hand, he ascended the rostra surrounded by a large following;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Caesar His constitutis rebus nactus idoneam ad navigandum tempestatem tertia fere vigilia solvit equitesque in ulteriorem portum progredi et naves conscendere et se sequi iussit.
examples.translation: These arrangements made, he caught a spell of fair weather for sailing, and weighed anchor about the third watch: he ordered the cavalry to proceed to the further harbour, embark, and follow him.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to speak to or accost one, to address; hence, also, to treat of or negotiate a matter with one
Latin: Ad aliquem orare
Latin: Petere, rogare; praesertim ab dis
English: to thirst, be thirsty (class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; īvi or ĭi, 4

examples.original: Omne animal terrestre alget, esurit, sitit;
examples.translation: Now every earthly living thing gets cold or hungry or thirsty;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et doleas oportet et sitias et esurias et senescas, si tibi longior contigerit inter homines mora, et aegrotes et perdas aliquid et pereas.
examples.translation: You must suffer pain, and thirst, and hunger, and old age too, if a longer stay among men shall be granted you; you must be sick, and you must suffer loss and death.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: firmly, immovably; steadily, constantly, without change; resolutely

examples.original: Quod enim deo pari consensu ambo voveratis, perseveranter usque in finem reddere ambo debuistis, a quo proposito si lapsus est ille, tu saltem constantissime persevera.
examples.translation: So now in this problem of yours the question is not involved whether you ought to return to intercourse with your husband;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a beast for sacrifice adorned with the fillet (vitta), a sacrifice, victim (cf. hostia).

examples.original: Qui Martem terra, Neptunum effugit in undis, Coniugis Atrides victima dira fuit.
examples.translation: Atreus, who escaped Mars on land and Neptune on the deep, was the dire victim of his wife.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Pari in meliora praesagio in Caesaris castris omnia aves victimaeque promiserant.
examples.translation: In Caesar’s camp birds and victims had with equal clearness given every promise of better fortune.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Legatos quippe nostros, ob ea quae deliquerant iure agentes, ne gladio quidem, sed ut victimas securi percutiunt, praefectos navium igne comburunt;
examples.translation: To make their action still more insulting, it was a woman that gave the order.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: That is nourished, brought up; for the most part

examples.original: Propter opes magnas ut perdidit hospes alumnum, Perdat ob exiguas te tuus hospes opes.
examples.translation: As the host slew his ward for his great wealth, so for thy little wealth may thy host slay thee.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Itaque illa non dico me expetere sed legere, nec optare sed sumere, contraria autem non fugere sed quasi secernere’ Quid ait Aristoteles reliquique Platonis alumni?
examples.translation: Do you see therefore that between your master Zeno and Aristo there is a verbal harmony but a real difference;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ulline Italiae alumni et Romana vere iuventus ad sanguinem et caedem depoposcerit ordinem, cuius splendore et gloria sordis et obscuritatem Vitellianarum partium praestringimus ?
examples.translation: Shall any child of Italy, any true Roman youth, demand the blood and murder of that order through whose splendid glory we outshine the meanness and base birth of the partisans of Vitellius?
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to take a little from any thing.

examples.original: Id erat liber aliquis antiquus pulcher aut rarior.
examples.translation: This was some old book, either beautiful or rare.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Secum habet ingenium, qui, cum libet, ”accipe” dicit;
examples.translation: I give place: my devices will not please so much as he.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Tum pulsus Etruria Libo, Vmbria Thermus, Domitius Corfinio.
examples.translation: Libo was driven out of Etruria, Thermus from Umbria, Domitius from Corfinium.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a joining together, connecting, uniting; union, conjunction.
Latin: pars orationis; verbum ut et vel autem
Latin: Actus coniungendi

examples.original: Ipsi quoque ad syllabarum distinctiones et coniunctionum ac praepositionum proprietates descenderunt et invidere grammaticis, invidere geometris.
examples.translation: Of their own accord they also have descended to establishing nice divisions of syllables, to determining the true meaning of conjunctions and prepositions;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Daughter of the Phoenician king Agenor, sister of Cadmus, and mother of Sarpedon and Minos by Jupiter, who, under the form of a bull, carried her off to Crete
Latin: filia Agenoris Regis Phoenicum, quam Iupiter, in bovis speciem transformatus, rapuit
Latin: continens, pars occidentalis Eurasiae
English: brotherly, fraternal.

examples.original: Sese tamen et amore fraterno et existimatione vulgi commoveri.
examples.translation: For all that, I feel the force of brotherly love and public opinion.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: liver; (food/medicine/divination/seat of feelings)
English: a mine or quarry, of gold, silver, iron, or stone
Latin: Fodina
Latin: Res quae ex fodina fossatur, ut, aurum, argentum, ferrum

examples.original: Levium metallorum fructus in summo est;
examples.translation: The yield of poor mines is on the surface;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Si Herculem vestrum dixeritis, porro reddemus; adsunt metalla, saxa nec desunt;
examples.translation: If you mention your Hercules, we shall straightway restore it to you;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: seventy
Latin: Septies dena. Numerus LXX

examples.original: Caesa ibi milia hominum duo ferme atque octingenti, capta quattuor milia ducenti septuaginta.
examples.translation: There about two thousand eight hundred men were slain and four thousand two hundred and seventy made prisoners.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Comprehensae extemplo earum comites magnum numerum matronarum indicaverunt; ex quibus ad centum septuaginta damnatae.
examples.translation: Their attendants being instantly arrested informed against a large number of matrons, of whom one hundred and seventy were found guilty;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Secunda classis intra centum usque ad quinque et septuaginta milium censum instituta, et ex iis, senioribus iunioribusque, viginti conscriptae centuriae.
examples.translation: The second class was drawn up out of those whose rating was between a hundred thousand and seventy-five thousand;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the office and dignity of a tribune, the tribuneship

examples.original: Ergo si esset libera haec civitas, non tibi frequentes succlamassent, ’abi hinc cum tribunatibus ac rogationibus tuis!’ Quid?
examples.translation: If you will not propose what is profitable to the people to accept, shall there be none to do it?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Reliqua iam praecipitantis tribunatus etiam post tribunatum obtrectatores eorum atque adversarii defenderunt, ne a re publica rei publicae pestis removeretur restiterunt, etiam ne causam diceret, etiam ne privatus esset.
examples.translation: The remaining acts of his tribunate, when it had begun to rush headlong upon ruin, were defended, even after he was tribune no longer, by the belittlers and opponentscof those whom I have just mentioned;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a circular figure, a circle: circulus aut orbis, qui
English: to set fire to, to kindle, to set in a flame, to burn, singe, scorch (cf. accendo), etc.
Latin: Accendere
English: honor, repute, esteem

examples.original: Ei mihi, non multum carmen honoris habet.
examples.translation: Alas, a poem is not much honoured.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Memoriae Domiti patris honores maximos habuit.
examples.translation: He paid the highest honours to the memory of his father Domitius.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: O quando ille veniet dies, quo nemo in honorem tuum mentiatur!
examples.translation: O when will that time come, when no one shall tell lies to compliment you!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Big/Little Dipper (s./pl.); north, north regions/wind; brooch w/7 stones
Latin: pluralis numerus: Septem stellae in constellatione stellari Ursae Maioris
Latin: singularis: Ventus qui ex regionibus septentrionalibus flat

examples.original: Aquitania a Garumna flumine ad Pyrenaeos montes et eam partem Oceani quae est ad Hispaniam pertinet; spectat inter occasum solis et septentriones.
examples.translation: Aquitania, starting from the Garonne, reaches to the Pyrenees and to that part of the Ocean which is by Spain: its bearing is between west and north.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Bellvm Parthicvm III, 11Dum Gallos per Caesarem in septentrione debellat, ipse interim ad orientem grave volnus a Parthis populus Romanus accepit.
examples.translation: The Parthian War 11. While in the north the Roman people by the hand of Caesar were conquering the Gauls, in the east they received a serious blow from the Parthians.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: clean

examples.original: Quod enim vis, ut ad te prolixam epistulam scribam, et hoc quidem debeo, fateor; debeo prorsus hoc tam dulci, tam sincerae, tam merae voluntati tuae.
examples.translation: Yet, when you want me to write you a lengthy letter, I do indeed owe you that, I must confess: I surely do owe that to your sweet, sincere, and single-minded desire.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Ad quod negotium mihi parvum tempus velut usque ad pascha impetrare volui per fratres a tua sincerissima et venerabili caritate et nunc per has preces volo.
examples.translation: It was for this task that I sought through my brethren to obtain from your dear Reverence a short space of time, say until Easter, and to that I now add this present supplication.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: staring, keen, piercing, wild, stern; hence, in gen., wild, fierce, grim, gloomy, savage, in aspect or character

examples.original: Ut fuerit torva violentior illa Medusa, Fiet amatori lenis et aequa suo.
examples.translation: Though she be more violent than grim Medusa, she will be mild and gentle to her lover.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Statura fuit eminenti, colore expallido, corpore enormi, gracilitate maxima cervicis et crurum, oculis et temporibus concavis, fronte lata et torva, capillo raro at circa verticem nullo, hirsutus cetera.
examples.translation: His eyes and temples were hollow, his forehead broad and grim, his hair thin and entirely gone on the top of his head, though his body was hairy.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: the very fruitful and luxurious

examples.original: Quare non est quod existimes ideo parum bene conpositum esse te, quod in Campania non es.
examples.translation: For this reason you should not refuse to believe that your life is well-placed merely because you are not now in Campania.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Iam Misenensem classem et pulcherrimam Campaniae oram descivisse, nec plus e toto terrarum orbe reliquum Vitellio quam quod inter Tarracinam Narniamque iaceat.
examples.translation: The fleet at Misenum and the lovely district of Campania have already deserted Vitellius, and he now has nothing left out of the whole world but the land that lies between Tarracina and Narnia.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Huic et divus Augustus dedit secreta mandata, cum illum praeponeret Thraciae, quam perdomuit, et Tiberius proficiscens in Campaniam, cum multa in urbe et suspecta relinqueret et invisa.
examples.translation: Tiberius, too, trusted him when he took his holiday in Campania, leaving behind him in the city many a critical matter that aroused both suspicion and hatred.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to cling together, to be united, either of that whose parts cling together, to cohere, or of that which cleaves to something else, to adhere.
English: a delighting, delight, pleasure, amusement (freq. and good prose)

examples.original: Et tamen vehementer cum adversario dimicans saepe ab eo vulnera accipio, cum delectationem oblatae laudis mihi auferre non possum.
examples.translation: Yet, strenuously as I struggle with the adversary, I often receive wounds from him, since I cannot rid myself of delight in the praise that is offered me.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a going or coming to or near, an approach.
Latin: Factum accedendi
Latin: Factum accedendi. Quid igitur hunc paucorum annorum accessio iuvare potuisset? (Laelius Ciceronis)

examples.original: Omnia enim alia non partes, sed accessiones sunt.
examples.translation: For all other things are not parts, but merely accessories.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Octo nimirum legiones unius classis accessionem fore.
examples.translation: No doubt eight legions are to go over to one poor fleet!
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Si, ut tu dicis, gratiae conciliandae causa, quadraginta istorum accessio milium quid valet?
examples.translation: If, as you maintain, it was to effect a reconciliation, what is the point of the odd forty thousand?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a pine, pine-tree; a fir, fir-tree: Pinus silvestris, Linn.
Latin: Species arboris generis Pinus
Latin: lignum eius arboris
English: a sea-robber, corsair, pirate (syn. praedo)
Latin: Praedo maritimus

examples.original: Sic per omnis aequoris portus, sinus, latebras, recessus, promontoria, freta, paeninsulas quidquid piratarum fuit quadam indagine inclusum est.
examples.translation: Thus, in every harbour, bay, shelter, creek, promontory, strait and peninsula in the sea, every single pirate was enclosed as it were in a net.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to take a stand or position, to stand still, remain standing; to stop, halt.

examples.original: Quare enim qui labi coepit, alicubi subsistat?
examples.translation: For how, if one has begun to slip, can one stop at any particular place?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ad omne fortuitum bonum suspiciosi pavidique subsistite;
examples.translation: Halt before every good which Chance brings to you, in a spirit of doubt and fear;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Consules ambo profecti sint ad arcem Carventanam, an alter ad comitia habenda substiterit, incertum diversi auctores faciunt;
examples.translation: The levy was then begun and preparation made for war, with the consent of all the orders.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to conquer completely, overcome, subdue.

examples.original: Volscis devictis Veliternus ager ademptus;
examples.translation: The Volsci, having been conquered, were deprived of the Veliternian land;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Eo anno Hernici devicti: cum Volscis aequo Marte discessum est.
examples.translation: This year the Hernici were conquered, while the campaign against the Volsci was indecisive.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Servius Tullius Veientes devicit et populum in classes divisit, aedem Dianae dedicavit.
examples.translation: Servius Tullius conquered the Veientes and divided the people into classes; dedicated a temple to Diana.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a shipwreck.

examples.original: Hoc consilio per conscios parum celato solutilem navem, cuius vel naufragio vel camarae ruina periret, commentus est atque ita reconciliatione simulata iucundissimis litteris Baias evocavit ad sollemnia Quinquatruum simul celebranda;
examples.translation: When this leaked out through some of those connected with the plot, he devised a collapsible boat, to destroy her by shipwreck or by the falling in of its cabin.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: faint, weak, dull, sluggish, languid (class.; cf.: lassus, fessus, fatigatus, defessus).

examples.original: Cum vero cessit voluptati, artes quoque eius actusque marcent et omnis e X languido fluidoque conatus est.
examples.translation: And when the soul has yielded to pleasure, its functions and actions grow weak, and any undertaking comes from a nerveless and unsteady source.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Chaereae contra, tribuno militum, sermo non pro manu erat, languidus sono et, ni facta nosses, suspectior.
examples.translation: On the other hand, Chaerea, a tribune of the soldiers, had a way of talking that ill-accorded with his prowess;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quippe suspectior illis quam morbo pallentibus color est, languidi et evanidi albent, et in vivis caro morticina est.
examples.translation: Their complexions are more alarming than those of anaemic invalids; they are lackadaisical and flabby with dropsy;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: closeness, come
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; xi, ctum, and anxum, 3

examples.original: Haec dicta vulgo creditaque cum indignitate angerent consulis animum, vocato ad concilium populo submissis fascibus in contionem escendit.
examples.translation: He summoned the people to a council, and with lowered fasces mounted the speaker’s platform.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quarta restat causa, quae maxime angere atque sollicitam habere nostram aetatem videtur, appropinquatio mortis, quae certe a senectute non potest esse longe.
examples.translation: It remains to consider now the fourth reason—one that seems especially calculated to render my time of life anxious and full of care—the nearness of death;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ea conluvio mixtorum omnis generis animantium et odore insolito urbanos et agrestem confertum in arta tecta aestu ac vigiliis angebat, ministeriaque in vicem ac contagio ipsa volgabant morbos.
examples.translation: This conflux of all kinds of living things distressed the citizens with its strange smells, while the country-people, being packed into narrow quarters, suffered greatly from the heat and want of sleep;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a blood-vessel, vein.

examples.original: Cernit tabe iecur madidum, venasque minaces Hostili de parte videt.
examples.translation: He saw the liver flabby with corruption and with boding streaks in its hostile half.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Hinc, Abaton quam nostra vocat veneranda vetustas, †Terra potens† primos sentit percussa tumultus, Et scopuli, placuit fluvii quos dicere venas, Quod manifesta novi primum dant signa tumoris.
examples.translation: Here too are the rocks which are commonly called the springs of the river, because they give the first clear indication when the water begins to rise.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to join one with another, to connect, unite
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Paci externae confestim continuatur discordia domi.
examples.translation: The foreign peace was immediately succeeded by quarrels at home.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Dimisimus catechumenos continuoque scriptum subscripsit.
examples.translation: We dismissed the catechumensa and straightway he subscribed the statement.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Omnis oratio aut continua est aut inter respondentem et interrogantem discissa.
examples.translation: Now all speech is either continuous, or split up between questioner and answerer.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: one that goes to something in order to see or hear it; hence
Latin: Testis, quae rem gesta visit
Latin: Qui rei iudicando designatus est
English: That happens by chance, accidental, casual
Latin: fortuitus, accidentalis
Latin: remissus, casualis, neglegens

examples.original: Hominem esse barbarum, iracundum, temerarium: non posse eius imperia diutius sustinere.
examples.translation: He is a passionate, a reckless barbarian: we can endure his tyrannies no longer.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: At ille temeraria usus ratione non cessit maiorum natu auctoritati, velut in sua manu esset fortuna.
examples.translation: But Chares, adopting a bold course, did not heed the advice of his elders, believing that he was the master of fortune.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timotheus

definitions: English: lock, bar, bolt; barrier

examples.original: Quid tum claustra montium profutura?
examples.translation: In that case, what will the mountain barriers avail us?
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Non est quod existimes magnis tantum viris hoc robur fuisse, quo servitutis humanae claustra perrumperent;
examples.translation: You need not think that none but great men have had the strength to burst the bonds of human servitude;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Suscepto igitur civili bello ac ducibus copiisque in Italiam praemissis interim Alexandriam transiit, ut claustra Aegypti optineret.
examples.translation: Therefore beginning a civil war and sending ahead generals with troops to Italy, he crossed meanwhile to Alexandria, to take possession of the key to Egypt.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: Britain
Latin: Insula in mari Germanico
Latin: Provincia Romana antiqua

examples.original: Caesar Atrebas venit, quem supra demonstraveram a Caesare in Britanniam praemissum.
examples.translation: Commius the Atrebatian, who, as shown above, had been sent forward by Caesar into Britain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Huius opera Commi, ut antea demonstravimus, fideli atque utili superioribus annis erat usus in Britannia Caesar;
examples.translation: This Commius, as we have before mentioned, had rendered faithful and efficient service to Caesar in previous years in the expedition to Britain.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Duas validissimas gentes superque viginti oppida et insulam Vectem Britanniae proximam in dicionem redegit partim Auli Plauti legati consularis partim Claudi ipsius ductu.
examples.translation: He reduced to subjection two powerful nations, more than twenty towns, and the island of Vectis, near Britain, partly under the leadership of Aulus Plautius, the consular governor, and partly under that of Claudius himself.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to cleave or stick to a thing.

examples.original: Sapiens adsectatorque sapientiae adhaeret quidem in corpore suo, sed optima sui parte abest et cogitationes suas ad sublimia intendit. Velut sacramento rogatus hoc, quod vivit, stipendium putat.
examples.translation: The wise man, the seeker after wisdom, is bound closely, indeed, to his body, but he is an absentee so far as his better self is concerned, and he concentrates his thoughts upon lofty things.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to shear, clip, crop, to shave, etc.

examples.original: Inclita Caesareis Genabos dissolvitur alis.\] Tu quoque laetatus converti proelia, Trevir, Et nunc tonse Ligur, quondam per colla decore Crinibus effusis toti praelate Comatae;
examples.translation: The Treviri too rejoiced that the troops were moved; so did the Ligurians with hair now cropped, though once they excelled all the longhaired land in the locks that fell in beauty over their necks;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a comparing, comparison (in good prose).
English: of or belonging to grammar, grammatical

examples.original: Quattuor milia librorum Didymus grammaticus scripsit.
examples.translation: Didymus the scholar wrote four thousand books.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Reliquit filium Orbilium, et ipsum grammaticum professorem.
examples.translation: He left a son Orbilius, who was also a teacher of grammar.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Aurelius Opillus, Epicurei cuiusdam libertus, philosophiam primo, deinde rhetoricam, novissime grammaticam docuit.
examples.translation: Aurelius Opilius, freedman of an Epicurean, first taught philosophy, afterwards rhetoric, and finally grammar.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: to build of wood (rare but class.)

examples.original: Hoc causa est, illud materia.
examples.translation: The former is its material, the latter its cause.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ex quo fit: haec materia est.
examples.translation: The agent is God; the source, matter;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: De homine dixi, fluvida materia et caduca et omnibus obnoxia causis;
examples.translation: So much for man,—a substance that flows away and falls, exposed to every influence;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: freedom, liberty, leave to do as one pleases, license.

examples.original: In primis tuendae pacis a grassaturis ac latrociniis seditionumque licentia curam habuit.
examples.translation: He gave special attention to securing safety from highway banditry and lawless outbreaks.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: In civitate discordi et ob crebras principum mutationes inter libertatem ac licentiam incerta parvae quoque res magnis motibus agebantur.
examples.translation: In a state distracted by civil strife and wavering between liberty and licence because of the frequent changes of emperors, even smaller matters caused excitement.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Maxima laus illi tribuitur mansuetudinis, pepercit gladio, sanguine abstinuit nec ulla alia re, quid posset, quam licentia ostendit;
examples.translation: To be sure, we bestow upon him the highest praise for his humanity;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the bottom of any thing (class.).

examples.original: De castello descendunt, in fundum proficiscuntur.
examples.translation: Leaving the castle they set out for the estate.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quaero abs te, simne deiectus: non de Fulciniano fundo;
examples.translation: I ask you, was I driven out?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum exsectio illa fundi in armario animadverteretur, quaerebant homines quonam modo fieri potuisset.
examples.translation: The theft was discovered next day, and the entire suspicion fell on the two slaves who were not forthcoming.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of or belonging to the market or
English: a feather on the body of a winged creature (syn. pluma).
English: to keep back, save up, qs. for future use; to reserve (very freq. and class.; cf. repono); constr.: aliquid (aliquem) ad aliquid, in aliquid, alicui, with a terminal

examples.original: Nam Claudium patruum non nisi in ludibrium reservavit.
examples.translation: As for his uncle Claudius, he spared him merely as a laughingstock.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Id exhauriri aliis potius patimur, ut nobis faecem reservemus?
examples.translation: Let this phrase cleave to your soul;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fabium illis Valentem, captivum et casibus dubiis reservatum, praegravem fuisse, nedum Primus ac Fuscus et specimen partium Mucianus ullam in Vitellium nisi occidendi licentiam habeant.
examples.translation: Will Primus and Fuscus or that leading representative of their party, Mucianus, have any liberty in dealing with you except the liberty of killing? Caesar did not leave Pompey unharmed or Augustus Antony.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: of himself, of herself, of itself, of themselves; one another, each other, etc.

examples.original: Sed ad bella externa prope supererant vires, abutebanturque iis inter semet ipsos certando.
examples.translation: But for foreign wars there was almost a superabundance of resources, and men misused them in quarrelling amongst themselves.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Praecipiti in occasum die ob pavorem magistratuum senatorumque, qui dilapsi ex urbe aut per domos clientium semet occultabant, vocari senatus non potuit.
examples.translation: The day hurried to its close. It was impossible to summon the senate because the senators had stolen away from the city or were hiding in their clients’ houses.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a syllable.

examples.original: Syllaba autem caseum non rodit;
examples.translation: Now a syllable does not eat cheese.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ipsi quoque ad syllabarum distinctiones et coniunctionum ac praepositionum proprietates descenderunt et invidere grammaticis, invidere geometris.
examples.translation: Of their own accord they also have descended to establishing nice divisions of syllables, to determining the true meaning of conjunctions and prepositions;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a tortoise.
Latin: Reptile qui habet carapacem ornatam
Latin: Carapax testudinis

examples.original: At milites legionis septimae, testudine facta et aggere ad munitiones adiecto, locum ceperunt eosque ex silvis expulerunt paucis vulneribus acceptis.
examples.translation: The enemy came out of the woods to fight in small groups, and sought to prevent our troops from entering the fortifications.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Testudinum putamina secare in laminas lectosque et repositoria iis vestire Carvilius Pollio instituit, prodigi et sagacis ad luxuriae instrumenta ingenii.
examples.translation: Carvilius Pollio, a man of prodigal habits and ingenious in inventing the refinements of luxury, was the first to cut the shell of the tortoise into laminæ, and to veneer beds and cabinets with it.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: she that is victorious, a conqueress, victress; adj., conquering, victorious.
Latin: Femina victoriosa
Latin: Qui vincit, victoriosus

examples.original: Praesto fuere Luguduni victricium victarumque partium duces.
examples.translation: At Lugudunum the generals of both sides, the victors and the defeated, awaited him.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Interea domitis Caesar remeabat Hiberis Victrices aquilas alium laturus in orbem, Cum prope fatorum tantos per prospera cursus Avertere dei.
examples.translation: Meanwhile Caesar was returning triumphant over conquered Spain to carry into a new world his victorious eagles, when the flowing tide of his successes was almost turned aside by Heaven.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Thrace
Latin: Regio vicina Macedoniae Moesiaeque. In hac area est urbs Byzantii

examples.original: Huic et divus Augustus dedit secreta mandata, cum illum praeponeret Thraciae, quam perdomuit, et Tiberius proficiscens in Campaniam, cum multa in urbe et suspecta relinqueret et invisa.
examples.translation: Tiberius, too, trusted him when he took his holiday in Campania, leaving behind him in the city many a critical matter that aroused both suspicion and hatred.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: that holds fast, that clings firmly, very tenacious.

examples.original: Nihil est, quod non expugnet pertinax opera et intenta ac diligens cura;
examples.translation: There is nothing that will not surrender to persistent treatment, to concentrated and careful attention;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to form into a heap, to accumulate, heap, or pile up (class.).

examples.original: Id cumulatum usuris primo se agro paterno avitoque exuisse, deinde fortunis aliis, postremo velut tabem pervenisse ad corpus;
examples.translation: Then the taxes had been levied, in an untoward moment for him, and he had contracted debts.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et paucorum dierum iter progressus prosperas apud Bedriacum res ac morte Othonis concidisse bellum accepit: vocata contione virtutem militum laudibus cumulat.
examples.translation: After he had advanced a few days, he heard of the success at Bedriacum and learned that at Otho’s death the war had collapsed;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: an awaiting, expecting, expectation

examples.original: In qua nunc exspectatione senatum populumque Campanum, coniuges liberosque nostros esse?
examples.translation: In what suspense are now the senate and the people of Campania, our wives and our children!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Erat hominum conventus maximus, summum silentium, summa exspectatio quonam esset eius cupiditas eruptura;
examples.translation: There was a great crowd present—dead silence—breathless anxiety as to what line of attack his greed would adopt.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Profectus cum exercitu ab urbe exspectatione hominum maiore quam spe in agro primum Nepesino cum Faliscis et Capenatibus signa confert.
examples.translation: Marching out from the City, where he left a greater feeling of suspense than of confidence, he first engaged the Faliscans and Capenates, in the Nepesine country.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: barley
Latin: Genus frumenti
English: displeasure, indignation, disdain.

examples.original: Nec raptis aut spes de se melior aut indignatio est minor.
examples.translation: The stolen maidens were no more hopeful of their plight, nor less indignant.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the front part of the body between the hips.
English: the muscle which separates the heart and lungs from the abdomen, the midriff, diaphragm

examples.original: Non opus est vasto vulnere dividere praecordia;
examples.translation: If you would pierce your heart, a gaping wound is not necessary;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Carmine Thessalidum dura in praecordia fluxit Non fatis adductus amor, flammisque severi Inlicitis arsere senes.
examples.translation: By their spells love steals into insensible hearts against the decree of destiny, and austere old age burns with forbidden passion.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: oaktree, esp. the Italian or esculent oak, sacred to Jupiter (cf. robur): quercus dicitur, quod id genus arboris grave sit ac durum, tum etiam in ingentem evadat amplitudinem
Latin: Quoddam genus arboris
English: Of or belonging to breathing, to wind, or
English: to cover before or in front, to cover over, cover, protect (class.; syn.: defendo, tutor).

examples.original: Trachalum adversus criminantis Galeria uxor Vitellii protexit.
examples.translation: Trachalus was protected against his accusers by Galeria, the wife of Vitellius.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to give one's assent to a thing

examples.original: Et hunc licet dicas non minus quam Socraten in servis se libertati addixisse, nisi forte Cn. Pompeium et Caesarem et Crassum putas libertatis socios fuisse.
examples.translation: And you may say that he, just as much as Socrates, declared allegiance to liberty in the midst of slavery—unless perchance you think that Pompey, Caesar, and Crassusa were the allies of liberty!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quod cum Deiotarus religione sua castissime tueretur, quem unum habemus in orbe terrarum fidelissimum huic imperio atque amantissimum nostri nominis, Brogitaro, ut ante dixi, addictum pecunia tradidisti.
examples.translation: The former, however, owes his kingly title, through us, to the senatorial pronouncement, while Brogitarus owes his, through you, to the price which he paid you.a . .
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: come back; to turn back, return (class.; syn.: revertor, redeo).

examples.original: Eum autem, cum modo regressus sum, periculosissime scandalizatum comperi de absentia mea;
examples.translation: When I returned recently, I found them offended to a very dangerous degree at my absence.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Vixdum regresso in Capitolium Martiale furens miles aderat, nullo duce, sibi quisque auctor.
examples.translation: Martialis had hardly returned to the Capitol when the soldiers arrived in fury. They had no leader;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: the beard, of men
Latin: Pili in vultu viri qui radi solent

examples.original: Quod insigne mansit et in posteris eius, ac magna pars rutila barba fuerunt.
examples.translation: This sign was perpetuated in his descendants, a great part of whom had red beards.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Hominem esse barbarum, iracundum, temerarium: non posse eius imperia diutius sustinere.
examples.translation: He is a passionate, a reckless barbarian: we can endure his tyrannies no longer.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the myrrh-tree, an Arabian tree, of which myrrh was the sap
English: between Delos and Paros, now
English: adapt

examples.original: Qui hoc modo se aptavit, cui vita sua cotidie fuit tota, securus est;
examples.translation: He who has thus prepared himself, he whose daily life has been a rounded whole, is easy in his mind;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Temporis ars medicina fere est: data tempore prosunt, Et data non apto tempore vina nocent.
examples.translation: The art of being timely is almost a medicine: wine timely given helps, untimely, harms.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Illa leget tempus (medici quoque tempora servant) Quo facilis dominae mens sit et apta capi.
examples.translation: She will choose a time (physicians also observe times) when her mistress is in an easy mood and apt for winning.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a lash, whip, scourge

examples.original: Iulianus ad L. Vitellium perductus et verberibus foedatus in ore eius iugulatur.
examples.translation: Julianus was taken before Lucius Vitellius, flogged, and slain before his eyes.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sic invenies servum qui flagellis quam colaphis caedi malit et qui mortem ac verbera tolerabiliora credat quam contumeliosa verba.
examples.translation: And so you will find the slave who would rather be struck with the lash than the fist, who considers stripes and death more endurable than insulting words.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quacumque vagatur, Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellona flagellum, Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, Nox ingens scelerum est;
examples.translation: He visits the corpses that sprawl on the wide plain; with his own hand he staunches the wound that would otherwise pour out all the blood of many a man.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: worthy of belief, credible
Latin: Qui credi potest (dicitur modo de rebus)
Latin: Probābilis

examples.original: Vix credibile memoratu est quantum superbiae socordiaeque Vitellio adoleverit, postquam speculatores e Syria ludaeaque adactum in verba eius Orientem nuntiavere.
examples.translation: The degree to which the insolent pride of Vitellius increased after couriers arrived from Syria and Judea and reported that the East had sworn allegiance to him is almost past belief.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: how long ago? how long? quamdiu id factum est?

examples.original: Quamdiu tibi satis nihil fuerit, ipse aliis non eris.
examples.translation: And as long as nothing satisfies you, you yourself cannot satisfy others.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quamdiu quidem illi licet suo arbitrio res suas ordinare, se contentus est et ducit uxorem;
examples.translation: As long as he is allowed to order his affairs according to his judgment, he is self-sufficient—and marries a wife;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nutriendus est hic pudor, qui quamdiu in animo eius duraverit, aliquis erit bonae spei locus.
examples.translation: This modesty should be fostered; so long as it endures in his soul, there is some room for hope.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: after-rest, i. e. rest, repose from labor, suffering, care, etc.; relaxation, respite, intermission, recreation

examples.original: Tu concessus amor, tu solus et ultimus illi, Tu requies fesso grata laboris eras.
examples.translation: Thou wert his freely given, his last and only love, thou wert his pleasant repose from weary toil.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ipsius verba sunt: ”Dum veniam ad id tempus, quo vobis aequum possit videri dare vos aliquam senectuti meae requiem.” XXV.
examples.translation: The cause of his hesitation was fear of the dangers which threatened him on every hand, and often led him to say that he was ”holding a wolf by the ears.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Bellvm Ligvricvm II, 3Peracto Punico bello secuta est brevis sane quasi ad recuperandum spiritum requies, argumentumque pacis et bona fide cessantium armorum tum primum post Numam clausa porta Iani fuit;
examples.translation: The Ligurian War 3. The Carthaginian war being ended, a period of rest ensued, brief, indeed, for the Roman people to recover their breath.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: the name of several celebrated Greeks; esp.

examples.original: Tale initium fuit Dionis et Dionysii simultatis, eaque multis rebus aucta est.
examples.translation: Such was the beginning of the hostility between Dion and Dionysius, and it was aggravated by many circumstances.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

examples.original: Hunc a Dionysio missum Karthaginienses suspexerunt, ut neminem umquam Graeca lingua loquentem magis sint admirati.
examples.translation: When he was sent by Dionysius to Carthage, he was so honoured that no native of Greece ever excited greater admiration.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Dion

examples.original: Antonius Gnipho, ingenuus in Gallia natus sed expositus, a nutritore suo manumissus institutusque (Alexandriae quidem, ut aliqui tradunt, in contubernio Dionysi Scytobrachionis;
examples.translation: He was set free by his fosterfather and given an education, at Alexandria, according to some, and in intimate association with Dionysius Scytobrachion; but this I can hardly credit for chronological reasons.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: a proper name.
Latin: species serpentis praesertim serpens fabulosa pinnati
Latin: signum militare
English: especially, chiefly; certainly; most, very much
Latin: Maximō modō

examples.original: Saevitiam ingenii per haec maxime ostendit.
examples.translation: The following are special instances of his innate brutality.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Verrius Flaccus libertinus docendi genere maxime claruit.
examples.translation: Marcus Verrius Flaccus, a freedman, gained special fame by his method of teaching.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Nam in provincias quoque grammatica penetraverat, ac nonnulli de notissimis doctoribus peregre docuerunt, maxime in Gallia Togata; inter quos Octavius Teucer et Sescenius Iaccus et Oppius Chares;
examples.translation: In fact, Grammar even made its way into the provinces, and some of the most famous teachers gave instruction abroad, especially in Gallia Togata, including Octavius Teucer, Sescenius Iaccus and Oppius Chares;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: flit about, to flutter (class.).

examples.original: Est lucum Silari iuxta ilicibusque virentem Plurimus Alburnum volitans, cui nomen asilo Romanum est, oestrum Grai vertere vocantes, Asper, acerba sonans, quo tota exterrita silvis Diffugiunt armenta.
examples.translation: Near Silarus’ groves, and eke Alburnus’ shades Of green-clad oak-trees flits an insect, named Asilus by the Romans;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: The faculty of foreseeing, predicting, divination
English: to seize on the passage before arrival at the destined place, to intercept.

examples.original: Unde existimo nonnullos tradere ausos, suspectum eum Augusto revocatumque ex provincia et quia cunctaretur, interceptum veneno.
examples.translation: This I have mentioned, rather not to pass it by, than that I think it true or even probable;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ea quamquam similia veris erant, certius tamen exploranda ratus dimittit equites, qui vagos praedatores in agris palantes intercipiant;
examples.translation: These reports were plausible enough; nevertheless he thought it right to obtain more authentic information.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mittuntur ad Caesarem confestim ab Cicerone litterae magnis propositis praemiis, si pertulissent: obsessis omnibus viis missi intercipiuntur.
examples.translation: Despatches were at once sent by Cicero to Caesar, with promise of great rewards if the bearers carried them safe;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: for a little while, for a short time (cf. parumper)
English: shamefaced, bashful, modest, chaste, virtuous

examples.original: Virginem ego hanc sum ducturus nuptamque pudicam habiturus.
examples.translation: This maiden I am going to wed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quid tibi nunc mores prosunt actumque pudice Omne aevum et tanto tam placuisse viro?
examples.translation: What now avails thy character, thy whole life chastely lived, thy having so pleased so mighty a lord?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: if anyone, if anything
entries.grammaticalClass: sīqua, sīquid or sīquod, or separately
principalParts: sīqua, sīquid or sīquod, or separately

examples.original: A! nimia est iuveni propriae fiducia formae, Expectat siquis, dum prior illa roget.
examples.translation: Ah, too confident in his own charms is a lover, if he wait until she ask him first.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Hoc unum moneo, siquid modo creditur arti, Nec mea dicta rapax per mare ventus agit: Aut non rem temptes aut perfice;
examples.translation: This only do I urge (if you but trust my art, and the rapacious breeze blows not my words across the sea): either make no venture or be successful;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fallitur, Haemonias siquis decurrit ad artes, Datque quod a teneri fronte revellit equi.
examples.translation: Deceived is he whoever has recourse to Haemonian arts, and gives what he tears from the forehead of a foal.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: of or belonging to selling, to be sold

examples.original: Fidem cum proposuisses venalem in provincia, valuit apud te plus is qui pecuniam maiorem dedit: concedo;
examples.translation: You exposed your honour for sale in your province, and the man swayed you most who paid you best;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nullos autem peius mereri de omnibus mortalibus iudico quam qui philosophiam velut aliquod artificium venale didicerunt, qui aliter vivunt quam vivendum esse praecipiunt.
examples.translation: And I hold that no man has treated mankind worse than he who has studied philosophy as if it were some marketable trade, who lives in a different manner from that which he advises.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: rainy, causing or bringing rain

examples.original: Omnia ista in longa vita sunt, quomodo in longa via et pulvis et lutum et pluvia.
examples.translation: I will touch the truth more closely, and say that you feared for your life.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Omnes autem istas arbores, quae, ut ita dicam, grandiscapiae sunt, ait aqua adiuvandas cisternina, quae si prodest, habemus pluviam in nostra potestate.
examples.translation: But all trees, he declares, which are, so to speak, ”thick-stemmed,”a should be assisted with tank-water; if we have this help, we are our own rain-makers.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Of or from silver, made of silver (cf. argentum, I. A.): polubrum, Liv. And. ap.
Latin: Color argenti

examples.original: His vaginae argenteae, baltea argentea: auratae vaginae, aurea baltea illis erant, et equorum inaurata tapeta.
examples.translation: The latter had silver sheaths and silver baldrics: the former gilded sheaths and golden baldrics, and their horses had gold-embroidered saddle-cloths.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to be green or verdant (syn. viridor).

examples.original: Metiri sua regna decet viresque fateri.
examples.translation: We must take the measure of our kingdom and confess our weakness.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Corpus quoque, etiam si magnas habet vires, non aliter quam furiosi aut phrenetici validum est.
examples.translation: This, then, is the sort of health you should primarily cultivate;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Est lucum Silari iuxta ilicibusque virentem Plurimus Alburnum volitans, cui nomen asilo Romanum est, oestrum Grai vertere vocantes, Asper, acerba sonans, quo tota exterrita silvis Diffugiunt armenta.
examples.translation: Near Silarus’ groves, and eke Alburnus’ shades Of green-clad oak-trees flits an insect, named Asilus by the Romans;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Fruitful, fertile (class.; syn.: ferax, fecundus, uber).

examples.original: Est tibi rure bono generosae fertilis uvae Vinea?
examples.translation: You have a fruitful estate and a vineyard abundant in fine grapes?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Sed tu praecipue curvis venare theatris: Haec loca sunt voto fertiliora tuo.
examples.translation: But specially do your hunting in the round theatres: more bountifully do these repay your vows.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fertilior seges est alienis semper in agris, Vicinumque pecus grandius uber habet.
examples.translation: In fields not ours the crops are ever more bounteous, and the neighbouring herd has richer udders.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to lay hold of a thing, in order to keep it back or to put it forward.
Latin: rem coeptam, ne ultra progrediatur, impedire, sistere
Latin: impedīre
English: of or belonging to the morning, morning- (class.)

examples.original: Nuper in ludo bestiariorum unus e Germanis, cum ad matutina spectacula pararetur, secessit ad exonerandum corpus;
examples.translation: For example, there was lately in a training-school for wild-beast gladiators a German, who was making ready for the morning exhibition;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to make mild, soft, or tender, make ripe or mellow; to make tame, to tame (class.).

examples.original: Quid enim ultra fieri ad placandos deos mitigandosque homines potuit quam quod nos fecimus?
examples.translation: For what more could have been done to mollify the gods and to placate men than we have done?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ad hoc panis usu carnisque coctae et dulcedine vini mitigatos Marius in tempore adgressus est.
examples.translation: When they had been further demoralized by the use of bread and cooked meat and the delights of wine, Marius opportunely approached them.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Temptavit tamen Antonius vocatas ad contionem legiones mitigare, ut castris iuxta pontem Mulvium positis postera die urbem ingrederentur.
examples.translation: None the less, Antonius assembled his legions and tried to calm and persuade them to camp by the Mulvian bridge and enter the city the next day.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a nutshell
Latin: Fructus quarumdam arborum stirpiumve qui consistit in lignum durus indehiscens quod nucleum cingit
Latin: Arbor quae nuces fert

examples.original: Nux OVID, Nux Ovid Sed, puto, magna mea est operoso cura colono!
examples.translation: But the toilsome husbandman, I ween, takes great thought for me!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quid tamen hoc prodest, media si luce palamque Verberor et tutae non licet esse nuci?
examples.translation: Yet what does this avail, if openly in broad day I am beaten, and if a nut tree may not be safe?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quattuor in nucibus, non amplius, alea tota est, Cum sibi suppositis additur una tribus.
examples.translation: In four nuts, and no more, is all his hazard, when one is added to the three beneath it.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: Whither pray? (class.): quo tu te agis? Char. Quonam, nisi domum?

examples.original: Quonam igitur haec modo gesta sunt?
examples.translation: But how in the world did this come about?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque subinde exsequuntur quaerendo a consule legati quonam se pacto paucos et infirmos crederet praesidio tam valido et armato vim allaturos.
examples.translation: And so the envoys persisted in demanding of the consul how he supposed that they, being few and weak, could force so strong and well-armed a garrison.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum centurionibus ad se vocatis: ”Quaenam illa inscitia belli ac pigritia est, aut quonam modo isti ex Sidicinis Campanisque victoriam pepererunt?
examples.translation: Then, calling the centurions to him, he said: ”What want of military skill, what slothfulness can that be? How did those people conquer the Sidicini and Campanians?
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to rise or raise one's self again, to appear again
Latin: iterum me elevo
English: causing death, destruction, or calamity; causing grief; deadly, fatal, destructive, calamitous, mournful, dismal

examples.original: Nubit genero socrus, nullis auspicibus, nullis auctoribus, funestis ominibus omnium. VI.
examples.translation: She is reluctant that her fair fame should any longer be damaged by dim and doubtful suspicion;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nil ipsa paterni Iuris inire peto: culpa tantoque pudore Solve domum, remove funesta satellitis arma Et regem regnare iube.
examples.translation: I beg you only to free our house from such guilt and shame; destroy the dangerous strength of the favourite, and bid the king be a king indeed.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Cattle for ploughing; and collectively, a herd

examples.original: Quid tibi cum speculo, montana armenta petenti?
examples.translation: What dost thou with a mirror, seeking the herds upon the mountains?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Est lucum Silari iuxta ilicibusque virentem Plurimus Alburnum volitans, cui nomen asilo Romanum est, oestrum Grai vertere vocantes, Asper, acerba sonans, quo tota exterrita silvis Diffugiunt armenta.
examples.translation: Near Silarus’ groves, and eke Alburnus’ shades Of green-clad oak-trees flits an insect, named Asilus by the Romans;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To send away or

examples.original: Et subinde matre etiam relegata paene inops atque egens apud amitam Lepidam nutritus est sub duobus paedagogis saltatore atque tonsore.
examples.translation: Then his mother was banished too, and he was brought up at the house of his aunt Lepida almost in actual want, under two tutors, a dancer and a barber.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Liviam Orestillam C. Pisoni nubentem, cum ad officium et ipse venisset, ad se deduci imperavit intraque paucos dies repudiatam biennio post relegavit, quod repetisse usum prioris mariti tempore medio videbatur.
examples.translation: At the marriage of Livia Orestilla to Gaius Piso, he attended the ceremony himself, gave orders that the bride be taken to his own house, and within a few days divorced her;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: your (pl.), of/belonging to/associated with you
English: grass (cf.: herba, faenum, cespes, glaeba).
English: a package, bundle, burden, load, pack; more freq. in the

examples.original: Qua re nuntiata Caesar celeriter sarcinas conferri, arma expediri iussit.
examples.translation: On report of this Caesar ordered packs to be speedily piled and arms got ready.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to draw away from underneath or by stealth; also, in gen., to draw off, carry off, withdraw, take away, remove, etc. (class.; syn. subduco).

examples.original: Iulium Burdonem Germanicae classis praefectum astu subtraxit.
examples.translation: Julius Burdo, commander of the German fleet, he saved by a clever ruse.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to blow into or upon any thing

examples.original: Huic decet inflatos laxe iacuisse capillos: Illa sit adstrictis impedienda comis;
examples.translation: This one it beseems to let her waving locks lie loose;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Satis constat ne Ciceroni quidem obtrectatores defuisse, quibus inflatus et tumens, nec satis pressus sed supra modum exsultans et superfluens et parum Atticus videretur.
examples.translation: Cicero himself, as is well known, had his detractors: they thought him turgid and puffy, wanting in conciseness, inordinately exuberant and redundant—in short, not Attic enough.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: busy, diligent, industrious, zealous, careful, unremitting, solicitous, assiduous, sedulous

examples.original: Haec a concubitu fit sedula, tardior illa, Haec dominae munus te parat, illa sibi.
examples.translation: An intrigue makes one more eager, another more sluggish; this one wins you for her mistress, that one for herself.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to bear, carry, or bring together, to collect; to prepare, to make, build, heap up, etc. (class. and freq.).

examples.original: Non sunt ista bona, quae in te isti volunt congeri;
examples.translation: What they wish to have heaped upon you are not really good things;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid? Vos pulcherrimam hanc urbem domibus et tectis et congestu lapidum stare creditis?
examples.translation: And so it is that on our side stands the state, on theirs the enemies of the state.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Est quoque uti possit magnus congestus harenae fluctibus adversis oppilare ostia contra, cum mare permotum ventis ruit intus harenam;
examples.translation: It is possible also that a great collection of sand blocks up the mouth against the stream, when the sea, stirred by the winds, rolls the sand inwards;
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: heterocl., fili

examples.original: Et tibi dant Stygiae ius in sua fila sorores.
examples.translation: Yet even to it the Stygian sisters gave power over their spinning.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sume itaque, mi fili, sume, vir bone et non in superficie sed Christiana caritate Christiane, sume, inquam, etiam libros quos desiderasti, confessionum. mearum;
examples.translation: Take then, my son, take, excellent Sir, Christian that you are not on the surface only, but with Christian love—take, I repeat, those books of my Confessions that you asked for;
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Sed rigidum ius est et inevitabile Mortis, Stant rata non ulla fila tenenda manu.
examples.translation: But fixed and inevitable is death’s law, unswerving are the threads, not to be checked by any hand.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: the connection of associates, colleagues, etc., colleagueship (rare)

examples.original: Collegium augurum ampliatum est, ut essent novem, cum antea quaterni fuissent.
examples.translation: The augural college was enlarged so that there were nine where before there had been four.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Anno deinde insequenti lex Terentilia ab toto relata collegio novos adgressa consules est; erant consules P. Volumnius Ser. Sulpicius.
examples.translation: In the following year the Terentilian law was brought up again by the entire college and menaced the new consuls, to wit, Publius Volumnius and Servius Sulpicius.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of or pertaining to a chariot.

examples.original: Patricii, cum sine curuli magistratu res publica esset, coiere et interregem creavere.
examples.translation: The patricians, since the state was without any curule magistrate, met and chose an interrex.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Licinius Sextiusque tribuni plebis refecti nullos curules magistratus creari passi sunt;
examples.translation: Licinius and Sextius were chosen again, and suffered no curule magistrates to be elected;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ita nec dissimulantem quid mallet nec petentem tamen, aedilem curulem cum L. Papirio Cursore factum.
examples.translation: And so, neither dissembling what he had in mind nor yet seeking it, he was elected curule aedile, with Lucius Papirius Cursor.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a daughter-in-law.
English: boyish, childish, youthful (class.)

examples.original: Cetera pusilla et puerilia sunt;
examples.translation: All other studies are puny and puerile.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Istiusmodi autem res dicere ornate velle puerile est, plane autem et perspicue expedire posse docti et intellegentis viri.”
examples.translation: A man of sense and education will be content to be able to express his meaning plainly and clearly.”
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a resinous species of pine-tree, the pitch-pine tree (syn. fax): Pinus combra, Linn.

examples.original: Nonne vides etiam, nocturna ad lumina linum nuper ubi extinctum admoveas, accendier ante quam tetigit flammam, taedamque pari ratione?
examples.translation: Do you not see also that, if you move a wick newly extinguished near a night-light, it kindles before touching the flame, and the same with a torch?
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: lower, that which lies beneath

examples.original: Non caeli nox illa fuit: latet obsitus aer Infernae pallore domus nimbisque gravatus Deprimitur, fluctusque in nubibus accipit imbrem.
examples.translation: The darkness was not the common darkness of night: the heavens were hidden and veiled with the dimness of the infernal regions, and weighed down by clouds;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to draw out, entice out, to lure forth, to bring out, to elicit (class.).

examples.original: Quid cum fictas fabulas e quibus utilitas nulla elici potest cum voluptate legimus?
examples.translation: But what of our reading fiction, from which no utility can be extracted?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Eodem anno Valerius consul cum exercitu in Aequos profectus cum hostem ad proelium elicere non posset, castra oppugnare est adortus.
examples.translation: The same year. Valerius the consul, having marched with an army against the Aequi, was unable to entice the enemy into a battle, and directed an assault upon their camp.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Papirius is fuit, cui cum se C. Publilius ob aes alienum paternum nexum dedisset, quae aetas formaque misericordiam elicere poterant, ad libidinem et contumeliam animum accenderunt.
examples.translation: The change in the law was occasioned by the notable lust and cruelty of a single usurer, Lucius Papirius, to whom Gaius Publilius had given himself up for a debt owed by his father.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to cover, to cover up or over (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Ibi mediis fere castris locus est consaeptus cratibus pluteisque et linteis contectus, patens ducentos maxime pedes in omnes pariter partis.
examples.translation: There, at about the middle of the camp, they had enclosed an area, extending approximately two hundred feet in all directions, with wicker hurdles, and roofed it over with linen.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: fasting, hungry, abstinent, not partaking of food.

examples.original: Nocte tota ieiuni mutique perstant.
examples.translation: All night long they must stand about, hungry and dumb.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non dest prolato ieiunus venditor auro.
examples.translation: By now mounds and hills are hidden;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Huius, Lyco, oratione locuples, rebus ipsis ieiunior.
examples.translation: His successor Lyco has a copious style, but his matter is somewhat barren.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an infectious or contagious disease, a plague, pest, pestilence.

examples.original: Pestilentia eo anno aliarum rerum otium praebuit.
examples.translation: An epidemic that year afforded a respite from other troubles.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Famem quoque ex pestilentia morbo implicitis cultoribus agrorum timentes in Etruriam Pomptinumque agrum et Cumas, postremo in Siciliam quoque frumenti causa misere.
examples.translation: They therefore sent to Etruria and the Pomptine district, and to Cumae, and finally to Sicily itself, for corn.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mox clade conversa, cum ex mora obsidii regem fames et ex fame pestilentia urgueret, recedentem Lucullus adsequitur adeoque cecidit, ut Granicus et Aesepus amnes cruenti redderentur.
examples.translation: Lucullus followed him and dealt him so heavy a blow that the rivers Granicus and Aesepus ran with blood.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a spot, mark, stain (class.).

examples.original: Hunc tu vitae splendorem maculis adspergis istis?
examples.translation: And would you dim with your sullying insinuations the lustre of that untarnished life?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: pitch
English: lightning, a flash of lightning

examples.original: Aspicies oculos tremulo fulgore micantes, Ut sol a liquida saepe refulget aqua.
examples.translation: You will see her eyes shooting tremulous gleams, as the sun often glitters in clear water.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Tunc laudant otium lene et sui iuris, odio est fulgor et fuga a rebus adhuc stantibus quaeritur.
examples.translation: Then they praise easy leisure and independence; they hate the glamour and try to escape while their fortunes are still unimpaired.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to sprinkle a victim with sacrificial meal (mola salsa)

examples.original: Hostiae erant phoenicopteri, pavones, tetraones, numidicae, meleagrides, phasianae, quae generatim per singulos dies immolarentur .
examples.translation: The victims were flamingoes, peacocks, black grouse, guinea-hens and pheasants, offered day by day each after its own kind.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Primum fuit belli consilium, ut in Albano monte festo die Latinarum Iulius Caesar et Marcius Philippus consules inter sacra et aras immolarentur.
examples.translation: The first plan of campaign was to murder the consuls, Julius Caesar and Marcius Philippus on the Alban Mount amid the sacrifices and altars at the celebration of the Latin Festival.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: incautious, heedless, improvident

examples.original: Nec aspernanda res visa neque incaute credenda.
examples.translation: It was not thought wise to spurn this offer, nor yet rashly to confide in it.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed primus dies impetu magis quam veterani exercitus artibus transactus: aperti incautique muros subiere, cibo vinoque praegraves.
examples.translation: The first day was spent in a furious onslaught rather than in skilful attacks appropriate to a veteran army.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ibi ingens hostium exercitus itinera occultus insederat, et postquam intrasse Romanos vidit saltum, repente exortus cum clamore ac tumultu incautos invadit.
examples.translation: At first the unexpectedness of the attack occasioned some trepidation, while the soldiers were putting on their armour and piling their packs in the midst.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: memorable, remarkable, worthy of being remembered; heard of, conceivable; worthy to be mentioned, fit to be spoken of (class.)

examples.original: Eo nulla pugna memorabilis fuit.
examples.translation: For this reason there was no memorable battle.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nihil ne ab his quidem tribunis ad Velitras memorabile factum.
examples.translation: Even these tribunes accomplished nothing memorable at Velitrae.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Dubitas ergo, an optimum sit memorabilem mori et in aliquo opere virtutis?
examples.translation: Do you doubt, then, whether it is best to die glorious and performing some deed of valour?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: what?  how?

examples.original: Hic tum iniectus est hominibus scrupulus et quaedam dubitatio quidnam esset actum.
examples.translation: This made people feel uneasy and somewhat doubtful as to what had happened.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: come back, to turn back, return (not freq. till after the Aug. period; only once in Cic.; in Cæs. not at all; syn.: redeo, regredior).

examples.original: Nunc neque te longi remeantem pompa triumphi Excipit, aut sacras poscunt Capitolia laurus;
examples.translation: As it is, no long triumphal procession awaits your return, nor does the Capitol demand your consecrated laurels;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Interea domitis Caesar remeabat Hiberis Victrices aquilas alium laturus in orbem, Cum prope fatorum tantos per prospera cursus Avertere dei.
examples.translation: Meanwhile Caesar was returning triumphant over conquered Spain to carry into a new world his victorious eagles, when the flowing tide of his successes was almost turned aside by Heaven.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: enough, sufficiently (objectively, so that one needs nothing more; whereas affatim subjectively, so that one wishes nothing more).

examples.original: Satius est amicum reparare quam flere.
examples.translation: It is better to replace your friend than to weep for him.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Satius est supervacua scire quam nihil.
examples.translation: It is better, of course, to know useless things than to know nothing.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His rebus Eumenes permotus, satius duxit, si ita tulisset fortuna, perire bene meritis referentem gratiam quam ingratum vivere.
examples.translation: Deeply moved by these communications, Eumenes thought it better, if such were Fortune’s will, to lose his life in requiting kindnesses than save it by ingratitude.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

definitions: English: to be lively or vigorous; to thrive, flourish, bloom; to be in honor, esteem, repute, etc. (class.; mostly of things, concrete and abstract; cf. valeo).
English: the soft fat or grease of animals, suet, lard
English: to fall forwards, fall or sink down, to prostrate one's self; of the wounded, the dying, suppliants, etc.

examples.original: Forte quodam loco male densatus agger pondere superstantium in fossam procubuit; atque ea, cum deos pandere viam fugae conclamassent, plures inermes quam armati evadunt.
examples.translation: By that opening—crying out that the gods were providing them a means of flight—they saved themselves, but more got away without their arms than with them.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the heel.

examples.original: Et si quis deus mihi largiatur ut ex hac aetate repuerascam et in cunis vagiam, valde recusem, nec vero velim quasi decurso spatio ad carceres a calce revocari.
examples.translation: And when I shall have set out to join them, assuredly no one will easily draw me back, or boil me up again, as if I were a Pelias.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make narrow, to straiten; only trop. and in eccl. Lat. to straiten, hamper, distress

examples.original: Ceterum magna habebunt discrimina variante materia, quae modo latior est, modo angustior, modo inlustris, modo ignobilis, modo ad multos pertinens, modo ad paucos.
examples.translation: There will be, of course, great differences according as the material varies, as it becomes now broader and now narrower, now glorious and now base, now manifold in scope and now limited.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: condemnation (good prose).

examples.original: Damnationem suam Rutilius sic tulit, tamquam nihil illi molestum aliud esset quam quod male iudicaretur.
examples.translation: Sentence of Conviction was borne by Rutilius as if the injustice of the decision were the only thing which annoyed him.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quapropter neminem dubitare existimo quin illa damnatio ambitus nulla ex parte cum causa Cluenti vestroque iudicio coniuncta esse possit.
examples.translation: Wherefore I hold it indisputable that this conviction for corrupt practice can in no way be connected with the case of Cluentius, and the jurisdiction of your court.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Si ex lege subsortitus non erat Iunius aut si in aliquam legem aliquando non iuraverat, idcirco illius damnatione aliquid de Cluentio iudicabatur?
