examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: wearing the toga, clad in the toga, gowned

examples.original: Non adtingam tragicos nec togatas nostras.
examples.translation: I need not touch upon the tragedians and our writers of national dramad;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Fecit et novum genus togatarum inscripsitque trabeatas.
examples.translation: He likewise originated a new kind of togatae, to which he gave the name of trabeatae.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Multi enim sunt ex his togatis, quibus pax operosior bello est.
examples.translation: For there are many of our toga-clad citizens to whom peace brings more trouble than war.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Full of envy, envious, invidious, hostile

examples.original: Satis ipsum nomen philosophiae, etiam si modeste tractetur, invidiosum est;
examples.translation: The mere name of philosophy, however quietly pursued, is an object of sufficient scorn;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quid si non habitu sic se gessisset in omni, Ut sua non essent invidiosa bona?
examples.translation: What if she had not so borne herself in all her ways that her blessings stirred no envy?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Tu autem, Laterensis, qui tum lacrimas meas gratas esse dicebas, nunc easdem vis invidiosas videri.
examples.translation: And you, Laterensis, who then expressed yourself as touched by my tears, now turn round and try to cast infamy upon them.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a bell (late Lat.)
Latin: | Magnum tintinnābulum
Latin: saec. XVI | Magnum tintinnābulum

examples.original: Eodem anno a Campanis Cumae, quam Graeci tum urbem tenebant, capiuntur.
examples.translation: In this same year Cumae, a city which the Greeks then held, was captured by the Campanians.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In qua nunc exspectatione senatum populumque Campanum, coniuges liberosque nostros esse?
examples.translation: In what suspense are now the senate and the people of Campania, our wives and our children!
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cum in praesidium Reginorum legio Campana cum praefecto Decio Vibellio missa esset, occisis Reginis Regium occupavit.
examples.translation: A Campanian legion, commanded by Decius Vibellius, being sent to protect the people of Regium, put the inhabitants to death and seized the city.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: deep, profound, vast (class.; syn. altus).

examples.original: Saeva quies pelagi, maestoque ignava profundo Stagna iacentis aquae;
examples.translation: A grim stillness broods over the dismal deep;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: sparing in any thing, esp. in expenditure; in a good and bad sense, frugal, thrifty, economical; niggardly, penurious, parsimonious (syn.: tenax, restrictus).

examples.original: Iam illa externa parce tu quidem;
examples.translation: As for external goods, you were, it is true, cautious;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nepesinis inde edictum ut arma ponant, parcique iussum inermi: Etrusci pariter armati atque inermes caesi.
examples.translation: The Etruscans were put to death, whether armed or not. Of the Nepesini, too, those who were responsible for the surrender were executed;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ne parce, precor: da nomina rebus, Da loca;
examples.translation: Be not grudging, I pray: give events their names, their places;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a place for keeping any thing, a chest

examples.original: Certare socii civesque, utri reciperatae arcis suum decus facerent;
examples.translation: The leader of each party urged on his followers.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Puta me non dicere, unde sumpturus sum mutuum: scis cuius arca utar.
examples.translation: And just assume that I am not telling where I intend to borrow the necessary sum;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Trepidi magistratus missis ad arcem exploratoribus cum tela et armatos tenere arcem multiplicato numero audirent, avertunt animos a spe reciperandae arcis;
examples.translation: The city was thronged with fugitives, and men who were hardly yet awake and most of them unarmed, began battering down the gates.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a drinking, a drink, draught, abstr. and concr. (class.).

examples.original: Ne hoc quidem intellego, quod animalibus satietas monstrat, quis cibo debeat esse, quis potioni modus.
examples.translation: I have not even the knowledge, which satiety teaches to animals, of what should be the measure of my food or my drink.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Negat enim tenuissimo victu, id est contemptissimis escis et potionibus, minorem voluptatem percipi quam rebus exquisitissimis ad epulandum.
examples.translation: He tells us that the simplest fare, that is, the meanest sorts of food and drink, afford no less pleasure than a banquet of the rarest delicacies.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a follower

examples.original: Minucio Fabius successor in Algidum missus.
examples.translation: Fabius was sent to Mount Algidus to succeed Minucius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quinctius Horatiusque successores Valerio in Volscos missi.
examples.translation: Quinctius and Horatius were dispatched to succeed Valerius against the Volsci.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Incohavit autem aquae ductum regione Tiburti et amphitheatrum iuxta Saepta, quorum operum a successore eius Claudio alterum peractum, omissum alterum est.
examples.translation: He likewise began an aqueduct in the region near Tibur and an amphitheatre beside the Saepta, the former finished by his successor Claudius, while the latter was abandoned.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: comes in view, visible; opp. occultus

examples.original: Visite turicremas vaccae Memphitidos aras, Visite conspicuis terna theatra locis;
examples.translation: Visit the incense-burning altars of the Memphian heifer; visit three theatres in conspicuous seats.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Conferta iacent cum corpora campo, In medium mors omnis abit, perit obruta virtus: Nos in conspicua sociis hostique carina Constituere dei.
examples.translation: When the dead lie thick upon the field, each death is merged in a common account, and valour, thus overlaid, is wasted.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Postquam spatio languentia nullo Mutua conspicuos habuerunt lumina voltus, \[Hic fratres natosque suos videre patresque,\] Deprensum est civile nefas.
examples.translation: When their eyes met, undimmed by distance, and they saw each other’s faces clearly, then the horror of civil war was unmasked.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to make a matter of reproach, to cast in the teeth, to accuse of any thing; also to charge, upbraid, reproach a person with something (syn. obicere); constr

examples.original: Ipse postremo Spurinna, non tam culpam exprobrans quam rationem ostendens, relictis exploratoribus ceteros Placentiam reduxit minus turbidos et imperia accipientis.
examples.translation: In the end Caecina himself, not so much reproving their faults as showing the reasons for his action, left some scouts and led the rest back to Placentia.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: easiness, ease, facility in doing any thing.

examples.original: Fabianus, vir egregius et vita et scientia et, quod post ista est, eloquentia quoque, disputabat expedite magis quam concitate, ut posses dicere facilitatem esse illam, non celeritatem.
examples.translation: Fabianus, a man noteworthy because of his life, his knowledge, and, less important than either of these, his eloquence also, used to discuss a subject with dispatch rather than with haste;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a begetting, generating, generation (post-Aug.)
Latin: Factum generandi
Latin: Saeculum
English: son of Priam and Hecuba, husband of Andromache, the bravest of the Trojans, slain and dragged three times around Troy by Achilles, Enn. ap.

examples.original: Fecit in Andromache prius hoc fortissimus Hector, Nec solum bellis utilis ille fuit.
examples.translation: Most valiant Hector of old did thus with Andromache, nor in war alone did he avail.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: when, while, as, since, although; as soon

examples.original: Sic enim sentio, ius legatorum, quum hominum praesidio munitum sit, tum etiam divino iure esse vallatum.
examples.translation: For I hold that ambassadorial rights, fortified as they are by human protection, are also reinforced by divine ordinance.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Di immortales suorum templorum custodem ac praesidem sceleratissime pulsum quum viderent, ex suis templis in eius aedes immigrare nolebant.
examples.translation: The immortal gods, when they saw the guardian and champion of their temples outrageously expelled, refused to remove themselves from those temples into his house.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Verum fac me multis debere, et in iis Plancio: utrum igitur me conturbare oportet, an ceteris, quum cuiusque dies venerit, hoc nomen, quod urget, nunc, quum petitur, dissolvere?
examples.translation: Let us grant, then, that I am in debt to many, and to Plancius among them; ought I then to declare myself to be a bankrupt?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Of oakwood, oaken

examples.original: Illo sano ac valente oratio quoque robusta, fortis, virilis est;
examples.translation: When the soul is sound and strong, the style too is vigorous, energetic, manly;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed ea clades ingentibus expiata victoriis, postquam per alios atque alios robustissima capta sunt oppida, vario quidem eventu.
examples.translation: But for this disaster atonement was made by great victories, when the strongest cities were captured under different leaders and with different results.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Ita dico: extrinsecus aliqua sunt incommoda, velut in corpore interdum robusto solidoque eruptiones quaedam pusularum et ulcuscula, nullum in alto malum est.
examples.translation: This is what I mean: there are external disadvantages, like pimples and boils that break out upon a body which is normally strong and sound; but there is no deep-seated malady.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a sufficiency, abundance (syn. saturitas).

examples.original: Cupiditates non Epicuri divisione finiebat sed sua satietate.
examples.translation: Epicurus’s classification of the desires meant nothing to him;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Vitam enim occupare satietas sui non potest tot res varias, magnas, divinas percensentem;
examples.translation: For surfeit of self can never seize upon a life that surveys all the things which are manifold, great, divine;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ne hoc quidem intellego, quod animalibus satietas monstrat, quis cibo debeat esse, quis potioni modus.
examples.translation: I have not even the knowledge, which satiety teaches to animals, of what should be the measure of my food or my drink.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: bright, shining, glittering, brilliant, etc. (class.; syn.: nitidus, lucidus, coruscus).

examples.original: Et certamen honestum et disputatio splendida!
examples.translation: Here is an honourable quarrel, fought out in high debate!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Elegans, non magnificus, splendidus, non sumptuosus;
examples.translation: He was tasteful rather than magnificent, distinguished rather than extravagant;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Deinde ea quae requirebant orationem ornatam et gravem, quam magnifice sunt dicta ab illis, quam splendide!
examples.translation: Then, in themes demanding ornate and dignified treatment, how imposing, how brilliant is their diction!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: that steals sacred things, that robs a temple, sacrilegious

examples.original: Verum haec ex comoedia quibus impiorum luxus et sacrilega superstitio convinceretur, proferre forsitan non debemus.
examples.translation: And yet perhaps I should not put forward these scenes from comedy to confute the wantonness and the sacrilegious superstition of the ungodly.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Sed illud plane, quod tales deos quaedam dei unius magni membra esse dixisti, admoneo, quia dignaris, ut ab huius modi sacrilegis facetiis te magnopere abstineas.
examples.translation: But as to your statement that such gods are portions of one great god, I give you plain warning: please refrain altogether from such irreverent jocularity.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to go, to pass
Latin: Transire, transgredi

examples.original: Civiline parum est bello, si meque meorque Obruit?
examples.translation: Is civil war still unsatisfied, if it destroy me and mine?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: equip, furnish, supply with any thing.
English: lead.
Latin: chem. Elementum chemicum cuius numerus atomicus 82 est
Latin: Res plumbea, ut
English: to work

examples.original: Erras enim, si tibi illam putas tantum terrestres operas promittere;
examples.translation: You are indeed mistaken if you think that philosophy offers you nothing but worldly assistance;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quorum si neutrum est, opera danda est ut verbis utamur quam usitatissimis et quam maxime aptis, id est rem declarantibus.
examples.translation: If neither source of difference is present, we must be careful to employ the terms most generally accepted and those most suitable, that is, those that convey the fact clearly.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cum eis in Samnium profectus, dum hostes operati superstitionibus concilia secreta agunt, Amiternum oppidum de Samnitibus vi cepit.
examples.translation: Proceeding with these forces into Samnium, while the enemy, busy with their superstitious rites, were holding secret councils, he carried the Samnite town of Amiternum by assault.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: per diaeresin exsolŭātur
English: a quarrel, strife, dispute, altercation, contention (class.)

examples.original: Cavendum vero ne etiam in gravis inimicitias convertant se amicitiae ex quibus iurgia maledicta contumeliae gignuntur.
examples.translation: And you must indeed be on your guard lest friendships be changed into serious enmities, which are the source of disputes, abuse, and invective.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a bearing, bringing (only in the trop. signif.). *

examples.original: Alba tum erat Latio caput, Iuli opus;
examples.translation: Alba was at that time the chief city of Latium, having been built by lulus;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sic valida Latio oppida capta sunt, Ardea, Ocricolum, Gabii, Suessa Pometia.
examples.translation: Thus the powerful cities in Latium were captured, Ardea, Ocricolum, Gabii, Suessa Pometia.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: very much, very many (class.): nescio quantulum attulerit

examples.original: At enim iudicia facta permulta sunt a Cluentio iudicium esse corruptum.
examples.translation: But, you may say, the result of many previous trials has proved that Cluentius bribed the court.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sunt et haec et alia in te falsi accusatoris signa permulta, quibus ego nunc non utor;
examples.translation: You display all these marks of the counterfeit prosecutor, and many others besides. But I will make no use of them at present.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Possum persequi permulta oblectamenta rerum rusticarum, sed ea ipsa quae dixi sentio fuisse longiora.
examples.translation: I might enlarge upon all the many charms of country life, but I realize that I have already said too much.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the name of several Greek philosophers.

examples.original: Zenoni an Cleanthi an Chrysippo an Panaetio an Posidonio?
examples.translation: To Zeno, Cleanthes, Chrysippus, Panaetius, or Posidonius?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In his igitur partibus duabus nihil erat quod Zeno commutare gestiret;
examples.translation: In these two departments then, there was nothing that Zeno need have desired to alter;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: De quibus etsi a Chrysippo maxime est elaboratum, tamen a Zenone minus multo quam ab antiquis;
examples.translation: Logic, no doubt, was very fully worked out by Chrysippus, but much less was done in it by Zeno than by the older schools;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Verb. neutr.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

definitions: English: a banished person, wanderer, exile.

examples.original: Neminem exsulum nisi ex senatus auctoritate restituit.
examples.translation: He recalled no one from exile except with the approval of the senate.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Ad cuius spectaculum commeare in urbem non solum praesidibus provinciarum permisit, verum etiam exsulibus quibusdam;
examples.translation: To witness the sight he allowed not only the governors of the provinces to come to Rome, but even some of the exiles;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Exsules servique, ad duo milia hominum et quingenti, duce Ap. Herdonio Sabino nocte Capitolium atque arcem occupavere.
examples.translation: Exiles and slaves to the number of twenty-five hundred, led by Appius Herdonius, the Sabine, came by night and seized the Capitol and the Citadel.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to strike or beat a thing to some point, to cast or throw down or against, to dash, somewhere by striking; esp. of ships which are driven or cast away by the wind. —Constr. with
English: daughter's husband; son-in-law
Latin: Filiae meae maritus
Latin: Sponsus filiae meae

examples.original: Quot genera tibi in hac dabo, quibus peccetur?
examples.translation: In this department, what countless varieties of fault I can show you!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Erat et cupidus voluptatum et eius generis intellegens et copiosus;
examples.translation: His appetite for pleasures was only equalled by his taste and ingenuity in devising them.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Numquam tibi, Magne, per umbras Perque meos manes genero non esse licebit;
examples.translation: In vain you sever with the sword the tie of kinship that binds you.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a hearer

examples.original: Facile est auditorem concitare ad cupidinem recti;
examples.translation: It is easy to rouse a listener so that he will crave righteousness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Diodorus, eius auditor, adiungit ad honestatem vacuitatem doloris.
examples.translation: Diodorus, his pupil, couples with Moral Worth freedom from pain.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam illa quoque inopia et exilitas minus intentum auditorem habet taedio interruptae tarditatis, facilius tamen insidit, quod exspectatur, quam quod praetervolat.
examples.translation: For that poverty-stricken and thin-spun style also makes the audience less attentive because they are weary of its stammering slowness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: I myself
English: a Roman surname, e. g. C. Vibius Pansa

examples.original: Sic enim in fastos actaque in publica relatum est. Nec tamen desunt, qui partim antecedente anno, Hirti ac Pansae, partim insequenti, Servili Isaurici L. que Antoni consulatu, genitum eum scribant.
examples.translation: Yet in spite of this some write that he was born in the preceding year, that of Hirtius and Pansa, and others in the following year, in the consulate of Servilius Isauricus and Lucius Antonius.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: slime, clammy moisture.
English: gerundive

examples.original: Et doleas oportet et sitias et esurias et senescas, si tibi longior contigerit inter homines mora, et aegrotes et perdas aliquid et pereas.
examples.translation: You must suffer pain, and thirst, and hunger, and old age too, if a longer stay among men shall be granted you; you must be sick, and you must suffer loss and death.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a cave, cavern, grot

examples.original: Ceterum ad Nequinum oppidum cum segni obsidione tempus tereretur, duo ex oppidanis, quorum erant aedificia iuncta muro, specu facto ad stationes Romanas itinere occulto perveniunt;
examples.translation: Meantime, at the town of Nequinum, while the siege dragged slowly on, two of the townsmen, whose dwellings abutted on the wall, dug a tunnel and made their way in secret to the Roman outposts.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a vessel for drawing water, a water-pot, water-jar
Latin: Vas quo aqua e puteis fluminibusve hauritur
Latin: Vas seplucrale, qua conduntur mortuorum ossa et cineres

examples.original: Fortuna recursus Si det in Hesperiam, non hac in sede quiescent Tam sacri cineres, sed te Cornelia, Magne, Accipiet nostraque manu transfundet in urnam.
examples.translation: If Fortune grant us a return to Italy, not here will these sacred ashes rest; but Cornelia will recover you, Magnus, and will transfer them from my hand to an urn.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a family cognomen; e. g.

examples.original: Bassus pudore seu metu, quisnam exitus foret, intra domum opperiebatur.
examples.translation: Bassus waited in his quarters, prompted by shame or by fear as to the outcome.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Seneca Lvcilio svo salvtem Bassum Aufidium, virum optimum, vidi quassum, aetati obluctantem.
examples.translation: On Conquering the Conqueror I have beheld Aufidius Bassus, that noble man, shattered in health and wrestling with his years.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Persius Lives of Illustrious Men ut quasi finitus esset. Leviter correxit Cornutus et Caesio Basso petenti, ut ipse ederet, tradidit edendum.
examples.translation: Cornutus made some slight corrections, and on the request of Caesius Bassus that he might publish it, turned it over to him for that purpose.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

definitions: English: to collect into a flock or herd, to assemble.
English: a she-goat, Cato ap.
English: to sweat, perspire.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Quibusdam etiam constantissimis in conspectu populi sudor erumpit, non aliter quam fatigatis et aestuantibus solet, quibusdam tremunt genua dicturis, quorundam dentes colliduntur, lingua titubat, labra concurrunt.
examples.translation: The steadiest speaker, when before the public, often breaks into a perspiration, as if he had wearied or over-heated himself; some tremble in the knees when they rise to speak;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to call together, to convoke, assemble; to call (esp. for consultation, to arms, etc.; class.; freq. in Cic. and the histt.).

examples.original: Convocat turbam, quisquis otio suo aliquam fabulam inposuit.
examples.translation: To advertise one’s retirement is to collect a crowd.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quae ne impedimentis gravibus agmen oneraret, convocari milites Decius iubet. ”Hacine” inquit ”victoria sola aut hac praeda contenti estis futuri?
examples.translation: Lest these should encumber the marching army with heavy baggage, Decius called the soldiers together and thus addressed them: ”Will this single victory or these spoils content you?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Vercingetorix tot continuis incommodis Vellaunoduni, Cenabi, Novioduni acceptis suos ad concilium convocat.
examples.translation: Having experienced three continuous reverses—at Vellaunodunum, Cenabum, and Noviodunum—Vercingetorix summoned his followers to a convention.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: in the same place (rare)

examples.original: Eodemque veneno C. Oppianicum fratrem necavit.
examples.translation: And he used poison, too, to murder his brother,G. Oppianicus.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quo contenderat pervenit, eodemque ut sequerentur ad Timotheum et Iphicraten nuntium misit.
examples.translation: He arrived at his destination, and sent word to Timotheus and Iphicrates to join him.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timotheus

definitions: English: the famous Greek philosopher of Gargettus

examples.original: Epicurus autem, in quibus sequitur Democritum, non fere labitur.
examples.translation: Epicurus for his part, where he follows Democritus, does not generally blunder.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Hoc Epicurus in voluptate ponit, quod summum bonum esse vult summumque malum dolorem;
examples.translation: This Epicurus finds in pleasure; pleasure he holds to be the Chief Good, pain the Chief Evil.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quae est enim aut utilior aut ad bene vivendum aptior partitio quam illa qua est usus Epicurus?
examples.translation: Nothing could be more useful or more conducive to well-being than Epicurus’s doctrine as to the different classes of the desires.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: not, not at all, by no means; not (as a particle)
English: untamed, unsubdued, ungoverned, unrestrained; untamable, ungovernable, fierce, wild (class.).

examples.original: Idem per Scythici profugum divortia ponti Indomitum regem Romanaque fata morantem Ad mortem Sulla felicior ire coegi.
examples.translation: Again, when the indomitable king obstructed Rome’s destiny, I drove him in flight along the isthmus of the Scythian sea;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Non voluptates illa temperavit, non cupiditates refrenavit, non iras repressit, non indomitos amoris impetus fregit, nulla denique animo mala eduxit.
examples.translation: No restraint upon pleasure, no bridling of desire, no checking of bad temper, no crushing of the wild assaults of passion, no opportunity to rid the soul of evil.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Res vero publica quamquam erat exterminata mecum, tamen obversabatur ante oculos exstinctoris sui et ab istius inflammato atque indomito furore iam tum se meque repetebat.
examples.translation: As for the republic, though it had shared my banishment, its phantom yet loomed before the eyes of its suppressor, and was even then demanding me (yes!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the quality of being antiquus

examples.original: Quanta notitia antiquitatis, scientia iuris auguri!
examples.translation: What a knowledge of ancient history! What skill in augural law!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to threaten, menace a person with any thing; constr. alicui aliquid, alicui aliquā re, with

examples.original: Huius adventus et Mithridatem insolita inflammatum victoria continuit et Tigranem magnis copiis minitantem Asiae retardavit.
examples.translation: His arrival restrained Mithridates, who was elated by the unusual experience of victory, and checked Tigranes, who was threatening Asia with great forces.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: hurt, harm, injury, which one does or suffers (v. Döderl. Synon. 2, p. 153 sqq.; not in Cic., but cf. noxia; syn.: injuria, contumelia).

examples.original: Miramur animalia quaedam, quae per medios ignes sine noxa corporum transeant;
examples.translation: We marvel at certain animals because they can pass through fire and suffer no bodily harm;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ibi in hanc sententiam locutum accipio: ”Etsi mihi nullius noxae conscius, Quirites, sum, tamen cum pudore summo in contionem in conspectum vestrum processi.
examples.translation: There he spoke, as I understand, to the following effect: ”Although I am conscious, Quirites, of no wrong-doing, nevertheless it is with great shame that I have come to this assembly to confront you.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sic ista sine noxa decipiunt, quomodo praestigiatorum acetabula et calculi, in quibus me fallacia ipsa delectat.
examples.translation: Such quibbles are just as harmlessly deceptive as the juggler’s cup and dice, in which it is the very trickery that pleases me.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to move or stir up thoroughly.

examples.original: His rebus Eumenes permotus, satius duxit, si ita tulisset fortuna, perire bene meritis referentem gratiam quam ingratum vivere.
examples.translation: Deeply moved by these communications, Eumenes thought it better, if such were Fortune’s will, to lose his life in requiting kindnesses than save it by ingratitude.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Est quoque uti possit magnus congestus harenae fluctibus adversis oppilare ostia contra, cum mare permotum ventis ruit intus harenam;
examples.translation: It is possible also that a great collection of sand blocks up the mouth against the stream, when the sea, stirred by the winds, rolls the sand inwards;
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: His rebus permotus Quintus Titurius, cum procul Ambiorigem suos cohortantem conspexisset, interpretem suum Gnaeum Pompeium ad eum mittit rogatum ut sibi militibusque parcat.
examples.translation: Alarmed by these events, Quintus Titurius, who had remarked Ambiorix at a distance encouraging his men, sent his interpreter, Gnaeus Pompeius, to him to ask him to spare himself and his troops.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a hoof, claw, talon; of a horse: totam quatit ungula terram, Enn. ap.
English: a very young man, =

examples.original: Hic magno cum pondere auri Thebas venit et Micythum adulescentulum quinque talentis ad suam perduxit voluntatem, quem tum Epaminondas plurimum diligebat.
examples.translation: Diomedon came to Thebes with a great amount of gold, and with five talents won the support of a young man named Micythus, to whom Epaminondas was greatly attached at that time.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Epaminondas

examples.original: Hic peradulescentulus ad amicitiam accessit Philippi, Amyntae filii, brevique tempore in intimam pervenit familiaritatem; fulgebat enim iam in adulescentulo indoles virtutis.
examples.translation: Eumenes, when very young, became the friend of Philip, son of Amyntas, and soon grew very intimate with the king, being conspicuous even in his youth for his high character.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Crates, ut aiunt, huius ipsius Stilbonis auditor, cuius mentionem priore epistula feci, cum vidisset adulescentulum secreto ambulantem, interrogavit, quid illic solus faceret?
examples.translation: Crates, they say, the disciple of the very Stilbo whom I mentioned in a former letter, noticed a young man walking by himself, and asked him what he was doing all alone.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: deprived or bereft of a husband or wife, bereft of a lover, spouseless, mateless, widowed.
English: the space of three years, three years

examples.original: Vixit annis viginti novem, imperavit triennio et decem mensibus diebusque octo.
examples.translation: He lived twenty-nine years and ruled three years, ten months and eight days.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Et cum haec paucorum mensium ratio in his libellis sit, facite ut vobis triennii totius veniat in mentem.
examples.translation: Moreover, the return contained in these papers is for a few months only; so you must allow, gentlemen, for the full three years.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Gaio et Lucio intra triennium defunctis adoptatur ab Augusto simul cum fratre eorum M. Agrippa, coactus prius ipse Germanicum fratris sui filium adoptare.
examples.translation: When Gaius and Lucius died within three years, he was adopted by Augustus along with their brother Marcus Agrippa, being himself first compelled to adopt his nephew Germanicus.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a kind of eagle

examples.original: O excubias tuas, Cn. Planci, miseras!
examples.translation: O the misery of your lonely watches, Plancius!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Kal. Dec. M. Aemilio Lepido iterum L. Munatio Planco conss. per bellum Philippense.
examples.translation: In fact it is so recorded both in the calendar and in the public gazette.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Tres in Belgis collocavit: eis Marcum Crassum quaestorem et Lucium Munatium Plancum et Gaium Trebonium legatos praefecit.
examples.translation: Three he stationed among the Belgae: in command of them he set Marcus Crassus, the quartermaster-general, and Lucius Munatius Plancus and Gaius Trebonius, lieutenant-generals.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a row of houses in town or country, a quarter of a city, a street
Latin: Via in urbe cum aedibus secundum eam
Latin: Oppidulum

examples.original: Agrorum atque vicorum populatione non contentus in ipsa Numidiae capita impetum fecit;
examples.translation: Not content with laying waste the fields and villages, he attacked the principal cities of Numidia.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nec solum modo vastum hosti relictum sed castellis etiam vicisque inlatus ignis: urbibus oppugnandis temperatum, in quas timor Etruscos compulerat.
examples.translation: The consul stopped short of attacking the walled towns, into which the frightened Etruscans had fled for refuge.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quando continget contemnere utramque fortunam, quando continget omnibus oppressis adfectibus et sub arbitrium suum adductis hanc vocem emittere ”vici”?
examples.translation: When will it be our privilege, after all the passions have been subdued and brought under our own control, to utter the words ”I have conquered!”?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to carry or convey down; to carry off, to convey away (freq. and good prose).
English: to kindle, take fire (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense and in Cic.; cf.: ardeo, ferveo, caleo, flagro, candeo, uro, etc., incendor, inflammor, etc.).

examples.original: In omnes personas hic exardescit affectus;
examples.translation: But indeed this emotion blazes out against all sorts of persons;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Excepi et pro patria solus exarsi, sic tamen, ut vos iisdem ignibus circumsaepti me primum ictum pro vobis et fumantem videretis.
examples.translation: I blazed alone for my country; but nevertheless those flames hedged you about on all sides, and I was but the first victim whom you saw smitten and smoking to save you.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Bellvm Civile Svb Lepido III, 23Marco Lepido Quinto Catulo consulibus civile bellum paene citius oppressum est quam inciperet: sed quantulacumque fax illius motus ab ipso Sullae rogo exarsit.
examples.translation: The Civil War under Lepidus 23. In the consulship of Marcus Lepidus and Quintus Catulus, a civil war which arose was suppressed almost as soon as it began.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: unknown.

examples.original: Si quis autem hoc uno nititur, quod sit ignobilis, procedit saepe longius, quam si idem ille esset cum isdem suis vitiis nobilissimus.
examples.translation: Indeed a man who has nothing but humble birth to support him often goes further than he would, had he the same defects though born of high degree.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Fulcinius fuit, recuperatores, e municipio Tarquiniensi, qui et domi suae cum primis honestus existimatus est, et Romae argentariam non ignobilem fecit.
examples.translation: There was one M. Fulcinius, gentlemen, a native of Tarquinii, who in his native place enjoyed an eminently honourable reputation and at Rome had a considerable business as a banker.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ceterum magna habebunt discrimina variante materia, quae modo latior est, modo angustior, modo inlustris, modo ignobilis, modo ad multos pertinens, modo ad paucos.
examples.translation: There will be, of course, great differences according as the material varies, as it becomes now broader and now narrower, now glorious and now base, now manifold in scope and now limited.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to be praised, praiseworthy, laudable (class. and freq.).

examples.original: Quod cum ita sit, perspicuum est omnes rectas res atque laudabiles eo referri ut cum voluptate vivatur.
examples.translation: This being so, it clearly follows that actions are right and praiseworthy only as being a means to the attainment of a life of pleasure.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam cui proposita sit conservatio sui, necesse est huic partes quoque sui caras esse, carioresque quo perfectiores sint et magis in suo genere laudabiles.
examples.translation: For he who aims at the preservation of himself, must necessarily feel an affection for the parts of himself also, and the more so, the more perfect and admirable in their own kind they are.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a lamp, oil-lamp.
English: a lung; and in
English: of blood, consisting of blood, bloody

examples.original: Quacumque vagatur, Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellona flagellum, Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, Nox ingens scelerum est;
examples.translation: He visits the corpses that sprawl on the wide plain; with his own hand he staunches the wound that would otherwise pour out all the blood of many a man.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Fessa iacet cervix, fumant sudoribus artus, Oraque proiecta squalent arentia lingua, Pectora rauca gemunt, quae creber anhelitus urguet, Et defecta gravis longe trahit ilia pulsus, Siccaque sanguineis durescit spuma lupatis.
examples.translation: The weary neck sinks down, the limbs reek with sweat, the tongue protrudes and the mouth is rough and dry; the lungs, driven by quick pants, give a hoarse murmur;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Excessive fear of the goas, unreasonable religious belief, superstition

examples.original: Sine cupiditatibus vos genui, sine timoribus, sine superstitione, sine perfidia ceterisque pestibus;
examples.translation: I brought you into the world without desires or fears, free from superstition, treachery and the other curses.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Verum haec ex comoedia quibus impiorum luxus et sacrilega superstitio convinceretur, proferre forsitan non debemus.
examples.translation: And yet perhaps I should not put forward these scenes from comedy to confute the wantonness and the sacrilegious superstition of the ungodly.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Cum eis in Samnium profectus, dum hostes operati superstitionibus concilia secreta agunt, Amiternum oppidum de Samnitibus vi cepit.
examples.translation: Proceeding with these forces into Samnium, while the enemy, busy with their superstitious rites, were holding secret councils, he carried the Samnite town of Amiternum by assault.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: at any time, ever; at some time

examples.original: Vestalibus nempe una illa sedes est, ex qua eas nihil unquam praeterquam urbs capta movit;
examples.translation: The Vestals surely have but that one dwelling-place, from which nothing ever caused them to remove but the capture of the City;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non unquam alias ante tantus terror senatum invasit; adeo valida res tum Clusina erat magnumque Porsinnae nomen.
examples.translation: Never before had such fear seized the senate, so powerful was Clusium in those days, and so great Porsinna’s fame.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Agitatum etiam in consilio est ut, si quando unquam severo ullum imperio bellum administratum esset, tunc utique disciplina militaris ad priscos redigeretur mores.
examples.translation: It was also urged in the council that if ever any war had been conducted with stern authority, now was the occasion of all others for recalling military discipline to its ancient courses.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: drinking readily, freely
English: to stretch forth or forward, to extend (syn. obtendo).

examples.original: Nolle in causa est, non posse praetenditur.
examples.translation: The reason is unwillingness, the excuse, inability.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Celsus et Paulinus, cum prudentia eorum nemo uteretur, inani nomine ducum alienae culpae praetendebantur;
examples.translation: As for Celsus and Paulinus, no one made any use of their practical knowledge;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: moisture
Latin: Nocturnus umor super herbas
Latin: aqua, stīllicidium
English: to be brilliant, glittering, to shine, glitter, glisten

examples.original: Fonte cadit modico parvisque inpellitur undis Puniceus Rubicon, cum fervida canduit aestas, Perque imas serpit valles et Gallica certus Limes ab Ausoniis disterminat arva colonis.
examples.translation: The ruddy river Rubicon glides through the bottom of the valleys and serves as a fixed landmark to divide the land of Gaul from the farms of Italy.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: hatchet with a broad edge (cf. bipennis).

examples.original: Honestum omne securum est, tranquillum est;
examples.translation: The honourable is wholly free from anxiety and is calm;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: T. Manlius consul filium, quod contra edictum eius adversus Latinos pugnaverat, quamvis prospere pugnasset, securi percussit.
examples.translation: Titus Manlius the consul had his son beheaded, because he had fought—albeit successfully—against the Latins in defiance of his edict.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Exanimati omnes tam atroci imperio nec aliter quam in se quisque destrictam cernentes securem, metu magis quam modestia quievere.
examples.translation: All were astounded at so shocking a command; every man looked upon the axe as lifted against himself, and they were hushed with fear more than with reverence.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: thirst
Latin: Appetitus humoris, cupiditas bibendi

examples.original: Vesperascente die sitim haustu gelidae aquae sedavit.
examples.translation: As evening approached he slaked his thirst with a draught of cold water.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: In voluptate corporis (addam, si vis, animi, dum ea ipsa, ut vultis, sit e corpore) situm est vivere beate.
examples.translation: Bodily pleasure (and I will add if you like mental pleasure, so long as this, as you hold, is understood to have its source in the body) constitutes happiness.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Est autem situm in nobis ut et adversa quasi perpetua oblivione obruamus et secunda iucunde ac suaviter meminerimus.
examples.translation: We have the power both to obliterate our misfortunes in an almost perpetual forgetfulness and to summon up pleasant and agreeable memories of our successes.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: A lover, a friend, in an honorable sense (syn.: amans, amicus, studiosus): vir bonus amatorque noster

examples.original: Ut fuerit torva violentior illa Medusa, Fiet amatori lenis et aequa suo.
examples.translation: Though she be more violent than grim Medusa, she will be mild and gentle to her lover.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Mars pater, insano Veneris turbatus amore, De duce terribili factus amator erat.
examples.translation: Father Mars, plagued by frenzied love of Venus, from a terrible captain became a lover.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ut semel Aetola Venus est a cuspide laesa, Mandat amatori bella gerenda suo.
examples.translation: No sooner was Venus hurt by the Aetolian spear than she bids her lover wage her wars.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to rest one's self, to rest, repose (very freq. and class.).

examples.original: Post quae dimotis omnibus paulum requievit.
examples.translation: After this he sent all away and rested for a time.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: and not, nor, and that not, and lest: utinam ne in nemore, etc.... neve inde, etc., Enn. ap.
English: an excusing, excuse (freq. and class.); constr. with

examples.original: Et numquid ad rem pertinet, sive interposita sit ad recedendum necessitatis excusatio sive non sit?
examples.translation: And does it really affect the point, whether the excuse of necessity for leaving the town was inserted or was not?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Ac morositas tamen et ea vitia, quae dixi, habent aliquid excusationis, non illius quidem iustae, sed quae probari posse videatur : contemni se putant, despici, illudi;
examples.translation: Yet moroseness and the other faults mentioned have some excuse, not a really sufficient one, but such as it may seem possible to allow, in that old men imagine themselves ignored, despised, and mocked at;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an acorn, and, in gen., any acorn-shaped fruit, beechnut, chestnut, etc.
English: a complaining, complaint (class.).
English: to press down or under.

examples.original: Omnes illos megistanas et satrapas et regem ipsum, ex quo Idomenei titulus petebatur, oblivio alta suppressit.
examples.translation: All the grandees and satraps, even the king himself, who was petitioned for the title which Idomeneus sought, are sunk in deep oblivion.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Institutum etiam ab iisdem consulibus ut senatus consulta in aedem Cereris ad aediles plebis deferrentur, quae antea arbitrio consulum supprimebantur vitiabanturque.
examples.translation: Up to that time they were wont to be suppressed or falsified, at the pleasure of the consuls.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to recover, regain
Latin: Iterum possidere

examples.original: Hunc Epaminondas recuperavit, bello persequens Alexandrum.
examples.translation: He was rescued by Epaminondas, who made war upon Alexander.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pelopidas

examples.original: Bellvm Ligvricvm II, 3Peracto Punico bello secuta est brevis sane quasi ad recuperandum spiritum requies, argumentumque pacis et bona fide cessantium armorum tum primum post Numam clausa porta Iani fuit;
examples.translation: The Ligurian War 3. The Carthaginian war being ended, a period of rest ensued, brief, indeed, for the Roman people to recover their breath.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed hos praecipue Titus Quinctius domuit, ille dictator ab aratro, qui obsessa et paene iam capta Manili consulis castra egregia victoria recuperavit.
examples.translation: These were subdued chiefly by Titus Quinctius, the dictator who was summoned from the plough and by a famous victory rescued the camp of the consul Manilius, which was beleaguered and almost captured.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: On this side

examples.original: Mittuntur etiam ad eas civitates legati quae sunt citerioris Hispaniae finitimae Aquitaniae: inde auxilia ducesque arcessuntur.
examples.translation: They even sent deputies to those states of Nearer Spain which border on Aquitania, inviting succours and leaders from thence.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: His nuntiis litterisque commotus Caesar duas legiones in citeriore Gallia novas conscripsit et inita aestate in interiorem Galliam qui deduceret Quintum Pedium legatum misit.
examples.translation: These reports and despatches prompted Caesar to enrol two new legions in Hither Gaul, and at the beginning of summer he sent Quintus Pedius, lieutenant-general, to lead them into Inner Gaul.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to tie, bind, bind together, bind up, bandage, bind fast, etc.
Latin: Copulam ad res applicare, vincire
Latin: Instrumentum rusticum, qui in terram subigitando et sarriendo adhibetur; species asciae aut unius dentis aut bidens

examples.original: Ast alias manicaeque ligant teretesque catenae, Seque tenent remis: tecto stetit aequore bellum.
examples.translation: The sea was no longer visible, and the battle became stationary.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Execranda autem superstitio ligaturarum, in quibus etiam inaures virorum in summis ex una parte auriculis suspensae deputantur: non ad placendum hominibus sed ad serviendum daemonibus adhibentur.
examples.translation: It is an accursed superstition to wear amulets,a among which must be reckoned also the earringsb that men wear on the top part of the ear on one side;
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to decorate, adorn, embellish, grace, beautify (class, and freq.).

examples.original: Noscitabatur tamen in tanta deformitate, et ordines duxisse aiebant aliaque militiae decora vulgo miserantes eum iactabant;
examples.translation: He was recognized nevertheless, despite the hideousness of his appearance, and the word went round that he had commanded companies;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: To lead aside or apart, to draw aside; to lead away, carry off; to set aside

examples.original: Seducere me debeo et quid suadeam circumspicere.
examples.translation: I ought to go into retirement, and consider what sort of advice I should give you.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: His accensi vocibus patres consilia inde non publica, sed in privato seductaque a plurium conscientia habuere.
examples.translation: In these deliberations there was but one guiding principle, that by fair means or foul the defendants must be got off.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Otiosum enim hominem seductum existimat vulgus et securum et se contentum, sibi viventem, quorum nihil ulli contingere nisi sapienti potest.
examples.translation: For the mass of man-kind consider that a person is at leisure who has with-drawn from society, is free from care, self-sufficient, and lives for himself;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: copious (post-class.)

examples.original: Quod si istis ipsis voluptatibus bona aetas fruitur libentius, primum parvulis fruitur rebus, ut diximus, deinde eis, quibus senectus, etiam si non abunde potitur, non omnino caret.
examples.translation: But granting that youth enjoys pleasures of that kind with a keener relish, then, in the first place, as I have said, they are petty things which it enjoys;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to devise something by careful thought, to contrive, invent, feign.

examples.original: Hoc consilio per conscios parum celato solutilem navem, cuius vel naufragio vel camarae ruina periret, commentus est atque ita reconciliatione simulata iucundissimis litteris Baias evocavit ad sollemnia Quinquatruum simul celebranda;
examples.translation: When this leaked out through some of those connected with the plot, he devised a collapsible boat, to destroy her by shipwreck or by the falling in of its cabin.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: a vine, grapevine.

examples.original: Siquis amas, nec vis, facito contagia vites;
examples.translation: If you love, nor wish to love, see that you shun contagion;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Propria virtus est in vite fertilitas, in homine quoque id laudandum est, quod ipsius est.
examples.translation: In a vine the virtue peculiarly its own is fertility; in man also we should praise that which is his own.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ait vilicus mihi non esse neglegentiae suae vitium, omnia se facere, sed villam veterem esse.
examples.translation: My bailiff maintained that the flaws were not due to his own carelessness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a mouse
Latin: Exiguum animal, incola domuum, penori et vestibus et chartis infestissimum, sed idem felium et mustelarum insidiis ad necem semper quaesitum
Latin: Instrumentum manuale quo data in computatra introducuntur

examples.original: Fata vetant, murique vicem Fortuna tuetur.
examples.translation: Fate is against them, and Fortune performs the office of a wall.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Muri autem omnes Gallici hac fere forma sunt.
examples.translation: All Gallic walls are, as a rule, of the following pattern.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Aequi se in oppida receperunt murisque se tenebant.
examples.translation: The Aequi retired to their towns and kept within their walls.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a reaping and ingathering of the fruits of the earth, a harvest (class.).

examples.original: Messium impetus per stratos caede hostes cum globo fortissimorum iuvenum extulit ad castra Volscorum, quae nondum capta erant.
examples.translation: Messius pressed on with a band of courageous youths over the slain bodies of his enemies, and reached the Volscian camp, which had not yet been taken;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: an enterprise against the enemy, an expedition, campaign: tripartito milites equitesque in expeditionem misit, *

examples.original: Expeditionem unam omnino suscepit eamque modicam.
examples.translation: He made but one campaign and that of little importance.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Expeditio in Cyprvm III, 9Aderat fatum insularum.
examples.translation: The Expedition to Cyprus 9. The fate of the islands was sealed;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Venit in curiam tamen expeditionem Parthicam meditans.
examples.translation: Yet he came into the senate-house thinking of his campaign against Parthia.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a property, peculiarity, peculiar nature, quality of a thing (class.)
Latin: Qualitas quae propria alicui rei est

examples.original: Non opus est exhortatione, ne consilio quidem, ut colorum proprietates oculus intellegat, a nigro album etiam nullo monente distinguet.
examples.translation: There is no need of encouragement, or even of counsel, for the eye to be able to distinguish different colours;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ipsi quoque ad syllabarum distinctiones et coniunctionum ac praepositionum proprietates descenderunt et invidere grammaticis, invidere geometris.
examples.translation: Of their own accord they also have descended to establishing nice divisions of syllables, to determining the true meaning of conjunctions and prepositions;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: four times
Latin: Quattuor vicibus
English: trunk of tree; piece/block of wood; blockhead

examples.original: Posteaquam reus factus est, primo negabat se opus in acceptum referre posse; cum instaret Habonius, in me causam conferebat, quod eum codicem obsignassem.
examples.translation: After his prosecution, he first said for some time that he could not certify that the work had been duly carried out;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of or belonging to a grandfather, coming from a grandfather, ancestral.

examples.original: Id cumulatum usuris primo se agro paterno avitoque exuisse, deinde fortunis aliis, postremo velut tabem pervenisse ad corpus;
examples.translation: Then the taxes had been levied, in an untoward moment for him, and he had contracted debts.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Audire te arbitror, Scipio, hospes tuus avitus Masinissa quae faciat hodie nonaginta natus annos : cum ingressus iter pedibus sit, in equum omnino non ascendere;
examples.translation: I think, Scipio, that the news reaches you of the daily activities of your grandfather’s friend and host Masinissa, now ninety years old;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Hence derivv.
English: to interrupt by speaking, to disturb, molest, etc. (syn. obloquor; class.).

examples.original: Magno malo ulla voce interpellatum silentium luitur.
examples.translation: There is a grievous penalty for the slightest breach of silence.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vt ipsi concedi non oporteret, si in nostros fines impetum faceret, sic item nos esse iniquos, quod in suo iure se interpellaremus.
examples.translation: As it was not right to give way to him, if he made an attack on Roman territory, so likewise the Romans were unjust in obstructing him in his own jurisdiction.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: after

examples.original: Si extra est, posteaquam acciderat, recessit.
examples.translation: If it is outside, it withdraws after having affected the object.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic Philodamus, posteaquam ius suum obtinere non potuit, ut humanitatem consuetudinemque suam retineret laborabat.
examples.translation: Unable to maintain his rights, Philodamus now did his best to maintain his accustomed courtesy.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Cuius in regnum posteaquam L. Lucullus cum exercitu venit, plures etiam gentes contra imperatorem nostrum concitatae sunt.
examples.translation: On the arrival of Lucullus and his troops in Armenia, yet other nations rose against our general;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: descent, lineage, race, family.

examples.original: Ne mutas quidem bestias minus alere ac fovere si quid ex progenie sua parum prosperum sit;
examples.translation: Why even the dumb brutes, if one of their young is unfortunate, do none the less cherish it and foster it.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Book VIIGalba • Otho • Vitellus Galba I. Progenies Caesarum in Nerone defecit: quod futurum compluribus quidem signis, sed vel evidentissimis duobus apparuit.
examples.translation: Galba Book VIIGalba • Otho • Vitellus Galba I. The race of the Caesars ended with Nero. That this would be so was shown by many portents and especially by two very significant ones.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: of or belonging to a king, kingly, royal, regal.

examples.original: Forte erat in thalamo virgo regalis eodem;
examples.translation: It chanced that in the same chamber was the royal maid;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Idem iterum Sulla superavit: tum sine dubio habuit regalem potestatem, quamquam rem publicam recuperarat.
examples.translation: Once again Sulla prevailed; and then beyond all doubt he wielded a king’s power, albeit he had restored the republic.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: wisely, sensibly

examples.original: Et ille, mitteret omnes vel occideret, sapienter ut senior suaserat: hic armis exutos mittere sub iugum maluit, ut nec amici forent beneficio et post flagitium hostes magis.
examples.translation: The latter, with the wisdom of advanced years, had advised him either to let them all go free or else to slay them all;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: brisk, nimble, quick, prompt

examples.original: Multi in utroque exercitu sicut modesti quietique ita mali et strenui.
examples.translation: There were many in both armies obedient and law-abiding, as well as many unprincipled and energetic.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Praeerat classi Claudius Apollinaris, neque fidei constans neque strenuus in perfidia;
examples.translation: The fleet was commanded by Claudius Apollinaris, who was neither strong in loyalty nor determined in treachery;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Quod si animo strenuo fecissent, futurum ut adversarii non possent resistere, cum et intra vallum et foris caederentur.
examples.translation: If they would act vigorously, the enemy would be unable to resist, since they would be assailed inside and outside of their intrenchments.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Datames

definitions: English: causing wonder or admiration, wonderful, marvellous, extraordinary, singular, strange (class.).
English: out of tune, hence giving a disagreeable sound, harsh, rough.
Latin: Absonus; dissonans
Latin: Irrationalis, incongruus; delirus, stultus, ridiculus

examples.original: Illud autem absurdum est, quod dicitur beatum quidem futurum vel sola virtute, non futurum autem perfecte beatum.
examples.translation: But it is absurd to say that a man will be happy by virtue alone, and yet not absolutely happy.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English:  (class.)

examples.original: Decius se pro re publica devovit;
examples.translation: Decius sacrificed himself for the State;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ergo si sapiant et mentem verba sequantur, Devoveant umbras proxima quaeque meas.
examples.translation: So, could they think and words follow their thought, all the nearest would execrate my shade.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Haec tibi, quem meritis precibus mea devovet ira, Evenient, aut his non leviora malis.
examples.translation: Such ills shall befall thee whom my anger execrates with merited curses, or ills no less than these!
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to slip or glide away, to fall out
English: easily broken, brittle, fragile (class.; esp. freq. in the transf. signif.; cf.: caducus, fluxus).

examples.original: Fragilibus innititur, qui adventicio laetus est;
examples.translation: It is a fragile support—this delight in adventitious things;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed propera, ne vela cadant auraeque residant: Ut fragilis glacies, interit ira mora.
examples.translation: But be speedy, lest the sails sink and the breezes fail: like brittle ice, so perishes anger by delaying.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Forma bonum fragile est, quantumque accedit ad annos Fit minor, et spatio carpitur ipsa suo.
examples.translation: A frail advantage is beauty, that grows less as time draws on, and is devoured by its own years.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: hostile, inimical, enraged

examples.original: Ob ea infensus consulibus senatus, quorum cunctatione proditi socii essent, dictatorem dici iussit.
examples.translation: The nomination fell to Gaius Claudius Inregillensis, who named as his master of horse Gaius Claudius Hortator.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Huic infensi milites erant, quod semper adversatus novis consiliis fuisset et, ne particeps eorum esset, ab Lautulis fugisset.
examples.translation: The men were incensed at Salonius because he had always opposed their mutinous schemes, and had fled from Lautulae that he might not share in them.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quo cum Antiates aliique Volsci praeparatis iam ante, si quid ab Roma moveretur, copiis occurrissent, nulla mora inter infensos diutino odio dimicandi facta est.
examples.translation: There he was opposed by the Antiates and the other Volsci, with forces which they had levied in advance, in case any measures should be taken by the Romans;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A sketch, image, resemblance, likeness, kind
Latin: Quomodo
Latin: Eo modo quo

examples.original: Non habebant domos instar urbium.
examples.translation: They had no houses as big as cities.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quaecumque est veneris subita violata rapina, Gaudet, et inprobitas muneris instar habet.
examples.translation: She whom a sudden assault has taken by storm is pleased, and counts the audacity as a compliment.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Itaque ne si iucundissimis quidem nos somniis usuros putemus, Endymionis somnum nobis velimus dari, idque si accidat mortis instar putemus.
examples.translation: The prospect of the most delightful dreams would not reconcile us to falling asleep for ever: Endymion’s fate we should consider no better than death.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: To prolong

examples.original: Consules creati Q. Fabius et P. Decius, Ap. Claudius praetor, omnes absentes; et L. Volumnio ex senatus consulto et scito plebis prorogatum in annum imperium est.
examples.translation: Quintus Fabius and Publius Decius were chosen consuls and Appius Claudius praetor—all three being absent —and the senate passed a decree, which the people ratified, prolonging for a year the command of Lucius Volumnius.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a flight of steps or stairs, a staircase; a ladder, scaling-ladder.

examples.original: Et ne in muris quidem satis firma spe cum corona militum cincta iam scalis caperetur urbs, ad quattuor milia militum praeter multitudinem imbellem sese dedidere.
examples.translation: The Volsci, a race more spirited in beginning than in prosecuting war, were defeated in the struggle and fled in disorder to the walls of Satricum.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Postremo oppida quoque vi expugnare adortus, primo Cutinam ingenti ardore militum a volnerum ira, quod haud fere quisquam integer proelio excesserat, scalis cepit, deinde Cingiliam.
examples.translation: The soldiers fought with great fury to revenge their wounds, for hardly a man had come unhurt out of the battle; and first Cutina was carried by escalade, and then Cingilia.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: The north wind; pure Lat aquilo
Latin: Ventus qui a septentrionibus flat
English: the Corinthians (Pauline letters)
Latin: liber Novum Testamentum quae continens duae epistolae: I Corinthios: 16 capitula II Corinthios: 13 capitula
Latin: liber Novum Testamentum quae continens duae epistolae

examples.original: Cuius adversarii opem a Corinthiis petierunt ducemque quo in bello uterentur postularunt.
examples.translation: His opponents sought aid from Corinth and asked for a leader to conduct the war.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Timoleon

examples.original: Posthocproelium conlatum omne bellum est circa Corinthum ideoque Corinthium est appellatum.
examples.translation: After this battle the entire war centred about Corinth and hence was known as the Corinthian war.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

definitions: English: moist, wet, soaked, drenched (rare until after the Aug. per.).

examples.original: Plenum epulis madidumque mero Venerique paratum Invenies;
examples.translation: You will find him sated with feasting, drunken with wine, and ripe for amorous dalliance;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Cernit tabe iecur madidum, venasque minaces Hostili de parte videt.
examples.translation: He saw the liver flabby with corruption and with boding streaks in its hostile half.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a furrow made by the plough (cf.: lira, porca): sulci appellantur, quā aratrum ducitur, vel sationis faciendae causā vel urbis condendae, vel fossura rectis lateribus, ubi arbores
English: a little sharp point or sting (syn.: mucro, acus, aculeus).
English: to sit apart

examples.original: Non est, quod putes magnum, quo dissidemus;
examples.translation: There is no need for you to suppose that our difference is great;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cum Octavio collega Cinna dissedit: utrique horum secunda fortuna regnum est largita, adversa mortem.
examples.translation: Cinna fell out with his colleague Octavius; upon each of these prosperity bestowed a tyrant’s power, adversity death.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Inest hoc tempore haud obscurum odium atque id insitum penitus et inustum animis hominum amplissimorum: dissident principes: captatur occasio.
examples.translation: At the present time hatred does more than merely rankle; it is engrained and inured in the souls of our proudest;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: firmness, durability, strength (class.; syn.: constantia, firmitudo, perseverantia).

examples.original: Quid est autem, quare hanc animi firmitatem non credas in virum sapientem cadere, cum tibi in aliis idem notare sed non ex eadem causa liceat?
examples.translation: But why is it that you refuse to believe that the wise man is granted such firmness of mind, when you may observe that others have the same, although for a different reason?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a sailing, navigation

examples.original: Ad illud aes alienum solvendum opus est negotianti navigatione prospera, agrum colenti ubertate eius, quam colit, terrae, caeli favore;
examples.translation: To pay his debt of money, the business man must have a prosperous voyage, the farmer must have fruitful fields and kindly weather;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Erat quidem corpus validum ac forte sortitus et illi nomen latitudo pectoris fecerat, sed navigationes ac pericula multum detraxerant viribus;
examples.translation: To be sure, he was the fortunate possessor of a strong and sound body (his very name was given him because of his broad chesta);
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac sic accidit, uti ex tanto navium numero tot navigationibus neque hoc neque superiore anno ulla omnino navis, quae milites portaret, desideraretur;
examples.translation: And eventually, of all that number of ships and in all those voyages, not a single ship carrying troops in this or the previous year was missing.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: A Roman prœnomen, esp. of persons of the gens Claudia; hence

examples.original: Tandem invisi plebi consules magistratu abeunt, Servilius neutris, Appius patribus mire gratus.
examples.translation: Servilius had the goodwill of neither party, but Appius was in high esteem with the senators.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed ut praecipua commemorem, Appius Caecus societatem cum rege Pyrrho ut parum salubrem iniri dissuasit.
examples.translation: But to mention only the principal instances, Appius the Blind advised against forming an alliance with king Pyrrhus as not at all expedient.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Consul Appius negare ius esse tribuno in quemquam nisi in plebeium; non enim populi sed plebis eum magistratum esse;
examples.translation: The consul Appius declared that the tribune had no authority over anybody but a plebeian, seeing that he was not a magistrate of the people, but of the plebs;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: pallid (cf.: lividus, luridus).

examples.original: Hoc est, quod tristes docemus et pallidi?
examples.translation: Is this the matter which we teach with sour and pale faces?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: why not?

examples.original: Quidni tu ista vota saepe facias?
examples.translation: And of course you should offer those prayers frequently.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: At si inutile ministeriis corpus est, quidni oporteat educere animum laborantem?
examples.translation: But if the body is useless for service, why should one not free the struggling soul?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sane liceat; ut quidem iudicetis et feratis de meliore suffragium, quidni non permittam?
examples.translation: I shall of course allow you to pass judgment and cast a vote as to the better course.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: but, on the other hand/contrary; but yet; at least

examples.original: Ast alias manicaeque ligant teretesque catenae, Seque tenent remis: tecto stetit aequore bellum.
examples.translation: The sea was no longer visible, and the battle became stationary.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: Neutr., to rattle, crack, creak, rustle, clatter, tinkle, jingle, chink, etc.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; ŭi, ĭtum, 1

examples.original: Hic alter inperitus est, rebus suis timet ad omnem crepitum expavescens, quem una quaelibet vox pro fremitu accepta deicit, quem motus levissimi exanimant;
examples.translation: This man in his second state lacks knowledge fearing for his own concerns, he pales at every sound; any cry is taken for the battle-shout and overthrows him;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: altar, fittings for burnt offerings; burnt offerings; high altar

examples.original: Id primo quidam abnuentes iuraturos se obtruncati circa altaria sunt;
examples.translation: Some there were at first who refused to take this oath;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Admovebatur altaribus magis ut victima quam ut sacri particeps adigebaturque iure iurando quae visa auditaque in eo loco essent, non enuntiaturum.
examples.translation: The man was brought up to the altar, more like a victim than a partaker in the rite, and was sworn not to divulge what he should there see or hear.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to engrave in relief upon metals (esp. silver) or wory, to make raised work, to carve, engrave; later also, to cast

examples.original: Negant fas esse agi cum populo, cum de caelo servatum sit.
examples.translation: These assert that proceedings in assembly are sacrilegious when observation of the heavens is in progress.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ignota obscurae viderunt sidera noctes Ardentemque polum flammis caeloque volantes Obliquas per inane faces crinemque timendi Sideris et terris mutantem regna cometen.
examples.translation: The darkness of night saw stars before unknown, the sky blazing with fire, lights shooting athwart the void of heaven, and the hair of the baleful star—the comet which portends change to monarchs.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Natura sic ab iis investigata est ut nulla pars caelo, mari, terra (ut poetice loquar) praetermissa sit.
examples.translation: Natural Philosophy the Peripatetics have investigated so thoroughly that no region in sky or sea or land (to speak poetically) has been passed over.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to multiply, increase, augment.

examples.original: Trepidi magistratus missis ad arcem exploratoribus cum tela et armatos tenere arcem multiplicato numero audirent, avertunt animos a spe reciperandae arcis;
examples.translation: The city was thronged with fugitives, and men who were hardly yet awake and most of them unarmed, began battering down the gates.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ab hoc sunt imperatoris Galbae avus ac pater: avus clarior studiis quam dignitate—non enim egressus praeturae gradum—multiplicem nec incuriosam historiam edidit;
examples.translation: The former, who was more eminent for his learning than for his rank—for he did not advance beyond the grade of praetor—published a voluminous and painstaking history.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: corporeal, pertaining to the body

examples.original: Etiamnunc est aliquid superius quam corpus. Dicimus enim quaedam corporalia esse, quaedam incorporalia.
examples.translation: What, then, will be the term from which these things are derived?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or belonging to generation or birth, causing generation or birth, fruitful, generative, genital
English: in the same place, in that very place, just there.

examples.original: Ibidem saepius et per complures cantavit dies;
examples.translation: In the same city he sang frequently and for several successive days.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to burn around, to scorch (opp. exurere, to burn entirely up); also, with an extension of the idea, to burn wholly up, to consume

examples.original: Q. Fabium Ambustum dixerunt et P. Aelium Paetum magistrum equitum;
examples.translation: They designated Quintus Fabius Ambustus, with Publius Aelius Paetus to be master of the horse.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Dictus P. Valerius Publicola; magister equitum ei Q. Fabius Ambustus datus est.
examples.translation: The choice fell on Publius Valerius Publicola, who was given Quintus Fabius Ambustus as master of the horse.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Contigit hoc etiam Thetidi: populator Achilles Iliaca ambustis ossibus arva premit.
examples.translation: This befell Thetis also: Achilles the destroyer rests his charred bones upon the Ilian fields.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to command by a nod or sign

examples.original: Nutantem aciem victor equitatus incursat;
examples.translation: When their line wavered, the enemy’s victorious horse suddenly attacked;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Non vivunt contra naturam qui pomaria in summis turribus serunt? Quorum silvae in tectis domuum ac fastigiis nutant, inde ortis radicibus quo inprobe cacumina egissent?
examples.translation: Or raise waving forests upon the roofs and battlements of their houses—the roots starting at a point to which it would be outlandish for the tree-tops to reach?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: rich, plump, corpulent; of a country, etc., rich, fertile, fruitful.

examples.original: Spolia opima Feretrio Iovi lata.
examples.translation: Spolia opima dedicated to Jupiter Feretrius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Longe maximum triumphi spectaculum fuit Cossus spolia opima regis interfecti gerens. In eum milites carmina incondita aequantes eum Romulo canere.
examples.translation: By far the greatest spectacle in the triumph was Cossus, bearing the spoils of honour of the slain king, while the soldiers sang rude verses about him, comparing him to Romulus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: Aristotle, a very learned and distinguished pupil of Plato
Latin: Philosophus Graecus

examples.original: Itaque illa non dico me expetere sed legere, nec optare sed sumere, contraria autem non fugere sed quasi secernere’ Quid ait Aristoteles reliquique Platonis alumni?
examples.translation: Do you see therefore that between your master Zeno and Aristo there is a verbal harmony but a real difference;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Persecutus est Aristoteles animantium omnium ortus, victus, figuras, Theophrastus autem stirpium naturas omniumque fere rerum quae e terra gignerentur causas atque rationes;
examples.translation: Aristotle gave a complete account of the birth, nutrition and structure of all living creatures, Theophrastus of the natural history of plants and the causes and constitution of vegetable organisms in general;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Inviolability, sacredness, sanctity

examples.original: In incessu, in statu, in habitu, in omnibus motibus vestris nihil flat, quod inliciat cuiusquam libidinem, sed quod vestram deceat sanctitatem.
