examples.translation: In walking, in standing, in deportment, in all your movements, let nothing be done that might attract the desire of anyone, but let everything be in keeping with your holy character.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: asunder, apart, separately (freq. and good prose; syn. seorsum)

examples.original: Huius de vita et moribus plura in eo libro persecuti sumus quem separatim de eo fecimus rogatu T. Pomponii Attici.
examples.translation: Concerning this man’s life and character I have given fuller details in the separate book which I devoted to his biography at the urgent request of Titus Pomponius Atticus.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Cato

examples.original: Huc Mithridates cum uno cui maxime habebat fidem ante aliquot dies venit compluribusque locis separatim gladios obruit eaque loca diligenter notat.
examples.translation: Mithridates went to the spot several days in advance, with a single companion in whom he had the greatest confidence; and in several different places, which he carefully marked, he buried swords.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Datames

definitions: English: to be faint, weary, languid (cf.: languesco, marceo, torpeo).

examples.original: Ille caput labens et iam languentia colla Viso patre levat;
examples.translation: At sight of his father the son raised his sinking head and failing neck;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Nec minimam partem ex agris is maeror in urbem confluxit, languens quem contulit agricolarum copia conveniens ex omni morbida parte.
examples.translation: And in no small degree this affliction flowed from the country into the city, for the fainting crowd people of countrymen brought it, gathering from all quarters with disease.
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Postquam spatio languentia nullo Mutua conspicuos habuerunt lumina voltus, \[Hic fratres natosque suos videre patresque,\] Deprensum est civile nefas.
examples.translation: When their eyes met, undimmed by distance, and they saw each other’s faces clearly, then the horror of civil war was unmasked.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: luxurious

examples.original: Elegans, non magnificus, splendidus, non sumptuosus;
examples.translation: He was tasteful rather than magnificent, distinguished rather than extravagant;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Erat autem in Caesare cum facultas atque elegantia summa scribendi, tum verissima scientia suorum consiliorum explicandorum.
examples.translation: Caesar possessed not only the greatest facility and refinement of style, but also the surest skill in explaining his own plans.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Concinnus deinde et elegans huius, Aristo, sed ea quae desideratur a magno philosopho gravitas in eo non fuit;
examples.translation: Lyco’s pupil Aristo is polished and graceful, but has not the authority that we expect to find in a great thinker;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a tame swine
Latin: Sūs domesticus; animal speciei Sus scrofa seu S. domesticus
Latin: Sus domesticus; animal speciei Sus scrofa seu S. domesticus

examples.original: Semper enim boni assiduique domini referta cella vinaria, olearia, etiam penaria est, villaque tota locuples est, abundat porco haedo agno gallina, lacte caseo melle.
examples.translation: For the provident and industrious proprietor always has his store-room and cellars well filled with oil and wine and provisions;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a Roman surname in the Julian gens

examples.original: Non ita multo post Iuniam Claudillam M. Silani nobilissimi viri filiam duxit uxorem.
examples.translation: Not so very long afterward Gaius took as wife Junia Claudilla, daughter of Marcus Silanus, a man of noble rank.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

examples.original: Sed nec primum impetum barbarorum Silanus, nec secundum Manilius, nec tertium Caepio sustinere potuerunt;
examples.translation: Silanus could not withstand the first attack of the barbarians, nor Manilius the second, nor Caepio the third;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Caesar Mvltis de causis Caesar maiorem Galliae motum exspectans per Marcum Silanum, Gaium Antistium Reginum, Titum Sextium legatos delectum habere instituit;
examples.translation: For many reasons Caesar anticipated a more serious rising in Gaul; and he decided to raise a levy through the agency of Marcus Silanus, Gains Antistius Reginus, and Titus Sextius, lieutenant-generals.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to spring out, spring forth, to break forth, appear quickly (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; in Cic. and Caes. not at all).

examples.original: Nec cruor emicuit solitus, sed volnere largo Diffusum rutilo dirum pro sanguine virus.
examples.translation: No red blood spouted forth from the gaping wound, but a slimy liquid, strange and dreadful, came out instead.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: inactivity, laziness, idleness, sloth, listlessness, cowardice, worthlessness (syn.: socordia, desidia, inertia, pigritia, segnities; opp.: fortitudo, alacritas).

examples.original: Plura de extremis loqui pars ignaviae est.
examples.translation: To talk at length about the end is cowardice.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Postulamus ut ii, qui maxime ignaviam increpant, adsint nobis habentibus dilectum. Acerrimi cuiusque arbitrio, quando ita placet, rem agemus.” Redeunt in tribunal;
examples.translation: The most severe amongst you, since such is your pleasure, shall guide our procedure.” They returned to the tribunal, and purposely commanded to cite by name one of those who were present.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et quemadmodum temeritas et libido et ignavia semper animum excruciant et semper sollicitant turbulentaeque sunt, sic improbitas si cuius in mente consedit, hoc ipso quod adest turbulenta est;
examples.translation: And just as Rashness, Licence and Cowardice ever torment the mind, ever awaken trouble and discord, so Unrighteousness, when firmly rooted in the heart, causes restlessness by the mere fact of its presence;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an inborn or native quality, natural quality, nature (class.; cf. ingenium).

examples.original: Horum in quolibet cum indoles eadem quae in Alexandro erat animi ingeniique;
examples.translation: Any one of these was as highly endowed with courage and talents as was Alexander;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Numquid tu invisos esse Lacedaemoniis liberos suos credis, quorum experiuntur indolem publice verberibus admotis?
examples.translation: Do you imagine that the Lacedaemonians hate their children when they test their mettle by lashing them in public?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Atque ea in optima quaque indole maxime apparent, in qua haec honesta quae intellegimus a natura tamquam adumbrantur.
examples.translation: And these traits are most apparent in the noblest characters, in which the moral excellences, as we understand them, are already roughly outlined by nature.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a breast, pap, esp. of females, rarely of males; also, a teat, dug of animals.
English: the condition of beatus, happiness, felicity, blessedness, beatitude; a word coined by Cic.
English: of adverse, unfavorable, evil omen; ill-boding, inauspicious, ominous, portentous (cf.: sinister, funestus)

examples.original: Consistam lentisque oculis laetusque videbo Strata per obscenas corpora nuda vias.
examples.translation: I will stop, and leisurely with glad eyes gaze on naked bodies strewn on the unsightly roads.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quid, qui clam latuit reddente obscena puella, Et vidit, quae mos ipse videre vetat?
examples.translation: What of him who lurked in hiding while the girl performed her obscenities, and saw what even custom forbids to see?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to fill up, stuff, cram

examples.original: Eiusmodi vocibus referta sunt carmina, refertae historiae.
examples.translation: A single tree is not remarkable if the whole forest rises to the same height.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Semper enim boni assiduique domini referta cella vinaria, olearia, etiam penaria est, villaque tota locuples est, abundat porco haedo agno gallina, lacte caseo melle.
examples.translation: For the provident and industrious proprietor always has his store-room and cellars well filled with oil and wine and provisions;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an island in the Mediterranean Sea, on the coast of Asia Minor, renowned for its fruitfulness, its rich mines, especially of copper, and for the worship of Venus
Latin: Insula Graeca vicina Anatoliae Syriaeque

examples.original: Expeditio in Cyprvm III, 9Aderat fatum insularum.
examples.translation: The Expedition to Cyprus 9. The fate of the islands was sealed;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Post id proelium eundem Pausaniam cum classe communi Cyprum atque Hellespontum miserunt, ut ex iis regionibus barbarorum praesidia depelleret.
examples.translation: After that battle Pausanias again commanded the allied Greeks, being sent with a fleet to Cyprus and the Hellespont to dislodge the garrisons of the barbarians from those regions.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Pausanias

definitions: English: a wedge.

examples.original: Eo nisi corporibus armisque rupere cuneo viam.
examples.translation: Thither, by dint of main strength and arms, they forced their way with a wedge.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Praecipiti cursu vaesanum Caesaris agmen In densos agitur cuneos, perque arma, per hostem Quaerit iter.
examples.translation: With headlong speed and fury Caesar’s men charged the close-packed columns, forcing a way through shields and through soldiers.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: One who lays legal claim to a thing, a claimant; hence, also, a maintainer, defender

examples.original: Aut pia te caeso dicatur adultera, sicut Qua cecidit Leucon vindice, dicta pia est.
examples.translation: Or may an adulteress be called righteous for slaying thee, as she was called righteous by whose vengeance Leucon fell.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Contionante Vitellio postulantur ad supplicium Asiaticus et Flavus et Rufinus duces Galliarum, quod pro Vindice bellassent.
examples.translation: When Vitellius was addressing his troops, the soldiers demanded the punishment of Asiaticus, Flavius, and Rufinus, Gallic chiefs who had fought for Vindex.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to offer, sacrifice, immolate any thing in honor of the gods
English: , to swear together, or one with another, to band or combine together by an oath.
English: a slimy liquid, slime.

examples.original: Quorum nihil sapienti viro potest evenire;
examples.translation: But none of these things can happen to the sage;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ac ne principum quidem virorum insectatione abstinuit;
examples.translation: He did not even refrain from gibes at men of distinction;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Qua ut poteretur, virum eius Atticum Vestinum consulem in honore ipso trucidavit.
examples.translation: To possess the latter he slew her husband Atticus Vestinus while he held the office of consul.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to disapprove, blame, condemn, reject (class.; syn.: culpo, vitupero, criminor, etc.): multi, qui domi aetatem agerent, propterea sunt improbati, Enn. ap.
Latin: Putare aliquam rem non bonam esse

examples.original: Si sit aliquis malus, puto improbabitur;
examples.translation: If any man is bad, he will, I suppose, be regarded with disapproval;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Dum fuit Atrides una contentus, et illa Casta fuit: vitio est improba facta viri.
examples.translation: While Atrides was content with one, she was chaste also; she was made wicked by her husband’s sin.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Maxime fuit optandum Caecinae, recuperatores, ut controversiae nihil haberet, secundo loco, ut ne cum tam improbo homine, tertio, ut cum tam stulto haberet.
examples.translation: What Caecina would have most desired, gentlemen, was to have no quarrel with anyone: in the next place, to have no quarrel with such a knave;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Corinth, a celebrated commercial city in the Peloponnesus, pillaged and destroyed by Mummius, now the village Corinto or Gereme; it was situated on the Isthmus
Latin: Urbs in Corinthia, Graecia

examples.original: Uxores habuit Mummiam Achaicam, neptem Catuli proneptemque L. Mummi, qui Corinthum excidit;
examples.translation: He married Mummia Achaica, the granddaughter of Catulus and great-granddaughter of Lucius Mummius who destroyed Corinth;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Posthocproelium conlatum omne bellum est circa Corinthum ideoque Corinthium est appellatum.
examples.translation: After this battle the entire war centred about Corinth and hence was known as the Corinthian war.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

definitions: English: not foreseen, unforeseen, unexpected (class.)

examples.original: Tu ipse ex Siciliensi edicto hoc sustulisti; voluisti, ex improviso si quae res nata esset, ex urbano edicto decernere.
examples.translation: You yourself removed the clause from your Sicilian edict, merely expressing your intention to apply the principles of your city edict to meet any unforeseen contingencies.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sopater, cum hoc illi improvisum atque inopinatum accidisset, commotus est sane, neque in praesentia Timarchidi quid responderet habuit, nisi se consideraturum quid sibi esset faciendum;
examples.translation: Finding himself without warning in this unexpected situation, Sopater was greatly perturbed, and had no immediate answer ready for Timarchides, except that he would think over what he had better do;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Et forsitan, quem ille obrutum ignem reliquerit, ita ut totiens novum ex improviso incendium daret, eum se exstincturum.
examples.translation: And perhaps that fire which Fabius had left covered up, but so that it was continually breaking out into new flames, might be by him extinguished.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to lay the foundation of a thing, to begin, commence (syn. incipere; opp. absolvere, perficere; class.).

examples.original: Sed virtutem ipsam inchoavit; nihil amplius.
examples.translation: But of virtue itself she merely gave the germ and no more.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quod efficitur hac etiam conclusione rationis: Quoniam enim videmus esse quiddam quod recte factum appellemus, id autem est perfectum officium, erit etiam inchoatum;
examples.translation: The same thing is also proved by the following argument: We observe that something exists which we call right action; but this is an appropriate act perfectly performed;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: an old Italian deity. He was represented with a face on the front and another on the back of his head

examples.original: Bellvm Ligvricvm II, 3Peracto Punico bello secuta est brevis sane quasi ad recuperandum spiritum requies, argumentumque pacis et bona fide cessantium armorum tum primum post Numam clausa porta Iani fuit;
examples.translation: The Ligurian War 3. The Carthaginian war being ended, a period of rest ensued, brief, indeed, for the Roman people to recover their breath.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: a pitying, pity, compassion, commiseration (class.).
English: shaking, quaking, quivering, trembling, tremulous

examples.original: Aspicies oculos tremulo fulgore micantes, Ut sol a liquida saepe refulget aqua.
examples.translation: You will see her eyes shooting tremulous gleams, as the sun often glitters in clear water.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Aut quia crassior est certis in partibus aer, sub terris ideo tremulum iubar haesitat ignis nec penetrare potest facile atque emergere ad ortus;
examples.translation: Or else because the air is thicker in certain parts, therefore under the earth the trembling gleam of his fire hesitates, and cannot easily penetrate and come forth to its rising;
examples.author: Lucretius

examples.original: Haud magis expertus discrimine Caesar in ullo est, Quam non e stabili tremulo sed culmine cuncta Despiceret staretque super titubantia fultus.
examples.translation: Or was it greed for greater rewards that made the soldiers repudiate their cause and their leader, and again put up for sale the swords already stained with guilt?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: swiftness, fleetness, speed, rapidity, velocity.
English: Worthy of admiration, admirable, wonderful

examples.original: In edito stat admirabilis, celsus, magnitudinis verae.
examples.translation: He stands in a high place, worthy of admiration, lofty, and really great.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to run back, hasten back (class.).

examples.original: Fortuna recursus Si det in Hesperiam, non hac in sede quiescent Tam sacri cineres, sed te Cornelia, Magne, Accipiet nostraque manu transfundet in urnam.
examples.translation: If Fortune grant us a return to Italy, not here will these sacred ashes rest; but Cornelia will recover you, Magnus, and will transfer them from my hand to an urn.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Sed ubi totis castris in fama proditio, recurrens in principia miles praescriptum Vespasiani nomen, proiectas Vitellii effigies aspexit, vastum primo silentium, mox cuncta simul erumpunt.
examples.translation: But when the news of the treason spread through the whole camp, the soldiers ran to headquarters, where they saw Vespasian’s name put up on the standards and the statues of Vitellius overthrown;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: Jesus Christ
Latin: Vir creditus a Christianis esse Messias (Christus) et filius Dei
English: made of clay, earthen, fictile.

examples.original: Reliquae Pergamenae naves cum adversarios premerent acrius, repente in eas vasa fictilia de quibus supra mentionem fecimus conici coepta sunt.
examples.translation: When the other Pergamene ships began to press their opponents too hard, on a sudden the earthenware jars of which I have spoken began to be hurled at them.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

definitions: English: to move in the manner of waves, i. e. to wave, rise in waves, undulate, to move to and fro, be driven hither and thither

examples.original: Ergo et supra humana est et par sibi in omni statu rerum, sive secundo cursu vita procedit, sive fluctuatur et it per adversa ac difficilia;
examples.translation: He is therefore above earthly things, equal to himself under all conditions,—whether the current of life runs free, or whether he is tossed and travels on troubled and desperate seas;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Animum format et fabricat, vitam disponit, actiones regit, agenda et omittenda demonstrat, sedet ad gubernaculum et per ancipitia fluctuantium derigit cursum.
examples.translation: It moulds and constructs the soul; it orders our life, guides our conduct, shows us what we should do and what we should leave undone;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Reverti ad filium nostrum eumque inveni fluctuantem quibusnam verbis comprehendi posset illa cum iuratione promissio propter necessitates inruentes, quae possent eum ut abscederet, cogere.
examples.translation: I returned to our son, and found him at a loss for words in which to frame his promise confirmed by his oath, allowing for necessities that might occur to make his departure essential.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to wind or bind round
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; percŭcurri or percurri, percursum, 3

examples.original: Hoc ego si sic agerem, tamquam mihi crimen esset diluendum, haec pluribus verbis dicerem, per quae nunc paucis percurrit oratio mea.
examples.translation: If I were dealing with the charge as if I really had to disprove it, I should do so at length; whereas I am now dismissing it with a brief notice.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: pepper.
English: as, just as; exactly as

examples.original: Modus enim omnium prout necessitas erat;
examples.translation: For the limit everywhere corresponded to the need;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic prout a nobis tractatus est, ita nos ipse tractat.
examples.translation: As we treat this spirit, so are we treated by it.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et erant in civitate Lingonum octo Batavorum cohortes, quartae decimae legionis auxilia, tum discordia temporum a legione digressae, prout inclinassent, grande momentum sociae aut adversae.
examples.translation: Moreover there were in the country of the Lingones eight cohorts of Batavians, auxiliaries belonging to the Fourteenth legion, who at that time, owing to the discord of the moment, had withdrawn from the legion;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a small round fruit, a berry.
English: a gentle west wind, the western breeze, zephyr (pure Lat. Favonius); personified, son of Astrœus
English: a nest.
English: a boiling or raging heat, a violent heat, a raging, boiling, fermenting (class.; syn.: ardor, tepor, calor, aestus).
English: to laugh at, laugh to scorn; to scoff at, deride (class.).
Latin: Valde ridere, cum contemptu ridere
English: a period of five years, five years (class.)

examples.original: Consumetur, inquies. Scilicet exspectemus legitimum illud quinquennium;
examples.translation: It will be so spent, you will answer.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Atque id actum est praetore me, quinquennio ante quam consul sum factus.
examples.translation: And this took place while I was praetor and five years before I was elected consul.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Mam. Aemilius dictator censurae honorem, qui antea per quinquennium gerebatur, anni et sex mensum spatio finît;
examples.translation: Mamercus Aemilius, the dictator, limited the office of censor, which was wont to be held for five years, to the period of eighteen months;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: from heaven, by divine providence or influence (class.).

examples.original: Sed ut in ipsis dis immortalibus non semper eosdem atque alias alios solemus et venerari et precari, sic in hominibus de me divinitus meritis;
examples.translation: It is but right, conscript fathers, that collectively I should accord you the veneration due to the gods.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: A bath, a place for bathing

examples.original: Ii, quorum pedes dolor repetit, aut vino aut balineo abstinent.
examples.translation: Those whose feet are visited by pain abstain either from wine or from the bath.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non potest medicus per epistulas cibi aut balinei tempus eligere;
examples.translation: The physician cannot prescribe by letter the proper time for eating or bathing;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Adice nunc scordalum et furem deprensum et illum, cui vox sua in balineo placet.
examples.translation: Then, perhaps, a professional a comes along, shouting out the score; that is the finishing touch.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a black stripe in the shape of this fish, a black vein in the table-tops of citron-wood

examples.original: Lex de provocatione ad populum a Murena cos. tertio tunc lata est.
examples.translation: A law about appeals was then for the third time laid before the people by the consul Murena.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fannium Caepionem, qui cum Varrone Murena in Augustum conspiraverat, reum maiestatis apud iudices fecit et condemnavit.
examples.translation: Fannius Caepio, who had conspired with Varro Murena against Augustus, he arraigned for high treason and secured his condemnation.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Triumphavit L. Sulla, triumphavit L. Murena de Mithridate, duo fortissimi viri et summi imperatores, sed ita triumpharunt, ut ille pulsus superatusque regnaret.
examples.translation: One triumph over Mithridates was celebrated by Lucius Sulla and another triumph by Lucius Murena, brave men and great generals both, but their triumphs left Mithridates beaten and conquered—yet still upon his throne!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a fawning, like that of a dog

examples.original: Vulgus tamen vacuum curis et sine falsi verique discrimine solitas adulationes edoctum clamore et vocibus adstrepebat;
examples.translation: Yet the populace, careless and unable to distinguish between truth and falsehood, shouted loud the usual flattery, as it had been taught to do;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to free one's self from a connection with any one, to withdraw, leave, revolt from, = sciscendo deficere
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n.; īvi or ĭi, ītum, 3

examples.original: Mox circumlato eius per urbes, quae desciverant, capite Syria sine bello recepta.
examples.translation: After his head had been carried round the cities which had revolted, Syria was recovered without further fighting.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Primus statim impetus belli Bithyniam rapuit, Asia inde pari terrore correpta est, nec cunctanter ad regem ab urbibus nostris populisque descitum est.
examples.translation: The first assault immediately won Bithynia; whereupon Asia was seized by a general panic, and without delay our cities and peoples revolted to the king.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: His consulibus Fidenae obsessae, Crustumeria capta, Praeneste ab Latinis ad Romanos descivit. Nec ultra bellum Latinum gliscens iam per aliquot annos dilatum.
examples.translation: Praeneste went over from the Latins to the Romans, and it was no longer possible to postpone the Latin war, which had now been smouldering for several years.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: hopelessness, despair

examples.original: Sed ad desperationem nos vitia nostra perducunt;
examples.translation: But it is our vices that bring us to despair;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quin, ut censuram patris, ut tres consulatus, ut tot egregiae domus honores deceret, desperatione saltem in audaciam accingeretur.
examples.translation: No. You must prove yourself worthy of your father’s censorship, of the three consulships, and all the honours belonging to your famous house.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Libet aliquid habere quod vincam, cuius patientia exercear. Nam hoc quoque egregium Sextius habet, quod et ostendet tibi beatae vitae magnitudinem et desperationem eius non faciet;
examples.translation: For this is another remarkable quality that Sextius possesses: he will show you the grandeur of the happy life and yet will not make you despair of attaining it;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: thin, slight, slender, slim; meagre, lean
English: moisten

examples.original: Illis te manibus tangi, Briseï, sinebas, Imbutae Phrygia quae nece semper erant.
examples.translation: By those hands didst thou suffer thyself to be touched, Briseis, that were ever imbued in Phrygian blood;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Profecti Ap. Claudium, filium decemviri, praefectum urbis relinquunt, impigrum iuvenem et iam inde ab incunabulis imbutum odio tribunorum plebisque.
examples.translation: He was an energetic young man and imbued from his very cradle with hatred of the tribunes and the plebs.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a praising, praise, commendation; a eulogy, panegyric.

examples.original: Et cum aeque antiquus poeta ait ”laus alit artis,” non laudationem dicit, quae corrumpit artes.
examples.translation: To judge a man worthy of praise, is to praise him.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Aut sic et consolationes nega proficere dissuasionesque et adhortationes et obiurgationes et laudationes.
examples.translation: On this ground, you ought to say that consolation does not avail, and warning, and exhortation, and scolding, and praising;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: fifteen
Latin: Quattuordecim et alius. Numerus XV
Latin: quattuordecim et alius

examples.original: Prima acies hastati erant, manipuli quindecim, distantes inter se modicum spatium;
examples.translation: The first line, or hastati, comprised fifteen maniples, stationed a short distance apart;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ob easque res ex litteris Caesaris dies quindecim supplicatio decreta est, quod ante id tempus accidit nulli.
examples.translation: And for those achievements, upon receipt of Caesar’s despatches, a fifteen days’ thanksgiving was decreed, an honour that had previously fallen to no man.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Herodotus cum Roma revertitur, diebus, ut ipse putabat, quindecim ante comitia, offendit eum mensem qui consequitur mensem comitialem, comitiis iam abhinc triginta diebus habitis.
examples.translation: Herodotus on his return from Rome, fifteen days, as he imagined, before the election, found himself in the month following the election month, and the election over for a month already.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to make cool or cold; to cool off, cool (class.).
English: the eye-brow

examples.original: Haec disputamus attractis superciliis, fronte rugosa?
examples.translation: Is this what we discuss with contracted brow and wrinkled forehead?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: repulsively, disgracefully, shamelessly; in an ugly/unsightly manner

examples.original: Vel tu venandi studium cole: saepe recessit Turpiter a Phoebi victa sorore Venus.
examples.translation: Or cultivate the pleasures of the chase: ofttimes has Venus, vanquished by Phoebus’ sister, beaten a base retreat.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Haeserat in quadam nuper mea cura puella: Conveniens animo non erat illa meo: Curabar propriis aeger Podalirius herbis, Et, fateor, medicus turpiter aeger eram.
examples.translation: Lately my attentions were paid to a certain girl; she my passion did not favour: a sick Podalirius, I treated myself with my own herbs, and, I confess, I was a shamefully sick physician.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to chain or bind together (prob. not ante-Aug.)

examples.original: Conantes dicere prohibuit et in catenas coniecit.
examples.translation: To spy?” When they tried to speak he prevented them and flung them into chains.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ubi crudescere seditio et a conviciis ac probris ad tela et manus transibant, inici catenas Flaviano iubet.
examples.translation: But the troops saw through the ruse, thrust aside those who guarded the tribunal, and prepared to use extreme violence.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Primus invasit insulam Marcus Antonius cum ingenti quidem victoriae spe atque fiducia, adeo ut pluris catenas in navibus quam arma portaret.
examples.translation: Marcus Antonius made the first attack upon the island with such expectation of victory and confidence that he carried more fetters than arms on board his ships.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: fasten down; hence, to set slips, propagate by slips
English: a guest (pure Lat. conviva): parasiti Jovis, the gods, Varr. ap.
Latin: (In malam partem): qui cibi gratia assentatur, risum movet, aut contumelias patitur
Latin: conviva; et di, qui mensae eius adhibebantur
English: of or belonging to a classis.

examples.original: Cum classicum cecinit, scit non se peti;
examples.translation: When the trumpet sounds, the poor man knows that he is not being attacked;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Legio classica nihil cunctata praetorianis adiungitur;
examples.translation: The legion of marines without hesitation joined the praetorians.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Non proelia fessos Ulla vocant, certos non rumpunt classica somnos.
examples.translation: No battles call them from where they rest; no trumpet-call breaks their sound slumbers.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to use often, be in the habit of using; as a verb. fin. only a few times in Gellius in the

examples.original: Utar ergo illo non tantum tamquam recepto, sed tamquam usitato.
examples.translation: I shall, therefore, make use of the word, not merely as admitted, but as established.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to exhort, encourage: et dicerent castra capta esse, atque hos cohortarent uti maturarent, Quadrig. ap.

examples.original: Septimam decimam cohortem e colonia Ostiensi in urbem acciri Otho iusserat;
examples.translation: Otho had given orders that the Seventeenth cohort be brought from the colony of Ostia to Rome.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Nimium diu te cohortor, cum tibi admonitione magis quam exhortatione opus sit.
examples.translation: I am exhorting you far too long, since you need reminding rather than exhortation.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quinque cohortes, quas minime firmas ad dimicandum esse existimabat, castris praesidio relinquit;
examples.translation: He left as garrison for the camp the five cohorts which he regarded as least steady for action;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the whole side of an animal

examples.original: Eo nisi corporibus armisque rupere cuneo viam.
examples.translation: Thither, by dint of main strength and arms, they forced their way with a wedge.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Parcite ne castris: vallo tendetis in illo, Unde acies peritura venit.” Vix cuncta locuto Caesare quemque suum munus trahit, armaque raptim Sumpta Ceresque viris.
examples.translation: Be not careful of your camp; you will find quarters behind the rampart from which the doomed army is coming.” Almost before Caesar had ceased to speak, each went to his appointed task;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Qua pacta acceptaque cum parata cetera ad bellum essent sequique Etruscus iuberet, infitias eunt mercedem se belli Romanis inferendi pactos: quidquid acceperint accepisse ne agrum Etruscum vastarent armisque lacesserent cultores;
examples.translation: When this had been agreed upon and received, and the Etruscans, having completed the rest of their preparations for the war, bade their new allies follow them, the Gauls demurred.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: glowing hot, burning, fiery, glowing (class.; syn.: tepidus, calidus, ignĕus).

examples.original: Iamque dies medius tenues contraxerat umbras, Inque pari spatio vesper et ortus erant: Ecce, redit Cephalus silvis, Cyllenia proles, Oraque fontana fervida pulsat aqua.
examples.translation: And now midday had drawn short the unsubstantial shadows, and evening and morning were equally removed: lo! Cephalus, son of Cyllene, returns from the woods, and scatters spring water on his glowing cheeks.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Fonte cadit modico parvisque inpellitur undis Puniceus Rubicon, cum fervida canduit aestas, Perque imas serpit valles et Gallica certus Limes ab Ausoniis disterminat arva colonis.
examples.translation: The ruddy river Rubicon glides through the bottom of the valleys and serves as a fixed landmark to divide the land of Gaul from the farms of Italy.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: lowness (acc. to humilis, I.).
English: mist, vapor, fog, smoke, exhalation (syn.: nubes, nimbus).
English: to glide forward, to slide or slip along, to fall down (class.; in Cic. most freq. in a trop. sense).

examples.original: Quod responsum cum ipsi aliter interpretarentur, Iunius Brutus, qui cum his profectus erat, prolapsum se simulavit et terram osculatus est;
examples.translation: This response the princes themselves explained otherwise, but Junius Brutus, who had accompanied them, pretended to fall upon his face, and kissed the earth.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Brutus alio ratus spectare Pythicam vocem velut si prolapsus cecidisset terram osculo contigit, scilicet quod ea communis mater omnium mortalium esset.
examples.translation: Brutus thought the Pythian utterance had another meaning; pretending to stumble, he fell and touched his lips to Earth, evidently regarding her as the common mother of all mortals.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to roll back; to unroll, unwind; to revolve, return (class.; esp. freq. since the Aug. per.).

examples.original: Saepe enim in hiemem revolvitur.
examples.translation: For it often slides back into winter weather.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a drum, timbrel, tambour, tambourine.
English: to fasten together, to confine, hold in check, to repress, curb, restrain

examples.original: Homicidia compescimus et singulas caedes;
examples.translation: We check manslaughter and isolated murders;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to stand around in a circle, to take a station round; and, with the

examples.original: Quid ista, quae nos circumstant, alunt, sustinent?
examples.translation: What becomes of all these things that surround us, support us, sustain us?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to cry aloud = clamare: SI PARENTEM PVER VERBERIT. AST OLLE PLORASSIT
Latin: multis lacrimis et clamore flere
Latin: deflere, lamentari aliquid
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

definitions: English: wanton, petulant, sportive, playful, frolicsome, frisky, (syn.: petulans, procax).
English: backwards, bent backwards, thrown backwards, lying on the back

examples.original: Seneca Lvcilio svo salvtem Est quidem, mi Lucili, supinus et neglegens, qui in amici memoriam ab aliqua regione admonitus reducitur;
examples.translation: On the Shortness of Life A man is indeed lazy and careless, my dear Lucilius, if he is reminded of a friend only by seeing some landscape which stirs the memory;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Of or belonging to music, musical (class.).

examples.original: Nam et in arte musica quod bonum est, facit musicum.
examples.translation: For example, that which is good in the art of music makes the musician.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Bonum in arte musica duobus modis dicitur, alterum, quo effectus musici adiuvatur, alterum, quo ars.
examples.translation: Now the musical instruments have to do with his performance,—such as flutes and organs and harps;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: six hundred each.

examples.original: Hic locus ab hoste circiter passus sescentos, uti dictum est, aberat.
examples.translation: The spot, as has been said, was about six hundred paces away from the enemy.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Sedecim dico iudices, ut Oppianicus absolveretur, corrumpendos fuisse: ad Staienum sescenta quadraginta milia nummum esse delata.
examples.translation: I depose that, to secure the acquittal of Oppianicus sixteen jurors would have had to be bribed: 640,000 sesterces were paid to Staienus.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: sharply, vigilantly, fiercely; severely, steadfastly; keenly, accurately
Latin: Acri modo

examples.original: Pugnatum est ab utrisque acriter.
examples.translation: The fighting was fierce on both sides.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Germani acrius usque ad munitiones secuntur.
examples.translation: The Germans pursued most vigorously right up to the fortifications.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Ex his Pullo, cum acerrime ad munitiones pugnaretur, ”Quid dubitas,” inquit, ”Vorene?
examples.translation: One of them, Pullo, when the fight was fiercest by the entrenchments, said: ”Why hesitate, Vorenus?
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to lie in ambush, lie in wait for; constr. with

examples.original: Caesar ad colloquium Caesar adduceret: vereri se, ne per insidias ab eo circumveniretur: uterque cum equitatu veniret: alia ratione sese non esse venturum.
examples.translation: Caesar did not wish the parley to be broken off upon an excuse thus interposed; at the same time he could not venture to entrust his personal safety to Gallic horse.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Heraclius interea, cum omnes insidias fortunis suis a praetore fieri videret, capit consilium de amicorum et propinquorum sententia non adesse ad iudicium.
examples.translation: Heraclius meanwhile, seeing that every sort of treacherous device to undo him was being employed by the chief magistrate, took the advice of his friends and kinsmen, and resolved not to appear in court.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Equites cum intrare fumum et flammam densissimam timerent ac, si qui cupidius intraverant, vix suorum ipsi priores partes animadverterent equorum, insidias veriti liberam facultatem sui recipiendi Bellovacis dederunt.
examples.translation: The cavalry feared to enter the smoke and the thick belt of flame, and even if any more eager spirits entered therein, they scarce could make out the front part of their own horses;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: the hair of the head

examples.original: Et neglecta decet multas coma;
examples.translation: Even neglected hair is becoming to many;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Huic decet inflatos laxe iacuisse capillos: Illa sit adstrictis impedienda comis;
examples.translation: This one it beseems to let her waving locks lie loose;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quasque fuisse tibi canas a virgine iuras, Spargentur subito per caput omne comae.
examples.translation: And the white hairs that you swear have been there since maidenhood will suddenly be scattered over all your head.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to set, place, or post one's self before any thing (class.; syn.: adversor, repugno).

examples.original: Ea ne impedirent tribuni dictatoris obstitit metus.
examples.translation: The awe in which the tribunes held the dictator prevented them from interfering with the trial.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cum iam haud ita longe abesset a Peloponneso, obsistere ei conati sunt Athenienses et Boeotii ceterique eorum socii apud Coroneam;
examples.translation: He was already nearing the Peloponnesus, when the Athenians, the Boeotians and their allies attempted to stop him at Coronea;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Agesilaus

examples.original: Obstitit Antonius datisque defensoribus ad Vespasianum dimisit.
examples.translation: Antonius interposed, gave him a guard, and sent him to Vespasian.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: one that ploughs, a ploughman; freq.

examples.original: Hic tibi etiam multo magis quam paulo ante in aratoribus videndum et considerandum est quid velis.
examples.translation: And here you must consider, as with the farmers just now, but a good deal more carefully still, what line you mean to take.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Da mihi hoc, iam tibi maximam partem defensionis praecideris; non enim poteris aratores tibi iratos esse atque inimicos dicere.
examples.translation: Allow me this and instantly you have cut away the main prop of your defence, being then unable to allege that the farmers are angry and hostile.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Postulo ut mihi respondeat qui sit is Verrucius, mercator an negotiator an arator an pecuarius, in Sicilia sit an iam decesserit.
examples.translation: I demanded therefore that Carpinatius should tell me who this Verrucius was, merchant or banker or arable or pastoral farmer, and whether he was still in Sicily or had gone away.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the quality of bearing, suffering, or enduring, patience, endurance.

examples.original: Deinde etiam tormentorum fortis patientia optabilis est.
examples.translation: And, lastly, because a brave endurance even under torture is desirable.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ad contemnendam patientiam malorum animus patientia pervenit;
examples.translation: By enduring ills the mind attains contempt for the endurance of them;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Hic et bella gerebat ut adulescens, cum plane grandis esset, et Hannibalem iuveniliter exsultantem patientia sua molliebat;
examples.translation: Though quite old he waged war like a young man, and by his patient endurance checked the boyish impetuosity of Hannibal.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to pile or heap up (class.; syn.: struo, aedifico, condo, fundo).
Latin: Struere, aedificere

examples.original: Flaminius censor viam Flaminiam muniit et circum Flaminium exstruxit.
examples.translation: The censor Gaius Flaminius built the Flaminian Way and the Flaminian Circus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to flow forth or along (class.).
English: bile (the bilious fluid secreted by the liver, jecur, while fel is the vessel in which the fluid is contained): rufa, viridis, nigra, Ceis. 7, 18
English: An olive
Latin: Fructus oleae
Latin: Ipsa arbor
English: contrary to custom, unaccustomed to a thing; unusual

examples.original: Crescit insolenti superbia, crudelitas saevo, malignitas livido.
examples.translation: The haughty man increases his arrogance, the ruthless man his cruelty, the slanderer his spitefulness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Non tam insolens sum, quod Iovem esse me dico, quam ineruditus, quod Minervam sororem Iovis esse existimo.
examples.translation: My insolence in calling myself Jupiter is not so great as my ignorance in thinking that Minerva is Jupiter’s sister.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: these (beams) were held together by timbers laid in a straight direction
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; xŭi, xtum, 3

examples.original: Neque enim de more carinas Extendunt puppesque levant, sed firma gerendis Molibus insolito contexunt robora ductu.
examples.translation: They built no long hulls, no high sterns, as the custom is, but joined stout planks together on unwonted lines to carry heavy structures.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: to incite, excite, stimulate, instigate, provoke, exasperate

examples.original: Sic fraus proditorum irrita fuit.
examples.translation: Thus the deceit of the traitors proved fruitless.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Movet cerebrum non uno genere; alios in aliud irritat, hos in potentiam, illos in luxuriam.
examples.translation: It stirs the brain in more ways than one, goading men on to various aims,—some to power, and others to high living.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Si tibi magistratum abrogasset, minore ignominia te affecisset quam cum ea quae magistratu gessisti sustulit atque irrita iussit esse.
examples.translation: Had Metellus deprived you of your office, he would have inflicted a lesser disgrace upon you than by thus cancelling your official proceedings and declaring them null and void.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to say often or emphatically; to declare, maintain, assert repeatedly (good prose).

examples.original: Maximum bellum patribus cum plebe esse dictitant;
examples.translation: They persistently declared that it was the plebs with whom the senators were chiefly at war;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mater Antonia portentum eum hominis dictitabat, nec absolutum a natura, sed tantum incohatum;
examples.translation: His mother Antonia often called him ”a monster of a man, not finished but merely begun by Dame Nature”;
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Inde L. Tarquinius regnare occepit, cui Superbo cognomen facta indiderunt, quia socerum gener sepultura prohibuit, Romulum quoque insepultum perisse dictitans, primoresque patrum, quos Servi rebus favisse credebat, interfecit;
examples.translation: For he denied the rites of sepulture to his own father-in-law, asserting that Romulus had also perished without burial.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to strike with terror, to frighten, affright

examples.original: Est lucum Silari iuxta ilicibusque virentem Plurimus Alburnum volitans, cui nomen asilo Romanum est, oestrum Grai vertere vocantes, Asper, acerba sonans, quo tota exterrita silvis Diffugiunt armenta.
examples.translation: Near Silarus’ groves, and eke Alburnus’ shades Of green-clad oak-trees flits an insect, named Asilus by the Romans;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to renew, repeat, celebrate anew; to repair, restore; to erect, make

examples.original: Bello perfecto donum amplum victor ad mea templa portato, sacraque patria, quorum omissa cura est, instaurata ut adsolet facito.”
examples.translation: When thou hast ended the war with conquest, bring to my temple an ample gift, and repeat and accomplish in customary wise the ancestral rites thou hast neglected.”
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a seat, settle, chair, stool

examples.original: Ea posteaquam numerata est, contentus hac iniquitate non fuit; palam de sella ac tribunali pronuntiat si quis absentem sthenium rei capitalis reum facere vellet, sese eius nomen recepturum;
examples.translation: From his chair of office on the tribunal he announced publicly that if anyone should think fit to prosecute Sthenius in absence on a capital charge, permission to prosecute would be granted;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Any thing laid or stored up, a hoard, treasure, provision, store.

examples.original: Nec vero quemquam senem audivi oblitum, quo loco thesaurum obruisset.
examples.translation: I certainly never heard of any old man forgetting where he had hidden his money!
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Nam quod ad thesauros Gallicos attinet, rem suapte natura facilem difficilem interrogatio facit.
examples.translation: And touching the Gallic treasure—the thing itself is simple, but your questioning makes it difficult.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to climb
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; di, sum, 3

examples.original: Igitur nuntiantibus Hernicis in fines suos transcendisse hostes impigre promissum auxilium.
examples.translation: Accordingly, when the Hernici reported that the enemy had crossed their borders, they were promptly offered assistance.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to render old, to give age or duration to a thing.

examples.original: Nunc quoque te admonebo: morbi sunt inveterata vitia et dura, ut avaritia, ut ambitio;
examples.translation: And I shall remind you once more: the diseases are hardened and chronic vices, such as greed and ambition;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Eorum querella inveterata non modo familiaritates exstingui solere, sed odia etiam gigni sempiterna.
examples.translation: By their ceaseless recriminations not only are social intimacies usually destroyed, but also everlasting enmities are produced.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In hac ergo morum perversitate desideratur solito vehementius aliquid, quod mala inveterata discutiat;
examples.translation: Amid this upset condition of morals, something stronger than usual is needed,—something which will shake off these chronic ills;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: an Ethiopian

examples.original: Nam et signis insedit examen et adsuetae cadaverum pabulo volucres castra quasi iam sua circumvolabant, et in aciem prodeuntibus obvius Aethiops nimis aperte ferale signum fuit.
examples.translation: A swarm of bees settled on the standards; the birds which usually feed upon corpses flew round the camp, as though it were already their prey;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: unclean (in a moral and religious sense)

examples.original: Minucia virgo Vestalis incesti damnata est.
examples.translation: Minucia, a Vestal virgin, was convicted of unchastity.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Opillia virgo Vestalis ob incestum viva defossa est.
examples.translation: Opillia, a Vestal Virgin, was buried alive for unchastity.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fortissimae rei inertissima adstruitur, severissimae parum seria, sanctissimae intemperans usque ad incesta.
examples.translation: What elements so inharmonious as these can be found united?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: To cast or

examples.original: Haec recta et consummata felicitatem hominis implevit.
examples.translation: When this is right and has reached perfection, man’s felicity is complete.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quemadmodum clepsydram non extremum stillicidium exhaurit, sed quicquid ante defluxit, sic ultima hora, qua esse desinimus, non sola mortem facit, sed sola consummat;
examples.translation: It is not the last drop that empties the water-clock, but all that which previously has flowed out; similarly, the final hour when we cease to exist does not of itself bring death;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to rub one thing against another; hence, in gen., to rub away, wear out or diminish by rubbing, to waste, wear away, weaken, impair, exhaust.
English: an ancient chronicle of the Roman people, which was written on linen, and preserved in the temple of Juno Moneta

examples.original: Licinio libros haud dubie sequi linteos placet: Tubero incertus veri est.
examples.translation: Licinius sees fit to follow without hesitation the Linen Rolls: Tubero is uncertain where the truth lies.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nomina consulum horum Licinius Macer auctor est et in foedere Ardeatino et in linteis libris ad Monetae inventa.
examples.translation: Licinius Macer testifies that the names of these consuls were given both in the treaty with Ardea and in the Linen Rolls in the temple of Moneta.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ibi mediis fere castris locus est consaeptus cratibus pluteisque et linteis contectus, patens ducentos maxime pedes in omnes pariter partis.
examples.translation: There, at about the middle of the camp, they had enclosed an area, extending approximately two hundred feet in all directions, with wicker hurdles, and roofed it over with linen.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to give help or

examples.original: Eos per se ipsi Latini adsumptis Hernicis sine Romano aut duce aut auxilio castris exuerunt;
examples.translation: These the Latins, acting independently, with the assistance of the Hernici, but without either general or aid from Rome, despoiled of their camp.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Mittuntur etiam ad eas civitates legati quae sunt citerioris Hispaniae finitimae Aquitaniae: inde auxilia ducesque arcessuntur.
examples.translation: They even sent deputies to those states of Nearer Spain which border on Aquitania, inviting succours and leaders from thence.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Publico auxilio nullo adiuti sunt, valuitque apud Veientes—nam de ceteris minus mirum est—pacta cum Romulo indutiarum fides.
examples.translation: Official aid there was none, and the Veientes (for there is less to surprise us in the others) held firmly to the truce they had agreed upon with Romulus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: without risk/danger, safely, securely

examples.original: In tuto pars tui melior est.
examples.translation: The better part of yourself is on safe ground.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Parumper subsidiarios tutatus est locus;
examples.translation: For a little while the reserves were protected by their position.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Servilius, lenibus remediis aptior, concitatos animos flecti quam frangi putabat cum tutius tum facilius esse.
examples.translation: Servilius, more inclined to gentle measures, believed that it was safer, as well as easier, to assuage their fury than to quell it.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a bean, Vicia faba, Linn.; Gr.
English: happily

examples.original: Cornelius consul in Sardinia et Corsica contra Sardos et Corsos et Hannonem, Poenorum ducem, feliciter pugnavit.
examples.translation: The consul Lucius Cornelius fought successfully in Sardinia and Corsica against the Sardinians and Corsicans and against Hanno, the Carthaginian general.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of or belonging to corn

examples.original: Re frumentaria comparata equitibusque delectis iter in ea loca facere coepit, quibus in locis esse Germanos audiebat.
examples.translation: Having secured his corn-supply and selected his cavalry, he began to march into the localities in which the Germans were reported to be.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Quintum Tullium Ciceronem et Publium Sulpicium Cabilloni et Matiscone in Aeduis ad Ararim rei frumentariae causa collocat.
examples.translation: Quintus Tullius Cicero and Publius Sulpicius he stationed at Cabillonum and Matisco, Aeduan towns near the Arar, to secure the corn-supply.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a stage-player
English: to comply with, attend to, conform to, submit to, obey (cf.: oboedio, obsequor, pareo; class.).
English: to pluck or pull away, to pull or tear out, to tear off or away (freq. and class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a.; velli, vulsum or volsum, 3

examples.original: Fallitur, Haemonias siquis decurrit ad artes, Datque quod a teneri fronte revellit equi.
examples.translation: Deceived is he whoever has recourse to Haemonian arts, and gives what he tears from the forehead of a foal.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quam tamen mihi ex illis mulierculis dabis vix retractis a rogo, vix a cadavere revulsis, cui lacrimae in totum mensem duraverint?
examples.translation: In the case of men, no rules are laid down, because to mourn at all is not regarded as honourable.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: A Roman proper name, esp. in the Sulpician gens; whence Servii is sometimes used for Sulpicii, Oth. ap.

examples.original: Servius Tullius Veientes devicit et populum in classes divisit, aedem Dianae dedicavit.
examples.translation: Servius Tullius conquered the Veientes and divided the people into classes; dedicated a temple to Diana.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tum Tarquinius necessitate iam etiam ipsa cogente ultima audere, multo et aetate et viribus validior, medium arripit Servium elatumque e curia in inferiorem partem per gradus deiecit;
examples.translation: Being much superior to Servius in youth and strength, he seized him by the middle, and bearing him out of the senate-house, flung him down the steps.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: fineness, thinness, slenderness, minuteness (syn. tenuitas).

examples.original: Quaedam inutilia et inefficacia ipsa subtilitas reddit.
examples.translation: And certain arguments are rendered useless and unavailing by their very subtlety.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or belonging to time, lasting but for a time, temporary, temporal (mostly postAug.)

examples.original: An cuiusquam tibi temporalis salus carior esse debuerat quam huius aeterna?
examples.translation: Or ought anyone’s temporal welfare to have been more precious to you than his eternal welfare?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Si autem pax humana tam dulcis est pro temporali salute mortalium, quanto est dulcior pax divina pro aeterna salute angelorum!
examples.translation: So let it be your necessity and not your choice that slays the enemy who is fighting against you.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: lengthwise

examples.original: Curio Dacia tenus venit, sed tenebras saltuum expavit.
examples.translation: Curio reached Dacia, but shrank from its gloomy forests.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: quietness, stillness, tranquillity.
Latin: Status sine vocibus
Latin: Status pacis

examples.original: Sed non multum ad tranquillitatem locus confert;
examples.translation: The place where one lives, however, can contribute little towards tranquillity;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Aeque reliqua quoque inter se paria sunt, tranquillitas, simplicitas, liberalitas, constantia, aequanimitas, tolerantia.
examples.translation: In like manner, the other virtues are also equal as compared with one another: tranquillity, simplicity, generosity, constancy, equanimity, endurance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Haec est, inquam, societas, in qua omnia insunt, quae putant homines expetenda—honestas gloria tranquillitas animi atque iucunditas;
examples.translation: In such a partnership, I say, abide all things that men deem worthy of pursuit—honour and fame and delightful tranquillity of mind;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of or pertaining to the Capitol, Capitoline

examples.original: Inde consules C. Menenius P. Sestius Capitolinus.
examples.translation: The next consuls were Gaius Menenius and Publius Sestius Capitolinus.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Legatos T. Quinctium Capitolinum et M. Fabium Vibulanum sequi se dictator iussit.
examples.translation: The dictator bade Titus Quinctius Capitolinus and Marcus Fabius Vibulanus follow him as his lieutenants.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cum M. Valerio, Mani filio, Volesi nepote quaestor erat T. Quinctius Capitolinus, qui ter consul fuerat.
examples.translation: Marcus Valerius, son of Manius, and grandson of Volesus, shared the magistracy with Titus Quinctius Capitolinus, who had thrice been consul.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: all-powerful, almighty, omnipotent
English: not drunk, sober (freq. and class.).

examples.original: Si ille sanus est, si compositus, gravis, temperans, ingenium quoque siccum ac sobrium est;
examples.translation: If his soul be wholesome, well-ordered, serious, and restrained, his ability also is sound and sober.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to drive before one's self, to drive, push, or urge forward, to drive forth; to hurl, propel, hurl or cast down, to overthrow
English: a devil
Latin: Daemon malus, praesertim Satanas
English: favorable, well-disposed, gracious, kind, propitious (class.; cf.: faustus, prosperus, secundus).

examples.original: Quod primo ut augurium caelo missum laetus accepit tribunus, precatus deinde, si divus si diva esset qui sibi praepetem misisset, volens propitius adesset.
examples.translation: This the tribune first received with joy, as a heavensent augury, and then prayed that whosoever, be it god or goddess, had sent the auspicious bird might attend him with favour and protection.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to flee to a place for refuge.

examples.original: Quibus rebus cognitis ex perfugis et captivis, Caesar haec genera munitionis instituit.
examples.translation: Caesar had report of this from deserters and prisoners, and determined on the following types of entrenchments.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Qui cum propter siccitates paludum quo se reciperent non haberent, quo perfugio superiore anno erant usi, omnes fere in potestatem L. Labieni pervenerunt.
examples.translation: The enemy had no place of retreat, by reason of the dryness of the marshes, their refuge in the previous year; almost all of them, therefore, came and surrendered to Labienus.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Eo ex finitimis populis turba omnis, sine discrimine liber an servus esset, avida novarum rerum perfugit, idque primum ad coeptam magnitudinem roboris fuit.
examples.translation: Thither fled, from the surrounding peoples, a miscellaneous rabble, without distinction of bond or free, eager for new conditions; and these constituted the first advance in power towards that greatness at which Romulus aimed.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: lovely, delightful, pleasant, charming
English: a drop of a fluid (cf.: stilla, stiria).
Latin: Minima pars aquae, vel alterius materiae liquidae

examples.original: Aquilium et in Ti. Guttam video esse subscriptum.
examples.translation: Aquilius and Ti. Gutta.a What does that tell us?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Illud igitur Iunianum per vim factum est, Bulbi et Popili et Guttae contra Cluentium non est: Staieni etiam pro Cluentio est.
examples.translation: Junius’s case, then, was the outcome of violence: those of Bulbus, Popilius, and Gutta do not tell against Cluentius; while that of Staienus positively tells in his support.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: the spring.
Latin: Tempus anni quod inter hiemem et aestatem stat, ubi arbores folia edunt

examples.original: Veri boni aviditas tuta est.
examples.translation: The real good may be coveted with safety.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Deinde accusatorem firmum verumque esse oportet.
examples.translation: In the next place, a prosecutor must show firmness and honesty.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ver enim tamquam adulescentia significat ostenditque fructus futuros;
examples.translation: For spring typifies youth and gives promise of future fruits;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to be in agilation or in violent commotion, to move to and fro, to rage, to toss, to boil up.
Latin: Aestus esse

examples.original: Cui enim dubium potest esse, quin si aestus malum est, et aestuare malum sit?
examples.translation: For who can doubt that, if heat is an evil, it is also an evil to be hot?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Niger inficit horror Terga maris, longo per multa volumina tractu Aestuat unda minax, flatusque incerta futuri Turbida testantur conceptos aequora ventos.
examples.translation: A shudder of darkness blackened the ridges of the sea; the angry deep boiled with a long swell, wave following wave;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Itaque aestuabat dubitatione, versabat se utramque in partem, non solum mente verum etiam corpore, ut omnes qui aderant intellegere possent in animo eius metum cum cupiditate pugnare.
examples.translation: In an agony of indecision, he kept shifting first this way and then that, not only mentally but physically, so that all those present could see how fear was contending in his mind with cupidity.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of favorable or
English: by name, expressly, one by one, in detail (class.)

examples.original: Et ipsos nominatim iuvenes, pari comitate utrumque, nunc laudibus nunc promissis onerat.
examples.translation: Addressing each of the young men by name, he loaded them now with praise and now with promises.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His adductis, in eis filio propinquisque eius omnibus, quos nominatim evocaverat, consolatus Indutiomarum hortatusque est uti in officio maneret;
examples.translation: When these were brought in, among them his son and all his relatives, whom Caesar had summoned by name, he comforted Indutiomarus and exhorted him to abide in loyalty.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Cui quidem cum Ciliciam dedisses, mutasti pactionem et Ciliciam ad praetorem item extra ordinem transtulisti: Gabinio pretio amplificato Syriam nominatim dedisti.
examples.translation: It was to such an one that you first assigned Cilicia; then you altered your bargain, and transferred Cilicia, again by an extraordinary bestowal, upon a praetor;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: acquire, or procure again; to recover, retrieve; to restore, repair, renew (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; not in Cæs.; cf.: recupero, redimo, reficio).

examples.original: Satius est amicum reparare quam flere.
examples.translation: It is better to replace your friend than to weep for him.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or belonging to the stage, scenic, dramatic, theatrical (class.).

examples.original: Scaenicos ludos et assidue et varii generis ac multifariam fecit, quondam et nocturnos accensis tota urbe luminibus.
examples.translation: He exhibited stage-plays continually, of various kinds and in many different places, sometimes even by night, lighting up the whole city.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: on the other hand, on the contrary, again, in turn
English: the southeast wind (pure Lat. Vulturnus)
Latin: ventus, qui ex parte flat quae meridiem et orientem solem spectat
English: Commercial intercourse, trade, traffic, commerce

examples.original: Impedit enim consilium voluptas, rationi inimica est, mentis ut ita dicam praestringit oculos, nec habet ullum cum virtute commercium.
examples.translation: For carnal pleasure hinders deliberation, is at war with reason, blindfolds the eyes of the mind, so to speak, and has no fellowship with virtue.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: white, hoary
Latin: Haud ater; candidus sine nitore

examples.original: Exiguum est, quod deinde canam;
examples.translation: My next point is a small one;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Videtur autem species eius, equus et canis.
examples.translation: A particular animal, however, is seen, for example, a horse, a dog.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quasque fuisse tibi canas a virgine iuras, Spargentur subito per caput omne comae.
examples.translation: And the white hairs that you swear have been there since maidenhood will suddenly be scattered over all your head.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: of or pertaining to the censor, censorial

examples.original: O quantum erat saeculi decus, imperatorem triumphalem, censorium, quod super omnia haec est, Catonem uno caballo esse contentum et ne toto quidem!
examples.translation: For part of the animal was preempted by the baggage that hung down on either flank.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Inde hortatu L. Valerii Flacci, quem in consulatu censuraque habuit collegam, ut M. Perpenna censorius narrare solitus est, Romam demigravit in foroque esse coepit.
examples.translation: Then, with the encouragement of Lucius Valerius Flaccus, later his colleague in the consulship and the censorship—as Marcus Perpenna, the ex-censor, was fond of mentioning—he moved to Rome and entered public life.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Cato

definitions: English: a delaying, lingering, in a good or (more freq.) in a bad sense, a tarrying, delay, hesitation, doubt

examples.original: Sed in tanta mole belli plerumque cunctatio;
examples.translation: But a war of such scope can never be undertaken without hesitation;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Hoc ut scias ita esse, ad omne pulchrum vir bonus sine ulla cunctatione procurret;
examples.translation: This can be proved to you by the fact that the good man will hasten unhesitatingly to any noble deed;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nullus cunctationis locus est in eo consilio quod non potest laudari nisi peractum.” Aperire deinde armamentarium iussit.
examples.translation: The soldiers immediately seized arms without regard to military custom or rank, with no desire to distinguish praetorian or legionary by their proper insignia;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to retard or to check the growth of; hence, in a more extended sense, to destroy, efface, abolish; trop.
Latin: Destruere, delere
Latin: Terminare, finire

examples.original: Graviora vectigalia aut abolevit aut minuit.
examples.translation: The more oppressive sources of revenue he either abolished or moderated.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: Omnia ea auctor fuit Cornutus matri eius ut aboleret.
examples.translation: All these Cornutus advised the poet’s mother to destroy.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

definitions: English: For whom no revenge is taken, unavenged, unrevenged, not vindicated.

examples.original: Fortissimi milites non tamen nec vivi nec post mortem inulti fuere.
examples.translation: But the heroic soldiers were not unavenged, living or dead.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Cur igitur tu, qui pietate ad accusandum excitatus es, hunc Asellium esse inultum tam diu sinis?
examples.translation: Then why have you,a who were impelled to prosecute by loyalty to your father so long allowed this Asellius to go unpunished?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Non ipse tyrannus Sufficit in poenas, non omnis regia Lagi: Dum patrii veniant in viscera Caesaris enses, Magnus inultus erit.
examples.translation: Ptolemy himself and all the house of Lagus are not enough to quit the score: until the swords of his own countrymen pierce the heart of Caesar, Magnus will remain unavenged.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: the milt or spleen.
English: a thong.
English: changeable, mutable (class.)
English: future time, futurity, after - ages, succeeding generations, posterity (class.)

examples.original: Qua posteritas in saecula mittet Septimium fama?
examples.translation: With what infamy will posterity hand the name of Septimius down to future ages?
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a going away, setting out, departure (class.): profectione laeti, Pac. ap.

examples.original: Si hoc profectio et non fuga est.
examples.translation: What think you they all supposed, but that we were certainly attainted of some sin;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: His rebus fugae similem profectionem effecit.
examples.translation: By this means he made his departure like a rout.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Instructi intentique signum profectionis exposcunt.
examples.translation: They were drawn up in line and eager for action;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: As it pleases, as you (they, etc.) will, at pleasure
English: to count over, reckon, calculate, compute (syn.: numero, expendo).
English: to make or utter any harsh, shrill, hissing, whistling, grating, or creaking sound; to creak, hiss, whizz, whistle, rattle, buzz
English: to smooth, furbish, polish (class.; syn.: limo, levigo).

examples.original: Primum enim ipsa illa quae subtiliter disserenda erant polite apteque dixerunt, tum definientes, tum partientes, ut vestri etiam;
examples.translation: In the first place, even the topics that required close reasoning they handled in a neat and polished manner, employing now definition, now division;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Una per aetherios exit vox illa recessus Verbaque ad invitum perfert cogentia numen, Quod non cura poli caelique volubilis umquam Avocat.
examples.translation: Their voice alone speeds through the remote parts of heaven, and conveys the words that bind the reluctant deity, whom no care for the sky and revolving firmament ever distracts from listening.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: To weep over a person or thing; to lament, deplore, bewail
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; ēvi, ētum, 2

examples.original: Flaccum iam adultum, cuius exitum sub nomine Daphnidis deflet.
examples.translation: Virgil grow up, and whose death he laments under the name of Daphnis.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Feliciorem ergo tu Maecenatem putas, cui amoribus anxio et morosae uxoris cotidiana repudia deflenti somnus per symphoniarum cantum ex longinquo lene resonantium quaeritur?
examples.translation: Do you, then, think Maecenas a happier man, who, distressed by love and grieving over the daily repulses of his wayward wife, courted slumber by means of harmonious music, echoing faintly from a distance?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to lay open, tear up, turn up the ground

examples.original: At cum maturas fisso nova cortice rimas Nux agit, ad partes pertica saeva venit;
examples.translation: But when the new nut in due season shows chinks in its splitting rind thither comes the cruel rod;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cor iacet, et saniem per hiantes viscera rimas Emittunt, produntque suas omenta latebras.
examples.translation: The heart is flattened, the entrails exude corrupted blood through gaping cracks, and the caul reveals its hiding-place.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a stade
English: Thracian; gladiator with saber and short shield, gladiator

examples.original: Quippe Thracas in res suas traxerant, atque ita industriam Macedonum viribus Thracum, ferociam Thracum disciplina Macedonica temperavere.
examples.translation: They had induced the Thracians to support their efforts and had thus tempered the Macedonian persistence with Thracian energy, and Thracian savagery with Macedonian discipline.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: grown-up, adult
Latin: Aetate grandis, qui non iam infans est

examples.original: Flaccum iam adultum, cuius exitum sub nomine Daphnidis deflet.
examples.translation: Virgil grow up, and whose death he laments under the name of Daphnis.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Hanc virginem adultam forma excellentem Appius amore amens pretio ac spe perlicere adortus, postquam omnia pudore saepta animadvertit, ad crudelem superbamque vim animum convertit.
examples.translation: But finding that her modesty was proof against everything, he resolved on a course of cruel and tyrannical violence.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a consoling, consolation, comfort (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.).

examples.original: Aut sic et consolationes nega proficere dissuasionesque et adhortationes et obiurgationes et laudationes.
examples.translation: On this ground, you ought to say that consolation does not avail, and warning, and exhortation, and scolding, and praising;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Posidonius non tantum praeceptionem, nihil enim nos hoc verbo uti prohibet, sed etiam suasionem et consolationem et exhortationem necessariam iudicat.
examples.translation: Posidonius holds that not only precept-giving (there is nothing to prevent my using this word), but even persuasion, consolation, and encouragement, are necessary.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger
