examples.original: Itaque quae sunt eorum consolationes, quae cohortationes, quae etiam monita et consilia scripta ad summos viros!
examples.translation: As a result, think of their consolations, their exhortations, even their warnings and counsels, addressed to men of the highest eminence!
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a raven

examples.original: Interreges Q. Fabius Maximus M. Valerius Corvus.
examples.translation: The interreges were Quintus Fabius Maximus and Marcus Valerius Corvus.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Collega Corvo de plebe M. Popilius Laenas, quartum consul futurus, datus est.
examples.translation: As colleague of Corvus they elected the plebeian Marcus Popilius Laenas to be for the fourth time consul.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Itaque omni ope adnisi sunt, ut maximum ea tempestate imperatorem M. Valerium Corvum consulem quartum facerent;
examples.translation: They accordingly bent every effort to elect to his fourth consulship the greatest soldier of that age, Marcus Valerius Corvus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to reckon up, count over, count out (class.).

examples.original: Longum est omnia enumerare proelia.
examples.translation: It would be a long story to enumerate all his battles.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

examples.original: Dixerunt Halaesini, Catinenses, Tyndaritani, Hennenses, Herbitenses, Agyrinenses, Netini, Segestani—enumerare omnes non est necesse.
examples.translation: Halaesa, Catina, Tyndaris, Henna, Herbita, Agyrium, Netum, Segesta—all these have spoken; no need to complete the list;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Reliqui arborum fructus vix specie figurave, non modo saporibus sucisque totiens permixtis atque insitis, enumerari queunt.
examples.translation: The other fruits found on trees can hardly be enumerated, from their diversity in shape and figure, without reference to their different flavours and juices, which have again been modified by repeated combinations and graftings.
examples.author: Pliny the Elder

definitions: English: to rise up, rise

examples.original: Non exsurgit in plantas nec summis ambulat digitis eorum more, qui mendacio staturam adiuvant longioresque quam sunt, videri volunt;
examples.translation: He does not stretch himself or walk on tiptoe like those who seek to improve their height by deceit, wishing to seem taller than they really are;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: wildness, fierceness, savageness, roughness.
English: unmindful, not thinking, forgetful, regardless, negligent of a thing.

examples.original: Volscos consilii poenam non metuentes necopinata res perculit; armorum immemores obsides dant trecentos principum a Cora atque Pometia liberos.
examples.translation: They had no thought of resisting, and surrendered as hostages three hundred children of the nobility of Cora and Pometia, and so the legions were withdrawn without a conflict.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: fitness, convenience, suitableness

examples.original: Ut enim opportunitas illa, sic haec de quibus dixi, non fiunt temporis productione maiora.
examples.translation: For these things that I speak of, like opportuneness before mentioned, are not made greater by prolongation.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to bring forth, beget, generate, procreate, produce (class.).

examples.original: Is Numitorem atque Amulium procreat;
examples.translation: He begat Numitor and Amulius;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Liberorumne causa? At procreare potest.
examples.translation: Is it because he desires, a child?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: which or what in number, order, etc.; of what number, how many (class.)

examples.original: Sed quoto cuique habere se contigit?
examples.translation: But how few men are blessed with ownership of self!
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: elder brother of Saturn, and ancestor of the Titans, called

examples.original: Ostendit terras Titan et sidera texit.
examples.translation: The sun revealed the earth and veiled the stars.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Thessaliam, qua parte diem brumalibus horis Attollit Titan, rupes Ossaea coercet;
examples.translation: Thessaly is bounded by the peak of Ossa in the quarter where the sun rises in winter;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ipse caput medio Titan cum ferret Olympo, Condidit ardentes atra caligine currus Involvitque orbem tenebris gentesque coegit Desperare diem;
examples.translation: The sun himself, while rearing his head in the zenith, hid his burning chariot in black darkness and veiled his sphere in gloom, forcing mankind to despair of daylight;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: clothing, a garment, vestment, bedclothes, tapestry, etc.
English: of or belonging to life, vital.

examples.original: Illa enim utilia vitaliaque sunt;
examples.translation: For the one condition is useful and life-giving;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Vix etiam fueras paucas vitalis in horas, Obtulit invitae cum tibi Caesar opem;
examples.translation: Scarce hadst thou been like to live for even a few hours, when Caesar brought thee succour against thy will;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: blood relationship, kindred, connection by birth.

examples.original: Haec moverunt Veientes, ac pro se quisque Romano saltem duce ignominias demendas belloque amissa repetenda minaciter fremunt. Tarquinienses nomen ac cognatio movet: pulchrum videbatur suos Romae regnare.
examples.translation: The Tarquinienses were influenced by his name and kinship: it seemed a fine thing to them that one of their blood should be king in Rome.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: of or belonging to a flamen.

examples.original: Thrasymennus lacus, tertium fulmen Annibalis, imperatore Flaminio.
examples.translation: Hannibal’s third thunderbolt was launched at Lake Trasimene, where Flaminius commanded the Romans.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Flaminius censor viam Flaminiam muniit et circum Flaminium exstruxit.
examples.translation: The censor Gaius Flaminius built the Flaminian Way and the Flaminian Circus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A transcript, copy.
Latin: Exemplum, copia
Latin: Res exscribenda

examples.original: Ipsis permittimus, unde velint sumere exemplaria.
examples.translation: We allow the purchasers themselves to get their samples from anywhere they please.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Idea erat Vergilii facies, futuri operis exemplar.
examples.translation: The ”idea” was Vergil’s outward appearance, and this was the pattern of the intended work.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ceterum hic ipse M. Cato, a cuius mentione haec disputatio processit, vereor ne supra nostrum exemplar sit.
examples.translation: But this self-same Marcus Cato, the mention of whom started this discussion,a I almost think surpasses even our exemplar.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to put up again, put back again; to lay up
English: to smear, besmear, anoint with any fat substance, an unguent, oil, etc.
English: the Roman corn-measure, a measure, peck, containing sixteen sextarii, or the sixth part of a Greek medimnus (class.)

examples.original: Monstras mihi, qui sint modi flebiles;
examples.translation: You are showing me what the doleful keysb are;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Documenta cladis cruentus aliquandiu Aufidus, pons de cadaveribus iussu ducis factus in torrente Vergello, modii duo anulorum Carthaginem missi dignitasque equestris taxata mensura.
examples.translation: As proofs of the vastness of the slaughter the Aufidus for a long time ran with blood; a bridge of corpses was constructed by order of the general over the torrent of Vergellus;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Sed omnium istius modi querellarum in moribus est culpa, non in aetate.
examples.translation: But as regards all such complaints, the blame rests with character, not with age.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: he who (that which) points out, a pointer

examples.original: Minucius index bove aurata donatus est.
examples.translation: Lucius Minucius gave evidence against him and was presented with a gilded ox.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Ea res est Helvetiis per indicium enuntiata.
examples.translation: The design was revealed to the Helvetii by informers.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Itaque non ego vobis ut indicem praedas vestras, sed vos id cogendi estis ut in medium proferatis.”
examples.translation: And so it is not I that must be forced to tell of your plunder, but you that must be compelled to give it up.”
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to render dark, to darken, obscure (class.; syn.: obumbro, opaco).
Latin: Obscurum reddere, tenebras afferre, noctem offundere

examples.original: Deinde non quaerimus quid obscuretur aut intereat quia sit admodum parvum, sed quid tale sit ut expleat summam.
examples.translation: In the life of pleasure of which we spoke, one pleasure is lost to sight among the many;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Sepositus per eos dies Cornelius Dolabella in coloniam Aquinatem, neque arta custodia neque obscura, nullum ob crimen, sed vetusto nomine et propinquitate Galbae monstratus.
examples.translation: About this time Cornelius Dolabella was banished to the colony of Aquinum. He was not kept under close or secret watch, and no charge was made against him;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Contra ipsis omnia opulenta et fida, Pannoniam Moesiam Dalmatiam Orientem cum integris exercitibus, Italiam et caput rerum urbem senatumque et populum, nunquam obscura nomina, etiam si aliquando obumbrentur;
examples.translation: On the other hand, our own resources are rich and certain: Pannonia, Moesia, Dalmatia and the East are with us; their armies are undiminished;
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to use passionate gestures, to throw one's self about (espec. for joy), to be transported, to exult, to be joyful, cheerful (cf.: exsilio, exsulto)

examples.original: In his igitur partibus duabus nihil erat quod Zeno commutare gestiret;
examples.translation: In these two departments then, there was nothing that Zeno need have desired to alter;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: His rebus gestis, ex litteris Caesaris dierum viginti supplicatio a senatu decreta est.
examples.translation: And for these achievements, upon receipt of Caesar’s despatches, the Senate decreed a public thanksgiving of twenty days.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Pauci ex proelio lapsi incertis itineribus per silvas ad Titum Labienum legatum in hiberna perveniunt atque eum de rebus gestis certiorem faciunt.
examples.translation: A few who had slipped away from the battle made their way by uncertain paths through the woods to the cantonments of Titus Labienus, the lieutenant-general, and informed him of what had happened.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a habitation, dwelling, domicile, abode (freq. and class.; for syn. cf.: aedes, domus, tectum, casa, tugurium, habitatio, mansio, sedes, etc.).
Latin: Domus, aedes

examples.original: An domicilium Romae non habuit?
examples.translation: There can be no tampering with these;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: In hoc obnoxio domicilio animus liber habitat.
examples.translation: In this dwelling, which is exposed to peril, my soul lives free.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Nulla illis domicilia nullaeque sedes sunt nisi quas lassitudo in diem posuit;
examples.translation: They have no homes and no restingplaces except those which weariness allots for the day;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: An explanation, exposition, interpretation (class.)

examples.original: Sed quid ego haec interrogo, cum, si ego tacitus abissem, tamen tibi ad voluntatis interpretationem meae dirigenda tua sententia fuerit?
examples.translation: But why do I put these questions, since, had I gone off without a word, nevertheless your thoughts should have been directed to the interpretation of my will?
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the country Arabia, divided by the ancients into Petrœa (from its principal city, Petra), Deserta
Latin: Arabia, vel Arabia Petraea fuit regnum antiquum, cliens Romanum, in regione hodiernae Iordaniae
English: to move forward, cause to advance, push onward, advance.
Latin: Porro seu ultra movere

examples.original: Itaque confestim castra inde in agrum Rusellanum promovit.
examples.translation: Accordingly he advanced without delay into the district of Rusellae.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Promovent et Samnites signa; insequitur acies ornata armata-que, ut hostium quoque magnificum spectaculum esset.
examples.translation: The Samnites, too, advanced their standards, which were followed by the battle-line in gorgeous armour—a splendid spectacle, though composed of enemies.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Eodem die castra promovit et milibus passuum sex a Caesaris castris sub monte consedit.
examples.translation: On the same day he advanced and pitched his camp under a hill-side six miles from Caesar’s.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a psalm
English: a stake
English: The dawn, daybreak, morning
Latin: Tempus ortus solis; exordium diei
Latin: ponitur pro regione orientali

examples.original: Hunc Aurora diem spectacula tanta ferentem Quam primum croceis roscida portet equis!
examples.translation: The day that brings so great a spectacle—let dewy Aurora speed it hither on her saffron car!
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a means of transport, a carriage, conveyance, vehicle.
Latin: instrumentum quo aliquis vel aliquod vehi potest

examples.original: Vehiculum, in quod inpositus sum, rusticum est;
examples.translation: The vehicle in which I have taken my seat is a farmer’s cart.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Mittaturne ad te accommodissimum tibi vehiculum?
examples.translation: Am I to send you our most suitable conveyance?
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Cum paucissimis servis, quos unum capere vehiculum potuit, sine ullis rebus, nisi quae corpore nostro continebantur, ego et Maximus meus biduum iam beatissimum agimus.
examples.translation: My friend Maximus and I have been spending a most happy period of two days, taking with us very few slaves—one carriage-load—and no paraphernalia except what we wore on our persons.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: feeling shame (at any thing good or bad), shamefaced, bashful

examples.original: Sed bene concubitus primos celare solebant. Plena verecundi culpa pudoris erat.
examples.translation: But at first they concealed their meetings well, and full of shamefast modesty was their sinning.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to be rank, luxuriant, abound to excess (not in Cic. or Cæs.).

examples.original: Licet enim sine luxuria agere festum diem.
examples.translation: For one may keep holiday without extravagance.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Laeta enim principia magistratus eius nimis luxuriavere;
examples.translation: For the luxuriant beginnings of this magistracy took on too rank a growth;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non enim luxuria, sed inpensa sollemnis est.
examples.translation: For it is not luxury but an expenditure sanctioned by custom.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a country of central Italy

examples.original: Etruria erat vicina, proximi Etruscorum Veientes.
examples.translation: Etruria was close by, and the nearest of the Etruscans were the Veientes.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Intentus perficiendo templo fabris undique ex Etruria accitis non pecunia solum ad id publica est usus, sed operis etiam ex plebe.
examples.translation: Being intent upon completing the temple, the king called in workmen from every quarter of Etruria, and used for this purpose not only the state funds but labourers drawn from the commons.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Kalendas Decembris P. Mario Afinio Gallo coss. Natus in Etruria Volaterris, eques Romanus, sanguine et affinitate primi ordinis viris coniunctus.
examples.translation: He was born at Volaterrae in Etruria, was a Roman knight, but was connected by blood and by marriage with men of the senatorial order.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

definitions: English: a Roman family name

examples.original: Furius inde et C. Manlius consules.
examples.translation: To Manlius fell the command against the Veientes.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: T. Quinctius Capitolinus quartum et Agrippa Furius consules inde facti nec seditionem domi nec foris bellum acceperunt;
examples.translation: They experienced neither domestic sedition nor foreign war, but were threatened with both.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Eo anno C. Furius Paculus et M. Geganius Macerinus censores villam publicam in campo Martio probaverunt, ibique primum census populi est actus.
examples.translation: In that year Gaius Furius Paculus and Marcus Geganius Macerinus the censors approved a public building erected in the Campus Martius, and the census of the people was taken there for the first time.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the undiminished or unimpaired condition of a thing.

examples.original: Ex eodem numero L. Cassius, Cn. Heius, pari et integritate et prudentia: quorum nullius sententia est Oppianicus absolutus.
examples.translation: To the same category belong L. Cassius and Gn. Heius, their peers in honour and in wisdom. Of these not one voted for Oppianicus’s acquittal.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: Mercury, the son of Jupiter and Maia, the messenger of the gods; as a herald, the god of dexterity; in speaking, of eloquence; the bestower of prosperity
Latin: Deus Romanus, nuntius deorum
Latin: Primus planeta Solis; classice etiam stella Mercurii vocatur
English: To change throughout
English: to follow one in order to come

examples.original: In quo quae vestra defensio futura sit coniectura assequi non queo.
examples.translation: And here I cannot guess what your line of defence is to be.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Verum ne sic quidem quicquam dignitatis assequi aut spem de se commodiorem in posterum facere potuit.
examples.translation: But even so he could not attain any public position or inspire more favourable hopes of his future.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: raving, furious, enraged, savage, fierce
English: of or belonging to a rhetorician, rhetorical.

examples.original: Sed me ipse cohibeo, ne a te rhetorice potius quam veridice agere existimer.
examples.translation: But I refrain, in case you imagine that I am quarrelling about words rather than seeking truth.
examples.author: Augustine

examples.original: Docuit autem et rhetoricam, ita ut quotidie praecepta eloquentiae traderet, declamaret vero nonnisi nundinis.
examples.translation: He taught rhetoric too, giving daily instruction in speaking, but declaiming only once a week.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Aurelius Opillus, Epicurei cuiusdam libertus, philosophiam primo, deinde rhetoricam, novissime grammaticam docuit.
examples.translation: Aurelius Opilius, freedman of an Epicurean, first taught philosophy, afterwards rhetoric, and finally grammar.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

definitions: English: as, just as, just as if; as it were, so to speak; as much as
English: of or be longing to a triumph, triumphal

examples.original: Quare triumphalia ornamenta et in brevi spatio duplex sacerdotium accepit, praeterea consulatum, quem gessit per duos novissimos anni menses.
examples.translation: For this he received the triumphal regalia, and shortly after two priesthoods, besides the consulship, which he held for the last two months of the year.
examples.author: Suetonius

examples.original: O quantum erat saeculi decus, imperatorem triumphalem, censorium, quod super omnia haec est, Catonem uno caballo esse contentum et ne toto quidem!
examples.translation: For part of the animal was preempted by the baggage that hung down on either flank.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: The quality of one blandus; a caressing, flattering, flattery

examples.original: Facilis est illa occursatio et blanditia popularis; adspicitur, non attrectatur;
examples.translation: The compliment and the courtesy wherewith we woo popular favour are an easy task.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: hail, a hail-storm.
Latin: Glacies rotunda ex nubibus praecipitata
English: forward, pert, saucy, impudent, wanton, freakish, petulant.
English: to turn, twist, twirl, swing, whirl or brandish, etc. (class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Reddite igitur animas, quas truculenta vestra manus contorsit, et, sicuti a nobis vester Hercules redhibetur, sic etiam a vobis tantorum animae reddantur.
examples.translation: Restore then the souls that your ferocious hand has destroyed, and as we give back your Hercules, so do you restore these many souls.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: a wasting away, melting, dwindling, consumption corruption, putrefaction; a wasting disease, consumption, decline; plague, pestilence.

examples.original: Cernit tabe iecur madidum, venasque minaces Hostili de parte videt.
examples.translation: He saw the liver flabby with corruption and with boding streaks in its hostile half.
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Id cumulatum usuris primo se agro paterno avitoque exuisse, deinde fortunis aliis, postremo velut tabem pervenisse ad corpus;
examples.translation: Then the taxes had been levied, in an untoward moment for him, and he had contracted debts.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Insertum manibus chalybem nigramque per artus Stillantis tabi saniem virusque coactum Sustulit, et nervo morsus retinente pependit.
examples.translation: She purloins the nails that pierced the hands, the clotted filth, and the black humour of corruption that oozes over all the limbs;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: workmanlike, skilful, ingenious

examples.original: Additae huic classi duae fabrum centuriae, quae sine armis stipendia facerent;
examples.translation: There were added to this class two centuries of mechanics, who were to serve without arms;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Intentus perficiendo templo fabris undique ex Etruria accitis non pecunia solum ad id publica est usus, sed operis etiam ex plebe.
examples.translation: Being intent upon completing the temple, the king called in workmen from every quarter of Etruria, and used for this purpose not only the state funds but labourers drawn from the commons.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a part of the city of Syracuse

examples.original: Quid est, Q. Naso, cur tu in isto loco sedeas?
examples.translation: What is the reason, Quintus Naso,a that you sit there in the chair?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Ut quondam iuvenes, ita nunc, mea turba, puellae Inscribant spoliis ”Naso magister erat.”
examples.translation: As once the youths, so now let the women, my votaries, write upon their spoils, Naso was our master.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Exauctorati per eos dies tribuni, e praetorio Antonius Taurus et Antonius Naso, ex urbanis cohortibus Aemilius Pacensis, e vigilibus Iulius Fronto.
examples.translation: During these same days four tribunes were dismissed, Antonius Taurus and Antonius Naso from the praetorian cohorts, from the city cohorts Aemilius Pacensis, and Julius Fronto from the police.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: to cheat, beguile, defraud one of any thing (class.; syn.: fallo, frustror, circumvenio; inesco, deludo, decipio, etc.).

examples.original: Fraudem profecto in re esse, et A. Sempronium comitiis plus artis adhibuisse quam fidei.
examples.translation: It was by his wrong-doing, they complained, that their relations had been defeated for office.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et senatui nimis atrox visa sententia est, et plebem ira prope armavit: fame se iam sicut hostes peti, cibo victuque fraudari;
examples.translation: Starvation, they said, was now being employed against them, as though they were public enemies, and they were being defrauded of their food and sustenance;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Libri XVII Periocha Cn. Cornelius consul a classe Punica circumventus et per fraudem, veluti in conloquium evocatus, captus est.
examples.translation: Summaries Summary of Book XVII The consul Gnaeus Cornelius was surrounded by a Carthaginian fleet and was made prisoner by fraud, having been lured out as to a colloquy.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: smoke, steam, fume
Latin: vapor visibilis cum particulis carbonis, etc exiens a substantia urenti

examples.original: Dimidium fere spatium confecerat, cum ex fumo castrorum eius suspicio adlata est ad Eumenem hostem appropinquare.
examples.translation: He had covered nearly half the distance, when the smoke from his camp led Eumenes to suspect that the enemy were approaching.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Eumenes

examples.original: Equites cum intrare fumum et flammam densissimam timerent ac, si qui cupidius intraverant, vix suorum ipsi priores partes animadverterent equorum, insidias veriti liberam facultatem sui recipiendi Bellovacis dederunt.
examples.translation: The cavalry feared to enter the smoke and the thick belt of flame, and even if any more eager spirits entered therein, they scarce could make out the front part of their own horses;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: that flees or has fled, fugitive (not in Cic. or Cæs.; cf. fugitivus).

examples.original: Nititur, ut profugae desint alimenta senectae: Heu!
examples.translation: He strives that my exiled old age may lack sustenance: ah!
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Idem per Scythici profugum divortia ponti Indomitum regem Romanaque fata morantem Ad mortem Sulla felicior ire coegi.
examples.translation: Again, when the indomitable king obstructed Rome’s destiny, I drove him in flight along the isthmus of the Scythian sea;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Aeneam ab simili clade domo profugum, sed ad maiora rerum initia ducentibus fatis, primo in Macedoniam venisse, inde in Siciliam quaerentem sedes delatum, ab Sicilia classe ad Laurentem agrum tenuisse.
examples.translation: Aeneas, driven from home by a similar misfortune, but guided by fate to undertakings of greater consequence, came first to Macedonia; thence was carried, in his quest of a place of settlement, to Sicily;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to be wept over, to be lamented, lamentable (class.)

examples.original: Monstras mihi, qui sint modi flebiles;
examples.translation: You are showing me what the doleful keysb are;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to see into, perceive, understand.
Latin: Videre, cognoscere, mente capere

examples.original: Quibus igitur in rebus vis intelligi potest, si in his non intelligetur?
examples.translation: What circumstances may be understood to amount to force, if not these?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Verum ita est, uti dicis. Te deiectum debeo intelligere, etiamsi tactus non fueris.
examples.translation: But you are right—I am bound to consider you ejected even though you were not touched, am I not?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quo tempore quantam vim naturae bonitas haberet et vera nobilitas intelligere potuistis.
examples.translation: That event enabled you to realize the force of natural goodness of heart and true nobility.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: of or belonging to magic, magic, magical

examples.original: Docta, quid ad magicas, Erato, deverteris artes?
examples.translation: Why turnest thou, learned Erato, to magical arts?
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: paleness, wanness

examples.original: Non caeli nox illa fuit: latet obsitus aer Infernae pallore domus nimbisque gravatus Deprimitur, fluctusque in nubibus accipit imbrem.
examples.translation: The darkness was not the common darkness of night: the heavens were hidden and veiled with the dimness of the infernal regions, and weighed down by clouds;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a wagon, wain, cart.

examples.original: Patres bene coeptam rem perseveranter tueri; conferre ipsi primi, et quia nondum argentum signatum erat, aes grave plaustris quidam ad aerarium convehentes speciosam etiam conlationem faciebant.
examples.translation: They were themselves the first to contribute, and since there was as yet no silver coinage, some of them brought uncoined bronze in waggons to the treasury, and even made a display of their contributing.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Non dicam illinc hoc signum ablatum esse et illud: hoc dico, nullum te Aspendi signum, Verres, reliquisse, omnia ex fanis, ex locis publicis, palam, spectantibus omnibus, plaustris evecta exportataque esse.
examples.translation: I shall not allege that from this town this or that particular statue was removed. My charge is that Verres did not leave one single statue behind;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a small, soft feather; in

examples.original: Pluma tenebatur, quam remisit et fugit.
examples.translation: You grasped him only by a feather;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: the quality of asper, unevenness, roughness (opp. 2. levitas).

examples.original: Asperitas autem vocis fit ab asperitate principiorum, et item levor levore creatur.
examples.translation: The roughness of voice, moreover, comes from roughness of the elements, as also smoothness from smoothness.
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: just as much

examples.original: Ab ipsa enim semper tantundem absumus.
examples.translation: For death itself is always the same distance from us;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quotiens in mentem venerit, quantum tibi in servum liceat, veniat in mentem tantundem in te domino tuo licere.
examples.translation: And as often as you reflect how much power you have over a slave, remember that your master has just as much power over you.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Sed si aliquem amicum existimas, cui non tantundem credis quantum tibi, vehementer erras et non satis nosti vim verae amicitiae.
examples.translation: But if you consider any man a friend whom you do not trust as you trust yourself, you are mightily mistaken and you do not sufficiently understand what true friendship means.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: Neutr., to bring a war to an end, to finish a war. So rare in the act. form
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Eodem impetu castra capta debellatumque est.
examples.translation: By a single rush the camp was captured and the war ended.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et Mithridates quidem nocte illa debellatus est.
examples.translation: That night saw the final defeat of Mithridates;
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Debellandae sunt in primis voluptates, quae, ut vides, saeva quoque ad se ingenia rapuerunt.
examples.translation: To be conquered, in the first place, are pleasures, which, as you see, have carried off even the sternest characters.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of good or noble birth, noble, eminent (class.).
Latin: Natu nobili
Latin: Magnanimus

examples.original: Ne existimes nos solos generosa verba iactare;
examples.translation: But you must not think that our school alone can utter noble words;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Est tibi rure bono generosae fertilis uvae Vinea?
examples.translation: You have a fruitful estate and a vineyard abundant in fine grapes?
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Magna et generosa res est humanus animus: nullos sibi poni nisi communes et cum deo terminos patitur.
examples.translation: The human soul is a great and noble thing; it permits of no limits except those which can be shared even by the gods.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: intellectual, superior in intellect, endowed with a good capacity, gifted with genius, of good natural talents or abilities, clever, ingenious.

examples.original: Quod simul ut sensit, ”nunc, nunc, o Daedale,” dixit: ”Materiam, qua sis ingeniosus, habes.
examples.translation: Which when he knew, he said, ”Now, Daedalus, now is your chance to show your wit. Lo!
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: Sharing property with one (as brother, sister, relative), living in community of goods, partaking of in common

examples.original: At ille sapiens nihil iudicat suum magis quam cuius illi cum humano genere consortium est.
examples.translation: But our philosopher considers nothing more truly his own than that which he shares in partnership with all mankind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: A painter
Latin: Qui pingit
English: a place where trees are planted (esp. trees, about which the vine was trained), an orchard, plantation, vineyard planted with trees
English: a moving, motion (freq. and class.).
Latin: Factum movendi
Latin: mōtus < moveō

examples.original: Nulla sine motu ars, nulla mutatio est.
examples.translation: There is no art without motion, no change of any kind.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Reliquum anni quietum ab urbanis motibus et ab externis mansit.
examples.translation: The remainder of the year passed without disturbances in either domestic or foreign relations.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Tu T. Quincti, equitem intentus ad primum initium moti certaminis teneas;
examples.translation: Do you, Titus Quinctius, hold back your cavalry and watch for the first beginning of the mellay;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a. [jocus], to jest, joke (class.)

examples.original: In capitis mei levitatem iocatus est et in oculorum valitudinem et in crurum gracilitatem et in staturam.
examples.translation: Some jest at the baldness of my head, the weakness of my eyes, the thinness of my legs, my build.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to shake or toss violently (class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. freq. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

definitions: English: Bringing pestilence, pestilential

examples.original: Evidentissimum id fuit, quod, quacumque equo invectus est, ibi haud secus quam pestifero sidere icti pavebant;
examples.translation: This was most clearly seen in that, wherever he rode, men cowered as though blasted by some baleful star;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a pond in which fish are kept, a fish-pond.

examples.original: Cum esset in aedibus armarium, in quo sciret esse nummorum aliquantum et auri, noctu duos conservos dormientes occidit in piscinamque deiecit: ipse armarii fundum exsecuit, et HS . .
examples.translation: There was a safe in the house which he knew to contain a quantity of cash and of gold;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: offensive, foul, noisome, shocking, hideous, loathsome (class.; syn.: foedus, putidus).
English: eleven
Latin: Decem et alius. Numerus XI
Latin: Decem et alius

examples.original: Infestam inde patribus plebem interreges cum accepissent, ad undecimum interregem seditionibus certatum est.
examples.translation: The interreges found the commons hostile to the patricians, and the factional struggle continued until there had been eleven interreges.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to sound or ring again, to resound

examples.original: Feliciorem ergo tu Maecenatem putas, cui amoribus anxio et morosae uxoris cotidiana repudia deflenti somnus per symphoniarum cantum ex longinquo lene resonantium quaeritur?
examples.translation: Do you, then, think Maecenas a happier man, who, distressed by love and grieving over the daily repulses of his wayward wife, courted slumber by means of harmonious music, echoing faintly from a distance?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: A bivālve shell-fish, mussel
English: name of a Roman gens.

examples.original: Fusae Rutili copiae, fusae Caepionis.
examples.translation: The forces both of Rutilius and of Caepio were routed.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Exilium Metellus fortiter tulit, Rutilius etiam libenter;
examples.translation: Exile was endured by Metellus with courage, by Rutilius even with gladness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Damnationem suam Rutilius sic tulit, tamquam nihil illi molestum aliud esset quam quod male iudicaretur.
examples.translation: Sentence of Conviction was borne by Rutilius as if the injustice of the decision were the only thing which annoyed him.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to give ear, hearken, listen to one
Latin: Alicui aures praebere
Latin: Parere, obsequi, facere quod iubetur

examples.original: Certe id firmissimum longe imperium est quo oboedientes gaudent.
examples.translation: You have at hand the means of waxing great and supremely glorious.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Hos itaque, ut ait Sallustius, ”ventri oboedientes” animalium loco numeremus, non hominum, quosdam vero ne animalium quidem, sed mortuorum.
examples.translation: Therefore those who, as Sallusta puts it, ”hearken to their bellies,” should be numbered among the animals, and not among men;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: adjj. [puteo], rotten, decaying, putrefying, stinking, putrid.
English: a tall plant resembling the willow, the chastetree

examples.original: Ut fugiunt aquilas, timidissima turba, columbae, Ut fugit invisos agna novella lupos: Sic illae timuere viros sine more ruentes;
examples.translation: As doves, most timorous of birds, flee from the eagles, as the weanling lamb from the hated wolf, so feared they the men rushing wildly on them;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Semper enim boni assiduique domini referta cella vinaria, olearia, etiam penaria est, villaque tota locuples est, abundat porco haedo agno gallina, lacte caseo melle.
examples.translation: For the provident and industrious proprietor always has his store-room and cellars well filled with oil and wine and provisions;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: place into or upon (mostly anteclass. and post-Aug.).

examples.original: Sed Vergilius a Cremona Mediolanum et inde paulo post transiit in urbem.
examples.translation: Virgil, however, moved from Cremona to Mediolanum, and shortly afterwards from there to Rome.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Virgil

examples.original: Imperioso quoque Manlio cognomen inditum; Postumius nulla tristi nota est insignitus.
examples.translation: Besides, Manlius was given the surname Imperiosus—”the Despotic”—while Postumius received no such grim distinction.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Studuit Flaccus usque ad annum XII. aetatis suae Volaterris, inde Romae apud grammaticum Remmium Palaemonem et apud rhetorem Verginium Flavum.
examples.translation: Flaccus studied until the twelfth year of his age at Volaterrae, and then at Rome with the grammarian Remmius Palaemon and the rhetorician Verginius Flavus.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Poets. Persius

definitions: English: to pluck or pull, i. e. to deprive of the hair, feathers, etc.

examples.original: Non poterant salva esse, nisi vellent.
examples.translation: They could not survive except by desiring to do so.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Itaque pars magna bonitatis est velle fieri bonum.
examples.translation: You know what I mean by a good man?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ne parum locuples esset? at erat, et esset amplius si velles, populo cautum praedibus et praediis.
examples.translation: Even if the actual facts, the shamefulness of the wrong you were doing, left you unmoved;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to join or unite together, to associate; to do or hold in common, to share a thing with another, etc.
Latin: cōnexiōnem inter sē facere; coniungere ūnā; cōnectere
Latin: communiter aliquid habēre; commūnicāre

examples.original: Perpetuoque mihi sociatam foedere lecti Non patitur vivi funera flere viri.
examples.translation: And while I embrace the shattered fragments of my bark, he fights to possess my shipwrecked planks;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: a fight, combat, furious encounter (cf.: pugna, proelium, certamen, contentio, acies; freq. and good prose).

examples.original: Et nunc quiescerem ac tacerem libenter, nisi haec quoque pro patria dimicatio esset;
examples.translation: Even now I would gladly stop and hold my peace, were not this too the quarrel of my country;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Dictator ubi propiorem spe dimicationem vidit, ne militum virtuti damno locus esset, ignibus crebris relictis, qui conspectum hostium frustrarentur, silentio legiones educit;
examples.translation: So, leaving behind him numerous fires to deceive the enemy, he silently led the legions out.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A regular disposition, arrangement, in oratory

examples.original: Sed etiam si omnia a veteribus inventa sunt, hoc semper novum erit, usus et inventorum ab aliis scientia ac dispositio.
examples.translation: But even if the old masters have discovered everything, one thing will be always new,—the application and the scientific study and classification of the discoveries made by others.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: of or belonging to the day.

examples.original: Haud incertius diurno proelium fuit;
examples.translation: They could see to fight as well as in the daytime;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Quod nisi quieris, Menelae, hac dextra occides, diurnum accipit, in centunculo dormit.
examples.translation: Peace, Menelaus, or this hand shall slay thee!a receives a daily pittance and sleeps on rags.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to tear, pull, or pluck out (class.).
English: to make satisfaction, amends, atonement for a crime or a criminal; to purify any thing defiled with crime; to atone for, to expiate, purge by sacrifice

examples.original: Sed ea clades ingentibus expiata victoriis, postquam per alios atque alios robustissima capta sunt oppida, vario quidem eventu.
examples.translation: But for this disaster atonement was made by great victories, when the strongest cities were captured under different leaders and with different results.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Non id solum quaeritur, ut isto damnato bona restituantur iis quibus erepta sunt, sed et religiones deorum immortalium expiandae et civium Romanorum cruciatus multorumque innocentium sanguis istius supplicio luendus est.
examples.translation: The demand is not simply that he should be found guilty, and the property that he stole be restored to its owners: there must also be expiation for the violated sanctity of the immortal gods;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: A gathering, collecting.

examples.original: Totus inter stratum lectionemque divisus est.
examples.translation: The whole time has been divided between rest and reading.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Alit lectio ingenium et studio fatigatum, non sine studio tamen, reficit.
examples.translation: We ought not to confine ourselves either to writing or to reading;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Ad custodiendam linguae vel operis munditiam, cum lectione divina, etiam societas eorum qui Christo fideli devotione famulantur, plurimum iuvat.
examples.translation: Beside sacred study, the company also of men which serve Christ with faithful devotion is of great help in keeping pure lips and clean hands.
examples.author: Bede

definitions: English: goodness, worth, uprightness, honesty, probity; modesty (class.)
English: a state of confused hurry or alarm, agitation, confusion, consternation, trepidation (not freq. till the Aug. per.): numquae trepidatio? numqui tumultus? *

examples.original: Impulsa frons prima et trepidatio subsidiis inlata;
examples.translation: Their front was first driven in and communicated its disorder to the supports;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Equitem clara increpans voce, ut hostes exaudirent, redire in proelium iubet: nihil trepidatione opus esse;
examples.translation: The horseman he reprimanded in a loud voice, that the enemy might overhear him, and ordered him to go back and fight;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a reed, cane (less freq. than harundo)
English: to taste, to take a little of any thing (freq. and class.; cf.: libo, manduco, edo, etc.).

examples.original: Leporem et gallinam et anserem gustare fas non putant;
examples.translation: They account it wrong to eat of hare, fowl, and goose;
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: an executioner, hangman, Plaut Bacch. 4, 4, 37
English: a skin, hide (post-class. and rare)
English: of or belonging to natural philosophy or physics, natural, physical
English: To strew over, cover by strewing, bestrew, to thatch, floor, pave, spread, cover (class. in prose and poetry).
English: the time of equal days and nights, the equinox
English: to carry out or forth, to convey out, lead forth (rare but class.).

examples.original: Non dicam illinc hoc signum ablatum esse et illud: hoc dico, nullum te Aspendi signum, Verres, reliquisse, omnia ex fanis, ex locis publicis, palam, spectantibus omnibus, plaustris evecta exportataque esse.
examples.translation: I shall not allege that from this town this or that particular statue was removed. My charge is that Verres did not leave one single statue behind;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: during the day, in the daytime

examples.original: Castra opportunis locis erant posita ibique castella viginti tria facta, quibus in castellis interdiu stationes ponebantur, ne qua subito eruptio fieret: haec eadem noctu excubitoribus ac firmis praesidiis tenebantur.
examples.translation: In these piquets would be posted by day to prevent any sudden sortie; by night the same stations were held by sentries and strong garrisons.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: name of a Roman gens
English: that may be hurled or cast, that is thrown or hurled, missile (not in Cic. or Cæs.)

examples.original: Sparsit et missilia variarum rerum et panaria cum obsonio viritim divisit;
examples.translation: He also threw about gifts of various kinds, and gave each man a basket of prepared food.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: a taking possession of a thing; a seizing, occupying (class.).

examples.original: Numquam enim non succedent occupationes novae;
examples.translation: For there is never a moment when fresh employments will not come along;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Stulta est enim, mi Lucili, et minime conveniens litterato viro occupatio exercendi lacertos et dilatandi cervicem ac latera firmandi;
examples.translation: It is indeed foolish, my dear Lucilius, and very unsuitable for a cultivated man, to work hard over developing the muscles and broadening the shoulders and strengthening the lungs.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Huius igitur rei tractatus, si tamen ad liquidum a talibus, quales nos sumus, examinari potest, curam atque operam negotiosissimam postulat ac per hoc mentem ab his occupationibus otiosissimam.
examples.translation: The treatment of this problem, if indeed it can be clearly investigated by one such as myself, demands attention and the most laborious application, and therefore a mind quite free from such occupations as mine.
examples.author: Augustine

definitions: English: to be stiff, numb, motionless, inactive, torpid, sluggish, etc. (syn.: langueo, languesco, stupeo, rigeo).

examples.original: Frigere ac torpere senis consilia.
examples.translation: The old man’s strategy was cold and torpid.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: hateful, odious, vexatious, offensive, unpleasant, disagreeable, annoying, troublesome
Latin: plēnus odiō esse, molestus

examples.original: I nunc, claude fores, custos odiose puellae, Et centum duris postibus obde seras!
examples.translation: Go now, hateful guardian, bar the lady’s door, and add a hundred bolts to the sturdy posts.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: one who runs over to the enemy, a deserter (cf. perfuga).
English: to be fluid or liquid, to flow, melt, dissolve
English: a myrtle, myrtle-tree
English: plant, or set near something
English: toward; constr. with

examples.original: Tum ad equites dictator advolat obtestans ut fesso iam pedite descendant ex equis et pugnam capessant.
examples.translation: The dictator then dashed up to the knights and besought them, since the foot-soldiers were exhausted, to dismount and enter the fight.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A fine form, beauty

examples.original: Quis de exceptione et formula perpetietur ilea immensa volumina quae pro M. Tullio aut Aulo Caecina legimus?
examples.translation: Would anyone endure the interminable arguments about pleas and procedure which we get in the speeches delivered in defence of M. Tullius or Aulus Caecina?
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: unaccustomed, unusual (class.).

examples.original: Is labor urbano militi insolitus contundit animos.
examples.translation: The work involved was strange to the town troops and broke their spirit.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Huius adventus et Mithridatem insolita inflammatum victoria continuit et Tigranem magnis copiis minitantem Asiae retardavit.
examples.translation: His arrival restrained Mithridates, who was elated by the unusual experience of victory, and checked Tigranes, who was threatening Asia with great forces.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Quin et natalem Vitellii diem Caecina ac Valens editis tota urbe vicatim gladiatoribus celebravere, ingenti paratu et ante illum diem insolito.
examples.translation: Moreover, Caecina and Valens celebrated his birthday by giving gladiatorial shows in every precinct of the city on an enormous scale unheard of up to that time.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: a second time, to repeat (syn.: duplico, repeto).
Latin: aliquid tempore secundo agere, iterum facere; renovō, reficiō
English: or not, is used in the second half of a disjunctive interrogation, corresponding to -ne or utrum, and also without a corresp interrog, particle in the first half

examples.original: Ampulla enim sit necne sit, quis non iure optimo irrideatur si laboret?
examples.translation: But rid a man of bodily deformity or agonies of pain, and you earn his deepest gratitude;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Utrum enim sit voluptas in iis rebus quas primas secundum naturam esse diximus necne sit, ad id quod agimus nihil interest.
examples.translation: For whether pleasure is or is not one of the objects we have called the primary things in accordance with nature makes no difference for our present inquiry.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Petebatur a me frumenti copia, annonae vilitas: possem aliquid in ea re necne ratio non habebatur: flagitabar bonorum expostulatione: improborum convitia sustinere non poteram.
examples.translation: I was asked to procure plentiful supplies of corn, and a decrease in its price; but whether I had any powers in the matter or not was never taken into account.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: cut loose

examples.original: Metellus, simul ac venit Syracusas, utrumque rescidit, et de Epicrate et de Heraclio.
examples.translation: As soon as he reached Syracuse, he cancelled both judgements, that against Epicrates and that against Heraclius.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Refecto ponte, quem superioribus diebus hostes resciderant, exercitum traducit et secundo flumine ad Lutetiam iter facere coepit.
examples.translation: Repairing the bridge, which the enemy had cut down in the days preceding, he led the army across, and began to march down stream towards Lutetia.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Provinciae toti quam maximum potest militum numerum imperat (erat omnino in Gallia ulteriore legio una), pontem qui erat ad Genavam iubet rescindi.
examples.translation: From the whole Province he requisitioned the largest possible number of troops (there was in Further Gaul no more than a single legion), and ordered the bridge at Geneva to be broken down.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: a scale (of a fish, serpent, etc.).
English: to stop somewhere, to tarry, linger, abide, sojourn, remain, stay

examples.original: At nobis in ipsa commorandum est.
examples.translation: But our abiding-place should be in wisdom itself.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Caesar Avarici complures dies commoratus summamque ibi copiam frumenti et reliqui commeatus nactus exercitum ex labore atque inopia refecit.
examples.translation: Caesar halted at Avaricum for several days, and by the immense quantity of corn and all other supplies which he found there recuperated the army after toil and want.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: to come over or upon
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; vēni, ventum, 4

examples.original: Ita iam sua sponte aegris animis legati ab regibus superveniunt sine mentione reditus bona tantum repetentes.
examples.translation: The senate, having given them a hearing, debated the question for several days;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Sed supervenientibus ab urbe nuntiis ut occisum Neronem cunctosque in verba sua iurasse cognovit, deposita legati suscepit Caesaris appellationem iterque ingressus est paludatus ac dependente a cervicibus pugione ante pectus;
examples.translation: But when some messengers came from the city, reporting that Nero was dead and that all the people had sworn allegiance to him, he laid aside the title of governor and assumed that of Caesar.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: to dispute, quarrel, strive.
English: to come forth, stand up, arise, appear, rise, break forth (class. in prose and poetry; most freq. in Lucr. and the hist., esp. Liv.; in Cic. rare, perh. only once).

examples.original: Haec cum dixisset, risus omnium cum hilaritate coortus est, neque quisquam iudex ausus est de eo ferre suffragium.
examples.translation: When he had said this, there was laughter and merriment throughout the assembly and no juror ventured to vote for his condemnation.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Epaminondas

examples.original: Ferocioresque iterum coorti Valerius Horatiusque vociferari ut de re publica liceret dicere; dicturos ad populum, si in senatu per factionem non liceat;
examples.translation: They would address the people, they said, if they were restrained by a faction from speaking in the senate;
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Volscos deinde et Aequos, seu Carventana arx retenta in spem seu Verrugine amissum praesidium ad iram cum impulisset, fama adfertur summa vi ad bellum coortos;
examples.translation: Then came a rumour that the Volsci and Aequi, whether encouraged by their defence of the citadel of Carventum or angered by the loss of the garrison at Verrugo, had risen in prodigious strength;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to low, bellow (syn. boo).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n.; īvi and ĭi, ītum, 4

definitions: English: unfermented wine, must

examples.original: Temporibus certis maturam rusticus uvam Deligit, et nudo sub pede musta fluunt;
examples.translation: At fixed seasons the countryman picks the ripened grapes, and the vintage flows beneath his naked foot;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: of or belonging to the condition of a freedman

examples.original: Ateius Philologus libertinus Athenis est natus.
examples.translation: Lucius Ateius Philologus was a freedman, born at Athens.
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of Illustrious Men. Grammarians And Rhetoricians. Grammarians

examples.original: Equites Romani obtulere operam pecuniasque, etiam libertinis idem munus ultro flagitantibus.
examples.translation: This pretended devotion, which was in reality prompted by fear, resulted in enthusiasm for the emperor;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Eodem anno Cn. Flavius Cn. filius scriba, patre libertino humili fortuna ortus, ceterum callidus vir et facundus, aedilis curulis fuit.
examples.translation: In the same year a government clerk, Gnaeus Flavius, the son of Gnaeus, was curule aedile.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: careful; diligent, scrupulous; accurate

examples.original: Omnis enim est natura diligens sui.
examples.translation: For love of self is inherent in every species;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Plato ipse ad senectutem se diligentia protulit.
examples.translation: Plato himself, by taking pains, advanced to old age.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Cui ille: ”Tu quidem macte virtute diligentiaque esto!
examples.translation: The consul replied: ”For yourself, I commend your conduct and your diligence;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: door-post.

examples.original: I nunc, claude fores, custos odiose puellae, Et centum duris postibus obde seras!
examples.translation: Go now, hateful guardian, bar the lady’s door, and add a hundred bolts to the sturdy posts.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: to remove from
English: a Roman surname. So esp. L. Appuleius Saturninus, a tribune of the people A.U.C. 654; who, with C. Servilius Glaucia, was pronounced guilty of treason and put to death

examples.original: In hortos, in quibus devertebatur Saturninus, pergunt.
examples.translation: They hurried to the gardens where Saturninus had his quarters;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Interim Aponius Saturninus cum legione septima Claudiana advenit.
examples.translation: In the meantime Aponius Saturninus arrived with the Seventh or Claudian legion.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Seditio Apvleiana III, 16Nihilo minus Apuleius Saturninus Gracchanas adserere leges non destitit.
examples.translation: The Revolution of Apuleius 16. Apuleius Saturninus continued nevertheless to promote the Gracchan proposals;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: Any hard stone found in fields, a pebble-stone, a flint, flint-stone
Latin: Species dura crystalli, colore nigro, pullo, vel fusco. Chalybe icto, scintillas emittit

examples.original: Membraque vinxerunt tinctis ferrugine pannis, A male deserto quos rapuere rogo: Et, ne non fultum nuda tellure iaceret, Molle super silices inposuere caput.
examples.translation: They swathed his limbs in bands of dusky hue, snatched from a pyre abandoned as accursed; and lest it lie unpropped on the naked earth they set a flint-stone beneath his baby head.
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: covering/cover/protection; clothing; body armor
English: a couch running round three sides of a table for reclining on at meals, an eating-couch, table-couch.

examples.original: Fabricavit et deceris Liburnicas gemmatis puppibus, versicoloribus velis, magna thermarum et porticuum et tricliniorum laxitate magnaque etiam vitium et pomiferarum arborum varietate;
examples.translation: He also built Liburnian galleys with ten banks of oars, with sterns set with gems, particoloured awnings, huge spacious baths, colonnades, and banquet-halls, and even a great variety of vines and fruit trees;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: of or pertaining to cattle or oxen (class.)
English: call out together.
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Sed idem hoc omnes tibi ex omni domo conclamabunt, Peripatetici, Academici, Stoici, Cynici.
examples.translation: But this same watchword rings in your ears from every sect,—Peripatetic, Academic, Stoic, Cynic.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Quos cum apud se in castris Ariovistus conspexisset, exercitu suo praesente conclamavit: Quid ad se venirent?
examples.translation: He gave them instructions that they should ascertain and bring back to him the views of Ariovistus.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Id modo a multitudine conclamatum est ut L. Valerium et M. Horatium ad se mitterent: his se daturos responsum.
examples.translation: But the crowd called out in unison that they should send them Lucius Valerius and Marcus Horatius, to whom they would intrust their reply.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: Relating to or belonging to the head. In this signif. extant only in the

examples.original: Triumviri capitales tunc primum creati sunt. Censu acto lustrum conditum est.
examples.translation: A board of three to deal with capital offences was then chosen for the first time.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Is ab inimicis suis apud G. Sacerdotem praetorem rei capitalis cum accusatus esset, facile eo iudicio est liberatus.
examples.translation: Prosecuted by his enemies for a criminal offence in the praetor-ship of Gaius Sacerdos, he had no trouble, on that occasion, in securing an acquittal.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: T. Quinctius clamitat, cui rei capitalis dies dicta sit et de quo futurum propediem iudicium, eum indemnatum indicta causa non debere violari.
examples.translation: Titus Quinctius cried out that a man who had been charged with a capital crime and whose day of trial was at hand ought not to suffer violence, uncondemned and unheard.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to make booty, to plunder, spoil

examples.original: Pauci hostium evasere ex insidiis; praeda omnis recepta est.
examples.translation: But few of them escaped the ambush, and the spoils were all recovered.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Verum ex ista reperietis hereditate ita istum praedatum ut perpauca occulte fecerit;
examples.translation: But you will in fact find little concealment about the way in which he plundered that estate;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Itaque non ego vobis ut indicem praedas vestras, sed vos id cogendi estis ut in medium proferatis.”
examples.translation: And so it is not I that must be forced to tell of your plunder, but you that must be compelled to give it up.”
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: the cypress, an evergreen tree sacred to Pluto and used at funerals: Cupressus sempervirens, Linn.—
English: of yesterday, yesterday's
English: to grow in or upon any thing (perh. not ante-Aug.).
Latin: Maior fieri
English: untaught, unlearned, uninstructed, ignorant, unskilful.
English: a kept mistress, concubine of a married man.
entries.grammaticalClass: and, only in inscriptions; icis; f.

examples.original: Et Parin Oenone summos tenuisset ad annos, Si non Oebalia paelice laesa foret.
examples.translation: Oenone had kept Paris till life was o’er, had she not been harmed by her Oebalian rival.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quodque suae passa est paelex invita sororis, Excidat ante pedes lingua resecta tuos.
examples.translation: And, what the unwilling rival of her own sister suffered, may thy tongue cut out fall before thy feet.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Ante diem morior, sed nulla paelice laesa: Hoc faciet positae te mihi, terra, levem.
examples.translation: Now goes my spirit out upon the air whose name I once suspected: I faint, I die;
examples.author: Ovid

definitions: English: protection, defence, patronage (cf.: praesidium, clientela, tutela).

examples.original: Nullum est vitium sine patrocinio;
examples.translation: There is no vice which lacks some plea;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Harum utraque Macedonum patrociniis utebatur;
examples.translation: Both these parties depended upon the patronage of the Macedonians;
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Phocion

examples.original: Nam nec tu agitare et insequi poetas intermittis, et ego, cui desidiam advocationum obicis, cotidianum hoc patrocinium defendendae adversus te poeticae exerceo.
examples.translation: You on your part are never done assailing the poets with your invective, and I, whom you charge with neglect of professional duty, am daily retained to defend the art of poetry against you.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: standing open, open (syn. patens).
English: name of a Roman gens.

examples.original: A. deinde Postumius et T. Verginius consules facti.
examples.translation: Next Aulus Postumius and Titus Verginius were made consuls.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Adversus Tarquinium Superbum cum Latinorum exercitu bellum inferentem Aulus Postumius dictator prospere pugnavit.
examples.translation: Aulus Postumius the dictator fought a successful battle against Tarquinius Superbus, who was advancing with an army of Latins.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: In ea castra Q. Fabius, P. Volumnius, A. Postumius legati ab Roma venerunt questum iniurias et e X foedere res repetitum.
examples.translation: To this camp came Quintus Fabius, Publius Volumnius, and Aulus Postumius, envoys from Rome, to complain of the wrongs done and demand restitution, as provided in the treaty.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to spit back or

examples.original: Impatiens animus nec adhuc tractabilis artem Respuit, atque odio verba monentis habet.
examples.translation: The impatient and as yet intractable spirit rejects skill and holds in abhorrence words of counsel.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Licet haec ipsa et quae deinceps dicturus sum aures tuae, Materne, respuant, cui bono est si apud te Agamemnon aut Iason diserte loquitur?
examples.translation: Very likely you will not relish what I am saying, Maternus, or what I intend to state in the course of my argument;
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Sive enim non respuit, humanitate eius inritamur, sive contempsit, superbia accendimur.
examples.translation: If our love be not spurned, we are excited by its kindness;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: slowly, gently, soflly, gradually

examples.original: Si apud principes quoque haud satis prospere esset pugnatum, a prima acie ad triarios se sensim referebant.
examples.translation: If the principes, too, were unsuccessful in their fight, they fell back slowly from the battle-line on the triarii.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: s self under any thing; to fall down

examples.original: Deinde succubui et eo perductus sum, ut ipse destillarem ad summam maciem deductus.
examples.translation: For when I was still young, I could put up with hardships and show a bold front to illness.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Potius ergo illa dicantur, turpe esse, viri non esse debilitari dolore, frangi, succumbere.
examples.translation: If that be true, are you not guilty of a crime in advising him to end his life?
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Mors tamen eminuit clarorum in strage virorum Pugnacis Domiti, quem clades fata per omnes Ducebant: nusquam Magni fortuna sine illo Succubuit.
examples.translation: Yet one death was most noticeable in that carnage of famous men—the death of that stubborn warrior, Domitius. Fate led him from defeat to defeat;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a. [perh. for suppetito, from suppeto].

examples.original: Itaque Pometinae manubiae, quae perducendo ad culmen operi destinatae erant, vix in fundamenta suppeditavere.
examples.translation: Hence the Pometian spoils, which had been destined to carry the building up to the roof, barely sufficed for the foundations.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Fit quoque ut interdum non suppeditetur imago eiusdem generis, sed femina quae fuit ante, in manibus vir uti factus videatur adesse, aut alia ex alia facies aetasque sequatur.
examples.translation: It sometimes happens again that the image that follows up is not of the same kind, but what was before a woman seems to be changed into a man in our grasp;
examples.author: Lucretius

definitions: English: a military ensign, standard, banner, flag.

examples.original: Et Volumnius signa canere ac vexilla efferri castris iussit;
examples.translation: Volumnius, too, bade sound the signal and advance the banners from the camp.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Aquileiam progressae, proturbatis qui de Othone nuntiabant laceratisque vexillis nomen Vitellii praeferentibus, rapta postremo pecunia et inter se divisa, hostiliter egerant.
examples.translation: Their conduct filled them with fear, and then fear brought the reflection that acts might win them credit with Vespasian for which they would have to apologize to Vitellius.
examples.author: Tacitus

definitions: English: of the same mind, united, agreeing, concordant, harmonious (class. in prose and poetry).

examples.original: Illic depositis habitat Concordia telis: Illo, crede mihi, Gratia nata loco est.
examples.translation: Therein dwells Concord when the fight is o’er; there, believe me, was Reconciliation born.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Quae si perpetua concordia sit, quis non spondere ausit maximum hoc imperium inter finitimos brevi futurum esse?
examples.translation: And if this harmony should last, who would not make bold to warrant that our empire would soon be the greatest among the neighbouring peoples?
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Et in unica concordia inter ipsos, qui consensus privatis interdum inutilis est, summa adversus alios aequitas erat.
examples.translation: And while they maintained an unparalleled harmony amongst themselves—a unanimity sometimes prejudicial to the governed,—they treated others with the utmost fairness.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to carry, bring

examples.original: Hos consules Piso Q. Fabio et P. Decio suggerit biennio exempto quo Claudium Volumniumque et Cornelium cum Marcio consules factos tradidimus.
examples.translation: Piso makes these men follow Quintus Fabius and Publius Decius, omitting the two years in which we have placed the consulship of Claudius and Volumnius and that of Cornelius and Marcius.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: to make blunt or dull, to blunt, dull
English: a hungry person
Latin: famem habere

examples.original: Omne animal terrestre alget, esurit, sitit;
examples.translation: Now every earthly living thing gets cold or hungry or thirsty;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et quidem vel esurienti ad ista veniendum est.
examples.translation: Even though we starve, we must reach that goal.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Et doleas oportet et sitias et esurias et senescas, si tibi longior contigerit inter homines mora, et aegrotes et perdas aliquid et pereas.
examples.translation: You must suffer pain, and thirst, and hunger, and old age too, if a longer stay among men shall be granted you; you must be sick, and you must suffer loss and death.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: a Phœnician; v. 1. Phoenice, A.

examples.original: Nam ille alter fortasse tamquam phoenix semel anno quingentesimo nascitur.
examples.translation: And it is not surprising, either, that greatness develops only at long intervals;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: harmlessness.

examples.original: Ac primum quanta innocentia debent esse imperatores!
examples.translation: First, how great is the integrity needed by a general;
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Non id solum quaeritur, ut isto damnato bona restituantur iis quibus erepta sunt, sed et religiones deorum immortalium expiandae et civium Romanorum cruciatus multorumque innocentium sanguis istius supplicio luendus est.
examples.translation: The demand is not simply that he should be found guilty, and the property that he stole be restored to its owners: there must also be expiation for the violated sanctity of the immortal gods;
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: to double (class.)
English: a betrayer, traitor (class.)

examples.original: Sic fraus proditorum irrita fuit.
examples.translation: Thus the deceit of the traitors proved fruitless.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nemo umquam sapiens proditori credendum putavit.
examples.translation: No wise man ever felt that a traitor ought to be trusted.
examples.author: Cicero

examples.original: Falisci cum obsiderentur, mira est visa fides imperatoris, nec inmerito, quod ludi magistrum, urbis proditorem, cum his quos adduxerat pueris vinctum sibi ultro remisisset.
examples.translation: Veii was thoroughly plundered and destroyed. When the Falisci were being besieged, the honourable conduct of the Roman commander was a subject of admiration, and not without reason;
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: to set bounds to, mark off by boundaries, to bound, limit (class.; syn.: finio, definio).
Latin: Terminos constituere
Latin: Certis finibus circumscribere

examples.original: Ille enim habet suum finem, inania et ex libidine orta sine termino sunt.
examples.translation: For this has its bounds, but waywardness and the acts that spring from wilful lust are without boundaries.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: An exposing of an infant (post-class.), Justin. 1, 4, 9; 1, 5, 4.—
English: not to confess, to contradict, deny, disown.

examples.original: Cetera saepe tamen potuere admissa negari, Et crimen nox est infitiata suum: Nostra notat fusco digitos iniuria suco Cortice contactas inficiente manus.
examples.translation: Yet other crimes when committed can often be denied, and night disavows her guilty deed: injury done to me marks the fingers with dark juice, and my bark stains the hands that touch it.
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Qua pacta acceptaque cum parata cetera ad bellum essent sequique Etruscus iuberet, infitias eunt mercedem se belli Romanis inferendi pactos: quidquid acceperint accepisse ne agrum Etruscum vastarent armisque lacesserent cultores;
examples.translation: When this had been agreed upon and received, and the Etruscans, having completed the rest of their preparations for the war, bade their new allies follow them, the Gauls demurred.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: another name of the patriarch Jacob
English: the principal river of Italy

examples.original: Sic pleno Padus ore tumens super aggere tutas Excurrit ripas et totos concutit agros;
examples.translation: Thus the river Po, swollen with brimming estuary, overflows its banks though defended by dykes, and oversets whole districts;
examples.author: Lucan

examples.original: Ac primi quidem impetus turbo inter Padum atque Ticinum valido statim fragore detonuit.
examples.translation: The tempest of the first assault crashed with a mighty roar between the Padus and the Ticinus.
examples.author: Florus

definitions: English: as much as possible, extremely, exceedingly
English: to come before, precede, get the start of, to outstrip, anticipate, to prevent
Latin: Ante venire, praeoccupare
Latin: Antecellere

examples.original: Erectus Samnis Paelignusque et Marsi aemulatione quod Campania praevenisset, ut in novo obsequio, ad cuncta belli munia acres erant.
examples.translation: The Samnites, Paelignians, and Marsians were jealous because Campania had anticipated them, and eagerly undertook all services required by war with the enthusiasm that attaches to every new devotion.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Prius igitur quam ultra progrederetur, praeventus est ab Agrippina, quam praeter haec conscientia quoque nec minus delatores multorum criminum arguebant.
examples.translation: But before he could go any farther, he was cut short by Agrippina, who was being accused besides of many other crimes both by her own conscience and by informers.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: hoar-frost, rime

examples.original: Nihil praeter nives pruinasque et silvas habent.
examples.translation: Their territory consists entirely of snow, ice and forest.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Urebant montana nives camposque iacentes Non duraturae conspecto sole pruinae, Atque omnis propior mergenti sidera caelo Aruerat tellus hiberno dura sereno.
examples.translation: The mountains were nipped by snow, and the low-lying plains by hoar frost that would vanish at first sight of the sun;
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: a conversation, conference, discourse
Latin: Actio loquendi inter minime duos homines

examples.original: Eo, ut erat dictum, ad colloquium venerunt.
examples.translation: Thither, as agreed, they came for the parley.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: Dies colloquio dictus est ex eo die quintus.
examples.translation: A day—the fifth after that—was appointed for the parley.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

examples.original: In colloquium convenit, condiciones non convenerunt.
examples.translation: He had an interview with Scipio, but they could not agree upon terms.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: The Book On The Great Generals Of Foreign Nations. Hannibal

definitions: English: the Hebrews (Pauline letter)
Latin: decimus nonus liber Novum Testamentum, compositum tredecim capitula
English: to accuse one of something, to complain of, find fault with, blame (cf.: arguo, accuso, vitupero; class., but not in Cic.).—Constr

examples.original: Excepta vox est, cum teporem incusaret, statim futurum ut incalescerent : vernile dictum omnem invidiam in eum vertit, tamquam signum incendendae Cremonae dedisset, quae iam flagrabat.
examples.translation: This answer of some slave turned all the odium of what followed on Antonius, as if he had given the signal to burn Cremona, which was indeed at that moment in flames.
examples.author: Tacitus

examples.original: Ap. Claudium, quia dissuaserat legem, maiore nunc auctoritate eventum reprehensi ab se consilii incusantem, dictatorem consensu patriciorum Servilius consul dicit, dilectusque et iustitium indictum.
