definitions: English: to make soft or tender, to soften by steeping, to soak, steep, macerate (not in Cic. or Cæs.).

examples.original: Torquet ingratus se et macerat;
examples.translation: The ungrateful man tortures and torments himself;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: name of a Roman gens

examples.original: P. Valerio Publicolae datus e plebe collega C. Marcius Rutulus.
examples.translation: Publius Valerius Publicola was elected, with a plebeian colleague named Gaius Marcius Rutulus.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Nec variatum comitiis est, quin cum Manlio Naevio censor Marcius crearetur.
examples.translation: There was no dissenting opinion shown at the assembly, and Marcius was elected, along with Manlius Naevius.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Erat tum in castris inter primores iuvenum Cn. Marcius,4 adulescens et consilio et manu promptus, cui cognomen postea Coriolano fuit.
examples.translation: There was in camp at that time amongst the young nobles Gnaeus Marcius, a youth of active mind and ready hand, who afterwards gained the surname of Coriolanus.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: war, battle: civili Mavorte, Aus Idyll. 4, 65.— Hence

examples.original: Quacumque vagatur, Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellona flagellum, Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, Nox ingens scelerum est;
examples.translation: He visits the corpses that sprawl on the wide plain; with his own hand he staunches the wound that would otherwise pour out all the blood of many a man.
examples.author: Lucan

definitions: English: peeled barley, pearl-barley
English: a mother's brother, maternal uncle (a brother of the father, patruus).
Latin: Matris frater
Latin: Materterae maritus

examples.original: Sepultus est iuxta viam Appiam ad quintum lapidem in monumento Q. Caecilii, avunculi sui.
examples.translation: He was buried near the fifth milestone of the Appian Way in the tomb of Quintus Caecilius, his maternal uncle.
examples.author: Cornelius Nepos
examples.work: Excerpt From The Book Of Latin Historians. Atticus

examples.original: Nam avunculus maior Augustus quid de eo in utramque partem opinatus sit, quo certius cognoscatur, capita ex ipsius epistulis posui.
examples.translation: Finally to make it clearer what opinions, favourable and otherwise, his great uncle Augustus had of him, I have appended extracts from his own letters: IV.
examples.author: Suetonius

definitions: English: of or belonging to tablets, i. e.
English: a surname in the gens Aelia; e. g.

examples.original: Ad meliores transi: cum Catonibus vive, cum Laelio, cum Tuberone.
examples.translation: Change therefore to better associations: live with the Catos, with Laelius, with Tubero.
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Licinio libros haud dubie sequi linteos placet: Tubero incertus veri est.
examples.translation: Licinius sees fit to follow without hesitation the Linen Rolls: Tubero is uncertain where the truth lies.
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: A turf

examples.original: Est prope purpureos colles florentis Hymetti Fons sacer et viridi caespite mollis humus: Silva nemus non alta facit;
examples.translation: Near the purple hills of flowery Hymettus there is a sacred spring and ground soft with green turf: trees of no great height form a grove;
examples.author: Ovid

examples.original: Cadaver eius clam in hortos Lamianos asportatum et tumultuario rogo semiambustum levi caespite obrutum est, postea per sorores ab exsilio reversas erutum et crematum sepultumque.
examples.translation: His body was conveyed secretly to the gardens of the Lamian family, where it was partly consumed on a hastily erected pyre and buried beneath a light covering of turf;
examples.author: Suetonius
examples.work: Lives Of The Caesars 4. Gaius Caligula

definitions: English: plqpf. despoponderas

examples.original: Iuvenis evasit vere indolis regiae, nec, cum quaereretur gener Tarquinio, quisquam Romanae iuventutis ulla arte conferri potuit, filiamque ei suam rex despondit.
examples.translation: The youth turned out to be of a truly royal nature, and when Tarquinius sought a son-in-law there was no other young Roman who could be at all compared to Servius;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: Neutr., to depart from its race or kind, to degenerate (class.).
entries.grammaticalClass: v. n. and a.; āvi, ātum, 1

examples.original: Namque horum posteri meliores illi quidem, mea sententia, quam reliquarum philosophi disciplinarum, sed ita degenerant ut ipsi ex se nati esse videantur.
examples.translation: Their successors are indeed in my opinion superior to the philosophers of any other school, but are so unworthy of their ancestry that one might imagine them to have been their own teachers.
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: insolent, unyielding, obstinate, stiff-necked, stubborn, contumacious.

examples.original: At mores commodi. Quis contumacior?
examples.translation: Is it said that he is good-natured?
examples.author: Cicero

definitions: English: a maker, builder, framer, establisher, founder, author, compiler, etc.

examples.original: Primus ille et urbis et imperii conditor Romulus fuit, Marte genitus et Rhea Silvia.
examples.translation: The first founder both of the city and of the empire was Romulus, the son of Mars and Rhea Silvia.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Nec nominis homines tum pertaesum esse, quippe quo Iovem appellari fas sit, quo Romulum, conditorem urbis, deincepsque reges, quod sacris etiam ut sollemne retentum sit: superbiam violentiamque tum perosos regis.
examples.translation: Nor was it the name, said he, which had then disgusted men, since by this name Jupiter was duly called; and Romulus, the founder of the City: and the successive kings;
examples.author: Livy

definitions: English: a laying waste, ravaging, plundering, spoiling, devastation, etc. (not in Cic.).

examples.original: Vetusius consul missus est; is finis populationibus fuit.
examples.translation: Vetusius the consul was dispatched to them, and this ended the pillaging.
examples.author: Livy

examples.original: Agrorum atque vicorum populatione non contentus in ipsa Numidiae capita impetum fecit;
examples.translation: Not content with laying waste the fields and villages, he attacked the principal cities of Numidia.
examples.author: Florus

examples.original: Caesar suos a proelio continebat, ac satis habebat in praesentia hostem rapinis pabulationibus populationibusque prohibere.
examples.translation: Caesar kept his troops from fighting, accounting it sufficient for the present to prevent the enemy from plundering, foraging, and devastation.
examples.author: Gaius Iulius Caesar

definitions: English: A state of body, and esp. of mind produced in one by some influence (cf. affectio, I.), a state or disposition of mind, affection, mood: adfectuum duae sunt species: alteram Graeci

examples.original: Ex honestiore causa coit turpis adfectus?
examples.translation: Can a cause which is more honourable produce a passion that is base?
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: Indulgendum est enim honestis adfectibus;
examples.translation: For one must indulge genuine emotions;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

examples.original: In omnes personas hic exardescit affectus;
examples.translation: But indeed this emotion blazes out against all sorts of persons;
examples.author: Seneca The Younger

definitions: English: to make slow, to hinder, delay, retard, impede, prevent
entries.grammaticalClass: v. a. and n.; āvi, ātum, 1

definitions: English: the occupation of an artifex, a profession, trade, an employment, a handicraft
Latin: Professio artificis, ars vel artis exercitatio
Latin: Ab artifice opus ingeniose perfectum
English: to accommodate one's self to the will of a person; to comply with, yield to, gratify, humor, submit to; with
English: to be sure, certainly; well, upon by word; but, on the other hand
English: an overseer, superintendent.
English: by stealth, secretly, privily
English: a sharing, parting, partition; a division, distribution.
English: very little, very small, petty, insignificant (class.).
English: a surname in the gens Valeria.
